New Delhi did not even bother to acknowledge it." For him, "That was the turning point".

Heading: BJP’s second LS list out: Rajnath from Ghaziabad, Varun Gandhi from Pilibhit - Indian Express
Content:
After intervening on behalf of sacked Jet Airways employees, Raj Thackeray-led MNS has been approached by the employees of National Rayon Corporation (NRC) Ltd.

About 1,500 employees of the NRC met Raj at his residence on Tuesday, asking him to intervene on their behalf and discuss their demands with the management.

The company has reportedly entered a multi-crore deal. Many employees claimed that they had not been paid by the company for the last 10 months and were also being asked to vacate the residential premises to facilitate the handover. The employees asked Raj to save their livelihood.

"We fear that the handover is never going to take place. We will be rendered homeless and without jobs. He (Raj Thackeray) has assured us that MNS will be taking up the issue for us. We are sure that he will be able to solve our problem," said Anuradha Gangawane, who led the women's delegation to Raj's residence.

"The employees had not been informed about the deal and have not been paid for the last 10 months. We will definitely intervene on their behalf. We have told them to be cautious about any new construction activity on their premises," said Sanjay Ghadi, senior MNS leader who met the employees at Raj's residence.

Heading: Tapasi case: CPM men held guilty - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP on Tuesday declared its second list of candidates for the next Lok Sabha elections with party president Rajnath Singh set to contest Ghaziabad and party's young face, Varun Gandhi, set to make his Lok Sabha debut from Pilibhit.

Rajnath was campaigning for the party in Chhattisgarh and Varun in Pilibhit when the list was declared in Delhi on Tuesday. Rajnath has been making frequent trips to Ghaziabad in the last few weeks and is set to get a huge boost with a tie-up with the Ajit Singh's Jat-dominated RLD. The Jat-Gurjjar combine is expected to work to his advantage. As for Varun, he has been specially focusing on the youth agenda in and around Pilibhit.

Uttar Pradesh remains the weak link in the BJP's Mission 2009, and its second list, consisting of heavyweights, therefore, assumes significance. Among the 11 candidates announced on Tuesday, Murli Manohar Joshi will contest from Varanasi while Maneka Gandhi will shift from Pilibhit to neighbouring Aonla.

Party vice-presidents Kalyan Singh and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi will contest from Etah and Rampur respectively. Santosh Gangwar will fight to retain his stronghold Bareilly while MP Pankaj Chaudhary will fight from Maharajganj.

Yogi Adityanath will contest from Gorakhpur, Dalit leader Ashok Pradhan from Bulandshahr and Bhanu Pratap Verma from Jalaun. The announcement on Lucknow will take a while, and the final name will have Atal Bihari Vajpayee's nod. Party spokesperson Prakash Javadekar said: "Lucknow will also be declared in subsequent lists. UP list will be out in phases."

Heading: The Nano files: Gujarat to probe as ‘Cabinet note’ leaks - Indian Express
Content:
In a blow to the CPI(M) ahead of the coming bypolls and Lok Sabha elections, a Chandernagore fast track court on Tuesday found party's former Singur zonal secretary Suhrid Dutta and his accomplice Debu Malik guilty of the murder of Tapasi Malik. The quantum of their punishment will be announced on Wednesday.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Amar Kanti Acharya held Dutta guilty of murder, criminal conspiracy and tampering of evidence.

While Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee welcomed the verdict, demanding that "the Chief Minister immediately resign taking responsibility of such acts by his party leader", the CPI(M) state leadership said it would appeal in a higher court. Ruling out expulsion of Dutta from the party, they called him an old comrade.

The charred body of Tapasi, a member of the Save Farmland Committee, had been found inside the Singur Nano project site on December 18, 2006. As Mamata Banerjee sat on a dharna over the issue and it snowballed, the state Government had handed over the probe to the CBI. Investigators concluded that Tapasi had been raped and murdered, before being set on fire.

The CPI(M)'s Hooghly district secretariat member, Balai Sanpui, who came to the court along with thousands of followers and other senior party leaders, said the legal battle was not over yet. The party senior leadership had said the same.

Heading: ‘TN fishermen carry LTTE arms’ - Indian Express
Content:
Worried by the reported leak of a "Cabinet note" containing details of incentives being offered to Tata Motors for its Nano car project in Gujarat, the state Government will conduct an internal probe. "As soon as we learnt on Monday evening that a 'Cabinet note' was being circulated among mediapersons, we directed the Industries Department to inquire into the matter," said a senior CMO official, adding that the possibility of a corporate rivalry behind the leak could not be ruled out.

This is what the leaked note says:

• West Bengal had declined to sell the Singur land to Tatas for the project, only leased it for 90 years at graded lease rates. Modi sold the Sanand land to the automaker, payable in eight annual instalments. The 'note' also mentions that the Tatas might be exempted from paying stamp duty, registration charges and land transfer charges.

• West Bengal had offered to sell power for the Nano plant at Rs 3 per KWH. Apparently, the Tatas asked Gujarat to facilitate 220 KVA of supply and also to exempt it from paying electricity duty.

• The 'note' also suggests the Tatas wanted exemption from state labour policy clauses that insist on 85 per cent local employment, including a 60 per cent quota in managerial and supervisory jobs.

• The Gujarat Government had not "clarified" to the Tatas its rule that 50 per cent of the amount granted as state sops should be invested in the state itself, and that two per cent of it should be contributed to the rural welfare programme — Gokul Gram Yojana.

• The Tatas had allegedly pushed for another 100 acres of land near Ahmedabad to set up a township; a pipeline at the state's cost to supply natural gas to the Nano project site; provision for 14,000 cubic metres of water per day at the site; and permission to draw groundwater for immediate needs.

• The 'sops' the Tatas were being provided were to be considered as 'special exception', which other similar industries would not be eligible for.

Heading: Navy foils pirates’ bid to hijack ship - Indian Express
Content:
On the eve of his visit to India, Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa on Tuesday said the LTTE was using Tamil fishermen to get weapons. Rajapaksa, who came to Male for the swearing-in ceremony of the new Maldivian President, told The Indian Express: "The fishermen issue is being manipulated. The LTTE is using Indian fishermen to bring arms and weapons in their trawlers."

His statement may raise a storm at a time when the DMK and other Tamil Nadu parties have been putting pressure on the UPA Government over the Lanka issue, including claims of "firing" on Tamil fishermen by the Sri Lankan Navy.

Rajapaksa arrived in Delhi on Tuesday night to attend the November 13 BIMSTEC Summit. He will have a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on the sidelines of the summit. "I will tell him all this... he is a friend," Rajapaksa told Express at a reception hosted for the visiting dignitaries after Nasheed's swearing-in.

Asked about New Delhi's aggressive diplomatic posturing on the Lankan issue, Rajapaksa said: "There are LTTE sympathisers in the DMK, and leaders like Vaiko etc." He said he understood the pressure on the PM: "In coalition politics, you have to balance. I manage a coalition of 13-14 parties at home, this is politics."

He added that he wasn't disturbed by the flurry of statements made by India. "There is no difference of opinion." He also clarified that the PM didn't call him, "I called the PM". When asked about India's insistence on a political settlement, Rajapaksa said Colombo was for a "practical solution". "We want a political solution... but we want a practical solution," Rajapaksa was clear.

The President claimed that the LTTE was getting weaker, and that Colombo was ready to talk to them, if they gave up their armed struggle. "We have always said, lay down your arms and we are ready to talk peace," he said. Rajapaksa regretted that while they had even taken political steps to bring the Tamil leadership in the mainstream, "the LTTE wants a separate state". He added that the Tamils too do not support the LTTE. "Ultimately, it is up to the (Tamil) people... what (Tamil) people want... They are not with the LTTE."

Heading: Nasheed reaches out to India for help - Indian Express
Content:
This was a 30-minute deployment at sea that the Indian Navy would not forget in a long time. In a swift, surgical operation off the Somalia coast on Tuesday morning, helicopter-borne commandoes of the Indian Navy thwarted two piracy attempts and rescued Indian and Saudi Arabian merchant vessels from heavily armed sea robbers.

The operation, the first of its kind after the Navy deployed a warship to patrol pirate-infested waters in the Gulf of Aden last month, was carried out by INS Tabar — India's most modern stealth frigate — and involved its elite Marine Commando force that responded to two distress calls within a span of half an hour.

The first distress call came from a Saudi Arabian chemical tanker, the NCC Tihama, at 10 am. The tanker was being shot at by heavily armed pirates on board three speed boats off Aden. The Navy, which launched an armed helicopter with marine commandoes from INS Tabar within 15 minutes, thwarted the attack by firing "warning shots" at the pirates.

While the helicopter was on its way back to the warship, the Navy received another distress call at 10.30 am from the Indian registered MV Jag Arnav, located 25 nautical miles away, which too came under attack from a different set of pirates.

The armed aircraft was then diverted towards the Indian ship and reached just in time to prevent the pirates from boarding the merchant vessel. "We received a distress call that pirates are firing with automatic weapons on an Indian merchant vessel. The helicopter reached just in time when the pirates were trying to board the ship," a senior Navy officer said. There is still no word on whether there were any casualties in the operation, the officer added.

The MV Jag Arnav, a 38,265-tonne bulk carrier owned by the Great Eastern Shipping Co Ltd, had transited the Suez Canal a few days ago and was heading towards India when it came under attack from the pirates.

After carrying out the airborne operation, the Indian warship escorted both the Indian and Saudi Arabian warship to safer waters.

This is the second incident on the high seas where the Indian Navy has rescued merchant vessels from pirates. In the first case in 1999, the Navy rescued a Japanese cargo vessel Alondra Rainbow that was hijacked by a ten-member Indonesian pirate gang in the Malacca Straits. The vessel was intercepted 400 km off Goa after a high-speed chase.

The Indian Navy started conducting anti-piracy patrols in the Gulf of Aden from October 23, after strikes by sea robbers increased in the past few months. The patrols, sanctioned by the Defence Ministry after persistent requests by the Indian Navy, are being carried out off the Somalia coast.

In an indication that the Navy will respond with full force to any piracy attempts on Indian vessels, Navy Chief Admiral Sureesh Mehta said, "Indian Naval Ships operating in piracy-infected areas are always in a high state of alert and have the capability to intervene by air or ship-borne weapons. Their mandate is to ensure that the safety of our sovereign assets is maintained."

The Navy had been asking for permission to patrol the Gulf of Aden for the past few months after a series of piracy attempts on merchant ships in the area. The Navy, which has been trying to increase its reach in the region, wanted to coordinate patrolling efforts with foreign navies which have been carrying out similar patrols.

The Navy feels that it needs greater authority to tackle piracy off the Somalia coast. While the Navy has proposed that the Chief of Navy Staff be given the direct authority to sanction action against pirates in the high seas, the ministry has said that all permissions should be routed through the South Block.

Heading: PMO refers back elevation of 3 judges - Indian Express
Content:
Even before he was sworn into office on Tuesday, new Maldivian President Mohamed Nasheed made a crucial telephone call. With his country facing a severe foreign exchange crisis, Nasheed last night called up Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to help the tiny nation of islands through its "economic difficulties", top sources told The Indian Express.

The PM, it is learnt, took the call in Qatar and assured him of assistance. This could translate into a financial aid of sorts, details of which will be worked out in the coming days.

Nasheed informed Vice-President Hamid Ansari, who called on him on Tuesday afternoon after the swearing-in ceremony, about the call. The fact that Nasheed called even before he took oath explains the urgency of the crisis.

Ministry of External Affairs Special Secretary (Policy) Dinesh Jain, who accompanied Ansari during the meeting, said: "He talked about the economic difficulties facing the country in terms of foreign exchange reserves. The Vice-President clearly conveyed that we can help them."

These are the first desperate calls being made by the new democratically elected President of Maldives, whose economy relies overwhelmingly on tourism.

It accounts for 28 per cent of the GDP of this tiny nation of three lakh people, and more than 60 per cent of its foreign exchange receipts. In fact, over 90 per cent of government tax revenue comes from import duties and tourism-related taxes. With the global financial crisis looming large, the tourism sector in Maldives has been badly hit.

Earlier in the day, in his first presidential address, Nasheed said: "The state of the economy is a cause for concern. However, we have always worked with tenacity and determination, qualities that have enabled us to secure many achievements."

The new President has also called for India's help in the areas of energy (especially solar energy) information technology, science and technology, health and education.

Nasheed conveyed to Ansari that he wanted to privatise public enterprises, build a school and two new hospitals. He also wants to build a robust public transport system — for which he invited bids from Indian companies, besides making a general appeal to Indian businessmen to make investments.

According to Indian High Commissioner in Maldives A K Pandey, Nasheed wants to "deepen and develop" ties with India, and there will be "no pause, no interruption".

Ansari also met outgoing Maldives president Maumoon Abdul Gayoom — who did not attend Nasheed's swearing-in — and talked about his role in the democratic transition. Pandey said "there was no valedictory feel" to the meeting between Ansari and Gayoom.

Nasheed's 90-minute swearing-in ceremony — held in Maldivian parliament, the Majlis — was attended by around a thousand people, including dignitaries like Sri Lanka President Mahinda Rajapaksa and Jordan Princess Haya Bint Al Hussein. The elaborate ceremony was accompanied by a Quran recitation and a 21-gun salute.

Heading: First batch of uranium could come from Kazakhstan - Indian Express
Content:
The Prime Minister's Office has referred back to the Law Ministry a file containing a Supreme Court collegium's recommendations over elevation of three High Court judges to the apex court.

The decision to return the file was taken after Law Minister H R Bhardwaj briefed PM Manmohan Singh on the issue last week. The Law Ministry is learnt to have recommended to the PM to send the matter back to the SC collegium for "reconsideration".

With Bhardwaj reported to be out of town for the next four days, it may take some time for the file, which has reached his office, to be sent to Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, who heads the collegium.

An official said it is rare for a collegium's recommendations to be referred back. "But they are well within their right to raise questions about the decision," said the official about the clarification sought by the PMO.

The matter pertains to the recommendation of the Supreme Court collegium for appointment of Kerala HC Chief Justice H L Dattu, Madras HC Chief Justice A K Ganguly and Patna HC Chief Justice R M Lodha as apex court judges.

The Government feels that while recommending the elevation of these three judges, the collegium has overlooked the case of their seniors — Delhi HC Chief Justice A P Shah, Madhya Pradesh HC Chief Justice A K Patnaik and Uttarakhand HC Chief Justice V K Gupta—for appointment to the Supreme Court.

Heading: 9 tribals arrested for tiger poaching by electrocution - Indian Express
Content:
The first batch of imported uranium for one of India's fuel-starved nuclear reactors is likely to come from Kazakhstan with a purchase order in this regard expected to be finalised by next month, sources said.

Kazakhstan figures high on the list of countries India is negotiating with for procuring high-grade uranium following the waiver New Delhi was able to obtain from the Nuclear Suppliers' Group (NSG) in September.

Official sources said talks with a Kazakhstan company were in advanced stage and, if things worked out well, an order could be placed sometime next month. The actual receipt of uranium would take at least a couple of months more.

However, as of now, the imported uranium would only be a minor relief for India's nuclear reactors, which have been operating at 40-60 per cent of their operational capacity for several months now due to a severe fuel crunch.

India is still to finalise its separation plan, identifying the nuclear reactor, which it wishes to place under IAEA safeguards and, thereby, make them eligible for using imported fuel. Till the separation plan is completed, this imported fuel, whenever it arrives, can be used only at Unit-2 of the Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station (RAPS), near Kota in Rajasthan, as this facility is already under the IAEA safeguards.

Heading: Rane denies criticised PM, blames media - Indian Express
Content:
After pits, snares and automobile cable nooses, live high-tension electric wires used by poachers are turning out to be a huge threat to tigers.

Nine Gond tribals were arrested by Kanha Tiger Reserve authorities on Tuesday for killing a tiger and other protected animals in the reserve. The accused confessed to using a powerful 11,000 volt electricity line for electrocuting the animals. Tragically, while the target was deer and antelope meat, an 8-year-old male tiger also got killed after falling into a live electric trap.

"We have arrested nine villagers who have confessed that they manipulated live 11 KV wires to lay traps for animals. They first killed a large sambar deer in the buffer zone of the tiger reserve and consumed the animal. On November 2, they relaid the trap and a male tiger, which lived in the buffer zone and was out hunting, was caught in the trap. Forest authorities found the dead body of the tiger the next day. Even though the accused say they did not intend to kill the tiger, this is a serious tiger poaching case. Two people from the same community, who are the masterminds, are absconding," says Kanha Park director R P Singh.

He says this dangerous trend has come close to claiming human lives. "Ten days ago, a forest guard was caught in a similar electrocution trap but he was rescued," Singh adds.

Experts say using electrocution is a relatively new poaching method in Kanha.

Heading: Arunachal was never officially demarcated, says China - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to douse the controversy over his reported criticism of the Prime Minister over the inflation issue, Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane said that he had merely pointed to inflation being a serious issue. Blaming the media for twisting his words, he said that he had also stressed the need for the adoption of new technologies and the increase in the per capita income of the state to ensure that the Prime Minister's plans of India becoming a superpower by 2020 were fulfilled.

Rane, who has openly taken on Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh in the past, had criticised the state government in his recent tour of the state and pointed out that in case the Lok Sabha elections were to be held now, the Congress would perform poorly.The Konkan strongman has recently suffered a setback with two of his strong supporters in the party high command, former Maharashtra Congress president Prabha Rau and AICC general secretary and Maharashtra in- charge Margaret Alva being shunted out.

While Rau was appointed the Governor of Himachal and Deshmukh loyalist Manikrao Thakre was selected to head the state Congress in her place, Alva had to quit her party post on Tuesday after alleging that money had changed hands for the grant of Congress nominations in the recent Karnataka state Assembly elections.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, an upset Rane denied reports of him criticising Singh over rising inflation at a rally at Pathardi in Ahmednagar on Monday and said his comments had been distorted by the media. A news agency report earlier in the day had quoted Rane as saying, "the Prime Minister who once said inflation won't rise is today saying otherwise. If the Prime Minister is saying such a thing, then whom should the common man trust?"

However, Rane on Tuesday said Singh had spoken about the need to ensure that India became a superpower by 2020 and stressed that the people needed to cooperate in this regard. He added it was necessary to adopt new technologies and increase the per capita income. He added that in the rally he had pointed out Singh's backtracking on his earlier assertion that the impact of the economic crisis and inflation would not affect India as evidence of the issue being a serious one.

Heading: New row in Gandhi saga, fumes as Govt shifts press secy - Indian Express
Content:
China on Tuesday angrily rejected India's assertion that Arunachal Pradesh is its integral part, insisting that Beijing never recognised the "illegal" McMahon Line and that the status of the border state was "never officially demarcated".

Deeply regretting External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee's statement that Arunachal Pradesh was part of India, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Qin Gang said New Delhi has not taken into account the "historical facts." "We deeply regret the Indian side's remarks, that take no regard of the historical facts," Qin said when asked to comment on Mukherjee's comments on Sunday in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh that the state was an integral part of India and that China was "aware" of it.

"China and India have never officially settled demarcation of borders, and China's stance on the eastern section of China-India borders is consistent and clear-cut," Qin said at a regular bi-weekly news briefing. "The current Chinese government, as well as previous ones, has never recognised the illegal 'McMahon Line'," the official Xinhua news agency quoted Qin as saying. "India knows this," Qin said, referring to the McMahon Line, the demarcation line drawn on the map referred to the Simla Convention in 1914.

Although China disputes its legal status, the McMahon Line is currently the effective boundary between China and India. Mukherjee had also said that "China is often making claims on Arunachal Pradesh, but Arunachal Pradesh has a special place in our heart." "People of Arunachal Pradesh regularly elect two representatives to the Lok Sabha and there is an elected state assembly carrying out the responsibility of administration like any of other 27 states. The question of parting company of Arunachal or any of its part does not arise," he had said.

As for the pending boundary issue between China and India, the Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman said that China is willing to find a solution, which is "fair, and acceptable" to the two sides, through peaceful and friendly negotiation in the spirit of mutual understanding and adjustment. Mukherjee's rejection of the Chinese claim on Arunachal Pradesh follows the recent declaration of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh during a visit to the state that Arunachal was 'our land of rising sun'. This is the second time within a week that Beijing has reacted sharply to Mukherjee's remarks on China. On November 7, China had rejected an apparent 'China threat' remark made by him during a speech.

Heading: Khanduri brings 28 posts outside OoP Act - Indian Express
Content:
Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi, who has been the villain of the piece in the eyes of the CPI(M) for his criticism of the state Government's actions on various occasions, has now locked horns with the Left Front Government over the transfer of his press secretary Dhruba Basu. Basu, an officer of the Information & Culture Department (I&C) under Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, received the order on November 8.

The standard practice has been that the Government usually consults the Governor before the transfer of any Raj Bhavan officer. This time, the practice was not followed, annoying Gandhi. He immediately crossed swords with the I&C Department, demanding that the officer be given back to him.

Basu, supposed to be replaced by chief of news bureau Apurba Chatterjee, had joined his present duty in May 2000. He become an anathema to the CPI(M) as he was perceived to have given the maximum media mileage to the Governor. Basu, also the Bengali language teacher of the Governor, was allotted a flat at Raj Bhavan quarters about a year ago.

On Tuesday, principal secretary to the Governor Rajendra Kumar, on behalf of the Governor, wrote to the I&C Department, saying the press secretary be retained in his post. Basu, who is going to retire in March 2012, also wrote a letter to principal secretary to the I&C Department Dilip Chakraborty, requesting him to allow him to stay in his office at Raj Bhavan.

Chakraborty said the transfer of Basu, who faces allegations of misbehaviour towards his colleagues, was a routine affair. "His is a transferable job and he cannot object if he is moved out after working more than eight years at the same post. I don't know why he wants to stick to that post. But, well, if the Governor takes up the matter with us, we will have to do something because he is the head of this state," Chakraborty said. However, according to sources, there are officers in the CM's secretariat as well as the Raj Bhavan who have been in their posts for more than 10 years.

Heading: Terror accused ‘fears’ Gujarat cops - Indian Express
Content:
In a move to win over disgruntled partymen, Uttarakhand Chief Minister B C Khanduri has brought 28 new government boards outside the purview of the Office of Profit Act. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting on Monday evening.

Sources said the disgruntled MLAs had rejected most of the 23 posts brought out of the ambit of the Act last month, saying they were inconsequential and the important institutions still had bureaucrats in the driver's seat. The new list includes only 10 of the posts brought outside the purview of the Act earlier. The earlier list has been cancelled.

However, the decision has come in for criticism from the Congress. Senior Congress leader Suryakant Dhasmana said, "The BJP is now resorting to acts about which it had been levelling allegations against the Congress. We question the motive behind this decision? They had carried out a campaign against the Congress on the same issue. They should now tender a public apology for having misled the people."

The move by Khanduri is being viewed as an exercise to appease his dissidents, many of whom were unhappy at not being appointed to top posts of important public bodies.

Incidentally, the Cabinet decision came on the day Khanduri's bete noir Bhagat Singh Koshyari filed his nomination for the Rajya Sabha polls. A state Government spokesperson said any legal formality to take these positions out of the purview of the Act would be undertaken by the respective departments. Initially, Khanduri had allocated more than 40 posts for senior party leaders.

However, the MLAs felt sidelined after the party high command put a ban on further allocations of such posts.

Heading: Gujarat, Karnataka recipes in BJP’s Chhattisgarh gruel - Indian Express
Content:
Mohammed Shakeel, 24, one of the five accused in the September 13 serial blasts in Delhi, on Tuesday revealed his fear of "bodily harm" from the Gujarat Police.

"Hum tumhari haddi pasli ek kardengey," Shakeel quotes "a threat from the member of the Gujarat Police when the accused were taken to Gujarat" in his 14-page application before Justice Kailash Gambhir.

"The accused even put on record that he had been threatened by a member of the team from Gujarat Police when he was taken to Gujarat," states the application filed by advocates Jawahar Raja and Mayur Suresh for Shakeel, who claims he has "no previous criminal record". The application further criticises the decision of Delhi Metropolitan Magistrate Vinay Singhal to allow the Gujarat Police on October 27 to take Shakeel and four others — Mohammed Saif, Zeeshan Ahmad, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib Nissar — to Gujarat on a transit remand.

"That he was threatened with bodily harm by a member of the same police team which had sought his remand was reason enough to refuse the application for the remand (by the Gujarat Police)," submitted Shakeel's counsel.

"The Magistrate did not appreciate that the accused has already been extensively interrogated by the Gujarat Police while he was in custody of the Special Cell of the Delhi Police."

The counsel pointed out the magistrate's "error" in not appreciating how the accused persons were "coerced to sign several blank papers and write out elaborate stories that he dictated to write".

The Magistrate allowed the remand of the accused merely on the basis of "alleged disclosure statements regarding their active involvement in the Gujarat blasts", the application stated.

Justice Gambhir has sought a response from the Gujarat Police by December 11 on the allegations made by Shakeel, who has spent 39 days in custody since his arrest on September 21.

Seeking a declaration from the High Court that "custody of the petitioner (Shakeel) with either the Gujarat Police or the Delhi Police Special Cell from October 27 is illegal", the accused's counsel justified their argument in court on Tuesday that "maximum period of detention in police custody for any number of offences, howsoever serious, can only be 15 days so long as the offences are not part of entirely different transactions".

This defence submission is directly in conflict with the police version that FIRs registered against the accused in connection with the September 13 blasts were to be distinguished as separate cases involving separate probes.

The five accused were required for investigations into the blast in Ahmedabad on the evening of July 26, which claimed 56 lives and left several injured. The transit remand was given for the case registered with Maninagar police station there. They further submitted that as many as 27 accused had already been arrested in connection with the blast cases.

All five accused have been booked under various provisions of the IPC and the Explosive Substances Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in Delhi.

The Delhi Police had on November 1 apprised Justice Gambhir of the alleged recovery of "incriminating material", including laptops and CDs, from the arrested men. In a written reply to Justice Kailash Gambhir of the Delhi High Court, the police had listed their find as two laptops, a pen drive, video cassettes, 42 CDs used by alleged mastermind Mohammed Atif Ameen, Zeeshan and Shakeel.

Heading: MP minister held for row with officer - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP is banking on a heavy dose of populism apart from its newfound thrust on the "Gujarat formula" to beat anti-incumbency in Chhattisgarh, which goes to the polls in two phases on November 14 and 20.

The party's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani, who campaigned in the tribal belt of Jagdalpur and steel township of Bhilai on Tuesday, asked the electorate to vote the BJP Government back to power "for having delivered in the last five years". "A non-performing government, like the one at the Centre, must be shown the door when you vote in the parliamentary elections some months from now. Chief Minister Raman Singh, on the other hand, has been a performer on all fronts, and hence must be brought back to power," said Advani in Bhilai.

Earlier in the day, at a rally Jagdalpur, Advani reminded the voters how "Raman Singh is now being hailed as Chaur wale baba (one who offers rice)". While the state BJP looks up to Narendra Modi's Gujarat to flaunt its performance in infrastructure sectors like power, it is also discovering Tamil Nadu-kind of populism by offering "rice at Re 1 per kg" to below poverty families in the state. The BJP's counter offer came in response to the Congress's "Rs 2 per kg rice" offer a couple of days ago.

While Narendra Modi shunned populist measures in his bid to seek re-election for a second term, it was the Karnataka BJP that came up with the idea of "right to food" when its chief ministerial candidate B S Yedyurappa offered the poor rice at Rs 2 per kg. The Chhattisgarh BJP is now repackaging the idea as "Re 1 per kg of rice" scheme for BPL families and reaching out to almost half of the two crore voters in the state.

Advani wanted to know who was leading the Congress campaign in the state. "Everyone knows it's Mahendra Singh Dhoni who is leading the Indian cricket team after Anil Kumble. We have, similarly, Raman Singh leading our campaign in the state. But the Congress would like us to believe that a captain would be selected much after the match is over," said Advani.

The BJP organised close to 50 rallies across the state on Tuesday with senior leaders Rajnath Singh, Sushma Swaraj and Advani criss-crossing the state. While BJP spokesperson and in-charge of Chhattisgarh, Ravi Shankar Prasad, is accompanying Advani, Raman Singh and Dilip Singh Judeo are the two main campaigners from the state BJP.

The saffron party has fielded 32 candidates belonging to the Scheduled Tribe category in the state. The 90-member Assembly has 29 seats reserved for STs while the tribals constitute over 40 per cent of the electorate.

Heading: Six gangmen run over by Sarnath Express - Indian Express
Content:
The Madhya Pradesh Police on Tuesday arrested Minister Tukojirao Pawar in Dewas for allegedly threatening and misbehaving with a returning officer following a dispute over the nomination of a candidate.

Pawar had accompanied Fulchand Varma, the BJP candidate from Sonkutch, to Returning Officer Sanjana Jain's office on Saturday to press for the rejection of Congress candidate Sajjan Singh Varma's nomination as forms 'A' and 'B' were submitted a day after the last date of filing nominations. Pawar threw the papers at Jain and tried to intimidate the officials after she insisted that there had been no violation. He had also accused Jain of accepting a bribe for the late submission of Varma's papers.

The administration moved swiftly after the EC's tough stand of removing the District Collector on account of laxity in the matter. The police pre-empted Pawar's surrender by arresting him from his vehicle and bundling him into a police jeep. He has been remanded in judicial custody till November 24 along with Fulchand Varma. The BJP defended Pawar, saying the EC should go into the merits of his complaint rather than the words exchanged in the heat of the moment.

Meanwhile, Revenue Minister Kamal Patel is in the dock following a High Court order directing the CBI to probe the disappearance of a youth, who was last seen in the Minister's house in Harda. The youth's father had filed a habeas corpus petition when his son Durgesh, a college student, went missing early this year. Durgesh had been part of a group that attacked the house of Congress leader Rajendra Patel. The Congress leader had told the police that he fired back in self defence when the group fired at him. He alleged they had come to warn him to withdraw corruption cases he had filed against Patel. The court had issued notices to the Government, the DSP and the Minister. Before the due date of reply, the police filed a case against the minister's son and four others for destroying evidence. The state government had handed over the inquiry to the CID.

Heading: An issue called Salwa Judum - Indian Express
Content:
Six railway gangmen died on the spot when they were run over by the Allahabad-bound Sarnath Express around 11 am on Tuesday morning at Boghfam railway crossing between Maghiyari and Bargarh in Jhansi division of North Central Railways.

The deceased gangmen have been identified as Shiv Naresh, Hinchlal, Sobhalal, Bodhelal, Ram Gareeb and Bhagwandeen. Gangman Ramashre, who escaped unhurt and became the lone eyewitness, is in a state of shock.

He said seven of them were working on the track near the railway crossing where a goods train moved in from Allahabad on one track and the Sarnath Express going towards Allahabad on the other.

The gangmen and the guards on railway crossing duty could not see the Sarnath Express, resulting in the accident. The bodies of the gangmen were mutilated beyond recognition.

Till 1.30 pm no officer from the Jhansi division could reach the spot. However, Mau SDM S K Pathak and Bargarh Station Officer arrived at the spot and took stock of the situation.

Sources said the gangmen mistook the whistle of the Sarnath express for that of the goods train and shifted to the track on which the Sarnath Express was coming in.

North Central Railway chief PRO Rajesh Dutt Bajpai said the technical reason of the incident could only be ascertained after a high-level inquiry is completed. The GM NCR has ordered an inquiry into the incident and an immediate compensation of Rs 15,000 to the families of the deceased.

Heading: All quiet on the Congress front - Indian Express
Content:
The leader of opposition in the Chhattisgarh assembly, Mahendra Karma — more famous in these parts as the frontline leader of the anti-Naxalite Salwa Judum movement — is facing an uphill task in his efforts to score a hat-trick in the assembly polls from this tribal constituency in South Bastar.

The CPI's decision to field its young firebrand leader, Manish Kunjam, to take on the Congress veteran on his home turf has made the contest both tough and interesting. BJP nominee Bhairav Mandavi, also in the fray, is struggling to add a saffron dimension to the electoral fight.

But the Salwa Judum has overshadowed all other issues in this constituency, with an electorate of more than 1.73 lakh. While Karma and Mandavi are protagonists of the anti-Naxalite movement, Kunjam and his party have been opposing the campaign. The CPI claims that the campaign has uprooted people from their homes and resulted in large-scale killings of innocent people, caught in the conflict between Maoist rebels and Salwa Judum activists.

With the first phase of polling in the state round the corner, electioneering is still low key in this constituency. Neither the candidates nor their supporters have been moving into the more remote villages to canvass support in view of the threat from Maoists, who have given a boycott call. By and large, tribal voters remain indifferent towards polls, engaging themselves in routine chores and betting in cockfights. Two BJP leaders have been killed and a number of vehicles have been set ablaze.

Karma has been on the Naxalite hit-list for more than a decade — ever since he launched a 'people's awareness campaign' in 1989 against the Naxalites that morphed into the Salwa Judum. "No one can dispute the fact that Naxalism was a curse not only for Bastar but also for the entire country. People are fed up with violence and bloodshed. Whatever the criticism, I have reached a point of no return and will stick to my struggle against Naxalites," he told The Indian Express.

Interestingly, Karma was first elected to the assembly of undivided Madhya Pradesh in the early 1980s as a candidate of the CPI. Later, he moved to the Congress, became a minister and emerged as one of its top-rung leaders in the region.

Karma's main opponent, CPI candidate Manish Kunjam, president of the Adivasi Mahasabha, has in fact shifted from his home constituency of Konta to Dantewada to take on Karma. During the last few years, Kunjam has made efforts to mobilise the local population in the entire South Bastar region against alleged Salwa Judum atrocities. "Tribals cannot live in cages such as relief camps," he told The Indian Express. Kunjam has also been at the forefront of agitations mounted in the name of farmers whose land was being acquired for industrial development projects.

As the Congress and CPI lock horns, speculation is rife in this region that the rebels could change their strategy of poll boycott in order to ensure the defeat of pro-Salwa Judum leaders in South Bastar.

Movement with a cause?

• The story goes that frustrated by decades of Naxalite violence, a group of tribals convened a meeting at village Kotrapal in Dantewada region in June 2005 and decided to launch a movement to isolate the Maoist rebels. They named the campaign 'Salwa Judum', which in local Gondi dialect means 'peace mission'. These 'activists' were armed, allegedly by the state.

• When anti-Naxalite campaigners organised rallies and public meetings, the Maoist rebels retaliated with violence. Many tribals were caught in the crossfire. According to official figures, more than 1,100 people, were killed during the last three years.

• Because of the growing turmoil, hundreds of locals migrated to neighbouring states and others sought refuge in large numbers in government-run relief camps. It is estimated that more than 56,600 people were accommodated in 23 relief camps in the region.

• The Salwa Judum movement lost momentum this year and many villagers have returned to their homes, especially after Maoists assured them of their safety. Now, electoral rolls show that there are 13,591 voters in the 23 camps — nine in Dantewada and 14 in Bijapur. The majority of inmates are now Salwa Judum activists and Special Police Officers (SPOs) — locals recruited to assist the security forces in anti-Naxalite operations.

Heading: No links with RSS or Indian politics, says Sonal Shah - Indian Express
Content:
In spite of the constitution of the Congress Campaign Committee two months ago, the Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) held its first campaign committee meeting on Tuesday, less than a month before the state goes to polls. While the Congress campaign has remained largely dormant for the last two months, the ruling BJP has slowly but steadily announced its campaign across the state.

State Congress spokesperson Satinder Raghav says that veteran Congress leader Kamala Beniwal chaired the first Congress campaign committee meeting on Tuesday. Though the committee consists of 44 senior leaders from the state, only 30 turned up for the meeting. Most candidates who have secured tickets have begun campaigning in their constituencies sans directives from the campaign committee.

The last Congress rally in the state was held as far back as September 8, when party chief Sonia Gandhi kicked off the party campaign from Deoli in Tonk district. The only leader to have covered the state in recent days seems to have been former chief minister Ashok Ghelot, who toured the state three months ago.

The BJP's Maha Kumbh for party booth workers held on November 7 in Jaipur saw close to three lakh party workers turn up from across the state. "Equally important was the Kumbh's timing, just before announcing the first list of candidates, which ensured a good turnout," claims state BJP vice president Arun Chaturvedi.

It is not incidental, in this context, that the Congress' infighting over ticket distribution is far from over. The first Congress list saw bouts of protests in several districts in the state. The party high command is yet to disclose candidates for the remaining 54 assembly constituencies, most of which are controversial. For the first time, however, the BJP's first list has also managed to irk party workers, with the high command distributing tickets to candidates who jumped ship after being denied a Congress ticket.

Heading: ULFA, NDFB involved in blasts: Assam - Indian Express
Content:
Indian-American Sonal Shah, who has been appointed in US President-elect Barack Obama's transition team, has rubbished reports of her links with Indian right wing organisations like RSS and VHP and has come out with condemnation of "politics of division".

An eminent economist, Shah, who has been appointed as an advisory board member by Obama to assist his team in smooth transition of power, however said she was proud to be associated with NGOs dedicated to humanitarian missions, specifically for their work for quake-relief in Gujarat.

Shah, 40, is part of a panel comprising individuals with significant private and public sector experience who will offer their expertise in their respective fields to Obama's transition team.

"My personal politics has nothing in common with views espoused by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), or any such organisation. I've never been involved in Indian politics, and never intend to do so," Shah said. "I've always condemned any politics of division, ethnic or religious hatred, of violence and intimidation as a political tool."

She described as "internet rumours" and "factually inaccurate" the reports linking her to "Hindu nationalist groups through a variety of tenuous connections".

Shah said she was proud to have helped earthquake victims of Gujarat through NGOs working there. "Regarding relief work in 2001, I'm proud to have helped Gujarat earthquake victims, purely on the basis of humanitarian grounds. I've been privileged to do as a founder of the NGO Indicorps and as the director of Global Development for Google.org," she said.

In the statement issued in Houston, where she has been brought up after moving from Mumbai in 1972, Shah said she did not subscribe to the views of "such Hindu nationalist groups, and never have".

Elated by her selection by President-elect Obama, Sonal is eagerly looking to serve in this time of transition. "As an Indian-American, serving on the Obama-Biden transition team is a unique privilege. A presidential transition is always a time of excitement, and, in some cases, of rumours and unfounded gossip," she said.

Heading: Work begins to plug Kosi breach, may cost Rs 700 cr - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve days after nine simultaneous blasts left about 90 dead and over 300 injured in Assam, the state Government on Tuesday claimed the ULFA and National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB) were both involved in the terror strike.

"Involvement of some active members of National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB) has come to light during the course of investigation by the Special Investigation Team (SIT). The involvement of ULFA has also come to the fore," a press release issued by the Assam Government on Tuesday said. The Government claimed the "main culprits" had been identified and efforts were on to apprehend them. The SIT on its part had arrested as many as eight persons in connection with the serial blasts of October 30.

The Government, however, maintained silence on the possible involvement of jehadi groups including the HuJi, except for saying that "probable involvement of other organisations is also under investigation".

Heading: Security pact with Qatar gives India Gulf toehold - Indian Express
Content:
The Kosi breach-plugging project got underway on Monday, with 72 engineers from the state supervising the plugging of the 1.7-km breach at Kushaha in Sunsari district of Nepal. The river had burst its embankment on August 18 this year, flooding five Bihar districts.

"Vashistha Private Limited of Hyderabad signed a contract with us on November 3 and has started collection of materials at the breach site since Monday," Bihar Water Resources Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav told The Indian Express. The company has been awarded a Rs 72-crore contract for plugging the breach, to be completed by March 31. The minister said the initial cumulative expenses for plugging the breach, repairing three spurs and digging pilot channels would come upto Rs 250 crore. "Long-term project cost including repair of all 60 spurs, strengthening banks on both sides and the ongoing plugging is estimated at around Rs 700 crore," he added.

The state Cabinet has already allocated Rs 197.50 crore for the ongoing repairs. The Centre, which is to bear the entire expenditure, has advanced Rs 40 crore to the state government.

The Water Resources Minister said: "Our best men, right from chief to assistant engineers, have been at work to get the project done as per the design provided the Kosi Breach Closure Advisory Team headed by N Sanyal." He said water flow from the breach can be controlled by December-end, thereby paving way for it to recede into the Ganga at Kursaila at Katihar.

Heading: Fernandes puts JD(U) in spot, tells RS MPs to quit too - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's visit to Oman and Qatar, days before his departure for the G20 meeting in Washington, has given India a strategic toehold in the Gulf — two agreements on defence and security have been signed with Qatar, a country that is home to a US naval base. Short of having a permanent station in Doha, India will be ready to go calling whenever Qatari assets need protection.

With this one move, India is signalling to the region its readiness to play a larger-than-before role as it polices the Indian Ocean and the waters up to the Gulf of Aden. The pact allows India to take care of the defence requirements of Qatar, including intelligence sharing and manpower training.

As if to drive home the point about its growing military prowess, the Indian Navy on Tuesday, in its first-ever action after being deployed in the Gulf of Aden, thwarted an attempt by pirates to capture an Indian merchant vessel in the region.

Given the importance of the Indian Ocean due to its sizeable maritime hydrocarbon traffic and the country's growing stature as an emerging economic power, the deep-reach capability is of strategic significance.

The Indian delegation, comprising three ministers, Deputy Chairman of Planning Commission Montek Singh Ahluwalia and National Security Advisor M K Narayanan, is learnt to have gone all out to get their Gulf counterparts to wake up to the fact that India is a better place — both in terms of security and returns — to invest in than the west. According to a senior delegate, Oman and Qatar were told that the Indian banking system with certain controls is a better bet than the west.

The PM, on his part, announced the $100 million India Oman Joint Investment Fund with equal equity participation on both sides with an upper ceiling of $1.5 billion for infrastructure projects — telecom, health and urban infrastructure. Meanwhile, negotiations are at an advanced stage to spell out the modalities for a $5 billion fund for Qatar to invest in Indian energy and fertiliser projects. "In the next two-three months, we will work out modalities, identify projects in the areas of energy, power, fertiliser," Singh told reporters. He said he also discussed the likelihood of Qatar either investing in fertiliser plants in India or expanding production of fertiliser plants in Qatar with assured buyback in India.

Asked about the gloomy economic scenario back home, Singh said, "We are watching the situation on a day-to-day basis. I have set up a committee under my chairmanship headed by the Finance Secretary. If more is needed to stabilise our economy, it will be done. We are committed to provide all possible support and assistance to Indian industry and trade to ensure that Indian economy is least affected by this international economic crisis."

Singh indicated that the proposed Free Trade Zone between India and the GCC countries could become operational as early as 2009 when Oman would head the GCC. The area where a consensus is yet to be reached is the goods sector.

Asked when would prices of petroleum products be reduced, Singh said there were limitations to subsidies that could be offered and the OMCs were suffering a very heavy burden. "We have to consider the sustainability of the oil companies," he said.

Responding to another query, he said there was no question of being partial to airline companies as also the upper class since the government had to consider the employment angle if these companies closed down. "It is the duty of the government to help the middle class," he said.

Asked if he was satisfied with the efforts of the Maharashtra government to rein in Raj Thackeray and the MNS, he said it would not be proper for him to comment on internal matters when he was outside the country.

Heading: Party rallying to isolate her, Alva quits - Indian Express
Content:
On a day when Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee accepted the resignations of five JD(U) MPs, senior leader George Fernandes put the party leadership in a piquant situation by asking that MPs from Bihar in both Houses of the Parliament should quit.

The JD(U) had rejected the idea of its Rajya Sabha MPs also resigning over the MNS attacks against north Indians in Maharashtra, underlining that they were not directly elected by the people. Fernandes' statement thereby goes against the official line of the party and will jolt the JD(U)'s political strategy to outwit rivals Lalu Prasad and Ram Vilas Paswan. "It would be even better if members from Bihar from all parties in both Houses of Parliament also resign their seats to demonstrate unity of purpose," Fernandes said in a statement underlining that he had resigned and upheld the discipline of the party.

Lalu and Paswan have already termed the resignations of JD(U) MPs a "political gimmick" pointing out that the term of present Lok Sabha is nearing its end while wondering as to why Rajya Sabha MPs are not resigning. The two UPA leaders have also dared the JD(U) to get all its elected representatives in the state and the Centre to resign. Fernandes' statement will now give them an opportunity to get back at Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar.

Asked to react, party spokesman and Rajya Sabha MP Shivanand Tiwary said: "The parliamentary party had decided that only Lok Sabha MPs should resign as they were directly elected by the people. The party will consider George Fernandes' suggestion and see what purpose it will serve."

Already, opinion in the JD(U) is divided over not taking coalition partner BJP into confidence before deciding to get its MPs to resign. The BJP is learnt to have been severely annoyed over the issue.

Heading: Indirect tax collection down 5 pc - Indian Express
Content:
With the party taking a dim view of the allegations made by her and under attack from many quarters, Congress general secretary Margaret Alva resigned from her post on Tuesday.

Her resignation came a day after her meeting with Congress president Sonia Gandhi and A K Antony, chairman of the party's Disciplinary Action Committee (DAC). Later, Antony called on the Congress president to submit his report. Sonia is likely to take a call on Alva's fate shortly, and action against the 66-year-old veteran leader — who is a member of various high-level fora of the party — seems imminent.

Party leaders had lashed out against Alva for her charge that tickets were sold for the Karnataka elections. She had also questioned why relatives of leaders were getting tickets now when her own son Nivedith was denied the same during the Karnataka Assembly polls.

Even Rahul Gandhi, who has often talked of internal democracy in the Congress and who has said he is against relatives of leaders cornering tickets, denied that he was "unhappy" about ticket distribution. "As general secretary of the Youth Congress, I just make some recommendations as far as younger boys are concerned, that's all. I am not unhappy with the ticket distribution," Rahul told reporters.

He evaded a reply on whether Alva had committed breach of discipline.

However, Congress's chief spokesman M Veerappa Moily accused her of serious indiscipline, while Digvijay Singh and Ashok Gehlot also condemned her actions.

The voices of support were few, among them from senior leaders like Yogendra Makwana from Gujarat and R L Jalappa from Alva's state Karnataka. Moily said she would face action for her "gross violation of party discipline. As general secretary, she had access to the Congress president and as a member of the Congress Working Committee and Central Election Committee, she had several fora to raise her grievances at, he told reporters. "All of a sudden she comes out with scandalous allegations against her own colleagues... It is most unfortunate that she should come out in public. I don't know if she did it voluntarily or involuntarily or deliberately. The result is gross violation of discipline. As soon as the report (of the DAC) comes, a decision will be taken," said Moily.

He also questioned Alva's motives, saying: "She is unhappy that her son was denied a ticket. The motivation is clearly there. Is it not motivated? Otherwise she would not have talked of morals. It is not a moral issue."

Asked if Makwana, a former Union minister and the current chairman of the AICC Scheduled Castes cell, who had made similar allegations of sale of tickets, would also face action, Moily said: "He is immune to disciplinary action. Let us deal with Alva first, then we will come to Makwana."

Another former Union minister who backed Alva was Jalappa, who said there was truth to some extent in what she had said. "It is true tickets were sold. Senior leaders also know what had happened. If they are sensitive they can react. If not, it is okay," he said.

However, Alva has got little support from C K Jaffer Sharief, whose grandson was among the "relatives" denied ticket in the Karnataka elections and who Alva referred to in her charges. He said there was no need for her to talk to the media. "It's an internal matter... I was also upset but I went and talked then and there," he said.

While Congress sources said Alva's continuance as AICC general secretary looked "untenable" in the given circumstances, they admitted that going by precedence, she might still hope to escape any harsh action. There are several examples Alva can take heart from:

• Last year, Union minister Jairam Ramesh openly demanded resignation of Culture Minister Ambika Soni over the Sethusamudram affidavit. Senior leader R K Dhawan followed suit, criticising Soni and also demanding Ramesh's resignation. The party chose to ignore them after a general caution against airing grievances in public.

• Human Resource Development Minister Arjun Singh took a jibe at Sonia early this year saying that the decision-making process in the party had fallen in disarray and that evaluation of loyalty was done in a very narrow context. Singh was let off with just a snub.

• Former Karnataka chief minister S M Krishna, who headed the campaign committee of the party in the Assembly election, went on record on the day of the results saying that the Congress had got it all wrong. He was later rewarded with a Rajya Sabha berth.

Heading: NTPC bond issue gets good response - Indian Express
Content:
Indirect tax collections dipped five per cent in October 2008 reflecting the impact of the global financial crisis on Indian industry. Excise and customs, typically collected from businesses fell during the month. Collections fell from Rs 19,646 crore in October 2007 to Rs 18,664 crore last month, according to data released by the Finance Ministry today.

The news comes a day after the government said that exports plunged by 15 percent in the month of October due to falling demand in the Western markets. August also recorded a dismal industrial growth rate of 1.3 per cent.

The realisation from excise decreased by 8.7 per cent to Rs 9,265 crore from Rs 9,353 crore a year ago, while the collection from customs saw a decline of 0.9 per cent to Rs 9,399 crore as compared to Rs 10,293 crore during the same period last year.

However, for April-October, excise duty collection was Rs 66,621 crore in October compared to Rs 57,833 crore a year ago. Meanwhile, total service tax collected in April-October stood at Rs 29,867 crore compared to Rs 23,204 crore during the same period last year.

Heading: Central PSUs told to park surplus funds with state-owned banks - Indian Express
Content:
Companies with strong fundamentals and in evergreen sectors need not get tensed about credit in these turbulent times. Despite the global financial crisis and the domestic liquidity crunch, bond instruments of good companies continue to see a robust demand. National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) today said that it received an overwhelming demand — six times the size of the offer — for its series XXVIII bond issue today.

The power major closed the Rs 500-crore bond issue on the first day itself. "Against an issue size of Rs 500 crore, the investment commitments of over Rs 3,000 crore were received and the company decided to close it on the first day of issue (Monday). The issue generated lot of interest among investors thereby pulling down the yield for 10 year bonds to attractive levels of 11 per cent annualised. As compared to other bonds of similar maturity, the yields are lower by 20-30 basis points," the company said.

Heading: No bids may attract CVC ire, fear PSUs - Indian Express
Content:
Finance Minister P Chidambaram today asked chiefs of public sector undertakings to refrain from calling competitive bids from state-owned banks before parking their surplus funds as deposits. He also said given the economic situation at hand, the PSUs must adhere to the government guidelines that require them to park at least 60 per cent of their surplus as deposits with state-owned banks.

This is the latest non-monetary move by the government to help banks tide over the liquidity squeeze. Central PSUs together have a surplus of about Rs 1,00,000 crore, and according to the guidelines, Rs 60,000 crore must be deposited with state-owned banks. Competitive bids allow PSUs to extract the best possible deposit rate from banks. Even a 1 per cent lower deposit rate would mean that PSUs collectively lose Rs 1,000 crore in interest income.

Hitherto, PSUs, especially cash-surplus oil and telecom companies, called for bids from banks since most state-owned banks did not have a rate card on interest rates. Competition within banks ensured that PSUs put their funds in the bank which offered the highest deposit rate. After the finance minister's straight talk, most PSUs have agreed to his advice. In return, Chidambaram has promised he would prevail upon the state-owned banks to offer them lower lending rates.

ONGC chairman and managing director R S Sharma said his company had Rs 23,000 crore in surplus funds, and almost 85 per cent were invested in state-owned banks. But with the FM now asking companies to refrain from calling for competitive bids from state-owned banks, Sharma said his company would lose about Rs 350-400 crore a year.

The finance ministry had in January this year directed the PSUs to deposit at least 60 per cent of their surplus funds with the state-owned banks.

The meeting comes amid complaints by state-owned banks that public sector undertakings are not following the guideline issued in January on parking of 60 per cent of their surplus funds.

Petroleum Secretary R S Pandey later told reporters, "All petroleum PSUs have more than 60 per cent of their surplus funds parked with PSU banks." GAIL, which has around Rs 4,000 crore of investible surplus, parked the entire money in PSU banks, said its chairman Choubey.

SAIL has about Rs 15,000 crore surplus. Its chief Roongta said the company would follow the government's instruction. BSNL has around Rs 30,000-35,000 crore as surplus, and according to its chairman, 75 per cent of it is deposited with PSU banks.

Heading: RFQs to be off the roads - Indian Express
Content: Senior officials in the Department of Public Enterprises say the FM's suggestion is not in line with the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) guidelines. To earn higher interest rates, CPSEs with surplus cash call for bids from banks for depositing funds. As a result, PSU banks lose out deposits to private sector banks, which bid aggressively by offering higher interest rate for CPSE funds. The CVC can always question the PSUs why they preferred one bank over the other, despite being offered a lower deposit rate. "We had apprised the finance ministry of the issues raised by the chiefs of PSUs after the guidelines were issued in January," a senior official said. There was an estimated loss of 2 percentage points in parking deposits at the 'card rate' of public sector banks, the official said. In a case where all surplus is parked at the card rate, the annual loss to PSUs is estimated to be Rs 1,200 crore.

Heading: Ruckus over cutting pension benefits - Indian Express
Content:
The road sector has got a reprieve, but other infrastructure sectors such as ports, airports and railways will have to live with the new request for qualification (RFQ) guidelines which stipulate that only the top five bidders must be shortlisted for any project being bid out by the state.

The Delhi High Court has upheld the government's decision to restrict the final shortlist in big-ticket infrastructure projects to the top five bidders based on their scores to ensure that only serious players remained in the fray. Companies get points based on several factors including their net worth, experience in executing similar projects etc, and the top five in terms of their scores are to be short-listed for the financial bids.

In the roads sector, 53 projects worth Rs 55,000 crore that are to be bid out this year by the National Highways Authority of India will not be exempt from the controversial 3.5.2 clause in the RFQ. This clause specifies that there should be only five-six bidders in the final shortlist. However, all future projects in the roads sector, will not attract this clause.

The clause had stirred a hornet's nest in the industry with several players crying foul that the projects would be cornered by a select few. Movement on new road projects had come to a screeching halt since March this year with the NHAI and the government sticking to its guns and the industry lobby taking the matter to court.

Road developers claimed the clause favoured large players as more weightage was given to players that had undertaken infrastructure projects in a number of sectors and not just the sector in question.

The Delhi High Court has said that the government is free to experiment with the bidding process. The Planning Commission has held that such a scoring system keeps only serious and financially sound bidders in the fray as infrastructure project costs run into thousands of crores of rupees. In its judgment, the High Court has observed that clauses 3.5.2 and 2.1.18 of RFQ, are legal, valid and constitutional.

The judgment came on the petition filed by the National Highway Builders' Federation, seeking retrospective deletion of the clause to provide level-playing fields to all bidders.

Heading: Sensex plunges below 10,000 again - Indian Express
Content:
Labour representatives in the central board of trustees of Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) today came down heavily on the EPFO for unilaterally trimming the benefits of employees under the 37-year-old pension scheme.

"Currently, we have convinced the government to put the implementation of the notification on hold with immediate effect, and they have agreed to do so," W R Varadarajan, a board member representing CITU, said. But it was not clear wether the government has really held back the notifications.

The meeting, chaired by labour minister Oscal Fernandes,was dominated by labour unions creating a ruckus over the three notifications of the employee pension scheme (EPS) issued by the ministry in the last four months. These notifications reduced the benefits for retiring employees. The most damaging notification, according to them, was the decision to do away with a facility that allowed employees to get a lumpsum by forgoing a part of their monthly pension. Fernandes has now decided to look into the issue. The Indian Express had reported the labour ministry's decision to pare the benefits in a bid to wipe out the Rs 53,000-crore deficit in the EPS on October 8. The notification to disallow commutation of pension was issued in September.

Trade union representatives said there were ways to keep this scheme afloat other than cutting benefits."The rate of contribution can be raised from current 12 per cent to 15 per cent. Accordingly, EPF component can also be raised from 8.33 per cent at present to 10 per cent," AITUC secretary D L Sachdev told The Indian Express. The trade unions also rued the fact that while government was busy bailing out the private sector, by extending sops to private airlines, it had ignored pensioners.

Heading: Learning financial crisis at Harvard - Indian Express
Content:
Reversing most of the 800-point rise of the previous two days, the benchmark fell 696 points on Tuesday, its biggest fall in more than two weeks as fears of a protracted global recession saw investors cut their holdings again. The 30-share BSE Sensex declined by 6.61 per cent to close below 10,000 again at 9,839.69. The broader 50-share NSE Nifty index fell 6.66 per cent to 2,938.65.

Signs of a weakening Chinese economy, poor data from Japan and Britain and a grim corporate outlook reinforced fears on Tuesday of a prolonged recession fostered by the worst financial crisis in 80 years. "Looking at the news flow from the US, it seems that the bulls may not get any major respite on a sustained basis," India Infoline said.

Even domestic factors also influenced the sentiment. For the first time in the last five years, there has been a decline of over 15 per cent in India's exports in dollar terms in October 2008. "Adding to the bearishness, we hear about Indian companies cutting production and closing units. On top of this, the expansion plans and fund mobilisation of corporates have taken a hit. The Sensex has fallen below the 10,000 level thrice in the last one month," said BSE dealer Pawan Dharnidharka. "Investors are rushing to liquidate long positions as soon as the market reverses trend, whatever be the valuations."

In Europe, the key benchmark indices in UK, Germany and France were down by between 1.7 per cent and 2.51 per cent. In Asia, key benchmark indices in China, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, and Taiwan were down by between 2 per cent and five per cent. Russian regulators halted trading on one of the main stock indexes after it fell 6.5 per cent, dragged down by commodity and banking shares.

Reliance Industries, India's most valuable firm, fell 7.4 per cent, after having risen more than 11 per cent over two days, while ICICI Bank ended down 7.8 per cent. The two stocks, which together account for more than 20 per cent of the main index, contributed most to the market fall. Larsen & Toubro dropped 6.4 per cent and Bharat Heavy Electricals fell 9.7 per cent on concerns a slowing economy would result in fewer orders for capital goods firms, traders said.

Meanwhile, the Indian rupee today fell by 73 paise to 48.11/12 against the greenback as the sluggish equity markets weighed heavily on the domestic currency and oil refiners bought dollars to meet their import requirements.

—With agencies

Heading: Govt rejigs fees for spectrum - Indian Express
Content:
Despite amassing an almost $37-billion endowment, Harvard University is warning that the economic slowdown has reached America's richest university.

President Drew Faust said Monday the school was looking at ways to cut spending and would review compensation costs, which account for nearly half of the budget. Harvard was also reviewing its ambitious expansion programme, including plans announced early last year to expand across the Charles River from its Cambridge campus into Allston, she said. The university is considering the steps because the economic slowdown might reduce federal grants and the school's substantial endowment, Faust said. "We need to be prepared to absorb unprecedented endowment losses and plan for a period of greater financial restraint," she said.

Harvard's efforts to address the economic downturn mirror what is happening elsewhere in the country, including other Ivy League schools. Dartmouth College has announced that it would cut spending after its endowment, which also makes up about a third of its budget, lost $220 million. Trustees blamed the loss on poor returns on stocks and bonds because of the Wall Street meltdown.

Last week, Brown University announced a hiring freeze through January, and said it would review its capital budget to determine which projects could be delayed. Cornell University also recently announced a 90-day halt of construction projects and a pause on hiring staff members from outside the university through the end of March. Faust's spokesman declined to say how much Harvard's endowment has lost during the current economic turmoil.

Faust noted in an e-mail to faculty, staff and students that Moody's, the financial research and ratings service, had projected a 30 per cent decline in the value of college and university endowments in general in this fiscal year. If that were applied to Harvard's endowment it would mean a drop of $11 billion, but because Harvard's endowment was so large and so diversified it was more insulated from market volatility.

Faust warned in her e-mail that "we must recognize that Harvard is not invulnerable to the seismic financial shocks in the larger world. Our own economic landscape has been significantly altered."

Heading: Govt to pay interest to banks on unpaid farm debt scheme - Indian Express
Content:
Foreign telecom firms not currently operating in India but looking to enter the world's fastest-growing market as a third-generation (3G) services operator will have to pay more each year for spectrum.

The Telecom Commission, the apex government body for the sector, has decided to increase the annual fee for 2G radio spectrum by 1 percentage point across all bandwidths from January next year.

Such a move could hit firms like Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Essar. The government had earlier said operators winning 3G radio spectrum in a global auction due in January would have to pay 1 per cent of their revenue as the annual fee.

But telecom ministry spokesman Akshay Rout said that would be increased to 3 per cent for "standalone" 3G operators. Existing 2G operators which win 3G spectrum will be charged an annual fee according to their combined bandwidth. Mobile operators in India currently provide only 2G services, and pay annual fee varying between 2 and 4 per cent of their revenue, depending on the spectrum held. The spokesman said a proposal to levy a one-time spectrum enhancement fee on operators holding more than 6.2 Mhz of 2G spectrum also came up for consideration by the telecom commission but no decision was taken.

Heading: Ganguly returns home, waiting for Maradona - Indian Express
Content:
What's so 'special' about Hyderabad that it produces wristy wizards with uncanny consistency? The search for an answer takes one to the narrow uphill lanes of Teachers' Colony, and to the St John's cricket garden — the place where VVS Laxman started his cricketing journey.

Laxman's nursery is the makeover of an 18th century graveyard of an Anglican church. Neatly manicured grass, two turf and cemented tracks and a sophisticated gymnasium add glamour to the decor, but its most prized possession are six matting wickets on one side of the ground — an oddity at big cricketing centres where turf wickets rule the roost.

But, chief coach K John Manoj has had those wickets for close to two decades now, and for good reasons.

"One of the reasons why the Hyderabadis are wristy, other than the obvious inspiration they draw from ML Jaisimha and Mohd Azharuddin," elaborates Manoj, "is because they play a lot of cricket on matting wickets. A batsman doesn't have many options but to use his wrists when the ball comes into his ribcage at good pace. The trick is to use the pace of the ball and find the gaps," he says.

Matter of compulsion

In Hyderabad, matting wickets are also a matter of compulsion more than choice. The paucity of natural wickets — there are just seven grounds with turf pitches — and the sheer amount of school, college and club-level cricket diverts matches onto mat. Also Hyderabad receives rain during June to October, therefore matting wickets are easy to prepare in the run-up to the domestic season that starts late in October.

Clearly Manoj doesn't have many options, but even if he had, he wouldn't have traded mat for turf wickets. For, in order to able to tap the ball with the finesse of a Laxman, he says, one needs to play cricket on mat.

"I won't say it's impossible otherwise, but it's very difficult to develop a wristy player if he hasn't learnt to play on mat," he says.

"Anyone who's grown up playing on mat will be wristy and have good cut and pull shots in his repertoire. It's one of the reasons players down south are generally good with these," he says.

Probably, the only other thing he has taken equal care of are pictures and portraits of his most famous ward in his office. Strikingly, each one has Laxman in whites at the nets. "That's the first lesson he's learnt," says Manoj. "Even now, he makes sure that every time he comes for practice, he will enter the nets only in whites," he says, recalling with a smile Laxman's last visit, a day before the Delhi Test where he eventually scored a double hundred.

But it takes a lot more than a playing surface to become what Laxman is. Manoj remembers, as if it were yesterday, the 11- year-old who came to his academy to learn cricket.

The 3D effect

"Laxman was never afraid, he used to enjoy facing bowlers much older than him. The most important thing about him are the 3 Ds — discipline, dedication and determination," says Manoj, who has led Mohammad Azharuddin during his under-19 days.

"I knew he was special. Once I asked Azhar to open with Laxman. He was surprised, but I insisted and Laxman got a hundred."

These days Manoj is looking for the next Laxman. "My routine is the same, but my coaching techniques have changed. During Laxman's days, I used demonstrate it to him at the nets. Today, I make the wannabe Laxmans sit in a classroom and show them on television screens," he concludes.

Heading: Pujara slams third triple ton in a month, this time against Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
