If these officers don't allow these units to come up, where does the question of these industries creating pollution arise? A businessman's job is to make money. Your business is to stop environment pollution."

Takkar demanded a week's time for the PPCB to frame a policy that could keep a check on the industries that were creating pollution and issue closure notices if they continued violating environment rules.

"Rather than re-writing statutes and norms, these officers should abide by the rule of law. It is not the businessmen who are worrying us. The fact that is haunting us is that the PPCB is not doing its job properly. These businessmen are out to degrade the environment and the PPCB officers have been a silent spectator to it," the Chief Justice said.

Making it clear that the officers held guilty for issuing no-objection certificates to the industries will not go scotfree, Thakur held: "We will make sure that these officers are prosecuted. Unless these people are dealt with properly, such cases will keep happening. We will order a vigilance inquiry against the officers. This is a clear case of bribery. What we are going to do will hit some people very hard."

Takkar requested the court to allow the PPCB to draft a policy that would ensure no such lapses in the future. "Why are you losing sleep? Your chairman should be losing it. He needs time to fill loopholes in its norms," the Chief Justice asked Takkar.

In response, Takkar said there were certain loopholes in every stream that needed to be filled and since it was a technical field, the framing of policy would take a little time.

The PPCB has seven days now to submit the policy in the court.

Heading: Road rage again: man fires in air to threaten another - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Mohali, has developed an Internet-based software solution, e-Sanjeevani, to provide an interface between doctors and patients. Having successfully tested the pilot project, the centre has signed an MoU with six states to share the database of patients through the Common Services Centres (CSC).

"e-Sanjeevani is an upgraded version of our existing telemedicine application, Sanjeevani. It is a result of core resource and development effort in the area of medical informatics, healthcare, telemedicine and e-health. We signed an MoU in September and the software will be used by Bihar, UP, Tamil Nadu, Orissa, West Bengal and Assam at the CSCs, where the database will be stored for the use of doctors," said Dr J S Bhatia, Director, C-DAC Mohali.

C-DAC will conduct a pre-workshop conference on Friday, on the sidelines of the National Conference of Telemedicine Society of India — Telemedicon08, to create national awareness and visibility about its various e-products.

e-Sanjeevani is a web-based software, where a doctor can log on to the site just like an email account — with a specific user ID and password — and access the patients' database and transfer medical records electronically to other consultants. Doctors can chat among themselves to discuss a particular case. Patients, too, can have their specific ID and log on individually to have their medical update and online consultation with doctors.

"e-sanjeevani is user friendly as it has comprehensive electronic medical recorder with unique patient IDs. Online diagnostic test reports are available to the doctors, and expert tele-consultation among leading healthcare institutions and professionals in various specialties is possible," explained the director.

PGI has been running the pilot project of e-sanjeevani in which a database of 500 asthma patients has been fed and can be accessed any time by doctors on the Internet. Under the project, however, the patients do not have an access to their medical record.

Heading: After row in college, student attacked at Sec-11 market - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another case of road rage, a youth allegedly fired in the air for not being given way during a nagar kirtan procession in Saketri village in Mansa Devi Complex.

Gurpartap Singh alias Jockey, said to be in his late 20s, entered into a scuffle with the locals and in the process took out a pistol to threaten them.

Sources said the accused, a resident of Ludhiana, is a relative of former MLA Bachittar Singh from Kharar and owns a farmhouse near Siswan-Baddi road.

No one was reported injured in the scuffle and the villagers overpowered the accused and handed him over to the police. While the pistol was unlicensed, a .6 live cartridge, a baseball bat and a sword were recovered from the car of the accused.

Avtar Singh, the complainant, told the police he was riding his tractor during the nagar kirtan procession when Gurpartap tried to pass by.

"He asked me for way and when I told him to wait for a while, he lost his temper and threatened me of dire consequences. He also claimed he was a relative of a Punjab MLA," said Avtar.

The conversation, Avtar added, was followed with heated arguments after which the accused fired two shots in the air. When Avtar challenged Gurpartap, eyewitnesses said, he pointed the pistol towards him. Before he could fire, a youth who was participating in the procession overpowered Gurpartap.

The police have registered a case of attempt to murder against the accused and arrested him.

Heading: PU students pitch in to curb campus violence - Indian Express
Content:
A student of DAV College, Sector 10, was injured on Wednesday after a brawl with some outsiders at the Sector 11 market. The victim, Gokul Setia, a BA final year student, reportedly entered into an argument with some people in the college and was later attacked in the market.

According to eyewitnesses, the attackers hit Gokul on the chest with sharp-edged weapons and fled the scene.

Sources maintain that though Gokul is a supporter of the Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) and those who attacked him belonged to the Punjab University Students Union (PUSU), the fight, had nothing to do with party rivalry.

There was some confusion over the issue of jurisdiction as the students had approached the Sector-3 plice station while their college is located in Sector 10 of Chandigarh.

The complaint was, however, transferred later to the Sector-11 police station as the fight had occurred in that sector.

The incident has added fuel to the ongoing debate on the lack of security in the colleges.

Aman Godara, a student said, "We have approached the college authorities several times on the issue of security but they seem least interested. We will again take up the matter with them at the earliest."

Heading: ‘Career decisions should not - Indian Express
Content:
In a productive meeting of all students' body on Wednesday at the Panjab University, students joined hands with the authorities to help curb violence on the campus.

The meeting was addressed by Prof Naval Kishore, Dean Students Welfare. It was decided that if a student from any party is found involved in any incident of violence, action will be taken against him or her as per the rules of the university.

As both the students and the authorities put forward their suggestions to make the campus violence-free, student leaders said that the authorities should take independent steps to curb violence and minimise interference by the police. The students also suggested that a ban be impose on parties regularly involved in violence. It was also decided to hold an all-party meeting every month to ensure a peaceful environment on the campus.

Professor Naval Kishore said, "The students have joined hands with us and ensured full support in curbing violence. This step by students is highly appreciated."

Counselling cell

The university will set up a counselling cell to reach out to students to inspire them to avoid participating in violent clashes. The cell will have senior teachers and psychologists as members to help students.

Heading: Lifestyle to blame as diabetes catches them young, say experts - Indian Express
Content:
Rhea, a Class X student is preparing for her board exams but is very confused about what stream to take up in Class XII. Everyone tells her that she is a bright student and should opt for medicine, but she is not keen on science. Her father's dream is that she should become a doctor and he keeps reminding her of that everyday. She later takes up medical and her grades drop down below average and she realises that she made a wrong career choice.

Career decisions are based on a lot of factors, and aptitude is not the only one. Here are some tips you can use before deciding which stream is best suited for you.

APTITUDE IS NOT EVERYTHING
Though aptitude reflects a student's ability but it is combined with a lot of other factors which finally helps decide which stream one should take up. A student might have an aptitude in Mathematics but that does not mean he will do well in that field. Research shows that aptitude alone cannot be the only factor while deciding which stream to take up.

ACCOMMODATORS
There are people who learn from first hand experience and are fit for management. They enjoy carrying out plans and involving themselves in challenging tasks. Such people are meant for action oriented careers like defence, management, banking, politics, public relations among others.

DIVERGERS
Such students are best at viewing a concrete situation from many angles and give different point of views. Their main strength lies in their observation. A wide cultural interest, imaginative skills and sensitivity towards others is needed in fields like advertising, journalism, travel and tourism, art, music nursing, teaching among others.

CONVERGERS
Such students are good at finding practical use for ideas and theories. They have the ability to solve problems and make decisions based on finding solutions. They are more apt for solving technical issues rather than interpersonal problems. They should opt for medicine, engineering, computers, economics, applied sciences among others.

ASSIMILATORS
Such students are excellent at understanding a wide range of information and putting it into a concise and logical form. Such people will find that they are more focused on abstract ideas and concepts than people. Some related careers for you will be law, education, as a writer, in research and development, planning, as consultant, accountancy, information technology among others.

KNOW YOUR INTEREST
Student's interest is a major factor in identifying the ideal career for him. Students who are unhappy in their career later often admit that they chose a field like engineering based on the subjects they were good in school, only to realise later that they had made a wrong career choice. For example, a law student does not have to excel in academics but should have excellent soft skills and should like meeting people as well.

PLAN YOUR CAREER BY CHOICE
NOT BY CHANCE
Career should be planned after careful consideration and evaluation. List the various choices and evaluate them carefully after knowing your interest, personality type, aptitude and so on.

SHARPEN YOUR SOFT SKILLS
Plan your day, improve your study habits, learn time management skills, improve your leadership qualities, work on your analytical skills, take responsibility for your growth. Think big and think ahead.

BRODEN YOUR INFORMATION ON EMERGING NEW CAREER trends
Last but not least, keep yourself updated with the latest career trends. You live in an era where any dream can become a reality. As Walt Disney said, "If you can dream it, you can do it." Discover the infinite career options and understand what suits you the best.

Heading: National conference on telemedicine in city from Nov 14 - Indian Express
Content:
"The adverse effects of a sedentary lifestyle have seeped into the adolescent segment, too, with diabetes among teenagers rising at an alarming rate. Parents should focus on bringing healthy changes in the lives of their children," said Dr S K Jain, senior paediatrician at Fortis Hospital, while speaking at a seminar — Diabetes in Adolescents and Children — held at a local private school on Wednesday.

Talking about the Type I and Type II diabetes, Jain said that till recently, Type II was uncommon in children but of late, there has been a tremendous increase in the number of patients comprising children or teenagers.

"Till a decade ago, not many children suffered from Type II diabetes though Type I was common. With India emerging as one of the nations with the largest number of diabetics, 10 per cent of children suffer from Type II," added Jain.

Jain also gave an insight into the two types of diabetes. "Type I diabetes is an auto-immune process which makes its prevention impossible. Type II diabetes has more to do with the kind of life one leads. This explains why over 52 per cent Type II cases are preventable," said Jain.

Elaborating further on the Type II form, Jain said a child, in such cases, experiences excessive thirst, increased hunger and loss of weight despite eating properly.

From regular exercise to a healthy diet, Jain also briefed students on the treatments for the disease. "Type I can be treated only by insulin. But oral medication, right exercises and a nutritious diet can keep Type-II cases in control and also decrease the onset of the disease by 40 per cent," he added.

Heading: Maruti Suzuki fined for unfair trade practice - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 200 scientists and experts, including those from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) involved in the Chandrayaan-I mission, are expected to participate in the fourth national conference on Telemedicine Society of India — Telemedicon '08 — which is organised by C-DAC, Mohali and the PGIMER. The three-day conference will begin on November 14.

The conference is based on — "Telemedicine-Rural and Remote Reach" and is the first exclusive national conference being organised in India that covers the various facets of healthcare delivery through technology-based system.

"The conference aims to create awareness among the various healthcare providers, doctors and administrators about the ways and benefits of adopting the emerging telemedicine technology as an effective tool for healthcare delivery," said Prof S K Jindal, head of the telemedicine project in PGI.

The PGI already has a linkage with Bhutan through the telemedicine project and the conference will discuss the healthcare requirements in other SAARC countries, Africa and South-East Asia to help provide better insight into the development of telemedicine facility in these countries.

"The advantage of telemedicine in reaching out to the rural population has been well established through the experience of the present network," said J S Bhatia, director of C-DAC Mohali.

An exhibition displaying the latest technology involved in equipment, software and systems, medical informatics and innovative clinical methods for healthcare, will also be conducted during Telemedicon08.

Kalam to inaugurate conference

Former President Dr APJ Abdul Kalam will be in the city, on Friday, to inaugurate the 16th Annual national conference of Association of Medical Biochemists of India at GMCH, Sector 32.

Heading: To repair broken pipeline, locals gherao Jal Sansthan official - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Maruti Suzuki to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for adopting unfair trade practice.

The car manufacturing company is in the dock for issuing a wrong sale certificate to the complainant, who later alleged he was sold an old model despite paying for the latest one.

The forum also directed the Registering and Licensing Authority (RLA) to issue a fresh registration certificate to the complainant free of cost, mentioning the month and year of manufacture of the vehicle as January 2008.

The RLA had earlier listed the date of manufacturing as December 2007.

In January this year, complainant Surinderjeet purchased Maruti SX4 ZXI model from Chittosho Motors in Mohali and paid Rs 7,19,979.

In the insurance certificate, the year of manufacturing was 2008, but when he applied for a permanent number through the RLA, he was given the certificate of the model of December 2007. After the 'mistake' was communicated to the company, he was issued a fresh certificate showing the car as manufactured in 2008.

The RLA, however, refused to change the month of sale on the grounds that the year of manufacturing of the car was December 2007 according to its chassis number print and its original sale certificate form.

In its reply, Chittosho Motors admitted that the car was manufactured in 2007 and the documents were also issued pertaining to the same year, 2008. It was pleaded they could not be held liable for the acts and omissions made by the said sales manager of the car company.

Maruti Suzuki, in its reply, said the contract for the sale of the vehicle was with the Chittosho Motors who settled the terms and conditions.

They also denied issuing any document of sale to the complainant or if they were responsible for issuance of registration certificate.

The forum ruled that the vehicle was manufactured by Maruti, so they know the exact month and year of its manufacture while the entire written reply filed by it does not suggest anything regarding the same.

"It shows the tendency on the part of Maruti to conceal correct information not only from the parties, but the forum as well. Chittosho Motors as well as Maruti have been the most negligent in rendering proper service, due to which the complainant was harassed," said the forum.

Heading: Memory Infinite - Indian Express
Content:
Irked over irregular and contaminated water supply from broken pipeline for the last two months, the junior engineer (JE) of the Lucknow Jal Sansthan, V K Maurya, was barricaded in his office on Wednesday.

Residents from Aliganj, along with Lucknow Municipal Corporation's (LMC) Area Corporator, Shailendra Yadav, stormed into Maurya's office and held him captive. Only after work on the broken pipeline began in the evening, the residents agreed to free the JE.

Yadav said: "For the last two months, we have been complaining about problems like broken water pipeline, supply of dirty drinking water and open manholes in the area. But no action was being taken. Every time a complaint was made, we were told that there was no money for repair work. The civic body had given Rs 10 crore to the Lucknow Jal Sansthan for such work."

Maurya said: "Around 12 pm, residents and LMC Corporator Shailendra Yadav came to my office. Till repair work began in the afternoon, they refused to let me go."

He added, "Being a supervisory officer, my job is to get the work done on the instruction of my seniors. I have asked for the required material and staff. The work began in the evening."

Heading: Neighbouring Nightingale - Indian Express
Content:
Expert shows easy way to retain facts, figures

He writes on the blackboard 64 digits given to him by his audience and then turns around to shut his eyes and rattle the 64-digit number—if there is anything like that!—in the same order, accurate to the last digit. When everybody talks B K Chandrashekhar listens. And can repeat it to the minutest detail. But, when he addressed an audience comprising mostly children at Scholar's Home to announce opening of Memory Lab on the school's premises, everybody sat in rapt attention. He performed some amazing feats and revealed equally amazing facts. "Every function of the brain corresponds with the way computers work. But why are you surprised? Isn't computer a creation of man and his intelligence?" he reasoned, illustrating his assertion with examples of the computer's 'sleep mode' during which files are still being read, or opening too many windows that often causes the machine to 'hang'. He also launched an "animated cosmic energy card" and extolled the special qualities of the colour green.

"The Memory Lab makes learning easy, in fact, fun through the technique of associating words and numbers with colours and images," he said, explaining that though the left side of the brain is quicker to receive, it is the right side that retains and thus needs to be trained for an unfailing memory. "The most normal and intelligent children can be bogged by the clutter of information, but some simple exercises can go a long way to take the pain out of learning and make it fun."

He is an ex-Armyman who almost succumbed to cancer. Amidst sessions of chemo-therapy and despite shaking faith and falling hair, he saw a way out of his misery in Rajayog and Neurobics. "The body has its own mechanism of healing; we simply need to train our minds towards administering ourselves pills from our inbuilt pharmacy," he advises.

The Memory Lab 5-day course can be completed by any child from any school. "The discipline helps kids retain maximum knowledge and recollect it in testing times," he says, stressing association of words and numbers with movies, music and any of the everyday stuff.

Alt, Ctrl, Delete!
Yes, it is possible for us to delete our memory files too! Listen to memory expert B Chandrashekhar: "Working on a computer, you delete certain unnecessary files, but often forget to clear the recycle bin. As a result, the file may pop up and cause trouble. We can get rid of troublesome memories and even addictions by simply proving them wrong. If cigarette is your poison and you feel you must have it to de-stress, fight with stress without smoking. And when you survive the stress, you know you can do fine without cigarette. Similarly, if your agonised imagining somebody is conspiring against you, reason with yourself and get closer to reality to prove that notion wrong. The file will get deleted automatically!"

Heading: Buyer’s Market - Indian Express
Content:
It was the youngest of the 5-member group on a goodwill mission to India—Fariha Akram—who proved to be the redeeming feature with her mellifluous voice.

Even as others failed to impress with their unprepared text on human rights and their relevance in Pakistan, Fariha rendered classical vocal music with élan not expected from an artiste of her age. Hardly 10 years old, she started off with Raag Madhuri, much to the surprised of all.

Considered a tough task, Fariha with her naturally gifted, melodious and resonant voice captured the vibrant emotions, hues and colours of the Hindustani classical raag with ease.

It was followed by a presentation of Raag Bhairavi and some other classical songs. Accompanied by Guru Jahangir Iqbal and her father Mohd Akram on harmonium, Fariha's talent impressed the gathering and explained why Indian television channels were after her.

The unscheduled exhibition of paintings by Rehana Kazmi could not see the light of the day for reasons best known to organisers. Discussion on human rights movements in India and Pakistan started off by Rakesh, general secretary of Indian People Theatre Association (IPTA) Lucknow unit. He described liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation as LPG and wondered when it will trigger the blast.

Guest orator Ali Baba 'Taj' said artistes were more sensitive to human rights and hence it became imperative for them to take up the cause. He clarified that contrary to the popular belief, people from Pakistan were more vocal in taking up human right issues. Jahangir Iqbal, musician from Pakistan felt people had succumbed to the situation. "Majority is living on half truth and it will require a revolution to make human beings realise the necessity to understand the relevance of complete truth," he said.

Programme convener, Roop Rekha Verma of Saajhi Duniya looked forward to more such visits of "sensitive and learned" representatives from Pakistan.

Earlier, the group members visited historical monuments of Lucknow, including Bada Imambada.

Heading: EC removes 7 cops prior to Surasa bypoll - Indian Express
Content:
PICKED UP IN KANPUR: Pandey changed names, he backed Amarnath agitation; ATS alleges role in plot

The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), probing the Malegaon blast case, today detained Mahant Amritanand alias Dayanand Pandey, the head of the Sharda Sarvagya Peeth in Jammu, from his brother's house in Kanpur. The Mahant will be produced in court tomorrow and the ATS will seek a transit remand to take him to Mumbai for questioning.

ATS Joint Commissioner of Police Hemant Karkare told reporters in Mumbai that the Mahant had a role in the blast conspiracy and had attended several meetings in different parts of the country along with other arrested accused.

"Pandey has deep links with some of the arrested accused. He played a major role in the Malegaon blast conspiracy, and attended several meetings at places such as Bhopal, Indore, Deolali and Bhonsala Military School. He used several aliases and we are still verifying certain details. We cannot say for certain at this stage whether he is an ex-serviceman. He was mentioned by several of the arrested accused such as Purohit and Raikar, and we had his photograph and mobile phone numbers," Karkare said.

In Jammu, police questioned chartered accountant V K Kapoor and his son Pawan after the address of a trust the Mahant runs — Kashyapmeru Shankaracharya Amritanand Vedic Vishva Kalyan Trust — turned out to be their office-cum-residence at 248, Sector-1 A, Trikuta Nagar. The Kapoors said the Mahant used ATS picks up Jammu mahant from Kanpur the address to get the trust registered since he did not have a place of his own.

The Mahant, who moved around Jammu under police escort, is known to senior officials. He has been visiting Kashmiri Pandit camps — the Sharda Peeth shrine is in Pakistan Occupied Kashmir and Kashmiri Pandits have been demanding that they be allowed to visit it through the cross-LoC route — and been to the Valley several times. During the Jammu agitation over the Amarnath shrine land transfer, he addressed a press conference along with the Shri Amarnath Sangarsh Samiti convenor Leela Karn Sharma at Geeta Bhawan.

Sharma today said: "Many people, including religious gurus used to visit us, to extend support at that time. We knew nothing about them. He (the Mahant) was a very high profile, religious person. He even expressed concern about my safety, asked me to give him an application. He said he would talk to the Union Home Minister about getting me police protection."

In Lucknow, UP Addl DG (Law and Order) Brij Lal said: "The original identity of the suspect (Mahant) was Sudhakar Dwivedi, a native of Varanasi. The house from where the detention was made is owned by his brother Pushkar Dwivedi who is a lawyer in Kanpur. Maharashtra ATS ACP Manmohan Kulkarni came with a Nashik court order and a team of the UP ATS helped them in the operation."

The ATS landed at Bakarmandi Rawatpur locality in Kalyanpur area of Kanpur and picked up the Mahant around 2.30 pm.

According to Brij Lal, Pandey identified himself as Mahant Amritanand, the peethadheeshwar of Sharda Sarvagya Peeth in Jammu. He told police he had been living at 248, Sector-1 A, Trikuta Nagar in Jammu since 2003.

The Mahant told police he changed his name from Sudhakar Dwivedi to Dayanand Pandey eight years ago when he joined the peeth. His guru, he said, gave him the name Amritanand on completion of deeksha.

In Jammu, charted accountant V K Kapoor told The Indian Express that he came in contact with the Mahant some years ago at the residence of former BJP MLA Rishi Kumar Koushal who founded the Jammu Praja Parishad. The Mahant told Kapoor he wanted to float a charitable trust and sought his services as a chartered accountant.

"I agreed. Since he did not have any premises to open the trust office, he wanted to use my office-cum-residence address for the registration," Kapoor said, adding that the trust was registered in 2003.

He said he use to file the annual returns of the trust with the Income Tax department in Jammu. He is said to have told police that he had been asking the Mahant to change the trust address.

"Barring this, we knew nothing about him. Even I did not know him as Pandey. We only knew his name was Jagadguru Shankaracharya Swami Amritanannad Dev Teerath, Sarvaghyapeethadishwar," Kapoor said.

Ajay Charangoo, convenor of Panun Kashmir, said the Mahant had visited his residence four-five years ago. "He was introduced to me as a religious saint, I was not aware of his antecedents," he said. R L Bhat of Sanjeevi Sharda Kendra, another organisation of Kashmiri Pandits, said he had met the Mahant many times at functions. "He was a high profile person, moving under police escort. He used to visit migrant camps to give religious talks," Bhat said.

Heading: Maya holds election meeting at Hardoi - Indian Express
Content:
With only two days to go for the by-election to the Surasa Assembly seat in Uttar Pradesh, the Election Commission of India (EC) is trying hard to ensure free and fair polls. The EC's efforts, on the other hand, have virtually exposed the "nexus" between politicians and the police force in Hardoi.

So far, the EC has removed seven police officers posted in different police stations of Sursa who have spent around four years in the district. Besides the policemen, it has also removed Tehsildar (Sadar) A K Shukla and Block Development Officer Mahendra Deo Pandey from their posts.

The by-election was necessitated as the seat fell vacant after Bahujan Samaj Party's (BSP) National General Secretary, Naresh Agrawal, who had earlier won the seat as a Samajwadi Party (SP) nominee, resigned and joined the BSP. Now, the BSP has fielded Agrawal's son Sonu from the same constituency.

Prior to the election, the EC's move to trace police officers who have had a long tenure in Hardoi has yielded good results.

The BSP government assumed power last May. Subsequently, the UP Police undertook an exercise to shift policemen who were allegedly loyal to the SP. But it had little impact in Hardoi in the wake of Agrawal's decision to join the BSP.

Among the seven police officers removed, one is Harpalpur Station House Officer (SHO) Krishna Chandra Tewari. "In April, we had removed him from the same post during the by-election to the Bilgram Assembly seat. After the election, he managed get a posting in the same district. Thus, this time we had to remove him again," a source in the office of the Chief Electoral Officer said.

Surasa SHO Rajesh Singh, was another who has been removed by the EC. "He was posted in Hardoi district for over four years," a source in the state election office said.

The third officer to be removed was Kotwali Dehat SHO Rakesh Kumar Gupta, who has also completed four years of his tenure in Hardoi. Ram Narayan Ram, removed from the post of Baghauli SHO, has also been posted in Hardoi for over four years.

Three officers of the sub-inspector rank — Brij Kumar Dwiwedi, Shiv Narayan Rakesh and Shiv Kumar Singh — also have the same story to tell.

Lonar SHO Rati Lal Verma, meanwhile, was put on suspension two days ago by the Hardoi district police chief. This, after Block Pramukh Lalla Singh, also a BSP supporter, organised a "birthday party" for Verma that was allegedly attended by state ministers. This way, Verma had failed to ensure the implementation of the model code of conduct.

"While Section 144 of the CrPC was in effect, the SHO has played the role of a mute spectator," a source in the state election office said.

The Additional Chief Elections Officer, Amri Abhijat, said: "The UP election office is waiting for further instructions from the EC in connection to Block Pramukh Lalla's birthday party."

Heading: Injectable polio vaccine on govt platter soon - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Mayawati criticised the Congress-led UPA government at the Centre for ignoring Uttar Pradesh when it comes to the development of the state.

While addressing an election meeting at Numaish ground in Hardoi, Mayawati appealed to the people to vote for her party's candidate, Nitin Agrawal, in the by-election to the Surasa Assembly seat in Hardoi.

She slammed the Centre for not paying attention to her demands for trifurcation of Uttar Pradesh into Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Western UP.

Mayawati added that despite her request to provide a package of Rs 80 crore for the state's development, the Centre has not done anything in this regard. The chief minister also blamed the Centre for not taking any decision on her government's proposal to include the 15 Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Castes (SC) category.

"The Centre is sitting on another proposal regarding the increase in reservation for SCs," she said.

Attacking both the Congress and the BJP, Mayawati said: "Both the parties have ruled the state in the past and have failed to pay any attention towards the state's development. Their failure to carry out development works has forced people to migrate to other states in search of jobs." She accused both parties of patronising the capitalists. Mayawati also attacked the Samajwadi Party and said the previous government had only promoted hooliganism in the state.

Highlighting the achievements of her government, Mayawati said her government has decided to soon provide two-room houses for the poor. According to her, about 30 lakh people have already been given patta for lands.

Heading: Ambedkar Park row: SC refers petition to ‘different’ bench - Indian Express
Content:
Centre's advisory group gives its nod; recommends first use under public health scheme in 9 high-risk districts

The India Expert Advisory Group (IEAG) on polio eradication has finally given its nod for the use of Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) in the public health programme in India.

Nine high-risk districts of western Uttar Pradesh will be used as a test bed for the vaccine. It will be conducted alongwith with the ongoing oral polio vaccine drive. A few private practitioners have been using the injectable vaccine in India. Around 1.5 to 2 million children in the area are expected to be covered.

"We plan to take it (IPV) up probably by second half of 2009," said Dr RK Agarwal, president, Indian Academy of Paediatricians and a selected member of the IEAG on polio eradication. The next target will be Bihar.

The group met on November 10 and 11 in Delhi, and the decision came after a detailed discussion on the repercussions of IPV. The recommendations will now be placed before the Centre and the state government.

The decision also comes days after Bill Gates, chairman of Microsoft and co-chairman of Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation assured adequate funds for developing and using IPV in India.

The need for use of IPV was felt for long but the government was hesitant as it was not regarded as cost-effective.

Apart from its cost, which is five times more than OPV, trained health workers are required to administer the vaccine.

"The introduction of IPV was long overdue," said Dr Agarwal. "A recent study by the Indian Council of Medical Research has pointed out that there are a large number of non-responders to OPV in Moradabad and it is difficult to control the spread of polio in states like UP without the IPV."

Each and every child administered IPV will be closely monitored. Till date, 503 polio cases have been identified in India. Of these, the maximum — 259 cases — have been reported from Uttar Pradesh. From Bihar, 226 cases have been reported.

Uttar Pradesh also saw 52 children being infected with the virulent wild P1 virus — has highest figure in the country. The state was successful in controlling the spread of P1 virus for around 18 months but the virus recently resurfaced following its transmission from Bihar.

What is IPV
The Inactivated Polio Vaccine is not a "live" vaccine. Unlike the oral polio vaccine, the virus is inactivated and thus immunisation carries no risk of vaccine-associated polio paralysis

How does it work
The IPV needs to be injected and works by producing protective antibodies in the blood thereby preventing the spread of poliovirus to the central nervous system. An enhanced-potency IPV has been licensed in the US and is currently the vaccine of choice there

The doses
The first dose of IPV is given shortly after birth, usually between 1 to 2 months of age, the second dose is given at 4 months. The third dose is ideally given between 6 to 18 months. The fourth — a booster vaccine — is given at 4 to 6 years of age

Heading: Now, Maya to increase state’s share in mid-day meal scheme - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court Bench, hearing the row over change of land-use of Ambedkar Park in Lucknow, on Wednesday referred a petition opposing the Mayawati goverment's decision to build Kanshi Ram Research Institute in the park to a "different bench".

The petition opposing the state government's decision to build the institute in the park will be now placed before the Chief Justice of India, who will mark it to be heard by another bench.

The Bench, headed by Justice Altamas Kabir, which was to decide on the recall of its May 1 order vacating the Allahabad High Court stay, said he will not hear the matter.

This, after Justice Markandeya Katju questioned the opposition to the project by the Gomti Nagar Jan Kalyan Mahasamithi.

He observed, "It is a democratically elected government and can take up construction activities. You can vote them out if you are not happy with it."

Indicating that there was nothing wrong in the UP government's decision as it did not violate any statute or rule, Justice Katju asked the counsel for Mahasamithi, senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, to spell out the rules, guidelines and laws that have been violated by the government.

Just minutes before Justice Kabir referred the matter to the Bench of the CJI, Justice Katju said, "We (judges) are not political. We are neutral."

The Mayawati government had earlier changed the land use of 35 acres of the park area for setting up the institute.

On May 1, the Supreme Court, in an interim direction, had stayed the orders of the Allahabad High Court, which had earlier imposed a blanket ban on the construction or renovation of government buildings in the state.

It had issued notice to the Gomti Nagar Jan Kalyan Mahasamithi and others who had challenged the government's move to carry out construction activities claiming that these were in violation of the city's Master Plan.

The petitioners, besides challenging the government's move to demolish the existing structures, had sought restoration of certain buildings which had been demolished by the government.

By two separate orders on October 12, 2007 and November 6, 2007, the High Court restrained the state government from carrying out renovation, maintenance, construction and demolition activities in any of the government buildings.

Heading: Decks cleared, state may get WB loan soon - Indian Express
Content:
After the UPA government refused to increase its share in the mid-day meal scheme, the Mayawati government has decided to pitch in.

The government, after a cabinet meeting on Monday, decided to increase its share in the scheme by 50 paise, which will cost the state exchequer Rs 200 crore annually.

After large-scale siphoning of the budget allocated for the scheme — worth Rs 1,200 crore per year — and regular complaints from various districts regarding the poor quality of the meal, the government has decided to monitor the scheme with the help of reputed institutes and annual audits by professional chartered accountants.

The monitoring will be done by institutes like Giri Institute of Development Studies, Lucknow and Govind Ballabh Pant Social Research Institute, Allahabad. "Different institutes will be given different districts for monitoring of the scheme," said an official.

Two years ago, the Centre had calculated the cost of one mid-day meal, which stood at Rs 2 for primary schools, with the state government's share being 40 paise.

With inflation hitting an all-time high, the state government had requested the Centre to increase its share.

It was only after the state government's plea hit a dead end, they decided to increase their share by 50 paise and thereby increasing the cost to Rs 2.50 for primary schools. Similar hike has also been planned for the mid-day meal of upper primary schools.

Currently, around 1.85 crore children from 1.10 lakh primary schools and about 42,000 children from 36,000 upper primary schools are benefitting from this scheme.

After a series of surprise inspections, anomalies in the scheme came to the limelight in some schools in different districts.

"During the surprise checks it was found that some of the schools were not regularly providing mid-day meal to their students, whereas others were cooking the mid-day meal in unhygienic conditions," said an officer.

Earlier this year, in order to improve the scheme, the state government introduced a new gradation system. Under the system, the government allots points to schools on the availability and quality of food, resources available with the schools, hygiene in cooking and maintenance of records of beneficiaries.

The school scoring 75 to 100 points will get 'A' grade, while those scoring 60 to 74 will get 'B'. Similarly, those obtaining 50 to 59 will get 'C' grade and those with 35 to 49 points will get 'D'.

Heading: Cong, Gandhi implicating sadhus, say Singhal - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government may soon get a loan of Rs 15,242 crore from the World Bank (WB).

The multilateral financial institution has agreed to drop its demands of imposing fixed tenure on bureaucrats and implementation of tough anti-corruption mechanism in the state as a precondition for the loan.

Differences between the state government and the bank on the two issues have delayed the sanction of the UP Development Policy Loan (UPDPL), which the state government needs to finance its reforms programme.

The bank wanted the state to strengthen its anti-corruption mechanism by making the Vigilance Commission independent — on the lines of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).

The bank had also suggested that the state ensure fixed tenure for bureaucrats at field postings and major government agencies.

UP Chief Secretary Atul Gupta said: "The bank had a different perception of the issues. Recently we made a detailed presentation to put across our views and they accepted our contention. The issue has been settled now."

He said the government cannot ensure fixed tenures for IAS and IPS officers because as officers of the Central service, they also get Delhi posting or get promoted to the Centre.

On such instances, substitutes are required, hence reshuffle of the state bureaucracy becomes the only option.

"Regarding anti-corruption measures, we explained that the vigilance mechanism in the state is different from that of the Centre," he said. "While the Centre has CVC, we have the Lok Ayukta, which is an independent institution and can institute a suo motu inquiry against any bureaucrat or minister without approval of the state government."

Gupta said the negotiations with the bank for the loan had suffered because some senior officials were transferred, including the former principal secretary finance Shekhar Agarwal, who had moved to Delhi on deputation.

The negotiations are now being expedited and the loan is likely to be finalised within the present fiscal year of 2008-09, he added.

In May 2007, the UP government had approached the Centre for the sanction of Structural Adjustment Programme loan (SAP) from the World Bank for tiding over its finances.

A team of the bank had visited Lucknow in July 2007 and instead of the SAP, had suggested the UPDPL, linking it with the reforms programme.

Heading: BJP youth wings protest against Centre, colleges shut - Indian Express
Content:
The international president of Vishwa Hindu Parishad, Ashok Singhal, accused the Congress and UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi of implicating sadhus and Hindu organisations to gain political mileage and divert the attention of the people from its alleged failures at the Centre.

Speaking to mediapersons on Wednesday, he said: "Jihadi terrorism has spread its wings from Gujarat to Assam and from Jaumu to Tamil Nadu. Hundreds of bomb explosions and thousands of innocent deaths bear testimony to it."

Asked about the alleged involvement of Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur in the Malegaon blast, he said: "The Anti-Terrorist Squad has been repeatedly conducting narco analysis test on Sadhvi Pragya for a forceful confession."

Any move to implicate any sadhu in Uttar Pradesh will have dire consequences, he warned the UPA government.

Heading: Fake degree racket busted, 28 arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Several city colleges were shut down on Wednesday to protest against the alleged failures of the Congress-led UPA government to check terror activities across the country.

The protest was called by of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and Bharatiya Janta Yuva Morcha (BJYM). The protestors also demonstrated against the large number of Bangladeshi infiltrators staying across the country. They were also annoyed over allegations that the saffron brigade was involved in terror activities.

The prominent colleges where classes were affected included Dayananad College of Law, DAV College, DBS College, VSSD College, Deen Dayal Inter College and Jai Narain College.

Later in the day, raising anti-Congress slogans, ABVP and BJYM members marched towards Shikshak Park and held a meeting.

Addressing a gathering, ABVP City Secretary Harpreet Singh said: "Bangladeshi infiltrators are involved in terror activities, but the Congress-led UPA government has failed to keep a check on their activities. Names of several Bangladeshis have been included in the voter list, but so far no action has been initiated." He added that more protests will follow if the UPA government remained silent on the issue.

Former District President of BJYM, Shri Krishna Dixit, said: "To hide their failures in containing terror activities in the country, the Congress is targeting saffron brigade members." He added that the name of BJP parliamentarian Yogi Adityanath has been unnecessarily dragged into controversy.

"Prior to the Lok Sabha elections, it is a last minute effort by the Congress to make a dent in BJP's image," he added.

Heading: Indefinite strike by AMC employees continue - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad police detected a racket involving the sale of fake degrees of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan late on Tuesday night.

Twenty-eight people were arrested and thousands of fake degree certificates and Rs 2.27 lakh in cash were recovered from their possession.

Those arrested include Jagat Narayn and Deepak, both clerks in the Sammelan's office, and 26 buyers from Bihar and Jharkhand.

Kydganj station officer Ajay Seth said the police raided a hotel in Rambagh after receiving a complaint from a Jharkhand-based person that some officials of the Sammelan were selling fake degrees in the hotel room.

According to the police, the Shiksha Visharad degree of the Sammelan was earlier equivalent to the BEd degree and a degree-holder was eligible for a teacher's job in government schools.

In 2004, however, the state government derecognised the degree and subsequently, the Sammelan also stopped conferring it.

The Patna High Court, however, in its November 4 order, validated the Shiksha Visharad for jobs in Bihar, leading to a sudden increase in the demand for the degree.

The police said job seekers from Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh had been obtaining the degree for Rs 5,000 from Narayan and Deepak.

Thousands of fake degrees had been sold in UP since the Patna High Court passed its order, sources said.

Jivesh, a resident of Bihar, had paid the amount to obtain the degree but escaped the police net because he was not present during the raid in the hotel.

He said: "I came to know about the degree from my friends in Bihar. I wanted to get it for my wife, who is applying for the job of a government teacher in Hazjipur."

District police chief A M Jain said: "I will recommend imposition of the National Security Act against the accused."

Heading: Rash driving by BSP legislator’s son claims three lives - Indian Express
Content:
The indefinite strike by the employees and

officers of the Allahabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) continued on Wednesday. They were protesting against a sanitary inspector being allegedly assaulted by a ruling party corporator and demanded an FIR against him.

After their talks with the authorities remained inconclusive, the employees had started an indefinite strike on Tuesday.

On Tuesday, Bahujan Samaj Party Corporator Satish Kesarwani had allegedly assaulted sanitary inspector Brijesh Singh after he refused to pay him the commission against work done in his ward. Singh had alleged that Kesarwani had demanded commission from the money allotted for his ward. Kesarwani, however, refuted the allegation and said he had given the sanitary inspector Rs 20,000 for the purpose of some work in his ward, but Singh is yet to return the money.

The incident had irked AMC employees, who gathered at the office of the Municipal Commissioner M L Pandey and demanded an FIR against Kesarwani.

The officers of the AMC also supported the agitation by abstaining from work. On Wednesday, despite efforts from the municipal commissioner and Mayor Jitendra Nath Singh to settle the matter, the employees refused to budge from their stand. The president of Safai Union workers, Pradeep Kumar, said: "The corporation employees have been victims to such incidents from time to time. This time, the employees will not resume duty till the matter was settled in their favour." Pandey said, "We are trying to solve the impasse. We will be able to settle the matter by tomorrow." He, however, refused to comment why the corporation had not lodged an FIR against the corporator.

Heading: Kanpur ODI: Preparations far from over - Indian Express
Content:
Three people died after they were hit by a car driven by BSP legislator Bhagelu Ram's son Pappu, in Sultanpur on Wednesday.

Irate over the incident the villagers set the car on fire and assaulted the legislator's son before the police rescued him.

Circle Officer (CO) Kadipur Gopinath Soni said Pappu has been arrested under Section 304 causing death while driving rashly. The name of the victims were yet to be confirmed, said Soni.

According to the CO, the incident occurred when the victims, a 22-year-old youth was riding on a bicycle carrying his aunt and five-year-old sister, reached Orai village in Akhand Nagar. The Wagon-R hit them driven by Pappu hit them. After the accident, the car then rammed a tree.

The woman and the youth died on the spot while the villagers rushed the girl to the district hospital. She was declared dead on arrival, said Soni. Three family members of the MLA who were in the car managed to escape the mob fury when local police rushed to the spot.

Heading: Death after drinks and drugs: Cops turn scanner on peddlers - Indian Express
Content:
Following media apprehensions that preparations for the One-Day International cricket match between India and England, slated to be held in Green Park Stadium on November 20, will not be completed in time, the Uttar Pradesh Sports Directorate finally woke from it slumber on Wednesday.

Instead of reviewing the preparations at the stadium themselves, the officials asked those involved in the task to submit a progress report in Lucknow.

On November 12, the directorate has issued a directive to the concerned officials to complete the preparations within 3 days and hand over the stadium to Uttar Pradesh Cricket Academy (UPCA) on November 15.

At present, work on the players' pavilion, pavilion ground and media centre is incomplete. Work on providing Internet facility, power connections, green room, doctors' room and pavilion ground is also far from over.

Regional Sports Officer (Kanpur) Bula Ganguly said the work is being undertaken on a war footing and the department will meet the deadline.

Heading: Engineering college set to take root on univ campus - Indian Express
Content:
The death of a Ness Wadia College student at a Khadki apartment has highlighted the increasing drug use in Pune and the dangers involved.

Prima facie it appears that Ankit Arun Sharma (19), son of a Delhi-based businessman, died due to an overdose of drugs during a party with friends at Khadki on Friday night. Police are also probing other angles as the autopsy report points to a head injury as well. The cops are investigating a racket of peddlers who sell drugs at cheap rate to lure outstation students.

Ankit, a student of second year BBA, had failed in the final exams. He sat for the exams again, which concluded on Friday. That night, Sharma and three batchmates went to the home of a friend, Mohit Grover, at Laxmi Narayan Kunj in Khadki. There, they drank and took drugs. After the party, they went to sleep. The next morning, Ankit did not wake up. His friends rushed him to a local hospital where doctors declared him dead.

Khadki police have registered a case of accidental death. Inspector Ashok Shejal, who is investigating the case, said syringes, bottles and cigarettes have been seized from the place and sent for tests.

"The cause of the death has not been ascertained. The viscera of the deceased has been preserved for forensic tests. We are investigating how the youths got the drugs," he said.

Preliminary investigations reveal that Ankit bought brown sugar and other drugs from a peddler in Koregaon Park, where he used to live earlier. Koregaon Park is known to be a hub of drug peddlers.

Mohit told The Indian Express that he knew Ankit, as both were natives of Delhi. "I went to sleep about 12.30 am. Till then, no one had consumed drugs. When I woke up the next morning, Ankit did not respond to our calls. So we took him to a hospital," he said.

Police handed over Ankit's body to his parents on Sunday. Vice-Principal of Ness Wadia College Hemant Deosthali said, "Sharma had failed in the second year of BBA. We came to know about his death from media reports." The Anti-Narcotics cell of Pune police has started a parallel probe.

Website promotes drug dealers
City police have come across a website that displays addresses of drug-peddlers at various places across the country, including Pune. The website assures that drugs would be available at the mentioned spots. "There are many places to secure marijuana. These places are protected by cops who get paid a bribe every month. You may freely tell the cops where you secured it from," the website says. Additional commissioner of police (crime) said proper investigations are on and the website is being probed.

Heading: Milking its market stronghold, Katraj plans multi-flavoured ice-creams - Indian Express
Content:
The University of Pune (UoP) will soon have engineering and pharmacy colleges on its campus. Having accepted the proposal on Wednesday, the UoP will make the exception of starting a college for under-graduate courses on its campus.

Senior senate member Gajanan Ekbote mooted the idea of starting an engineering and a pharmacy college in the UoP campus while presenting his cut motion on the revised budget for UoP for 2008-09.

Replying to the cut motion, Vice-Chancellor Narendra Jadhav said the idea was welcome and a special allocation could be made in the next budget (2009-10).

"There are 170 engineering colleges in the jurisdiction of UoP of which only 14 are government run. There is a vast difference between the fee structures of government-run and private engineering colleges. If UoP starts a college on its campus, economically backward students will have another affordable alternative," he said.

"The university can start such a college in its purview. Moreover for such colleges, permission of central institutes such as AICTE or the Pharmacy Council is not necessary," said Ekbote. "The university has already started MBA and MEd courses on its campus on the same basis and the courses are getting tremendous response," he said. Senate members also applauded the suggestion and demanded that the UoP make allocation for it in the next budget.

The senate meeting also discussed the campus makeover. Presenting his cut motion, Atul Bagul asked the V-C about the recovery of Rs 40 lakh given to Engineers India Limited (EIL) — the company to which contract for constructing 17 new buildings is given.

On Tuesday, he had said that the UoP might revoke the contract with the EIL. But as the UoP had already given Rs 40 lakh to the company, senate members enquired what would happen to the money if the UoP cancelled the contract.

Bagul cited an example from another university where, in a similar case, the management council members who had given the green signal for a project were held responsible. He demanded that the amount should be recovered from the management council members.

In his reply, Jadhav said that of the Rs 40 lakh given to the EIL, Rs 20 lakh are in joint bank account, which is safe. "We will try to recover as much amount as we can from the EIL if the contract gets cancelled," he said.

Dubai calling
Vice-Chancellor Narendra Jadhav on Wednesday informed the senate members that the Ministry of Human Resource Department (MHRD) had in principal accepted UoP's Dubai campus plan. "The MHRD recently informed this to us," he said. It may be recalled that UoP's ambitious Dubai campus plan was to start by this September, but it ran into rough weather owing to lack of permission by some central government authorities.

Heading: ‘Men who planted Malegaon bomb’ were in Pune - Indian Express
Content:
What Amul is to Gujarat, Katraj may soon be to Pune. The brand, already a household name in the city for its milk supply, may soon become more appealing to the palate with its decision to produce multi-flavoured ice-cream.

Katraj Dairy, the popular name for the Pune District Federation of Co-operative Milk Producers', a district level co-operative organisation, will thus become the first milk co-operative in Maharashtra to plan a commercial venture on such a large scale. A plan has been prepared by Katraj Dairy and sent to the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) for its approval.

The co-operative is banking on its being a local company to add to the freshness quotient and make a dent in the highly competitive ice-cream market. Production is likely to start in a year's time and initial production of ice-cream will be up to one tonne. Incidentally, Katraj Dairy will be to celebrating its golden jubilee in March 2010.

The Rs 6-crore plan involves not just production of ice-cream but also the setting up of a bottling plant for packaging flavoured milk, modern technology for checking the quality of milk and filling milk cans, a homogeniser and a paneer press maker, among other things.

"Over the last three years, our business has seen a marked rise. There is a plenty of milk available at our plant and we have started producing by-products from it, which also increases our revenue. We want to step into large-scale ice-cream production and have forwarded a proposal to NDDB a couple of months back. We are hopeful that we will get a green signal very soon. If it happens, it will add a flavour to our golden jubilee celebrations in 2010. None of the milk co-operatives in Maharashtra have tried this on a large scale so far," said chairman of Katraj Dairy, Balasaheb Newale.

At present, Katraj Dairy, which was registered in 1960, sells 1.4 lakh litres of milk daily. It also sells some milk by-products including softy ice cream at its two parlours located at Katraj and Bund Garden. This year, it has also introduced pedha, a milk delicacy, in the market.

Katraj's marketing officer, S S Upasani said, "There is no trouble getting a nod from NDDB, which will also provide technical support to us. Presently, we just prepare ice-cream mix and then convert it into softies It is available in three flavours—mango, vanilla and chocolate—and has a good demand. But if we go into ice-cream production, we have to keep in mind the fierce market competition where we will have to compete with over a 100 existing brands. But as ours will be a local production house, we would be able to deliver fresh products than out-of-the-state brands".

"We have planned to advertise our products on buses and bus-stops. We will also use carrier-vehicles of our distributors for marketing purposes," Upasani added.

Heading: Plagued by theft, traffic system gets insurance - Indian Express
Content:
Sameer Dange and Ramji Kalsangra, who are suspected to have planted the bomb that exploded in Malegaon, had travelled to Pune in August, investigators say. It is not yet clear why they were in the city; both are absconding.

"Intercepts from mobile phone calls have confirmed that Dange and Ramji were in Pune. The purpose of their visit is being probed," said an officer of state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS).

The ATS is looking for the two. They are suspected to have left a motorcycle carrying the bomb at Malegaon on September 29. The explosion killed five persons and injured many others.

The police are probing if they contacted retired Major Ramesh Upadhyay, working president of Abhinav Bharat, and its treasurer Ajay Rahirkar during their Pune visit.

Based on the interrogations of Rahirkar, the ATS has interrogated some persons from Pune for allegedly funding Abhinav Bharat. Inspector Peter Lobo of Pune ATS said Rahirkar has revealed the names during interrogations.

Sources from ATS said many persons associated to the Hindu outfits in Pune had tremendous faith in Lt Col Prasad Purohit, as he had been a serving army officer and donated money to Abhinav Bharat. Funds also came in from Mumbai and others parts where Purohit had spread his network.

Rahirkar transferred funds to various members of Abhinav Bharat.

Heading: NECC-ITF: Shalini Sahoo storms into quarters - Indian Express
Content:
The Area Traffic Control System (ATCS) was taking a bit too long to get implemented. Reason: Technical equipment being installed for the project was being stolen on a regular basis. Harried by the thefts, the executing company, Keltron, hit upon the idea of insuring the Rs 14-crore system for five years.

"So far, we have lost two boxes comprising a Router, installed for the system," said D A Mathai, the company's executive engineer. Each router costs around Rs 25,000. The insurance company has refused to insure equipment less than Rs 1,000.

Pune Municipal Corporation traffic planner Srinivas Bonala, however, said: "Theft of the equipment was not a serious issue. But now, with new boxes being installed for safety of the equipment, even this irritant will disappear."

Admitting that it is difficult to ensure safety of the equipment at places that are less crowded during the night, he said an appeal had been made for public support to ensure that there was no theft.

As many as 70 cameras have been installed at various places in the city to ease traffic flow. But the ATCS, launched two years ago, is non-operational. The PMC decided to shift the service provider for connectivity to TULIP from BSNL as their charges were high compared to the private service provider. "We have set a deadline of January 1 to make the ATCS fully operational. By then, the new control room will also be ready," Bonala said.

The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing — the agency that developed ATCS for the city—- will soon undertake research for wireless connectivity of cameras directly to the control system, said Mathai.

The new control system will help book traffic violators and synchronise traffic signals. The PMC plans to cater to the operational cost by getting the traffic police to share the revenue it would save by this automised system of booking traffic violators.

The PMC will also start the Geographical Positioning System (GPS) on the PMT buses to track the position of the vehicles running on the Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) route. Similarly, all the garbage depot vehicles will be installed with the tracking system to ensure that they operate properly and on time to address the perennial problem of complaints against them.

Heading: Pune International Marathon  on December 7 - Indian Express
Content:
Shalini Sahoo of India continued her fabulous run, knocking out Uzbek wildcard entrant Alexandra Kolesnichenko in straight sets, to enter the quarterfinals at the $25,000 NECC- ITF women's tennis Championships sponsored by the National Egg Coordination committee (NECC) being organised by the Deccan Gymkhana and being played on their courts here.

In the second round match the Delhi player outplayed the 662 ranked Kolesnichenko 6-3,6-2 in a 1hr 15min match to make it to her first ever singles quarterfinal in her career.

Shalini broke the Uzbek junior in the 8th game to wrap the first set at 6-3. In the second set Shalini hit an array of winners and broke Alexandra in the 3rd and 5th games and establish her control over the match.

" I'm thrilled the way I'm playing and frankly didn't expect to go so far", she said. Sahoo was not even sure of participating in this event. "I was thinking of withdrawing from the event as I had reached the doubles final at Muzzafarnagar last Friday and wasn't sure of reaching Pune on time for the singles sign-in, but I took a chance and I'm happy to have taken the decision", Sahoo said. Sahoo was born in Orissa but did most of her training in Delhi.

She joined the Sirifort Tennis Academy at the start of her career but was unhappy with the coaching there. "The coaches there never used to let me play with the senior players and hence I could not improve my game. So, I joined the Saket Sports Academy where I had the opportunity to play with top ranked players like the Bisht brothers and Parul Goswami," Shalini also said that she does not have a coach. "I practice on my own. I do a lot of wall practice and service practice at the academy and that is enough for me", she said. She will face top seed Melanie South who played attacking tennis to put out Ankita Bhambri 6-2,7-5. Jing Jing Lu ended the challenge of other Indian and 292 ranked Isha Lakhani 6-3,7-5 to make it to the last eight. Second ranked 192nd ranked Ye-Ra Lee of Korea also moved into the quarterfinals with a 7-5,6-4 win over Thialnd's Suchanan Viratprasert. Fourth seeded Ksenia Palkina was the only seeded player to go through a harrowing time before overcoming Leonie Mekel of Neatherlands 6-1, 3-6, 6-1.

Serbian qualifier Bojana Jovanosvski, sixth seeded Kai-Chen Chang of Taipei along with her country mate I-Hsuan Hwang also made it to the last eight.

The Indian challenge also ended in the doubles as the teams of Rushmi Chakravarthy and Ankita Bhambri and Parija maloo and Poojashree Venkatesha were ousted in the quarterfinals.

Heading: Born to Dance - Indian Express
Content: The 23rd edition of the Pune International Marathon, conducted by the Pune International Marathon Trust (PIMT) under the aegis of the Athletic federation of India (AFI) will be held on December 7.  PIMT chairman and city MP Suresh Kalmadi stated in a press conference that the event conducted as a race against AIDS will feature long distance runners from 23 countries. The annual event, having caught the imagination of the people will also have over 50000 runners in various age groups for boys and girls offering a total prize money of Rs. 25 lakhs.The special feature of the Pune International Marathon is the 4.5 km 'AIDS Charity Run'.

Heading: Dr Sancheti’s ‘Indus Knee’ gets patent - Indian Express
Content:
Basking in the glory of T S Parthasarathy award at the 20th Spirit of Youth festival of music and dance held by the Music Academy, Madras, the bharatnatyam prodigy says dance takes her to another world

As a four-year-old it was the glittering costumes of ace bharatnatyam dancers cum actors Vyjantimala and Hema Malini that inveigled Shweta Prachande into exploring the various shades of the dance form. Now at 19, with numerous national and international awards and over a hundred shows in India and abroad to her repertoire, what lures Prachande to bharatnatyam is its rhythm and moves. "I enter another world while dancing. A world free from worries awaits me the moment I take my first step to dance. It is like a form of expression to me and the moves and rhythms energise me. I simply love to dance", shares an ecstatic Prachande.

Prachande who was also amongst the Indian delegates for commonwealth day celebrations in Maldives this year feels dance comes naturally to her, "Dance comes like a flow to me. It sweeps over me soothing my senses and refreshes me filling me with energy." Her dance classes started when she was just four and the journey has just begun. After completing her initial training in bharatnatyam she is taking an advanced course in it at Kalakshetra, Chennai from Priyadarsini Govind and Shajilal. The movement of any form of dance either classical or western is enough to create the urge to control the reigns of the rhythm and moves of the dance form. "Apart from bharatnatyam I am also learning ballet. It was after performing abroad I decided I will have to widen my horizons. Bharatnatyam is my first love but I want to explore dance in all its forms now," shares the ardent lover of dance.

With her dancing grace appreciated at the International Classical and Folk Music and Dance Festival in Russia and USA where she bagged the first prize the prodigy has a long way to go.

Prachande who is chosen for the T S Parthasarathy Award for the best dancer will recieve the award on the Sadas Day of 82nd Annual Conference and Concerts to be held on January 1, 2009 in Chennai.

Heading: BVU to bring first corporate varsity to city - Indian Express
Content:
The Sancheti Institute of Orthopaedics has received a patent for their indigenous knee. Known as Indus Knee, it has been designed by founder of the Sancheti Institute Dr K H Sancheti and has so far helped over 1,000 patients who underwent knee replacement surgery for arthritis.

Sancheti is the first orthopaedic surgeon who has designed such a knee and received a patent for it. It is one third the cost of an imported knee and costs around Rs 32,000 - Rs 35,000. An imported knee prosthesis costs nothing less than Rs 80,000 - Rs 90,000.

The surgeon said that he has developed an in-house fully-equipped workshop to design other joints like the hip, shoulder and elbow.

Eighty per cent of the population, suffering from a severe form of arthritis, were unable to afford the high cost of imported knee and could not go for a knee replacement surgery.

Sancheti's design is suited for the Indian population. Apart from being cost effective, it allows more than 130-135 degrees of knee bending. Crippled by arthritis, patients who could not stand or sit for a long time can now sit cross legged on the floor.

Sancheti conducted extensive research before he designed the artificial knee joint that is implanted in the body during the surgery. While 900 patients have benefited at Sancheti Institute, another 100 were assisted at clinics and hospitals in Mumbai, Indore and Hyderabad.

Now, the institute plans to market the product and have shortlised the Biorad company for the task.

Heading: Activists oppose hike in honorarium, dub corporators as ‘Nero’ - Indian Express
Content:
Foundation stone will be laid on the 234 acres acquired near phase I of Hinjewadi IT park on Dec 15

The Bharati Vidyapeeth University (BVU)'s 'Amplify Mindware' — Department of Information Technology and Management (DITM) — is coming up with a first-of-its-kind corporate varsity campus near Hinjewadi, which will have competency centres of Microsoft, SAP and other leading IT companies along with a student centre that will give professional courses in IT.

Joy Basu, chief operations officer of Amplify, on Wednesday said that the institute has already acquired 234 acres of land near Phase I of Hinjewadi Infotech Park and the foundation will be laid on December 15 this year.

"Other than IT companies, the campus will also be host to Queensland University of Technology (QUT), a couple of Israeli research centres, state-of-the-art sports centres that will run courses in sports medicine and biomechanics, palliative health care centre and corporate convention centre with a capacity of 10,000 persons," Basu said.

The first phase of the campus will be ready by December, 2009. An offshoot of this varsity will be set up in Beijing, China. The total investment amounts to $250 million, part of which is funded by BVU and part as debt and equity, he said.

In another venture, Amplify has tied up with Australia-based Queensland University of Technology (QUT) for dual degrees in computer science and technology at undergraduate and postgraduate levels.

"The tie-up will enable BSc students of Amplify to get an engineering degree from QUT within two years or get a masters degree from QUT in just one year, instead of two years," said Basu.

The tie-up will not only save the number of years a student puts in to acquire a foreign degree, but will also bring down the cost by almost 1/6th of what he/she will need to travel to Australia and get the degree, Basu said.

The curriculum of a bachelor's course at BVU and Queensland is compared and only those subjects or credit courses that are not covered by BVU are taught to students to get their dual degree. "Students will get their degree certificates from both BVU Amplify Mindware and QUT," Basu said.

Students and faculty from QUT will be trained in various IT modules by BVU Amplify. "Courses will be specially designed for the students and faculty for various durations," Basu said.

Considering the requirement of 'employable professionals' rather than freshers, Amplify will integrate Microsoft Dynamics and SAP modules in the existing undergraduate curriculum from the coming semester that starts in December.

Around 1,200 students will be able to get hands-on training in MS Dynamics and SAP projects, said Basu.

The BVU is on the verge of launching its academic programmes in digital media within a month. Basu said that BVU Amplify shall release a gadget that will enable students to access live lectures in the NVU campus and ask questions from anywhere in India.

"The gadget will be supported by VSAT network and computer-based training packages," he said.

Heading: Unaided colleges violating CAS rules: UoP senate - Indian Express
Content:
Civic activists in the city have come out in opposition against the Pune Municipal Corporation's (PMC) standing committee's unanimous decision to take Pune corporators' honorarium on par with the corporators in Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC).

The standing committee members on Tuesday gave approval to hike the amount of monthly honorarium by Rs 6,000. When the corporators in Pune get maximum honorarium of Rs 4,400, in Mumbai, it is Rs 10,000. Interestingly, the corporators hurriedly passed this proposal, just when there was another proposal of taking a loan of Rs 76 crore for carrying out development works in the city.

A panel of activists including Vivek Velankar, Jugal Rathi, S C N Jatar, Suryakant Pathak and noted cartoonist Mangesh Tendulkar have appealed the corporators to oppose this proposal, when it comes before the general body for discussion.

In a letter they have said, "The PMC is facing great financial crisis as reflected in its move to cut down the quantum of development works and to take loan from a bank. Hence, corporators' move of hiking the honorarium could only be likened with Nero, who kept on playing the fiddle, when Rome was burning."

"Before the election, corporators had gone to the public requesting them to give a chance to serve them. But it is not proper to hike the honorarium when the PMC is in the doldrums," says their letter.

Activist Vihar Durve said, "Corporators in Pune do not have any right to ask for a hike in honorarium, as there is a drastic difference between the budgets of Mumbai and Pune. There is also a huge gap between the revenue of these two cities. Instead of demanding more money, they should create a pressure group and keep a check on the civic administration for getting quality work done."

Civic activist Vijay Kumbhar said, "Even though I am not against the hike in honorarium of corporators as such, they went for it at a wrong time, just at a time when the PMC is going to take loan from Bank of Maharashtra. But, the corporators have the right to get sufficient amount of honorarium and 3,000-4000 is not enough in the current times.

"These elected members should get satisfactory money, which might also bring down the level of corruption to some extent."

Heading: To drive them to schools, ragpickers union gives goodies to their children - Indian Express
Content:
The senate members of the University of Pune (UoP) on Wednesday came down heavily on the managements of the unaided colleges affiliated to UoP for violating the rules regarding giving promotions to the teachers under the career advancement scheme (CAS).

Atul Bagul raised the issue while presenting his resolution regarding CAS. "Many colleges or their managements try to avoid giving promotions to the teachers under CAS although it is mandatory. The university should take cognisance and issue some guidelines," he said.

It is mandatory for the managements of the colleges to promote the teachers on the basis of their period of service. Senate members alleged that some teachers were not promoted even after 20 years of service.

Sureshchandra Bhosale said the teachers' organisations should take up the issue and adopt legal means, if necessary. Some members, however objected to this.

V-C Narendra Jadhav while replying said he appreciated the strong feelings of the members . "I also came across some complaints by young teachers. They alleged that they were not given proper treatment and denied promotions. The university will definitely look into the matter," he said.

Jadhav however clarified that according to rules the managements of colleges should recommend the names for promotion and that could not be done by the university. "But if the managements do not give proposals in time the university can demand explanation from them," he said.

On the issue of semester system for postgraduate courses, to which senate members had objected, Jadhav said the UoP would conduct a workshop within a month over pros and cons of the system and then decide whether it would continue or not.

V-C on admission issue
Jadhav assured the senate members on Wednesday that the issue of irregularities in the admissions of students of Person of Indian Origin (PIO) will be addressed in transparent way. The senate members had alleged that the V-C was under pressure in this matter. Jadhav, however, refuted the allegations and said, "A fresh charge sheet has been sent to the former director of the International Students Centre, where these irregularities took place and the UoP had received the reply of the director on that, which will be discussed in the management council," he said.

Heading: A bitter-sweet life - Indian Express
Content:
After scoring 96 per cent in accounts, Dutta Lokhande aspires to become a chartered accountant. However, this 17-year-old says he will take up any job to support his family.

Over 180 children, who gathered at Jyoti Savitrichi Lekra, the annual function of Kagad Kach Patra Kashtkari Panchayat (KKPKP), dream the same.
