KKPKP is a union of ragpickers, and during Lekra cash prizes are given to children of ragpickers to encourage its members to send their wards to school. KKPKP had started the school enrollment drive over a decade ago.

Addressing the gathering, Vidya Bal, veteran social activist, said that that unlike in other places, where children of ragpickers feel embarrassed to speak about their parents' job, here they take pride in accepting it. "Among other good things this endeavour have achieved, the best part is that the children have accepted their roots and have decided to build their future on that."

At the function, graduates received Rs 5,000, class XII students received Rs 4,000 and class X students were given Rs 3,000.

Speaking at the function, Baba Adhav, adviser of KKPKP, encouraged the children to work harder to make their parents' dream come true. He also urged the parents to let their wards dream big.

The function, organised at Ganesh Kala Krida Manch, saw 186 students receiving prizes. The Tech Mahindra Foundation, Forbes Marshall and two inviduals contributed to the prizes.

Commissioner of Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation Ashish Sharma was also present on the occasion.

KKPKP promotes education through various schemes:
* A cash prize of Rs 5,000 for 18-year-old unmarried girls who have cleared SSC exams
* Interest-free loan for higher education
* Notebook distribution programme
* Subsidy for extra tuition classes
* Bicycle-and-bus-pass-grant for girls
* A class for children who continue to work at the Uruli Devachi landfill

Heading: The marriage market - Indian Express
Content:
American standup comedian Azhar Usman feels that humour is the sugarcoating on the bitterness in the world

The definition of stand-up comedy extends much beyond the etymological meaning of the word and American standup comedian Azhar Usman understands that very well. Because for him, stand-up comedy is nothing but a sugarcoating on the bitter pill that includes tenacious issues like politics, terrorism and racial discrimination.

Tagged as 'America's funniest Muslim' by CNN, Usman was in the city to host a comedy show named — Fun-filled talk show on Usman's experiences as a Muslim American. At the Azam Campus on Wednesday, in a 45-minute interaction with the audience, Usman shared his experiences as an Muslim American in a humourous yet thought-provoking manner. From Osama to Obama and Chicago to Patna, nothing escaped his comments.

"Comedy for me is both — inborn as well as something that one develops further. Humour to me comes from my mother. I have always been cracking jokes but it became a profession four years ago when I gave up my career as a lawyer to become a stand-up comedian," says Usman.

He further adds, "I am not too political but yes, whatever I speak or put across is truth. I realised that in America where racial discrimination is a serious problem, there are stand-up comedians who use humour to put forth the most complicated challenges in an easy way. According to me, making people laugh is important, no doubt about it, but at the same time what is more important is to make people think and I am here to do that."

A firm believer in the power of comedy he feels, "The current scenario in the world is because of preconceived notions about people. It is politics that demonises people and humour and art that humanises them. I believe that using comedy as the tool we can bring people together and create a better place to live."

Heading: Traditionally  Bound - Indian Express
Content:
With recession engulfing one and all, the marriage scene in India is feeling the heat, as families say no to noveau rich NRI grooms and bank on indigenous dulhas

Blame it on the recession that has crippled the world's economy or Shah Rukh Khan, who has shed his NRI image to play an ordinary man in his next flick — the impact has been tremendous on the Indian marriage scenario. The marriage portals show a shift in choice of young brides and their families, as the age-old favourite doctors and engineers again catch the fancy of the would-be-brides and their parents' big time.

The credit for the shift in choice that is reflecting on the popular matrimonial portals could be rightly given to the dipping sensex. The preference for NRI grooms has shown a considerable decline, paving way for the indigenous heroes.

"Since the recession has hit the market badly, we have registered a 20 per cent decline in demand for NRI grooms. With financial institutions shutting shops and companies declaring bankruptcy, this was inevitable. In India, a lot of importance is attached to marraige, so parents want to take all possible measures to secure a good and stable future for their daughters. Moreover, now stability is more alluring to girls than glamour of being in foreign nations," says Murugavel Janakiraman, CEO, Bharat Matrimony.

"Marrying an NRI may sound very good on the surface but involves a lot of problem which people tend to overlook, while it becomes much easier to settle down in one's own land. And after the recession that has rendered many NRIs jobless, they no longer make the hot favourite of young Indian girls," observes Kajal Karnik, who recently chose a well-settled doctor as her life-partner.

While homemade heroes get to woo the most beautiful, they however choose to be modest while commenting about the latest trend. "I don't think trends affect marriages. On a philosophical note and not going by the dwindling sex ratio in India, there is someone for everyone. I need not worry whether girls want to marry NRIs or Indian professional, I will find my soulmate someday," says city-based software professional B Vikram.

Parents are the most apprehensive of all when it comes to the marriage of their daughters. And the recession has left them in deep thought before they browse the NRI sections in matrimonial ads for their daughters now. "My elder son-in-law is based in the US. Thankfully, the economic recession did not affect his job but the general scenario has forced us to give a second thought while we are looking for a suitable match for our third daughter. We have planned that we won't look for an overseas family."

Who knew the marriage market would be so susceptible to the highs and lows of the stock market?

Heading: Kang plugs for Indo-Pak collaboration in farm research - Indian Express
Content:
For Nafeesuddin and Aneesuddin Dagar, music is the connection to eternity

Preserving one of the most ancient rivulet of music, they are the 20th generation heirs to one of the richest legacies in Indian classical music, the Dagarwani Drupad. Ardently following their illustrious ancestry Nafeesuddin and Aneesuddin Dagar say that music is their way of life.

"Any kind of art can be mastered only if one is passionate and is willing to give his fullest. And for something like music, you have to dedicate your whole life to it," said Nafeesuddin Dagar while addressing a seminar for the students of liberal studies at FLAMES college in Lavale.

After initial training under their father, Ustad Sayeeduddin Dagar and uncles Ustad N Zariruddin Dagar and Ustad N Faiyazuddin Dagar, the duo is currently seeking guidance from their uncle, the renowned Ustad R Fahimuddin Dagar and cousin Faiyaz Dagar. "Music is a never-ending subject and we believe that the learning process must go on," say the two, adding, "Like our ancestors, we too want to devote our life to music and would also propose the same to our coming generations," says Aneesuddin.

With changing tastes, as the influx of western music has hit the current generation, Aneesuddin feels that whatever music one may hear for the moment, the charm of classical music will remain forever. "Fads may come and go but our cultural heritage is very strong and will never die," he says. While Nafeesuddin who feels that the glitz of reality shows on TV is a wrong way to groom young talent, says, "It is very difficult for the children to handle the limelight at such a young age... one failure can break their heart forever. Besides, their actual potential gets lost in the race of commercialisation."

Safeguarding the original form of Dagarwani tradition of Drupad, the contribution of the Dagar family to the perpetuation and enrichment of music has been precious and unique while representing a microcosm of the history of Indian classical music. "We are shouldering a family tradition and it's a big responsibility to maintain the family name. But it's the connection with eternity that gives us strength," says the duo.

Heading: Teachers put their best foot forward at science exhibition - Indian Express
Content:
Presiding over a felicitation function in the honour of a legendary Punjabi singer, Shaukat Ali in the local GGN Khalsa College for Boys, Dr Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU said that Punjabis living on both sides of the border had lot of commonality in their culture and agriculture.

He said that this commonality was our joint heritage that our litterateur, artists and intelligentsia were nurturing through their efforts. Dr Kang said that Punjab Agricultural University was endeavouring to approach the Central government through the government of Punjab for Indo-Pakistan collaboration in farm research.

He said that the agricultural problems faced by farmers of both Punjabs were similar and these could be better managed through collaborative efforts. He invited Shaukat Ali to the forthcoming PAU Kisan Mela wherein lakhs of farmers participate.

Earlier, President of Gujranwala Education Trust and former Pro-Vice-Chancellor of Guru Nanak Dev University, Prof Prithi Pal Singh Kapoor and principal of G.G.N. Khalsa College for Boys, Dr Inderjit Singh welcomed Dr Kang in the function.

Speaking on the occasion, famous folk singer Harbhajan Maan and comedy artist Bhagwant Maan said that Shaukat Ali was a towering figure in Punjabi folk singing in the world. They expressed that it was a rare occasion that four vice-chancellors including Dr. S.S.Johl, former Vice-Chancellor of Punjabi University, Patiala, Dr. S.P.Singh, former Vice-Chancellor, Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar, Prof Prithi Pal Singh Kapoor and Dr. Manjit Singh Kang were sitting in the audience.

Dr Jagtar Singh Dhiman, Additional Director of Communication, presented a set of PAU publications to Shaukat Ali.

Mohsin Abbas, son of Shaukat Ali enthralled the audience with his sufi singing for over four hours. Most of the songs by father-son duo focussed around cooperation, humanity, fraternity and peaceful co-existence.

Sitting among the audience were famous folk singers, Mohmd. Saddique, Harbhajan Maan, Bhagwant Maan, Yudhvir Manak, Angrej Ali, Gora Chak Wala, Ravinder Rangoowal, Balwinder Gill, lyricist Babu Singh Maan, Urdu poet Sardar Panchhi, Punjabi story writer, Gurdit Singh Kang, etc.

Heading: ‘Law is a spider’s web that traps the weak, while the strong escape’ - Indian Express
Content:
The science teachers of government schools put their best foot forward as they reflected their innovative ideas through teaching aids at the District Science Exhibition held here on Wednesday. Interestingly, these aids were made from waste material like empty shoe-boxes (cardboard box), cotton, egg shells, wood and hard board etc.

Out of the 14 exhibits displayed at BCM Arya Model Senior Secondary School, Shastri Nagar, the best declared was 'Ray box' prepared by Kusum Lata, a science mistress of Government Model Senior Secondary School at PAU. Adding to it was her confidence and enthusiasm with which she explained different type of functioning of "parallel rays".

Made of a mere shoe-box and a few convex and concave lenses and mirrors, Kusum depicted very clearly as to how parallel rays fall on a rough surface, and how they move on a concave mirror. Not only this, she also explained to the children of senior classes and other teachers about "laws of reflection" and how false image was created, binocular vision and total internal reflection.

Her explanation about "Myopia defect among children" and how it was removed with the help of concave lens in children and with convex lens in the elders was par excellence. Last but not least was her "Periscope' prepared by a thermocol glass which depicted how one viewed enemies in sub-marine.

The presentation about 'Ill effects of cell phone' by Kulwant Singh from Government High School, Ghulal, fascinated everyone. He explained how the radiations of cell phone affected our brain. He said, "Continuous radiations of cell phone result in boiling of an egg. So one can imagine as how much it affects our brain."

The model about the working of a generator by Kamaljeet Kaur, a science teacher of Government School, Nijampur, and Avtar Kaur's model "How respiratory system gets affected with smoke" were also eye-catching. Made with a very low cost, these aids were the working models. Many models of mathematics, which were made merely by spending Rs 50 to 100, proved that government school teachers were quite versatile.

Heading: City schools celebrate gurpurb with fervour - Indian Express
Content:
A two-day national seminar on "Legal Regulation of Election of India" was organised by the Department of Law, Punjabi University, at the Senate Hall on Tuesday.

Justice R S Mongia, chairman of the Punjab State Human Rights Commission said that a criterion should be designed for the electorate by which they are vested with the power to remove their elected candidates anytime, if they prove to be incompetent.

Mongia advocated the cause of fixing minimum educational qualifications and a sustained clean track record as a measure to contest the elections.

Presiding over the seminar, Punjabi University Vice-Chancellor (VC) Jaspal Singh said the use of muscle and money power has to be marginalised, if not completely eliminated, to ensure fair andfree elections.

"The increased participation of anti-social elements and those with criminal backgrounds cast doubts on the adequacy of our laws," said the V-C. He added that while a ceiling has been prescribed, yet the candidates take advantage of the "lacunae in law to pump unaccounted money into the electoral process".

"The efficacy of anti-defection laws is being tested, as politicians find ample ways to circumvent."

Ranbir Singh, V-C of National Law University, Delhi, said that the Election Commission needs to play a proactive role in defeating the evil designs of those bent upon "criminalisation of politics". M S Saini, Dean, Academic affairs, said: "Law is a spider's web that traps the weak while the strong escape."

Heading: Dr Pachauri reminds industrialists of their duty toward environment - Indian Express
Content:
The tiny tots of Kiddies Paradise School celebrated Guru Nanak Dev's birthday with enthusiasm. First of all, the children prayed and offered prayers to Sri Guru Granth Sahib. The little ones also recited shabads "Sat Guru Nanak pargataya" and "Ooncha dar Babe Nanak da" etc.

The whole atmosphere was devotional and blissful. Five children came dressed up as "Panj payaras". They also recited "300 saal guru de naal". Randhir Singh, the school director, congratulated the children on gurpurb and briefed them about Guru Nanak Dev. Guru ka Langar was also served on this occasion.

Love Dale School organised Parbhat Pheri to mark the Gurpurb.

Amrit Indo-Canadian Academy also celebrated Guruta Gaddi Diwas and birthday of Guru Nanak Dev with great zeal and enthusiasm.

The programme started with bhog of Sehaj Path. The vocal rendition of shabads from Guru Granth Sahib was given by school choir. The newly-constructed school hall reverberated with these recitations. School captain Jasman Singh (Class X) told people about the teachings and preachings of Guru Granth Sahib. Kulwaran Singh (Class X) highlighted the philosophy and life of Guru Nanak Dev. Kavishri by the students, also advocated the simplicity and benolevance of Guru Nanak Dev. Jasmeet Kaur enlightened the audience on the historical background of 300 years of Guruta Gaddi.

The principal, Jaskiran Kaur said that Guru Granth Sahib was a secular granth and taught us all to rise above petty differences and weaknesses.

Heading: CAPE-India holds quiz contest - Indian Express
Content:
Dr R.K. Pachauri, Director General, Energy and Resources Institute and Chairman, Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Changes (IPCC), delivered a lecture on the topic "Sustainable management of national resources: Role of corporate sector" at Hotel Park Plaza here on Tuesday. IPCC, t may be mentioned, has shared "2007 Nobel peace prize" under the stewardship of Dr R.K. Pachauri.

Dr Pachauri, while addressing the LMA members, said, "Eleven of the last 12 years were the warmest years of all times. Glacier cumulative balance has been declining. The average sea level change in 1961 was 1.81mm/year which has increased to 3.1 mm/year. Twenty five per cent of the African continent is under high-water deficit,"

He urged the corporate to develop low carbon product, adhere to clean environmental commitments, bring about changes in lifestyle etc. Dr Pauchauri praised the efforts of Israel, a water-deficient country, regarding its water management efforts even as he advocated carbon credits for cleaner environments, better energy efficient buildings and underground air tunnels for cleaner environment and conserving energy

Anil Kumar, President, LMA said it was a privilege for the association to interact with Dr Pachauri, who is a person of an international stature. "I am sure that the members would have learnt a lot about management of resources and role of corporate world in maintaining them," he said.

Earlier, V.K. Goyal introduced the speaker. Dr. K.N.S. Kang, General Secretary, LMA, while welcoming the speaker said that environment and ecology were rapidly degrading. Climatic change and global warming were the issues confronting the mankind.

Because of global warming, the Gangotri glacier would become extinct by 2030. The resources are required to be managed properly for maintaining the pace of unprecedented developments achieved in the world in recent decades. Rakesh Bharti Mittal spoke about the contributions of Dr Pachauri.

Heading: Few takers for Red Ribbon Express in city - Indian Express
Content:
Cape-India, a non-government organisation, on Wednesday organised a quiz contest at BCM Model Senior Secondary School. The quiz was organised to make students aware about "Care of animals and protection of Environment-India" (CAPE-India).

Teachers and students from different schools participated in the quiz. Various posters and banners related to wildlife were also displayed.

The questions related to wildlife and global warming were fielded by the students. Those giving correct answers were awarded with CAPE-India momentoes and certificates.

The key- note speaker, Dr Sandeep K. Jain said that Asiatic lions had become extinct from whole of Asia except India and that too in Gir Forests (Gujarat). Their number has been limited to 350 and population of Royal Bengal Tigers had come down to 1411 in the Census of 2008, despite the efforts taken by government and conservation agencies.

They are dying due to illegal poaching for their skins, bones and body parts. Similarly, elephants are killed for their tusks.

Students were also told about peacocks, deers and banned animals in circuses/street shows etc and asked to protect the wildlife and its habitat.

Heading: Govt asks PAU to assign probe to outside agency - Indian Express
Content:
Various members of the Red Ribbon Express train team, including its volunteers and brand ambassador in the city, on Wednesday rued the "lukewarm response" they received from both district authorities as well as the public in Ludhiana. This is despite the fact that Ludhiana has the highest number of AIDS patients in the state.

At present in the city, on its three-day halt, the train chugged in at the city railway station yesterday and was received by Health Minister Lakshmi Kanta Chawla.

On its second day in the city today, the train, which features an exhibition on AIDS/HIV awareness, found very few visitors.

Dr Avinash Sharma, a Canada-based psychotherapist, who has been roped in as the brand ambassador in the city, said he was disappointed with the kind of response the train has received so far.

"There has been no fruitful participation from the district administration. Even the function at the reception of the train which was held yesterday was overshadowed by political colour while it was supposed to be a public event," said Sharma.

Another official said, "Though the deputy commissioner is the one who invited everyone, he has not paid any visit so far."

While the number of visitors today increased to 2,618 as compared to yesterday's 938, organisers said it mostly comprised schoolchildren. "Most of the crowd today consisted of students from city schools and colleges, invited on the request of the Health department," said one of the team members.

Notably, Ludhiana has the highest number of AIDS cases in the state and features among the cities which have been listed as 'A' category cities, indicating high rate of prevalence.

Complaining about the lukewarm response to the Red Ribbon Express train, some people also raised objections about choosing an odd location - railway station goods shed - apart from failing to generate public curiosity by hand-outs, bill boards or posters.The train has visited various cities of the country as part of its one year tour since December 1 last year. They said that in other cities, the train has been placed at the platforms where it can invite more crowds but the organisers chose Railway Station Goods Shed here, located in the corner of the station.

"It is only the students from various schools and medical institutes who have been visiting the train. While it is important that students become aware of various aspects related to AIDS, it is also important to create awareness among the segment of population which is unaware.

But it seems no public curiusity was generated about the train ahead of its halt in the city, since the general public is still not aware of this," complained a member of the staff working for the Red Ribbon Express.

A volunteer who was guiding students into the train said," I had come along with a group of students from my college where I teach but found nobody to guide the visitors at the entrance. So we volunteered to work here. I feel that the visitors' inhibitions need to be taken care of with proper guidance at the exhibitions."

The one-year long journey of the train, which will culminate on December 1 in Delhi, aims to create awareness among the public about the various aspects of AIDS.

Heading: Dengue shows no sign of slowdown: 62 fresh cases registered - Indian Express
Content:
In an unprecedented move that puts the autonomy of an institution at stake, the Punjab Government has ordered Punjab Agricultural University to hand over the inquiry regarding charges of sexual harassment against Director Students Welfare Dr Dulcha Singh Brar "to an outside agency".

All this is allegedly being done at the behest of the accused without considering the fact that the university has a standing committee which is inquiring into the case.

The university received a communication affecting the same a couple of days ago.

PAU Joint Secretary Gurwarayam Singh said that as per November 10 order, the office of Finance Secretary Development has asked Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang to hand over the inquiry to some independent agency. When asked about the reason for this move, the joint secretary said, "The request had been made by accused Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, who in his application, written to the Punjab Government, has claimed that he does not expect to get justice from the committee."

Notable here is that a woman employee of the university had levelled charges of sexual harassment against Brar following which the standing committee of the university headed by Dean College of Home Science Dr Neelam Grewal had been asked by the V-C to initiate an inquiry into the matter. This committee has already recorded the statement of the complainant and her witnesses while Dr Brar has refused to record any statement till the time the university furnishes him a copy of the complaint. Dr Brar has presented himself before the committee thrice and every time the meeting has ended in a deadlock.

While the vice-chancellor could not be contacted for his comments, former V-C Dr Kirpal Singh Aulakh, while condemning the move of the government said, "The Supreme Court guidelines on how to tackle issues of sexual harassment at any work place are very clear. The state government should stay away and let the PAU handle the matter. During my regime too, I was once asked by the state government to institute a said committee which I refused to do so. I wrote back to the state government clearly stating that the university has its own laws through which we can handle our issue."

Former research director of the university, Dr S S Johl, said: "While Dr Brar has the right to express his concerns over the committee but thePAU can handle the matter on its own. The state government has this weird system wherein when it comes to power it exercises it but when it comes to responsibilities it shirks. Take the example of PAU pensioners; they are not the responsibility of the state government.

Similarly when it wanted the land at Bathinda, the government simply ordered PAU to part with it and now a similar treatment has been meted out in this case. The manner in which the government is operating as far as the PAU is concerned, is simply killing the institution."

Heading: 16 buildings on Mall Road get notices for violating building bylaws - Indian Express
Content:
The Health department claims that there has been a substantial dip in the number of fresh cases of dengue and the disease would decrease in the coming days.

However, the information received from various hospitals has put the fresh number of cases at 62. As many as 49 cases of the disease were reported at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital today. The Christian Medical College and Hospital registered six cases while Mohan Dai Oswal Cancer Hospital admitted seven cases.

Meanwhile, the Health department today confirmed 27 more cases of dengue apart from putting another nine 'in the suspected category'.

"There is a substantial decrease in the fresh cases. We consider the period from November 15 to February 15 as a 'healthy season' and the number of various kinds of diseases visible in this duration is very low. It is because the period sees a low level of temperature making it impossible for the mosquito larvae to evolve," said Dr JP Mangla, district epidemiologist.

Heading: Rattled by construction at doorstep, rickety building collapses on family - Indian Express
Content:
Following the instructions of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, the Town Planning department of the Municipal Corporation has issued notices to 16 building owners on the Mall Road for violating building bylaws.

The owners have been given a six-day period to start rectifying the flaws or face action for the same.

With three days having passed, no building owner has come forward with a plan to make alteration in their buildings.

Confirming the same, Hemant Batra, Municipal Town Planner (MTP) said, "The notices have been issued following a public interest litigation (PIL) filed in the High Court. The violations include lack of parking space in the under-construction buildings or violation of norms of floor area ratio (FAR) including others."

There are a number of buildings on the Mall Road that have parking problem apart from other violations.

Batra said, "For the time being, notices have been sent only to the under- construction buildings and they will have to make necessary changes in their building plans else we would be forced to demolish their buildings."

Heading: A pit 10 feet deep: prime suspect in cave-in, main obstacle before firemen - Indian Express
Content:
Adjacent digging likely cause: civic authorities

A six-storey building in a congested street near Crawford Market, shaky to begin with and made shakier by ongoing construction and digging in the neighbourhood, collapsed early on Wednesday morning, crushing to death six members of a family.

The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation will investigate if an adjacent 10-foot pit and vibrations from underground digging in congested Nagdevi Street had affected Sayyed House, 71 years old and matchbox-like.

It collapsed at 5 am, killing Dr Imran Sayyed (38) his wife Dr Rihana (28) and their two children, Omar (12), Mariam (6), as well as Imran's brother Salman (25) and a relative, Fahad Sheikh (20). The doctor was staying with his family on the fourth floor in the rear of the building, while the two cousins were on the fifth floor. The doctor's family was found under the rubble on the first floor.

The house is now being emptied and the rescued residents will be given accommodation soon.

Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak agreed that the damage could have been caused by the piling work. "It could be that vibrations while digging rattled the weak portion of the building and resulted in the collapse. We will investigate."

This construction, by Rubberwala Developers, and was being carried out right next to Sayyed House. It had allegedly been a bone of contention between the developer and the residents over the last few years. Relatives of the dead said they were being forced to be part of the redevelopment project but wanted nothing to do with it.

"We had told them that if we want to redevelop the building we will do it on our own. Those in the building were our family and relatives; why would we join hands with others?" said Sufiana Sayyed, younger brother of Dr Imran.

He alleged that construction often caused the building to vibrate. He said the family had complained to mhada many times.

MHADA officials claimed that following the complaints, an architect was sent in August to inspect the building. "The residents did not allow the architect to carry out a survey saying they were in a dispute with the developer who is building on the next plot and that talks of redevelopment were on," said a MHADA official.

MHADA officials said they will soon survey the area. "Most of the buildings are more than 80 years old and vulnerable. We will ask them to go for redevelopment," said deputy chief engineer of MHADA, Balbir Sehgal.

Tabrez Sheikh, director of Rubberwala Developers, said that it was "coincidental" that Sayyed House collapsed. "The top two floors were illegal and had weakened the structure. Our construction work did not affect the structure in any way."

Pydhonie police have registered a case of accidental death, inspector Samsher Pathan said.

Heading: Doctor parents wanted doctor children, never - Indian Express
Content:
The 10-foot pit that is believed to have caused the collapse also hindred rescue work. That combined with a three-foot pile of debris to challenge the Mumbai Fire Brigade, who also struggled to negotiate the narrow bylanes in congested Crawford Market.

"There was a lot of debris and almost no access inside. Firemen eventually entered through the front entrance — the rear had collapsed — and through the windows," said deputy chief fire officer P D Kargupikar.

"We had a tough time rescuing the people who were trapped inside the debris as the pit was too deep to negotiate. The debris collected too was way too much. We could not carry out the rescue operations as swiftly as we wanted to," he said.

The priority was to rescue as many as people alive as possible. "It was unfortunate that all six buried under the debris died. All four of the doctors' family four were on the first floor; the two relatives were also under the rubble," he said.

The structure was 71 years old the walls and the slab was thick, at least eight inches instead of the four that one would have today. "All the six suffered heavily under the weight of the debris before they died," said a fireman.

The firemen also struggled to clear the debris. Five floors had caved in from the rear, while many overhanging walls and loose rubble added to the problem. This was cleared by manual hammering instead of a mechanical crane as it could have damaged the remaining standing structure. Around 30-35 inches rubble remains at the spot.

The fire brigade reached the spot minutes after getting the call. But because of the pit, the actual work started late.

"As soon as we heard the noise we called up the fire brigade and they immediately reached the spot. However, by then six members of my family were already trapped in the rubble, which was fast collecting in the construction site pit," said Sakhi Hasan, a resident of a neighboring building. Forty-seven fire officials, 3 ambulances and 8 fire engines were used for the rescue operation.

Heading: Bank staff transfers Rs 2 crore to bogus accounts - Indian Express
Content:
Young Omar and Mariam had just returned from their Nani's home in Lonavala, where they had spent the Diwali vacation. With schools reopening on Monday, brother and sister reluctantly joined their parents on the way home on Sunday evening.

It was to be their last vacation. Omar and Mariam died in the collapse along with their parents, Dr Imran Sayyed (38) and Dr Rihana.

Dr Rihana was so serious about their studies that she had given up full-time practice. "The kids wouldn't miss a day of school. They had returned on Sunday so that they could attend school on Monday," said one of Rihana's relative.

The children went to St Xavier's School. Omar was in fifth standard and Mariam in fourth. Their parents wanted to make them doctors like themselves.

Dr Imran was a visiting orthopaedic in Bacha's Memorial Bellevue Nursing Home,

Marine Lines, and had a private clinic in Ambedkar Nagar, Colaba. Corporator Vinod Shekhar of Colaba said that Dr Imran would often treat slum dwellers at low fees. Dr Rihana assisted him in the evening at his clinic and was also among the visiting faculty at J J Hospital, relatives said.

Younger brother Salman Sayyed (25) owned a mobile shop near his house and his cousin Fahad Sheikh (20) had only recently come from Lucknow. Both died.

The entire Sayyed family lived in the building, but last night only a few were actually staying there. "My mother and sister are currently in Lucknow preparing for the latter's wedding. Our other brothers have moved to Saudi Arabia," said brother Sufiana Sayyed.

Sayeed Rumana Fauzaan (30), a cousin of the family, said they heard the noise and escaped by the front entrance. "We were sleeping; my brother Imran's cries woke me up. As soon as I realised what had happened, I picked up my kids and rushed out. But a lot of damage had already been done," he said.

After a gruelling eight hours, the six bodies were brought out from the heaps of rubble, the last one being that of little Mariam.

Heading: India’s biggest photo journalism awards to be out tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
The Cuffe Parade police have arrested a woman bank employee charging her with transferring Rs 2 crore from the bank funds to two bogus accounts in a Kolkata bank through electronic transaction.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone I) Vishwas Nangre-Patil said that last week police had arrested Abdul Wahid, a former bank employee in this connection. Thirty-five-year-old Malathi Gada Kanchan was arrested on Wednesday.

Investigation by the Cuffe Parade police revealed that Kanchan executed the heist and her boyfriend Shashikumar Shetty planned it. The unmarried couple, that was living together, allegedly wanted the money to buy a flat.

Kanchan, who was employed as a junior officer in the bank's Nariman Point headoffice, was in charge of transferring money to its other branches. "Kanchan is cyber savvy and very adept at IT transactions. Her work profile required her to transfer huge amounts up to Rs 1 crore based on the demand cited by other branches via Real Transaction Gross System.

On October 24, Kanchan received two 'one crore requisition' demands from the bank's Borivali branch via fax. She immediately transferred the total sum of Rs 2 crore to two bank accounts in Kolkata as per the demand. However, the requisition slips had been faxed by Shetty and the accounts in Kolkata had also been fraudulently created by the duo," said Assistant Police Inspector Tukaram Mane, who is investigating the case.

The Nariman Point branch realised that something was amiss after finding that the Borivali branch had not sent any such requisition slip. The bank's General Manager Hari Babu filed a complaint with the Cuffe Parade police station.

The transaction was traced to Kanchan and to add to the police's suspicion, a couple of days after the transaction had been made, Kanchan failed to show up for work. They arrested Wahid, who was Kanchan's former colleague and allegedly gave an insight on the heist.

"Rs 1 crore each was transferred to two accounts. The money then went to three other accounts. All these accounts were bogus and had been opened a few months back," said Inspector P N Jagtap.

The Cuffe Parade police immediately went to Kolkata and personally notified the bank authorities there about the transaction. The bogus accounts were subsequently frozen.

Heading: Petition against Raj Thackeray bail: High Court asks him to reply - Indian Express
Content:
IPPA Awards: 8,801 entries, 226 photographers, 18 awards, one grand prize

The Indian Express Group once again lets pictures do the talking with The India Press Photo Awards 2008, instituted by the Ramnath Goenka Foundation in 2004 to identify, promote and reward excellence in photojournalism and documentary photography.

Cloistered for three days in a conference room at the Taj President, Mumbai, the three judges—photojournalists Prashant Panjiar, Pablo Bartholomew and Harsh Man Rai—sifted through 8,801 entries by 226 photographers to come up with one grand prize-winning image and one winner from each of the 18 categories. The awards will be announced on November 14 in Mumbai.

Over endless cups of green tea and filter coffee, the winners that emerged have set a new precedent for photojournalists, both established and aspiring. "Despite the two year gap after which this competition has come about, I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of work and the innovation in ideas, image-making and story construction," says Pablo Bartholomew, whose image of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy in 1984 won the World Press Photo's Picture of the Year Award.

The judging process was intense—the photographs had to pass through three rounds of scrutiny. But it was after the first round that the judges felt "the need to reward novelty."

"Photojournalists have always dared to experiment. But in the past 15 years, the work of photojournalists have stagnated and story-telling in photojournalism has become old-fashioned," says Prashant Panjiar, who has served on the jury of several photo awards, including the World Press Photo Awards in 2002 and the Ramnath Goenka Press Photo Awards 2004-2006.

On the need to encourage innovation, Pablo says, "By 'new', we mean a different kind of treatment and approach to stories, the courage to shoot out-of-the-box ideas and images that are powerful while being part of a story."

The judges maintained that while classic journalism wasn't bad, it tends to get repetitive and clichéd. So the small number that bucked that trend was noticed and they are the ones who will walk away with most of the honours.

Harsh Man Rai, the third judge on the panel, is the Group Creative Director of Man's World and Verve magazines.

Shailendre Pandey of Amar Ujala won the Picture of the Year for 2004. His picture of a young boy crying on the telephone as he informs his relatives of his sister's suicide—her body is seen hanging from the fan in the same frame—presents the news in its darkest reality. In 2006, Vipin Pawar of DNA won the Picture of the Year for his picture of the Gateway of India stabbing incident.

Heading: Hindu activists framed under political pressure: Gopinath Munde - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday asked MNS chief Raj Thackeray's lawyers to file an affidavit giving a timeline of developments that took place at the Kalyan magistrate's court on October 22.

Justice V K Tahilramani has now adjourned the hearing of the petition, filed by the state government, till November 25.

The petition challenges the Kalyan sessions court's order not to arrest the MNS chief during the pendency of his anticipatory bail application and the magistrate's order recalling his own earlier order giving Raj's custody to the Railway Police.

The Kalyan session judge had granted Raj anticipatory bail which has been extended till December 5. This was in connection with a case registered by the Government Railway Police (GRP) on October 22 for destruction of property.

Justice V K Tahilramani said she would not interfere with the sessions court's order giving Raj interim relief as the government had an opportunity to raise the same issues before that court.

The High Court will only consider the second issue, she said.

On October 22, Raj was brought to Kalyan magistrate's court by Dombivali police, which had booked him in a case related to MNS workers' attack on north Indian candidates of a Railway Board examination.

The magistrate granted Raj bail. However, the Government Railway Police moved the court, seeking Raj's custody, as they wanted to produce him before the Railway court in a similar case.

According to the prosecution, the Magistrate gave the GRP Raj's custody, but immediately Raj's lawyers pointed out that they had filed an anticipatory bail application before the sessions court, which had restrained the police from arresting Raj till October 24.

The magistrate then recalled his earlier order granting GRP Raj's custody.

The state has now challenged these orders stating that it is illegal as the facts indicate that Raj was already taken into the custody of railway police due to which the advance bail application was infructuous. "There is no averment as to why the petition was not served upon the state prior to moving of the application especially since Raj was in the custody of Kalyan police who then handed over his custody to the railway police," the state has contended.

The state has urged the High Court to call for the records and proceedings from the Kalyan court and quash the anticipatory bail given to Raj and to stay further proceedings of the anticipatory bail application.

"They are disputing certain facts. So they have to file a reply on that," said special public prosecutor Rohini Salian.

Heading: MNS vs north Indians: BJP skips Deshmukh’s all-party meeting - Indian Express
Content:
BJP general secretary Gopinath Munde alleged on Wednesday that political pressure was behind efforts to link Hindu groups to the Malegaon bomb blasts.

The former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister referred to statements by two leaders —NCP president Sharad Pawar and present Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil — who had accused Hindu groups of involvement even before investigations into the blasts had been completed.

"My question is whether the statements of two NCP leaders before the completion of investigations indicate an attempt to frame Hindutva organisations," said Munde. Such moves, he said, were aimed at slandering Hindus so that "committed" voters (minorities) would stay loyal to the ruling dispensation.

He said that Pawar had also spoken of adherents of one religion being targeted for their involvement in terror attacks, while people from the other (majority) community were also involved in it.

Munde also accused the state police of trying to defame the army. "Just as sadhus and saints are being defamed, so is the army," said Munde. Referring to media reports that quoted unnamed police sources over the RDX being used in the blasts coming through army depots, he said, "This is a big allegation by the police against the armed forces."

He said no such evidence was mentioned in the remand report. He dared the DGP, Mumbai Police Commissioner and the ATS chief to given details of the investigations in a press conference; if the charges were not substantiated, he asked them to apologise to the army. "A sense of demoralisation can creep in into the army," charged Munde, while stating that the army officer arrested in the case was not in charge of the army depots storing RDX.

Of the arrest of Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur and Lt Col Prasad Purohit, he said, "Police officers can do it under political pressure." He mentioned his stint as home minister and said he had "friends in the police even today", which gave him access to information.

Munde alleged that the police had not managed to recover any evidence linking the accused to the bomb blasts. Though fake foreign-made live cartridges were seized from two of the accused, Munde said it was not possible to conduct blasts with those.

Munde alleged the reason behind the crackdown was that after the blasts in eight states, demands were for strong anti-terror acts to tackle the SIMI and IM. "This would have estranged committed voters (of the Congress and its allies) and so, there is a conspiracy to defame Hindus," he added.

Munde also alleged that one of the arrested accused in the Malegaon case, whose family had met him, was being tortured by the police to turn a government approver. "If this accused dies in the beatings, then the police will be responsible," said Munde.

Munde attacked the decision to conduct a narco analysis on the arrested Sadhvi thrice, saying it was unprecedented in India, and alleged that no such tests were conducted on the alleged Indian Mujahideen operatives who were arrested recently for their involvement in serial blasts in local trains in Mumbai. "Why this discrimination?" he said.

Heading: State Govt sets out to appease Marathis - Indian Express
Content:
Under fire after the Maharashtra Navanirman Sena (MNS) launched its campaign against north Indians, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Wednesday called an all-party meeting and led a delegation to Governor S C Jamir to protest the wrong impression being created about the state by leaders from other states.

It was meant to be an all-party delegation. But the BJP boycotted the meeting and the trip, while the Shiv Sena attended only the meeting. Earlier, the BJP had also boycotted the all-party meeting held at Mantralaya, while leader of the Opposition Ramdas Kadam (Sena) attended, but attacked the Congress-NCP led state government for its failure to maintain law and order.

Speaking to reporters after his meeting with the governor, Deshmukh said that the MNS agitation was the result of a tiff between the two (Thackeray) brothers and added that it was for this reason that the Sena had stayed away from the meeting with the governor. He also said it was not necessary for politicians from Bihar to worry about the security of their people in Maharashtra. The state government was competent to look into the issue.

The draft of the memorandum presented to the governor said that "the allegations about people from other states residing in Maharashtra feeling not secure is completely false. The culture and tradition of Maharashtra was never narrow or parochial and that efforts to defame Maharashtra state on this issue may endanger our national unity and integrity."

Deshmukh requested the governor to convey the same to the President and Prime Minister.

Speaking at the all-party meeting held earlier at Mantralaya, Deshmukh said the propaganda about migrants being unsafe in Maharashtra after a couple of stray incidents was wrong and defamed Maharashtra. Hence, it was essential for leaders of Maharashtra to follow the example of leaders from other states and put forth the state's point of view.

The BJP has cited the state government's inconsistency on the issue to boycott the meeting and delegation and alleged the Congress- NCP led state government was fuelling the MNS agitation.

Meanwhile, Kadam told reporters that the state government had failed to maintain law and order and justified his party's move to stay away from the meeting with the governor on the grounds that it was now the government's job "to wipe the sin off." On being questioned whether there was a rift between the Sena and the BJP over attending the meeting, Kadam said instead of boycotting the meeting, he had been present and taken the state government to task.

Heading: Students fall sick after drinking flavoured milk - Indian Express
Content:
With Raj Thackeray's Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) hijacking the Marathi agenda from the Shiv Sena and triggering polarisation of north-Indian politicians, the Maharashtra government is also looking for a welfare measure that will aim exclusively at the Marathis.

However, the problem lies in the fact that any such exercise will not be constitutional and the state has no law to penalise those employing 'outsiders'.

According to a senior minister, the government wants to do something exclusively for the Marathi-speaking majority in the state.

"We already have a rule that directs industries to employ 80 per cent of the local residents. But the definition of a local person is one who has been living in the state for the past 15 years or more," he said.

"If we have to score over Sena and MNS, we need to make a change in the definition of a local person. We need to do away with the requirement of a person being domiciled in the state for 15 years, and instead, replace it with a 'Marathi' person," he added.

He pointed out that he had made a suggestion to issue an ordinance to the effect, but other ministers found it an extremely radical measure. He said the government could have approached the central government with a proposal to change the definition. The government could have made a provision that only those who speak Marathi could be employed in the state, he said.

Issued about three decades ago, the existing rule states that any person domiciled in the state for the last 15 years could be considered a local person for preferential employment. But this was just a resolution, and not an Act, he said.

"Because of this, the government is not able to take action against industries and offices that don't employ local people," he said, pointing out that the government could also, as an alternative, make a law and start taking action against defaulters, in order to send a signal that the government was taking care of local people.

The senior minister further said that apart from changing the definition, the government could make it mandatory on the employers to hire jobseekers registered with government employment exchanges only. "If this is done, it would provide a major relief to local unemployed youth as only locals are registered with employment exchanges," he said.

When contacted, minister for industries Ashok Chavan admitted that there was no Act legislated by the state on the issue. He, however, said that since the constitution granted equal status to all Indians irrespective of their language or region, it would not be possible for the government to change the definition of a local person.

He said that employers who do not follow the government directive (of recruiting locals) face action in the form of denial or reduction in concessions granted by the government.

Heading: Civic corporators to get lessons - Indian Express
Content:
A year after the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation introduced the flavoured milk scheme, 11 students from Tardeo municipal school fell ill after consuming the tetra-packed milk. The incident took place at the Tardeo Marathi Municipal school, Bane compound at 1.30 in the afternoon when the tetra-packs of Elaichi flavour were distributed to the students. The Tardeo police station has registered a case of food poisoning.

Even after repeated incidents of students falling ill on drinking the milk, civic officials said that the scheme would continue. They added that a 12- year- old girl got nauseous and started vomiting after consuming the milk. Seeing her, many other students felt nauseous and reported uneasiness. Around 11 students were taken to Nair hospital.

Joint municipal commissioner (education), Chandrashekhar Rokde admitted to the incident. "It was not a serious incident. We are not withdrawing the flavoured milk scheme,'' Rokde said.

When contacted Dean, KEM hospital, Dr Sanjay Oak said, "The children were kept for observation for four hours and were discharged later. We admitted one girl as her parents were apprehensive. There was nothing abnormal about the children.''

A report submitted by Dr Oak, to the BMC on the incident said that of the 40 children, ten developed nausea and this may be because of storage problem of the tetra-packed milk, personal hygiene or psychological problem. The report said that while precautions can be taken, due to reactions to flavoured milk there could be more such cases.

The Rs 100 crore flavoured milk scheme was mired in controversy after it was introduced last year. Tetra packs of flavoured milk worth Rs 11 each were procured from Haryana and distributed to students in Mumbai's municipal schools. However, two incidents of adulteration were soon reported wherein 48 students complained of uneasiness and vomiting. Uproar over the incident made the BMC withdraw distribution and a committee to undertake precautions was appointed. Consumption of the tetra packs was later made optional for students.

Heading: Metro rail project: MMRDA counselled on avoiding delay - Indian Express
Content:
Civic corporators will soon get a dose on gender sensitization to develop a culturally sensitive approach towards development.

The state of the world population report 2008, "Reaching Common Ground: Culture, Gender and Human Rights", which was released on Wednesday, emphasises that culture is a central component of successful development of countries, and must be integrated into development policy and programming.

All India Institute of Local Self-Governance along with United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) will train all the corporators, especially from Bhiwandi, Mira road and Ulhasnagar, on gender bias.

Anuja Gulati of UNFPA said "After being trained, these corporators will monitor clinics with sonography machines and appoint sex selection committees at ward level to avoid cases of sex selection."

The report further stated, "International development agencies ignore culture or marginalize it at their peril. Advancing human rights requires an appreciation of the complexity, fluidity and centrality of culture by intentionally identifying and partnering with local agents."

Present at the release, Vandana Krishna, secretary and commissioner of family welfare for Maharashtra agreed that there is a cultural bias at both community level and among medical professionals. "There is a judgmental attitude even among the health professionals dealing with teen pregnancies," she said.

"Women often become victims of rape, early marriage leading to early pregnancy and improper medical care during pregnancy leads to high Maternal Mortality Rate and Infant Mortality Rate," Krishna said, adding that even NGOs can bring about a change in people's attitude towards cultural biasness.

The state health department along with United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) will do a pilot test of 'SAFE KIT' to be made available for rape victims. "We will test the kit at Sion hospital, Thane civil hospital and another hospital in Pune for six months. If the response is positive then we will upscale the project. This will help in proper collection of evidence to be produced in courts in rape cases," said Gulati.

Krishna added, "When it comes to using contraceptives, women usually are not the decision makers. Strong patriarchal system is hindering development in several areas. Hence it is very important to sensitize not just the woman but husbands and in-laws as well," she said.

The state government is focusing on improving communication skills among the locals so that they can help in promoting health and family welfare programmes, Krishna said.

Releasing the third edition of youth supplement to UNFPA's State of the World Population report, Director of Maharashtra Health directorate Dr Prakesh Doke said, "Youth across the country have the potential to overcome the taboos attached to culture as they have new ideas and are bold to bring a positive change especially in tackling human rights violations."

Heading: Now, a dedicated helpline for railway commuters - Indian Express
Content:
Rail Vikas Corporation MD writes to authority head, urban development secretary about possible 'technical' hurdles, ways to avoid them during first-phase procurements

The Mumbai Rail Vikas Corporation (MRVC) has written to the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) suggesting steps to be taken in order to avoid delay in the procurement of rakes for the first phase of the Mumbai Metro project on the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar stretch.

The Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd (MMOPL), a joint venture between the Reliance Infrastructure, MMRDA and Veolia Transport, a French company, would be procuring 16 rakes from China.

In a letter written by MRVC managing director P C Sehgal to MMRDA commissioner Ratnakar Gaikwad and urban development department secretary T C Benjamin, Sehgal has informed MMRDA about the possible 'technical' hurdles and ways to avoid them in the procurement process. Sehgal was a part of the team that had visited China last month to oversee the progress of rake manufacturing being done there.

"We have received a letter from Sehgal in which he has suggested ways to monitor the production of the rakes for the Metro phase I. The suggestions would prove quite useful for us to avoid delay as he has a rich experience in this field," said Gaikwad.

The MRVC is responsible for the procurement of 191 rakes under the two phases of Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP). But the procurement was delayed due to various reasons. However, the city got its first new EMU rake under the MUTP Phase I after Sehgal took over as the managing director of MRVC. He was also the chief engineer of the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW) and has expertise in rakes.

Sehgal, in the letter, has asked the MMRDA to look in to the various manufacturing aspects of the rakes and precautions that needs to be taken in installation of electrical equipments during manufacturing. He has also recommended various tests that are to be done during various stages of manufacturing and before the rake is commissioned.

The letter also suggests MMRDA officials of preparing pert charts which would help keep a tab on the manufacturing progress. The chart shows various stages of the manufacturing process. The method is being used by the MRVC to check progress of their rakes.

Transportation of the rakes was another important part of the communication. The letter stated that a proper arrangement needs to be done in this case as the rakes would be transported through the sea route. Recommendations have been made in this regard as it not only involves transporting the rakes from the port but also putting them on tracks. In case of the EMU rakes, which run on the suburban tracks, they are directly brought to the city from the Integral Coach Factory in Chennai.

Heading: Blog on Raj encounter: Cops seek legal opinion - Indian Express
Content:
Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil on Wednesday launched a dedicated Government Railway Police (GRP) helpline to benefit all the rail commuters across the state.

According to Krish Pal Raghuvanshi, additional director general (Railways), the helpline was started with the help of Vodafone, a mobile phone service provider. Now, the commuters in distress, can dial 9833331111, a number which according to the police is easy to remember. Though the helpline is based in Mumbai, commuters across the state can avail of the service.

"Vodafone has also given us 76 telephone lines of which 38 would be in the city railway police stations and the rest would be installed across the railway police stations in the state. So, whenever, a distress call is received from anywhere in the state, we can immediately forward it to the concerned police station and the person in distress can get relief. This would also prove to be beneficial for women commuters," said Raghuvanshi.

Presently, except the control room of the Mumbai Railway Police, the railways does not have a dedicated telephone number for commuters in distress. "Many a time, the phone is busy. So, commuter can dial the helpline which is easy to remember. With this, a commuter from Nasik can also be avail of help without dialling an STD number," added Raghuvanshi.

The GRP is also planning to popularise the helpline through advertisements in railway coaches.

Heading: Naik’s statement: Top cop meets ulemas - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch has taken strong exception to a blog entry on the Rahul Raj police encounter that was posted on the internet by a 27-year-old youth from the city. The entry hurls abuses at the police and the state government and alleges that it's a staged encounter. Politicians like Raj Thackeray and Lalu Prasad Yadav should be killed, the blog states.

According to the Crime Branch, it's now seeking legal opinion on whether it can take any action against the youth. The blog entry was posted on November 6 by the youth, who resides in Thakur Complex, Kandivali. The Cyber Crime Investigation Cell of the Crime Branch stumbled on the post as part of its routine monitoring to keep tabs on sensitive content on the internet.

"During a check on the internet, we came across the blog entry. It was highly critical of the Rahul Raj shootout, and alleged that the police had staged the encounter. It was titled 'The truth about the the Kurla bus encounter' and the youth had hurled several abuses at the police and the government. He also asked people to kill Raj Thackeray and Lalu Prasad Yadav," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

According to the police, the youth hailing from a north Indian family, is born and brought up in Mumbai. He is an electronics and telecom engineer and has an online advertising business, said the police.

"We questioned him and recorded his statement. We are now seeking legal opinion on whether we can take any action against him for inciting violence. We have also notified the Computer Emergency Response Team in New Delhi to block the post," said Maria.

Heading: Primary accused in union leader murder case has gangland connections: Crime Branch - Indian Express
Content:
Islamic scholar Zakir Naik who is scheduled to address an Islamic conference in the city between November 14 and 24 recently attracted the ire of certain Muslims after a controversial statement.

Various members of Muslim ulemas and intellectuals had arrived at the Joint Commissioner's office with recorded tapes of Naik's lectures dating back to five years. "In some previous lectures recorded around five years ago Naik had made some statement like 'Hum Allah se mangte nahi' and as a slip of the tongue the 'mangte' was heard as 'mante'. 'Allah ko mante nahin' would be atheism and that infuriated the religious Muslims and led to the controversy," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Law and Order), K L Prasad.

After various Muslim ulemas and other Muslim leaders voiced their dissent and even demanded that the conference be banned, Naik has given a written statement that he will not raise issues which will hurt the other sects of Islam.

"Following the recent spate of verbal exchange of words between Naik and certain other sections of Shia and Sunni Muslims, reconciliation seemed necessary. The issue had the potential to flare up into a law and order situation and hence a meeting was planned in my office," said Prasad. "The contentious issues and a controversial statement attributed to Dr Zakir Naik were discussed and finally an amicable solution was found after Naik agreed to give a statement, which written in Urdu promises that 'he will not raise issues which will hurt other sects of Islam," added Prasad.

Once this was pointed out the Muslim religious leaders were pacified and Naik's statement was welcomed, said Prasad.

Heading: Deplorable state of consumer courts under HC scanner - Indian Express
Content:
The Samta Nagar police might have arrested six persons in connection with the murder of Shantaram Kanade on Sunday morning at the society office at Evershine Millenium Paradise. But according to the crime branch officials, the case is not as simple as it seems to be.

An officer attached to the crime branch said on condition of anonymity, "We have information that Vijay Salvi alias Tambad has connections with the Chotta Rajan gang. Moreover, we believe that the murder was not a result of the dispute between Kanade and Salvi for the post of the secretary of the building. The motive is something else and more complicated."

Though the Samta Nagar police are sticking to the theory that Kanade was murdered over a dispute for the post of the secretary and Salvi is a businessman dealing in marble in London, Crime Branch sleuths seem to believe that there is more than what the police have known about them. When contacted, DCP Ajit Patil (Zone 12) said, "Salvi has three criminal cases against him at Mulund and Samta Nagar. He is into marble business in London. He left for London before the incident and has not come back yet. So we have not been able to apprehend and question him. The six arrested have confessed to have killed Kanade on Salvi's behest and said that they work as Salvi's bodyguards."

Quizzed whether Salvi has connection with any underworld gang, Patil said, "We are trying to gather more informations about Salvi, though we have not had any information so far about the possibility of Salvi having any connections with any organised crime organisations. As far as the motive goes, it was because of the dispute between Salvi and Kanade over the post of the secretary."

Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria said, "On our records, Salvi has links with the Chotta Rajan gang. We are also conducting parallel investigations to know whether the motive of the murder was the dispute over the post of the secretary of the society."

Heading: Deadline for retrofitting engines of 532 BEST buses extended till December 31 - Indian Express
Content:
The deplorable condition of Consumer Disputes Redressal Forums and the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has come under the Bombay High Court scanner.

A division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice S J Kathawalla was hearing a petition filed by Consumer Courts Advocates' Association grieving about lack of infrastructure, space and facilities due to which the courts were in a terrible condition.

The court has now asked the petitioners to make the Finance Secretary and Chief Secretary parties to the petition so that if need be, the court can direct them to explain the situation. The court has, however, directed the Secretary of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Department to file a reply in this regard before the next hearing on December 3.

Petitioners allege that none of the orders passed by the court since 2006 have been implemented by the authorities. They contended that the condition of consumer courts in other states was better than those in Maharashtra.

Justice Patel observed that there has been no planning or vision on this issue and asked the government why they are not taking any serious action.

Lawyer for petitioner, Rita Joshi, told the court that Members of consumer courts are conducting their duties from the bar room.

Petitioners, among other things, have sought for better infrastructure, fast-track courts, appointment of judges in service instead of retired ones, renovation of state commission and filling up of 157 staff vacancies.

According to the petition, since the inception of various District Forums in Maharashtra, a total of 1,61,279 cases have been filed, out of which 45,649 cases have been disposed off till August 2005. As for the State Commission, 6,078 cases have been filed since its inception, out of which only 3,900 cases have been disposed off till August 2005.

The petition further states that about 25,564 appeals and 15,707 miscellaneous applications have been filed in the state commission, out of which only 14,079 appeals and 9,123 miscellaneous applications could be disposed off till August 2005.

Petitioners are also seeking facilities such as canteen, adequate sitting space, furniture, toilets, library, electronic boards and internet facilities.

"The condition is really bad as there is no space and not even facility to go to toilet," said petitioner advocate Uday Wavikar.

Heading: Gorai dumping ground to be revamped - Indian Express
Content:
The BEST undertaking's process to phase out old vehicles by retrofitting with Euro-II (BS-II) engine for 532 buses has been extended till December 31. BEST has also come out in support of Traffic Restraint Scheme (TRS). This was told to the Bombay High Court by petitioner Bombay Environmental Action Group (BEAG), an NGO.

Hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by BEAG seeking the implementation of the TRS in 2003, a division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice S J Kathawalla has now kept the matter for final hearing.

The transport commissioner to the state government had earlier told the court that it was the considered view of the state government that implementation of the Traffic Restraint Scheme (TRS), proposed for the decongestion of vehicular traffic flowing into the island city, is untimely and impractical.

However, counsel for petitioner Shiraz Rostamji told the court that the BEST was in fact supporting the scheme. Rostamji while citing the state of cabs and buses submitted that unless they were encouraged, they would not grow.

He further said that the density of traffic had increased and the average speed had come down to 8 kmph from 20 kmph.

However, Justice Patel while keeping the case for final hearing told the state government to discourage their officers from visiting foreign countries for this purpose as it would be unnecessary expense.

Meanwhile, Sunil Karlekar, chief engineer, Transport, in an affidavit informed the court that they had complied with all the directions except for phasing out 532 buses for which they sought time till December 31.

So far BEST has phased out all buses which are more than 15-years-old and replaced them with Euro-II CNG engines. It has also inducted 100 CNG buses per year commencing from 2004-05 for a period of six years. When contacted, BEST lawyer D G Dhanure confirmed that BEST was supporting the TRS system.

However, Transport Commissioner Shyamsunder Shinde, in an affidavit filed earlier had stated that "the implementation of the TRS, at this point in time, looking at the public transportation effort, the constraints earlier stated in the scheme's implementation and the focus on provision first rather than restrictive regulation renders the TRS untimely and impractical."

"Massive effort has been launched to improve Mumbai's public transport. Some of such projects as cited have been completed, others are ongoing and their impact should be positive in easing congestion," Shinde said.

The court had earlier expressed dissatisfaction with the fact that the government has not dealt with the problem seriously and directed the government to file an affidavit stating what measures it proposes to take will avoid the clogging up of the island city.

BEAG in its PIL pressed for the implementation of the scheme earlier proposed by a committee led by former transport commissioner V M Lal. The committee had come up with 100 suggestions to reduce Mumbai's vehicular pollution, one of which was the TRS.

Heading: State to upscale Matrutva Anudan - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Gorai have reason to cheer as the Gorai dumping ground is gearing up to metamorphose into a green mound. It will host a park and if possible a gold course, at a height of 31 meter from the ground, overseeing the picturesque creek. Relief has come for the residents of the area after 25 years as the ground was till now being used to dump the city's 1200 tonne of garbage.

While the stench and the heaps of garbage have been covered up, it will still take another three-five years, till the revamped dumping ground cum 'green park' is open to public. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has completed 90 per cent of the work related to the closure of the Gorai dumping ground following a Supreme Court directive on shutting it as the place had attained its maximum capacity of 1200 tonne/day .

"Municipal solid waste has been scientifically composted and arranged in layers at the height of 31 meter to form a mount slope and has been covered with high density plastic so that rain water does not seep in the garbage and decompose it," said executive engineer (Solid Waste Management), Pundlik Awate .

"A geo-thermal net covered with asbestos will be put up on the plastic which will later have 300 cm of soil layer and will be covered with grass and bushes," he added.

The revamped dump mound will also have around 40 wells which will collect methane gas. "Methane gas would be produced from the decomposition of the waste. Depending upon the quantity of the gas, the civic administration will also be able to generate two- three mega watt electricity," said executive enginner (SWM), Ajay Lavgankar.

Non-emission of methane in the atmosphere is also expected to earn the BMC carbon credits. Certified Emission Reductions (CERs) or carbon credits of 31033 tons/ annum will be generated annually after the closure of the ground which may be traded in the market.

To prevent black watery Leachate (pollutant) that seeps through the garbage, from polluting ground water, small construction tracts have been constructed surrounding the 19 hectare dump. The Leachate will be separately collected and then treated at Versova pumping station and later released in sea water.

The closure of Gorai dumping ground is being carried by Indian firm, United Phosphorus Ltd and Dutch firm Van Der Weil at the cost of Rs 37 crore.

Heading: Staff crunch may force Tadoba tiger reserve to close down - Indian Express
Content:
The state health department is planning to upgrade its 13-year-old programme that encourages institutional delivery. Matrutva Anudan Yojana that was started in 1995 in tribal areas to encourage institutional delivery will now cover all the women in the state who deliver in government hospitals.

According to National Family Health Survey -III, only 75 per cent of women give birth at institutions. It's established that low turn out at institutions for delivery is directly proportional to rise in Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) and Infant Mortality Rate (IMR).

"Matrutva Anudan Yojana , will soon be upscaled across Maharashtra and cover all women who deliver at government hospitals. All the women delivering at the hospitals will get Rs 800. The state has sanctioned Rs 200 crore for the same," said Shomita Biswas, joint secretary, Family Welfare, Maharashtra. "The women need to register themselves with the hospital and will get Rs 400 during Antenatal check-ups and the remaining Rs 400 will be given post delivery. This scheme is entirely funded by the state government," she said.

The Central Government-sponsored Janani Suraksha Yojana scheme under Reproductive and Child Health programme II in the state —- it was started recently in Mumbai — only caters to Below Poverty Line (BPL) women and women belonging to schedule tribe and schedule caste. To tackle the shortage of gynecologists in the state, the public health department is planning to hire gynecologists from public and private hospitals from city area of each district on contract basis.

"We're considering the idea of contractual doctors who will provide their services in villages for a stipulated time. This can be the second best option," said Vandana Krishna, secretary and commissioner, Family Welfare, Maharashtra. "We're also planning to train MBBS doctors in conducting natural delivery also child care," she added.

Heading: Tome to thrill - Indian Express
Content:
Priyanka Chopra: Untouched by plastic surgery, uncensored in Fashion and unedited on Dostana

Is looking good and being fit important to you?
Yes.

Have u ever had plastic surgery?
No.

A news channel the day before had an interview with a surgeon, with pictures of you before and after you went under his knife. Have you met this doctor?
I found out about that doctor and he is of an ill repute. And it's shocking more so because I come from a family of doctors and believe this profession is next to godliness. Sadly, such unethical doctors still practise.

Are you going to sue him?
This time, I will probably take action against him.

This has been a year of mixed fortunes for you.
And I hope to end it on a positive note with Dostana. The movie looks really good, but then I feel this way about all my films.

With the camaraderie between Abhishek Bachchan and John Abraham, did you feel left out?
All the time. They're both so fantastic that I really wish them for each other. Poor Ash (Aishwarya Rai) and Bipasha (Basu).

Shooting in Miami was one long party?
It's been the best outdoor in my entire life. Miami is a mixture of Bombay and Goa—lethargic in the day and lively at night. We even shot at that pace. With seagulls, waves and people skating around, life was a long vacation.

It's Tarun Mansukhani's debut as a director.
He scripted and directed the film and given that Karan Johar came on the sets only five times, he carried the entire film on his shoulders. The results are fabulous. People at the preview were rolling on the floor laughing; my brother fell off his chair.

You're being pitched for the National Award for Fashion?
I'm a very practical person. It's the biggest honour but I'm not expecting anything because I don't want to be heartbroken.

In an industry dominated by male protagonists, how was it playing a pivotal role in Fashion?
I worked very hard on Meghna Mathur's character. I wanted the physical graph to come across as the character developed. Hence I gradually changed my diet and look for the film. I'm pudgy in the first half, but as the film progresses, I begin to look like a model.

What about your future projects?
I'm looking forward to Ashutosh Gowarikar's What's Your Rashee and Vishal Bhardwaj's Kaminey, which release next year.

Goldie Hawn complimented you for Fashion.
Is Hollywood the next step?
Hollywood is not a target, but neither was Bollywood. But I believe I am destiny's child.

Heading: Project Paris - Indian Express
Content:
Film: Dostana

Director: Tarun Mansukhani

Cast: John Abraham, Abhishek Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra, Boman Irani, Bobby Deol

Rating: ***

Running at: Inox (Form, City Centre, Swabhumi)

Even if you don't enjoy a very hot and a not-very-hot man pretending to kiss onscreen, even if you cringe at your love handles every time Priyanka Chopra comes in view, even if you are severely allergic to ridicule and prejudices, go and watch Dostana. Because, it's lame, ridiculous, and maybe a little undiplomatic for the righteous, but then, it's fun. The kind of fun which has not come your way as a movie in a long long time.
