For starters, you don't get to see the kind of abs you get to see here (which is a disciplined version of saying how good John Abraham looks every frame of the film), and you get quite a refresher's course in dressing cool. Then, it has a couple of really groovy songs. And finally, the cast, looks like they are having one big party, where all of us are invited.

So, Dostana, despite its several logical failings and sensitivity roadblocks, takes you on a roller coaster ride. A ride that ends with such a heroic plunge into the cheesy, that you already have your sides split with laughter, before you try brushing the dust off your grey cells. Sam (Abhishek Bachchan), a nurse, and Kunal (John Abraham), a photographer, bump into each other after a night out with two girls sharing an apartment. They are both looking for an apartment, and instantly fall in love with the first one they land inspecting. However, the owner refuses to let the apartment out to two young men as it belongs to her niece Neha (Priyanka Chopra) who also stays there. Desperate to get the flat, the two decide to pose as a gay couple. What follows is a laughathon.

Tarun Mansukhani's average storyline works only because he seems to have got the cast bang-on. John looks every bit the fashion photographer he is cast as, and Abhishek Bachchan looks adequately goofy as a male nurse. Though their histrionics (especially Abhishek's attempts at looking gay and funny in a dream sequence) are not extraordinary, they don't fall short of the spirit of the film. Because the loudness, despite itself, goes along well with the rhetoric of the film. Priyanka Chopra does a commendable job as a perky, sweet, fashion journalist. The motley cast, which includes Boman Irani in a cameo, is top notch. From Neha's disastrous aunty (Sushmita Mukherjee) to the weepy, theatrical mother played by Kirron Kher, Mansukhani's support cast has a lot to do with the crispness of the film. Vishal Shekhar's music is quite engaging, and Shilpa Shetty, still looks in good shape.

PS: Bobby Deol, well, is not very funny. But he's getting there.

Heading: Catterati - Indian Express
Content:
As the Tranoi Fair celebrates India in its Autumn-Winter edition, designer Abhishek Dutta gets a surprise invite

While he was prepping the models and giving last-minute tucks for his comeback show at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week last month, designer Abhishek Dutta had little inkling that someone in the audience already had big plans for him. "I saw Michael Hadida, the owner of the prestigious Tranoi Fair, in the front row and was happy, particularly because he had earlier come to my stall and browsed through the clothes. But I was so busy ensuring everything went off without a hitch that I didn't think anything beyond that," says Dutta.

It was his return to the Delhi Fashion Week, after four consecutive showings at the Lakme Fashion Week in Mumbai. Now, Dutta can book another ticket - to Paris and its prestigious Tranoi Fair.

Dutta's collection—a series of quirky outfits that included zippered cargos, khadi jackets, shorts and capris and dresses with appliqués, all in linen and cotton - subtly played up the Indian theme on overtly western silhouettes, and won him accolades from fashionistas. Much later, the designer from Kolkata came to know that Hadida had included him and newbie designer duo Nidhi and Pankaj for the Autumn-Winter edition of the fair, scheduled to take off in Paris between March 2 and 5.

Incidentally, Tranoi is celebrating India as its theme at this year's fair, with an India Pavilion showcasing the works of over 15 of India's top designers. "I first heard the news from the media, but it was only when there was a correspondence from Hadida's office that I was convinced that I was actually going," laughs 29-year-old Dutta, who launched his prêt-a-porter label, Adnormal, in 2004, and now supplies to over 20 stores across the country, including Kimaya and Aza. While the designer is busy working on the orders that he has received after the fashion week, his blueprint for Tranoi is also ready. "I am not into bling bling since it's only suited to the Indian context. I'm working towards developing new fabrics and reviving old weaving techniques, so that my Indian sensibilities come across even on a western silhouette," says Dutta, who counts actors Vidya Balan, Salman Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, and Raima and Riya Sen among his clients.

Heading: Rs 911-crore facelift for Ahmedabad Civil Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Girls over goals

The Global Millennium Development Goals Summit at Jai Hind College on November 11 saw pretty faces Juhi Chawla and Celina Jaitley among the luminaries in the audience. The summit was hosted by the college along with The World Federation of United Nations Association and was organised for a discussion of the Eight Millennium Development Goals set by the United Nations. We don't know about the world's goals, but we think that one of Juhi's goals should be to lose weight quick. Or is it that hideous printed kurta paired with those passé red tights that makes her torso seem out of proportion? She should hire a new stylist or take a leaf out of Celina's book and keep it simple.

Showstopper Celina looked classy in her casual dress and toned down makeup.

Heading: Teen confesses, mother tries to shoulder blame - Indian Express
Content:
Modi says the 'innovative initiative' aims to improve state's human development index

In its bid to tone up the medical services in Gujarat, the state government has chalked out an ambitious Rs 911.68-crore project to upgrade and restructure the Ahmedabad Civil Hospital, which is considered the biggest in Asia. The project will be implemented soon and executed in three phases, ending with the state's Golden Jubilee Year—2010.

Chief Minister Narendra Modi announced this at a New Year luncheon organised for the media at his official residence in Gandhinagar on Wednesday. Under the project, the bed capacity at the hospital, which currently stands at 2,150, will be increased to 5,150.

Though Modi did not mention any Central assistance for the project, a senior official in the State Health Department told Newsline later that the UPA government has chipped in with Rs 120 crore under the Prime Minister's Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY). A couple of years ago, the Centre had provided nearly Rs 100 crore for the same purpose.

Modi said the project was his government's "innovative initiative" aimed at bringing about qualitative changes in the health care services and improving the human development index (HDI) in the state. "Patients from Gujarat as well as from the neighbouring states of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh will also be benefited by the modernisation of Asia's biggest hospital," he said.

At present, the hospital, spread over 110 acres of land in Asarwa, provides health care services to over 6.50 lakh patients every year.

Under the project, the hospital will have one additional trauma centre besides multi-specialty and super-specialty health care facilities. The medical colleges located in the sprawling hospital complex will also get a facelift under the project.

In the first phase, the renovation and restructuring work of all the blocks of the Civil Hospital, B J Medical College, Dental College and Hospital, Paraplegia College, operation theatres, new trauma centre, Ophthalmic Institute, Nursing College and other related infrastructure in the complex will be undertaken at a cost of Rs 289.05 crore.

In the second phase, involving Rs 235 crore, renovation and upgradation of medical students' hostels, professors' residential houses, housing blocks of the hospital staff, students' mess and a guesthouse will be taken up. The third phase costing Rs 325 crore will involve works related to parking facilities, beautification of the entire hospital complex, and the day-to-day needs of patients among others.

All old buildings and temporary constructions will be removed from the hospital complex as part of the project. It is also envisaged to upgrade the existing power and water supply networks and drainage system. Moreover, fire fighting and emergency services will be upgraded and a special system for solid waste and medical waste disposal will be developed.

Heading: Swami Ashimananda likely to surface at religious function today - Indian Express
Content:
The Shilaj hit-and-run case in which three persons were killed and two others injured took unexpected twists and turns on Wednesday night when Pravin Gandhi from Swaminarayan Society in Paldi area appeared before the Sarkhej police along with his family members: wife Jayshree, son Sidhhant and daughter Krupa.

Initially, Jayshree (41) told the police that she was driving the car when the family was returning home after having a picnic in Thol Bird sanctuary on Sunday when the accident happened.

But later, during a separate interrogation of the family members, it came out that Jayshree was lying and it was her son, Sidhhant (18), who was in the car along with his girlfriend and two other friends on the day of accident. In fact, Sidhhant has confessed this before the police.

Superintendent of Police, Ahmedabad Rural, S S Trivedi said: "Initially, the woman had confessed before us that the family was returning from a picnic when the incident happened. However, right from the beginning, we doubted her version of the story."

He added: "So, we interrogated all the family members separately. During her interrogation, she broke down and told us to talk to her husband about the matter. The subsequent interrogation of Sidhhant and his father revealed that Sidhhant was in the car along with his girlfriend and two other friends."

Trivedi further said that Jayshree confessed before the police that she had made a false statement to save her son's future.

According to the police, Sidhhant is studying commerce in a city-based college. Investigations are on to find the other three friends of Sidhhant, who were with him in the car.

According to Trivedi, the police had some evidence to prove that Jayshree was not present at the accident spot on Sunday night. "It has also been found that apart from Sidhhant and three of his friends in the car, there was another group of his friends, which was following them on motorbikes. So, we are investigating to find out if the group had any booze party nearby," Trivedi added.

The police had recovered two empty bottles of beer from the car after the accident.

Heading: Police summon Gujarat VHP office-bearers for questioning - Indian Express
Content:
Swami Ashimananda Maharaj, who vanished after coming under the scanner of Mumbai police's Anti Terror Squad (ATS) in connection with the Malegaon bomb blast, may turn up to rub shoulders with prominent local leaders of the RSS, VHP, BJP and other Sangh Parivar outfits on Thursday.

He will inaugurate a nine-day Ramkatha event in Tapi district on Thursday and also be the chief guest at the high profile event, according to the organisers, Ramkatha Sewa Samithi of Vyara.

The Swami would share the dais with prominent leaders like Vijay Patel, BJP MLA of Dangs, Hitendra Upadhyay, BJP general secretary of Tapi, Mansinh Patel, BJP district president of Surat, Mahuwa Mohan Dodiya, former BJP MLA of Mahua, VHP leader Bhagu Gamit, Mahipal Thakur, district president of Gujarat Dharma Jagran Manch Dangs, Jayanti Kewat, senior BJP leader in Navsari, and many others.

The Swami hit the headlines recently when the ATS raided his ashram in the Dangs district in connection with the Malegaon blast. The police also revealed that he was in touch with prime suspect Sadhvi Pragya Thakur. He went underground immediately and no one really knows his whereabouts ever since.

Nevertheless, the organisers appear unfazed by it. They have been busy distributing elaborate invitation cards for the event showing the Swami as chief guest. "We have seen Swami Ashimanandji's name in the newspapers. But he is innocent. Our own sources have had a talk with him and he has assured that he would definitely attend the inaugural function. He will remain with us for sometime at the venue and then leave," said Narsinh Choudhary, president of Ramkatha Ayojak Samithi, which proposes to use the funds generated from the event to build a Hanuman temple at Chunarwadi village.

The event is expected to draw a huge crowd. The invitation cards are being distributed in most talukas of Surat, Navsari, Valsad and Dangs districts. "We expect a huge turnout and have made elaborate arrangements for accommodation and other facilities," said Ranjeet Choudhary of the Samithi.

Newsline contacted some of the invited guests for the programme. Former Congress MLA and MP from Vyara in Surat district, Amarsinh Z Choudhary, said: "My name appears on the invitation and the organisers had contacted me earlier for the function. They, however, have done a wrong thing by inviting only VHP, RSS and BJP leaders as guests. I am in Ahmedabad to attend a private function so I will not attend the event."

Ex-BJP MLA Mahuwa Mohan Dodiya said: "The event will be a good thing for the tribal area. The tribals should know the Hindu religion, as they are our brothers. Swami Ashimanand Maharaj is very close to me and I had met him at Sabridham in the Dangs two years ago. He is my closest friend. He has a good nature and is a great orator. He has worked a lot for the development of the tribals and was also involved in re-conversion. We have full faith in him and he is not involved in any anti-national activity. I am sure that he will attend the function."

Vijay Patel, BJP MLA from the Dangs, said: "We are happy that somebody is doing a good job in spreading Hindu religion among tribals. I will not attend the function, as I have to attend a party meeting at Dharampur village. I will also be busy with my party workers for the upcoming elections. If I get time, I will attend the function. I know Swami Ashimanandaji Maharaj and he is a down-to-earth person. He has done a lot of work for the tribal people. I have full faith in him. I was also present during the Sabri Kumbh Mela and had come very close to him. I do not want to say anything about his attendance of the Ramkatha."

Heading: July 26 blasts:  DCB files chargesheet against 26 accused - Indian Express
Content:
Gandhinagar police on Friday summoned two senior VHP office-bearers in connection with the case of "defamatory SMS" against Chief Minister Narendra Modi, for which they had earlier arrested VHP joint secretary Ashwin Patel.

The police, for interrogation, summoned Kaushik Mehta, general secretary of Gujarat VHP and close aide of Dr Pravin Togadia, and Rajesh Shastri, VHP president of north Gujarat region.

"We have summoned these two leaders to record their statement and interrogate them regarding the SMS case. We have asked them to come to the police station tomorrow," M L Ninana, in-charge SP of Gandhinagar told PTI.

The police had arrested Ashwin Patel on Diwali eve for allegedly sending "defamatory SMS" about Chief Minister Narendra Modi and trying to create social tension between different communities in the state. He has been booked under various sections of forgery and also under sedition.

Earlier, on Tuesday, the Sessions Court of Gandhinagar had rejected Patel's bail plea.

Heading: Sakkar Baug museum gets new home at Taj Manzil - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly three months after the first arrest was made in the July 26 serial blasts case, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on Wednesday filed chargesheet against 26 people. They have been made accused in the Civil Hospital and L G Hospital blast cases.

They have been booked under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code, Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, Explosives Act, Arms Act and the Information Technology Act.

DCB officials have claimed they have enough direct and substantial evidence to show that the blasts were plotted during a three-day training camp held at Halol, near Pavagadh from January 13 this year.

A senior DCB official said: "It was the training camp held at Wagamon, Kerala in December 2007 where the seeds of terrorist action were first sown. It was at the Halol camp that the blast plan was initiated. It was decided there that 'now the time has come to do something'."

According to DCB officials, the chargesheet clearly established the details of the Halol training camp.

It has the statements of Tata Sumo owner who had rented his vehicle to be used in the camp as also the details and the shop from which tents for the camp were rented out. The vehicle has already been seized by the police.

The chargesheet, which cites 511 witnesses, reportedly also has documentary evidence obtained from the Khunda Peer Dargah, located at the Champaner-Pavagdh foothills near the training camp site. It shows that all the accused had stayed there just before the training camp started.

The official said, "The registration records for staying in the Dargah premises establish that the accused had stayed there. Also, we have corroborative evidence in the form of cellphone records of the accused, which shows their presence in that area."

The accused include alleged blast masterminds like Mufti Mohammad Abdul Bashr, Sajid Mansuri, Safdar Nagori, three suspects of the Jaipur serial blasts and Raizuddin Nasir, who was brought on a transit warrant from Karnataka. Nasir, who has allegedly taken training in Pakistan and has close links with the Lashkar-e-Toiba, is said to have shown inflammatory CDs at the Wagamon training camp and motivated those present towards radical violent action.

According to the DCB, the 59-page chargesheet that contains an annexure running close to 2,000 pages, clearly establishes that Indian Mujahideen is a more radical breakaway faction of the banned SIMI. It lists 58 people, including Abdul Subham alias Tauqueer and Qyamuddin Kapadia as absconders. The Madhya Pradesh Police had arrested Kapadia on November 10. His custody has not yet been handed over to the Gujarat Police.

DCB officials said that a group of accused had visited the city prior to the blasts on July 11 and 12, and planned it with the help of their local cadre. This group, which includes several key players involved in other bomb blasts in the country, had later left for Delhi on July 25 by the Rajdhani Express.

In line with their stated theory in the various remand applications submitted by the DCB in the case so far, the chargesheet further says the blasts were triggered to avenge the 2002 post-Godhra riots and spread Islam in the country.

Officials said that supplementary chargesheets with more incriminating evidence against the accused may follow soon. Also, chargesheet in other of the total 20 cases registered in the aftermath of the blasts is expected to be filed soon. Thirty-seven people have been arrested by the DCB in the case so far.

Those named in the chargesheet are Jahid Sheikh, Imran Sheikh, Iqbal Sheikh, Samsuddin Sheikh, Gyasuddin Sheikh, Arif Kagzi, Usman Agarbattiwala, Yunus Mansuri, Sajid Mansuri, Abu Basher, Naved Kadri, Javed Sheikh, Abbas Sameja, Aiyaz Sayyad, Salim Sipahi, Umar Kabira, Safdar Nagori, Hafez Hussain, Sibli Abdul Karim, Kamruddin Nagori, Amil Parvez, Mohammad Ali, Raziuddin Nasir, Atik-ur-Rehman, Mehndi Hassan and Imran Ahmed alias Raja.

Heading: Govt accuses Philips electronics of cheating - Indian Express
Content:
Department of Museums contemplates installing tight security system at the palace

The Sakkar Baug museum – located in the heart of the Junagadh Zoo – will be shifted to the Taj Manzil palace.

Though the specific reason for the shift is not known, it is speculated that as the visitors to the museum had to pay fee even for zoo, it kept them away.

The new location of the museum is spacious and will also help the department to display the two centuries-old nawabi treasure more effectively.

"Earlier, the museum was located in an 11,000-square-foot area, whereas in the Taj Manzil, the display area is as big as 22,000 square feet. And the palace, with its ivory flooring, furniture and staircases, is itself a museum," said S N Pandey, Director of the State Department of Museums.

In addition to shifting the artefacts from the Sakkar Baug museum, the nawabi treasure from 17th to 19th century will be kept on display.

"The treasure and belongings of all the nine nawabs of Junagadh have been kept with the Junagadh collector. All these things will be displayed in the museum in various categories," said Pandey.

"The collection of Rs 10 and Rs 2 as fee from the visitors of the zoo and the museum does not matter. But this new place will certainly get more tourists as it is centrally located and it can be accessed more easily," said Pandey.

Taj Manzil was earlier occupied by the Junagadh Ayurvedic College before it shifted to Ahmedabad. The Department of Museums is in the process of signing an MoU with a Delhi-based company to install heavy security system in the museum.

"The display of such priceless artefacts calls for heavy security. We will be incorporating the latest security measures, including bullet-proof showcases, alarm system, and cameras," said Pandey.

Sources said the old Sakkar Baug museum will be converted into a conservation lab for museum artefacts.

Heading: Maharashtra gains foothold in Gujarat co-op bank sector - Indian Express
Content:
Says the company installed 108 X-Ray, CT scan machines in hospitals without obtaining type approval

The state government on Wednesday lodged a complaint with police against Philips Electronics India Private Limited (PEIL) accusing it of violating radiation protection rules while installing X-Ray and CT scan machines in government hospitals across Gujarat.

In a complaint lodged with the Sector 7 police station in Gandhinagar, Dr J L Meena, State Quality Assurance Officer attached to the Health Commissionerate, said that PEIL had supplied as many as 108 X-Ray and CT scan machines to the government in 1998.

The company installed them in 23 district-level hospitals and six medical colleges of Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat, Rajkot, Bhavnagar and Jamnagar.

In the complaint, Meena said the private firm had failed to obtain the type approval certificate from the Atomic Energy Regulations Board (AERB) before supplying and installing the equipment, the police said.

They added that PEIL senior director Anjan Bose has also been named in the complaint.

He said that although PEIL had supplied and installed the equipment in government hospitals about 10 years ago, the lapse was detected only a few days ago when he visited the office of the AERB in Mumbai.

"During my visit, I learnt from a board official that PEIL had not obtained a quality check approval from it before installing the machines. This prompted us to file a complaint of cheating against the company," he told Newsline after filing the complaint.

The Health official said in the complaint that the company had also failed to get the machines duly checked for quality assurance as mandated under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962. Not only this, PEIL also violated Radiation Protection Rules, he alleged in the complaint, the police added.

Meena alleged that this lapse on the part of the company could have inflicted diseases to patients such as blood and skin cancer, and posed health hazards to pregnant women while undergoing X-Ray or CT scan tests.

He said: "This is the first instance in the country wherein a state government has lodged a police complaint against a private firm for flouting relevant rules and conditions under the Atomic Energy Act and that of the AERB."

To a query, Meena said the possibility of replacing the machines could not be ruled out.

"Our Health Department cannot play with the lives of people, including those who operate the X-Ray and CT scan machines in these hospitals," he said.

Heading: Asbestos-related diseases give tough time to Gujaratis - Indian Express
Content:
Certain provisions stop Gujarat banks from expanding their network and shareholder base

The fall of Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank (MMCB) in 2001 following the Ketan Parekh securities scam had a cascading effect on the financial health of nearly 60 urban co-operative banks (UCBs) in Gujarat.

Some went in liquidation while many others are struggling to survive. Despite the apex bank's policy of encouraging mergers and acquisitions, most good banks in the state have by and large remained disinterested in taking over of weaker banks. The reason: Strong banks do not want to take the burden of additional financial liabilities, unwanted stakeholders and existing employees.

This gave a much-desired opportunity to the multi-state co-operative banks of Maharashtra to gain a foothold in Gujarat's co-operative banking sector. So far, Maharashtra banks have acquired nearly half a dozen UCBs of Gujarat.

The major banks evincing interest in Gujarat for expansion of their network are Cosmos Bank, Kapol Bank, Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank, Nasik Merchants Bank and Saraswat Bank. The banks fancied them were erstwhile Co-operative Bank of Ahmedabad, Manekchowk Co-operative Bank, People's Co-operative Bank, National Co-operative Bank and the latest being Nutan Sahakari Bank.

Banking sector sources say that certain provisions stop Gujarat-based UCBs from expanding their network and shareholder base. They say that only an urban bank can take over another urban bank. The RBI does not sanction the acquisition of an urban bank by a state co-operative bank.

According to Jyotindra Mehta, chairman of the Gujarat Urban Co-operative Bank Federation, big banks like Cosmos and Abhyudaya are keen to acquire UCBs of Gujarat. "Gujarat is safe and best for expanding banking business after Maharashtra where they have already grown," he said

National Co-operative Union president Ghanshyam Amin says the state's UCBs are not in favour of taking over weak banks as they do not want to take up financial liabilities and staff of weak banks. "Post merger, they will have to accommodate new shareholders, meaning one more pressure group capable to disturb the voting pattern and ultimate change in power equations," said Amin.

Amin, who is also a former chairman of the erstwhile Co-operative Bank of Ahmedabad which merged into Cosmos Bank, Pune, said that with such a mindset, even banks with some surplus funds are unwelcome.

"On the other hand, Maharashtra banks got ready branches with existing accounts, which are otherwise hard to come by in the present age of competition. Also, Gujarat is any day a good business destination for the co-operative sector," he said.

Heading: After Makwana, Lalji Mer follows suit; likely to join BJP on Nov 21 - Indian Express
Content:
"It has been a disgusting life," says Manga N Patel, sitting on the lone bench at a tea stall in Parshavnath Nagar locality of Chandkheda in Ahmedabad. With tears rolling down his face, Patel walks away saying he is in no mood to talk further. Similar has been the response of scores of other people working in factories which use asbestos.

The case in question is a recently published dossier titled 'India's Asbestos Time Bomb' by the renowned International Ban Asbestos Secretariat (IBAS) that has termed Gujarat as the 'Asbestos Hot Spot.'

The dossier, which was circulated at the recently concluded fourth meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP-4) of the UN's Rotterdam Convention on the Prior Informed Consent (PIC) Procedure in Rome, lists the 'Golden Corridor' of Gujarat as the major hub for asbestos use.

The corridor stretching from Mehsana in north to Vapi in south, housing over 31,000 working factories, has a routine occupational exposure to asbestos in power generation, ship-breaking, cement production, insulation, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, friction materials and safety equipment factories.

The dossier mentions power generation industries like the Ahmedabad electricity corporation (now known as Torrent Power) as widely using asbestos for boilers and furnaces. Although there are cases like Patel, a former boiler room operator, being paid Rs 1.60 lakh by the company as the out-of-court settlement amount, cases of compensation for the Asbestos Related Disease (ARD) victims are far and few between.

Also, due to the widespread availability of limestone in Gujarat, there are a lot many industries manufacturing asbestos cement sheets. The IBAS names Shree Digvijay Cement Company Limited, Ahmedabad as the main culprit in this regard. Up till now, the Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has compensated eight individuals for ADR. All of them were workers of the Digvijay Cement.

Ship-breaking is another source of asbestos exposure to workers, most famous being the site at Alang near Bhavnagar. The controversy surrounding Clemenceau and Blue Lady, carrying asbestos waste and radioactive materials, is still fresh in the public memory.

'ARDs claim more lives than any other work-related illness'

According to the IBAS, India employs nearly one lakh workers in both organised and unorganised sectors of the asbestos industry, with majority of them in Gujarat. The cumulative asbestos consumption in India between 1960 and 2008 is estimated to exceed the seven-million-tonne mark. It is also estimated that ADRs like malignant mesothelioma, asbestos-related lung cancer and asbestosis kill more people than any other work-related illness. Although blue and brown asbestos are banned, white asbestos continues to be used in India. But what is most shocking is the stance taken by the Indian Government along with Canada and Russia at COP-4, by vetoing the inclusion of chrysotile on the PIC list. The inclusion would have made it mandatory for the exporters to provide information to the importing countries on the hazards posed by the chemicals to both the human health and environment.
—ENS

Supreme Court's January 1995 ruling
The Supreme Court, in response to a public interest litigation filed by the Consumer Education and Research Centre, passed an order on January 21, 1995, which included:

* Maintenance of health records for 40 years since employed or 15 years after leaving employment (in the asbestos industry)
* National Institute of Occupational Hazard should decide on diagnoses in case of disputes
* Rs 1 lakh compensation to be paid to the asbestos-related disease victims
* Special monitoring of small-scale asbestos manufacturing units
* Regular reviews of permissible limits for asbestosSetting up membrane filter test facilities for measuring dust levels
— ENS

— (With inputs from Parimal Dabhi)

Heading: With Dholai port still not in sight, no respite for fishermen in south Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
Sounding the bugle of revolt by resigning from the party, senior Dalit leader of the Congress Yogendra Makwana seems to have motivated many other disgruntled partymen to quit the party.

Now, senior Congress leader Laljibhai Mer, a prominent Koli community representative from Surendranagar in Kathiawad region, has decided to leave the party. While Makwana has floated his own National Bahujan Congress party, others have opted for the BJP keeping in view its 'bright future' in the state.

Laljibhai is likely to join the saffron party at a function in Surendranagar on November 21 in the presence of BJP state president Parsottam Rupala. While Rupala could not be contacted, Surendranagar district BJP leaders as also the sources in the state BJP office confirmed that Lalji is all set to join them.

Congress sources, too, confirmed of Laljibhai leaving the party. According to sources close to him, the Koli leader does not expect to get the party ticket for the Surendranagar Lok Sabha seat in the forthcoming elections. The Congress will be fielding BJP MP Somabhai Patel from Surendranagar in return for his support to the UPA government during the trust vote in the Lok Sabha, sources said. Somabhai was subsequently suspended from the BJP for violating the party fiat.

Two days ago, the entire Dahod district Congress unit, including district Congress president Bijal Damor, walked en masse into the BJP-fold. The Congress had already weakened considerably in the tribal-dominated district when the BJP won this Lok Sabha seat in the last polls.

According to the Congress sources, several top party leaders in Vadodara, the political hub of central Gujarat, are in touch with the BJP in a bid to join the ruling party. A highly placed source in the Vadodara Congress said these leaders did not expect good future of the Congress, so they are contemplating an exodus.

On the disgruntled elements leaving the party, chief spokesperson Arjun Modhwadia said the Congress would not lose anything politically with these people leaving. Makwana, he said, was given Lok Sabha ticket thrice but lost the polls on all three occasions. Similarly, Laljibhai lost the last general elections from Surendranagar. "Such people need not be retained in the party," he added.

Meanwhile, the Dalit leaders in the Congress launched a scathing attack on Makwana, describing him as a critic of Dr B R Ambedkar. Congress MLA Shailesh Parmar said that Makwana in his book 'Kapada Chadan', had also criticised Mahatma Gandhi.

Heading: Pak marine officials arrest 16 Indian fishermen, seize three boats - Indian Express
Content:
Rana Kharva is a 40-year-old fisherman from Valsad. He has to sail to Mumbai regularly, which is over 150 nautical miles from his place, to sell his catch.

This is despite the existence of a fishing port in nearby Dholai.

Kharva is not alone: another 2,000 of his kind daily burn extra fuel to reach Mumbai. They have been waiting for the Dholai port to become functional, which was inaugurated by Chief Minister Narendra Modi in 2006. The wait seems to be far from over.

The State Fisheries Department has been losing revenue in lakhs every month to neighbouring Maharashtra because of this. The two departments—fishing and maritime board—are to be blamed for this. Even after two years of the formal inauguration of the port, they have failed to put up basic facilities required to begin operations.

The port is jointly funded by the Central and state governments. It is constructed by Gujarat Maritime Board and managed by Gujarat Fisheries Department. The Dholai project was worth Rs 15 crore and was touted as a boon for four districts of south Gujarat—Valsad, Navsari, Bharuch and Surat—where fishing is one of the major economic activities.

But despite having most of the major facilities including jetty, berthing, auction hall, gear shed and boat parking area with a capacity of 800 boats, the port remains non-functional.

"When functional, Dholai port can initially generate revenue of approximately over Rs 2.5 lakh per month for Navsari fishing circle office," said D K Patel, Assistant Director, Fisheries, Navsari region.

Even today, it is not clear when the port will be operational, for internal roads and sweet water system for cleansing fish have not been constructed.

"There are over 2500 boats among the four districts of south Gujarat. For more than 10 lakh people living here, fishing earns their bread and butter," said Suresh Kharva, a fishing board member.

He added, "First, there was no port in all these years. Now, there's a dedicated fishing port, which has been inaugurated but not operational."

Most of the fishermen have found markets in Mumbai. Some also operate from other ports in Gujarat including Porbandar and Veraval. But that just adds up to their expenditure.

"We have to bear extra transportation charges per trip for going to Mumbai. Sometimes, we have to spend extra time and money to find agents to secure best deals in our neighbouring state," said Rana.

The Fisheries Department has been unable to decide on the source of sweet water; planning and designing of the water supply project is still a far cry.

"The department has been thinking over to bring water either from near by water supply scheme at Devda or dig bore wells in the port premises itself," said Patel.

While Devda water supply is located 10 km away, the department is yet to check the feasibility of the bore well project.

Heading: Senior advocate alleges misuse of govt housing by High Court judges - Indian Express
Content:
The Pakistani Marine Security Agency (PMSA) arrested 16 Indian fishermen and seized three boats near Kori creek in Jakhau waters in the Arabian Sea bordering Pakistan on Wednesday.

"Sixteen fishermen were arrested and are lodged in a jail in Karachi," said National Fishing Forum Secretary (Gujarat), Manish Lodhari.

With this, the total number of fishermen arrested in the last three years has gone up to 450 and the number of boats seized to 382, said sources.

According to Lodhari, the arrested fishermen hail from coastal belts of Diu, Wanakbara and Mangrol. All the three seized boats had Porbandar registration. "The arrests were made in wee hours. Our counterparts in Pakistan confirmed that they [Indian fishermen] were brought in Karachi on Thursday," said Lodhari.

The arrest on Wednesday happened a fortnight after the first-ever delegation of Gujarat Government failed to get release of Indian fishermen lodged in Pakistani jails. The delegation that visited Pakistan in mid-October had comprised boat owners, fishermen and a government official.

While the delegation's request to meet Indian fishermen in Karachi jail was turned down by the Pakistan Government, they also found that more than half of Indian boats in possession of the Pakistan government were auctioned off by its marine agency. The Indian Coastal Guard authorities have requested the Gujarat Fisheries department to ensure that fishermen carry proper documentation while going out in the sea, said sources. If lapses were found during on-board checking of Indian trawlers at high sea, the fishermen would be sent back to the shore to face legal action, they said.Fish-rich Jakhua is a major activity zone in the Arabian Sea and so is the adjoining area in Pakistani waters. Fishermen take all necessary precautions while going to Jakhua so as to not to stray into Pakistani waters, said Velji Masani, vice-president of National Fishing Forum.

Heading: Old is gold: Veteran litterateur traces history of Shukravaari Bazaar - Indian Express
Content:
While arguing a case before Justice Kalpesh Jhaveri of the Gujarat High Court on Tuesday, senior advocate Yatin Oza pointed out that there are high court judges who had either retired or resigned, but are still occupying their official accommodations in contravention of the law.

Oza was arguing a case pertaining to raising the rent of his client R V Rathwa, a constable in the railway police. Rathwa, who had been transferred from Ahmedabad to Viramgam, had retained the accommodation in the railway colony in Asarwa for his family and children.

Although he had joined office at the new place immediately after his transfer on June 9, 1986, he did not vacate the house, as his children were studying in Ahmedabad. Owing to his failure to vacate the house, the Railways increased his house rent by Rs 200 per month and claimed an amount of Rs 10,000 from him for a period between September 1, 1986 and December 12, 1990. He moved the court seeking the quashing of the railway order.

While representing Rathwa in the court, Oza argued that the law must apply equally to everybody whether a constable or a judge. He told the court that there were at least two judges of the high court—Justice B J Sethna and Justice J N Bhatt—who were still occupying government accommodation even though they had left service. While one of them had resigned in April 2007, the other retired as chief justice of the Patna High Court on July 19, 2005.

Justice Sethna had resigned in April 2007, following a controversy involving physical attack on another judge. But he continues to occupy a palatial bungalow in the Judges Bungalow Colony in Bodakdev. Justice Sethna, however, refused to comment.

Justice J N Bhatt had retired as chief justice of Patna High Court on July 19, 2005, yet he is occupying a government bungalow in Shahibaug.

Heading: Indus Saraswati Trust Heritage project gains momentum - Indian Express
Content:
During the rule of the Gaekwads, Shukravaari Bazaar or Friday flea market extended from Harni Road till the Collectorate office. Newsline accompanies veteran poet and writer, Aziz Qadri in a walk down the memory lane, as he traces the history of the market and reminisces his own life vis-à-vis the market.

If the various historical records of Baroda are to be believed, the Shukravaari Bazaar has been there since the Gaekwads started ruling Baroda. "After constructing four gates in the early 19th century, Fatehsinh Gaekwad I had allotted land outside the gates to the poor for living as well as trading in the area," said Aziz Qadri (76), who has been writing about Vadodara from various references. The market soon spread to the Harni side and a cattle market also started on the other side.

The original vendors in the market were blacksmiths, cloth merchants and farmers. Smithy was not found outside Baroda, which is why the city was considered a hub for iron implements. Interestingly, sources reveal that prostitution in the form of "playhouses" also flourished near the market, underlining the liberal nature of Shukravaari Bazaar. "The vendors coming from distant places would make merry in these houses. The playhouses never created any problem," said Qadri.

In 1942, there was communal trouble in the market. "It was a rare one, but with the intervention of the king, Sir Sayaji Rao Gaekwad, the trouble was brought under control in half-an-hour and the market resumed functioning," recalled Qadri, who was present during the trouble.

Cloth merchants had a separate space in the market. Records show that before independence, around 200 cloth vendors used to do business at the same space where Padmavati Shopping Complex stands now. Sir Sayaji Rao Gaekwad wanted to build a garden from Jubilee Baug to Nyay Mandir surrounding the present Sur Sagar Lake. The presence of cloth merchants close to the garden would have attracted commoners to the market. "However, in 1947, after Partition, the space was given to refugees for their makeshift shelters," Qadri added.

It is this market again that opened the doors of the world of literature to Qadri.

"I started going to the market with my grandfather when I was eight. We would buy sweets and paper for my copies," recalled Qadri, who later found all his favourite books and writing pens in the market. Nearly 80 per cent of books in the personal library of this winner of several literary awards in Urdu and Gujarati were acquired from Shukarvaari Bazaar.

As a child, Qadri would count the number of carts bringing produce from Padra, Savli and Karjan. His visits to the market became frequent, as his interest in literature grew. "I was amazed when I found a rare book on Persian language published by a Sanskrit poet from Amreli for Rs 5," he said.

His interest in calligraphy started from this market.

"I bought original German Staedler and Fellowship pens with gold plated nibs for Rs 2," he said showing his pen collection.

He expressed shock over the allegation that goods sold in this market are stolen. "I want to ask what they have done to bootleggers and drug peddlers. It is a proof that Vadodara is a Sanskar Nagari. Now, they are just murdering the city, which is a bigger crime," he said.

Heading: Villagers intensify stir against railway project - Indian Express
Content:
The Indus Saraswati Trust Heritage project seems to be gaining momentum with the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) authorities recently conducting a series of meetings with officials of the Vadodara Revenue Department.

It was during the tenure of Manoj Soni, former MSU Vice-Chancellor, when a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed with the Global Heritage Fund during the last Vibrant Gujarat summit. According to the agreement, a land near Sindhrot was to be allotted for this ambitious project. The deal, however, could not concretise and the new location is yet to be finalised.

Prof Ramesh Goyal, V-C, said: "During discussions with the Global Heritage Fund and Revenue Department officials, suggestion to earmark the land for the project at Sherkhi village was made. However, nothing can be commented till the deal is done on paper. Nearly 30 acres of land is expected to be allotted for this project."

There was some opposition from the farmers at Sherkhi, which now seems to have been sorted out, said Goyal, adding, "I have been talking to the concerned authorities regularly."

According to varsity officials, the state government is showing a keen interest in the project as it is also a party to the MoU besides MSU and the Global Heritage Fund.

The deal, which is expected to take shape by 2012, will have significant role of MSU's Archeology department.

The artifacts and materials excavated from the Indus Valley are expected to be installed in the museum as well as at the center for excellence for research on the Indus Valley. All the works of art are excavated by the Archeology department, MSU.

Heading: AMC to attend Shanghai World Expo 2010 - Indian Express
Content:
In what could prove to be a turning point in the movement launched by the people of 31-odd villages against the Indian Railways' Dedicated Freight Corridor project, representatives of Vadodara District Farmers' Society met Minister of State for Railways, Naran Rathwa, and Gujarat state Congress President Siddharth Patel.

Hasmukh Bhatt, President of Vadodara District Farmers' Society, said they have written a letter to Railways authorities against the project. The seven-point letter says that most of the people affected by the project do not own anything other than their land plots.

It also brings out the fact that almost all the land plots have been acquired by Vadodara Urban Development Authority (VUDA) for their mega city project.

According to Bhatt, VUDA has marked a 640-meter road passing through one of the villages in Vadodara district for project.

Meanwhile, the Railways officials have taken the argument by the action committee into consideration.

However, they said the whole movement has been instigated by the builders lobby in the city.

Heading: On duty, traffic cop killed in accident - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) will take part in the Shanghai World Expo 2010 in China between May 1 and October 31, 2010. Senior AMC officials currently in China are expected to work out the participation details on their return.

Municipal Commissioner I P Gautam said on Wednesday that the AMC would be among 100 cities taking part in the expo where participants would deal with the urban development scenario, technology transfer and technology parks during the six-month period. The details will be worked out on return of officials in a couple of days, he said.

The expo will have a 500-day countdown from December 17 this year. "We are getting a grant of 0.3 million dollars from the Shanghai government for participation in the event, which will have a buyer-seller meet in the areas of modern technology from around the world," he said. The expo will give China a chance to bring the world at its doorstep in a major way.

Incidentally, May 1, 2010 – the launch date of the expo – coincides with 50 years of foundation of Gujarat, which has set golden goals of progress to mark the occasion. The expo will give the state an opportunity to showcase its growth at the world forum, where 70 million people are expected to visit over a period of six months.

When asked as to what this event will mean to the AMC in terms of gaining a mileage in the world forum, Gautam said the benefits are yet to be ascertained in the light of opportunities coming its way. He said the participation would be under the guidance of and in consultation with the state government.

China had officially decided nine years ago that Shanghai would bid for the 2010 World Expo. Shanghai won the bid on December 3, 2002, at the 132nd General Assembly of the International Exhibitions Bureau, which was established by a diplomatic international convention signed in Paris in 1928. Its function is to regulate the frequency and quality of exhibitions.

Heading: Trade union workers formulate module for enforcing ban on smoking - Indian Express
Content:
The assistant sub-inspector was transferred to Kathlal 6 months ago

In a shocking incident, a truck mowed down a 52-year-old traffic policeman near Moti Sapar village in Kheda district on Tuesday evening.

According to Kathlal Town police Inspector P L Patil, the incident occurred around 6.15 pm when the victim, Assistant Sub-Inspector Chandu Rupaji, was performing his duty.

After finishing his shift on Tuesday evening, Rupaji was going home when the truck hit him from behind. Rupaji died on the spot, the police said.

"Truck driver Raju Vasava was also injured in the accident. Vasava is undergoing treatment at a Kathlal dispensary. We will arrest him as soon as he is released from there," said Patil.

"Around six months ago, Rupaji was transferred to Kathlal," said Patil. The Kathlal police said that previously, Rupaji was posted at Harsol village in Sabarkantha.

Rupaji is survived by three daughters and two sons.

Heading: Two nabbed with 13 kg charas, sent to judicial custody - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the special committee's efforts to implement the Supreme Court order banning smoking in public and workplaces have mellowed down, trade union members on Wednesday formulated nine ways of making workplaces smoke-free.

A congregation hosted by Bejon Mishra, Executive Director of Delhi-based Consumer Voice, and city-based NGO, Faith Foundation, brought together 42 trade union members to bring in the perspective of factory workers in formulating modules of implementing the ban on smoking in public places in an orderly manner.

After the daylong discussion, the trade union members formulated the strategies by which the 'no smoking rule' can be curtailed among the workers and in work places. "A rule, when enforced on someone, is bound to be broken. It is better to understand the psyche of the people and mould the ban in them as a behaviour," said Mishra.

Although it has been over a month since the ban on smoking has been enforced across the country, the result has not been very encouraging. In a recently filed RTI application by the Faith Foundation, it was found that no strict implementation or positive results have been noticed in six cities of Gujarat after the rule was imposed. In Vadodara, however, over 92 cases have been registered till date.

"It will not work well unless people themselves realise that by smoking they are not just killing themselves but also others around them," said Anant Christian, who heads Faith Foundation.

In the meeting, trade union members stressed on bringing together the owners and workers in industries and work places while implementing the ban. They also opined that an active member in every department must be identified to monitor the issue, sensitise the workers and also take strict action. This should reach workers in villages and slums as well, they opined.

"The workers should be made to take this ban just as seriously as it is to wear uniform in office," said Keshu Thakkar, president of Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS).

The organisations will approach the state government with the nine modules formulated at the convention for statewide implementation.

Heading: Schools to have pure drinking water under Central project - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahmedabad zone unit of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) arrested two persons with nearly 13 kg of charas near Vadodara late on Monday.

The duo has been booked under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and sent to judicial custody.

Acting on a tip-off, the NCB sleuths nabbed Dinesh Kumar Yadav, a resident of Rajasthan, and Inayat Rasul Miya Sheikh, a resident of Vadodara, with a consignment of 2.3 kg of charas at Dumad Chowkdi, near Express Highway in Vadodara. The arrests were made when Sheikh had come to receive the contraband material from Yadav.

"Further interrogation resulted in the additional recovery of about 10.5 kg of charas from Sheikh's residence," said Ayush Mani Tiwari, NCB zonal director.

The NCB also seized Rs 61,270 and the motorcycle used by Sheikh for collecting the contraband goods.

Sources in the NCB said that Sheikh has been in the business of charas trafficking for several years now.

In 1996, he was sentenced to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment on similar charges. He, however, seemed to have started the business again after coming out from the jail, sources said.

Heading: Man held for raping minor - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre sponsored 'Jalmani' project, which aims to provide potable water facility in government schools in rural areas, will be inaugurated in Gujarat on November 14.

State's Water Supply Minister Nitin Patel will inaugurate the project at Madal village in Tharaj taluka of Banaskantha. The same day, state's Education Minister Ramanlal Vora and Forest and Environment Minister Kirit Rana will dedicate a system at Badoli village in Idar taluka of Sabarkantha, and Bhalgamda village in Limbdi in Surendranagar district respectively.

In the first year of the project, one-lakh water purification system units will be installed across schools in the country, with help from the respective state governments. In Gujarat, the Water and Sanitation Management Association will implement the project in three schools, in association with the gram panchayat, village education committee and primary teachers association.

According to a Gujarat State Information Bureau release, each system with a capacity of purifying1,000 litres per day will cost Rs 40,000, including operation and maintenance cost for the first five years. Water thus purified will cost 3 paise per litre. The respective schools will own the systems.

Heading: Fantastic five - Indian Express
Content:
A minor girl was allegedly kidnapped and then raped by her neighbour near Kim village in Surat district on Monday afternoon. The accused, Raju Thakur (37), was arrested on Wednesday on charges of kidnapping and rape.

According to police, a member of the Shrivastav family, the victim is four-year-old and a resident of Yoginagar society in Katargam.

On Monday, when the girl was playing outside her house, Thakur took her to Kim village where he raped her, said the police.

The victim's father searched for her in the nearby areas and learnt from his neighbours that his daughter was last seen with Raju Thakur.

On failing to spot Thakur, the family lodged a kidnapping complaint against him with the Katargam police. The accused works as a textile worker in a private firm at Katargam GIDC.

On returning home, the girl narrated the story to her family following which the family caught Raju from his house and handed him to the Katargam police.

During interrogation, Raju confessed to have committed the crime. He said he was heavily drunk at the time of the act.

The girl and the accused were sent to the SMIMER Hospital for medical examinations.

Katargam Sub-Inspector V S Kolcha said, "The medicals reports are awaited."

Heading: Bay Watch - Indian Express
Content:
Vijay Tendulkar's new compilation of plays for children shows he wasn't just inspired by politics

Forty years ago, Vijay Tendulkar used to attract a very young audience. As they applauded, six of his plays—written especially for children—enjoyed the spotlight. Since their stage run wasn't long enough, these plays soon faded into obscurity. Now, five of them are staging a comeback, albeit in print.

The book, simply called Five Plays for Children, is translated by Pune-based Ajay Joshi and published by Scholastic. In its introduction, Joshi says, "Much has been written about Tendulkar's plays and the playwright himself, but little is available on the six plays he wrote for children."

It isn't difficult to find the reason behind it. "These plays seem to have been tucked away from the arc lights, overpowered by the powerful presence of his path-breaking adult writings," the translator adds. Joshi, who started translating the plays into English early last year, had to work on retaining the original flavour, pun and nuances in English.

Another challenge was to unravel what Tendulkar wanted to communicate. Interestingly, the period when the legendary playwright wrote the plays coincides with the creation of some his greatest plays like Gidhade, Shantata! Court Chalu Aahe and Sakharam Binder. "Tendulkar wrote the children plays in the 1960s and the early 70s," says Joshi. So many find it incredulous that the dramatist who appeared to be such a harsh critic of the society, could come up with plays are so gentle. Tendulkar's sixth play for children couldn't be included in the collection as Joshi couldn't trace it in time.

It's Sulabha Deshpande who made Tendulkar write these plays. The actor, who was teaching at the Chabbildas School, Dadar, was part of the theatre movement to move away from the traditional musical theatre. Tendulkar too, was involved in this movement of presenting more relevant and realistic theatre. Deshpande urged the late dramatist to write plays for her school so that her students could take part in competitions. Deshpande says that coming from Tendulkar, the plays were amazingly "simple and straightforward".

Joshi, however, has a different take on it. "The plays have the Tendulkar touch—with multiple layers." For each play, Tendulkar adopted a distinct form and context. "He used the idioms of folk theatre for The King and Queen Want Sweat (Raja Ranila Gham Hava). This is said to be the precursor to Sakharam Binder," Joshi says.

The book has four more plays— The Wedding of the Village Headman's Daughter (Patlachya Poricha Lageen), Bobby's Story (Bobbychi Goshta), The Play of the Nosey Parker (Chambhar Chaukashiche Natak) and Missing: A Father (Baba Haravale Ahet).

Though these plays were not widely staged, Awishkar Theatre Group has produced them in the past. In fact, the memory-tickling black-and-white images of the plays in the book are sourced from the group. The collection's cover serves as another pointer to the plays; the illustrations on it are inspired by the characters of the plays.

Heading: Waxing Lyrical - Indian Express
Content:
John Abraham on homosexual films and playing gay

Whose idea was it to make you wear yellow swimming trunks?
I wanted to wear black trunks and come out of the Miami water but Karan Johar, a marketing maverick, insisted on yellow. He told me the colour will make a difference. I remember when we shot the scene; Karan told me that this will be the shot of the film.

Did you have any reference point for the shot?
When I was walking out of the water, I wanted it to be just like Daniel Craig in Casino Royale. He looked so cool; he wasn't showing off his body. It looked as if this is what he does everyday. I wanted to evoke the same response so I refrained from flexing that would have made me look like a bodybuilder.

How did you take this whole 'Bromance' angle in Dostana?
I didn't even think about it. I was so convinced with the script that I had no qualms in getting in the rhythm of the whole 'pretending to be gay' thing. Also since Abhishek Bachchan and I are such good friends off-screen, there wasn't any awkwardness between us.

Not even when you're doing a close dance with Abhishek?
Not even then. I was so comfortable with him. I'm so glad it was Abhishek. He's such a great guy and made the whole experience of Dostana so special for me.

So are you ready to do a full-on gay film, like Brokeback Mountain?
If I'm convinced about the script and the role, I have no qualms. I'd love to do a film like Milk where Sean Penn plays a gay activist. You know, a homosexual film can be more than just about two guys kissing. It can be about a cause too like Philadelphia.

If the role demanded would you kiss a man on-screen?
I haven't thought about it. I'll cross this bridge when I come to it.

Do guys make passes at you?
It does happen and I deal with it the same way I would if a woman had made a pass at me. I respect them but I'm awkward at accepting compliments anyway. I just give my crooked smile and move on.

What does girlfriend Bipasha Basu think of your gay act?
She loves the songs. She is excited to see the film. Bipasha has always been bang-on about my films. She has a very good feeling for Dostana.

Must say your dancing skills have improved tremendously especially in the Desi Girl track. What happened?
I had gulped down a drink called Energize and it was as good as 20 cups of coffee. My choreographer, Farah Khan, told me to go all out and I did. Later on, she told me that it looked as if I was possessed.

When is Aashayein releasing?
It's a very small film, made with Rs 3 crore. Aashayein needs the right kind of a release and a separate marketing strategy. It just keeps getting pushed because we don't want to release it between the biggies. I've given it my blood, sweat and energy for over a year. It's a very special film for me and I'm dying to see how the audience reacts to it.

What changes have you observed in yourself in the five years that you've been in the industry?
I'm still unsure about myself. There has been no change in my mindset. I guess, every actor yearns to create a space for himself which I've succeeded in. Some actors are on the X axis and some on the Y, John Abraham is on the Z axis. My audience likes me. People tell me I'm a star. But I yearn to be known as a good actor that's why I do films like No Smoking, Zinda, Water and Kabul Express. Today my audience knows what is a John Abraham film.

What is a John Abraham film?
It has to have an edge. It can be a total psycho crazy film like No Smoking that nobody understood or it can be an edgy romantic comedy like Dostana. I just want to experiment; if it's a highway then I'm an off-roader.

Heading: A big bite - Indian Express
Content:
Prasoon Joshi talks about his songs in Ghajini and how interfering Aamir Khan is

In B-town, everyone is on song, even if it is a shaven, tattooed Aamir Khan who can't remember his phone number. Little wonder, Prasoon Joshi found himself penning poetry for all the brawn and brawl on display in Ghajini. "It is a pacy thriller with a lot of action and high energy, but the songs are extremely important to the narrative," says Joshi who has written five songs, all composed by AR Rahman, for the Khan starrer.

The film is a remake of a Tamil movie that was released three years ago, with songs written by N. Muthukumar, but Joshi says the Hindi soundtrack is completely original. "I did not even listen to the southern version as I did not want to be influenced in anyway," says Joshi, who, however, watched bits of the film to "gather a feel of it".

A little-known fact about ad man Joshi is that he is a trained classical musician who likes to compose and sing as well, but he has given them a miss in Ghajini. "I think it is very important for a lyricist to have a sense of music since it's then that the song shapes up wholly," says Joshi.

He has composed and sung jingles for Alpenliebe and Happy Dent, among others. "But it's not something I'd do for films," he says.

Bollywood has heard enough complaints of Aamir Khan's interference, but Joshi thinks otherwise. "He is a very intelligent man and when he has a suggestion, it's often valid. When it is not, we argue a lot and whoever has a more powerful logic wins. So I'd say there's close understanding and mutual respect that allow us to bounce ideas off each other," he says.

If Joshi's poetry is not enough, then maybe you can watch the songs for another reason — one of them has Khan sporting six different hairstyles. Guess it's all relevant to the narrative.

Heading: BJP sets ball rolling with public meets - Indian Express
Content:
It turns out there's nothing a Mac can't do. Rolling Stone magazine joined hands with Reliance Digital's iStore on Monday to host a workshop on using Apple software to create music. Loy Mendonsa—of the Shankar, Ehsaan and Loy trio—known for spinning magic on the synthesiser, demonstrated the uses of Apple's 'Garage Band' to an audience comprising of the likes of Luke Kenny, Ehsaan Noorani, Gary Lawyer, Uday Benegal, Punjabi rapper Hard Kaur and several young, amateur musicians who interacted with Loy and his son Shane.

Editor Radhakrishnan Nair looked evidently pleased with the whole event.

Showstopper The demonstration is part of a series organised by 'Amplify Your Music', Rolling Stone's initiative to encourage interactions between professional and amateur musicians.

Heading: Election panel looks at new ways to make info available to voters - Indian Express
Content:
"Sugar was Rs 20 per kg earlier but now the Congress wants it to be Rs 50 -- a round figure. Change ka problem nahi hoga." Venkaiah Naidu takes on the Congress on price rise

The Delhi BJP on Wednesday kicked off a series of public meetings. While their main speakers are reserved for the last four days, Sushma Swaraj addressed residents in R K Puram, Sector 7 and Venkaiah Naidu held a rally at Laxmibai Nagar and Gole Market, leaving the crowd in splits with his sharp one liners.

L K Advani will be doing the rounds on November 25 and 26. Hema Malini has given a tentative date for November 24. Star bahu Smriti Irani, meanwhile, is booked for a pre-run on November 21 and 26. Bajrang Dal founder and firebrand Vinay Katiyar will be speaking on November 17 and 18 to build up the campaign early on.

Dr Murli Manohar Joshi, Rajnath Singh, Yashwant Sinha and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi are all booked for the early days.

Himachal Pradesh CM Prem Kumar Dhumal will be in the city to garner support in Northeast and East delhi on November 20.

Naidu Speak
* Naidu said one Congress worker once commented that the price rise was inevitable as "Sab koi ko ek din upar jaana hai, aaj price upar jaa raha hai". To this he said, "Ab Congress ko janta upar bhejega."
* "Congress ka haath aam aadmi ke saath vishwasghaath."
* During their (Congress) time people had only one channel, Doordarshan, which was door se darshan. And during the BJP's time, there is Zee TV, me TV, Maa TV, Aa TV and also late night!"
* "The Congress has too many hands. The right hand proposes, left hand opposes and the mind disposes."
* "The Congress has several drivers. Manmohan on the driver's seat, Sonia on the steering wheel, Lalu on the power brake, another on the clutch and another changing the gears."
— Compiled by Sweta Dutta

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Ramwati Devi - Indian Express
Content:
In the absence of any relevant data, it's anybody's guess as to how many registered voters choose to stay away from the polling booths on Election Day. The Election Commission reckons almost 30 per cent of the electorate does not vote due to lack of information. This also includes many who are turned away from the polling booths for a variety of reasons.

In a bid to set right this sorry state of affairs, the Office of the Chief Electorate Officer will introduce a range of measures aimed at ensuring that all voters have access to important information.

First off, an SMS service will let electors obtain information such as the name of their Assembly constituency, polling station number, serial number in the voter's list and address of the polling booth. "This is the first time we are providing such services, essentially to ensure that voters have all the details before they show up to cast their votes. It will eliminate cases where voters sometimes turn up at the wrong polling booth or take a long time to find their serial number in the list," Satbir Silas Bedi, Chief Electorate Officer, Delhi, said.

The Election Office has tied up with MTNL to provide this service. "We are also discussing this possibility with other mobile service providers, so that more people can avail of the facility," Bedi said.

Also in the offing are plans to set up a call centre for a few days leading up to Election Day. "We will set up a dedicated call centre, where electors can call to get all relevant details," Bedi said.

Not wanting to take any chance when it comes to ensuring a large voter turnout, the Election Office will also set up voter assistance booths near polling stations for the first time. "We are sure this measure will go a long way in streamlining the voting process," a senior officer at the Election Office said.

Help at hand
Voters can send an SMS to 53535 with their election card number to avail information. Alternatively, they can call a hotline number that will soon be launched. Voter assistance booths on polling day will help streamline the process.

Heading: AIIMS docs  threaten stir - Indian Express
Content:
Age: 39 years
Constituency: Vasant Vihar
Profession: Domestic help

For 20 years now, Ramwati Devi has voted for the Congress. That's because Indira Gandhi and her party understood the problems faced by people living in slums, people on the margins, the ones left behind by the new India, she says.

For years, Ramwati, her daughters and husband have worked hard to be able to buy their own house. It still remains a dream, she says.

In the shanty she lives in, the lack of space is one of lesser worries. Clean water and other amenities are lacking and to top it all, she fears she might be evicted and their only dwelling will be demolished, she says.

This year too she will vote for the Congress, hoping that maybe one day, she will get her own home and have enough savings to retire, she says.

On inflation
Buying basics has become such a challenge now, Ramwati says. "Look at the price of tomatoes," she says. "They are skyrocketing." She says her family survives mostly on potatoes and cooks only one meal a day, because they simply can't afford the luxury of two meals.

On housing
Housing for poor and low-income groups is limited and what is available is out of bounds for them. In the slums, basic amenities are lacking and owning a house is a distant dream, she says. "We don't want a mansion," she says. "We only want a proper house."

On education
Ramwati says she is paying through her nose for her son's education at a private school, which charges Rs 300 a month, money that could have gone towards food for the family. Her daughter dropped out of government school. The education wasn't good here so she enrolled her son in a private school, hoping that one day he will find a proper job and move out of the slums, she says.

"If government schools were good, why would I spend so much?" she asks. "The system is bad. It keeps the poor in their misery forever." Any government that takes over must make the education system better, she says.

Heading: Parents hunt for information two days before Modern list - Indian Express
Content:
Resident doctors at AIIMS have threatened to go on a strike starting Saturday, in protest against an advertisement for the recruitment of reserved category candidates issued earlier this week.

The advertisement, issued on behalf of the director of AIIMS, invites applications for 95 posts from SC/ST and OBC candidates, leaving out general category aspirants.

Over 1,200 resident doctors held a general body meeting on Tuesday and decided to stay away from work if need be. "The advertisement is illegal and unconstitutional. The faculty members are also supporting us in this move. How can all vacant posts in the institute be offered under a special recruitment drive? This will make it 100 per cent reservation," Dr Kaushal Kant Mishra, member of Resident Doctors' Association, said.

AIIMS faculty members are planning to take the matter to court.

Heading: DMRC carries on with tank project - Indian Express
Content:
Two days before Modern School distributes forms for admissions to nursery, parents are turning to the Internet for more information.

In a newspaper advertisement on October 22, the school announced it would distribute registration forms only on one day, November 15, between 8.30 am and 1 pm. No other information, on what documents parents need to carry with them on Saturday, has been made available. Other details, including submission dates, too have not been made public.

Officials at the school told Newsline that information on submission dates would be released to parents when they come to collect the forms on Saturday.

And because no other information is available on the admission procedure for the school's Humayun Road and Vasant Vihar branches, parents are increasingly flocking to blogs and online community portals, hoping to find some information. Even if nobody knows this information is accurate.

And in blogosphere, rumours are creating even more confusion. On www.nurseryadmissions.com, a portal launched last year to share information on nursery admissions in the city, parents have started numerous threads, asking others if they know whether they will be called for interactions, interviews, or asked to submit the forms the same day. A post even said the school had changed its dates for distributing forms to November 17.

Elsewhere, rumours that parents will have to submit forms the same day have driven some into frenzy. "I don't know what papers to take with me," one parent said. "Does the birth certificate have to be attested? Should I carry my own diplomas and transfer papers too?"

"Is interview on the same date?" another parent asked on a community portal.

The Directorate of Education (DoE) has said its guidelines must be followed or schools could face action. According to these guidelines, private, unaided and recognised schools must make their admission criteria — the total number of seats in pre-primary classes; total number of seats for students from economically backward sections; date, place, mode of distribution and receipt of registration forms; list of supporting documents needed at time of admission; infrastructure and faculty details; and fee structure — available to the public by November 30.

"Modern School will be done with admissions by that time," Sanjay Singh, a parent seeking admission for his daughter at Modern School, Vasant Vihar, said.

Many schools in the city have openly violated DoE guidelines. In a letter sent to schools earlier this month, the DoE said several schools were flouting rules and such non-compliance would be viewed seriously.

What is causing even more panic is that the school will be distributing forms only for a few hours. It won't be surprising if parents started queuing up early in order to get a form.

Parents should carry these
1. Two copies of attested birth certificates
2. Immunisation card/certificate from the child's doctor
3. Two copies of attested residence proof
4. Diplomas, degree certificates of parents
5. Six copies of the child's photograph and at least two copies each of yours and your spouse's
6. Medical certificate stating the child is in good health

Heading: Police to meet RBI on lax security measures at robbed bank - Indian Express
Content:
Despite HC ruling against riverbed construction, Metro goes ahead with water tank project

Despite the High Court ruling that all constructions on the Yamuna floodplains would be built at the developer's own risk, the Delhi Metro is going ahead with its massive overhead concrete water tank. Located in the middle of the Yamuna banks, it is part of the construction of a depot for the Dwarka-Noida stretch adjoining the two new stations —Akshardham and Yamuna Bank— on the river bank.

The Delhi High Court had recently ruled that "any person raising construction (on the river bank area) was doing so at their own peril".

Environmentalists fighting for legal protection of the river banks say transgressions on the already-choked river bank are increasing day by day. Delhi Metro, however, claims they couldn't find another spot on the line for making the depot (where trains are repaired, washed and housed). It further said that constructing the water tank was "essential'" for the depot.

"We have the permission of the Central Water and Power Institute, Pune, IIT Delhi and the Yamuna Standing Committee for building the stations and the depot. The water-tank we are building is an integral part of the project. Water to clean the trains will be stored here. Most of the water will be recycled, and such a structure could only be made using concrete," said Anuj Dayal, spokesperson, DMRC.

"We did not get a place elsewhere on the Dwarka-Noida line to build the depot and the water-tank. In fact, our original plan was for 80 hectares, but we voluntarily reduced it to 30 hectares, keeping environmental concerns in mind. We have also created a drainage system so that the water can be absorbed by the flood plain. This is a very long line and it might be possible that the DMRC needs to build another depot if this one turns out to be too small," he said.

"It is difficult to understand how the Delhi Metro could not find place either in Noida or elsewhere to build the depot. This is a poor excuse. The river bed is quietly being turned into a large concrete structure. Many structures coming up here are permanent and permission to create such concrete structures only sets forth a multiplier effect," said Manu Bhatnagar, INTACH.

"Despite the fact that there are many cases pending in court regarding protection of the river bed and flood plain, the fact is that they still do not enjoy any legal protection. I filed a PIL in September 2007 for the same, but there is still no clear law on construction on the river bed or flood plains," said environmentalist Vinod Jain.

A recent HC judgment passed by an expert committee set up under the chairmanship of R K Pachauri said, "If the committee finds any construction, complete or incomplete, likely to affect adversely the ecology of the river or the flood plain, an interim report may be submitted."

The High Court further said that the court may pass any order it "may deem appropriate" on the issue and any construction being built on the river bed or flood plain was being built at the builders' "peril".

Heading: Now, evening courts for dispensing bounced cheque cases - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Delhi Police were unable to reach a breakthrough in the Hauz Khas bank robbery case, senior police officers said they would be taking action against the absence of a basic security apparatus in the bank where the robbery occurred.

Joint Commissioner of Police, (Southern Range), Ajay Kashyap said, "There was a serious lack of basic security measures; we are thinking of taking up the issue with the concerned authorities."

"We will have a coordination meeting with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and we will take up this issue in the meeting," Kashyap added. He, however, didn't confirm whether they would be writing to the concerned authorities or not.

Police officers said the bank did not have CCTV surveillance, no alarms and no security guard was present at the time of the incident. "The main security guard at the bank had gone on leave and his replacement too, was absent when the incident occurred," a senior police officer said.

Senior police officers said that as per RBI security guidelines and advisories, every bank should have CCTV cameras installed and alarms in place.

Delhi Police Public Relation Officer Rajan Bhagat said, "We issue advisories to banks from time to time and hold meetings with them regularly to thwart such untoward incidents."
