Meanwhile, the Delhi Police on Wednesday released three sketches of the suspects involved in the Monday robbery.

The sketches have been prepared as per the description provided by eyewitnesses.

On Monday, a few armed assailants had robbed a sum of Rs 7 lakh from a UCO Bank branch and two customers in the bank premises in Hauz Khas. The bold robbery had stunned even police officers as the incident occurred around 4 pm.

A customer present inside the bank, Prakash Chand Negi, was hit on the head with the butt of a gun by one of the assailants as he tried to stop them.

Heading: Committee meets HRD minister for action in spitting incident - Indian Express
Content:
Inaugurating the Delhi judiciary's ambitious project — evening courts for trimming down the pendency of bounced cheque cases— Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan urged young lawyers to take it as an opportunity for honing their legal acumen.

"The evening courts will be an opportunity for young and junior lawyers to have frequent appearances in courts and sharpen their skills as the cases would not involve very high stakes," said Justice Balakrishnan at the inauguration of the six evening courts at the Patiala House Court premises.

The CJI said the huge pile-up of cases at the magisterial courts was "disappointing", adding that the figures displayed the "sad state" of the country's judiciary.

There were more than five lakh cases under the Negotiable Instrument Act pending at subordinate courts in Delhi; every year lakhs of cases get added to them, he said.

Pointing to the existing limited infrastructure at the disposal of the judiciary, the CJI added that evening courts or "double shift" courts would make the most of the existing infrastructure and manpower.

"The ultimate objective is to make best use of the available infrastructure to serve the people," he said.

The Chief Justice of Delhi High Court, Justice A P Shah, who was also present at the ceremony, said the evening courts would employ the alternate dispute redressal method, that is, go for amicable resolution so that cases are settled expeditiously.

"The enthusiasm of litigants and lawyer is evident from the fact that till Tuesday evening, the courts had received 198 requests referral to evening courts," said Justice Shah.

Also present at the function were Justices Mukul Mudgal, Madan B Lokur, District and Sessions Judge Mamta Sehgal and I K Kochhar.

The evening court— ¿ three at the Patiala House complex and another three at Karkardoo—a ¿ will be hearing cases from 5 to 7 pm on working days beginning Wednesday.

The Metropolitan magistrates will decide cases of bounced cheques upto an amount of Rs 25,000 on rotational basis under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Cases will be transferred to them from all magisterial courts in the same complex.

Heading: Chain snatchers strike again in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Disappointed with the Delhi University for taking no action over the spitting incident at the Arts Faculty on November 6, 'University Community', the organisation that hosted the seminar titled 'Communalism, fascism and democracy: rhetoric and reality', met the Human Resource and Development Minister Arjun Singh on Wednesday. In a memorandum submitted to the HRD Ministry, the University Community demanded "stern action against the culprits so that democratic academic atmosphere of debate in the campus is maintained".

On November 6, the ABVP had tried to disrupt a talk by S A R Geelani and a member spat at him twice. The ABVP brigade also broke windowpanes at the venue and hurled abuses at people present.

"We had requested the University Vice-Chancellor to take concrete action, but so far nothing has been done," said Shruti Pandey, a member of the organising committee. She said Arjun Singh expressed surprise over the issue when the team met him and promised to forward the memorandum to the Vice-Chancellor of DU, Deepak Pental.

Members of the University Community said strict action should be initiated against the "attackers" because the disruption of the seminar signifies the fact that democratic space is rapidly shrinking at the university campus and there is a growing intolerance towards differences of opinion.

Arjumand Ara, a teacher at the university said, "The problem is not so much the attack as the university not taking any action against it. If they do not step in and discourage such behaviour, the culture of debate in the university will be put under threat." She added that Arjun Singh urged them to continue organising more such debates in future.

Heading: ‘Spat at Geelani since it’s more humiliating than shooting one dead’ - Indian Express
Content:
NOIDA citizens seem to have no respite from snatchers active in the area. In the latest incident, a 52-year-old woman was dragged over a distance of six feet in broad daylight as two motorcycle-borne assailants snatched two gold chains she was wearing. The woman fainted shortly after the incident.

Around 3.30 pm on Wednesday, two motorcycle-borne assailants followed Santosh Kumari, the victim, and her husband Baburam, residents of Chaura village in Noida. Santosh Kumari said the snatchers dragged her over a few feet, holding her by neck. "I grabbed the T-shirt of one of the assailants, but had to let go after they dragged over a distance of six feet," the senior citizen said.

According to Baburam, the couple was traveling on a motorcycle along with their three-year-old grandson when the incident happened. "We were coming from Faridabad. The assailants started following us from the Nithari turn on a bike and hit our vehicle at the Adobe crossing. My grandson fell off and the motorcycle fell on my leg. I saw my wife grabbing hold of one of the motorcyclists, but she fainted soon after she was dragged."

The couple has registered a complaint at the Sector 24 police station. Commenting on the growing incidents of snatching in the city, Ashok Tripathi, SP (City) said, "We have taken note of the incidents. We will be deploying personnel in plainclothes in the area. Decoy lady constables wearing gold chains will also be deployed, accompanied by two constables in plainclothes to nab the snatchers."

Heading: No truck with BSP after polls: Jaitley - Indian Express
Content:
There is not one Vinay but thousands who want the government to act and ensure a safe environment in the country," says Vinay Singh, who spat on Delhi University lecturer S A R Geelani at a seminar in Arts Faculty last week.

Singh, a Law graduate from Delhi University, claims his "inspiration" for the act — roundly condemned by students, teachers and university Vice-Chancellor Deepak Pental — was the Gandhian Dharam Pal, who passed away recently. "I had had accompanied him (Pal) to the airport two years ago. As we discussed the Indian polity, he told me, 'This country's politics cannot be improved. People have to act and slap those who have turned this country into a joke. If you cannot slap, spit on their faces'. For me, spitting signifies rejection."

Once part of Akhil Bhartiya Vidyarthi Parishad, the BJP's students' wing, Singh said he looked for other platforms to register his angst.

Ajeet, project manager and activist at Govindacharya's office, said Vinay Singh had worked for a few months with the former BJP general secretary during the Bihar movement. "Being a resident of Bihar, he was involved in the movement like many other youths who had worked with Govindacharya," Ajeet said. "But he left soon to join some other group."

A general secretary with the Sri Ram Sena, Singh said when he spat on Geelani, 30 youngsters present at the venue supported him. "I spat because I do not want to indulge in extremism of any sort," he said. "Sadhvi Pragya (accused in the Malegaon blasts case) was taken twice for narco-analysis and lie-detector tests, but those tests have never been performed twice on any terrorist.

"Politicians in this country have stopped on three Ms: mike, mala and manch."

He claimed many ABVP activists joined Sri Ram Sena due to the growing unrest in the youth organisation. Singh has even hit upon a 'logic' to justify such acts: "Evolving innovative ways like spitting, which is more insulting than shooting a man, reduces the danger of a volcanic eruption of suppressed angst against the government." The ABVP, meanwhile, denies any association with the incident.

Heading: Chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
The actor talks about playing a superstar on TV and his Bollywood comeback

What's your character like in Mumbai Calling?
I play Chunky La Funga, the superstar of India in the finale episode of Mumbai Calling. The original character was written for the series Goodness Gracious and it was inspired by my star status during the early '90s. But this time around

Sanjeev Bhaskar wanted me to portray the role and I was more than happy to play a superstar.

This is your debut as an actor on television.
Although I have made appearances for reality shows, technically this is my debut as an actor on TV. It was a totally different experience working with a complete foreign crew. It was shot exactly like a movie, only the cameras used were different. We can term it as a crossover serial. Allan Mckeown who is producing the show has done a fantastic job of putting this programme together.

How was it working with Bhaskar?
He is laugh-a-minute. There is never a dull moment when he is around and he makes sure shooting is as much fun. I have been friends with him from the days of Goodness Gracious and Kumars at No 42. But I have never managed to get tired of his jokes. The only other person I can compare him to is Navjot Singh Sidhu.

Do you have plans of doing more shows on television?
I was highly appreciated for my stint as judge in Zara Nachke Dikha. Star has now offered me another show, but I am not supposed to divulge any information about it.

You got coloured sunglasses into vogue after Zara Nach Ke Dikha.
When I first entered Bollywood, I had a fetish for sunglasses. Every time I had an outdoor schedule I used to buy these sunglasses but I never got a chance to wear them then. When I was invited to be the judge, I thought why not make good use of them.

You are known for your comic timing. How have you perfected the art?
Maybe it's just inherent. But sadly enough my wife doesn't think I'm funny at all.

You have been termed as the Bangladeshi superstar. Are you still doing films for them?
I have stormed back to Bollywood now. I stopped doing Bangladeshi films long ago. I'm looking to explore Sri Lanka and Nepal. I don't want to leave any neighbouring territory unexplored.

What's happening on the Bollywood front?
I have loads of film offers and my plate is pretty full for the next year or so. I'm doing Khalbali — a film that has 27 comedians. Besides, there is Inder Kumar's Daddy Cool, Shortcut, a couple of films with Mukta Arts, Hello Darling, where I play the character of Elvis from Ulhasnagar, Sankat City and Paying Guest.

Heading: NGOs campaign to draw youth to booths on poll day - Indian Express
Content:
The royal snub
There are several unhappy murmurs doing the rounds at the BJP office about party chief ministerial candidate Vijay Kumar Malhotra's behaviour towards MLAs. With election dates close, enthused MLAs are taking their best workers to Malhotra for words of encouragement. He has, however, rebuffed them with a quiet nod or, at times, without even a second look.

Out of the picture
Television actor Vani Tripathi is rumoured to have been considered as the BJP candidate for New Delhi (versus Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit) and then as front-runner for another seat in the city. However, she is nowhere in the picture now and will be going off to the US to accept a global leadership award. It's been a quick and sudden end to what people thought would be an interesting political debut for the actor and daughter of a Delhi-based Hindi professor.

Pro-incumbency will ensure win: Dikshit
Claiming that dissidence within the Congress would not mar the prospects of her party on November 29, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit on Wednesday lashed out at her detractors, saying only those who did not get tickets were unhappy. She said "pro-incumbency" would ensure a Congress win. "There is nothing on record to suggest that our chances will suffer because of anti-incumbency," she said.

Heading: Sasur vs bahu: BJP's Babbar takes on daughter-in-law - Indian Express
Content:
Two NGOs in the Capital are going the extra mile to draw the city's youth to the polling booths come November 29. This is in addition to efforts being made by the Delhi Electoral Office to involve the youth in voting.

While the electoral office has started broadcasting jingles to promote voting, Jaagore and Exercising Franchise for Good Governance (EFG) have set up websites and helplines that tell you why you should vote and how you can register yourself.

Still in its initial stages, EFG will become fully functional starting November 19, after which it plans to organise "jogs for democracy" at popular parks in the city. On November 27, the NGO plans to organise a human chain with the help of 600 college students, to encourage more people from every strata to vote these elections.

Jaagore, set up in partnership with Tata, has a fully functional website (www.jaagore. com), where one can get voter ID forms and also find out about the nearest polling booth. If that is not enough, one can dial the helpline number provided on the website for more information.

Commenting on the necessity of such an initiative, Vikas Ratanjee, Jaagore coordinator in Delhi, said, "When every service, starting from mobile connections to banking, can have a customer service, then why not something as important as voting? Very soon, we will also start setting up camps at various universities to encourage young voters to participate in elections."

He says more than one lakh people from all over India have registered themselves on the website.

Uttam Prakash of EFG said he took up the initiative after noticing the falling percentage of voters in the Capital.

Heading: Nicole wins over hearts - Indian Express
Content:
In a slight twist to the familiar saas versus bahu saga, the Delhi elections will witness an interesting sasur versus bahu fight.

O P Babbar and daughter-in-law Anita Babbar will contest against each other from the Tilak Nagar Assembly seat. And both Babbars are confident of winning the elections.

"This is my eighth election from this area and I know that the people are with me," O P Babbar says. He is contesting the elections from the BJP side and has never lost an Assembly election from Tilak Nagar.

But daughter-in-law Anita feels that like the United States, there can be a revolution in Tilak Nagar. "When Americans can elect Obama, why can't the people in Tilak Nagar vote outside the BJP?" Anita asks.

O P started his campaign on Wednesday, and hosted a prayer meeting in his house, followed by a community lunch. "I have faith in the Guru Granth Sahib and it is important to take the blessings of the almighty before starting off with the campaign," he says.

His entire family will be busy campaigning the next two weeks. "We have been going from door to door, meeting the women. Both my daughters and daughters-in-law have divided the area for campaigning," O P's wife Janak Babbar says.

O P says the family is with him and not with Anita. "She is like a daughter to me. We had asked her not to contest these elections. It effects the reputation of the family. She is already serving as a Congress councillor and has three-and-a-half years left in the MCD," O P says. "She should not have taken this step."

But Anita says it was a decision made by her party and so here she is. "If the party wants me to contest the elections I will," Anita says. She says she is equally popular with the people. "When I became a councillor there wasn't a single park that had been maintained. I had roads and schools built," she says.

Anita wants to keep her personal life separate from her political life. "I am a literate woman and I know how to deal with politics and personal relations. They are two separate issues," Anita says.

O P says he had flyovers and underpasses built in his constituency long before Anita started her political career. "I have been working in this area from much before Anita was born," he says.

But Anita feels her six-year report card is better than her father-in-law's 40-year report card. "I can tell people what I have done for the area. I have been receiving positive response and I can promise them a better future," she says. "When I became the councillor, the area was facing serious problems in terms of bad roads, choked sewer lines and poorly maintained parks. I have worked in this area and people know me for that," Anita says.

She will start her campaign from November 15.

Choudhary vs Choudhary
Choudhary Raj Singh is busy campaigning in Nangloi and is sure the BJP will win.

In the 2002 MCD elections, he had campaigned for his brother, Choudhary Vijendar Singh, in the area. Vijendar, who was contesting for the Congress, was ill. In 2003, when Vijendar contested the Assembly elections, Raj helped once again. Vijendar won both polls.

Raj is busy campaigning once again but this time, it's for himself. He wanted a ticket to fight the Assembly elections but the Congress refused. "People know me in the area and wanted me to work for them. So I moved to the BJP. Vijendar is like a younger brother. But now we are political rivals," he says. Vijendar agrees it's not personal. "Politics and personal relations cannot be mixed. I respect him," he says.

Heading: All for a losing cause - Indian Express
Content:
Nudging each other and whispering excitedly among themselves, the young tennis players gathered at the DLTA Complex on Wednesday made no pretended attempts at organisation. Despite the repeated calls to order and the requests to fall in line, they had eyes only for the tennis star in front of them.

Nicole Vaidisova, who is in India for a short visit, was scheduled to make an appearance at the Reebok Tennis Clinic to dispense a few tips, and she didn't disappoint. Accompanying her was Indian Olympian Sunitha Rao, and the duo spent a few minutes hitting a few shots around court as necks craned to catch a glimpse of the players. On the occasion, Vaidisova and Rao also gave away a few tennis scholarships, funded by Reebok, to budding talents in the sport.

National women's champion Ratnika Batra, Ankita Bhatia and Tarannum Handa were the recipients of this two-year benefit, and for the icing on the cake, they also got their chance to have a few extended rallies with the players.

Heading: Delhi selectors fight over team’s fitness - Indian Express
Content:
Services pacer Rakesh Kumar's four five-wicket hauls have ended in his team's defeat

The Services team owe a lot to the services left-arm pacer Rakesh Kumar has rendered with his five-wicket hauls, even though all of those efforts have been for a lost cause.

Kumar's latest came during the ongoing match against Vidarbha that spearheaded the visitors' paltry 151 in the first innings-- his fourth five-for in as many matches.

Kumar doesn't relish the enormity of the feat — it's tentatively being termed as a record, although not yet confirmed. He's disappointed for not ending up on the right side of the result despite his figures.

"It started with my debut against Assam last year. Then against Vidarbha, I got another (five-for) with a match total of eight wickets. The next came against Tripura in the first game this season. I don't know whether it's a record or not but with the team losing each of those matches, it's a bit disappointing for sure," says the 25-year old.

Skipper Sumeet Tomar readily discards the for-a-losing-cause argument saying, "If anybody does well with the bat or the ball and the team lose due to the poor performances of the rest, you can't discount his contribution. After all, when you do well, you don't do it so that your team lose."

Interestingly, Kumar says he had never bowled with a leather ball until he joined the Indian Navy six years back. "I used to play tennis ball cricket in Sikar (his hometown in Rajasthan) and joined the Navy through entrance exam in 2002. I used to stay with Krishna Chadra (former services player) and occasionally gave him knocking. He liked the way I bowled and told me to meet the coach (Raghuvir Singh Jhala). I went for the trials and got selected for the Navy team. But there was no vacancy for a pacer in the playing eleven," recalls Kumar.

"In 2005 I played my first one-dayer for Navy. On debut, I was economic but wicket-less. In 2006, I was again picked for the limited-over team, but missed the Ranji squad. In 2007, I finally made it."

Navy coach Raghuvir Singh Jhala, who is also joint-coach of the Services team, calls this so-near-yet-so-far phase a training period for Kumar who was a better volleyball player than cricketer initially. "I first saw him playing volleyball at one of our camps. Then a batsman (Krishna Chadra) told me about his abilities and brought him to the nets. It's his action and the rise he extracted off the pitch that surprised me. Then he underwent a training of one-and-a-half years.

"Now he's become the main bowler of the Services team and can move the ball on any kind of wicket. His back-spin release is an asset for a swing bowler," says Jhala.

Adding to the last point Vidarbha skipper Pritam Gandhe recollects the way Kumar almost single-handedly wrecked his team last year. "Initially, he looked to pitch the ball on a certain spot and once he found it, he started working on the swing. He moved it both ways, confusing the batsmen," approves Gandhe.

It must have been a déjà vu for the Vidarbha batsmen when they again found Kumar almost unplayable in the first innings. But they can take heart in the fact that while Kumar stretches his five-for streak, Services seem all set to maintain their losing record.

Heading: Vidarbha sniff victory after Fazal’s double ton - Indian Express
Content:
Even before Delhi had conceded the first innings lead in their Ranji Trophy match versus Hyderabad in Uppal, the blame game started within the DDCA ranks.

Daggers are out within the selection committee on the issue of the overall fitness standards of the team.

Ashish Nehra could only bowl three overs before pulling his hamstring on Tuesday. This latest injury and the 'reported' niggles of other team members have resulted in the selectors taking potshots at each other.

"The selectors want a complete review of the fitness of the team. We want a detailed report of the team in writing by the physio, once the team returns," Anil Jain, one of the selectors, said.

Adding fuel to the fire, another questioned the fitness standards of others in the team and held the chairman of selection committee, Chetan Chauhan, accountable for "falsifying facts".

"Chetan made us believe that the entire team is fit, but clearly they re are not. Nehra, Awana, Nanda and even Manhas is not fit," he told Sportline.

However, Chauhan has dismissed any suggestion that he was responsible for the "fitness problems" of the team.

"I have not made any commitment on behalf of the team regarding their fitness to the selection committee. These are all false accusations," he said.

"We selected the team based on the fitness assessment of the physio and the captain and the coach's recommendations," he clarified.

Heading: Booked for fun - Indian Express
Content:
Vidarbha opener Faiz Fazal was the quickest to finish with his lunch and slipped into his batting gear before murmuring a prayer. By then he had added 54 runs to his overnight 119, taking his side to an imposing 361-run lead over Services and the quest for a maiden double ton was only an appetizer that kept him itching to take strike.

An hour into the post-lunch session, he came out unbeaten, with a patient 200 off 393 balls, still reluctant to take out his wet helmet. Vidarbha declared at 346 for five extending the target for Services to 421 with four and a half sessions of play left.

In between, came some authoritative sweeps off AK Mohanty, couple of cover drives against Pankaj Kumar followed by customary handshakes from the Services players. It was a chanceless, career-best knock, but still not among Fazal's favourites. "I would rate a couple of 80s against HP and Haryana higher as they came in difficult conditions," asserted the left-hander.

Ominously for Services,Vidarbha pacers Sandeep Singh and Mohammad Hashim had their tails up. Opener Tahir Khan went back early, while Alind Naidu accounted for Madhusudan Reddy. And as skipper Sumeet Tomar, after scoring a half-century, fell to left-arm spinner Madhusudan Acharya in the last over of the day, the hosts were in a familiar situation -- staring down the barrel.

Brief scores: Vidarbha 151 and 346 for 5 decl (F Fazal 200 no, R Paradkar 58; P Kumar 4/82) vs Services 77 and 96 for 3 (S Tomar 63).

Heading: State Line - Indian Express
Content:
India's first literary festival for children is all set to open in Delhi

Children don't always believe reading is fun, so here comes a festival that promises to change their minds. Bookaroo, India's first literature festival for children, will kick off in the Capital on November 22. "Two days packed with exciting events. By the end of it, we hope, children will see books as trendy and enjoyable," says Anita Roy of Young Zubaan, one of the organisers.

Some of the other organisers are bookstore Eureka, writers Anushka Ravishankar and Subhadra Sengupta as well as publisher Young Zubaan and literary consultancy Siyahi. Around 35 major writers, publishers, illustrators and performers have joined hands, so that the programme list is varied and quirky and kids, with their short attention spans, don't get bored. The initial fervour has been encouraging — more than 1,200 registrations ever since word about the festival spread in schools.

"Let's Sing Along with Anushka Ravishankar," the first event on Day One, is already full but there are seats left for several others. Go on an adventure with Jo Williams called "Charmseekers' Challenge" or get under the skin of birds and beasts in "Panchantantra in Wonderland." The interestingly titled "Pchak! Pchak!" has writer Padmini Mongia reading from her new picture book about a pair of crocodiles in the backwaters of Kerala whose baby refuses to open her mouth.

Writer Subhadra Sen Gupta will teach children to make their own cartoon stories in "Comic Shomic" as well as take them on a tour of Sanskriti Museum on a time travel story. "It's about how a bunch of children find themselves in 19th century Delhi," says Sen Gupta.

While most events are for specific age groups, special sessions like a meeting with celebrity American graphic novelist Jeff Smith is open to all. "And there's something for grown-ups too," says Roy. Wendy Cooling, one of UK's foremost educationists, will meet parents, teachers and librarians in the programme, "It's Never Too Early To Start".

Bookaroo will be held on November 22 and 23 at Sanskriti, Anand Gram, Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road.Time: 10 am-5pm. Log on to www.bookaroo.in.

Heading: Play On - Indian Express
Content:
Kashmiri artist Rajendar Tiku makes subtle statements through his art

I don't like to make political comments," states Rajendar Tiku just before guests start trouping into Gallery Espace to give their verdict on the Kashimiri artist's work. Titled Metaphors in Matter, his solo in Delhi after five years may not be directly depictive of the violence that has plagued the war-torn valley, but deeper interpretation of each title and with slight reflection the silent statements seem obvious. With Black Key in bronze, Tiku portrays the inability to find a key to resolve the problems in Kashmir and My House in the Snow acts as a personal memoir, depicting his cherished memory of his house submerged in snow. In The Site- n Tiku makes use of the now almost defunct Sharada script, but he fades the lettering engraved on the dever stone, lest it allow onlookers to read his mind. "Each work is open to interpretation," he says.

While he has been careful to avoid any direct connotations in the 25 sculptures on display, he does confess that the influence of the surroundings cannot be negated. "After all, art is personal," he smiles, looking at a gold-gilded wood sculpture titled Sprout, based on Kashmiri poet Shama Kaul's poem 'Humne boyi hai apni asthiyon ki paniri— hum ugenge' (We have sown the seedlings of our remains— we shall sprout again). "The words aptly describe the situation in Kashmir," says Jammu-based Tiku, who travelled to Jaipur and Kashmir to work on the sculptures. "I wanted to make use of the local material that was available in these places," says Tiku, as he looks at the work titled Site x. "This is inspired by the Martand Sun Temple," he shares.

As he invites the reaction to his work from art connoisseurs in Delhi, Tiku does realise that in times of recession the price tag will attract most attention. "Everyone seems to be more interested in the price," he smiles.

The exhibition at Gallery Espace is on till December 6. Contact: 26326267

Heading: Wife to Max: point out docs guilty of surgery ‘mishap’ that led to top CII exec’s death - Indian Express
Content:
After their tentative debut last year, the Atelier Youth Theatre Week comes into its own this month with a schedule that offers the best of campus histrionics. This year there will be 12 college plays, four more than the eight that was put up last year. While St Stephen's College adapts Victor Hugo's Les Miserables as Aadhi Raat ke Baad, Miranda House will take on Spanish play Iron by Rona Munro, a psychological drama about an encounter between a woman visiting her mother in prison. Shri Ram College of Commerce on the other hand, tackles existentialism in an original play called Sifar.

"It's significant that a number of entries deal with the notions of freedom and the nationalism," says Kuljeet Singh, festival director. Sri Venkateswara College, for instance, presents Jean Paul Sartre's Men without Shadows in which five men are questioned on charges of conspiring against the state by burning down a village. Kirori Mal College's original script deals with harsh interrogations of terror suspects; in this case, a lecturer from the University of Iraq (see left) is being interrogated for having incited students to protest against the government. On the other hand, Khalsa College brings the action closer home, to Kashmir in their reworking of Albert Camus' Just Assassins.

The festival also includes guest performances by Chhaon and The Actor Factor Company.

The Atelier Youth Theatre Week will be held from November 24 to 28 at various colleges in Delhi.

For more details, see www.atelierexpressions.com. Contact: 9891092386

Heading: Das couple says Lokkhi given ‘simple’ punishments, shows sample to police - Indian Express
Content:
A month after Jayant K Bhuyan, deputy director general of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), died "accidentally" after a bypass surgery at a city hospital, his family is awaiting the final report from the hospital explaining the sudden death.

Not ready to take the hospital's answer that it was not "medical negligence" but an "accident" that led to her husband's death, Ramola Bhuyan said, "I want the doctors responsible to be pin-pointed."

Ramola will meet the Max Hospital administration on Thursday to discuss the report that Max has put together to explain the circumstances leading to his death. Bhuyan died on October 6 following a triple bypass heart surgery at Max Devki Devi Heart and Vascular Institute in Saket.

Ramola said the hospital authorities had informed her soon after Bhuyan's death that he died of an "accident" during the surgery. The hospital, she said, told her that a wrong tube was inserted into the patient's heart, which released oxygen into his brain in a large dose that led to brain damage.

In their defence, Max authorities maintain that they have not hidden facts from the family, and the incident was not triggered by medical negligence. "We have been straightforward and forthright with the family. There is a difference between an accident and negligence," Pervez Ahmed, executive medical director, Max Healthcare, said. "It is unfortunate that the accident resulted in death of the patient but it was not (due to) medical negligence."

He will meet Ramola Bhuyan on Thursday and share findings of the internal investigation. "We cannot share that report with the media because patient confidentiality is our prerogative," Ahmed said. "If the family wants to share it with the media, it is their choice."

Ramola Bhuyan said, "It is difficult to digest the fact that no one is responsible for my husband's death. Accident or gross negligence, the truth is that hospital instruments do not levitate on their own."

The family, meanwhile, is mulling over the possibility of taking the concerned doctors to court.

Bhuyan, 58, was admitted to Max Hospital in Gurgaon after a heart attack on September 29. He was later moved to Max Devki Devi Institute at Saket. An angiography revealed that three of his arteries were blocked and that he needed an immediate open-heart surgery. Dr Inderjit Virdi led the team that operated on him.

The surgery was scheduled for October 4. "In the evening, they informed us that the surgery was successful and he was moved to the ICU," wife Ramola Bhuyan said.

At that stage, the doctors had informed the family that the patient's liver and kidney were functioning well but his brain function could be assessed only after the effect of sedatives reduced.  Ramola said the hospital told her the following morning that he had suffered an extensive brain injury. "When I reached the hospital they (doctors) said he had died."

Heading: Move over big brothers, crorepatis in fray from ‘fringe’ parties - Indian Express
Content:
Gurgaon residents Debokjyoti Das and his wife Paromita, under probe for cruelty to their teenaged help Lokhhi, had once filmed the nature of the 'punishment' they meted out to the help for disobedience.

Paromita Das showed the short clip — captured in her mobile phone — to the police soon after the couple's arrest on Saturday morning. She was trying to argue that it was a 'simple punishment', police sources said.

The Das couple was arrested on Saturday after their neighbours alerted the National Commission for Women (NCW) the evening before that the couple reportedly beat up the girl again. They were released on bail within hours. The 13-year-old girl was rescued by the NCW and non-governmental organisation Shakti Vahini.

Any form of cruelty — whether it is a slap or grievous harm — is bailable under the same charges in the Indian Penal code: Section 323 for 'voluntarily causing hurt', 342 for 'wrongful confinement' and 374 for 'unlawful compulsory labour'. Apart from these, the couple has also been slapped with Sections 15 and 16 C of the Child Labour Act.

In her confession, Paromita said she called for Lokhhi as soon as she came home from work on Friday evening. The girl, she said, had locked herself inside the bathroom. Paromita confronted her for disobedience when she came out, but Lokhhi told her she had been cleaning inside. Paromita said Lokhhi 'raised' her voice and that is when she 'lost her patience'. She hit her, so hard that Lokhhi collapsed on the floor, and then 'beat her up'. The couple had earlier denied they physically harmed the girl.

Paromita, an associate director at Atharva Biosciences' molecular diagnostic division, told the police: "I am also a human being with a threshold to my patience. It had to top off somewhere."

In the last few days, Paromita has often said that she has a taxing job, an ailing mother-in-law, and is always on her toes because of her two small children.

When asked how much Lokhhi was paid, Paromita told the police: "I never paid her directly as she wouldn't know what to do with it. Though I am not sure, my uncle who recommended Lokhhi, paid Rs 500 to her father every month."

The couple also said that Lokhhi lied frequently. When asked why they did not send her back, Paromita said: "We had once called her father but he did not understand what we were trying to say. We are both working and have very few leaves. It was not possible for us to drop her off at her village." Lokhhi is from Karimganj in Assam.

Later in the confession, Paromita contradicted what she had said earlier about the girl's pay. "I planned to keep her till my kids grew up and would have then given Rs 20,000 to Lokhhi," she said. She also said the couple could not afford the Rs 2,000-a-month help placement agencies were offering.

Heading: Metro man fights for national values - Indian Express
Content:
The relatively newer entrants in the Delhi Assembly elections — Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and Shiromani Akali Dal — are creating ripples in the run up to the polls after a candidate from each party declared assets at Rs 100 crore or more.

While BSP's Kanwar Singh Tanwar, fighting from Chattarpur constituency, created waves by declaring his assets at Rs 150 crore in the affidavit filed during the nomination process, Manjeet Singh Sirsa, the Akali Dal candidate for the alliance with BJP, is being considered the second richest candidate in the fray. He declared assets worth Rs 100 crore. With a flourishing medical business in London and a booming real estate business in Delhi and Gurgaon, Tanwar owns two Prados and two S-class Mercedes Benz.

Up next is Sirsa, who comes from the village of the same name in Haryana and is contesting from Jangpura. The Akali candidate said he owns properties worth at least Rs 20 crore in Punjabi Bagh, Karol Bagh, Inderpuri and Gurgaon. In his declaration, he also named properties in Chhwal and Rewal, in Punjab and Haryana respectively.

"I have three cars, including a Mercedes and a Volkswagon," he said. Both imported cars, they are worth "at least a crore after depreciation in cost".

A scrutiny of the list of assets declared by nominees says Rajinder Gupta, the BSP candidate from Greater Kailash-I, owns properties in prime areas such as Barakhamba Road, Amrita Shergill Marg, Greater Kailash-I, Gurgaon, and Raghubir Nagar. These properties, as per Gupta's affidavit, is valued at Rs 6 crore.

The BSP candidate reportedly earns approximately an annual Rs 25 lakh from these properties.

Besides property, Gupta and his wife have investments worth around Rs 2 crore, including Rs 10 lakh invested in mutual funds alone, the affidavit says. Gupta is pitched against BJP's chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra and Congress' Jitender Kochar, a former MCD councillor.

Heading: Evening courts: monkey menace forces CJI to stay off Tis Hazari - Indian Express
Content:
After giving the city a world-class inner-city rail system, Metro man E Sreedharan is now on a new track. The Padma Vibhushnan awardee has formed a society to restore national values, which he says is an issue that merits immediate attention.

The society — Foundation for Restoration of National Values — has an impressive list of board advisors, including former Justice M N Venkatachaliah, Tata Group chairman Ratan Tata, and former Central Vigilance Commissioner N Vittal. The organisation aims to influence leaders and opinion-makers from fields such as law, judiciary, public administration, corporate sector, education and healthcare.

The foundation's first two-day summit will be held at India Habitat Centre on November 18-19. Among speakers are Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha L K Advani and former President A P J Abdul Kalam. "We will propagate values like national interest, commitment towards the Indian Constitution, the national flag and national motto," Sreedharan said.

Heading: Life term for Suhrid, Debu in Tapasi case - Indian Express
Content:
If one was asked to think up the connection between the evening courts inaugurated today and the monkey menace, one would probably be left amused by the query. But such is the nuisance of the marauding monkeys in the Tis Hazari court premises that the authorities avoided holding evening courts at its premises.

Taking further precaution, the authorities settled on the Patiala House court as the venue for the evening court project's inauguration ceremony on Wednesday, ensuring a hassle-free evening for Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan and the others.

The tale of the tails, however, is not new at the Tis Hazari premises. According to court sources, monkeys have been parading the premises for years now. "It is a known fact that judges and court staff try to finish off their work early as these monkeys get most active during late evenings," a court official said.

"Judges who have late sittings scheduled for any day are even provided with extra protection to evade trouble."

On their part, the court authorities have indulged in varied methods to ward off the monkeys. From deploying langurs, a fellow simian that other monkeys dread, to employing a few 'chosen' court staff specifically for keeping these animals at bay, they have tried it all.

Besides a circular in 2005 by the district and sessions judge asking the court staff not to work after 5 pm due to "security reasons", an administrative civil judge had even issued a circular warning court staff of punitive action, in case they failed to check the alarming vandalism of the monkeys at Tis Hazari courts.

"Everyone in the court seems to be in hurry as soon as the clock strikes 4, as the monkeys swing into action. They can be seen occupying staircases and all the floors," a court staff said.

The situation is not too different, though a little milder, in the other subordinate courts. In February last year, a three-legged simian had got into the court of Additional Sessions Judge R K Yadav at Karkardooma district courts in East Delhi. The animal had jumped to the judge's podium and begun tearing off pages from law books. The judge sent a strong letter to the municipal corporation, demanding immediate action to rid the court premises of monkeys.

But despite being besieged with several orders from the High Court to banish monkeys out of all court premises, the municipal corporation has had little success till date.

Heading: ‘Tata’s exit will not be complicated’ - Indian Express
Content:
Suhrid Dutta, CPM Hooghly district committee member and aide Debu Malik received a life sentence on Wednesday for the murder of Tapasi Malik.

Amar Kanti Acharya, the additional district and session judge of the Chandannagar fast track court, however, turned down CBI counsel Partha Tapaswi's appeal that they deserved capital punishment. The murder, the judge said, took place due to personal reasons and can't be called political.

Acharya, who had pronounced the guilty verdict on Tuesday, announced the punishment in a packed court around 2.40 pm. A fine of Rs 10,000 was imposed on each accused as well.

The defence advocates said they would move higher courts challenging the verdict.

Dutta and Malik had been produced before the court around 1.50 pm amid tight police security. "I'm not guilty," Dutta shouted while being taken out of the court. They were later taken to the Chandannagar sub-divisional correctional home.

Apprehending trouble, prohibitory orders under Section 144 CrPC had been imposed around the court premises. Several hundred supporters of Trinamool Congress and CPM had come to attend the proceedings. But they were not allowed to enter the court premises. Trinamool supporters, who were demanding capital punishment for the accused, took out a rally after the punishment was pronounced.

Describing the judgment as a "gross miscarriage of justice", Dutta's advocate, Arindam Bhattacharjee, said there was no direct evidence against Dutta. Making similar claims, Malik's advocate, Kishor Mondal, said the verdict was given "on basis of circumstantial evidence".

The Trinamool-backed Singur Krishi Jami Raksha Committee (SKJRC) and the victim's family welcomed the judgment. "We are thankful to the CBI for handling the case properly," said Manoranjan Malik, Tapasi's father. "The officers of the Criminal Investigation Department in fact tried to establish that my daughter had committed suicide. The chief minister should step down," he added.

Tapasi's mother Molina, however, said, "We would have been happier had both of them been hanged."

Under the banner of SKJRC, several hundred villagers took out a rally from Bajemelia when the news reached Singur.

Heading: CPM cries conspiracy, refuses to expel Suhrid - Indian Express
Content:
The exit route for Tata Motors from Singur will not be a complicated one, Principal Secretary of state for commerce and industry, Sab-yasachi Sen, has assured.

"As and when the Tata Motors takes out all the equipment from the site, they can terminate the lease with the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) — but not before that. The same applies for the 290 acres of land that is with the vendors," said Sen.

He said the factory site has many types of equipment that had been assembled with the help of engineers from Japan and Germany.

"Assembling the unit took about two years. The state government has to give them legitimate time to bring out all the equipment. Even if not two years, we are expecting them to take anything between six months to a year," said Sen.

He said the commerce and industry department will keep a layout ready for possible future projects. "We will conduct a survey of the land and prepare a blueprint with roads, drainage, sewerage and the overall layout. The area might be taken by a single company or two companies or we may even have an industrial park. Layout for all options will be prepared," the minister said. He, however, added that only when the existing lease agreement is terminated, concrete progress can be made with other companies. The land lease is renewed every year and the present lease will lapse in March.

WBIDC Managing Director Subrata Gupta, meanwhile, confirmed that vendor companies have already started approaching WBIDC for terminating the lease.

"Recently we received a letter from one vendor company stating that they would like to terminate the lease and take the money back," said Gupta.

Sen also said the proposal for Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemical Investment Region (PCPIR) at Nayachar has been sent to the 14-member high-power committee chaired by the cabinet secretary. The proposal was approved by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers two days ago.

"We hope the high-power committee will clear it soon. Then the proposal will go to the Cabinet," he said.

Regarding Salim group's investments in Gujarat, he said: "We have no apprehensions of the group pulling out its projects from West Bengal. Both Mahabharat Motors and New Kolkata International Development Pvt Ltd (NKID) are on track. It is a big group which can invest anywhere it wants," added Sen.

Heading: ‘Tapasi verdict proves CPM atrocities’ - Indian Express
Content:
Despite its district committee member from Hooghly Suhrid Dutta and his aide Debu Malik receiving a life sentence for the murder of Tapasi Malik, CPM still backed its leader and his aide in Singur.

Biman Bose, the party's state secretary and Left Front chairman, said: "There is no question of expelling Dutta. No action will be taken against him. This is a conspiracy against him and we will appeal against the verdict to a higher court."

He was speaking at the sidelines of the inauguration ceremony of Vidyasagar Mela in Ghatal, West Midnapore.

"Dutta is not guilty. There is no evidence against him. He will continue to be our party's leader," Balai Sabuin, CPM district secretariat member of Hooghly, told The Indian Express on phone.

Trinamool Congress and the Congress, meanwhile, welcomed the court's order and demanded Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's resignation.

Lambasting the state government, Congress Legislative Party leader Manas Bhuniya said: "The chief minister has failed to protect the people of the state. In fact, he tried to suppress the truth. He should immediately resign," he said at a media conference.

He also alleged that the state police have become "mere puppets" in the hands of the ruling CPM. It was only because of the CBI that the real culprits were caught.

At a rally in Burdwan, Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee echoed the sentiment.

"Bhattacharjee's hands have been marred with blood and he should resign immediately. The party is killing innocent people all over the state," she said.

Heading: Fund shortage: hospitals wait for dengue kits - Indian Express
Content:
The Socialist Unity Centre of India (SUCI) has welcomed the verdict of the Chandernagore court that sentenced the CPM Hooghly district committee member, Suhrid Dutta, and his aide Debu Malik to life imprisonment in the Tapasi Malik murder case on Wednesday.

SUCI state secretary Pravash Ghosh said: "The verdict proved that the CPM was behind such atrocities. It has now become clear that the party is responsible for all the illegal activities in the state — be it in Nandigram or Singur."

He was speaking on the sidelines of a mass meeting held to commemorate the 91st anniversary of the Great November Revolution in Russia.

Ghosh claimed that though the Trinamool Congress and his party have not formally joined hands, the incidents of Singur and Nandigram necessitates the formation of a mass movement for which the two are now united.

"Whatever atrocities were reported during the Congress' regime in the state earlier are now occurring during the CPM rule," said Ghosh.

Heading: Tribals run their writ, admn disappears - Indian Express
Content:
While the city remains in the grip of vector-borne diseases, the state health department has not been able to supply dengue test kits to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and the state-run hospitals due to paucity of funds.

Significantly, Health Minister Surjya Kanta Mishra had earlier claimed that the state did not need any help from the Centre to combat the vector-borne diseases, as it could manage the situation on its own.

The statement has boomaranged. The department had recently withdrawn its approval for the test kits it had sanctioned for the KMC.

Deputy Mayor Kalyan Mukherjee said: "The health department had asked us to place a formal request for dengue test kits. Subsequently, we submitted a requisition for 10,000 kits. Initially, the department had sanctioned these but later withdrew the sanction."

He added: "We were told that since the KMC does not have proper infrastructure to conduct dengue tests, it is not being provided with the kits. We, however, have 110 trained professional and 83 clinics in several wards."

The 110 laboratory technicians were trained at the School of Tropical Medicine (STM) for testing blood samples for dengue, said another official.

The department, however, denied that the KMC had sent any requisition for the kits. "We never received any proposal from the KMC. Instead, we asked the civic body to refer all the suspected cases to the STM as it has the infrastructure to conduct tests," said Sanchita Bakshi, Director (Health Services).

She, however, admitted that the department does not have adequate funds. "We cannot supply the test kits to the state-run hospitals, as we do not have funds to procure a large number of kits. The STM has Elisa reader by which dengue tests can be conducted without the kits," added Bakshi.

Incidentally, the STM authorities have a different take. "The health department supplied a few test kits, which got exhausted soon as the situation is serious. Everyday we are receiving at least 80 to 100 cases and we need to conduct dengue tests for them," said a senior doctor of the STM. "We have now started procuring kits as our ELISA reader is also not functioning," he added.

Heading: Jindal not affected by Salboni agitation - Indian Express
Content:
With over 10 villages in Lalgarh being virtually taken over by the Maoists, tribals have begun running a parallel administration in the area.

Convinced that the movement has some popular support, the district administration is hesitant about using force to quell the agitation.

On Wednesday, locals dug up more roads in and around the area, effectively cutting off Jhargram, Goaltore, Binpur, Belpahari and Lalgarh from the rest of the state. Police sources revealed that top Maoist leaders had gathered in Katapahari on Wednesday to chalk out the future course of action.

Police have remained inactive in most areas. District Magistrate N S Nigam, who requested the government not to apply force against the tribals, said though all political process has failed so far, "I am not in favour of any police action against the villagers."

CPM state secretary Biman Bose admitted that a large section of the villagers have also joined the Maoist-backed agitation.

"We are aware that some of our people are also involved in the movement as they have been forced to do so. We, however, feel that the situation is under control," Bose said.

For the last six days, the administration has been in constant dialogue with the four main political parties of the region - the CPM, the Congress, the Trinamool and the Jharkhand Party - along with the tribal organisation Bharat Jakat Majhi Marwa.

Representatives from all these parties admitted the villagers were no longer listening to them. Villagers of Katapahari and Dalilpur said they want a direct dialogue with the administration.

Villagers of the 10 gram panchayats under Lalgarh have taken an initiative to form 10 village committees with one mother committee to assist and guide them. The mother committee can then directly interact with the administration to discuss issues to end the deadlock.

The district administration, however, said it was not possible for the administration to accept the demands put forward by the villagers. Their demands include:

* An unconditional apology from Superintendent of Police Rajesh Singh in the presence of the press and villagers

* Punishment for policemen involved in the raids

* Rs 2 lakh compensation for the villagers who have been injured or assaulted

* Apology by policemen involved in the November 6 raid

Nigam said the government was ready to discuss the compensation issue but the other demands could not be met.

In Lalgarh town, meanwhile, most businessmen and traders belonging to non-tribal communities are agitated that there is no electricity or drinking water

supply for the last seven days. CPM district committee secretary Dipak Sarkar said, "We are aware of the situation. But we cannot do anything."

Heading: Govt flouted own rule in Raj Bhavan transfer - Indian Express
Content:
The Jindal group is not worried about the prospects of its proposed steel plant in Salboni, even as the area continues to be affected by agitations.

"Salboni blast had nothing to do with the Jindal project. The villagers are protesting against the police atrocities in villages," said Biswadip Gupta, Chief Executive of JSW Bengal Steel.

Gupta claimed that certain political groups were behind the blast, who wanted to affirm their presence in the area.

"We have signed an agreement with the state government that we will set up only a steel project in Salboni and nothing else. There has been a communication gap between the villagers and the local administration regarding the project," he said.

Gupta added the company is considering distributing pamphlets among villagers that the proposed project will not be a real estate SEZ and residential complexes will not be constructed in the area.

He said: "We have considered many factors before setting up the SEZ. The Center and the state found the area suitable for the purpose."

He further added that the chief minister and the district magistrate of West Midnapore have assured them of ample security, if needed. " While we do not need police protection at the moment, we are definitely concerned about the security of 600 workers working on the plant site since November 3," he said.

Heading: Nazrul Islam case: HC asksNazrul Islam case: HC asks govt to collect fine from guilty officer govt to collect fine from guilty officer - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has flouted its own rule by transferring Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi's press secretary Dhruba Basu without first sending a panel of names to the Governor.

As The Indian Express reported on Tuesday, Basu, an officer of the Information & Culture (I&C) department under chief minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, received the order on November 8. Gandhi was immensely annoyed as he was not consulted before the move.

On Tuesday, his secretary KS Rajendra Kumar wrote on his behalf to the I&C Department, with a request that a panel of officers be sent to the Governor, from whom he could select the officer of his choice and the transfer be put on hold.

Basu himself wrote a letter to I&C principal secretary Dilip Chakrabarthy on Wednesday, in which he requested that he be allowed to continue in his present post till he retires in March 2012.

"We will put both the letters before the chief minister and await his decision. However, we want to reiterate that there is no standard practice of sending any panel to the department where an official is being transferred," Chakrabarthy said.

But the rules of the Home (personnel) department say otherwise. "An officer of the rank of principal secretary can be transferred anytime. But when an officer below that rank, a special secretary, joint secretary or deputy secretary, has to be transferred, a panel of names has to be sent to that department. That is mandatory," an officer of the Home department told The Indian Express.

Before he selected KS Rajendra Kumar as his secretary, Gandhi rejected a panel of three IAS officers sent to him for the post.

On Wednesday, Basu refuted allegations of misbehaviour levelled against him by some officials of I&C department. Chakrabarthy had said they received allegations that Basu misbehaved with his colleagues. "I am shocked to hear this allegation. I have never misbehaved with anybody. That is not my nature," Basu told The Indian Express.

His colleagues at the Raj Bhavan unequivocally vouched for him.

According to them, he is one of the most polished and polite officers there. "Nobody has heard him shout at anybody. We can't understand who has fed I&C secretary all this gibberish," one of them said.

Heading: Painter dabs heritage hues to Kolkata trams - Indian Express
Content:
A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court upheld an order on Wednesday earlier passed by its single Bench directing the state government to pay Re 1 as compensation to IPS officer Nazrul Islam for harassing him by initiating an inquiry against him.

The Bench comprising Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Sanjib Banerjee also directed the government to ascertain the responsibility of the state government official, who had caused the harassment, and collect the amount from him.

On June 25, Justice S P Talukdar had directed the state to hold the officer responsible for harassment, who had conducted the inquiry against Islam.

The Judge had also directed that a compensation of Re 1 be deducted from the salary of the errant officer and be paid to Islam within four weeks.

Though the state government had subsequently paid Re 1 to Islam, it also filed an appeal before the Division Bench against the order.

On Wednesday, the Division Bench upheld the earlier order that the penalty should be collected from the guilty officer.

In 2006, the State Vigilance Commission had initiated an inquiry against Islam, now Inspector General (Welfare), after it received a letter from an unknown person, which said the police officer had amassed wealth disproportionate to his known sources of income.

Islam then filed a petition in the HC challenging the inquiry. He also alleged that the inquiry had caused him harassment and mental torture.

Heading: Now, JU students will decide when they want to sit for exams - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-seven trams renovated with the paintings of artist Samir Biswas were unveiled on Wednesday.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya flagged off the trams and said the heritage trams will add a new dimension to the trams and will draw tourists towards tram rides. The trams carry paintings of heritage buildings and various sights of Kolkata.

Biswas, who made the paintings, said he traversed the entire city to get a feel of what should be painted on the trams. "I began from the south, the house of Sabarna Raichowdhury and travelled up to the gullies of north Kolkata. I also visited the eastern area, where new developments were taking place," he said.

While the exterior of a tram portrays the city's landscape such as the river and the boats, the interiors have familiar landmarks like the Victoria Memorial.

"Kolkata is a heritage city and the tram is an integral part of it. There can be no better way to visualise the city than taking a heritage ride in a tram," said Biswas. Besides, promoting the city's heritage and tourism, the authorities hope it brings denizens to the trams.

Heading: Jains protest against idol theft - Indian Express
Content:
Reeling under the pressure of students threatening to boycott examinations, the Jadavpur University (JU) authorities have asked students of the engineering faculty to chalk out the academic calendar and come up with a new date for semester examination.

The students have been asking the university to defer the semester examination scheduled from November 14. In a deputation submitted on November 6, the students had threatened to boycott examination if the academic calendar was not changed.

In the executive council meeting on Wednesday, the students' representatives refused to accept a fresh proposal to begin examinations from November 24. Following this, Vice-Chancellor Pradip Narayan Ghosh has asked the students to decide on the new examination date. According to the students, the examination should begin from December 1. "Some of the class tests, viva and lab projects are not yet over. So how can we sit for the examination?" a student said.

The students are reportedly ready to start the next semester the very next day after the examination is completed. "While our placement begins on April 1, the semester examination continues till April 10. By changing the academic calendar, we can also finish the next semester examination before April 1," said Abhishek Chakraborty, a fourth-year student.

Heading: Driver commits suicide after ‘murdering’ domestic help - Indian Express
Content:
Thirty-six days after the ancient ashtadhatu idol of Lord Parswanath was stolen from the Parswanath Digamber Jain Temple at Alipore, the Jain community in the city is up in arms.

The community alleged that there could be a possible conspiracy behind the theft and declared a reward of Rs 1 lakh to anyone, who provides any information which might lead to the recovery of the idol.

"Even after so many days of the theft, there has been no news about the idol. The Jain community is affected by the incident and have decided to do our bit to trace it," said Vinod Jain, a member of the Shree Parswanath Digamber Jain Temple.

Some members alleged that a private housing company, which is developing a residential complex within the same area where the temple is situated, might be behind the theft. The company allegedly wants the temple to be relocated.

"The culprits did not touch the valuables worth Rs 1 lakh inside the temple but stole the idol, which does not have much monetary value," said Bhagchand Kashliwal, a trustee of the temple.

The community alleged that the administration has not been able to trace the idol and its non-recovery has caused discontent among the Jain samaj in Kolkata.

"We have already appealed to Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, Left Front chairman Biman Bose, Minority Affairs Minister Abdus Sattar, and the police commissioner about the issue," said a community leader.

"We condemn the whole incident. The government is trying to recover the idol," said Faiyaz Ahmed Khan, Member Mayor-in-Council, Information and Public Relations.

Heading: Empty stalls, no buyers, Kolkata film mart has a ‘surreal’ feel - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of Jodhpur Park on Wednesday woke up to the news of a gruesome murder and suicide. The bodies of a domestic help and a driver were recovered from an apartment in the area.

Preliminary investigation indicated that the domestic help, Arati Das (41), was sexually assaulted and then hacked to death by the driver, Kartik Mondol (38), who later committed suicide.

"The body of Das was found with multiple stab wounds. The driver's body was found hanging from a ceiling fan. We have sent both the bodies for postmortem," Deputy Commissioner of Police (south) Rajesh Subarna said.

Das and Mondol were working for Madan Mohan Banerjee, a retired professor of the Calcutta Medical College Hospital, the police said. Das was attached with the household for the last 30 years. Mondol started working as a driver for Banerjee five years ago.

On Wednesday morning, Banerjee found that Das's room was latched from outside. As he opened the door, he found Das lying on the bed in a pool of blood. She had deep wounds all over her body.

Banerjee raised an alarm and informed the police. Later, Banerjee went to look for Mondol and found his body from Mondol's room.

"We are not sure. But it seems that Mondol used to demand sexual favours from Das. In all probability he sexually assaulted Das and then murdered her with a knife. Later, he went to his room and committed suicide," said an officer of Jodhpur Park police station.

Heading: Maradona bigger than Pele: Rummenigge - Indian Express
Content:
The inauguration of the film market at the Kolkata Film Festival (KFF) may have seen the presence of cine personalities like Nandita Das and Goutam Ghose, but insiders claim that the market has a long way to go.

Wednesday saw empty stalls and disenchanted visitors at the market's enclosure. The stalls of distribution agencies like Priya Entertainment and those of DVD companies wore a deserted look.

French film journalist Barbara Lorey quipped: "I have been to many festivals around the world, and I can say that the Kolkata film market is a surrealistic experience. The people at the counters drew a blank when I asked them about the films they are selling."

The scribe added, "They didn't even have brochures of the films to distribute. The organisers should pull up their socks."

Arijit Dutta of Eastern Indian Motion Picture Association, the organisers of the market, claimed that there should be enough buyers to sustain such an endeavour. "A market cannot function without buyers. Despite all our efforts, we have failed in attracting them," he said.

Nilanjan Chatterjee, director of the KFF, claimed that the film markets have succeeded in becoming a platform for interaction between the society and the cine community. "The growing importance of the film sector in India has been a function of the cultural and economic changes, which have aligned the Indian society with the developed world," he said.

Many, however, felt that the film mart of the KFF might end up being a case of taking too many eggs in one basket. "Juggling a festival with a film market is a daunting task. A proper film market, like the one at Cannes needs a lot of resources. The KFF shouldn't follow other film festivals," said Swiss Film Historian Marcy Goldberg, who is in the city to attend the festival.

Heading: Ponting warns that Twenty20 cricket could kill off Tests - Indian Express
Content:
German legend unfurls Burdwan academy blueprint, renowned club FC Bayern Munich to provide technical support for 5 years

Football-crazy Kolkata seems to have turned into a hotspot for the sport these days. Just days after it was announced that the legendary Diego Maradona would be visiting the city this December, star German footballer of yesteryears Karl-Heinz Rummenigge dropped in at the city and unfurled plans of launching an academy in the district of Burdwan, in Bengal.

The former World Cupper Rummenigge, who is currently the chairman of the world-renowned FC Bayern Munich club, was in town on a brisk trip, to announce details of an academy that will be set up in a joint venture among Burdwan District Sports Association (BDSA), FC Bayern, Techno India Group and the state sports department. The academy, which will be launched at the far-away village of Jhinguti near Burdwan town, will see the heavyweight German club providing technical support.

"This academy is going to be FC Bayern's first set-up away from home," announced Rummenigge, chairman of the world-renowned football club.

Rummenigge's visit, which is expected to be followed next month by the high-profile trip of Maradona, is being seen as part of a healthy developmental initiative taken by the Left Front state government these days.

Just days back, CPI(M) Member of Parliament Shamik Lahiri announced the itinerary of the legendary Maradona's whistlestop tour. The Argentine great will inaugurate a world-class football school in South 24-Parganas. And today, it was the turn of state industry and commerce minister Nirupam Sen to unfurl the Rummenigge project.

A Memorundum of Understanding (MoU) is yet to be signed, but Rummenigge made it clear that FC Bayern would prove all the necessary technical support on a long-term basis and will closely monitor the progress of the academy, which will be called the Bengal Techno Bayern Academy (BTBA). The Sports Authority of India's (SAI) Burdwan centre has provided a 23-acre plot of land for the football school.

Even as he rattled off details of the project, Rummenigge wished Maradona good luck over his new innings as national coach of the senior Argentine team. "Talking about Maradona, It was great to play alongside him in two editions of the World Cup (1982 and 1986). I pray for his success as the national coach of Argentina. We are still great friends, and I believe he is so passionate about the game that he is bound to get success," Rummenigge said.

In fact, Rummenigge feels Maradona was a greater player than Brazil's Pele. "Maradona played in various clubs outside his country. But Pele confined himself to only Brazil for almost his career. And the scenario was not that tough during Pele's time," Rummenigge said.

As for the new initiative in Bengal, the FC Bayern chairman explained: "We are different from the European clubs. We generally do not aim at short-term partnerships and immediate financial gains. Our philosophy is to build up the infrastructure and create a pool of potential kids. From that point of view, I feel India is one of the biggest resources in terms of soccer, and it needs to improve the standard of the game, so that it can one day participate in the World Cup, and not just be content with playing the World Cup qualifiers."

FC Bayern, as Rummenigge outlined, will nurture the academy students through its own unit of coaches. In addition, the club will train hand-picked Indian coaches of the BTBA. Rummenigge said: "Some promising boys from this academy could also be picked and taken to FC Bayern's own academy for training and they can also be given the scope to appear at trials for FC Bayern."

However, the organisers stayed away from revealing details of the costs that would be incurred in initiating the entire project. Nirupam Sen revealed other details, saying: "We will have five grounds where two will have artificial grass. Apart from floodlights at each ground, the academy will have a rehabilitation centre, gyms and a school for the academy kids." Techno India will construct the school and foot the bills for five years, which could come to Rs 5 crore per year.

Heading: ‘As a generation we are numb to violence around us’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after returning from an acrimonious and dramatic Test series loss to India, Australia captain Ricky Ponting has warned of the dangers posed to the game by a preoccupation with Twenty20 cricket.

Ponting said the money on offer in the Indian Premier League, the rebel Indian Cricket League and other emerging Twenty20 tournaments threatened the future of national teams. "We cannot afford to lose teams such as New Zealand and the West Indies from international cricket, but my fear is that this could happen if the game cannot strike a balance between Tests and the IPL's riches," Ponting wrote in his 2008 Captain's Diary, launched on Wednesday.

"Unless such a balance is achieved, I could see some countries' cricket teams declining in the way Zimbabwe's sides have struggled over the past few years. The best cricketers in the game want to keep representing their country, but if it's going to be costing them money then there are tough decisions ahead.

"If the IPL keeps growing ... the next generation might opt for franchise over country," warned Ponting.

Support from Warne

Shane Warne has defended Ricky Ponting amid intense criticism of his tactics in the Test cricket series loss to India, but has advised his 'mate' to dine out with a couple of his critics in order to learn more about captaincy.

Fearing a match's suspension for slow over-rate, he used his part-time bowlers on the fourth day of the Nagpur Test.

"I feel for (Ponting) as he has been copping it from all angles and all because he went away from what he does best — attack," Warne wrote in a syndicated newspaper column on Wednesday.

"Having played with him for a long time, (I can say) he was one of the guys who put the team first — always. I just think he got it wrong this time and I'm sure he will be a better captain for the experience."

Heading: Waist, hip size key to predicting health risk - Indian Express
Content:
Prasoon Joshi talks about his Ghajini experience

In B-town, everyone is on song, even if it is a shaven, tattooed Aamir Khan who can't remember his phone number. Little wonder, Prasoon Joshi found himself penning poetry for all the brawn and brawl on display in Ghajini. "It is a pacy thriller with a lot of action and high energy, but the songs are extremely important to the narrative," says Joshi who has written five songs, all composed by AR Rahman, for the Khan starrer.

The film is a remake of a Tamil movie that was released three years ago, with songs written by N. Muthukumar, but Joshi says the Hindi soundtrack is completely original. "I did not even listen to the southern version as I did not want to be influenced in anyway," says Joshi, who, however, watched bits of the film.

Heading: AIDS will spread like ‘bushfire’ in India: UN - Indian Express
Content:
A large European study has confirmed that simple measurements of the waist and hips may offer a better way of predicting obesity-related death than a standard, but more complicated, system of relating weight to height.

The standard body mass index, or BMI, method does not work very well for some people, such as the elderly or body builders, and researchers have begun building a case that it is better to look at waist circumference or the ratio of waist size to hip size. Among people with comparable BMIs, having an extra 2 inches around the waist increased the annual risk of death by 17 per cent for men and 13 per cent for women, according to the team led by Dr Tobias Pischon of the German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke in Nuthetal, Germany.

When they calculated the waist-to-hip ratio by dividing a person's waist size, measured at the navel, by the biggest part of their hips, the Pischon group found that the risk of death increased by 34 per cent for men and 24 per cent for women every time that ratio increased by 0.1.

Hip circumference alone did not predict death any better than BMI, which is a person's weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters, the researchers found.

They used data from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition database, involving 359,387 people in nine countries.

Even among people of normal weight, men with the biggest bellies had more than twice the death rate of the slimmest. For women, the rate was 79 per cent higher if their weight was in the normal range yet their bellies were big.

The findings, published in the 'New England Journal of Medicine', "underscore the importance of assessing the distribution of body fat even among persons of normal weight and challenge the use of cut-off points to define abdominal obesity, at least when they are used to predict the risk of death," the researches wrote.

Earlier research had suggested that men should not have a waist-to-hip ratio above 0.95, and in women it should be no higher than 0.8.

Heading: Think differently to solve different kinds of problems - Indian Express
Content:
HIV/AIDS infections will spread like 'bushfire' in parts of India if the country fails to check a spike in the number of intravenous drug users, the United Nations AIDS agency said on Thursday.

India has the world's third highest caseload with 2.5 million infections. It has an estimated 200,000 intravenous drug users, many of whom are in the remote northeast region which borders the opium-producing Golden Triangle of Myanmar, Thailand and Laos.

"If we don't prevent new infections in new emerging populations like injecting drug users, it can go up as bushfires. We may see a major surge in infections," Peter Piot, the Executive Director of UNAIDS, said.

He also raised concerns about the spread of drugs in India. "Drug use is moving a bit everywhere, we can see it in Bihar, UP and in Kashmir, it is kind of moving across the northern part of the country," Peter Piot, head of UNAIDS said.

"I was really shocked to hear what was going on."

Official figures show that more than 10 per cent of intravenous drug users in India are infected with HIV, a higher prevalence than among prostitutes. The country's overall HIV/AIDS prevalence rate is about 0.9 per cent for those aged between 15 and 49.

Heading: Acupuncture doesn't boost chances of conceiving by IVF - Indian Express
Content:
Certain kind of thinking process is best suited for certain kind of problem solving, according to a new study.

Researchers investigated whether middle school students solved geometry problems more successfully than their peers when they were provided with clues consistent with their own style of thinking.

The cognitive styles that were identified and the related clues were verbal, spatial, and shape-based.

They found that regardless of the type of clue provided, spatial and verbal thinking styles were useful for solving the geometry problems, while shape-based thinking was much less effective.

The study shows that geometry problems are solved most successfully through certain styles of thinking.

"Our research may have an impact on the teaching of geometry, and perhaps mathematics in general," the authors conclude.

"Specifically, teaching students how to think spatially and manipulate and hold in mind images may improve their performance in geometry class. Thus, it is important for students to consider other thinking styles than approaches usually taught in most introductory geometry classes in the US," the researchers added.

The study has been published in the journal Mind, Brain, and Education.

Heading: Live surgeries using Internet may soon be possible - Indian Express
Content:
Acupuncture during IVF treatment does not increase women's chances of having successful pregnancies, a new research has shown.
