The first is that there needs to be ample rupee liquidity and ample dollar liquidity, so that managers of financial firms are not running from pillar to post dealing with crises. In recent days, many banks in India have raised interest rates on deposits. They are, doubtless, hoarding liquidity, given fears that the money market might choke up. The RBI governor needs to address the insecurities of banks by coming out with a major speech where he makes clear his analytical framework and sketches policy responses to future events. If banks are more confident about the RBI's operating procedures of monetary policy, deposit rates and hence lending rates will go down and not up.

The second front that needs to be opened is an urgent de-bottlenecking of financial regulation. The R.H. Patil, Percy Mistry and Raghuram Rajan reports have sketched a well-thought-out programme for financial sector reforms. The delays in implementation of these reports have cost us dear. As an example, the problems of the money market, non-banking financial companies and mutual funds were critically about the lack of implementation of bond market reforms detailed in these three reports. There is now no time to lose. A well-functioning financial system must be urgently obtained.

Heading: Speculation rife as Advani calls on Rajni - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP, which has been on the defensive since its ministers and candidates ran into legal troubles, has rediscovered a bit of aggression thanks to Congress leader Margaret Alva. The advertisements released by the ruling party on Wednesday featured only Alva and her allegations that tickets were on sale in her party and that the Congress lost elections in Karnataka and Gujarat due to this reason. The state BJP had earlier released advertisements featuring Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Mahatma Gandhi to further its Hindutva credentials.

"Instead of correcting itself and acting on what she said, the Congress has shown the door to a senior leader like Margaret Alvaji," a beaming Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said.

"When a party sells tickets to its own people one does not know what will it sell if it comes to power," it read and exhorted people, "save Madhya Pradesh from being sold".

The Congress had a tough time defending itself on the issue—it could neither criticise Alva openly nor talk about her allegations. "The high command has already clarified that tickets were given to candidates by taking 'winnability' as the sole criterion," Congress leader Chandraprabhash Shekhar said.

Till Tuesday, the BJP was on the backfoot, forced to defend its erring ministers and their relatives like Tourism Minister Tukojirao Puar, who openly threatened a returning officer, and Revenue Minister Kamal Patel's son Sudeep against whom a CBI inquiry has been ordered. Incidentally, Puar and BJP candidate Phoolchand Varma, who were arrested on Tuesday in connection with the intimidation, were released on bail.

The Minister had claimed that he would not apply for a bail. Faced with the prospect of remaining in jail till November 24 with only a day left for campaigning, he applied for bail.

BJP state president Narendra Tomar was in Dewas to show solidarity with Puar, the party candidate from Dewas, and Varma, its candidate from Sonkutch. Both had got themselves admitted to a hospital soon after a Dewas court sent them in judicial custody till November 24.

Heading: Turnout no issue, won’t  coerce voters: CEC - Indian Express
Content:
Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh on Wednesday claimed he was offered an "obscene" sum of money by the "cartel of mobile operator" to keep his mouth shut on the spectrum allocation scam.

"A representative of the telecom cartel met me recently and offered obscene sums of money to maintain silence on this issue," Singh claimed. "This bribe offer indicates there is a large scam," he added.

Singh's claim came days after he, along with SP chief Mulayam Singh Yadav, met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to raise the issue. "I have also apprised UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in writing," said Singh adding, "Being the supporting party of the Government, we don't want to be a party to this scam. If we are not heard on this issue, I will personally approach the Supreme Court to look into the matter."

Singh alleged a scam by the "cartel" of Airtel, Idea, and Vodafone by violating TRAI norms on spectrum utilisation. He said extra burden has been put on the small mobile operators, while large operators were benefiting at their expense.

Heading: SC expands Article 21 to cover personal - Indian Express
Content:
Four days ahead of the first phase of polling in Jammu and Kashmir, the Chief Election Commissioner, N Gopalaswami, on Wednesday met politicians and all officials associated with the polling process in Srinagar and emphasised the need for free and fair polls in the state. "Nothing less than free and fair polls will be acceptable to us," he told reporters Wednesday evening.

On being asked whether security forces would compel voters to vote on the polling day, Gopalasawmi said the police, the Army or any other security agency would never be allowed to coerce voters. "We are not concerned about the meagre poll percentage. Our aim is to hold free and fair polls in the state. For us, weather is a big challenge, despite that all poll arrangements have already been completed." He termed the security situation as good.

Regarding the concerns of the political leaders who had met him earlier in the day, he said that the leaders were assured every facility. About late distribution of election cards, Gopalswami said that there were 13 other documents that could be used as an alternate to election cards. When asked about the arrest of separatist leaders for running the poll boycott campaign, he said that the law would take its own course. Earlier, he had held separate meetings with District Election officers and SSPs of all the districts and discussed the security and poll arrangements in Kashmir.

Heading: Hosni Mubarak to visit India after 25 yrs - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday expanded the scope of Article 21 — protection of life and personal liberty — saying the reputation of an individual is an important facet of his fundamental right under the Constitution, which must not be transgressed.

"If a person is sent to jail, then even if he is subsequently released, his reputation may be irreparably tarnished," the Bench of Justices Altamas Kabir and Markandeya Katju said, adding that there must be a justification for the arrest or detention of any person.

"The reputation of a person is a facet of his right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution," underlined the Bench, while reminding the authorities, especially the police, that it was all right to possess the "power to arrest" but its justification was "another thing". The police officer must be able to justify the arrest apart from his power to do so, it expressed while recalling a decision of a larger bench of the court.

"Arrest and detention in police lockup of a person can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person," Justice Katju, who wrote the verdict, emphasised. Quoting from chapter 2, shloka 34 of the Bhaghavat Gita, where Lord Krishna said to Arjuna, the judge said how "for a self respecting man, death is preferable to dishonour".

The observations formed part of the decision, where the court quashed a detention order dated May 22, 2008 passed against Deepak Gopaldas Bajaj, a Mumbai resident, under Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974 (COFEPOSA).

Elaborating the power of HCs and the apex court to set aside a preventive detention order at the pre-execution stage, the Bench said if the individual against whom such an order is passed approaches court and is able to convince it that the said order suffers from infirmity, the order must be quashed.

"There is no reason why the court should stay its hands and compel the petitioner to go to jail even though he is bound to be released subsequently (since the detention order was illegal)," it held while observing that such exercise would be "a meaningless and futile".

Heading: Bhonsala officials questioned by ATS quit - Indian Express
Content:
Egyptian President Mohamed Hosni Mubarak will be visiting India from November 16 to 19. This will be his second visit to India after a gap of 25 years.

The government-to-government agreements expected to be signed during the visit are extradition pact, space cooperation and exemption of visa for officials and diplomats.

Agreements between the Egyptian Government and Indian private firms on IT, human resources training, petrochemical, plastic, health and medicine are also likely to be inked during the visit.

Mubarak will be accompanied by wife Suzanne and a large delegation, including Egyptian Foreign Minister Ahmed Aboul Gheit, Information Minister Anass Ahmed Nabih El-Fiqqi, Communication and IT Minister Tarik Mohamed Kamel Mahmoud, Trade and Industry Minister Rasheed Mohamed Rasheed and other senior officials and business delegates.

During the visit, Mubarak will be meeting President Pratibha Patil and will hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. He will also meet Vice-President Hamid Ansari, UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee and Leader of Opposition L K Advani.

Briefing mediapersons, Egypt's Ambassador to India Mohamed Higazy said that 16 ministers from Egypt have visited India in the past two years. When asked why Mubarak is visiting India after such a long time (he last came here in 1983), Higazy said, "Since 1991, the governments of both the countries have been busy carrying out economic reforms at domestic level."

The Indian-Egyptian relationship was established, according to the Egyptian envoy, during the Nehru-Nasser era when the Friendship Treaty was signed in 1955. "In recent history, similarities and synergies between the two countries have brought them even closer," Higazy said.

On the aspirations of both countries to join the UN Security Council as a permanent member, he said, "This has been under discussion constantly. The two countries are identical in their quest for more democratic reforms."

Heading: Centre likely to send back three other state terror laws - Indian Express
Content:
The commandant and a clerk of the Bhonsala Military School in Nashik, who were questioned by the state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) in connection with the September 29 Malegaon blast, have resigned. Principal Ramesh Kute said Commandant S S Raikar, a retired colonel, and Rajan Gaidhane had put in their papers.

"We do not know the reason as they have not mentioned it in the letter," Kute said.

The resignations came even as the school admitted that its Nagpur campus hosted a Bajrang Dal training camp way back in 2001, as claimed by investigators. However, it denied that the camp had anything to do with explosives or bomb-making.

The school has also confirmed to The Indian Express that four Abhinav Bharat members arrested for the Malegaon blast, including retired Major Ramesh Upadhyay, met on its Nashik campus in September this year, but in connection with a blood donation camp and other such initiatives.

The ATS suspects that the Bajrang Dal activists who trained in Nagpur attended another training camp in Sinhagad, Pune, in 2003, along with some members of other, lesser-known Hindu groups. While the Bajrang Dal activists have been linked to the 2006 Nanded bomb blast in which two Hindu activists were killed, members of the other groups are suspects in this year's Malegaon blast. Moreover, some of their trainers are suspected to be common, with arrested Lt Col Prasad Purohit suspected to have been present at the Sinhagad camp.

"We only provided our campus for training as we have a lot of space. We get such requests... and we offer assistance as we can use some financial help," Diwakar Kulkarni, Secretary of the Central Hindu Military Education Society which runs the school, told Express. While ATS investigators say the Nagpur camp lasted for 40 days, Kulkarni put the duration at 12 days.

"We don't know what happened in those 12 days. But we can assure you that no explosives- or bomb-making was taught," he added. "In Nagpur, our school is many kilometres away from the city. We rent out our grounds only during vacation so that students are not disturbed. We do not know what they did and assume that it must have been some social initiative."

Kulkarni also said that Commandant Raikar had told investigators that a meeting of Abhinav Bharat had taken place on the Nashik campus on September 15. "Raikar was approached by Major Ramesh Upadhyay as they have worked together. The meeting was basically to discuss a 50-point social agenda starting with a blood donation camp of Abhinav Bharat. I can assure everyone that neither in 2001 nor now was there any talk of making bombs, not for 40 days, not for even an hour," he said.

The Bhonsala school and the education society which runs it are headquartered in Nashik and have a branch in Nagpur. It was founded in 1937 by staunch Hindutva proponent Dr B S Moonje and its students are called "Ramdandees" or followers of Lord Ram.

The ATS is probing links, if any, between the Malegaon blast and other blasts in Maharashtra and wants the police custody of Rakesh Dhavde, arrested for the Malegaon blast, saying they want to question him further as they suspect he played a key role in organising the 2003 Sinhagad training camp. They also want to question him in connection with the blasts in Parbhani, Jalna and Aurangabad.

The Nanded probe had also found that a person called Mithun Chakravorthy and another unnamed person had trained participants in Sinhagad in bomb-making. ATS sources say that they suspect a laptop computer belonging to Lt Col Purohit contains the names of 54 participants in the Sinhagad camp. The laptop is yet to be found.

Heading: Using GUJCOC, BJP says Cong playing terror politics - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed anti-terror laws in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka are set to meet the same fate as the one from Gujarat, which the Centre has refused to approve, it is learnt.

Anti-terror laws passed by the Assemblies of the three BJP-ruled states have been pending before the Centre for its approval for many months now. Sources said since they contained exactly the same provisions as in the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime Act (GUJCOCA), their fate was not going to be any different whenever their cases come up for decision.

As reported by The Indian Express on Wednesday, the Centre had sent the GUJCOCA bill to President Pratibha Patil with the recommendation to return it to the Assembly without signing it.

Sources said the decision on each one of these proposed laws will be taken separately in the order they were submitted to the Central Government. Gujarat's case was disposed of first as it was the first one to send it. Gujarat had submitted its Bill in 2004. Rajasthan's case has been pending since 2006 while Madhya Pradesh sent its Bill last year. A similar law sent by Uttar Pradesh last year had been withdrawn by the Mayawati Government.

Sources said the Centre's refusal to approve these laws was consistent with its long-held stand that some of the provisions in them, relating to stringent bail provisions and confessions made to police, were draconian and went against basic human rights.

They said the Centre was not in agreement with similar provisions contained in the Maharashtra version of the same law, MCOCA, which is under operation in Maharashtra and Delhi, and has been the reason why a number of states have been blaming the Centre for adopting double standards. They pointed out that the approval to MCOCA was given by the NDA Government and the Centre is not empowered to withdraw its assent. It has to be repealed by the respective state government only.

Heading: Asimananda among invitees at Ram Katha - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP on Wednesday latched on the Union Home Ministry's communication to President Pratibha Patil — recommending that the GUJCOC Bill, 2003, be sent back to the Gujarat Assembly unsigned — as it upped its offensive against the UPA Government for "pandering to vote bank politics in the ongoing Malegaon blasts".

Reacting to The Indian Express report in its November 12 edition, former BJP president M Venkaiah Naidu accused the Centre of "creating obstacles" for states in their war on terror. The party, simultaneously, upped its offensive against the Congress-led Government for what it called a "motivated campaign on Malegaon blasts".

"Prime Minister Manmohan Singh may talk of dealing with terror, but the Government actually creates hurdles in way of states in enacting anti-terror laws to protect its people," he said. "GUJCOCA is on the lines of MCOCA. It has still not been given the Presidential assent...," he added.

Speaking in Raipur, BJP president Rajnath Singh attacked the UPA Government's "attempts to raise the bogey of Hindu terror". "The Government is playing with fire by painting terrorism with communal colour," he charged.

The BJP president also warned against any attempts "to drag" the Gorakhpeeth in Gorakhpur — which is represented by BJP-backed Yogi Adityanath in the Lok Sabha — into the ongoing Malegaon blast investigation.

"It is unimaginable that Yogi Adityanath could be involved in any violent activities. Linking Adityanath to the (Malegaon blast) case is not procedural but political," said Rajnath.

Adityanath, a fellow Thakur, wields influence in eastern Uttar Pradesh and is perceived to be a rival of the Rajnath camp in Uttar Pradesh.

With L K Advani underlining the supremacy of law and saying the guilty, if any, should be punished, second-rung BJP leaders took care to endorse his stand. Venkaiah said that the guilty should be punished after an "impartial probe", Rajnath too said "my party is not against punishing the guilty if found so in a fair probe".

Heading: ‘This election will make no difference’ - Indian Express
Content:
Swami Asimananda Maharaj, who is missing since his Dangs ashram was raided by the Mumbai Police's Anti Terror Squad (ATS) in connection with the Malegaon blast, is slated to attend a high-profile nine-day Ram Katha event in Tapi district of Gujarat, beginning Thursday, along with prominent local Sangh Parivar leaders.

According to the organisers, the Ramkatha Sewa Samithi of Vyara, Asimananda will both inaugurate and be the chief guest at the event.

He is expected to share the dais with Dangs BJP MLA Vijay Patel, BJP Tapi general secretary Hitendra Upadhyay, BJP Surat district president Mansinh Patel, former BJP Mahua MLA Mohan Dadhaya, and VHP leader Bhagu Gamit, among others.

Among the VIPs whose name figures in the invitation list is former Congress MLA and MP from Vyara in Surat district Amarsinh Z Choudhary. However, he claims that while the organisers are very close to him and had talked to him before putting his name in the invitation list, he would not attend the function. He adds: "The organisers have done one thing wrong, they have only invited VHP, RSS and BJP leaders as guests."

Dangs MLA Patel also won't be attending the function, though he says this is because he has to attend a party meeting. "If I get the time, I will attend," he says. Patel added that he had full faith in Asimananda. "I know Swami Asimananadji Maharaj and he is a down-to-earth person and has done a lot of work for tribal people."

The Ram Katha Samiti itself seems unfazed by the fact that Asimananda's name has come up in terror investigations. "We have seen Swami Asimanandaji's name in the newspapers. But he is innocent. Our own sources have had a talk with him and he has assured that he would definitely attend the inaugural function... He will remain with us for sometime at the venue and then leave," says Narsinh Choudhary, president of the Ram Katha Ayojak Samithi.

Heading: Keeping an eye on CPI - Indian Express
Content:
Once upon a time he was the Kashmiri separatist liked by both New Delhi and Islamabad for his moderate image. But Hurriyat chairman, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, no longer makes the grade. He feels abandoned by the Central Government which he holds responsible for jettisoning a formal process of dialogue with the Hurriyat. Dialogue with New Delhi, he says, has only undermined the Hurriyat's credibility.

"The Hurriyat stands by the dialogue process. In fact, the initiative to start talks with New Delhi in 2004 was not New Delhi's alone. The Hurriyat went against the general drift of separatist politics in the Valley by talking to New Delhi," says Mirwaiz. "And if this process today stands derailed, the Hurriyat is not the cause".

Mirwaiz says New Delhi mistook the decline in violence in Kashmir as the return of normalcy and abandoned talks with the Hurriyat. For him, the recent groundswell of support for the "azadi" sentiment is the result of the Centre going slow on the peace process and drifting towards a "status quo-ist" posture on Kashmir. "I have always maintained this: That New Delhi gets serious on Kashmir only when there is violence in the state. There is no regard for the sentiment and political aspirations of the people which they have expressed time and again through peaceful protests," he says.

The Centre appears to be responding with elections to the recent mass uprising in the state, he says, without bothering to engage with the grievances of the people. "Look how New Delhi has responded. Kashmir in the recent past has witnessed the largest peaceful protests seen anywhere in the world. But in response, New Delhi has thrust an election on the state, knowing well that there will be negligible participation of the people," says Mirwaiz. "I wonder where this approach is going to lead us".

Mirwaiz says the Hurriyat wants people not to participate in the polls. "The boycott campaign will go ahead," he says. However, he says that the government is not letting the Hurriyat lead a peaceful campaign.

Elections haven't changed anything, he says. "Elections were never the issue with us. They make no sense in the absence of the settlement of the larger Kashmir conflict. Our position is that elections over the past six decades have resolved nothing. The Kashmir problem as it existed at the time of Partition remains the same. This election, similarly, will make no difference".

Asked if he is ready to engage with New Delhi if invited for a dialogue, Mirwaiz expresses his inability to continue with a "futile exercise". "Though the Hurriyat believes in the institution of dialogue, we don't think fruitless talks offer any solution. We no longer have an appetite for dialogue for the sake of dialogue," he says. He urges the Centre to take on board "historical and ground realities" if it is serious about talks on Kashmir. "Otherwise, dialogue only ends up creating new complications and stirring up fresh trouble."

He says the Hurriyat will follow a model of the dialogue with the Centre initiated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. "We stand for a peaceful negotiated settlement to the Kashmir dispute. But we will not be part of the dialogue with the crowd and alongside people who have no issue with New Delhi," he says. Kashmir, for him, needs a bigger and more serious initiative which treats genuine Kashmiri leadership as a party to the dispute and its resolution.

Heading: Comeback Kid - Indian Express
Content:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) foresees a post-poll scenario: A hung assembly in Raipur in which the party can play a role after winning a couple of seats from the Naxalite affected Bastar region.

"Though the Left parties and the BSP are not in a pre-poll alliance, both parties are all set to win a sizeable number of seats which could be sufficient to force a hung assembly," says CPI national executive member Chhatranjan Bakshi. Neither the BJP nor the Congress would be able to secure absolute majority in the 90-member House and legislators of other parties would emerge as a 'balancing factor' in the state politics, he says.

The CPI had a presence, and even legislators, from Bastar region in undivided Madhya Pradesh. However, its candidates could not win the 1998 polls of Madhya Pradesh and the new state's maiden polls held in December 2003. In the previous polls, CPI polled only 1.08 per cent votes but its candidates finished second in Dantewada (ST) and Konta (ST) constituencies while in Keshloor (ST) the party stood third. The CPM secured 0.29 per cent votes in the last elections.

However, the scenario may have changed for the CPI in Bastar, particularly because of its stand opposing the Salwa Judum — the controversial anti-Naxalite movement of South Bastar — and its crusade to protect the interests of farmers, whose land is being acquired for setting up greenfield steel plants in Bastar region.

In the forefront of the CPI campaign is tribal leader Manish Kunjam, who takes on Congress heavyweight and leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, Mahendra Karma, from Dantewada constituency. Apart from Kunjam in Dantewada, Ramnath Sarfe from Chitrakote-ST, Mahendra Sethia from Jagdalpur, and Rama Sodi from Konta are being seen as candidates with the potential to make a dent in their respective constituencies.

Senior CPI leaders, including Gurudas Dasgupta, have visited Bastar to canvass support for party candidates who have ventured into the inaccessible villages where candidates of other parties were apparently reluctant to go because of the Naxalite threat.

Heading: Expert group gives nod to Injectible Polio Vaccine - Indian Express
Content:
In Mizoram, they address the elderly and the respected with the prefix 'Pu', equivalent to 'Sir' in English. Short of 87 by only three months now, Brigadier Thenphunga Sailo is no ordinary Pu. A former chief minister, and the first Mizo to have risen to the rank of brigadier, Sailo is also a veteran of several wars, including World War II.

And that is the reason why the United Democratic Alliance (UDA), a new non-Congress umbrella outfit, has projected Brigadier Sailo as its candidate for the chief minister's post in the approaching elections in Mizoram. "Brigadier Sailo, in fact, had retired from active politics five years ago, making way for younger people to take over. But the way things are in the state at the end of 10 years of MNF rule, the people have been compelled to recall him," says Clement Lalrema, coordinator of the UDA.

The UDA is a front cobbled by three parties opposed to the return to power of either the ruling Mizo National Front (MNF) or the Congress. The constituents of the UDA are Mizoram People's Conference (MPC), Zoram Nationalist Party (ZNP) and the Zoram Kuthnathawktu Pawl (ZKP) — the last was so far a non-political workers' union.

Born in 1922, Brigadier Sailo, apart from being the first Mizo officer in the Army, also served in the Allied Army in the Burma sector during the World War II. As a brigadier, he is said to have done a commendable job during floods in Bihar and Orissa in the 1960s. Upon retirement in 1974, he returned home to establish the Human Rights Committee (HRC) that aimed to provide relief to people who suffered during counter-insurgency operations carried out by the Army in the then Lushai Hills district of Assam. The Mizo rebellion, in fact, remains the first and only instance in India where the Government deployed the Indian Air Force in counter-insurgency operations.

In 1975, Sailo converted the HRC to People's Conference, a political party that swept the 1978 Assembly elections in Mizoram, by then a Union Territory. His government lasted one full term and then lost to the Congress. Subsequently, Sailo's party was rechristened as the Democratic Party, and later as the Mizoram Janata Dal. A few years later, he renamed the party as the Mizoram People's Conference (MPC), which today is a constituent of the UDA.

The brigadier has some health problems. "But that does not deter him from going out for campaigns. He is not only campaigning for himself, but also for other candidates of the UDA," says Lalrema, pointing out that 'Big Boss' is giving between seven and eight hours a day for the campaign. "It is not a joke for an aged person like him, but his enthusiasm is boosting the campaign further," he says.

"The people are fed up of corruption. First it was the Congress government. And then 10 years of MNF's misrule. It has disgusted and frustrated the people like never before," says Sailo.

He is pitted against Ruatkima, a former general secretary of the Young Mizo Association (YMA) fielded by the MNF, while the Congress has nominated a woman candidate, Lalthankimi, against him in Aizawl West II.

Heading: Trainer MiG crashes in Assam, pilots safe - Indian Express
Content:
In a revolutionary step, the India Expert Advisory Group (IEAG) on polio eradication has given its nod to use Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) for the first time in India. The advisory group has given its approval to use the vaccine in nine high risk districts of western Uttar Pradesh as the test bed for the vaccine in addition to the on going Oral Polio Vaccine drives.

The group had met on November 10 and 11 in Delhi, and the decision came after a detailed discussion on the repercussions of the usage of IPV. The recommendations of the IEAG will now be placed before the Central as well as State Government for final policy decisions. Interestingly, the decision comes just a few days after Bill Gates, chairman of Microsoft and co-chairman of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation gave an assurance of providing adequate funds for developing and using the Injectible Polio Vaccine in India.

Though the need for use of IPV has been felt for long in India, the Government had been hesitant about using it as it was not regarded cost affective in terms of large scale usage. Apart from the cost of the vaccine, trained health workers would be required to administer the IPV as it needs to be injected in the body of the child rather than simply given as an oral polio drop as was the case earlier.

According to experts, IPV is being recommended initially for Uttar Pradesh because as per the initial survey conducted by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) last year, a large number of children in western U P have been found to be resistant to the Oral Polio Vaccine and have stopped responding to it.

"The introduction of IPV in the Indian scenario is long overdue.We plan to take it up probably by the second half of 2009," said Dr RK Agarwal, president Indian Academy of Pediatrician and one of the selected members of the IEAG. According to sources after UP, the next target would be Bihar.

What is IPV?

The Injectible Polio Virus is a dead polio virus - the polio virus is inactivated and thus immunisation with IPV carries no risk of vaccine-associated polio paralysis. On the other hand, the OPV, given as a drop at present in India, is a live virus. The IPV needs to be injected and works by producing protective antibodies in the blood thereby preventing the spread of poliovirus to the central nervous system.

Heading: HRD Ministry mulls PhD tie-up with Microsoft - Indian Express
Content:
A train MiG aircraft crashed in Sivasagar district of Upper Assam on Wednesday morning, but the two pilots managed to bail out and land safely with the help of parachutes, official sources said.

The crash occurred at around 10.25 am and the aircraft was later located near Erenga-Goriapathar village under Mathurapur police station. The two pilots, Squadron Leader Sapandeep and Flight Lieutenant Nandgopan, who were rescued by officials of the Army's 66 Field Regiment located nearby, were later admitted to

Crashes in 2008

January 31: MiG-27 crashed near Hashimara in North Bengal. Wing Commander ejected safely

February 15: MiG-21 crashed near Bhuj in Gujarat. Pilot ejected to safety

April 30: Hawk trainer crashed in Bidar, Karnataka. No serious injury caused to pilots

May 12: HPT Kiran trainer crashed in Medak, Andhra Pradesh. Woman trainee pilot killed

May 23: MiG-21 crashed near Bagdogra. Pilot safe

September 1: MiG-29 fighter aircraft crashed in the Arabian Sea, 50 km west of Jamnagar air base. Pilot ejected safely

November 12: MiG-21 trainer fighter aircraft crashed in upper Assam's Sivasagar. Both pilots bailed out safely the Air Force hospital at Jorhat.

Giving details, Wing Commander R K Singh, PRO at the Indian Air Force's Eastern Command headquarters at Shillong, said over telephone that preliminary reports indicated that the aircraft, a 'type 69' trainer MiG, had an engine failure. "A court of inquiry has been ordered," he said. The aircraft was based at the Chabua base in Dibrugarh district.

Meanwhile, Sivasagar DSP Shyamal Saikia said the aircraft suffered heavy damage and caught fire after it landed in a paddy field, 36 km from Sivasagar town. There was however no civilian casualty, he confirmed. Fire tenders from the ONGC headquarters at Nazira were rushed to the site to douse the fire, he said.

Heading: Probe on as 2,000 trees cut to set up colony - Indian Express
Content:
The Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry is working out ways of cooperation with Microsoft to churn out more PhDs in computer science in the country.

At a brainstorming discussion held in the Ministry on Wednesday, Microsoft's director of strategy at Microsoft Research India Vidya Natampally, along with a set of IIT professors and other experts agreed to work on a programme to address the shortage of researchers in IT . Tentatively termed "PhD Pipeline", this was the first round of discussions between Microsoft, the HRD Ministry and experts to give an impetus to IT research.

"This was a preliminary round of discussion to intensify our efforts to improve research quality in the country. The issue needs to be taken up seriously and modalities of cooperation with Microsoft in the area are being worked out," a senior official said.

While India produces some 200,000 BTechs in the IT/Computer Science/Electrical Engineering streams, there are a mere 50 PhDs per annum in computer science, Vidya Natampally pointed out.

Though India's engineering graduates are increasingly turning towards IT as a career, there are hardly any takers for research in the field leading to a major academic vacuum in the higher education sector."The need for more attention to research is obvious.While in USA there are between 1,500-1,800 PhDs in IT against 75,000 graduates in the field, in India it's just 50 against 200,000 of IT graduates. While we have a whole range of programmes with 16 partner institutions in India, possibilities of a tie-up with the HRD ministry are being discussed," he said.

The Microsoft- HRD ministry discussions come almost a week after Microsoft founder Bill Gates launched 'DreamSpark' in India - a software giveaway for an estimated 10 million-plus qualified students.DreamSpark will provide students free access to the latest Microsoft developer and designer tools . Gates had also addressed IIT, Delhi students and asked India to pump in more money for creating young "brilliant minds" by opening new IITs and universities to provide global level skills.

Heading: 3 run over by BSP MLA’s son - Indian Express
Content:
Authorities in Uttarakhand have initiated a probe into the alleged illegal felling of more than 2,000 trees over the last six months near Gajana village in New Tehri. The felling, allegedly for developing a new private colony, apparently took place in connivance with officials of the Forest Department in the district. According to sources, the colony is being developed by one Virender Singh Sajwan alias Pappu and some senior forest officers supposedly have plots in the colony.

"I have ordered a probe into this serious matter. The information is that more than 2,000 trees were chopped while the permission was sought for cutting only 40 trees. I have detailed the Additional District Magistrate and Chief Development Officers to go to the spot and count the trees that have been chopped," said Tehri District Magistrate Saujanya. She has called for all the notifications and orders related to the development of the colony. "We need to investigate what permissions were sought and what was granted over the period of time," the DM said.

The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) RBS Rawat said that forest authorities had also taken a serious note of the incident and that a departmental probe had been initiated into the matter. "Initial findings have revealed that the trees were cut on a private piece of land. But cutting of trees in excess of the permission granted by the department is a serious matter and we are investigating it on priority," he said.

Meanwhile, Sajwan has claimed that the colony was being developed on private land and only those many trees were being

chopped for which permission had been granted by the administration.

Heading: First instance of poll violence in J-K - Indian Express
Content:
Rivals and biggest names in Bihar politics — Lalu Prasad, Ram Vilas Paswan and Nitish Kumar — shared a common platform yet again, this time to pave way for the state's development.

The occasion was laying the foundation stone for reconstruction of Rs 3,200-crore fertilizer plant at Barauni, approved by the Union Cabinet recently. The plant is due to be completed in four years.

While the Chief Minister's presence is being taken as Paswan's big gesture to keep Nitish in good faith, the coming together of Lalu and Paswan, RJD and LJP sources said, hinted towards the two parties planning to share Lok Sabha seats in their bid to get maximum votes.

Sharing the dais, the three leaders were unanimous on "not playing politics" for the development of the state. The Chief Minister responded to Paswan's invitation by announcing to waive off Rs 275-crore electricity bills due against the fertilizer company.

Nitish said: "I will always take a step forward if it is about the state's development. I do not understand why Laluji does not invite me to his railway functions. After all, I will end up praising him." He, however, said that he won't spare either "Laluji, whose party still talks of lantern (RJD symbol) when it's time for electricity, or Paswanji at the hustings".

When it was Lalu's turn, he offered to play elder brother to Nitish. "Nitishji keeps committing mistakes, but I forgive him because he is my younger brother."

LJP President Ram Vilas Paswan too assured the state of "zero politics on development". He said the fertilizer plant would help realize a big dream for the state and employ over 25,000 people.

Heading: The Raman Effect - Indian Express
Content:
In the first instance of poll violence in the state, unidentified persons hurled a grenade on National Conference (NC) candidate Mubarak Gul in Srinagar on Wednesday. No one was injured in the attack. Police said the incident took place minutes after Gul went inside a party worker's house in the Eidgah locality of the old city in the afternoon. Gul is the NC nominee from Eidgah constituency which will go to polls in the last phase.

"The grenade was tossed towards the house where Gul was staying, but it missed the target and exploded in a nearby compound," a police spokesperson in Srinagar said. "No one was injured in the blast but window panes of some houses nearby were damaged."

SP (North) Abdul Waheed Shah said that the police has registered a case and investigations have begun. No arrests have been made yet.

Heading: Biggest photo journalism awards on Nov 14 - Indian Express
Content:
Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Raman Singh appears well poised in this constituency where he is pitted against sitting Congress legislator Uday Mudaliar in a multi-cornered contest. Rajnandgaon goes to polls on November 14.

In 1998, this region had given a boost to Singh's political career when he defeated Congress stalwart Motilal Vora to enter Parliament and become a minister in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee ministry. Now, in 2007, it is here that he has initiated his son Abhishek, who along with his mother Veena Singh, is heading the poll campaign.

"I am indebted to this constituency, which helped me defeat a Congress heavyweight like Motilal Vora. It was a turning point in my political life," says Singh. "It's the reason I preferred to contest from here, after shifting from the Dongergaon constituency."

While Singh is busy canvassing support in the remaining 89 constituencies across the state, his wife and son have extensively toured Rajnandgaon which comprises a municipal corporation and 82 village panchayats. The delimitation exercise did not affect this assembly segment, which has an electorate of 1,65,211 voters, including 82,199 women voters. The region was ruled by Vaishnav Rajas; the town was home to famous Hindi litterateurs and poets such as Padamlal Punnalal Bakshi, Gajanand Muktibodh, Baldev Prasad Mishra and Nannulal Chotiya.

In the last five years, Rajnandgaon has developed into the state's educational hub with seven engineering colleges and one ayurvedic college coming up in the private sector. BJP workers claim the credit goes to Singh — an ayurvedic physician-turned-politician — as these institutions got the necessary clearances without delay.

At Thakurtola village, a large number of people, mostly women, wait for the arrival of Veena Singh at night. Seeking votes for the Chief Minister in the local Chhattisgarhi dialect, she promises, "After the election, Doctor Sahib and I will first go to the village which gave him the highest number of votes. Do you want to invite us first?" At another village, Singh's son Abhishek, an engineering graduate, receives a rousing welcome from party workers. Then he is taken around the village and introduced to people.

At least a few local BJP leaders are concerned about the Chief Minister's family members becoming active in politics. But they remain tightlipped for obvious reasons. "It seems that Dr Sahib has placed his handkerchief on both the Assembly and Lok Sabha seats, just as people occupy seats in buses," says one.

While the welfare schemes and other initiatives launched by Singh during his five-year tenure are the focus of the BJP campaign, the Chief Minister has now promised the people of this constituency that he will set up a steel plant — bigger than the public sector Bhilai Steel Plant in neighbouring Durg district — if the BJP retains power.

Congress candidate Uday Mudaliar — who won the December 2003 polls by a wafer-thin margin of 40 votes — faces a Herculean task this time because of the presence of the Chief Minister in the fray. "My poll plank is corruption as people in this district are aware about the level of corruption that prevailed during the BJP regime," he says. Mudaliar is concentrating on making personal contact with voters, village to village, instead of resorting to show of strength that usually takes place in any VIP constituency. His son and other family members are also canvassing support for him.

Among the other 12 candidates in the fray, the BSP has fielded Maulesh Tiwari to test his electoral fortunes from this constituency. Conspicuous by his absence during the election campaign is former BJP MP from Rajnandgaon, Pradeep Gandhi, who was expelled from the Lok Sabha and later from the party following his involvement in the cash-for-query scam. Considered close to Singh, it was Gandhi who vacated his Dongergaon Assembly seat to enable the Chief Minister to contest the Assembly bypolls after his election as BJP legislature party leader in December 2003.

Heading: From Assam to Kerala, via ‘missed call’, love finds a way - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Express Group once again lets pictures do the talking with The India Press Photo Awards 2008, instituted by the Ramnath Goenka Foundation in 2004 to identify, promote and reward excellence in photojournalism and documentary photography.

Cloistered for three days in a conference room at the Taj President, Mumbai, the three judges—photojournalists Prashant Panjiar, Pablo Bartholomew and Harsh Man Rai—sifted through 8,801 entries by 226 photographers to come up with one grand prize-winning image and one winner from each of the 18 categories.

The awards will be announced on November 14 in Mumbai.

The winners that emerged have set a new precedent for photojournalists, both established and aspiring.

"Despite the two-year gap after which this competition has come about, I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of work and the innovation in ideas, image-making and story construction," says Pablo Bartholomew, whose image of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy in 1984 won the World Press Photo's Picture of the Year Award.

The judging process was intense—the photographs had to pass through three rounds of scrutiny. But it was after the first round that the judges felt "the need to reward novelty".

"Photojournalists have always dared to experiment. But in the past 15 years, the work of photojournalists have stagnated and story-telling in photojournalism has become old-fashioned," says Prashant Panjiar, who has served on the jury of several photo awards, including the World Press Photo Awards in 2002 and the Ramnath Goenka Press Photo Awards 2004-2006.

On the need to encourage innovation, Pablo says, "By 'new', we mean a different kind of treatment and approach to stories, the courage to shoot out-of-the-box ideas and images that are powerful while being part of a story." The judges maintained that while classic journalism wasn't bad, it tends to get repetitive and clichéd. So the small number that bucked that trend was noticed and they are the ones who will walk away with most of the honours.

Harsh Man Rai, the third judge on the panel, is the Group Creative Director of Man's World and Verve magazines.

Shailendre Pandey of Amar Ujala won the Picture of the Year for 2004. His picture of a young boy crying on the telephone as he informs his relatives of his sister's suicide—her body is seen hanging from the fan in the same frame—presents the news in its darkest reality. In 2006, Vipin Pawar of DNA won the Picture of the Year for his picture of the Gateway of India stabbing incident.

Heading: India unveils n-capable Shourya - Indian Express
Content:
Ordinarily Abdul Nazer and Bairabi Daveri would have never met; then, "love" found a way. He was a Muslim youth from Kerala working in a hotel in Bangalore, she a Hindu mother living in an Assam village. One day in early August, a "missed call" from her to him bridged all that separated the 29-year-old Nazer and Bairabi, 24.

She was dialling a relative's number in Karnataka when she realised she had got the wrong number, and disconnected. That was Nazer's number. Curious, he called back. Bairabi apologised, he answered in Hindi, and the two got talking.

What started that day has now led to a hunt from Assam to Chavakkad in Kerala for Nazer and Bairabi, who are now living together. Bairabi's first husband, Damanan Daveri, a constable, is determined to bring her back to his home and their two little daughters. Three days ago he came to Chavakkad with an Assam Police squad to take Bairabi, now converted and called Fathima, back. After Bairabi testified that she had gone to Nazer of her free will, a local court released them.

After fleeing her Assam village, Bairabi had lived for a while in Bangalore with Nazer. Daveri traced them the same way as they had met, through mobile phone details. He first went to Karnataka, and after a call made by Bairabi to Assam was found to have come from Kerala, he landed in Chavakkad — Nazer's native place.

According to the Chavakkad police, the Assam Police had come looking for Nazer and Bairabi based on Daveri's complaint that his wife had been kidnapped. "Daveri had no idea of the person with whom his wife had eloped. He told the police his wife had taken away gold ornaments and cash," police sources said.

However, when the Assam Police produced the duo at a local judicial court at Chavakkad, they had nothing to prove the charges. They could not even produce a copy of the FIR filed by Daveri. After Bairabi told the court she hadn't been kidnapped and left on her own, the court released them.

Afraid that Daveri may return with a fresh copy of the FIR from Assam, Nazer and Fathima have gone into hiding.

Heading: All hands on deck in Mayawati’s poll plan - Indian Express
Content:
India has test-fired a new nuclear capable surface-to-surface missile that will enhance its second strike capability and hit targets within a range of 600 km. The 'Shourya' missile system was test-fired from the Interim Test Range at Balasore in Orissa on Wednesday morning by DRDO.

The test came as a surprise to experts as the previously unknown missile system has never been discussed by DRDO scientists.The Shourya has been described as a canister launched short-range surface-to-surface missile and appears to be a variant of an existing missile system already in service with the Army.

"The DRDO has termed as successful the flight-test of the 'Shourya' missile system. This developmental flight trial of 'Shourya' missile system is a part of the ongoing technology development work undertaken by the DRDO," a Defence Ministry statement said.

What makes the missile unique is the canister system that makes it easy to transport and hide from the enemy. The missile would not need an elaborate launching pad system and would be easier to fire from hidden locations and underground facilities.

The canister would also make it easier to transport and give it a longer service life, DRDO says. "The missile has a unique feature of simplicity of operation and maintenance. It can be easily handled, transported and stored within the canister for longer shelf life," the DRDO spokesperson said.

Experts say the missile is designed for easier storage and transport to enhance India's second strike capability of responding to a nuclear attack. "The missile would be easier to hide from the enemy and with the canister system will be capable of being fired from underground locations. Given India's no-first-use policy, it would form a crucial part of the nuclear arsenal," a missile expert said.

The importance of the system can be gauged from the fact that the Defence Minister termed it as a 'milestone' while congratulating DRDO scientists. "The successful test-firing of the new state-of-the-art canisterised missile marks another milestone in the country's missile programme," Antony said in a message to DRDO.

Heading: Reveal way of arriving at CAT answers: CIC - Indian Express
Content:
Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati's MPs, MLAs are working over time for the Assembly elections in five states. Jobs have been allotted to each minister, MP and MLA and each Bhaichara Committee coordinator, with a special mention not to violate the EC's guidelines. Mayawati has instructed her MLAs to gather in Delhi on November 14 when they will be allotted different duties.

On Sunday, Mayawati started her poll campaign by holding her first election rally in Durg, Raipur (Chhattisgarh). In her programme schedule, Madhya Pradesh is slated for November 17 and 24, and the proposed dates for Rajasthan are November 26 and December 4.

"She will be addressing five public meetings in each state," said a party leader. Her trusted lieutenant Satish Chandra Mishra, whose duties have not been defined, is expected to accompany her in most of these meetings.

The party had deployed state in-charges in Delhi, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh (the states which are going to the polls, along with Mizoram) immediately after winning a majority in the UP state Assembly last year, party insiders said. They are more or less camping in these states since then.

Cabinet ministers Badshah Singh and Rangnath Mishra, have been camping in MP while Cabinet minister Nakul Dubey and Sewa Ram are spending most of their time in Chhattisgarh. Aligarh MLA Mahendra Singh and Ganga Charan Dinkar, are working as permanent in-charges of Delhi.

Party sources confirmed that Mayawati herself is spending her weekends in Delhi for the last year. Working on the formula of social engineering, the BSP chief has given specific caste-wise duties to senior party leaders like Naseemuddin Siddiqui, who is working to woo Muslim voters and is sorting out election-related preparation in each state. Brajesh Pathak is working to bring in Brahmin voters for the party while Cabinet minister Anant Kumar Mishra who was earlier roped in for Rajasthan, has now been deployed in Delhi. Paras Nath Maurya, chairman Pichhara Varg Ayog, and Cabinet minister and the party's state president Swami Prasad Maurya are regularly touring states to woo the backward communities.

Heading: Polls knocking, Cong shuts the door on Alva - Indian Express
Content:
Taking the process of transparency in the prestigious Common Admission Test (CAT) a step further, the IIMs may soon have to reveal the rationale behind the 'answer key' to the CATquestions. Applicant Gautam Puri, MD of Career Launcher, a coaching institute for CAT aspirants, has filed an RTI application before the Central Information Commission (CIC) to get IIMs to explain in detail the basis of selecting/deciding upon the right answers against which all CAT aspirants are judged.

While IIMs have been keeping the logic behind the 'answer key' a secret claiming that the answer key selection process record is destroyed immediately after the exam, CIC has directed IIMs to provide the guidelines on the basis of which this documentation is destroyed. Under section section 19(8)(a) of the RTI, the CIC is empowered to direct a public authority to take steps to make "necessary changes to its practices in relation to the maintenance, management and destruction of records."

Heading: Sena in, BJP keeps off CM meet on ‘outsider’ issue - Indian Express
Content:
Congress president Sonia Gandhi on Wednesday accepted Margaret Alva's resignation as AICC general secretary "with immediate effect" and also relieved her from the membership of the Congress Working Committee (CWC) and the Central Election Committee (CEC) on grounds of indiscipline.

The Congress high command's decision came a day after Alva submitted her resignation to Sonia and less than a week after she made the controversial allegation about sale of party tickets in the last Assembly elections in Karnataka. Disciplinary Action Committee chairman A K Antony had on Tuesday evening submitted his findings to the Congress president.

With a host of disgruntled party leaders from Karnataka, including R L Jalappa and Siddaramaiah, as also others like AICC Scheduled Castes Cell chairman Yogendra Makwana coming out in Alva's support, the ruling party at the Centre decided to crack the whip on her immediately so as to send strong signals to those rising in rebellion. The party was very anxious about the possible fallout of this controversy in the ensuing Assembly elections.

According to sources, Alva was told to put in her papers when she met Sonia on Monday evening to explain the reasons for her outburst.

"She (Alva) also realised that she had committed some mistake somewhere and, therefore, she had offered her resignation. Going to the media maligns the party's image," said AICC spokesperson Shakeel Ahmed. Asked if the Congress still considers her a loyal and committed party leader, he said: "She is still in the party. She is a loyal worker. Posts come and go."

To a question if the party would institute any inquiry into the allegations of sale of tickets, Ahmed said: "At this stage we don't think there is any need of any inquiry."

Consequent upon Alva's resignation, the high command gave temporary charge of the seven states under her to other leaders. While Antony was given Maharashtra, Motilal Vora got Haryana, Mohsina Kidwai Punjab and Chandigarh, and Oscar Fernandes Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland.

There was jubilation in the Vilasrao Deshmukh camp in Maharashtra over Alva's exit, as she had repeatedly called for the Chief Minister's removal and was crucial in bringing his rival, Narayan Rane, into the party fold.

Heading: Tapasi murder convicts awarded life imprisonment - Indian Express
Content:
Under fire after the Maharashtra Navanirman Sena (MNS) launched its anti-north Indian campaign, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Wednesday called an all-party meeting to discuss the issue and lead an all-party delegation to Governor S C Jamir to protest the wrong impression being created about the state by leaders from other states.

While the BJP boycotted the meeting and the delegation, the Shiv Sena attended the meeting. Earlier, the BJP had boycotted the all-party meeting held at Mantralaya, while leader of the Opposition Ramdas Kadam (Sena) attended it to attack the Congress-NCP-led state Government for its failure to maintain law and order.

The BJP has cited the state Government's inconsistency on the issue to boycott the meeting and delegation and has alleged that the Congress-NCP Government was fuelling the MNS agitation.

Kadam told reporters that the state Government had failed to maintain law and order and justified his party's move to stay away from the meeting with the Governor on grounds that it was now the Government's job "to wipe the sin off". On being questioned whether there was a rift between the Sena and the BJP over attending the meeting, Kadam said instead of boycotting the meeting, he had been present and taken the state Government to task.

Speaking to reporters after his meeting with the Governor, Deshmukh said the MNS agitation was the result of a tiff between the two (Thackeray) brothers and it was for this reason that the Sena had stayed away from the meeting. He said politicians from Bihar need not worry about the security of their people in Maharashtra, as the state Government can look into the issue.

The memorandum presented to the Governor said, "The allegations about people from other states residing in Maharashtra feeling not secure are false. The culture and tradition of Maharashtra were never narrow or parochial and that efforts to defame Maharashtra on this issue may endanger our national unity and integrity." Deshmukh requested the Governor to convey the same to the President and Prime Minister.

Heading: Presence of Indians on sub possible: Russian expert - Indian Express
Content:
The two convicts in the Tapasi Malik murder case, CPI(M) Hoogly district committee member Suhrid Dutta and his aide Debu Malik, were on Wednesday sentenced to life imprisonment by Additional District and Session Judge of Chandernagore first fast track court.

The judge, Amar Kanti Acharya, however, turned down CBI counsel Partha Tapaswi's appeal that it was a "rarest of rare" case and deserved capital punishment.

The judge observed that the murder took place because of personal reasons and could not be called a political murder.

Besides life imprisonment, the two convicts were asked to pay a fine of Rs 10,000 each. The advocates of both the accused said they would move higher courts to challenge the verdict.

Apprehending law and order trouble, prohibitory orders under Section 144 of CrPC were imposed around Chandernagore sub-divisional court premises on Wednesday. Hundreds of supporters, both from the Trinamool Congress and the CPI(M), had come to Chandernagore to witness the court proceeding.

Both Dutta and Malik were later taken to Chandernagore sub-divisional correctional home.

Describing the judgment as a "gross miscarriage of justice", Dutta's advocate Arindam Bhattacharjee said, "We would move the Calcutta High Court against the verdict of the trial court. It was a case of acquittal because there was no direct evidence against Dutta."

Malik's advocate, Kishor Mondal, said, "The verdict was given on the basis of circumstantial evidence. We will go to higher court."

The victim's family in Singur welcomed the judgment. "We are happy to hear that the murderers have been awarded life imprisonment. We are also thankful to the CBI for handling the case in the right way. The CID officers, in fact, tried to establish that my daughter had actually committed suicide. The Chief Minister should step down," Manoranjan Malik, Tapasi's father, said.

Heading: Gyanendra may enter politics to ‘serve nation’ - Indian Express
Content:
Amidst Russian media reports that the Russian K-152 Nerpa nuclear attack submarine was to be transferred to India after current sea trials, the possibility of Indian naval personnel having been on board the sub has not been ruled out by Russian experts.

However, soon after the accident the Indian Navy had immediately issued a statement saying that there had been no Indians on board.

A Russian expert, on condition of anonymity, said that in the past Indian teams had been on board the vessels ordered by them. "The Indian Navy, which was to get the submarine some time next year, was monitoring its completion at the shipyard in Komsomolsk-on-Amur and trials of its various systems at all stages, and their presence on board during trials was quite possible," he said.

A local daily close to the Kremlin reported on Wednesday that the submarine, that had met with an accident on Saturday night, was to be leased to India for 10 years. An agreement to this effect was to be signed after the completion of the sea trials in the Sea of Japan.

On late Saturday night 20 people including 17 civilian technicians, had been killed and 21 injured due to an abrupt release of deadly Freon gas in the sub. Russia has been keeping the nuclear submarine lease deal under wraps, unlike Indian diplomatic and naval officials, who said it was part of the Gorshkov package signed in January 2004.

Heading: 'I never did films for cash, but it'll be nice to be rich' - Indian Express
Content:
Nepal's dethroned king, Gyanendra, will enter active politics soon as the people will push Gyanendra to "serve the nation", a top aide of the former monarch has said.

"He is silent for a while," Faniraj Pathak, former press secretary of the Narayanhiti royal palace said, adding that Gyanendra will not remain silent for long.

"Just like the former Cambodian king, he will enter national politics sooner rather than later, people themselves will pull Gyanendra into politics to serve the nation," he was quoted as saying by Kantipur online on Wednesday.

Royalists claim Gyanendra will join active politics. Pathak said there are people who wish the former king should speak his mind. That is why he is mooting the issue, the former royal aide stressed. He underlined that just like former monarchs in India, Gyanendra will serve the nation by embarking upon active politics one day.

Pathak said according to his understanding the former royal family will actively participate in serving the nation in a new role. "The former crown prince and princess or new (junior) crown prince or princess will definitely be active in the country's politics, if not the former king or queen," said Pathak.

Gyanendra has been living a simple and easy life since he shifted from the Narayanhiti Palace in central Kathmandu to the Nagarjuna forest lodge on the outskirts of the capital in June, according to sources in Nepal's Armed Police Force, which is tasked to provide security to Gyanendra.

"There is no sign of stress on his face. He looks like he looked in the Narayanhiti," said Prof Madhav Bhattarai, the former palace priest (Nayab Bada-Guruji).

According to Bhattarai, the former king's daily routine includes writing poetry, performing pooja, surfing the Internet and observing and enjoying the natural scenery around the palace. He spends more time in reading books and worshiping.

Heading: McCain defends Palin on TV show - Indian Express
Content:
As he wandered around the slums of Mumbai, Simon Beaufoy, smallish, blondish English screenwriter, noticed packs of stray dogs lining the tiny, crowded alleyways.

"The dogs would sit in the sun, apparently asleep," he says. "They were really mangy. Absolutely rabies-on-legs-type dogs. And you had to tread carefully over them... They always appeared to be asleep, but if you looked closely, you'd see one of their eyes a tiny bit open. They were watching everything."

"It was a nice metaphor for the lowest of the low," Beaufoy recalls, "for this person who apparently knows nothing, who is worthless, but actually he's been watching all his life, and he knows everything."

That's why Beaufoy coined the title 'Slumdog Millionaire' for the name of his new movie, directed by Danny Boyle. Slumdog refers to the title character, Jamal, a street urchin who claws his way into adulthood and winds up a contestant on the Indian version of the game show 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire'. Jamal is poised to win Rs 20 million when he's arrested and accused of cheating.

Slumdog is based loosely on Q&A: A Novel, a collection of short stories, by Vikas Swarup. Aside from the original conceit, the operatic, kinetic narrative of the film springs from Beaufoy, who deftly balances a fusion of memory and reality, of Jamal's nerve-racking stint on the TV show, his brutal police interrogation, the story of his hardscrabble life and the idiosyncratic fashion by which he's come to know the answers to the questions.

The film evokes "the rapacious development" of modern India. "The place is on steroids," says the writer, who immersed himself for weeks in the neighbourhoods of Mumbai, listening to conversations at tea stands.

"You have to be careful making that kind of film that you don't parachute yourself in as a middle class white guy from London," he says.

Beaufoy started out as a documentary filmmaker. The filmmakers were shocked when their $3.5-million indie, 1997's 'The Full Monty', turned into a worldwide sensation, grossing about $257 million. Before the film's release, Beaufoy was so broke that he sold his share in the project — for a mere 500 pounds — an interest that wound up being worth millions.

"I never did a film for cash, though it would be nice to be very rich... I didn't come here because I wasn't good enough technically. I felt that I had to go away and learn to write." Beaufoy stayed in England making small films that interested him.

"You can't do subtext and nuance in India. You have to be operatic and dramatic. It's no coincidence that all these Bollywood films have singing and dancing. I was infused. I was writing in a way I hadn't written before."

"I never felt sorry for a single person I met," Beaufoy says. "...you expect to wander the slums and see all these poor people and go, 'Isn't it sad.' You don't feel that for a minute. They're all living their lives."

Heading: McCain camp approached me for V-P, but I declined: Jindal - Indian Express
Content:
John McCain announced that he would run for President in February 2007 on The Late Show With David Letterman on CBS. On Tuesday, in his first public appearance since he delivered his concession speech November 4, he provided a bookend to his campaign on The Tonight Show With Jay Leno on NBC.

Aside from wryly indicting his own "personality", McCain declined to speculate on why he lost the election.

He defended his running mate Sarah Palin, whom some of his own aides have blamed for his defeat. He said he "couldn't be happier with Sarah Palin" and identifying her as part of a group of young governors, including Bobby Jindal of Louisiana and Tim Pawlenty of Minnesota, who represent "the next generation of our party".

He added: "Our party has a lot of work to do. We just got back from the woodshed."

McCain also recycled a joke he repeatedly used on the trail to describe his state of mind after his loss in the 2000 Republican presidential primaries.

"I've been sleeping like a baby," he said. "Sleep two hours, wake up and cry."

McCain praised Obama as inspiring "millions of young people" and echoed the call for unity from his concession speech: "Now it's time for America to join together and support the man who was just elected President."

Saying that the "one thing Americans don't want is a sore loser", McCain spoke of returning to the Senate.

Heading: Americans clamouring for all things Obama - Indian Express
Content:
Indian-American Governor of Louisiana, Bobby Jindal, has disclosed that he was approached by the McCain campaign to be a possible running mate of the Republican nominee in the November 4 polls, but he declined the offer as he was satisfied with his current position.

"They actually contacted me and asked me to be vetted. And we politely declined. I said I was honoured that they wanted me to do that, but the reality is that I do have the job that I want. I've been Governor for about a year now," he told MSNBC when asked if he was surprised when the Republicans did not even attempt to vet him.

The 37-year-old Louisiana Governor said he was "flattered" when he was asked to be vetted. But, added that "I told them what I said all along, which was that I've got the job that I want. I certainly support the ticket, but didn't want to be part of the ticket... I was even flattered to be mentioned in the same sentence with some of those other names."

The election of Obama as the 44th President of the US has started off a thinking in many quarters that anything is possible in the American democracy and that someone like Jindal could make it to the Oval Office in the near future.

Jindal argued that one would have to look past the McCain campaign to see why the party lost on November 4.

"I don't think it was just about the campaign. When you look at the Republican party, there are basically three things we've got to correct for us to start winning elections again.

Number one, our actions have to match our rhetoric," Jindal said.

"The Republican party has talked about spending discipline, cutting taxes and yet we were defending out-of-control spending in Washington we would have rightfully criticised in the other party," he said while listing his reasons for the loss of the party in the polls.

About the number two step, Jindal said, the Republicans have to root out corruption within their own ranks. "A week before the election, you've got our most senior Senator (Republican Ted Stevens) convicted of federal charges. We can't defend behaviour again that we would rightfully criticise on the other side."

"Most importantly, we again have to be the party of solutions. We have to apply our conservative principles to the challenges that are confronting the American people, whether it's the rising cost of healthcare, whether it's the economy, whether it's international challenges. We have to show real solutions. It's not enough — you can't win an election simply by criticising the other side."

Jindal said McCain and Sarah Palin were "very gracious" on election night. "I think it's so important.

We need to support the President-elect, the new Congress. The election is over. Whether you voted for the President-elect or not, we all need to support him. We need him to be successful."

Heading: Obamas drive magazine sales - Indian Express
Content:
Much as Barack Obama has kindled unprecedented interest in presidential politics, so too has he prompted a flood of merchandise, collectibles, television deals and book contracts.

Presidents always have inspired such capitalism. But marketing experts say the historic nature of this election and the strong brand that the campaign cultivated have sparked incredible demand for all things Obama.

"It's the biggest thing for publishing since Harry Potter," said Dermot McEvoy, a senior editor at Publishers Weekly, an industry trade journal.

The effects of Obamamania are trickling down. Vendors have taken to the streets and the Internet to sell Obama-themed T-shirts, buttons, bobblehead dolls, coffee mugs, wine bottles, magnets, greeting cards, neon signs, mobile phones and framed art prints. Despite worries about the economy, consumers are snapping them up.

"This is phenomenal. I've never seen anything like it in my life," said Edward Robert El, 64, a street vendor in downtown Los Angeles. He sold more than 3,000 buttons with photos of Obama and the Rev Martin Luther King Jr.

He was selling the buttons, which cost him 80 cents/piece, for $3 on Friday outside the Los Angeles Times building.

At least nine books about the President-elect and the 2008 campaign are coming out in the next few months, McEvoy said, including The Obama Menu: Dinners with Barack Obama and Deciding the Next Decider: The 2008 Presidential Race in Rhyme.

Some journalists covering the campaign have struck deals for books about Obama, including Newsweek magazine White House correspondent Richard Wolffe and Time magazine senior political analyst Mark Halperin, and more are expected.

PublicAffairs, a New York publishing house that focuses on political books, will release A Long Time Coming: The Historic, Combative, Expensive and Inspiring 2008 Election and the Victory of Barack Obama, by Evan Thomas and the staff of Newsweek, and reprint a paperback version of a book co-written by Rahm Emanuel, Obama's new Chief of Staff.

"People are interested in Obama and his victory in a distinctly unusual way," PublicAffairs founder Peter Osnos said.

The TV business is getting in on it. Two days after the election, HBO announced that it had acquired an untitled documentary about Obama's campaign that was produced by actor Edward Norton's production company, Class 5 Films.

There are undoubtedly more video compilations of Obama's campaign events and speeches to come, said Peter Sealey, professor of marketing at Claremont Graduate University.

Heading: Palin rehashes 2008, rehearses for 2012 - Indian Express
Content:
People magazine featured Barack Obama on its latest cover. There's something familiar about the upcoming issue of Us Weekly.

For the second week in a row, and the third time in six months, Barack Obama is pictured on the magazine's cover, this time in a white oxford shirt, hugging his daughters, Malia and Sasha.

Last week, President-elect Obama appeared with his wife, Michelle, under the headline, "Their Amazing Journey."

Last week's issue sold more than 1.1 million copies on the newsstand. That is just about what the magazine sells when it puts its array of Hollywood celebrities on the cover.

The Obamas' starring role is not just about magazine sales. It also reflect the rise of politics as an entertainment theme.

Heading: Obama won’t meet G20 leaders at summit - Indian Express
Content:
One of the more disconcerting leaks about Sarah Palin turned out to be true. Palin arrived in Phoenix on election night hoping to deliver her own concession speech. "It was a great speech," Palin told Matt Lauer on the Today show on Tuesday.

Aides to McCain told her it was not customary for the No 2 to speak. She said: "But, you know, I thought, even if it was unprecedented, so what, you know?" Palin told Lauer. "Geez, let's do something a little bit out of the box there." And now she is. Palin is on a speed date with history. She put herself on full display, in interviews with NBC and Fox News before McCain had a chance to take a no-victory lap on The Tonight Show. Palin could be turning to television to restore her tarnished image, jumpstart a 2012 presidential bid, or both. Palin's interviews dragged the subject back to her campaign woes. "I'm like, 'OK, God, if there is an open door for me somewhere... Don't let me miss the open door'... 'And if there is an open door in '12 or four years later... then I'll plow through that door'."

Heading: His team moves to keep distance from lobbyists - Indian Express
Content:
The world is waiting for President-elect Barack Obama, and some of its most prominent leaders are flying into the United States this weekend clamoring to meet him. But they will have to keep on waiting.

The leaders of 19 foreign powers — including Britain, France, Germany, Russia and China — converge on Washington on Friday for an emergency economic summit meeting hosted by President Bush. Although invited, Obama has opted to stay in Chicago and will not meet any of the leaders separately.

Coming so soon after last week's election, the summit meeting has proved an uncomfortable moment for the President-elect and an early test of his handling of international diplomacy. Even as aides are closing his campaign headquarters and just beginning to assemble a governing team, they are fending off interest from foreign governments eager to take the measure of Obama and trying to avoid tying him to the Bush administration.

Several Obama advisors used the word "awkward" to describe the situation. But Robert Gibbs, a senior advisor to Obama, said: "While some may say it's awkward that he's not there, it would be far more problematic to be there. We firmly believe there is only one President at a time."

The situation has already fostered misunderstandings. A Kremlin official told reporters in Moscow that President Dmitri A Medvedev of Russia would probably meet Obama during his trip to the US this weekend, even though the Obama camp has ruled that out.

The potential for even more significant misunderstanding was underscored last weekend when a quick, seemingly perfunctory telephone call by Obama returning the congratulatory call of Poland's President led to a dispute about what was said about missile defence. If confusion over such a delicate issue could arise from a roughly five-minute phone call, Obama advisors reasoned, then the prospect of longer encounters in person with foreign leaders at this point would be fraught with peril. He has not even designated a Secretary of State, Treasury Secretary or National Security Advisor.

Instead, the Obama team is scrambling to arrange for surrogates to meet with visiting foreign officials while emphasising that Bush remains the nation's leader until January 20. "It's not appropriate for two people to show up for this meeting," said John D Podesta, co-chairman of Obama's transition team.

The White House expressed no disappointment and vowed to work closely with the President-elect. "We continue to work with the transition team on the financial summit and will keep them up to date," said Gordon Johndroe, a White House spokesman. Foreign affairs veterans said Obama was trying to avoid being forced to take positions on matters he is not yet authorised to decide, much less take ownership for the problems and decisions of Bush.

"I sort of understand why he can't go to that meeting," said Rep Howard L Berman, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. "What if the administration makes a suggestion that he doesn't agree with? Should he pop up and say something? Is his silence acquiescence? I think he's making the right call."

The period between an election and inauguration has often fostered tension when it comes to foreign affairs. Lyndon B Johnson wanted his successor to support peace talks with North Vietnam and arms talks with the Soviet Union, but Richard M Nixon undercut those efforts. The first President Bush sent troops to Somalia after his re-election defeat but before Bill Clinton's inauguration.

The protocol for making first contacts with foreign leaders can be complicated and delicate. New presidents have traditionally made Canada's prime minister the first foreign leader they meet with after taking office, a nod to its singular status as the nation's neighbour and trading partner.

Obama called for "a globally coordinated effort with our partners in the G-20" during a campaign stop in Miami in September.
