"Since Sujata was suffering from thalassaemia, her immunity was very low. She was susceptible to viral attack," said Deb Dwaipayan Chattopadhya, Chief Municipal Health Officer.

"Even then she was not tested for malaria or dengue. This is why the hospital authorities have mentioned 'unknown fever' as the cause of death," he added.

Heading: ‘Every time a blast takes place his name crops up... when the Assam blasts took place, I got scared’ - Indian Express
Content:
The members of Santal Engineering Students' Association have denied the involvement of Maoists in the tribal movement in West Midnapore.

Altogether, there are 425 Santal students — members of different Santal associations — studying in different engineering colleges in West Bengal. Ten of them reached Jhargram early on Thursday morning, the others will be there by Friday.

Rupchand Saren, a final-year student of Bengal Engineering and Science University, said the police and the administration are labelling tribals in West Midnapore, Bankura and Purulia as Maoists. Over the last few years, they have been harassed by police every time there is a blast or a murder. The Salboni blast was no exception.

Claiming that the tribals in West Bengal have been oppressed for long, he described the movement in Lalgarh as an outburst of their grievances. The movement has found support from different social organisations in Kolkata.

Heading: PETA activists hold protest outside KFC outlet - Indian Express
Content:
Express meets 62-year old Ishaq Ali Khan, father of Amir Reza Khan, head of the Indian Mujahideen and accused in American Center attack

Every year since his son had left home in 2001 on the day of Eid, he sits near the telephone, waiting for him to call. And when the calls come he and his wife talk for over an hour. This year too, he waited. But no call came.

But Ishaq Ali Khan, father of Amir Reza Khan who has been accused in several cases of terror attacks in India, including the attack on American Center in 2002, has not lost hope.

"I am sure he will call on Bakr-Eid," 62-year old Ishaq, who runs a business in building materials, told The Indian Express, sitting in his Beniapukur home in central Kolkata.

Apart from his alleged involvement in the American Center attack, Amir has also been accused of being involved in the abduction of Kolkata shoe merchant Partha Roy Burman in 2001. He was one of the seven who had been served with a death sentence in the American Center attack case.

And it's he and Hasan Imam who still elude the police.

Only last week Mohammed Sadiq alias Sadaqat, who shot dead six cops in the American Center attack, was caught by the Mumbai police.

Amir, according to the police, is the head of the Indian Mujahideen, suspected to be behind the recent serial blasts across the country.

Ishaq says he gets scared whenever a blast takes place.

"Every time a blast takes place his name crops up. When the Assam blasts took place, I got scared thinking that his name would come up. He is touted as the head of Indian Mujahideen but let me tell you, he never cared even for his mohallah. He was quite an introvert. How can a person like him head an all-Indian organisation?" he asked.

Ishaq Ali Khan stays with his wife Hasina Khanam. He had five sons —- Asif Reza Khan who was also involved in the abduction of Partha Roy Burman and was later shot dead by Gujarat Police when he allegedly tried to flee from them in 2001; Ali Reza Khan, a real estate developer; Amir Reza who, police suspect, is in Pakistan now; Imran Reza Khan, a businessman and Ehtasam Reza Khan, a student.

At present, only the elderly couple stay at their Beniapukur house. Their sons have settled down in different parts of the city and all his five daughters have been married off. When Amir called last year, Ishaq had asked why he committed such a crime (the attack on the American Center).

"But my son said he was staying in Dubai and denied his involvement in any crime. He said he was engaged in business there," the elderly man said. He also said that he had no complaints against the police. "They never created any trouble for me. They never disturbed me," Ishaq said.

He said he had told Amir's wife that she had the liberty to get married again. "Amir cannot come back. His wife and daughter have gone back to her parental home in Lucknow. We have told her she is free to get re-married but I don't know what she has done," he added.

Heading: CII plans seminar to attract investors to eastern region - Indian Express
Content:
The activists of the People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) carried out a protest against Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) at its New Market outlet on Thursday.

The protest was a part of the animal rights organisation's international campaign to pursue KFC to deal strictly with its suppliers' cruel treatment of birds.

According to the PETA, video footage obtained after an "undercover investigation" of a US slaughterhouse in West Virginia show the birds being cruelly treated by workers.

"Every bird KFC serves has endured a tortured life and a painful death. We are not asking people to become vegetarian as it will be impractical, but we are urging them not to have food from KFC until the company implements basic animal welfare standards," said PETA campaign coordinator Rahul Patil.

"I believe that like others, KFC must adhere to the standards set for animal welfare," said Sumit Bhattacharya, a regular at the outlet.

According to PETA reports, KFC suppliers pack chickens in filthy and crowded warehouses.

The birds are drugged for breeding and millions are scalded to death in de-featuring tanks.

"PETA India has already written a number of letters to KFC executives about these issues. But KFC has refused to abide by the norms and is trying to hide behind its Animal Welfare Advisory Council in US, despite five of its members resigning in frustration," said Patil.

The protestors called for adoption of animal care standards, switching to controlled atmosphere killing and mechanised chicken gathering, with the laying down of transparent welfare standards.

Heading: Technicians make up for Tollywood  at film fest - Indian Express
Content:
To attract investments in the eastern region of the country, Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) is holding an exhibition, the first of its kind in the region to be held in Kolkata.

The four-day exhibition, 'Biz Bridge — Resurgence East', to be held from November 19-22, aims to bridge the gap between manufacturers and customers.

Several companies of key manufacturing sectors like infrastructure, steel, power, automobiles, chemical and petrochemicals will participate in the event, as producers from five states of the eastern region will share a common platform.

"We are trying to showcase the eastern region, which is lagging behind in manufacturing. We expect over 5,000 delegates from various sectors like government bodies, automobile industries, power departments and ancillary units," said Biswadip Gupta, former chairman of CII. Of the 100 participant companies, a few will be MNCs, he added.

Commerce and Industries Secretary Sabyasachi Sen said the state government is keen help the ailing steel and sponge iron units facing closure in the state.

"I have proposed to meet the sector representatives to understand the situation. We are ready to offer our support to the sector," he added.

Following the global recession, the steel industry is in the docks, leading to production cuts even by majors like JSW Steel, Essar Steel and Ispat Industries.

Heading: PTTI crisis: Govt banks on Pranab to solve deadlock - Indian Express
Content:
While the 14th edition of the Kolkata Film Festival (KFF) may have won the reputation of an "international film festival without local stars", the Tollywood film industry has not exactly gone unrepresented at the fest.

The bustling Eastern Indian Cinetel Welfare Trust stall at the Nandan complex stands as a proud representative of the local film industry. "This stall is to create awareness about the film technicians of Tollywood. We are an integral part of the film industry too," said Bulu Mukherjee, a member of the trust.

Founded in 1997, the trust was created to fund the pension of aged film technicians of the Tollywood film industry. "The technicians are a neglected lot. They are not eligible for pension or any kind of retirement benefits. Which is why we thought that such a funding body was necessary," Mukherjee added.

Noted actors Sabyasachi Chakraborty, Prosenjit and Soumitra Chatterjee are members of the trust. "We provide pension to more than 40 aged technicians and facilitate the education of their children. We also hand over Rs 10,000 to the widows of technicians," said Mukherjee.

The stall has been an integral part of the festival for the last few years. "This year, a lot of people got interested in our stall. People are attracted to the colourful T-shirts that we have on display," Mukherjee said.

Heading: BESU outlines code of conduct for students and teachers - Indian Express
Content:
The West Bengal government is pinning hopes on External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee for resolving the Primary Teachers Training Institute (PTTI) issue.

The School Education Minister, Partha De, is looking forward to meet Mukherjee in Delhi to seek his support before approaching the Human Resources and Development Ministry. Last month, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee had written to the external affairs minister and sought his intervention to resolve the PTTI crisis.

A student delegation led by Chhatra Parishad, the student wing of the Congress, also met Mukherjee last month in Kolkata. "I will meet Mukherjee once he reaches Delhi. I am waiting for my officers to return," said De on the sidelines of a programme in the city on Thursday. Earlier, the education minister had approached the Ministry of Human Resources and Development without much success. The minister said, "The students are distressed and confused. It is our duty to make them understand the problem," said De.

Last week, the minister had to face an attack on his convoy by protesting students at Bishnupur in Bankura. Eleven students have been sent in judicial custody till November 17 for the attack. Meanwhile, officials of the School Education Department are hopeful that the crisis is nearing a solution.

"According to the National Council of Teacher Education statutes, in many states where the PTTI diploma is of one year, there is a scope to convert it to a two-year course," said an official.

The PTTI crisis has cast a shadow over the primary education system in the state with vacancies of primary teachers rising to 38,000 and not a single recruitment in the last two years.

Heading: Ray’s childhood home gets revamped - Indian Express
Content:
Following the recent spurt in violence on the campus, the Bengal Engineering and Science University administration (BESU) has come up with a new set of code of conduct for students and teachers.

The new code for students has more specific provisions for punishment and inquiry on misconduct by a student.

For rules governing the teachers, Vice-Chancellor N R Banerjea said a committee comprising former teachers and former vice-chancellors will be set up.

Even as the university implemented a fresh code of conduct, the undergraduate students who were asked to vacate their hostels, are yet to return to the campus. On November 6, the authorities had suspended the undergraduate classes for an indefinite period.

"The Board of Management on Thursday acknowledged that the first year and second year students were not involved in the violence. So, we have asked the students to return to the university," said the V-C.

According to the authorities, the students need to come to the university along with their parents, who will have to sign a declaration. The hostel superintendents will search the room of every student for hockey sticks or iron rods.

The authorities, however, have not yet decided on the return of the third and fourth year students. An internal inquiry on the last week's violence will be conducted by Moloy Banerjee, a professor of the university, head of the department of electrical engineering and information and technology and hostel superintendents of Wolfendon Hall and Richardson Hall. The report will be submitted in about four-six weeks, the authorities said. "All these measures by the vice-chancellor are to suppress the students," said a student.

"It is an attempt to undermine the authority of teachers. Anything against the interest of the university and the teachers will not be obeyed," said Manas Hira, spokesperson of BESU Teachers' Association.

Ireland delegation to visit BESU
Bengal Engineering and Science University will host a delegation from the Queens University of North Ireland from November 19 to 20. The delegation comprises Queens University Vice-Chancellor Peter Gregson and industrialists from North Ireland led by Lord Diljit Singh Rana. The university will honour Gregson and Rana with Doctor of Science degrees.

Heading: Trinamool prepares for Nov 15 Singur rally - Indian Express
Content:
Immortalised in Satyajit Ray's writing, the Atheneum Institute has finally been given a facelift. Moved to 100 A Garpar Road, the house where Ray spent his childhood, it is now a higher secondary school.

As the school with its new and revamped infrastructure is all set to embark on a new journey, the school paid a tribute to its past by unveiling a statue of poet Sukumar Ray, father of Satyajit Ray, on Thursday in the school premises.

Those who attended the function include Actor Soumitra Chatterjee, former Justice Shyamal Sen and Subhas Naskar, Minister for Irrigation.

Chatterjee, who described the Ray family as one of most intellectual families in Bengal after the Tagore family, recited poems from Abol Tabol, one of the most hilarious creations of poet Sukumar Ray.

In one of the classrooms in the school building, Haradhan Mukherjee, spread his collection of archives of the legendary filmmaker explaining to each onlooker about the earliest published sketches of Ray, as old as 1943 and reviews of Pather Panchali and various other materials related to the filmmaker.

The school also plans to set up an archive of the works of the three generations of the family — grandfather Upendrakishore Roychowdary, father Sukumar Ray and Satyajit Ray — on the ground floor from where his father Sukumar Roy brought out the well loved magazine Sandesh.

Ray, in his book Jokhon Chhoto Chhilam, has given a vivid description of the building and the institute.

The institute was set up in 1894 in the nearby Sukeas Lane. After which the school also had an address on 59 Garpar Road and in 1927 shifted to its present address in the rented house, then owned by Mullick and Estate.

Till August 2007, the school was housed in the rented building after which the owners tried to use the property for real estate business.

Declared a heritage building by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation in 2007, the civic body along with the support of other individuals bought the school from the owners Mullik and Estate.

The KMC paid the lion's share of Rs 15 lakh in the Rs 25 lakh transaction from its heritage funds.

"It is a well-known school with the building having its own identity. Earlier, the place was in a very bad condition. Now, it is a lot better following the revamp," said Tanmoy Chakraborty, Class XI student of the school.

Manoranjan Suar, Principal of the school, described the efforts by the school as a tribute to the Ray family, whose legacy provided the institute with a slice of history very few can boast of.

Heading: AIFF cracks down on over-aged players, new rule puts Bengal in a spot - Indian Express
Content:
The Trinamool Congress is preparing itself to face any kind of hurdle during their rally in Singur on November 15. On November 2, a public rally, which was addressed by Mamata Banerjee, was marred by violent incidents.

Banerjee, who will be present at the rally on Saturday, has already declared the day as Tapasi Malik Divas.

"We are not taking any chances. We are prepared to face any challenges on November 15," said Trinamool leader in Singur Becharam Manna. He was reacting to a possibility of the CPM attempting to jeopardise the meeting. "We have not forgotten how the CPM tried to stop Banerjee from entering Singur on November 2," Manna said.

The CPM-backed Save Nano Committee members had set up road blockades on the way to Singur on November 2. A number of vehicles were burnt and many Trinamool leaders, including Leader of the Opposition of the state Assembly, Partha Chatterjee, were also injured. Banerjee's convoy was stopped at Dankuni.

There were clashes between the Trinamool and the CPM and the police had to resort to lathicharge to disperse the mob.

Heading: Bengal strike back, but much too late - Indian Express
Content:
In a heartening change in policy and outlook, the All India Football Federation (AIFF) finally seems to have woken up to the perils and problems of overlooking cases of over-aged players taking part in junior national events.

The AIFF, in a recent circular to all the state associations in the country, has informed the AIFF that it has appointed a team of observers and doctors, who would be deployed at the venues for the Under-19 junior national championship this season. And in cases of complaints from protesting teams and players, and also at the behest of the AIFF-appointed observers and doctors, the players in question would have to compulsorily undergo MRI tests.

Interestingly, the team Bengal, who were runners-up in the BC Roy Trophy last time, are in a bit of a spot as a result of the new development. Bengal coaches Ranjan Chowdhury and Prasanta Chakrabarty have been compelled to reject some promising U-19 players who participated in the Kolkata Premier League (KPL) and represented as many as 10 senior club teams this season.

Meanwhile, apart from the over-age issue, a few boys of outstanding merit have joined the preparatory camp that commenced on November 10 at Bidhannagar Municipality Sports complex. Both the coaches are expecting the inclusion of a few quality junior players like Rajib Rao (defender), Munna Mullick, Kallol Pal (midfielder) and Sevak Hembram (strikers), who are expected to lake up for the unavailability of the juniors who are now being struck off the roster.

The BC Roy Trophy, originally scheduled to be start on November 25, has now been deferred by a month and will begin on December 24 at Villai, in Chattisgarh.

Bengal are expected to kick off from the pre-quarterfinal stage, alongside Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu. Only one from these three teams will qualify for the quarter-final stage.

As of now, there are 60 players in the ongoing preparatory camp. The coaches are likely to trim the list down to 35 players. The Indian Football Association (IFA) meanwhile has assured that it will provide proper accommodation at Villai for the players, apart from making their travel arrangements.

The coaches are also planning to request the IFA to provide daily allowances and tiffin for the 35 players during their training period. Ranjan Chowdhury said: "I hope the IFA will not disagree with my request. The players will be motivated if they are given small daily allowances along with required food after training."

Heading: Celebrating childhood - Indian Express
Content:
Their fast bowlers made a last ditch effort on the fourth day to eke out a result, but the Bengal batsmen's overall showing was far too limp to make an impact in the opening match of the Ranji Trophy Plate Group campaign.

In the end, Utpal Chatterjee's boys ended up with a tame draw in their opener against Madhya Pradesh in Gwalior, and they will be lamenting conceding the all-important first innings lead to the home team.

After being dimissed for yet another modest total today — Bengal managed 227 in their second innings — the visitors came tantalising close to snatching victory out of nowhere after the Madhya Pradesh batsmen faltered big time while chasing 160 for outright victory off 39 overs.

Yet again, the Bengal new ball bowlers gave their skipper Laxmi Ratan Shukla a glimmer of hope as Ranadeb Bose and Ashok Dinda removed hosts' top order in no time. Eventually, Hrishikesh Kanitkar & Co saw off the challenge from the Bengal bowlers, finishing their second innings on 63 for 6 off 29 overs. Bengal were left lamenting as another session's play or a slightly better display on the batting front would certainly have effected a result in their favour.

Earliee in the day, Bengal stumper-batsman Wriddhiman Saha compiled a neat 83 and newcomer Avik Chowdhury carved out a well-deserved 60 to form the backbone of the Bengal second innings. The duo put on 119 runs for the fifth wicket and powered Bengal from 30 for 4 to a much more respectable 227.

Despite their best efforts, and the early inroads made by Bose (2 for 15) and Dinda (1 for 26), Bengal just didn't have enough runs on the scoreboard in both the innings to ensure a victory, eventually beginning their Ranji campaign with just an unimpressive 1-point.

Heading: Green conviction - Indian Express
Content:
On Children's Day today, schools promise to take their kids on a roller coaster ride with a host of exciting activities. Shashi Priya and Aaditi Jathar find out

With the leap of a new generation as the guru-shishya relationship is transcending to a new avatar, the celebrations on Children's Day will get vibrant and exuberant today. It's no more only about children standing in a queue for sweets; from filmi entertainment to ramp walk, an exciting lineup of colourful activities has been planned by the various schools in the city to make the day special for their kids.

At Blossoms Public School (BPS), the kids from the junior and senior kindergartens will start their day with an inter-house Maharashtrian folk dance competition followed by an elocution competition. A fancy dress competition for the nursery, KG, and upper KG students is also organised for the little ones. While children will be dressed to the best the KG teachers will put up a cultural programme too. "To revive the memory of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru a speech has been arranged as we strongly believe that children should understand the importance of this day," says Kamla Bisht, principal, BPS. The day for these kids will conclude with distribution of prizes and sweets.

Fun filled celebrations will make a difference in the regular school activities at Judson High School in Pimpri as they will celebrate Fun Day today. Making the children extremely delighted to commemorate the birthday of Pandit Nehru, these kids will walk to schools in casual outfits where they would have jumping castles awaiting their surprise and it will be the teachers who would entertain them with skits, dances and fashion show. "We thought it is a unique idea to surprise our students. It will be fun for children to see their otherwise strict teachers walking the ramp," shares Shabana Sayeed, a teacher at JHS.

Making the day memorable, Phoenix School will present each child with a gift and films like Finding Nemo, Bal Ganesh and Hanuman will be screened in the school. Following a similar trend at Dr DY Patil School the film Salaam Bacche will be showcased to mark the celebrations along with dance performances by their teachers. Poly Mukherjee, principal of Christeria School in Nigdi, says the academy would be starting a new activity centre soon, which would be an ideal gift for their students. "At the activity centre students can enjoy and have fun; moreover, the activities here will help them in their overall development," she says.

While Shikshan Prasarak Mandali's English Medium School (SPM) will take the kids to a picnic at Saras Baug and will also stage a play at the school along with other activities, Sundarabai Marathe Vidyalaya in Kharadi has planned a short trip to a park near the school along with a visit to Behere's old age home. "The idea is to inculcate affection and affinity towards senior citizens," says Sanjay Somwanshi, principal, SMV. The Genba Sopanrao Moze Secondary and Higher Secondary School has organised a Hindi poem recitation and elocution competition and Shri Sant Dnyaneshwar Vidyalaya on Paud road will hold essay, debate and drawing competitions in the later this month as examinations as going on in the school.

Heading: I Dream Of Genie - Indian Express
Content:
Kids of APRA not only sacrifice their holidays to make the environment green and clean, but also set example for elders to follow

The future flag bearers of the society have, it seems, taken their responsibility a bit too seriously and have set to work even before they come in the category of teens. The kids of APRA (Anand Park active kids group) have taken up the task to bring back greenery to the city that has almost lost its natural charm given the unplanned concrete development.

The small wonders are between the age group of 10-13 years. And the Club has a mission to complete during the holidays. To begin with, they have started taking signatures of the residents of Anand Park to ensure their participation in the task. Among a long list of many different tasks that they plan, planting saplings and stopping the use of plastic bags are of prime importance.

Girish Deshpande, the man behind this idea says, "They are sacrificing their playtime to work for a noble cause. Our plan is to create a healthy environment in Pune so that everyone can breathe in fresh air. I believe that kids can do what we elders often fail to do."

Neel Deshpande, a 12-year-old member of the club, says, "We have taken about 100 signatures till now and we target 500, which needs to be achieved in three weeks time." He comes back from school at 4:30 in the evening and starts his game of collecting signatures. Most of the times he gets a positive response but there are times people don't care. Neel, however doesn't loses hope. Another soldier for green, Rucha Gahanlalde, a student of VIII standard, says, "Whenever we find a plastic lying anywhere, we pick them up and tell people not to use them." On being asked how long they will carry their mission, a strong determined Rucha gave answered, "We are working for ourselves and shall continue till we get satisfaction." An 11-year-old Aarti Abhiyankar is much enthusiastic over the whole thing. Expressing her happiness she says, "I have learnt a lot of new things related to environment protection. I love my work of saving the mother nature."

With a dream of green, clean and beautiful city the kids are planting saplings. They are spreading a message among the common public that the way they use polythene bags can really bring an imbalance in the environment. The future depends on the present and thus all the plastic in the garbage heap at the corner of your locality can be the reason of your sorrows in future. However, the effort might appear to be a drop in the ocean, but the zeal to make an effort to make environment cleaner and greener is worth appreciating and also worth supporting.

Heading: For communal harmony, cops organise volleyball tourney - Indian Express
Content:
Kids share their wishful fantasies with Genie on Children's Day

Alice has her wonderland, Cinderella has a fairy Godmother and Harry Potter is the ace wizard. While all these imagoes spilled the magic beans in the mind of the young ones, they have always mooned for a mascot who would embark their fantasies too. On Children's Day today, these innocent little ones get wishful with our Genie who is out to hear his little masters.

I want a dream house like Barbie that is completely painted in Pink and I want my school to teach me everything about chocolates, so I'll ask Genie to grant this wish. He should also take me all around where I can do a lot of shopping
– Kajal Bafna 13 years

I will ask Genie to give me all his magic powers so that I can have a competition with Harry Potter. I also want him to carry my school bag everyday for me and show me the world inside his lamp. I want to be very strong and want to be a pilot and ride a spacecraft to Jupiter.
– Parth Shah, 8 years

I want Genie to give me 40 video games, 100 bikes and 300 cars. I want to be the best cricketer in the world so I want him to give me a magic bat.
– Siddhant Sanghvi, 12 years

I want Genie to give me lots of soft toys and a gown like Cinderella. I want a very big house on the beach and it should have a Toyland on one end and a Chocolate inn on the other.
– Namrata Oswal, 11 years

– Siddhanti Jain, 10 years

Heading: Eyeing polls, Congress public awareness campaign goes hi-tech - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when Pune is emerging as the hub of radical organisations like Indian Mujahideen, the city police have come up with the idea of Kaumi Ekta police chashak, a volleyball competitions for encouraging communal harmony in the society. Pune police have encouraged local corporators and social activists in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad area to form volleyball teams including persons from different religions and castes.

"Khel hai toh mel hai," said city police commissioner Satyapal Singh while inaugurating the Kaumi Ekta volleyball competition at the Mathurawala ground in Wanavdi Bazaar organised by the Zone IV police on Tuesday. Singh said that increasing incidents of violence in the name of religion, caste, creed and language is a major concern. Sports is a good activity that would encourage communal harmony and eliminate the fear factor in the society," he said.

As many as 16 teams formed by corporators in Wanavdi, Hadapsar and Kondhwa participated in the volleyball matches at Mathuralawala ground. Additional commissioner Dhananjay Kamlakar, deputy commissioner Jalinder Supekar, senior inspectors V S Sonawane, Shivajirao Kanase and local corporators were present at the function.

The city police will organise volleyball competitions in other parts of the city also. The winning teams in all the four police zones will again compete for the kaumi ekta prize.

A volleyball competition organised by the Bharati Vidyapeeth police station will start at Bharati Vidyapeeth ground on Friday evening. "We have seven volleyball teams for the competition, three of which are formed by local corporators," said inspector Ukhaji Sonwane of Bharati Vidyapeeth police station.

Heading: Karanth Festival to begin tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
Gearing up for the forthcoming polls, the state unit of Congress on Thursday announced the launch of a public awareness campaign throughout the state to convey achievements of the Congress-led government in the state and centre in the last four years through hi-tech presentations.

The Janjagran Vikas Yatra will reach the city on November 19 and cover the Pune rural on November 27.

"We will be launching the state wide awareness campaign from Jalgaon on November 19 on the birth anniversary of Indira Gandhi and it will continue till December 28," state congress spokesperson Anant Gadgil told reporters.

There are many decisions in favour of all sections of societies taken by the Congress-led government at state as well as centre, he said adding the awareness campaign will reach the public to enable them take advantage of it and simultaneously acknowledge the government work.

There will be at least 60 rallies at the campaign, Gadgil said adding that the state Congress has designed a proto type specially designed vehicle, rath, for the purpose.

The participants will be making presentations using computers to explain the government efforts, he said.

On the issue of the sons of soil, the congress spokesperson said the state image was being unnecessarily maligned by various political parties.

"The opposition Shiv Sena and BJP have a difference of opinion on the issue. If they cannot come together on one issue then how are they going to jointly rule the state or country," Gadgil said.

Gadgil keeps mum on Pune LS seat
State Congress spokesperson Anant Gadgil maintained silence over the Pune Lok Sabha seat while making it clear that he would abide by the party decision on candidature for the seat.

"I will abide by the decision of the party high command on party candidature for Pune Lok Sabha," he said when asked on whether he would contest the Lok Sabha.

The state leaders of Congress and NCP have started preliminary talks on the seat sharing, Gadgil said the criteria for party candidature would be clear after some time.

Incidentally, Gadgil, who belongs to anti-Suresh Kalmadi camp, was kept away from the scheduled function of city Congress to felicitate State Agriculture minister Harshwardhan Patil for the victory of his panel in Karmayogi Shankarraoji Patil Sugar cooperative mill at Indapur. The function was later cancelled due to death of a Congress leader.

Heading: Paramount Airways launches Pune-Chennai flight - Indian Express
Content:
Samanvay, a theatre group in the city will organise B V Karanth Festival on November 15 and 16 at Yashvantrao Chavan Auditorium, Kothrud. Veteran actor Shreeram Lagoo will inaugurate the festival at 5.30 pm on November 15.

"The festival will be a tribute to late B V Karanth, the pioneer of amateur theatre in Karnataka," said Kiran Yadnyopavit of Samanvay. "Karanth started a theatre group titled Beneka in 1974 and staged milestone plays like Hayavadana, Jokumaraswamy, Sattavara Neralu, Kattale Belaku and Gokula Nirgamana. Festival is an attempt to showcase his work before audience," he said.

Yadnyopavit said the festival would showcase Karanth's plays Hayavadana, Jokumaraswamy and Gokula Nirgamana in original cast. "Besides these plays, there will be a musical programme on Karanth's creations," he said.

"With his amazing directorial skills, Karanth brought in a unique approach to theatrical experiments conveying thought provoking messages to the audience," said Yadnyopavit. "Through activities of Beneka, Karanth brought in cultural renaissance through theatrical renderings of renowned playwrights like Girish Karnad, Chandrasekhar Kambar, Sriranga, P Lankesh and G B Joshi. Through the festival we are trying to bring the essence of his theatre in Pune," he said.

Yadnyopavit said the festival would showcase a photo exhibition featuring works of Karanth. The festival is open for all and tickets are available in the range of Rs 500, Rs 300 and Rs 200 for the whole festival.

Heading: Jaipur Foot camp distributes artificial limbs, calipers for free - Indian Express
Content:
Paramount Airways launched its direct flight services from Pune to Chennai on Thursday. This is a daily flight, which will leave Pune at 10.10 pm and reach Chennai at 12.05 am. With the introduction of this direct flight, Pune passengers will get an easy connectivity to Coimbatore, Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram and Madurai from Chennai.

M Thiagrajan, managing director of Paramount Airways, officially announced the launching of Pune- Chennai flight at a press conference on Thursday. This is the third centre of the company in Western India. "We have launched this sector as a part of our expansion strategy," he said.

"We have a market share of 26 per cent in the Southern skies and now we are concentrating on Western India. Pune is the third centre in Western India after Ahmedabad and Goa," said Thiagrajan. He said the airline was also interested in carrying cargo such as automobile components and flowers to places like Coimbatore and Madurai through connecting flight from Pune.

"The Pune- Chennai sector will be profitable as an average 65 per cent load factor per month is expected," he said. "The company is looking to start flights from Nagpur, Bharuch and Por Bandar in near future," said Thiagrajan.

"We have five aircraft of new generation embraer family series and we will add two more to it in the near future," he said.

Heading: NECC-ITF : South’s power proves too much for Sahoo - Indian Express
Content:
Shreekrishna Gupta from Kanpur was barely 12 years old when his right leg was amputed due to a severe infection. Life changed for him when he heard about the Jaipur foot some 22 years ago as not only did it allow him to walk but it also gave him a livelihood. Gupta and Bhanwar Singh Rajawat, a 40-year-old from Jaipur itself are two of the 15 such hapless people who are now helping make `Jaipur foot' for others who face the same plight as the.

Both Gupta and Rajawat are now in Pune as part of the Jaipur Foot camp conducted by the Bhagwan Mahaveer Viklang Sahyata Samiti (BMVSS) and Dow Chemical International Pvt Ltd (Dow India) and feel much satisfaction in doing their bit for other physically challenged people.

The camp is underway till November 14 and provides free fabrication and distribution of approximately 350 artificial limbs and calipers to the physically challenged enabling them regain mobility and a normal life.

"In 1982 I met with an accident and lost my leg. Two years later I was fortunate to get a Jaipur foot and the organisation also offered me a job to make these artificial limbs,'' says Rajawat.

The BMVSS Jaipur, set up in 1975, is the world's largest organization for the handicapped, benefiting more than one million handicapped in India and abroad, by providing artificial limbs, calipers and other aids and appliances since its inception.

Since most of its patients are below the poverty line, this assistance has been provided totally free of charge. In the last financial year alone, BMVSS with support from various sensitive sources and organizations helped more than 66,000 handicapped people get back on their feet.

The organisation of Jaipur Foot camp in Pune is an extension of Dow India's recent announcement of providing support of Rs 1 crore to BMVSS. "There are 1.25 million amputees in India and every year, 25,000 people lose their limbs to diseases, accidents or other hazards," said Dr. Ramesh Ramachandran, CEO and President, DOW, India. As a part of its ongoing corporate citizenship programmes, Dow India has been associated with the Jaipur Foot initiative since 2005.

In addition to committing financial resources to BMVSS, Dow India's polyurethane unit at Kalwa, Mumbai along with Pinnacle Industries has utilized its expertise to introduce the revolutionary polyurethane (PU) Foot, which has been highly acknowledged by global orthopedic experts.

These organisations are currently working on the next generation polyurethane foot coated with a protective elastomer layer to enhance the life of the PU foot by cent per cent.

Heading: T20 cricket: Namdeorao Rukari Memorial attracts top teams - Indian Express
Content:
Top seeded Melanie South stopped the winning run of Shalini Sahoo to enter the semifinal of the $25,000 NECC- ITF women's tennis Championships, being organised by the Deccan Gymkhana and being played on their courts here.

In the quarterfinals played today, the robust British player easily outplayed

Sahoo 6-2, 6-2 in a match that lasted for an hour. South will now take on fourth seeded Ksenia Palkina of Kyrgyzstan.

Palkina, ranked 220th easily accounted for sixth seeded Kai-Chen Chang of Taipei 6-3, 6-4. Qualifier Bojana Jovanovski of Serbia continued with a fabulous run in the event comprehensively beating I Hsuan Hwang of Taipei 6-2, 6-2 to make it to the last four of the tournament. Bojana will take on eighth seeded Jing Jing Lu of China. Jing Lu had an easy outing as second seeded 192 ranked Ye-Ra Lee of Korea conceded her match due to fever after being down 5-2 in the first set.

Sahoo who evolved a lot of interest with her performance, started well winning two games in a row, but South played solidly and won the next six games to win the set 6-2. In the second set Sahoo was broken in the first and third games to let South walk off with the match.

"I tried to play my best, but was beaten by the speed and pace of South", Sahoo admitted after the match. "It was the first time I was playing a high ranked player and it was truly a great experience for me. I've got a feel of what top class tennis is," said the qualifier.

"I owe my performance to my father B.C Sahoo who has supported me all along and want to continue my form in the future." she said. Shalini however had the consolation of getting eight WTA points and $686 (Rs.25, 000) for her effort. Melanie South praised Sahoo's effort, saying she played well, but was probably overwhelmed by the occasion.

"I am playing well", said South who plays at the British National Training centre at Roehampton. "I'm looking at taking a title here, which will be the third of the year," she said. Elora Dabija(Rou) /Bojana Jovanovski (Srb) will take on the Chinese Taipei pair of Kai-Chen Chang/ I Hsuan Hwang in the doubles finals. In the doubles semi- final the pair Dabija and Jovanovski scraped past the pair of Julia Parasyuk(Rus) and Korina Perkovic(Ger) 3-6,6-1,10-4 , while the Chinese Taipei pair of Chang and Hwang (Tpe) defeated Jade Curtis / Emily Webley Smith of Great Britain 6-4,6-2.

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Gracy Singh - Indian Express
Content:
On Children's Day, think twice before lavishing your loved ones

Though a reason to splurge on kids is just an excuse these days, Children's Day makes for the perfect occasion to splurge on them. From special outings to a hair makeover to an all new wardrobe, options are aplenty.

"If my kids had their way, I would be shopping for a car right now," laughs model Waluscha Robinson, "But both my kids will have to make do with the Sony Vaio that we gifted my daughter Chanel on her birthday recently." She finds spending up to Rs 50,000 on educative gadgets an investment.

Designer clothes and bags for kids have always made for sought-after gifts, what with special kids' line by Burberry (where a T-shirt costs Rs 2,500 and a shirt Rs 6,500), Armani and Moschino to name a few. But a kids' salon as a concept has picked up remarkably. "I'll treat my 12-year-old to a fancy hairdo this Children's Day; it's a step towards educating him about grooming," grins Indrani Chatterjee, a banker, who plans to take her son Arvind to Watermelon, a kids' salon in Bandra. She will be spending anything between Rs 500 to Rs 1,200 there. There's also Tears To Cheers, Warden Road, where the tots sit in car-shaped seats and watch cartoons on a private TV while getting a chop (for Rs 350).

The most common activity parents indulge their kids in every Children's Day is to take them for an event. Classic Animation Studio, in an attempt to fire the imagination of animation-loving children (five to 14), is organising a day camp at Deokane, a village 120 km from Mumbai. Apart from launching their new animation film, Buji, the animation studio has planned a fun-filled day of activities, games, animation workshops and performances.

And while your child's away at the camp, you could have your interior designer over to do up his/ her room. You can choose from bed and bath linen with their favourite cartoon characters like Mickey Mouse, Sponge Bob and Winnie the Pooh by Portico New York (Rs 500 onwards), innovatively designed furniture for their room by @home (Rs 5,000 upwards).

The much publicised sentimentality of Bhavna Jasra's First Impressions is a great option to mere photographs of your kids. "To mount a 3-D model of your loved ones' feet and hands in gold, is the warmest way to show them your love," says the entrepreneur who charges Rs 15,000 for a set in bronze. Jasra's Photo Concept with Krsna Mehta is an alternate for those with a tighter budget. "We personalise the everyday articles used by children, like bags, satchels and folders."

Parents who believe that a gift for Children's Day should be a tad serious and educative can enroll their children in one of the many hobby classes on offer these days. Toddlers Activity Centre in Worli is a 2,000 sq ft facility for children of up to 14 years. Programmes to introduce toddlers to speech and action, art, craft, music and ballet classes are some of the activities on offer. However, one wonders what a three-month-old will gain from a yoga class, especially if it makes you lighter by Rs 3,000. There are other such options too; Bhanu's Fit Kids at Tardeo charges an average of Rs 350 per session lasting 50 minutes, where one story is told and one craft model is made, mostly by the accompanying maids. Whatever happened to the good, old drive and ice cream with dad.

Heading: Veryfilmy - Indian Express
Content:
A verbal exchange was reported between the Gandhinagar police and the VHP leaders of Gujarat during a four-hour questioning of the latter here on Thursday in connection with the "defamatory SMSes" sent against Chief Minister Narendra Modi and the state government.

Sources said that when the investigating officers asked the three VHP leaders to hand over their mobile phones for the forensic test, the latter put up a great deal of resistance.

Pradesh VHP General Secretary Kaushik Mehta reportedly shot back at the investigating officers and said: "This (mobile phone) is our personal property which we cannot part with. If you want it, then first obtain the necessary orders from a court of law."

According to sources, the police ultimately relented and stopped pressing for the cellphones.

Later, Mehta told mediapersons that during the questioning, the police insisted that they hand over their mobile phones for the forensic science laboratory test. "But, we put our foot down and refused to give our handsets to them," he said.

At first, Mehta refused to divulge what statements he and two other two VHP leaders had given to the police. But on persisting, he said the police wanted to know if they had received an SMS from Ashwin Patel, the arrested VHP leader, and whether they had forwarded the same to other organisation workers across the state. "Is it an offence to receive and forward an SMS on one's personal mobile phone?" he said.

He also attacked the Narendra Modi government and accused it of "harassing innocent VHP workers in Gujarat," besides "creating an atmosphere of terror in the VHP rank and file."

Gandhinagar Deputy Superintendent of Police Manoj Ninama, who is investigating the case, declined to disclose what statements the VHP leaders had given to the police during the questioning. He said: "We have recorded their statements and will summon more VHP workers for questioning later in the case."

It may be mentioned that on Wednesday the Gandhinagar police had issued summons to the three VHP leaders and asked them to present themselves on Thursday for questioning in connection with the case.

Responding to the summons, Mehta, Rajesh Shastri, VHP leader of the north Gujarat region, and Jagdish Dwivedi, former Ahmedabad city BJP general secretary, presented themselves before the police.

On the Diwali eve, the police had arrested Gujarat VHP Joint-Secretary Ashwin Patel for allegedly sending "defamatory SMSes" about Modi and his government, and trying to create social tension among different communities in the state.

Patel has been charged with sedition and forgery. Last Tuesday, the Sessions Court in Gandhinagar had rejected his bail plea.

Since the arrest of Patel, the VHP workers have been organising demonstrations, denouncing the arrest, and accusing the Modi regime of "harassing and victimising" the VHP cadres in Gujarat.

"The BJP government, it seems, is bent upon destroying the forces of Hindutva in the state. After arresting Ashwin Patel, the police have now started raiding the houses of VHP workers, and are issuing summons to them. We condemn this high-handedness of the police," said state VHP spokesman Ranchhod Bharwad.

Heading: Dad’s The way - Indian Express
Content:
Ratan Tata may have shifted his Nano car plant from Singur in West Bengal to Sanand in Gujarat, but this ambitious project is unlikely to move forward without facing any political hindrances.

While the recently formed Maha Gujarat Party (MGJP) by the BJP rebels will go on an indefinite dharna at the Ahmedabad Town Hall from Friday, the CPI (M) has announced an elaborate protest programme in December.

The Left party will hold dharnas, rallies, human chain programmes, public meetings and satyagrah to oppose the project.

The MGJP has opposed the state government's decision to give Tata Motors exemption on 85 per cent jobs reserved for the locals. Former Gujarat home minister and MGJP president Gordhan Zadafia and general secretary Sunil Oza will hold the dharna with a demand to cancel the deal.

"Tata is no NGO. They have come here to do business. When Chief Minister Narendra Modi has given a number of soaps, including soft loans, it has done injustice to the people of Gujarat by allowing them not to follow the 85 per cent reservation system," said party secretary Siddharth Parmar.

"Why should the Gujarat government favour a company that has outrightly rejected to provide employment to Gujaratis?" asked the party in a press note released here on Thursday.

The CPI(M), on the other hand, is protesting against a number of issues, including allotting the land to the Tatas even as most of the industries — diamond, chemical, textile, steel — are falling victim to the global meltdown.

"During financial crisis, when most of the industries are feeling the heat of the global meltdown, the state government can only see Tata and Nano," said a party release.

The CPI(M) in its executive committee meeting held at Ahmedabad on November 11 and 12 decided to launch a series of protests from December 1.

According to CPI(M) state secretary Arun Mehta, the programme will be organised for 15 days.

The party said that while several tribals have been fighting for their right to own a piece of land for years, the government gives away lands to business houses overnight.

Heading: 15 more ancient gold coins seized from labourer - Indian Express
Content:
Abhishek Bachchan has established himself as an actor, but he's still papa's boy

He's dressed in a floral pink and white shirt but sports a short crop and kohl-lined eyes these days. Abhishek Bachchan is clearly in that stage of metamorphosis — from Sameer in Dostana, to his character in Mani Ratnam's Raavan — where a look in the mirror doesn't leave one flattered. But he's got his attitude in place, and that's probably what matters.

Confident about Dostana, which releases today, he clarifies that neither is the film anywhere close to the 1984 namesake nor is the gay plot between him and John Abraham the mainstay in the story. "Such subplots naturally get more attention, making our jobs even more difficult," he sighs.

The film is a comic caper about two friends pretending to be gay while apartment-hunting in Miami. But things go haywire when both fall in love with Neha (Priyanka Chopra).

"Dostana's the funniest film I've ever seen," claims Bachchan. "We had a preview and my family loved it." What adds to it, he says, is the fun he had during the shoot. The 32-year-old laughs as he recollects shooting the ballroom dance sequence with Abraham. "Every time there were such sequences, we'd go over the top with jokes." But Bachchan gives his co-star credit for making him dance since he's a trained ballroom dancer. The two have shared camaraderie since Dhoom days. "John even taught me how to workout," smiles the actor, referring to his new lean look that he now sports at 84 kilos.

As opposed to Bachchan's otherwise simple dressing, stylist Aki Narula has experimented with his look in Dostana. "I just loved sporting the cargos, loose jeans, summer scarves, pastels and prints that Aki had me wear for the film—they just added to the Miami mood," he says.

The film, though directed by debutant Tarun Mansukhani, clearly bears that Karan Johar touch (Mansukhani has assisted Johar since Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, he even played a cameo in the film). But Bachchan is quick to point out that the sense of humour is distinctly Mansukhani's: "Tarun's worked with Karan for over 10 years but the small twists and the edge in the script totally belongs to Tarun. And that's where he stands out."

He may sport a grim public image but what can ensure a smile on his face is the mere mention of his dad, Amitabh Bachchan. "He's doing fine now. Yes, his illness was a trying time for the entire family but he's not just a strong guy, he's Superman."

Bachchan's come into his own as an actor over the last couple of years but he is yet to learn to accept criticism gracefully, it seems. The actor went into a tizzy when informed by the media relations that the press was unhappy with his interviews. "Did I give you a boring interview?" he asks. When we say yes, he turns boisterous, jumping on to the sofa in the lobby like a two-year-old.

Let's not even get into what couch-stomping did to Tom Cruise.

Heading: Cong, NCP vie for Pune seat - Indian Express
Content:
The police on Thursday recovered 15 ancient gold coins, all of the same lot that some labourers had found while digging for a swimming pool. The total found at the construction site of the swimming pool in Shaniwar Peth is 862.

The crime branch recovered the latest 15 coins from Nijappa Santappa Talkeri (35), a worker from Karnataka. Talkeri, who was arrested, was later released on bail by a local court.

On November 7, crime branch sleuths had arrested three labourers who found a copper vessel filled with ancient gold coins at the construction site of a swimming pool of the Pune Municipal Corporation-run N V Gadgil School. The labourers sold half of the coins to a jeweller and were trying to flee with the rest when police nabbed them. The police had then recovered 847 gold coins weighing 3.175 kg worth Rs 42 lakh from the accused. They were arrested under sections of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.

Investigations reveal that Khadki jeweller Surajbhan Agarwal had assured to pay Rs 4 lakh and some gold jewellery to the labourers against the antique gold coins. The 15 coins recovered on Thursday weigh 51.4 gram and are worth Rs 54,000.

Historians believe the price of all the recovered coins could well be over Rs 2 crore in the international market.

Meanwhile, police are worried about the safety of the coins as they are kept along with stolen material recovered from thieves and robbers arrested in various crimes. "We have informed the district collector about the coins, as laws stipulate," said police inspector Ram Jadhav of the crime branch. "We have also informed the Archaeological Survey of India authorities. We have kept the coins safe. But many history enthusiasts have approached us to see it. So we don't want the coins to remain with us for long. ASI authorities say their department is authorised to keep the coins. We will hand over the coins to the authorities concerned as per the orders of district collector," he said. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime), Anil Kumbhare, said most of the coins carry the mark of a saint referred to as protector of Venice on one side and infant Jesus on the other. These are Roman coins from the medieval period. The remaining coins are asharfis or muhars having Urdu and Persian inscriptions and were used during Akbar's regime.

Heading: Two times lucky - Indian Express
Content:
A 45-year-old woman was killed and at least five others were injured in a cave-in that took place at an under construction site in Shah-e-Alam area here on Wednesday afternoon.

The mishap occurred when some portion of mud on a carter being dug for the basement of a commercial building collapsed.

The woman, identified as Nanduben Parmar, succumbed to her head injuries while being taken to a nearby hospital. The condition of another labourer Neeu Vaghela, who is undergoing treatment at the L G Hospital, is said to be critical.

The Maninagar police said the other injured persons were discharged from the hospital after primary treatment.

The police have filed a case of accidental death. Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services personnel conducted the rescue operation that lasted for over three hours.

Heading: Purohit tortured, family tells court - Indian Express
Content:
After Khosla ka Ghosla, Dibakar Banerjee hopes to hit the jackpot again with Oye Lucky Lucky Oye

Dibakar Banerjee does not like comparisons to Hrishikesh Mukherjee. "He had his style of filmmaking and I have mine," he defends, "the only point of similarity is that we both made films about ordinary people."

Banerjee's directorial debut, Khosla ka Ghosla about a middle-class family caught in a land scam, hit bull's-eye with the multiplex going audience. Expectations are now riding high on his next film, Oye Lucky Lucky Oye. But the pressure rests easy on Banerjee's shoulders even as he excitedly talks about his new film. "It's about a thief who's very special," he says, "unlike other thieves, who never want anyone to find out anything about them, this guy wants everyone to know he's the one who committed the crime. He has a talent for stealing and he's very proud of his 'craft'. If you haven't figured out it's him, he'll call you and tell you that he did it!"

It's obvious that Banerjee is attracted to stories that are a little out of the ordinary. And, he says, that tendency also affected the choice of his movie's leading man, Abhay Deol. "Abhay likes to look at the unusual side of things. He doesn't believe in doing what everyone else does. In that sense, we're very alike," he explains, "Moreover he's a very intense actor. That doesn't usually come out since he plays it cool, but he's one of the most focused actors I've met. This intensity of his will take him a long way," he predicts.

Banerjee is, in fact, very upbeat about all the actors in his movie. "We've deliberately not repeated any of the cast members from Khosla. We wanted to work with old and established actors like Paresh Rawal and also some new faces. In fact, there are 10 new actors in this film, five of whom have never acted before."

The music in his films, says Banerjee, also plays a very important role in the narration. "In most Indian movies, music plays a very important role in drawing the audience to the theatres and in providing breaks throughout the narration," he says, "I'm not entirely comfortable with that idea. So instead, even the songs are pushed into the background and become an integral part of the storytelling." The soundtrack of Khosla was a huge hit for the freshness of its sound and Banerjee has made sure that this time too, the audience has something new to listen to. "We've recruited a young talent called Sneha Khandwala. She actually went backpacking in Haryana and Punjab and brought back the old, forgotten melodies and poetry from those regions. You'll hear a lot of folk music on this soundtrack; we've even got folk singers singing here."

Heading: Diabetes is serious, but you can still have a long, healthy life - Indian Express
Content:
The family of serving army officer Lt Col Prasad Purohit, arrested in connection with the Malegaon blast, has filed an affidavit in the Nashik Chief Judicial Magistrate's court alleging physical and mental torture and harassment by the Anti-Terrorism Squad.

Purohit, a resident of Pune, was taken into custody after midnight on November 5 and shown as arrested in the morning. He was produced in the Nashik Chief Judicial Magistrate court which remanded him to police custody until November 15, and also allowed the Anti-Terrorism Squad to conduct narco-analysis tests on him.

An affidavit was filed by a relative, Vilas Anand Dalvi, today in the same court alleging that the family had "specific information that Purohit has suffered physically and psychologically after he was detained in ATS custody". The affidavit alleges that he has been badly beaten and his left hand is completely paralysed, the fingers of his right hand fractured and his knees were injured badly.

The affidavit alleges that the investigation agency has forcibly taken him for narco-analysis tests when he is "physically and psychologically" unfit. The family has also alleged that Purohit is being made to undergo two narco-analysis tests when the court had allowed only one.

The affidavit urges for Purohit's medical check-up to be done by a civil surgeon in the presence of two senior doctors and two doctors from the army.

Heading: Red Ribbon Express stutters, flop  show blamed on poor publicity - Indian Express
Content:
Vidya Gokhale was barely 19 when she went into a diabetic coma. The world literally came crashing down for this youngster who was told that without insulin she would die. For the last 20 years, she has not missed her daily quota of four injections of insulin!

Even as the world observes yet another Diabetes Day on November 14, there are several children suffering from an auto immune disorder known as Type 1 diabetes that is irreversible once it strikes.

And yet, Vidya assures there is no need to panic. Working as a peer educator at the diabetes unit of KEM Hospital for the last four years, she admits that finding out that one has diabetes is scary. "Type 1 diabetes is serious, but we can still live long and healthy lives," she smiles as she provides useful tips at the unit for parents of such children.

Dr C S Yajnik, director of the diabetes unit of KEM Hospital says Type 1 diabetes is usually diagnosed in children and young adults. He explains that the body in Type 1 diabetes does not produce insulin which is a hormone required to convert sugar (glucose) starch and other food into energy needed for daily life.

Dr Shailaja Kale, diabetologist, said over 500 children suffering from juvenile diabetes were being treated and counselled at KEM Hospital.

In fact, a unique recipe competition will be held on November 15 at the OPD of the unit. "The important things is that their blood sugar levels need to be monitored throughout their lives," said Kale.

A unique project is also being conducted by the founder of Diabetes Care and Research foundation Dr Abhay Mutha. "We look after 105 children from the age of three years to less than 18 who are suffering from Type 1 diabetes. We sponsor their insulin, counsel them and provide treatment at Ruby Hall Clinic," said Mutha, who is also the chief diabetologist at Ruby Hall Clinic. The cost of caring for each child is at least Rs 3,000 per month, he said.

While Mutha's foundation has organised a roadshow on Thursday and Friday and a walkathon from Shaniwar Wada till Bal Gandharva Rang Mandir, the diabetologist feels a great deal of awareness needs to be created about Type 1 diabetes.

According to Dr Neelam Kumari, physician at the KEM diabetes unit, the cost of bringing up a child suffering from juvenile diabetes is three times more than the normal child.

Heading: National meet on telemedicine  from today - Indian Express
Content:
The last day of the Red Ribbon Express' three-day halt in the city recorded another poor turnout, the lowest in the three-day stay at the city railway station.

The train could only manage to attract a crowd of 850 visitors today, which was even less than that of day one when 938 visitors had come to see the exhibition in Red Ribbon Express train. Some of the members of the team working in Red Ribbon Express blamed it on poor publicity given to the train ahead of its arrival.

However, the number of visitors from among the general public was evidently high today, giving some solace to the organisers and volunteers working in the train. Some of them remarked that it was nice to see people coming voluntarily to see the exhibition and asking questions to clarify their doubts.

The visitors also expressed appreciation for the volunteers for imparting knowledge about the disease. "Their work is highly appreciable and it has been a good attempt to create awareness. But there could be some signboards to direct us to the goods shed at the station," said Emmanuel, a visitor from CMCH.

"It was really a very nice experience working as a volunteer with the Red Ribbon Express for three days. We are a group of 30 students and two teachers and everyone has got the satifaction of making people aware of the deadly disease. But we wished there could be more crowd as we had yesterday," said Jyoti, a teacher from Guru Angad Dev School of Nursing.

The visitors kept trickling in ones and twos till 5 o'clock in the evening today. "We had heard about the train so we were just curious about it and therefore came here since it is a holiday also," said Vonod Kapoor, a working professional visiting along with his two friends.

Dr Chanchal Jaggi, Ayurvedic Medical Officer, who was also working as a volunteer at an exhibit showing the importance of getting the delivery conducted at hospital, said about 20 per cent of the visitors showed complete ignorance about various aspects of the disease, let alone the medicine available for HIV positive pregnant women to avoid the disease in the child."

The train will now head for Ambala tonight from where it will leave for Chandigarh, it is learnt.

Heading: Amateur circuit’s rising star - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 200 scientists and experts, including those from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) involved in the Chandrayaan-I mission, are expected to participate in the fourth national conference on Telemedicine Society of India — Telemedicon '08 — which is organised by C-DAC, Mohali and the PGIMER. The three-day conference will begin on November 14.

The conference is based on — "Telemedicine-Rural and Remote Reach" and is the first exclusive national conference being organised in India that covers the various facets of healthcare delivery through technology-based system.

"The conference aims to create awareness among the various healthcare providers, doctors and administrators about the ways and benefits of adopting the emerging telemedicine technology as an effective tool for healthcare delivery," said Prof S K Jindal, head of the telemedicine project in PGI.

The PGI already has a linkage with Bhutan through the telemedicine project and the conference will discuss the healthcare requirements in other SAARC countries, Africa and South-East Asia to help provide better insight into the development of telemedicine facility in these countries.

"The advantage of telemedicine in reaching out to the rural population has been well established through the experience of the present network," said J S Bhatia, director of C-DAC Mohali.

An exhibition displaying the latest technology involved in equipment, software and systems, medical informatics and innovative clinical methods for healthcare, will also be conducted during Telemedicon08.

Heading: Vikram closes the gap on Rashid - Indian Express
Content:
Seventeen-year-old Rashid Khan is one of the few Indian golfers who have won the Indian amateur title twice and has two back to back wins in the Indian Amateur Tour this season in the form of Golden Greens Amateur and Northern Indian Amateur. And now the Delhi lad is very keen on adding the Chandigarh title to his kitty. "I will be quite happy if I win this title. It will be my third title in a row," said Rashid at the end of the day's proceedings at Chandigarh Golf Club on Thursday.

The Delhi golfer though has plenty to do to reel in the two players besides him in the Indian circuit-Rahul Bakshi and Chikkarrangappa- who will be hoping to turn the tide against Khan in the next few months. "I have been playing well for the past season. It has been my swing on which I need to work upon as the coming months will see me participating in a plenty of tournaments. My putting has been right and I need to be more consistent on the Indian Amateur Tour," said Rashid who is currently based in Delhi and is a regular at Delhi Golf Club.

Positive trimmings

LAST month also saw Rashid playing in the Eisenhour Trophy and Nick Faldop Series Final in Brazil, an event where he finished a poor 21st, but the Delhi golfer reckons that the experience will help him in the international arena. "It was learning experience for me. Both Eisenhour Trophy and Nick Faldo Series provided me an opportunity to play with some of the best junior gold players in the world. It helped a lot in improving my game and apart from playing; I also gained a lot on the mental aspect of the game. Nick Faldo Series sees the participation of over 80 top golfers across the world and everyone is eager to perform well there," said Rashid and after an after thought added. "Although I finished a poor 21, I guess I will be more prepared for the next time,"

There is plenty to look for Rashid in the coming season as he will be participating in the Volvo Masters of Asia in December along with Chandigarh's Rahul Bakshi before playing in the domestic circuit again.

"I will be playing in Pune for an amateur tournament before I take part in the Volvo Masters of Asia to be held in Thailand in December. I will be playing along with Rahul Bakshi and both of us are expecting a good result in Thailand. We will definitely like to end the season on a high," teed off Rashid.

Heading: Rajni grabs gold in 44 kg category - Indian Express
Content:
On a day when the wind went up at the Chandigarh Golf Club, so did the scores. A steady breeze through the day and tough pin placements meant that no player in the field was able to break par. But as the round drew to a close, the protagonists still remained the same and the stage is set for a two way battle on the final day between Vikram Rana and Rashid Khan. Rashid will go into the last round with a two stroke lead but if the conditions remain as difficult as they were today then we could see some changes at the top. Vikram got off to an inauspicious start after three putting from a distance of a little over two feet on the first hole. A triple bogey on the first and a bogey on the par 5 second seemed to indicate that he would fade away leaving Rashid lonely on top of the leaderboard. He said "I still don't know what happened on the first and I am searching for answers. Although it was a short putt the ball lipped out on both occasions". But he regained ground with an eagle from the centre of the fairway on the short par 4 sixth and reduced the deficit to one stroke. "I just hit a good shot there I guess. It got me back in to the round and kept me in the thick of the action".

A final score of four over 76 was still not that bad considering he is trailing the leader by just two strokes behind and three shots clear of the next best player in the field. Abhinav Lohan was the only one who left the course without any battle wounds as he returned a card of even par 72, which moved him up to third spot and in to the last group for the final round. Abhinav Lohan who had a good outing at the LG Golden Greens Amateur where he was in contention for his first win on tour fell back on the last two days. A good round today has given him another chance and he would be looking to make the most of this opportunity.

Local lad Aman Guron who would be hoping to keep the LG Samarvir Sahi Amateur trophy within Chandigarh, had an off day and slid down the leaderboard. With 18 holes left it remains to be seen if Rashid can pocket another title on tour or whether one of the men behind can stop his run.
