It further states that 'the university has planned several academic programmes and infrastructure development at Kalina for which this land will be required'.

In another letter to the principal secretary of the housing, Khole wrote that the University needed the land for hostels for the students as well as residential quarters.

Heading: HC admits transferred Indian convict’s plea seeking release - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai traffic police is going in for a major revamp of the city's traffic management infrastructure. In six months, the city will get its first Autonomous Traffic Control (ATC) signals along the city's VIP corridors which will be the latest in the stream of improvements funded by the World Bank. This will upgrade the traffic management infrastructure to an international level with the help of Mumbai traffic police and the BMC traffic department. The most significant is a video wall, which is in essence a big screen that can be divided into sections containing data feeds sent from the new signals and video footage from the 95 CCTV cameras already installed in the city. This will bring about a major improvement in the present system where 7 CCTV's are presently being used to monitor the same footage. Along with this, officers in the control room can, at the push of a button, adjust any problem that may come up on the city roads by re-arranging signals.

In the present system, the timers are reset manually, but with the installation of the video wall and ATC technology this can now be done by the staff in the control room. The Mumbai traffic police will also extend the network to three other main corridors in Mumbai (east-west and north-south) and make signals systems almost entirely autonomous. The traffic signals and traffic movements will be controlled by the officers sitting in the control room who will manage traffic throughout the city.

As opposed to the present signals that operate on a timer that changes lights according to a set time, the new signals will now actually measure traffic congestion on the road and adjust lights to prevent bottlenecks. This means that commuters while travelling during rush hour will not have to worry about red signals as they will be set accordingly to allow smooth flow of traffic by increasing the time allotted to green signals in that direction. The signals will be connected to each other and the traffic control room via MTNL lines allowing better co-ordination and efficient traffic management.

The new signals are led-based and are extremely versatile and can accommodate any symbols fed by the people in control room. For example if the road ahead is congested or blocked due to a procession or any other reason, instead of sending a police man to divert traffic to the left or right, the signal will on a command from the control room will do the job by displaying an arrow in the right direction.

Along with the ATC, other initiatives are already in place such as an area wise subscriber only SMS alert sytem, a bulletin board on the Mumbai traffic police website with traffic information and a multicoloured board, part of verbal messaging system (VMS) has been set up at RTI junction at Peddar Road allowing the police to send a message to commuters at once.

Most of the traffic systems are managed by the old control room infrastructure but after the revamp it will become easier for officers to control it.

"It will free our officers to catch actual violators and take away the stress of directing traffic as this is autonomous," said Jont Commisioner of Police Sanjay Barve. " With time management and more efficiency at hand, the officers will have more time to catch violators. The video wall will also help in gathering data and comparing information received from traffic signals with that of the CCTV cameras and help us gauge situations," he added.

However, Barve believes that the advantage of this system is its flexibility and versatility. "This will be extremely helpful in times of festivals and VIP visits," he added.

Heading: Court asks state to review murder convict’s early release plea - Indian Express
Content:
Transferred Indian convict from Mauritius who was sentenced to 15 years imprisonment, now has a ray of hope after the Bombay High Court recently admitted his petition for his release under Indian laws.

Amin Abdul Hamid Zariwala, presently lodged in Byculla Central Prison, had moved the Bombay High Court after failing to get any respite from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) under the Repatriation of Prisoners Act 2003.

Other transferred convicts in similar situation are now waiting for the outcome of the petition. The High Court in August had directed the MHA to take a decision on a representation made by Zariwala, an Indian national, convicted to 15 years imprisonment in Mauritius for smuggling heroin. He was later transferred to Mumbai after which he sought to be released as he has served more than 10 years— which is the prescribed sentence under Indian laws— in jail.

The Ministry, however, rejected the representation after which Zariwala amended the petition and challenged the order.

Neeraj Kansal, director, MHA, in an affidavit states that both the contracting countries had enacted the Act to "facilitate the social rehabilitation of sentenced persons into their own countries by giving foreigners, who have been convicted and sentenced as a result of their commission of a criminal offence, the opportunity to serve their sentences in their own society."

"So the underlying principle behind such transfer is social rehabilitation of the sentenced person," Kansal states.

Moreover, Kansal also states that as per the treaty, the transferring state alone shall decide on any application for review of judgement for which he shall have to approach the courts in Mauritius.

Advocate Rizwan Merchant, who appeared for Zariwala, told a division bench of the court that this was just the tip of the iceberg as there are other convicts who are waiting for the outcome of this petition. According to Merchant, there are some convicts who have been sentenced to 35 years imprisonment by courts in Mauritius.

Zariwala contended that his sentence should be made compatible with the laws of the country under the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act. Zariwala was arrested on July 7, 1995, in Mauritius for allegedly importing 77.8 gram of heroin. Subsequently, on October 25, 1996, the Supreme Court of Mauritius sentenced him to undergo 15 years imprisonemnet for charges under the Dangerous Drugs Act. His appeal for reducing the sentence period too was turned down in November 1997.

However, in October 2005, an agreement was signed between the Indian and Mauritius governments whereby opportunity was given to Indian nationals convicted in Mauritius to be transferred to India to serve the remaining sentence within their own society, to facilitate social rehabilitation of the prisoners into their own countries under the Transfer of Prisoners (Republic of India) Regulations 2006.

Heading: Malvani murder: Police say interior designer killed during robbery attempt - Indian Express
Content:
A 40-year-old murder convict got new hope for being freed after the Bombay High Court struck down a state government order that stated he should spend 28 years in prison before his plea for an early release can be considered.

Devidas Balaji Raut, who is lodged at the Nagpur Central prison, was sentenced to life imprisonment on February 25, 1994 for committing a murder. Since then, he has spent over 14 years in jail including the remission period. In 2006, he moved an application before the Home department requesting the state to consider his plea for premature release considering his good behaviour in prison and the undergone period.

However, the state government, by its order dated July 10, 2006, rejected Raut's plea after categorising him under category 6 (a) of the guidelines for premature release of prisoners sentenced to life imprisonment. This category is for the prisoners who escaped from lawful custody while undergoing an imprisonment or who absconded while on parole or furlough. Under the category, the state considers the plea for early release of the convict only after he spends 28 years in jail. Later, Raut challenged the order in the high court.

On Monday, a Division Bench of Justice D D Sinha and Justice A P Bhangale observed that "the accused had escaped from the custody of the police on July 3, 1993, for which he was prosecuted and convicted for a year's sentence". This was before Raut was convicted to life imprisonment. The Bench thus observed that "the (state government's) order is completely silent on this aspect and, therefore, in our view, suffers from non-application of mind, hence cannot be sustained in law".

The Bench, then, directed the state government to reconsider the categorisation of Raut as a convict after taking into consideration the relevant facts and circumstances, including the aspect of applicability of provisions of category 6 (a), and take a decision on his plea within eight weeks of this order.

Heading: Ailing Thane civic body SoS to BEST - Indian Express
Content:
Contrary to its earlier theory that 25-year-old interior decorator Fayyaz Siddiqui alias Aseem Khan's murder could have been a result of a love affair gone awry, police now claim that Khan was killed during a robbery bid.

A joint team of the Malvani and Malad police, which was investigating the case, said two youth entered the bungalow, inside which Khan's body was found, with an aim of robbing valuables and thinking that it was unoccupied.

Senior Police Inspector Jaywant Hargude from the Malvani police station said, "Khan, who was supervising the interior decoration of the bungalow, would regularly go there after dinner and spend the night there. On Monday morning, when Khan did not return home, his father Naseem Khan tried calling him up. But when he received no answer, he went to the bungalow and found the front door lock broken. On venturing inside, he discovered his son's body and a hammer with blood stains lying nearby, and contacted the police."

"During investigation, we discovered that Khan's mobile phone had been missing. While trying to track the culprits, we received information that a youth working as a daily-wage labourer in the Ambujwadi slums of Malvani was trying to sell a brand new mobile phone. We suspected the phone could be the one taken from the murder spot and we picked up Vijay Shinde (23), the youth from the slums," said Police Inspector Deepak Phatangare from the Malad police station, who was part of the investigating team.

On interrogating Shinde, he confessed to his involvement in the murder and disclosed the name of his accomplice, one Shankar Kurade (19) who also worked as daily-wage labourer, said the police.

Heading: East-west skywalk in Kalyan soon - Indian Express
Content:
After allowing the Brihanmumbai Transport and Electric Supply (BEST) to ply on its routes, the Thane Municipal Transport (TMT) has now sought the management expertise of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region's transport giant.

Officials from the BEST undertaking, TMT and Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC) held a meeting last week in which the TMT and TMC approached the BEST undertaking for help.

  "We have approached BEST undertaking for help," said TMC Commissioner Nandkumar Jantre. The TMT is a transport arm of the TMC and provides transport service to commuters in Thane. "We have asked for BEST officials to be sent on deputation and a proposal is to be tabled before the TMT committee and the TMC." The BEST officials, if appointed, would help the TMT in cutting its losses. Plans are also in store to take help from the former BEST workers.

These ambitious plans might hit a roadblock. A week ago, when the BEST undertaking started its services on the Mulund-Borivli route via Ghodbunder Road (Thane), the Sharad Rao-led union of the TMT and auto-rickshaws went on strike to protest BEST entry in Thane. "Mooting this proposal will be difficult, but it needs political consensus and that has to be worked out as we have no option," said a TMT official.

The ailing transport arm has failed in terms of providing quality service to the commuters and has little options. The TMT, currently, has 288 buses in its fleet of which 196 are more than 15 year-old and worth scrapping. Due to this, the cost of travelling per kilometre also increases. It needs 500 buses in its fleet so that it can improve its services and add 60 more routes. However, with a budget of Rs 100 crore, it suffers a loss of Rs 4-5 crore every year.

"We have received an request from the TMT and TMC. When we get an official communication from the TMT, we will depute out men," said BEST undertaking general manager Uttam Khobragade.

Heading: Dombivli resident scripts encyclopedia of inventors in Marathi - Indian Express
Content:
In order to ease traffic congestion in Kalyan, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority will construct a 1.4 km skywalk connecting eastern and western sides of the suburban railway station.

The decision to construct the skywalk, with an estimated cost of Rs 83.90 crore, was taken after a meeting of MMRDA official with Vasant Davkhare, deputy chairperson, Maharashtra Legislative Council, elected representatives and officials of the Kalyan-Dombivali Municipal Corporation.

The proposed skywalk will be constructed in two parts, according to the MMRDA spokesperson. The skywalk begins from Kalyan Railway Station (west) to Gurudev Hotel and from Gurudev Hotel to Shivaji Chowk and is 630 metre long and seven metres wide, the remaining area that is yet to be decided, the width is four metres and length is 770 metres. This skywalk will connect the three existing rail over bridges at Kalyan station.

Metropolitan Commissioner Ratnakar Gaikwad said that the skywalk is an ambitious project and is constructed under Station Area Traffic Improvement Scheme and will help ease traffic congestions on railways station. "MMRDA will also work on the extension of the existing skywalk at Dombivali, said Gaikwad.

The skywalk at Kalyan is part of the Rs 600-crore project initiated by MMRDA to decongest station areas in Mumbai and Mumbai Metropolitan Region. In all there are 50 skywalks proposed by the MMR, of which 11 skywalks are proposed beyond Mumbai municipal limits. The first skywalk was constructed at Bandra east, which connects it to Kalanagar. The work on the exclusive walkway is underway at Virar and Kanjurmarg, which is a skywalk cum hawking plaza.

Encroachments at Juhu lane cleared
The strenuous drive of 45 minutes from Juhu to SV Road will now be cut down to 10 minutes , as the encroachments on the NC Phadke Marg have been removed under the road widening drive of MMRDA. The widening of road of NC Phadke Marg is from Local Self Government Andheri to Gulmohur Road and the Juhu Lane was a missing link as it was impossible to travel through it.

"Before the demolition it used to take 45 minutes to reach SV Road from Juhu however now the motorists to cover the same distance in 10 minutes," said Dilip Kawathkar, Joint Project Director (Public Relation). In all, there were 947 illegal encroachments and in the past two years, MMRDA has successfully managed to remove 940 encroachments. Those that were authorised were rehabilitated at Oshiwara and Poonam Nagar respectively. The remaining seven structures were demolished two days ago. Of these, five authorised encroachments have been relocated at Oshiwara, other two were illegal , Kawathkar said.

Heading: Prince of tides - Indian Express
Content:
Here's a 21-year-old with a jewellery brand of her own

Jagmeeta Thind Joy

When they say starting out young, they must mean this. She's all of 21 but is already spearheading a jewellery brand of her own. She's Chitwn D Malhotra who is all set to introduce the city's fashion frat to Dillano, her one-year-old creation. "Dillano is an Italian word that stands for nature, from which I am much inspired," says the confident young lady as she showcased some of her works on Thursday afternoon at Hotel Mountview. The lineup included a contemporary collection of diamond jewellery in unique designs. "Diamonds are getting colourful and the designs are bold," says Chitwn. The fact that she's been awarded the 'Most Innovative Designer of the Year' by the World Gold Council when still in college then comes as little surprise. "I have always been creatively inclined," tells Malhotra who completed a two-year professional diploma from Jewellery Designing And Technology Institute, Noida to get her started on to a career in design. "Dillano is a year old but we have already exhibited our work in numerous exhibitions held across the country," mentions the Delhi-based designer who has her father's full support for the venture. "Dillano is a high-end BIS approved hallmarked brand and we are all set to showcase this season's collection at Hotel Taj starting November 14," pitches in her father Deep Malhotra, who is also the company's chairman.

These times of recession don't seem to bother the Malhotras either. "You know jewellery buying in India is attached with a lot of emotion. The marriage season has begun and a bride's not going to buy just because these are bad times. In fact gold shopping hasn't seen a slump, not yet," says Chitwn who seems to be forging ahead with her expansion plans. "For starters, Dillano plans to open a flagship showroom by 2009 in a five star hotel in Delhi as well as cities like Chandigarh, Ludhiana and Indore," informs the designer who aims to go international by 2010. Way to go!

Heading: Baby’s day out - Indian Express
Content:
He may have earned the reputation of an entertainer, but Salman Khan hates to talk

Expect him to do the unexpected. Salman Khan, who enjoys the reputation of being a late-comer, is already parked on a chair outside his vanity van at Mehboob Studio. Dressed in a brown tee, media's favourite bashing boy patiently indulges in elaborate interviews. His personal staff—secretary, media relations, body guards, tea vendor and assorted 'friends'—hang around to ensure his comfort, bringing the otherwise deserted studio alive.

His media friendliness is apparent but he candidly attributes it to his "duty" towards his producers. "With three films ready for release, the producers are on my head to promote them. It isn't that I hate the media—I'm just not the sort who talks. Why talk when a look can convey it all?" he winks.

The last two years have been rather unusually quiet for Salman at the box-office— he's done special appearances in films by his friends and family, each of who have carried a thank-you note in the credits. He insists it embarrasses him. "I wish they'd stop," he states as his volume drops a notch. In the same breath he stresses that he never does a film for his loved ones if he doesn't like the script.

After teasing his fans with cameos, Khan's next, Yuvvraaj, is one of the biggest releases for the year. Khan affirms that the film's family plot is what made him sign it. "But I'm not a family man yet," he says with his signature sarcasm intact.

This is the first time he's working with director Subhash Ghai. "I thought he'd bore me, pakao me, but he was okay," he smiles mischievously. The actor shares camaraderie with Anil Kapoor but Zayed Khan had him impressed. "More than shooting, we were partying at each other's expense."

The formal look he sports, designed by Ashley Rebello and sister Alvira Khan, is a sharp contrast to his popular shirtless avatar, but he doesn't mind that for a change. His sole complaint: "They made me spike my hair blonde." That's only one of Salman's three looks in Yuvvraaj. "I later pull my hair back as it grows out; and then there's this advantage of working with Ghai— he makes his actors wear caps," he laughs.

With four releases lined up, 2009 is going to keep Salman, who turns 43 next month, busy. While Main Aur Mrs Khanna and London Dreams are romantic dramas, Wanted: Dead and Alive and Veer end his hiatus as an action hero after Garv in 2003. "Wanted was painful—there are a lot of gory scenes—and all the stunts have been done by me," he says.

On a lighter note, there's a sequel to Andaz Apna Apna, a film that never worked at the box office but was "a blackmarket hit". "It's my favourite but Katrina (girlfriend Kaif) didn't even smile when she saw it," Khan adds, seemingly disappointed. "I feel sorry for the producer—he must be dying of poverty somewhere."

Heading: Physical Education - Indian Express
Content:
This Children's Day, think twice before lavishing your loved ones

Though a reason to splurge on kids is just an excuse these days, Children's Day makes for the perfect occasion to splurge on them. From special outings to a hair makeover to an all new wardrobe, options are aplenty.

"If my kids had their way, I would be shopping for a car right now," laughs model Waluscha Robinson, "But both my kids will have to make do with the Sony Vaio that we gifted my daughter Chanel on her birthday recently." She finds spending up to Rs 50,000 on educative gadgets an investment.

Designer clothes and bags for kids have always made for sought-after gifts, what with special kids' line by Burberry (where a T-shirt costs Rs 2,500 and a shirt Rs 6,500), Armani and Moschino to name a few. But a kids' salon as a concept has picked up remarkably. "I'll treat my 12-year-old to a fancy hairdo this Children's Day; it's a step towards educating him about grooming," grins Indrani Chatterjee, a banker, who plans to take her son Arvind to Watermelon, a kids' salon in Bandra. She will be spending anything between Rs 500 to Rs 1,200 there. There's also Tears To Cheers, Warden Road, where the tots sit in car-shaped seats and watch cartoons on a private TV while getting a chop (for Rs 350).

The most common activity parents indulge their kids in every Children's Day is to take them for an event. Classic Animation Studio, in an attempt to fire the imagination of animation-loving children (five to 14), is organising a day camp at Deokane, a village 120 km from Mumbai. Apart from launching their new animation film, Buji, the animation studio has planned a fun-filled day of activities, games, animation workshops and performances.

And while your child's away at the camp, you could have your interior designer over to do up his/ her room. You can choose from bed and bath linen with their favourite cartoon characters like Mickey Mouse, Sponge Bob and Winnie the Pooh by Portico New York (Rs 500 onwards), innovatively designed furniture for their room by @home (Rs 5,000 upwards).

The much publicised sentimentality of Bhavna Jasra's First Impressions is a great option to mere photographs of your kids. "To mount a 3-D model of your loved ones' feet and hands in gold, is the warmest way to show them your love," says the entrepreneur who charges

Rs 15,000 for a set in bronze. Jasra's Photo Concept with Krsna Mehta is an alternate for those with a tighter budget. "We personalise the everyday articles used by children, like bags, satchels and folders."

Parents who believe that a gift for Children's Day should be a tad serious and educative can enroll their children in one of the many hobby classes on offer these days. Toddlers Activity Centre in Worli is a 2,000 sq ft facility for children of up to 14 years. Programmes to introduce toddlers to speech and action, art, craft, music and ballet classes are some of the activities on offer. However, one wonders what a three-month-old will gain from a yoga class, especially if it makes you lighter by Rs 3,000.

There are other such options too; Bhanu's Fit Kids at Tardeo charges an average of Rs 350 per session lasting 50 minutes, where one story is told and one craft model is made, mostly by the accompanying maids.

Whatever happened to the good, old drive and ice cream with dad.

Heading: Children’s Day: ‘Offenders’ turn cops’ guests - Indian Express
Content:
I discovered the hard way that tearing a ligament is much worse than breaking a bone. When I fell off my four-inch wedge heels. Nearly two months ago. Nothing really prepares you for the pain or the slow recovery process. Not even the fact that I had been down this road six years ago.

I knew I had the legacy of a weak left ankle but what didn't sink in is the fact that it would be prone to letting me down.

I was even more hurt when my regular orthopaedic surgeon refused to take my SOS calls.

Saturday noon injuries, according to his assistant, needed to wait till Monday evening for treatment. It was the start of the weekend and the Hippocrates oath had been locked up at the office.

Luckily a friend gave me a physiotherapist's number. Not only did the doctor return my call, she had her junior waiting for me when I hobbled in, wincing in agony. Half an hour later, I walked out. Better. Still hurt but cheerful as the pain was 50 per cent less. Since then, I have gone back every day and now I am actually gloating about my injury. Because I had discovered a tiny hamlet of professionals who still care. Located opposite Babulnath Temple, this charitable clinic is run by a dynamic doctor and her assistants. They charge 1920s' prices but give you 21st century treatment. From the exercise they prescribe to the equipment they use—everything is just right. It may lack the shine and sparkle of some of our newer facilities but it has the one thing they lack: Compassion.

When I watch the team deal with the older people who come with age-related ailments, they are gentle, yet firm. And always patient. If someone wants to ask the same question again and again, they take the time to reply.

Strangely, their time management is also perfect. No matter how crowded it gets, or how late you arrive for an appointment, they take you in. When I asked how they managed, their reason was simple: "Your time is as valuable as ours." I have perhaps another month left but I know I shall miss coming here. Because I like to be reminded of a time when doctors could be counted on. Also time tends to stand still here. No one watches the clock. They watch the patient.

Which is why I am bewildered at doctor's attitudes—specially the orthopaedic ones. They actually discourage you from going for physiotherapy. Perhaps they feel that once they pronounce a person well, they can disengage from the healing process. But that is only half the battle won. From personal experience, I can say that this time my ankle hurt less and healed faster this time—as compared to the last. Sure there was no short cut to rest but even while I was in bed, a long-term view on wellness was being worked out.

I am still a month away from full recovery but I am promised that once that happens, the left leg will be stronger than before. I believe them because I have seen the results. Be it a niggling pain in the back or a slight twinge in the wrist,

I have seen it all fixed. So write your own prescription for pain: Ignore doctor's orders and visit a physiotherapist.

(The columnist is Editor-in-Chief, ELLE)

Heading: From furniture to pets, no escaping thefts in VIP area - Indian Express
Content:
After Khosla ka Ghosla, Dibakar Banerjee hopes to hit the jackpot again with Oye Lucky Lucky Oye

Dibakar Banerjee does not like comparisons to Hrishikesh Mukherjee. "He had his style of filmmaking and I have mine," he defends, "the only point of similarity is that we both made films about ordinary people."

Banerjee's directorial debut, Khosla ka Ghosla about a middle-class family caught in a land scam, hit bull's-eye with the multiplex going audience. Expectations are now riding high on his next film, Oye Lucky Lucky Oye. But the pressure rests easy on Banerjee's shoulders even as he excitedly talks about his new film. "It's about a thief who's very special," he says, "unlike other thieves, who never want anyone to find out anything about them, this guy wants everyone to know he's the one who committed the crime. He has a talent for stealing and he's very proud of his 'craft'. If you haven't figured out it's him, he'll call you and tell you that he did it!"

It's obvious that Banerjee is attracted to stories that are a little out of the ordinary. And, he says, that tendency also affected the choice of his movie's leading man, Abhay Deol. "Abhay likes to look at the unusual side of things. He doesn't believe in doing what everyone else does. In that sense, we're very alike," he explains, "Moreover he's a very intense actor. That doesn't usually come out since he plays it cool, but he's one of the most focused actors I've met. This intensity of his will take him a long way," he predicts.

Banerjee is, in fact, very upbeat about all the actors in his movie. "We've deliberately not repeated any of the cast members from Khosla. We wanted to work with old and established actors like Paresh Rawal and also some new faces. In fact, there are 10 new actors in this film, five of whom have never acted before."

The music in his films, says Banerjee, also plays a very important role in the narration. "In most Indian movies, music plays a very important role in drawing the audience to the theatres and in providing breaks throughout the narration," he says, "I'm not entirely comfortable with that idea. So instead, even the songs are pushed into the background and become an integral part of the storytelling." The soundtrack of Khosla was a huge hit for the freshness of its sound and Banerjee has made sure that this time too, the audience has something new to listen to. "We've recruited a young talent called Sneha Khandwala. She actually went backpacking in Haryana and Punjab and brought back the old, forgotten melodies and poetry from those regions. You'll hear a lot of folk music on this soundtrack; we've even got folk singers singing here."

Heading: Life’s beautiful and full of fun for this king of humour - Indian Express
Content:
Law and order has always been a vexed issue in Le Corbusier's city. But the bad news now is that even 'VIP areas' have lost their edge and a VIP's neighbours can no longer expect a reprieve from the attentions of petty thieves.

Forget manhole covers and garden furniture, even dogs brought in to guard one's property are no longer safe.

A case in point would be Sector 28A, where securitymen are deployed round-the-clock at the home of parliamentarian Pawan Kumar Bansal.

His neighbours, however, get a nasty surprise every other morning, when anything in their yard that's not nailed down, goes missing.

A number of residents living in Sector 28-A have approached the police complaining of thefts. The concerned police station — Sector 26 — has, however, not only failed to do the needful but abstained from registering cases.

One such case was reported by a retired Major, a resident of House No. 56, Sector 28-A. Major Jagatpal Singh Brar (Retd) told the police on November 8 that the wrought iron furniture (six chairs and a centre table), which were lying in the front lawn of his palatial house, were stolen in broad daylight. The complaint found no ears and after more than a week, the police have not yet registered a case on Brar's complaint.

"A sub-inspector from Sector 26 police station visited my house and questioned me for long. While I answered all his queries and asked him to redress my complaint, he simply started lecturing me against registering a case. He told me that I will have to go through a long legal hassle and even if the police recover my stolen furniture, it will be of no use as it would be the court's property. This is the attitude of our police. I wonder if they are waiting for something disastrous to happen," said Major Brar.

"It was a theft in broad daylight. I came out of my room about 4 pm and found the furniture stolen. For the police, however, this is nothing but a legal hassle," added Major Brar.

This is not all. A large number of manhole covers have also been stolen from outside various houses on the same street. Captain Bhushan Nanda, attached to Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, lives in House No. 50 on the same street and narrated his experience. "A few days ago, manhole covers outside my house were stolen. About a couple of weeks ago, somebody entered my residence and took away the stabilisers by cutting the electricity wires. My golden retriever pup and a dog have been stolen. My servant's bicycle was taken away — all these thefts, within a span of few months. What are the police for? The situation is serious indeed."

Many other houses have also not been spared, especially when it comes to manhole covers and other petty household articles. "Manhole covers were even stolen from outside House No. 55 of Dr H S Pannu, who retired as Head of Department (Pathology, PGIMER) and also from House No. 57. When will the police take action?" a distraught resident of the area told Newsline.

SHO laments lack of manpower
Inspector Raghbir Singh, Station House Officer, Police Station-26, said: "I have only three personnel to guard the whole sector. There are two head constables and one constable for Sector 28. As far as the matter of not registering the case goes, I will verify it. If such is the case in the area, I will personally patrol there regularly. It is not that we don't do anything. We have arrested two minor boys, while stealing manhole covers. Both have been sent to the juvenile home."

Heading: HUDA eyes Mansa Devi parking - Indian Express
Content:
Hailing from a family of farmers who now run a dhaba, 25-year-old Jaswant Singh never imagined his childhood talent of mimicking others would take him places.

The young artiste has had many a firsts in life. Till date, he is the only member in his family to go to college and none of his relatives, even distant, ever performed on stage.

The young and talented comedian impressed the world with his impeccable sense of humour at the Great Indian Laughter Challenge-IV. Shooting to instant 15 minutes of fame, especially with his mimics of Bollywood actor Sunil Shetty, Jaswant made it to the finals and was ranked sixth.

"I feel contented that I made it so far in a show which hosted comedy maestros from far flung places of the country. The competition was tough and I am happy I made a mark," gleams Jaswant.

A Masters in History from Ludhiana, Jaswant recalls his days in Chandigarh in 2004 when he did stand-up comedy acts with laughter king Khayali at Sector 17 Plaza.

"I would crack jokes, do acts of mimicry and add loads of humour in the story. This started when I was really young. But my talent was noticed after I entered college and participated extensively in youth festivals. This was followed by winning laughter show — Hasde Hasande — on MH1 channel in 2006," Jaswant says.

After spending more than three months in Mumbai for the laughter challenge, Jaswant is now flooded with offers to host live shows, besides offers from films. He is planning to shift to Mumbai soon. "It's back to the routine life after the show. I am ready to establish myself, but it is versatility in stand-up comedy where my focus lies at present," he says, adding he doesn't want to be confined to doing mimics alone.

Speaking more about the laughter challenge, the comedian says the presence of Bollywood legend Shatrughan Sinha on the panel of judges made things work for him. "I learnt a lot from him and his comments, which I always took in stride, took me where I am today," Jaswant says.

"The programme has provided platform to not only for Indians, but comedians from Pakistan and America. This is the ultimate encouragement for an artiste," he adds. Ask him about his favourite joke on the show and he takes no time. Everything pertaining to his acts of actor Sunil Shetty were well received and are his favourites too. "It all depends on one's creativity and I used to weave my script myself. Life is fun and full of humour, and that's how I see it," he signs off.

Heading: UT senior counsel crosses sword with UT Advisor - Indian Express
Content:
Plans to carve out residential plots, says 'prime land' just used during Navratras

In what seems to be a brazen attempt to rob the devotees of a major facility, the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) is planning to carve out residential plots by sacrificing the huge strip of parking at the Mata Mansa Devi temple in Panchkula.

Justifying its proposal sent to the state government, the HUDA authority stated that since the mela parking is mostly utilised during the 18 days of the two Navratras,

it was not wise to "waste" such prime land.

The development authority is saying this while brushing aside the fact that the same parking provides facility to lakhs of devotees who visit the temple especially during the Navratras as well as rest of the year.

Interestingly, the state government never misses to boast that lakhs of devotees visit the temple during the Navratras but the development authority is more bothered about minting money.

Ironically, the authority had been eyeing the area for earning big bucks by allotting plots though the development plan of the residential pocket provided for 100 metre wide belt for mela parking in layout plan of Sector 6 in Panchkula.

As an alternative, the HUDA has decided to transfer four acres of land near Sheetla Mata Mandir to the Mansa Devi Shrine Board, which will be used for parking. However, the area is grossly insufficient in view of the large vehicular traffic to the Mansa Devi temple, sources said.

HUDA, in its letter to the state government, has stated: "It is requested that the development plan may be amended, so as to omit the provisions of mela parking in Sector 6."

The authority has also allotted a few plots to the probable buyers and had been pressing the government to give the land to them. "An early decision is requested so that those who had been allotted plots (due to the authority's fault) in the mela parking area can be given possession."

"We have acquired additional land for the mela parking near the Sheetla Mata Mandir because plots in this parking area have been allotted through a draw of lots in 2006. We are only incorporating it in the development plan now," said T C Gupta, HUDA Chief Administrator.

Heading: Closed since Sept 2005, Kharar mill incurs loss of Rs 83.47 crore - Indian Express
Content:
UT senior standing counsel Advocate Anupam Gupta has questioned the motives of the Advisor to UT Administrator Pardeep Mehra, who had given a 'note of dissent' on the Medicity Project.

In a strongly-worded legal opinion which runs into 21 pages, Gupta has questioned Mehra's note as an afterthought and raised eyebrows over his 'impartiality'. The opinion was sought and approved by UT Administrator Gen S F Rodrigues (Retd).

The Advisor's note is 'clearly aimed at torpedoing the project after nine long months of complete silence' reads the opinion, and 'betrays a disturbing similarity' with the petition filed in the Punjab and Haryana High Court against the Medicity Project. The High Court had initially, in a PIL, restrained the Administration in February from accepting bids on the Medicity project. The stay was vacated on July 4 after a detailed reply by the Administration. Mehra had been dealing with the Medicity file since November 5, 2007, but voiced his objections only towards July-end this year.

"It is only when we move away from the public eye into the darkness of our own fears and ambitions that things become suspicious," Gupta said, responding to Mehra's caution that the project has been in the public eye for quite some time. The burden of selecting the best applicant for the project included the option of not selecting anyone if no one measures up to the challenge, reads the opinion. "The public eye will settle for nothing less, unless the eye itself is blinkered," he said.

Observing that Mehra was "unable to see land as anything more than land, rather than as medicine or education (or hospitals or schools)", Gupta pointed out — whether it be Chandigarh or any other city or region in the country, there can never be enough hospitals or schools. And the day healthcare ceases to be a priority on the agenda of the governance, government itself would cease to be relevant.

Warning against parting with precious urban land at a throwaway price, Mehra had, in his note, questioned the valuation of land for the Medicity Project recommending that the reserve price should reflect the present cost of urban land in Chandigarh.

Joining the issue with Mehra, Gupta said Mehra had "betrayed a complete lack of understanding of the very concept of a welfare state". His approach, Gupta said, would "subordinate the making of public policy to the depredations of a market victimised by its own greed and propensity for speculation. The speculator's estimate of the cost of urban land cannot, and must never, be the index of the commitment of the welfare state to public welfare or of its ability to fashion public policy to that end".

Taking on Mehra for his loaded reference to the danger of selling 'crown jewels' by undervaluing the land for the Medicity project, Gupta said: "The dazzle of regalia can be blinding but those who speak of crown jewels must first learn to distinguish between the real jewel and the fake."

The real jewel in the crown, said Gupta, Le Corbusier's Chandigarh, was saved last year by the repeal of the Apartment Rules. Had the rules not been repealed, he said, the city would have been up for grabs by the highest 'bidder' in a self-propelled, market-driven 'auction' replicated in every street and sector every other day.

Heading: Out of the books - Indian Express
Content:
The KHARAR Textile Mills (KTM), a unit of National Textile Corporation (NTC) Limited in Kharar, which was under closure, has incurred a cumulative loss of Rs 83.47 crore till March 31, 2008.

NTC chairman-cum-managing director (CMD) K Ramachandran Pillai has confided this to the Secretary (Labour), Union Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, in a letter, a copy of which is in possession with Newsline.

Pillai has urged the Centre to accord approval for the

closure of KTM among 12 "unviable" NTC units in the country, including Suraj Textile Mills (STM) in Malout (Punjab) and Sree Bijay Cotton Mills (SBCM) in Bijaynagar (Rajasthan).

Citing heavy losses as the main reason for the proposal, Pillai claimed that sufficient pumping of investment from time to time could not yield any concrete result so far.

KTM is lying closed since September 2005 after almost 800 of its employees were relieved by offering Modified Voluntary Retirement Scheme (MVRS) while remaining 78 staffers, including 21 NTC-graded officers and supervisors, 16 mill-graded clerical staff and 41 workers, will be terminated following the unit's closure.

Pillai said that KTM was a yarn spinning textile industry and it had last produced 4.84 lakh kg yarn before September 2005, since when its production, sale and purchase activities were lying completely stalled.

Since its virtual closure, the unit had incurred Rs 255.43 lakh administrative cost on paying the salary and wages to its remaining 78 staffer with no manufacturing and selling cost.

Presently, KTM has no finished products and raw material in its stocks barring store spare components worth Rs 2.04 lakh.

Prior to its closure, the unit had registered total sales of Rs 526.98 lakh from yarn and waste material in 2005-06.

Surprisingly, the Board for Industrial Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) had considered the proposal of KTM's revival at its meeting on May 27, 2008, before finally approving its closure among 12 unviable mills on September 5, 2008, said the KTM Workers' Union president Dinesh Prasad.

NTC had planned modernisation of its 29 mills, including KTM, in different parts of Delhi, Punjab and Rajasthan through joint venture partners in July 2006.

Of the two NTC mills in Kharar, Panipat Woolen Mills (PWM) had already been closed with its plant and land also sold out after relieving the workforce while the "surplus" land of KTM had already been sold.

Heading: Class Apart - Indian Express
Content:
Innovation is the new mantra of education as learning gets a 180 degree makeover

Teachers need to stop teaching so that learning can happen," Taran Guron quotes as I look on in wonder. A raised eyebrow and he follows, "See, the need today is for teachers to do less and students to do more, that's what education should be all about. It was, in fact, some years back that educators felt this. A trip around the schools in town will show you that we haven't taken long to adapt," remarks Guron who is part of The Achievers Programme. And true enough, not only are chalk-boards vanishing but classrooms have now become a fun and activity zone. And the transformation is not only in mood of the class, the walls too have stories and fairy tales to tell, the fans sport a colour of Holi. In short, Jacks and Jills of today have their hands full.

"Education at primary and higher levels has become a lot about interaction, activity and movement. Students are no longer constantly asked for 'pin-drop silence' or 'be seated'," tells Guron and we begin to wish we could be 10 again! "Many of us do, the 'chalk & talk' method is history now. Internet is being involved in teaching. Students can search for data online, and prepare presentations. As for Achievers, we believe that what students need to be taught is how and where to get the information, and how to use that information in real life, rather than rote learning or cramming. Learning should become more experimental and more meaningful."

Schools are now introducing math labs, robotics labs, the globe has been replaced by Google earth. Dramas, quizzes, brain-teasers et al have become a part of the curriculum. The game of monopoly is being used in economics for financial literacy. Students play ear, brain, nose, hand as part of biology lessons. Preeti Jishtu who heads Crucible at St John's to help boys with creative writing in English tells, "Since this session we are inviting journalists and writers to interact with the students. After the session the boys have the liberty to write, then they read their work to each other. They are happy that through this non-instructional way they get to think out of the box and get tips on grammar as well. They retain better this way." At Vivek High School, students are involved in various activities ranging from sports to needle work. "It is mandatory for students to choose two activities in the year. Debating societies and drama is a culture that has built up enhancing students' confidence, their concentration and learning abilities," Anu Chaudhary explains. While there are changes in the teaching styles, emphasis is also on looking at children as growing individuals as against only students. "Social skills are essential since children are exposed to too much too soon, a lot that we as mentors cannot control. So it is important that we prepare them for the changes," Shalini Sharma tells of her social skills programme. Shalini and Kimberley Beauchamp inculcate a lot of fun, puppetry and give children a chance to "make friends with their feelings". They feel that it's important to teach children to deal with emotions like anger, sadness, jealousy. "Our programs supplement school education and introduce children to a 'feelings language' that prepares them emotionally for life. We create a safe learning environment where feelings are not only recognized but used to attach meaning to learning. Lot of fun activities make the students eager to come and return!" That's because every lesson is taught as a story. On their trip to the dinosaur museum, for example, students learnt that the dinosaurs never had any friends because they were so angry and mean.

While the young ones no longer wait for the recess bell, the higher classes will have to wait for complete change. Harleen Kohli, resource mentor, CEVA, explains, "Parents and teachers at this level still have different ideas of what education and learning mean. A lot of changing needs to be done. We are working with pre-nursery and primary classes. As for classes above, we are trying to work out how transformation in education system can happen, space and resources are an issue." She emphasizes that activity based learning is best to relieve the students of stress and anxiety. "For instance, we learn science from daily experiences. Even adults learn best within a context. We need to get over our thinking that learning is a lot of information and no skills." While we wait for that, the juniors are all play and fun. Can we please go back to school again?

Heading: Psychologists to offer free services to children, adults at Ivy Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Prasoon Joshi talks about his songs in Ghajini and how interfering Aamir Khan is

In B-town, everyone is on song, even if it is a shaven, tattooed Aamir Khan who can't remember his phone number. Little wonder, Prasoon Joshi found himself penning poetry for all the brawn and brawl on display in Ghajini. "It is a pacy thriller with a lot of action and high energy, but the songs are extremely important to the narrative," says Joshi who has written five songs, all composed by AR Rahman, for the Khan starrer.

The film is a remake of a Tamil movie that was released three years ago, with songs written by N. Muthukumar, but Joshi says the Hindi soundtrack is completely original. "I did not even listen to the southern version as I did not want to be influenced in anyway," says Joshi, who, however, watched bits of the film to "gather a feel of it".

A little-known fact about ad man Joshi is that he is a trained classical musician who likes to compose and sing as well, but he has given them a miss in Ghajini. "I think it is very important for a lyricist to have a sense of music since it's then that the song shapes up wholly," says Joshi. He has composed and sung jingles for Alpenliebe and Happy Dent, among others. "But it's not something I'd do for films," he says.

Bollywood has heard enough complaints of Aamir Khan's interference, but Joshi thinks otherwise. "He is a very intelligent man and when he has a suggestion, it's often valid. When it is not, we argue a lot and whoever has a more powerful logic wins. So I'd say there's close understanding and mutual respect that allow us to bounce ideas off each other," he says.

If Joshi's poetry is not enough, then maybe you can watch the songs for another reason — one of them has Khan sporting six different hairstyles. Guess it's all relevant to the narrative.

Heading: Young Sparkle - Indian Express
Content:
Three senior psychologists from the district have decided to offer their services during a week-long screening of children and adults beginning from Friday at Ivy Hospital in Sector 71.

Starting this facility from November 14, Children's Day, psychologists Simmi Waraich, Harnoor Sandhu and Nitika Gupta will be available at the hospital to address childhood and adolescent behavioural problems, parenting issues, relationship counselling and other problems related to academics, exam anxiety, headaches, somatic problems and anger management among children and adults from 10 am to 5 pm daily.

"The aim is to promote awareness about these issues and prevent problems at an early stage by focusing on parent-child relationships and building self esteem in children, which is a prerequisite to prepare children for future challenges in life," Dr Simmi told Newsline.

She said children often show signs of stress which need to be identified. "A fearful or sad child may get stomach aches, may cry without reason and show withdrawal symptoms. Some children become irritable when under stress, tease siblings or peers and lose temper easily. Stress reactions can occur anywhere," explained the psychologist.

Advising parents on ways and means to manage stress among children, Dr Simmi said, "Do not expect the child to change suddenly. Start enforcing rules one at a time. Make a routine and stick to it without getting into debates. Listen to your children without cutting them off. Give importance to their their opinion. These are only some of the things that need to be introduced regularly by parents."

Discussing marital assessment for couples, she said there are certain aspects that determine the strengths of a relationship.

"A relationship's ability to stand strong in the face of things that life throws is vital, be it normal daily frustrations or extremely stressful external events," she added.

The psychologists have also developed a simple checklist that couples can use to get an estimate of the strength of their relationships.

"It is an interesting way to understand one's relationship better and areas to be focussed upon to build it further," the doctor concluded.

Heading: Kiddie Meal - Indian Express
Content:
He may have earned the reputation of an entertainer, but Salman Khan hates to talk

Expect him to do the unexpected. Salman Khan, who enjoys the reputation of being a late-comer, is already parked on a chair outside his vanity van at Mehboob Studio. His personal staff—secretary, media relations, body guards, tea vendor and assorted 'friends'—hang around to ensure his comfort, bringing the otherwise deserted studio alive.

His media friendliness is apparent but he candidly attributes it to his "duty" towards his producers. "With three films ready for release, the producers are on my head to promote them. It isn't that I hate the media—I'm just not the sort who talks. Why talk when a look can convey it all?" he winks. The last two years have been rather unusually quiet for Salman at the box-office— he's done special appearances in films by his friends and family. He insists it embarrasses him. "I wish they'd stop," he states. After teasing his fans with cameos, Khan's next, Yuvvraaj, is one of the biggest releases for the year. Khan affirms that the film's family plot is what made him sign it. "But I'm not a family man yet," he says.

This is the first time he's working with director Subhash Ghai. "I thought he'd bore me, pakao me, but he was okay," he smiles mischievously. The actor shares camaraderie with Anil Kapoor but Zayed Khan had him impressed. "More than shooting, we were partying at each other's expense."

The formal look he sports, designed by Ashley Rebello and sister Alvira Khan, is a sharp contrast to his popular shirtless avatar, but he doesn't mind that for a change. His sole complaint: "They made me spike my hair blonde." That's only one of Salman's three looks in Yuvvraaj. "I later pull my hair back as it grows out; and then there's this advantage of working with Ghai— he makes his actors wear caps," he laughs. With four releases lined up, 2009 is going to keep Salman, who turns 43 next month, busy. While Main Aur Mrs Khanna and London Dreams are romantic dramas, Wanted: Dead and Alive and Veer end his hiatus as an action hero after Garv in 2003. "Wanted was painful—there are a lot of gory scenes—and all the stunts have been done by me," he says.

On a lighter note, there's a sequel to Andaz Apna Apna, a film that never worked at the box office but was "a blackmarket hit". "It's my favourite but Katrina (girlfriend Kaif) didn't even smile when she saw it," Khan adds, seemingly disappointed. "I feel sorry for the producer—he must be dying of poverty somewhere."

Heading: Style file - Indian Express
Content:
Hotel Maya Palace's children's food festival comes well-timed

What better way to treat your kids than by taking them out for a special meal this Children's Day. Keeping the same in mind, Hotel Maya Palace (Sector 35), known for their thematic food fests is out with another well-timed one. Starting November 14, the hotel's Mirchi Kum restaurant will roll out a food festival specially designed for children. "Instead of making it a fast food affair, we have culled out kid-friendly dishes from various world cuisines," mentioned the hotel's business strategy and management consultant, Deepak Gupta. With a theme titled 'Feel Special, Eat Special', the festival brings in Lebanese, Italian, Shanghai, Mexican, Arabian, Continental and Chinese fare at special prices. "For example our special combo meal brings in a cola drink, French Fries, spring rolls, a soup, two varieties of noodles and rice along with Manchurian and followed up by dessert. Normally, this would cost Rs 199 but we have a special festival price of Rs 149," lists out Prem Rana, senior manager (operations) with Maya Palace. The special menu brings in the likes of 'Chicken Fajita with Salsa sauce', 'Creamy Fettuccine with Broccoli', 'Chicken Mushroom with Bamboo shoot rice' to an Arabic delicacy 'Sayyadieh' (fish with rice) to list a few. To bring in fun with food, the first day of the festival - November 14 - and the last day - November 30 will bring in activities like Tattoo making, magic shows and a Mickey Mouse too! "That's not all," says Gupta mentioning the discount on at the regular menu. "Parents can avail of discounts based on the age of their child. If they have a 14-year-old along, they get the same amount of discount," added Gupta. There will also be surprise gifts for kids celebrating their birthdays in the restaurant.

Heading: Six employees of automobile company booked for stealing SUVs - Indian Express
Content:
New brew
It's time to raise a toast to coffee all over again. UK's largest coffee chain and a leading global brand, Costa Coffee has formally inaugurated its first outlet in Chandigarh in Sector 35 B. Speaking at the launch, Paul Robinson, Country Head, Costa Coffee India remarked, "Costa's coffee experience has received a fantastic response across all cities of presence. We look forward to receiving a similar response from Chandigarh residents." Costa's Mocha Italia Coffee is prepared from the choicest beans in India under supervision from Costa Roastery in Lambeth, UK. Besides its authentic Italian Coffee, coffee based drinks and beverages, Costa offers a variety of complementing food to complete the experience. Costa Coffee is today UK's fastest growing retail brand as well as among the fastest growing F&B retail brands in the world. It currently has more than 1000 outlets in 18 countries and is growing at the rate of five stores a week worldwide. When it comes to the brand's expansion plans in the country, Anil Laroia, COO of Costa Coffee tells us, "We plan to add a couple of additional stores in Chandigarh, depending on availability of prime locations, this year. Costa Coffee is already present in surrounding cities like Ludhiana, Panchkula and Karnal. Across India we are targeting a total of 75-80 stores by the end of this financial year."

Kind gesture
MAKING the most of 'World Kindness Day', city-based radio station Big 92.7 FM got its radio jockeys - RJ Satya and RJ Shalini to go to the Kusht (leprosy) Ashram in Sector 47 on Thursday morning and distributed woollen clothes and blankets amongst the kids and patients. Satya and his friend played guitar for the kids. Both the RJs went to Jeevan Mukt Nishulk Vidyalaya at Jagatpura, Sector 48 where they distributed the woollens amongst the children sitting in the classrooms. The next stopover for the entourage was Missionaries of Charity in Sector 23 where they handed over the woollens and clothes to the sisters. To reach out to the poor and needy, the radio station launched 'Raahat Abhiyan' - an initiative aimed at providing clothes to the needy. The project received a very good response from the city residents with tonnes of clothes collected in mere 10 days.

That's IT!
NIIT through its largest education centre in North India, NIIT Zirakpur, carried out a special seminar on IT trends for Indian Air Force personnel at IAF High Grounds Station. Inaugurated by Station Commander Group Captain RKS Shera at Alankar Auditorium, presentations on various IT career courses were given by Managing Director MS Randhawa and Centre Head Shikha Khosla among others. "Today's employment scenario is all about strong skills, innovation and competition. IT professionals with specialized training are much in demand," said Khosla.

Heading: Police crackdown on farmers - Indian Express
Content:
Six employees of Mahindra and Mahindra were booked on charges of stealing two Scorpio cars from the company's stockyard in Daria village on October 3 this year.

The theft, however, came to light only later. While the hunt for the culprits is on, no arrests have been made yet.

The accused have been identified as Dharambir, who was working in the showroom for the past 12 years and his accomplices Dinesh, Rohit, Ricky, Vijay and one security guard. The case was registered on the complaint of Bhenny John, deputy manager of the showroom.

Police said that Dharambir was terminated from the job some time ago on account of being "unprofessional" as he used to give away the cars directly from the stockyard to the customers, while the routine process demanded that the cars be sent to the dealer's showroom first.

All the other accomplices named in the FIR are said to be close associates of Dharambir and were also employees of the showroom.

The accused allegedly prepared a forged gate pass, a fake invoice letter, sale letter and delivery note of the vehicles and managed to get it cleared from the staff.

"The execution of the fraud was carried out in the a very clever way. Since they were all employees, they were aware of the entire process and the loopholes of the showroom and thus planned it accordingly. In the papers, the vehicles were shown as sold, but later it was found that they were never sold and all documents that were produced turned out to be fake," said Chiranji Lal, the investigating officer in the case.

The police said that since Dharambir was a trusted employee and had been working for many years, he managed to con the showroom managers easily.

Heading: City defies market doom, Estate profit up by 42% - Indian Express
Content:
Over 20 held, many go underground ahead of statewide agitation today

Police initiated a massive crackdown and arrested over 20 farmer leaders in Tarn Taran, forcing many to go underground ahead of statewide agitation starting tomorrow against the ruling SAD-BJP government in the state and the UPA at the Centre.

At least seven farmers' bodies have joined hands to block rail and road traffic on Friday in protest against the non-announcement of Rs 250 bonus on paddy, shortage of fertilisers and rising prices.

Satnam Singh Pannu, head of the Kisan Sangharsh Committee (KSC) that would lead the protest, said their prominent leaders, including Kulwinder Singh Dadehar, Beera Singh, Lakhwinder Singh Khairdeen and Amrik Singh Jandoke, were picked up from their homes by the Tarn Taran police and more such reports were pouring in from other neighbouring districts. "We are shocked that the police have started arresting the farmers to thwart our protest. We have asked other leaders to hide tonight," said Pannu.

The Indian Express found out that similar "precautionary measures" have been taken by the cops in Amritsar (Rural), Gurdaspur and Batala police districts also. "If the government thinks it will be able to spread fear among farmers, it is mistaken because our resolve will be further strengthened," said Sawinder Singh Chautala, a farmer.

He feared that more leaders might be arrested tonight.

Meanwhile, Principal Secretary to CM Darbara Singh has called a meeting of farmers' associations in Chandigarh. "This government is indulging in double-speak. On the one hand, they have called the meeting in Chandigarh for talks and on the other police jeeps are making rounds in the rural areas to pick up our leaders. What does the government want to convey?" asked Pannu, adding that a group of their representatives would go for the meeting, but their agitation would not be called off, as they know nothing would come out of the meet.

Apart from the KSC, various factions of Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU), including Ekta, Sidhpur and Krantikari, Kirti Kisan Union, Punjab Kisan Union and Jamhoori Kisan Union, have jointly given the call for protest.

Farmers are agitated over the silence of the government on paddy bonus. "Besides, the shortage of fertilisers is hitting the farmers hard, as sowing of wheat is hampered all over the state. We are also demanding linking of the procurement price with price index," said Pannu, who has also gone underground.

Farmers said the prices of fertilisers, insecticides, pesticides and diesel have increased manifold, leading to hoarding. "We want the government to check hoarding and fix MSP of sugarcane at Rs 200 per quintal, cotton at Rs 2,000 and wheat at Rs 1,800. The loans of poor farmers should be waived," he said.

Heading: Amritsar has new plans for solid waste - Indian Express
Content:
Despite a hurting financial crunch triggered by the global meltdown, the Chandigarh Estate Office has earned Rs 93.5 crore as revenue through registry of residential properties for the year April 1, 2007-March 31, 2008.

At Rs 311.5 crore, the revenue rose by 42 per cent as compared to the previous year, 2006-07, when the Chandigarh Sub-Registrar's Office registered Rs 218 crore as profit. The rise in revenue has been registered in the year that faced worse market conditions and continuous crash in the stock market.

Even the number of residential properties registered an increased by around 1,000 within this period. In 2006-07, the total number of residential properties registered with the Sub-Registrar's Office was 5,066 through various deeds like sale, transfer, gift and mortgage. In 2007-08, the number rose to 6,019.

"The year 2006 brought forward Chandigarh as a sought-after real estate destination that resulted in the entry of almost all major developers from across the country. Everybody wanted to earn a quick buck and as much as possible, through real estate. Within a year, the boom started to subside when speculators left the market after earning their share of profit," says Manoj Kashyap, Regional Director, JLL Meghraj.

The picture, however, is entirely different barely 20 kilometres from the city. While numerous private developers, both national and local, were trying to grab the share of profits earned through properties, they are now hardly able to sell 50 per cent of their units.

Standing by the figures and data of the Sub-Registrar's office, local property consultants believe that Chandigarh can never lose its charm in attracting home-seekers. "The movement in residential properties in the city has not been affected by current recession. A prospective home buyer's first preference is the city despite the exorbitant property prices," says Mangat Rai Baboota, a real estate consultant.

Heading: Gurpurb celebrated with fervour in region - Indian Express
Content:
Municipal Corporation signs MoU with Mumbai-based company for project

Amritsar's ambitious solid waste management programme, a brainchild of BJP Lok Sabha MP Navjot Singh Sidhu, which had been hanging fire for almost a year, is likely to see the light of the day soon. Amritsar Municipal Corporation has signed an agreement with a Mumbai-based company for the project.

With the implementation of this project, Amritsar will be the first district in Punjab, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir to have such a system for solid waste management.

About a month ago, the Municipal Corporation signed the agreement with Mumbai-based Antony Solid Waste Management Company. The project is likely to begin from the first week of December. The project was announced by Sidhu last year, and was expected to be implemented from January 2008. Sources say it got delayed due to the nonchalance of the authorities concerned.

A team led by Sidhu had also visited Hyderabad in connection with the project. Municipal Commissioner DPS Kharbanda said that with this project, the process of solid waste collection and management would be mechanized. "The company will operate on a build-operate-transfer (BOT) system," he said.

The system, he revealed, will include door-to-door collection of garbage through special bins and mechanized carriages. The processing and disposal of solid waste would be covered in another phase.

Kharbanda said that there is a proposal to manufacture electricity, manure, fuel and construction material from the waste.

He asserted that the company will invest in the project, and MC will not spend anything on it. The fuel that is generated will be used to generate power for the city. "This will help the city become self-reliant in power generation to an extent," he said.

Kharbanda said no worker of the Municipal Corporation will be ousted because of the project. When contacted, Mayor Shawet Malik said the system will help in keeping the city clean and green.

The disposal of solid waste management is now emerging as a major issue all over the country. With rising population, large tracts of land are being used as garbage dumps for solid waste.

Heading: Growing popularity of better DTH services hits cable television hard - Indian Express
Content:
The 329th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev was celebrated with great enthusiasm in the holy city on Thursday.

According to sources, Gurpurb was celebrated with fervour also at Nanakana Sahib in Pakistan, the birthplace of Guru Nanak. Thousands of Sikhs from all over the world converged at the gurdwara there.

Back home, thousands of devotees took a holy dip in the sacred 'sarovar' of Harmandar Sahib today. Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and his wife Surinder Kaur Badal performed the sewa of cleaning the utensils and shoes. They also served food to the devotees at Harmandar Sahib, along with SGPC chief Avtar Singh Makkar.

Badal congratulated the devotees at the gurdwara, and urged everyone to follow the teachings of Guru Nanak.

Earlier, a 'Jaloo' (an exhibition of ancient Sikh jewellery) was held at Harmandir Sahib, Akal Takht and Gurdwara Baba Atal Sahib for three hours. The temple complex was tastefully decorated with colourful lights.

A religious 'diwan'(Congregation) was also organized at Gurdwara Manji Sahib, in which several raagis, dhadis and schoolchildren recited gurbani verses. Speakers threw light of the teachings of Guru Nanak. Fireworks were also arranged in the evening.

Langars were organized in several parts of the city. A parbhat pheri was taken out from Bhai Veer Singh Hall. It ended at the Golden Temple.

Heading: Punjab top brass back from trip down south, to woo IT biggies - Indian Express
Content:
Cable television is slowly losing popularity in face of direct to-home (DTH) services in the city. And while cable operators are making all attempts to get hold of the market, companies like Reliance and Tata are offering plans to rope in as many customers as possible.

Tata Sky, Big TV, Dish TV are some of the key players that have been able to establish themselves in spite of the monopoly of cable operators for the last many years.

"Of the total 2.7 million customer base that we have built up since Tata Sky was launched in August 2006, the regional market forms a sizeable chunk of the same. It is a very important market for us and keeping this in mind, one of our four customer care centres is in Mohali," says Vikram Mehra, chief marketing officer, Tata Sky.

A senior official of Dish TV says, "This region shares a major part of our 4.4 million customer base. People are now becoming more inclined towards DTH, which has led to an increase in the number of viewers."

Companies, meanwhile, give various reasons for an increase in the base of DTH services. "DTH gives high definition quality picture whereas the reception quality of cable is not up to the mark. A customer also gets to watch a variety of channels through DTH. In this way, he gets value for money," says Dr Rupesh K Singh, head, corporate communication, Reliance.

He adds: "DTH has received a tremendous response in the rural areas since it is mobile. It saves villagers the hassle of installing long cables."

Quick redressal of complaints, interactive applications and packages to suit every pocket are the other reasons for its popularity.

Regarding his experience with DTH, Kunal Sekhri, a customer, says: "It has been six months since I switched to DTH and I have not encountered any problem till yet. From sharp colour to a variety of channels, I can avail numerous services at an economic cost. Cable transmission is poor in quality, apart from frequent disruption of service that we had to face earlier."

Heading: High Court allows firm disqualified by Bathinda Improvement Trust to participate in auction - Indian Express
Content:
A Punjab government contingent comprising Industries Minister Manoranjan Kalia, Principal Secretary Industries SS Channi and MD Punjab Infotech Rakesh Verma has returned after their tour to Hyderabad and Bangalore.

The contingent visited several IT companies, met the industry captains there, and pitched for Punjab's suitability as an IT investment destination. According to the minister, the response to their proposals was positive.

"A lot of players have evinced interest in investing in Punjab. The state is a bit of a late starter in IT, but we hope to make up the lost ground very quickly," he claimed.

Kalia assured that the state's present inadequacy in three critical components for IT industry, viz infrastructure, power and human resources, is temporary. "I have been assured by the Chief Minister that we will be power surplus by 2015. We have guaranteed 24 hour uninterrupted power supply to any IT player who chooses to invest in the state," said Kalia.

The two senior officers expressed confidence in the state's young technocrats. Said Channi, "There are 30,000 youngsters graduating as engineers in Punjab every year. Given the right opportunities, they will like to stay in the region only. Also, adequate skill replenishment and upgradation programmes are being worked out by the government in association with consultants."

To hardsell its case as a future IT destination, Punjab has roped in the services of Ernst and Young, a consulting group.

Kalia's argument that if Andhra and Karnataka can convince industries to invest on barren patches of land, then Punjab certainly has an advantage, perhaps hints at the major glitch. Unsuitability of land in southern states ensured that land acquisition didn't run into the sort of problems which it encounters in arable states like Punjab. "Land won't be an issue. We already have earmarked land at Ropar and Kapurthala which are being proposed as IT/ITes special economic zones," said Manoranjan Kalia.

Heading: Govt using public money to malign Congress’ image, says Khaira - Indian Express
Content:
Company had accused the Trust of 'irregularities' in finalising bidders

Bathinda Improvement Trust has allegedly committed irregularities in finialising the goods carrier companies that could participate in the restricted auction of Goods Booking Agency sites, under the Trust's Transport Nagar scheme.

Delhi Punjab Goods Carrier (DPGC) Limited, whose name was not included in the final list of participants, had cried foul over the selection process, and filed a petition in Punjab and Haryana High Court. Following this, the court has issued directions that the company be allowed to take part in the auction scheduled on Friday. The court has also issued notice of motion to the Trust for November 17.

DPGC's name was removed from the list of participants, released by the Improvement Trust on November 4. The Trust had earlier included DPGC in its list, prepared in August. DPGC moved court after the release of the "final list", in which its name was not included. Thirteen applicants were selected by the Trust to participate in the auction.

Estate Officer of the Trust Gora Lal Jindal, when contacted, claimed that after the "detailed scrutiny" of the applications, it was found that DPGC had not provided complete information. "Hence their application was rejected," he claimed.

Gora Lal added that 27 more sites were to be auctioned, and DPGC could be considered if it fulfilled all formalities. However, DPGC spokesperson Pardeep Goyal called the move "a deep-rooted conspiracy".

"The record has been tampered with, to remove the name of our company. Gross irregularities have been committed by the Improvement Trust in the whole process," alleged Goyal.

He stressed that if the information given by them was incomplete, the Trust should have written to the company about it. Trust Administrator Kamal Kishore Yadav said that the matter had not been brought to his notice by the goods carrier company in question. "If they have any court order, we are bound to honour it," said Yadav.

Heading: Liquor vends in Sector-45A market irk residents - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee has objected to the use of public money to malign the image of Congress by way of "misleading" advertisements issued by the SAD-BJP government on a World Bank scheme.

Congress MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira said huge government-sponsored advertisements appearing in newspapers were a "bundle of lies". The advertisement issued by the Water Supply and Sanitation Department criticises the previous Congress government, saying, "The Congress left you in tears of despair, we replaced the tears with waters of hope."

"It was fine if the advertisements were issued by the SAD from party resources, but using people's money to gain political mileage shows the frustration of the Akali rule."

The advertisement highlights a World Bank scheme for rural water supply and sanitation project worth Rs 1,280 crore. Both the SAD and the Congress are now claiming the credit for it. "This project was sanctioned by the previous Congress government. Besides, the Central government, headed by Manmohan Singh, was instrumental in getting World Bank's help," he said. "The government's talk of reducing the contribution of the general category households is also deceptive," he said, demanding that the Election Commission of India takes cognisance of this "politically-motivated propaganda".

Heading: Kasauli church pastor suspects arson - Indian Express
Content:
With the presence of liquor vends outside the houses of four Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) employees in the Sector-45A market, there seems to be no end to the nuisance being faced by them everyday.

These liquor vends are opposite House Nos 503, 508 and 526 and one behind House No 490.

Sanjeev Goel, a resident says: "It is difficult to step out of the house in the evening. There is chaos on the road with a number of people sitting in their cars and drinking. This goes on till late in the night."

"Owners of these vends also cook non-vegetarian food in the open. Though rules clearly state that the tavern of the vend should have a separate kitchen, this is not being followed. Also, in the absence of toilets, people urinate in the open," says Rajiv Sharma, vice-president, CHB Residents' Welfare Association.

Manoj Kumar, another member of the association says: "It becomes difficult to let children go out and play. In fact, residents cannot even stand in the balcony of their houses. Traffic jams have become a common feature in the area."

A railing that had been put on the berm between the V5 road and the approach road in front of the market has been removed from most of the places or the stands have been broken. A notice near the railing, warning those damaging it, with a fine, is a witness of the mockery being made of the rules.
