In fact, the road berm itself is encroached with tea shops, juices corners and other such outlets. And with encroachment of the parking space by rickshaw pullers and scrap dealers, the problem is aggravated all the more.

Another resident, Arjun Singh, says: "There was a proposal to construct a boundary wall in front of the houses, but it has not materialised till now. Till then, we are trapped in our own houses."

Heading: Girl’s abduction: Villagers gherao Baddi police station, demands SHO’s transfer - Indian Express
Content:
Claims windows broken, kerosene odour detected

Suspecting foul play behind the fire incident that badly damaged the Baptist Church in Kasauli on Wednesday night, pastor of the church Ashok Masih today demanded a high-level probe into the incident.

The fire completely destroyed the antique furniture in the church, a model of the church installed on the main gate of the building and ceiling of the hall. The church is considered a unique example of colonial architecture of the British era.

The building of the Baptist church was constructed in 1923. The town had three churches, of which one was destroyed in a fire in 1857.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Ashok Masih said he suspected that some miscreants had thrown kerosene through windows of the main hall and set the church on fire. He said he had also informed the police about his suspicions. He claimed that initially it was

assumed that the fire broke out due to a short circuit, but officials of the electricity board, who had visited the church, had ruled that out.

After the fire was extinguished, the window panes of the church's hall were found broken and an odour of kerosene was detected.

Masih said despite the huge loss to the property and building, except the Kasauli Naib - Tehsildar, none of the senior officials had bothered to visit the damaged church building. Even Kasauli MLA Dr Rajeev Sehjal, who was in town on Wednesday, did not visit the church.

Meanwhile, Additional Superintendent of Police S.R. Rana said though the police have not received any formal complaint from the pastor, he had directed the Kasauli police to conduct a thorough investigation in the case.

Rana said he had also directed the investigating officers to lift samples from the spot which could help in ascertaining the actual cause of the fire. He said if arson was established during the investigation, strict action would be initiated as per the law.

Heading: The bitter pill: Diabetes hits home and hard too - Indian Express
Content:
Upset over the alleged failure of the police in not tracing a girl kidnapped by three local youth, hundreds of villagers, including leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party and opposition Congress, today staged a dharna and gheroed the police station at Baddi.

The girl, Reena Chaudhary, of nearby Haripur Sandoli village, was allegedly kidnapped by three youth of Nalagarh on October 31. After this, the girl's father, Madan Lal, had lodged a first information report with the Baddi police, stating that his daughter was kidnapped by Imtyaj, Rishabh and Naresh of Nalagarh town.

After this, the family members and villagers had been visiting the police station to enquire about the progress made by the police in the case. They had also taken up the issue with the Baddi SHO.

However, after the police failed to trace the girl after two weeks, a large number of villagers today staged a dharna outside the police station for over two hours. The slogan-shouting protesters were demanding immediate transfer of the SHO. The agitators lifted the dharna only after the SHO assured them that special teams had already been constituted to nab the culprits and trace the girl.

The protesters finally gave a two-day ultimatum to the police, warning that they would block traffic on National Highway-21-A if nothing was done. When contacted, Additional Superintendent of Police S.R. Rana said he had directed the investigating teams to trace the missing girl as soon as possible.

Heading: Shopping mall brings down Zirakpur building, no casualty - Indian Express
Content:
As the city marks the World Diabetes Day on Friday, here are some bitter truths. Diabetes, predominantly a lifestyle disease, continues to tighten its grip on the urban population and across all age groups.

A study of the profile of the elderly patients (above the age of 61 years) by GMCH in Sector 32 found that out of 273 patients registered with Geriatric OPD, the overall prevalence of diabetes was as high as 27.1% as compared to 12.1% in a study conducted in south India.

All the patients had Type II diabetes, found the study titled — Profile of Diabetes Mellitus in Elderly of Chandigarh, India — published in the Internet Journal of Endocrinology.

The study further revealed that obesity was prevalent in 22 diabetic patients (29.7%) and positive family history for diabetes was found in 17 patients (27%), much higher than the earlier studies available in the country which pegged the incidence at around 17%.

Interestingly, sedentary lifestyle was followed by 47.3% of the diabetics used in the study. Among these patients, 18 (24.3%) were diagnosed for diabetes after a routine check-up while 21 per cent were diagnosed accidentally.

"Only 31 (41.7%) were adhering to diet control while 9 (12.1%) continued to smoke and 10 (13.5%) boozed regularly despite knowing the consequences. Reasons for irregular treatment in 28 per cent cases were mainly the failure to understand the importance of adhering to the treatment, lack of family support and expensive medicine," noted the researchers.

"Lifestyle changes are required to avoid diseases like diabetes and patients need continuous motivation to undertake treatment and follow dietary restrictions. There is a need to have a holistic and multi-disciplinary approach for management of diabetes in the elderly," noted the study.

While the GMCH, through its study, established the growing incidence of diabetes, the Department of Community Medicine, PGI, too had published the rising figures of the disease in the city a couple of years ago and found that the disease has trickled down to the younger population.

More than six per cent of the city residents between 35 and 54 years and more than 10 per cent of population above 55 years of age were reported to be suffering from diabetes. Eleven per cent of the male population above the age of 55 years suffers from diabetes, followed by 13 per cent of women.

Dr J S Thakur of the Community Medicine said the department is engaged in conducting another study with the Department of Endocrinology at the PGI to find reason behind the rising number of patients in Chandigarh and their metabolic syndrome.

"Diabetes affects nearly 10-15 per cent of residents in the city and this is a very high number for any population," says Dr Thakur.

"Prosperity has led Indians to eat more while physical work is diminishing from the daily lives. This is the reason ailments like Type II diabetes are on the rise," added the doctor.

IF YOU ARE DIABETIC
* Have periodic blood and urine check-up
* Never stop medication even if you have fever, nausea, and/or even when you are fasting
* Make it a habit to have monthly weight check-up
* Wear shoes all the time. If you don't want to wear shoes indoors, wear slippers with hard soles for good support
* Maintain a healthy lifestyle and avoid eating junk food. Eat in moderation and follow a regular exercise regime

Heading: CFL bulb scheme to be launched from Nov 23 - Indian Express
Content:
A Major tragedy was averted when a double-storey commercial building collapsed while another was partially damaged, following the digging of a basement adjacent to these buildings for the construction of a shopping mall near the Dhakoli railway crossing on Panchkula-Zirakpur highway on Thursday afternoon.

Though no casualties were reported, a JCB machine, stationed at the digging site was damaged as the concrete structure fell on it. As per reports, the incident took place around 3.30 pm.

A shopping mall is coming up on 2,000 square yards and is situated adjacent to the two double-storey buildings. Since the damaged showroom was planned to be demolished to facilitate the mall, the developers claimed no monetary loss as the structure was supposed to be razed later.

These buildings hosted offices of Unicity builders, an architect and a local Patwari earlier. Project director Sushil Bindal claimed that no digging work was in progress during the time of the incident owing to Gurpurb celebrations.

He added that the building collapsed, following the vibrations of a passing train on the Ambala-Kalka track, which is situated close to the buildings.

Railway and local police officials also visited the spot later in the day. The police will, however, investigate all aspects of the case, SHO Ranjot Singh added.

Heading: Ex-dy speaker Dharampal passes away - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh is ready to begin distribution of free CFL bulbs to nearly 16.3 lakh domestic consumers under Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal's innovative energy saving scheme — Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana —conceived almost four months back.

On November 23, Dhumal is flying to Kullu, an energy-surplus district, to launch the scheme, which is expected to cost the Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board Rs 80 crore.

Two leading CFL manufacturers — M/s HPL-Socomec, which has secured the mainly supply order for providing 10 lakh packs (four bulbs each) of CFL bulbs —while the rest of the supplies will be made by M/s Phoenix, another major CFL manufacturer.

Himachal Pradesh expects to save at least 72 MW of power everyday on full implementation of the scheme.

R.K. Jain, HPSEB's chairman, has already appointed member (Administration) Nisha Singh and HPSEB secretary Dr M.P. Sood as nodal officers to oversee the distribution of bulbs to consumers. When contacted, HPSEB secretary Dr M.P. Sood confirmed, "The distribution of CFL bulbs will start on November 23."Currently, a team of HPSEB engineers are on the job to inspect the CFL bulbs to be supplied by the two companies.

Heading: I am confident about my performance: Deepinder Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
Former deputy speaker of state Vidhan Sabha Dharampal Thakur died of a massive cardiac arrest at Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC) on Thursday morning. He is survived by his wife, son and daughter. Born on October 27, 1949, in Tun-Badyar village of Arki constituency, Thakur started his political career in 1978. Thakur was first appointed president of Youth Congress of Arki in 1978. He was elected to the state Assembly from Arki in 1990 and represented the constituency till 2007. He was elected deputy speaker of the Vidhan Sabha in 2003 and remained on the post till October 2007. After denial of a party ticket, Thakur unsuccessfully contested the election from Arki in 2007. He was later expelled from the party for anti-party activities. A large number of BJP and Congress leaders attended his cremation.

Governor Prabha Rau and Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal have mourned Dharampal Thakur's sudden death.

Former Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh also expressed shock over the death of Dharampal Thakur. Virbhadra Singh said Thakur discharged his duties as legislator and Deputy Speaker with distinction and contributed not only in development of his constituency Arki, but the entire Solan district. President of HP Congress Committee Kaul Singh Thakur mourned the untimely death of Thakur. In his message, Kaul Singh said Thakur was a loyal leader who started his career from the panchayat level and pursued people' issues till the Assembly.

Heading: 402 cases of child labour in one year - Indian Express
Content:
Even though the election schedule is yet to be announced, local MP Deepinder Singh Hooda has kicked off his election campaign by opening an election office for the Youth Congress.

Talking to The Indian Express, in an exclusive interview, he said, "I am a sitting MP and I am confident to contest from Rohtak. I will go to the people and ask about the development works undertaken during the last four years.''

He said when the screening committee distributes the ticket, under the guidance of the party High Command, it will consider the individual performance and I am confident about my performance and service provided to the people of Rohtak.

"Wheels of development were jammed during the previous regime. It is now showing results'', he added.

As a part of the election campaign, he addressed eight public meeting besides attending tea parties at the house of influential dignitaries.

Though frequent visit of Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda to Rohtak anger his critics, but supporters of Deepinder are confident that it will help in ensuring his victory.

In a bid to make Rohtak an educational hub, four education institutions will be set up, namely Polytechnic College for Women, ITI, National Institute of Fashion and National Institute of Designing.

Heading: INLD-BJP alliance hopes to sweep Lok Sabha polls - Indian Express
Content:
A campaign carried out by the state government has revealed there have been 402 cases of child labour in the last one year, said N C Wadhwa, Special Secretary, Labour.

Talking to The Indian Express, on the eve of the Children's Day, Wadhwa said out of the total cases detected, 318 were a result of direct raids on the offenders, while 84 cases had

been detected during routine checks.

The offenders are being prosecuted and have been fined Rs 20,000 each. As it is a serious offence, the offenders can even land in jail, said Wadhwa. The state government had launched a special campaign on November 14, 2007, for keeping a check throughout the year. A similar campaign would be launched again tomorrow, said Wadhwa. "The idea is to eliminate all forms of child labour in the state,'' he added.

"Letters have been despatched to DCs of all the districts of the state to launch the campaign, through their supervision teams, with the help of labour officers and department staff. Four raiding parties have been prepared for the purpose. We will put up posters and banners at prominent public places, warning people against employing children in factories, dhabas and as domestic help, said Wadhwa. He said three children rehabilitation centres would be inaugurated tomorrow at Yamunanagar, Panipat and Faridabad by S K Gulati, Financial Commissioner and Principal Secretary, Labour, Employment and ESI. "The state government has earmarked Rs 43.50 lakh for the expenditure of each rehabilitation centre for a year.

Each rehabilitation centre will have a provision for 50 children. They will be allowed to stay at the centre till they reach the age of 14,'' said Wadhwa.

The children at the rehabilitation centres would be given food, lodging, clothes and training in vocational skills. "We are starting three centres tomorrow, but rehabilitation facilities in three more districts will also be started.

Under the National Child Labour Project, special schools are being run at Gurgaon, Faridabad and Panipat where day care centres provide special facilities to poor children including mid-day meals and education under Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan,'' he said. The government also runs "bhatta shalas" or special schools for children of brick kiln workers in Jhajjar, Panipat and Kurukshetra, he added.

Heading: Run for ‘tiranga’ - Indian Express
Content:
The recent NDA rally at Sonepat may have failed to live up to their expectations, leaders of Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) are still enthusiastic about the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections.

After the initial hiccups, the BJP leaders, except MLA Ram Kumar Gautam, are in favour of the alliance and expect good results in the next polls."The tie-up will help both the INLD and the BJP. Together we can win all the seats in the LS polls," said Sampat Singh, senior INLD leader and former finance minister of Haryana.In the 2004 Lok Sabha and 2005 state assembly elections, the two parties had separated and faired very poorly.

Out of the 10 Lok Sabha seats from the state, the BJP managed to win just one seat from Sonepat, while the INLD drew a blank. In the state assembly elections of 2005, the INLD's strength was reduced to 9 from 47 in the previous poll.

Similarly the BJP's strength too was reduced from six seats in the previous term to just two in 2005. The Congress, on the other hand, managed to increase its strength from 21 to 67 seats. Together the INLD and the BJP polled 39 per cent votes and had there been an alliance between the

two, they could have faired better.

INLD-BJP alliance had won all ten seats during the 1999 LS polls, where they had contested five seats each.This time the BJP has been demanding six seats, giving four to the INLD. But the INLD would like to have it the other way round.

The Congress, though is not affected by the alliance. "It is an mutual pact of opportunism and the Congress will sweep the polls like the last time,'' said Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda.Phool Chand Mullana, president of Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee, said the Congress party has a strong footing and the INLD-BJP pact will not have any effect on the electorate. "

Heading: Four of Mohali family die in road accident - Indian Express
Content:
A state-level "tiranga run" will be organised on November 16 at the Dronacharya stadium, Kurukshetra to mark the week long celebrations of the birth anniversaries of Jawahar Lal Nehru and Indira Gandhi.

The run is being organised by MP Naveen Jindal, who had won the legal right to hoist the national flag on private premises.

In a statement issued here today, Jindal said he is trying to create a sense of responsibility and awareness about the national flag.

His efforts started on October 22 when a tiranga march was organised at Kurukshetra. Similar marches were held at Kaithal and Yamunanagar.

Jindal said every segment of the society, rich or poor, professionals, businessmen, traders, and others, should contribute to the progress of the nation by following ideals of the national flag.

He said he was inspired by Rahul Gandhi during the Hyderabad annual summit of the Congress when he said "My tiranga, my religion". A door-to-door campaign is being carried out for the run.

Heading: Mahant taken to Mumbai, cops claim he knew Sadhvi, Lt Col - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after Indian Navy warship INS Tabar rescued two merchant vessels from pirates off the Somalia coast, New Delhi said on Thursday that a UN peacekeeping force is needed to prevent piracy attacks in international waters.

Raising the issue at a meeting of the International Maritime Organisation in London, India said that a peacekeeping force under a unified command is needed to prevent attacks in the Gulf of Aden, the Arabian Sea and off the coast of Somalia. The Indian delegation, led by Secretary (Shipping) A P V N Sharma, said that urgent steps are required to provide security to international shipping in the pirate-infested region considering that "12 per cent of the world's sea-borne oil trade, about 50 per cent of the world's sea-borne dry bulk transportation and 33 per cent of the world's container trade" passes through the vital sea lane.

At the conference, the Indian delegation said that a joint effort is needed to curb such incidents at sea. Sharma said that the "disjointed efforts" currently being made by several countries — Russia, NATO and EU warships are already patrolling the region — is leading to some naval forces "giving assistance to only ships of a particular flag, or to those having seamen of a particular nationality".

It may be recalled that the Indian Navy has already requested the Government for greater autonomy to curb piracy in the region and give it the authority to liaison with friendly navies operating in the Gulf of Aden.

Heading: State, Centre lock horns over the fate of JE vaccine - Indian Express
Content:
Mahant Amritanand alias Dayanand Pandey, arrested from Kanpur on Wednesday by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad which is probing the Malegaon blast case, was flown to Mumbai on Thursday after a Lucknow judicial magistrate accepted the ATS request for transit remand.

UP ATS officials, who were present when Pandey was questioned by the Maharashtra policemen, claimed he admitted he knew Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur and Lt Col Shrikant Purohit — both are under arrest for their alleged roles in the case — but denied he had anything to do with the blast. He said he came into contact with them while he was in Pune some years ago, an official said, adding that Pandey did not spell out exactly when he met them. The official claimed that Pandey also dropped names of some religious leaders-turned politicians who he said visited him at a temple in Faridabad near Delhi and in Jammu.

According to the official, Pandey said he had cleared the National Defence Academy entrance exam in 1987 and was an Air Force aspirant. He did not finish training and returned home. While in Varanasi, he came in contact with some gurus and moved to Jammu where he later became head of the Sharda Sarvagya Peeth.

Heading: Stamp duty takes a hit as recession sets in - Indian Express
Content:
Two months have already passed and the state government is yet to decide the fate of 4.6 lakh doses of Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine.

The state government discontinued the vaccine on the grounds that the stock supplied by the Centre was low on efficiency due to heat exposure.

According to experts, it is advisable to use the vaccine within three months after it undergoes stage three of heat exposure, as further delay would completely render it ineffective.

While the chances of the entire stock becoming unfit for use have increased with time, the fate of this huge stock of vaccine is still undecided owing to lack of communication between the Centre and the state government.

On the part of the Centre, Dr S D Khaparde, Deputy Commissioner, Infectious Disease and Immunisation, said: "We have asked the state government officials to return the supply, which we might use for routine immunisation drive. But they have not yet sent the stock."

As far as the supply of the fresh stocks is concerned, to which the Centre had agreed earlier, he said: "We can decide on this issue only after assessing the current position of our stock and the requirement for other states in the near future."

On the other hand, the officials of the state government said that they have still not received any such communique from the Centre about returning the supply. As per the current information received, it is the Centre, which is supposed to take back the supply.

"We are waiting for the Centre to take the supply back and send us the fresh stock, as promised," said a senior officer involved with the immunisation activity in the state. Around 400 children, meanwhile, have died in eastern Uttar Pradesh due to encephalitis.

JE vaccination of around 10 lakh children in 11 high-risk districts of the state is still pending due to the shortage of vaccines.

"We can act only when the Centre sends us the fresh stock of vaccine. Without the vaccine, we cannot undertake the JE vaccination under the routine immunisation," said Dr V S Nigam, Assistant Director, Communicable Disease wing of the state government.

Heading: Now, Lok Sabha candidates to campaign with flags, posters - Indian Express
Content:
For the first half of fiscal year 2008-2009, exchequer shows a shortfall of Rs 280 crore

The recession is showing its effect on the real estate market — thereby hitting the state's revenue collection from stamps and registration.

There is sharp decline in overall registration of properties — particularly in western Uttar Pradesh, the revenue bowl of the state.

Apart from the lucrative border areas of Delhi- Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida, places like Moradabad, Rampur and Bijnor have also taken a hit. So have the districts under Agra division — Glass City Ferozabad and Hatharas — now known as Mahamaya Nagar.

By the end of September 2008, the revenue collection should have been 50 per cent of the target. But against the target of Rs 5,770 crore for the current fiscal 2008-09, the actual collection in the first six months is little over Rs 2,600 crore — a shortfall of nearly Rs 280 crore.

"Even after the 37 per cent reduction in stamp duty, there is no corresponding increase in registration of properties. This is certainly due to the recession and its impact on the real estate market," said Desh Deepak Verma, principal secretary, Stamps and Registration.

Earlier, the stamp duty in the state was Rs 8 on every Rs 1000. From April 1, it has been reduced to Rs 5 per Rs 1000.

"Besides first-time registration, there is a clear decline in the resale of the residential and commercial properties, which has affected the revenue," said Verma.

He, however, added that owing to red tape and corruption, urban development authorities — including Ghaziabad Development Authority, Noida, and Greater Noida — have also failed to give possession of plots to allottees despite receiving payment.

In a bid to cut red tape and streamline the process of registration, the state government has mooted a proposal for the web-based registration of properties.

According to the plan, this is to implemented through a public-private-partnership model. The project is estimated to cost Rs 100 crore, which will be met by the private investor who will be selected through competitive bidding.

Heading: New syllabi for High School, Intermediate examinations - Indian Express
Content:
Home owners are not going to be happy about this.

But with the Election Commission (EC) going easy on billboards and wall writings, the upcoming Lok Sabha polls may revert to its colourful past.

According to the new guidelines by the EC, political parties and candidates can put up temporary and easily removable advertisement materials like flags and banners in private premises with the voluntary permission of the occupant.

"This way, flags, banners and posters of political parties will be visible in every constituency during the Lok Sabha elections," a source in the office of the UP chief electoral officer said.

According to sources in the state election office, the EC has decided to suppress its earlier instructions after hearing the plea of several political parties in this connection.

At the same time, the EC has introduced a new feature — educational institutions, including their grounds, shall not be used for political campaigns and rallies.

It has also made it clear that no wall writing, pasting of posters or papers, erecting or displaying cutouts, hoardings, banners, flags, etc shall be permitted on any government premises. Such premises will include any government office and its campus, the guidelines added. "No party or any candidate will use public property for putting up advertisement materials," a source said.

When it comes to private premises, the political parties and the candidates will have to inform the concerned returning officers that they have put up flags and banners.

According to an EC guideline, the parties will have to obtain prior written permission from the owner of the property and submit photocopies of the same within three days to the returning officer.

The EC has also issued a pro forma for submitting the permission that the candidate obtains from the house owner. In the prescribed pro forma, the contesting candidate will have to disclose the expenditure incurred or likely to be incurred on hoarding, banner, posters etc. Besides, details like size of the hoardings, banners and posters will also have to be mentioned.

The permission of the house owner should be an act of free will and not extracted by any pressure or threat. Such banners or flags should not create any nuisance to others, the guidelines stated.

Moreover, the expenditure incurred through this shall be added to the election expenditure of the candidate. But the expenditure incurred on exclusive campaign for a party, without indicating any candidate, shall not be added to the candidates' expenditure.

Regarding the defacement of hall or auditorium and other public properties, the EC guideline stated: "In case of halls, auditoriums, meeting venues owned or controlled by the government, local authorities, PSUs, co-operatives — if laws or guidelines governing their use do not prelude political meetings, there is no objection to it."

The guidelines also added that it has to be ensured that the allocation was done on an equitable basis and there was no monopolisation by any party or candidate.

In such venues, displaying banners, buntings, flags and cut-outs may be permitted during meetings subject to any restrictions under the laws or guidelines in force.

Such banners or flags shall be removed by the party or individuals who will use the premises immediately after the meeting, the guidelines stated.

Heading: Kanpur ODI: BCCI officials inspect Green Park Stadium - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Secondary Education Board has decided to introduce comprehensive changes in the syllabi for High School and Intermediate courses to avoid putting extra strain on its resources.

"We have decided to drop a number of subjects which only a few students opt for.

Setting up of question papers for these subjects and their evaluation was putting a strain on our resources," Secretary of UP Board Prabha Tripathi said.

"Subjects like German, Tibetan, French, Russian, Latin and Chinese languages besides defence affairs, have been dropped from the list of optional subjects for the High School examinations," she said.

"Similarly, German, Tibetan, Russian, French, Latin and Chinese languages in addition to statistics, religious art and elements of mechanical engineering and electrical engineering have been removed from the list of subjects for Intermediate examinations," she added.

Worried over the poor performance of examinees for long, the UP Board was particularly rattled this year when nearly 60 per cent of its students failed in the High School exams while nearly one-third of those appearing for Intermediate exams passed. To arrest the passing percentage, the board has introduced some changes in question papers too. Tripathi said that question papers for some subjects have been restructured, both for High School and Intermediate examinations.

"The changes in question papers have been introduced following complaints that candidates were finding the 100-marks question

paper too lengthy and were unable to solve them in the time allotted to them," Tripathi said.

"In the High School examinations, Sanskirt and Urdu used to have one question paper each of 100 marks. Now, both subjects will have two question papers of 50 marks each," she said.

Heading: Malegaon blast: mahant warns govt against more arrests - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the recent retirement of Anil Kumble and Sourav Ganguly as part and parcel of the game, Rajiv Shukla, Chairman of Finance Committee, BCCI, claimed several young prospects have emerged in the country in the last few years.

During inspection of the Green Park Stadium on Thursday, he said: "We will definitely miss the experience of Anil Kumble and Sourav Ganguly, but we have promising youngsters in Piyush Chawla, Pragyan Ojha, Amit Mishra and Vikrat Kohli."

Shukla, also the Secretary of the UP Cricket Association (UPCA), said the country is fortunate to have a bunch of talented players who can replace seniors after their retirement. He said: "It is up to the player to decide the right time of his retirement, therefore we do not interfere in the issue."

Justifying the payment of Rs 1 crore by UPCA for the forthcoming India-England one day match, Shukla asserted the thrust is on holding a good match and providing better facilities to spectators. He praised the chief minister, district administration and the sports department for their help in holding the match.

Shukla said the UPCA is yet to take a final stand on the issue of construction of its own stadium. "The state government has offered a few sites in Lucknow, but we are yet to finalise the site," he added. Kunwar Fateh Bahadur, Principal Secretary, Home, also inspected the preparations at the stadium on Thursday.

Heading: Centre sends team to survey malnutrition deaths in UP - Indian Express
Content:
Anticipating more arrests in the future by Mumbai Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) in connection to the Malegaon blast, Faizabad-based Mahant Gyan Das said the move to touch any sadhu or members belonging to the akharas will have violent repercussions both for the state and the Central government.

The chief of the 13 akharas spread across the country, Das warned that the army of nagas will come onto the streets if the police entered the muths and arrested any member.

Reacting to the arrest of two sadhus in connection with the blast case, Das said: "I don't know Sadhavi Pragya Thakur or Swami Amritanand. They are self-styled sadhus. But any move to touch my members will land the government in deep trouble."

He added: "We are the real sadhus, as we have relinquished worldly pleasures and materialism in the real sense. We don't play politics in the name of religion like these self-styled sadhus."

Heading: Welcome! - Indian Express
Content:
With malnutrition cases from eastern Uttar Pradesh on the rise, the Centre has instituted a special team to make surprise visits to the marked districts — Varanasi, Ghazipur, Sonebhadra and Chandauli.

All this to ensure that all malnourished children in the marked districts receive the supplementary food provided under the Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS). The team will check the reports on malnutrition deaths and also the status of the supplementary food being used by the entire family.

Dr Amita Jain, member of the special team and also

A-Z Programme, which provides technical assistance to ICDS, said: "Although the ICDS aims at being the single biggest scheme to cater to malnutrition, it is a proven fact that 65 per cent of children below 6 years in rural UP are still malnourished."

"There have been regular reports of malnutrition deaths from eastern UP, specially districts like Varanasi, Pratapgarh and Sonebhadra. The team will check the facts behind the deaths, survey the ICDS centres in these areas and check the availability of supplements for children," said Jain. The team will present its report to the Centre by January.

Heading: Baby’s Day Out - Indian Express
Content:
If there's a getaway waiting with open wings for guests of all kinds...it's the Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary

After about a decade, Nawabganj Bird sanctuary is again abuzz with activities. The arrival of hundreds of winged guests is giving a busy look to the sanctuary, lying neglected for the past many years due to official apathy.

Courtesy efforts of Unnao district administration and the forest conservator Eva Sharma, the Kulli Van lake is full of water inviting birds from across the shores. With winter arriving, species of Cotton Teal, Pintail, Open-billed Stork and Sarus (crane) can already be seen rowing and spreading hues in the area, especially during morning and evening.

Experts says so far some species have arrived from Siberia and Central Asia and hopefully around 100-odd varieties that used to flock the park till few years ago, would be seen again. Known for major wildlife attractions, the small sanctuary spreads in an area of 3 sq km and comprises an area around a shallow lake which forms a perfect spot for migratory and water birds for a long stay.

Located about 45 km from the State capital on Lucknow-Kanpur national highway, sanctuary is the home to a large range of birds, both resident and migratory. While migratory birds residing here include Greylag Goose, Pintail, Common teal, Cotton teal, Red Crested pochard, Brahmini duck, Gadwall, Shoveller, Wigeon, Coot and Mallard etc, resident and locally migratory birds comprises of Spotwill, Sarus crane, Painted Stork, White Ibis, Black Ibis, Dabchick, Whisling teal, Open billed stork, White necked stork, Black necked stork, Spoon bill, Pheasant tailed jacana, Broze winged Jacana, Purple moorrhen, White breasted Water hen, Indian Moorhen, Grebe, Cormorant Darter, Lapwing, Egret, Purple heron, Pond heron, Stone curlew, King fisher, Night jar, Tern Vulture, Kite, Partridge, Hawk Wagle, Koel, Dove, Pigeon, King Crow, Baya, Muniya, Golden Oriole, Barbet, Babler, Indian Roller, Bee-Eater, Parakeet, Drongo, Hoopoe, Finch, Peacock, Brain fever bird, Comb Duck, etc.

The sanctuary is also known to be the habitat of fishes like Katla, Mangur, Saul, Sindhi, Kavai and reptiles like Cobra, Viper, Krait, Ratsnake and Water Snake.

Unfortunately, the Deer Park, which used to be a major attraction for tourists, is lying empty. This small park, comprising the deer, was established in the vicinity of the sanctuary and was famous for Spotted Deer and Barking Deer. Another past attraction of the sanctuary, peacocks, too are conspicuous by their absence.

As part of conservation of lake and its surroundings, Government of Uttar Pradesh declared the area as a sanctuary in 1984.

The picturesque sanctuary, which was developed subsequently, became famous as an ideal place for photographers and picnic lovers.

To enhance the knowledge of visitors regarding birds, an Interpretation Centre was also established in the sanctuary.

There is also the provision of film shows related to wildlife. Presently, the centre is also being renovated and upgraded with modern facilities, says Eva Sharma.

"Also, the sanctuary is being beautified and given a chic look so that tourists could feel at home here," says Rajshekhar, District Magistrate Unnao.

He terms the sanctuary as the pride of the region.

Interestingly, with the sanctuary in shape again, restaurant and rest houses run by Tourism department are also ready to greet guests.

Heading: Nanavati Report Part-II may not meet Dec 31 deadline - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
I'm currently listening to Anup Jalota's latest album of sacred chants on Lord Krishna.

What's your DVD pick?
An animated film called Barbie.

Heading: Modi-maligning SMSes: VHP leaders refuse to part with handsets - Indian Express
Content:
Thicker than the first part, it covers role played by Modi and other leaders in the post-Godhra riots

At the fag end of the 12th extension of its original term, the Nanavati-Mehta Commission is most likely to miss its December 31 deadline for submitting the second part of its probe. This part relates to the post-Godhra riots that left hundreds dead.

The Commission had submitted the first part of its report on September 18 and had held that the burning of the Sabarmati Express train was a 'pre-planned act' and part of a 'conspiracy'.

Commission chairperson Justice G T Nanavati told Newsline on Thursday that it will be difficult for the Commission to release the second part of the report before December 31.

"The work is going on, but it may take one or two more months before the report is ready,'' he said."

He, however, refused to discuss anything more about the report.

According to the Commission's terms of reference, the much-awaited second part is to deal with, among other things, the role played by Chief Minister Narendra Modi, other leaders, political and social organisations during the riots.

This vital term of reference for the Commission was added on July 20, 2004 under heavy pressure from civil rights groups.

The Commission had come in for a lot of flak after the first part of the report gave a clean chit to Modi and his ministers in the post-Godhra riots even as the second part dealing with the issue was yet to be tabled.

The first part had concluded that there was no evidence to show "any lapse in providing protection relief and rehabilitation to the victims of the communal riots and in the matter of not complying with the recommendations and direction given by the NHRC," on part of the chief minister, his council of ministers or police officers.

Sources in the Commission say that the sheer enormity of the paperwork involved and huge number of riot-related depositions have made it very difficult for the Commission to complete the work before the December 31 deadline.

"The second part of the report is going to be more voluminous than the first part. It deals with incidents and cases spread across Gujarat while the first part was only about the Godhra incident. Also, a sizeable number of the 40,000 affidavits filed before the Commission deal with the riot-related compensation claims,'' the sources added.

Those in the know of things say that the second part of the report is more important than the first part as it deals directly with the question of the 'role and conduct' of the political establishment of the time, including Chief Minister Narendra Modi and organisations like the Bajrang Dal and the Vishwa Hindu Parishad .

Heading: Baroda Dairy row takes ‘saffron’ scalp - Indian Express
Content:
Go baby
Purav Bhandare sure is on a roll. The eight-year-old actor, who started his career in the public eye at just four, is in talks with UK film director Steve Barron for a role in his yet-untitled film. Barron, who's best known for his cult comedy, 1993's Coneheads, was looking for a young face and Santosh Sivan, who'd worked with young Purav in Tahaan, recommended him. The young actor has already auditioned for the role and is now just awaiting the final call for formalities.

International calling card
Cat-eyed beauty Celina Jaitley does not believe in resting on her laurels. After the amazing response her latest Bollywood venture, Golmaal Returns, got at the box office, Celina is now set to woo the international audience with her first international film Love Has No Language. She was recently spotted at the movie's premiere in Auckland, New Zealand, along with her Australian co-star, Ben Mitchell and New Zealand rugby star Monty Beetham. The Kiwi rugger was apparently quite taken with Celina's beauty and the lovely lass herself was floored by all the warmth and attention she received.

Shining star
Divya Dutta's prospects in films have never been better. She started out on the idiot box, and graduated to small but significant roles in movies like Veer-Zaara and has now finally landed herself the lead role in Zee Limelight's first presentation Oh My God!! She's acting with Vinay Pathak, Saurabh Shukla, and Harsh Chhaya in the movie, which is about a simple man, who with god's help, comes to term with his big dreams and his journey thereafter. Divya even appeared as a celebrity judge on Sony Television's hit comedy show Comedy Circus - Kaante ki Takkar to promote her movie which will release on December 5 this year.

Heading: Realty check: Meltdown has no impact on Muslim ghettos - Indian Express
Content:
MLA Madhu Srivastava resigns from BJP after being slapped Rs 17 lakh recovery notice

BJP Legislator from Waghodia, Madhu Srivastava, on Thursday evening, resigned from the party and the post of the Baroda Dairy chairman.

This comes a day after the registrar of the Gujarat state cooperatives, P Sompura, issued notices to Srivastava, the vice-chairman, managing directors and 19 office bearers of the dairy for the recovery of Rs 17 lakh as surplus payment on the sale of milk packaging.

It was during the audit that Sompura discovered that around Rs 17 lakh was to be paid to the contractors. Along with Srivastava, three other officials, Rangesh Patel, Chandravadan Patel and Kirti Singh, holding key posts in the Baroda Dairy, have resigned.

Srivastava told Newsline: "I tendered my resignation to state BJP president Purushottam Rupala at 6 pm on Thursday after I received a notice from the Gujarat state cooperative. I don't want my party to bear the expenses."

Rupala also confirmed that Srivastava's resignation has reached his office. "We cannot comment on anything as of now, but it is true that we have received his resignation," he said.

Srivastava, the three-time sitting BJP legislator from Waghodia, climbed up the political career thanks to his 'Robin Hood' image. Originally from Uttar Pradesh, Srivastava started in Vadodara as a small time offender, in the bootlegging industry, before graduating to the Assembly elections after debuting as an Independent in the civic polls.

His latest brush with controversy was getting caught in a sting operation. It is believed that the BJP used his strong-arm tactics to force and bribe Zaheera Sheikh and her family to turn hostile during the Best Bakery case trial in the Vadodara fast-track court.

Heading: Plans afoot to improve Tuna catch - Indian Express
Content:
Dream house still a distant dream in these areas due to high demand

It's a tough time for many Muslims in the state, herded into the ghettos on one side and done in on the other side by the space crunch fuelling the spiralling land prices. This is while the global meltdown and the correction in real estate prices are actually driving prices down elsewhere.

Land prices in the Muslim-dominated ghettos of Guajrat have been steadily increasing. Limited availability of land in specific areas, very few schemes adhering to clearances (NA/NOC) and high demand are said to be the reasons behind the price rise.

The residential land price in the Navrangpura area of Ahmedabad, which has a small Muslim population, has gone up from Rs 9,000 per square yard (sq yd) to Rs 15,000 per sq yd, while commercial property rates have gone up from Rs 12,000 sq yd to Rs 35,000 sq yd in the last two years. The ghettos have seen a jump of over 80 per cent in the last three years.

Instances galore

Last year, Ismail K Sheikh, a 35 year-old businessman, postponed the purchase of a 2BHK flat in Elecon Towers near Vishala Circle (Juhapura) of Ahmedabad thinking prices were inflated and it would come down in coming years. The price of this medium-sized (115 sq yd) flat was around Rs 6 lakh then. Today, the same flat costs something between Rs 14 lakh and Rs16 lakh.

"I have lost all hope of owning a house in the Muslim populated areas here. The prices have gone beyond reach," said Sheikh, adding, "Forget about the lower middle class, the prices are now out of reach of even the middle class families."

The 'high demand and low supply' has made the prices move northward in Ahmedabad's Muslim dominated areas like Juhapura, Jamalpur, Khanpur, Kalupur, Danilimbda, and Bapunagar. Similarly, the land prices are on the rise in the Tandalja area of Vadodara.

Contrary to this, land and flat prices in non-Muslims

areas have either stabilised or gone down by over 15 per cent, according to experts. They predict the prices in Muslim ghettos will continue to grow by nearly 30 per cent every year.

"The prices are rising because the development in these areas is vertical rather than horizontal," said Shekhar Patel, president, Gujarat Institute of Housing and Estate Developers (GIHED). "It is sad that the city is divided into small pockets like these," he added.

After the 2002 riots, security has become the priority for the Muslim buyers. "For the last several years, minorities have very little option to live in Ahmedabad. There is a scarcity of land, therefore the prices will keep going up," said JV Momin, a builder in the walled-city area of Ahmedabad.

In fact, Muslim ghettos are attracting investments in the real estate sector from non-Muslim builders, who share their profits with the local builders.

"Many non-Muslim builders are investing money in the Muslim-dominated areas as the return is much more and assured due to a higher demand," said Nizam Khan, a builder in Vadodara.

A small ghetto called Muslim Society at Navrangpura in Ahmedabad is turning out to be a gold mine for the Muslim real estate developers. Mohammed Husain, who recently finished construction of Munshi Villa in the area, said "A lot of educated and informed are coming forward to buy houses. People now want construction that adheres to all the building bylaws. Very few such schemes are available and that is why prices are going up."

In the non-Muslim areas, prices of residential and commercial properties might further go down. "As far as commercial properties are concerned, over 60 per cent has already been bought by the investors expecting more than 9 per cent returns during a period of three to nine years," said Kiran Gandhi of LJ Hooker (Ahmedabad), an Australian real estate major.

"There is a possibility of distress sell in the commercial properties. But for now, everyone is sticking to the wait and watch policy," he added.

However, GIHED's Patel believes that due to the industrial development between Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar, the prices may not go down drastically.

Heading: Now, Nano to brave political onslaught in Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
Marine Products Export Development Authority to help develop special design boats, which are expected to increase revenue of fishermen by 90 per cent

Plans are afoot to revive Gujarat's fishing industry by changing the design of over 10,000 fishing boats having trawling nets. The new design will help fishermen easily catch Tuna fish, one of the most popular export varieties.

The renovation project supported by the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) will serve two purposes: It is expected to shoot up the revenue of state fishermen by a whopping 90 per cent due to the improved quality and quantity. The hydraulic system will also address the environmental issues, including allowing young fish to grow and reproduce, and help protect other resources getting caught in the nets.

In this regard, the MPEDA announced a

50 per cent subsidy in its first meeting with the Gujarat Boat Association members in Porbandar. On the first day, over 20 members came forward for boat renovation.

"A hook-line system costs nearly Rs 10 lakh. The MPEDA is providing a subsidy of

Rs 5 lakh per boat," said Jignesh Visavadia, NPEDA co-ordinator, Gujarat. "If not all, the MPEDA aims to convert at least half of the boats into Tuna specific," he added. The project will be implemented in phases.

A team of experts brought by the MPEDA from Australia shared their experience with Saurashtra boat owners and fishermen in this regard on Thursday. In the new system, trawling nets will be replaced by hook-line, winch monofilament, hydraulic pump and refrigerator water can. There are over 10,000 boats that venture into sea from the Saurashtra coast.

Although the boat owners will have to spend over Rs 5 lakh from their own pocket, they may not mind it, as the new system promises to increase the revenue by many folds. "Not only it guarantees the best quality Tuna fish, but it will also cut down the fuel consumption by 50 per cent. Unlike trawlers that should be moving all the time, boats with hydraulic system can be stationed when catch is available," said Jivan Jungi, president of the Boat Association.

According to boat owners, the fuel consumption in boats with hook-line is expected to go down by 1,000 litres as against the 2,000 litres in trawlers. Further, the increase in catch of Tuna fish means increase in export orders. "Tuna is the most popular fish across the world. At present, Gujarat fishermen are not very lucky to find Tuna fish in significant quantity," Jungi added.

For the MPEDA, it will also ensure that other marine resources, including young fish that get caught in net, get protected. "The hook-line system will ensure selective fishing of adult fish only," said Visavadia.

Heading: Under ATS scanner, Ashimananda fails to turn up for nine-day Ram Katha event - Indian Express
Content:
Abhishek Bachchan has established himself as an actor, but he's still papa's boy

He's dressed in a floral pink and white shirt but sports a short crop and kohl-lined eyes these days. Abhishek Bachchan is clearly in that stage of metamorphosis — from Sameer in Dostana, to his character in Mani Ratnam's Raavan — where a look in the mirror doesn't leave one flattered. But he's got his attitude in place, and that's probably what matters.

Confident about Dostana, which releases today, he clarifies that neither is the film anywhere close to the 1984 namesake nor is the gay plot between him and John Abraham the mainstay in the story. "Such subplots naturally get more attention, making our jobs even more difficult," he sighs.

The film is a comic caper about two friends pretending to be gay while apartment-hunting in Miami. But things go haywire when both fall in love with Neha (Priyanka Chopra).

"Dostana's the funniest film I've ever seen," claims Bachchan. "We had a preview and my family loved it." What adds to it, he says, is the fun he had during the shoot. The 32-year-old laughs as he recollects shooting the ballroom dance sequence with Abraham. "Every time there were such sequences, we'd go over the top with jokes." But Bachchan gives his co-star credit for making him dance since he's a trained ballroom dancer. The two have shared camaraderie since Dhoom days. "John even taught me how to workout," smiles the actor, referring to his new lean look that he now sports at 84 kilos.

As opposed to Bachchan's otherwise simple dressing, stylist Aki Narula has experimented with his look in Dostana. "I just loved sporting the cargos, loose jeans, summer scarves, pastels and prints that Aki had me wear for the film—they just added to the Miami mood," he says.

The film, though directed by debutant Tarun Mansukhani, clearly bears that Karan Johar touch (Mansukhani has assisted Johar since Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, he even played a cameo in the film). But Bachchan is quick to point out that the sense of humour is distinctly Mansukhani's: "Tarun's worked with Karan for over 10 years but the small twists and the edge in the script totally belongs to Tarun. And that's where he stands out."

He may sport a grim public image but what can ensure a smile on his face is the mere mention of his dad, Amitabh Bachchan. "He's doing fine now. Yes, his illness was a trying time for the entire family but he's not just a strong guy, he's Superman."

Bachchan's come into his own as an actor over the last couple of years but he is yet to learn to accept criticism gracefully, it seems. The actor went into a tizzy when informed by the media relations that the press was unhappy with his interviews. "Did I give you a boring interview?" he asks. When we say yes, he turns boisterous, jumping on to the sofa in the lobby like a two-year-old.

Let's not even get into what couch-stomping did to Tom Cruise.

Heading: Cops, foresters rescue stranded pilgrims in Girnar - Indian Express
Content:
Swami Ashimananda Maharaj, who is under the scanner of the Mumbai Anti-Terror Squad in connection with the Malegaon blast, did not turn up at a nine-day Ram Katha event he was supposed to inaugurate at Tapi on Thursday.

As Newsline reported, Ashimananda, who remained incommunicado after the police put cast a veil of suspicion over him for his alleged involvement in the blast, was supposed to inaugurate the event in the presence of the leaders of the RSS, VHP and the BJP.

Invitation cards in this regard had been distributed widely, and the organisers had claimed that he was contacted through some sources and had assured them that he would come as the chief guest.

The local BJP Parliamentarian, MLA and other senior leaders whose names were mentioned in the invitation, also chose to stay away. They instead opted to attend a function organised in the neighbouring Mahuwa taluka where state Home Minister Amit Shahwas the the chief guest.

Even Subhash Padvi, BJP president of Tapi district, remained absent at the function. "I had to go to Amit Shah's programme. I will attend the Ram Katha event on Friday with my supporters. I have given my explanations to the organisers," he said.

The organisers of the event, which logged an unexpectedly sparse devotee turnout, however, maintained that they are still trying to get Ashimananda for the event.

"He is a well-known figure among the local tribals. His absence has affected the programme. We have come to know that he is busy with some work in south India. He has switched off his mobile phone. We are trying to locate him," said Narsinh Chaudhury, president of the Ram Katha Ayojak Samithi.

Heading: Police on hot pursuit of punters - Indian Express
Content:
A Group of seven people, including two women and two children, who had gone missing in the dense forest in Girnar region on Wednesday night, were rescued after a three-hour long operation at night.

The group had gone to the sanctuary from Derwan village for Parikrama and lost their way inside.

Nirbhay Thaker, a resident of Jetpur city, who was a part of the group, said: "My friends and I reached Zinabawa Madhi around 5.30 pm. Half an hour later, we found ourselves completed isolated and trapped in the forest. Within minutes, we were enveloped in complete darkness."

He added: "We heard the roars of lions from a very close distance. The women and the children started crying, but we could do nothing. We were helpless. It was so dark that we could hardly see even our fingers from a close distance. We witnessed death from a very close distance."

He said fortunately his cellphone was still catching the network and he immediately contacted the 108 Emergency Service. Around 10.15 pm, the police and foresters located them in the forest and rescued them.

Lalji Bhai Bhatt, Junagadh police control room, in-charge, said: "As soon as we received a message from the 108 Emergency Service about these missing people, we passed on the message to the Junagadh superintendent of police and the concerned forest officers."

"Considering the seriousness of the matter, a team of forest and police officers immediately rushed to the Girnar North Range forest area and three hours later, rescued them safely," he added.

Heading: Who’s to be blamed for rise in asbestos-related deaths? - Indian Express
Content:
All known bookies to be in preventive custody before Rajkot ODI

The Police in Rajkot have initiated a special drive to curb instances of illegal betting during the India-England One Day International (ODI) on November 14.

Betting has been in practice in Saurashtra, including Rajkot, for a long time. It takes place in Rajkot during ODIs, but this time since the match itself is being played in Rajkot, the local police are taking special precautions to curb betting.

Rajkot Police Commissioner Sudhir Sinha told Newsline that they are keeping tabs on every bookie earlier arrested in betting cases.

All the known bookies will be taken under preventive custody to restrict betting activities, he said.

He added: "This time, we have put our officers at various mobile operator companies' offices and all mobile service providers have been ordered to keep a watch on all phone connections which has witnessed over 10 to 20 times rise in incoming or outgoing calls. Our officers will check the location of the particular suspected mobile number and inform our ground staff who will then investigate it further. We will also take printouts of the call record as documentary evidence."

On being asked about the need for this advance monitoring, he said: "After the increased usage of mobile phone in the betting business, the bookies have started operating from outside the city limits, which is out of the local police station's jurisdictions."

He further said that from the mobile phone network, they can easily map out the location of the bookies. "We are finding out ways to curb criminal activities with the help of an advance technology," he said.

These apart, the police have also deployed personnel in plainclothes to keep strict watch for any suspicious activity. Generally, bookies put up their people in the ground to know the latest updates of the match.

Heading: Woman found dead under mysterious circumstances - Indian Express
Content:
Official denies use of asbestos in power companies even as the latter admit to using it for boiler and turbine insulation

It has been a life of agony, pain and compromise for Hemalata, daughter of Kishan Goplani, an ex-worker of the erstwhile Ahmedabad Electricity Corporation (now Torrent Power), who died a slow and painful death in 1996 because of asbestosis.

Although Hemalata received Rs 1.5 lakh in an out-of-court settlement in 2008, this is among a few lucky instances in the battle against the asbestos related diseases (ARDs).

Such is the state of apathy and indifference by the government that V N Patel, director Industrial Health, Hygiene and Safety, Ahmedabad denied any knowledge of asbestosis cases in the region.

He was ignorant of the report submitted by the National Institute of Occupational Hazards (NIOH) in 2005, with findings of suspected asbestosis among Torrent workers.

He also had no information about a 2007 diagnosis camp organised by Dr V Murlidhar, founder member of the Occupational Health and Safety Centre, Mumbai, which identified eight cases of asbestosis — five in torrent workers, one spouse of a worker and two Digvijay Cement workers.

To top it all, Patel even denied that power companies are using asbestos in boiler and turbine insulation.

"Now, only glass wool is being used for insulation," he said.

This is when Torrent Power officials themselves admitted to the prevalent use of asbestos. Torrent Power said it would look into the IBAS dossier and would reply to all its findings soon.

Moving to the cement manufacturing sector, the Ban Asbestos Network of India did a survey of about 600 workers of Digvijay Cement in 2008, of whom, 103 showed symptoms of asbestosis.

Even in 2003, Kalyaneshwari, a voluntary organisation, had medically examined 93 former workers of the company, of which 24 were found suffering from ARDs.

Kalyaneshwari later filed a Public Interest Litigation in the Supreme Court in this connection and the judgement is awaited.

P A Nair, Chief Executive Officer, Digvijay Cement, could not be contacted despite several attempts.

Even the credibility of NIOH has come into question, with the cases like the one in November 2007 when it failed to confirm its original diagnosis of 2005 when Torrent Power workers were found to have symptoms of ARDs.

The second diagnosis was done on the insistence of Torrent for an out-of-court settlement with workers.

Overall, the situation is so precarious that the IBAS has termed the 'shameless betrayal of civil society by the political-industrial establishment' as a 'crime against humanity'.

Heading: Friday Bazaar: vintage bike lovers fear closure - Indian Express
Content:
A 20-year-old married woman was found murdered under mysterious circumstances at her house in Vastral village on the outskirts of Ahmedabad on Wednesday evening .

The Ramol police have registered a case of murder against unidentified persons and further investigations are on. The police, however, suspect some inside hand in the crime.

The deceased was identified as Meena Chaurasiya, a resident of Krushna Kunj Society near Karicut Canal in Vastral. Her husband Ghanshyam, who runs a small

furniture manufacturing unit, has lodged a complaint with the police.

The police said the incident occurred between 4 pm and 6 pm when the victim was alone at her house.

The deceased's sister-in-law Kalavati Chaurasiya had come from her native place for some treatment, and the incident occurred after Kalavati left the house around 4 pm. When she came back, she saw Meena lying unconscious on the floor in the drawing room.

She immediately informed Ghanshyam, who was then at the factory. He rushed home and informed the police about the same.

The police said the woman was strangulated with a thick rope. Inspector S R Gohil said: "The motive behind the murder is unknown. But some inside hand seems evident since the killers had a friendly entry into the house. Apart from that, we have also recovered two glasses filled with water from the room in which the incident occurred. The victim had also put a pot on the gas stove to prepare tea for the two unidentified persons."

Gohil said some neighbours told them that they had seen two persons entering the house around 4.30 pm. "It is quite evident that the murderers were known to the deceased and so we are investigating the case in that direction also," he said.

The couple were married one-and-a-half-year ago and did not have any child.

Heading: VUDA puts brake on freight corridor, says land reserved for urban development plan - Indian Express
Content:
After the artists, antique collectors and historians, it is now the owners and collectors of vintage bikes who feel that the closure of the Shukarvaari Bazaar will destroy an important part of Vadodara's history.

On the brink of closure, the Shukarvaari Bazaar weaves the tale on the pursuit of vintage bikes lovers, who have lifted nuggets from the rubbles and brought fifty-year-old single cylinder motorcycles 'on the roads' – right from the rare automobile parts imported from the UK and the US – which are cherished by all bike freaks and mechanics in the city.

The leisure pursuit for Rajgopalan Gowda, the former director of M S University (MSU) was to mend models of bikes, some as old as 60 years. "I had five bikes, four twin cylinders and one single cylinder," said Gowda.

According to Gowda's friends, bringing bike accessories from the Shukarvaari Bazaar was his favourite past time. After giving finishing touches to his Nortons, Gowda wheeled it through the entire campus, they said.

Along with his mechanic, Ganesh Maroo, Gowda used to go to the Machhi Bazaar, a part of the Shukarvaari Bazaar, sharp at 7. 30 in the morning for the spares. "I got every thing, right from the head light to the tail lights and even magnetos that allow the passage of current to the spark plug," said Gowda, a sexagenarian, who now teaches at Sumandeep Vidyalaya.

While Gowda seems to have lost the hobby, and has sold all his bikes to people in Pune and Bangalore, Maroo is afraid of the times ahead after the flea market shuts down.

At Fatehpura, Maroo has a garage which appears to be gathering dust, but houses models of vintages bikes such as 500 cc BSA, Triumph, 250 cc Triumph, 330 cc Ariel and Lambretta scooters.

According to Maroo, everything from unique levers, carburettors, meters, switches and hand switches was available in the market.

"In my 20-year career as a mechanic, I had developed an eye and a rapport with the Waghri community at the Bazaar. If my vintage bike needed a spark-plug, it was available in the trashes in the heaps of junk sold by the Waghri community. The closure of the Shukarvaari Bazaar will mean that the key to start my vintage bike is lost," he said.

Heading: Modi opens railway manufacturing site at Savli - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Ministry and the Vadodara Urban Development Authority (VUDA) seem to be passing the buck on the issue of the alignment of the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) on the 640 metres of land reserved by the latter in around 31 villages of the district.

Minister of State for Railways Naran Rathwa has said that there is no clarity from VUDA on the land. Top officials at VUDA on the other hand, assert that the land, which is already acquired by VUDA under the year 2031 development plan, cannot be given to DFC since it is reserved under a Central government project.

It was during a recently held meeting between Rathwa and representatives of 31 villages whose land will be acquired for the DFC that the Minister came clear on the issue. He said the Railways is facing an ambiguity on the issue of the 640 metres of land already reserved by VUDA.

"Issues such as uniformity in stamp duty for industrial, commercial and residential zone in the villages, where the DFC is expected to come up, are still not clear. Moreover, the farmers' representatives have contended why the DFC is not being built on the 640 metres stretch that is already occupied by VUDA," said Rathwa. He told Newsline that he has already convened a meeting in this regard with the Revenue Department, Divisional Railways Manager, VUDA and the DFC, on Friday.

Responding to the query made on the allotment of the 640 metres of land and the DFC railway line, Rathwa said VUDA is not coming clear as to which piece of land has been reserved and why it is not being allotted for the same.

Interestingly, while villagers have opposed the DFC alleging its non-compliance, VUDA officials have said that they have no problem in giving a No Objection Cerificate (NoC) to it.

VUDA Deputy Collector Y L Dave said: "It is the Revenue Department, which is responsible in providing the land acquisition to the DFC. We just have to give an NoC. There were some papers, which were forwarded by the DFC on the NoC issue; as of now, there are no problems."

Heading: Star Ruby case: SOG nabs absconder - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday inaugurated a new state-of-the-art railway vehicle manufacturing facility of the Canadian company, Bombardier, at Savli in Vadodara.

Even after having been in India for the last 35 years, Savli will be the first manufacturing unit of the aerospace and railway transportation manufacturer in the country.

Modi also made no delays in giving Bombardier the needed 1.40 lakh square feet land at Savli. The Savli manufacturing site, built in a record 18 months is ready to manufacture the first lot of railway coaches.

In its first production, the company will roll out MOVIA railway vehicles for the Delhi Metro by March 2009.

The new production site, representing an investment of 33 million euros, will directly generate 750 new jobs dedicated to railway vehicle production. Around 2,000 people are expected to get indirect employment.

Earlier, Bombardier had its propulsion and control centre and software development centre in Vadodara.

Laurent Beaudoin, the chairman of Bombardier Inc. said, "The Indian rail industry has witnessed great changes and expansion, and with this new manufacturing site, the cost of production will go down heavily."

Narendra Modi also showed keen interest in future prospects to enter the global market.

"It was only in September last year that the talks on the manufacturing site had started and I got

the land sanctioned in 40 days. Now, the company aims to bring out their first railway coach by March. Things are certainly going fast," said Modi.

He added: "Although the Railways is with the central government, we in Gujarat are keen on developing surface transportation. We have the ship-breaking yard at Alang but want to have more such yards. The aim is to emerge as a manufacturing hub and enter the global market."

Modi, also discussed his elaborate plans of expanding modes of public transportation in the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model to decrease the amount of traffic on the road. "There is no point in focusing on flyovers; instead we should work on multi mode transportation and multi storeyed railway stations," he said.

He said the state government has also taken up the Waterway Transport Grid seriously and has started preparing a detailed project, for which the Narmada Canals will be utilised.

"This mode of transportation will be a much cheaper option. Plans are in progress to develop the project by getting water from the Daman Ganga river through gravity and then connect it to Sabarmati," he said.

Heading: 45-year-old woman killed, five injured in Shah-e-Alam cave-in - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara police on Thursday arrested the key accused in the Star Ruby case in which three people were killed in a robbery attempt.

The case was solved long ago, but Bhala Pandor, a key accused, absconded soon after. Pandor was the person who had actually worked as a contract killer and had hired four others to carry out the heist.

According to a press note issued by the city police, Pandor was nabbed from near the Jodhpur village of Sehra taluka in the Panchmahals district on Thursday.

"We were tipped off about Pandor's whereabouts by informers. He was changing names and locations since the last two years, and we finally nabbed him from the State Transport bus depot in Jodhpur. We will produce him before the court on Friday and seek his remand. The case has been solved, but we will still learn about the missing links," said Special Operations Group (SOG) Sub-Inspector H M Alsika.

It was Pandor who had taken money from kingpin Jayanti Pateliya to kill Mihir Thakkar, Darshan Thakkar and Balkrushna Patel, who were carrying the ruby.

The ruby was owned by one Sameer Jagot of Vadodara and was being taken to Jaipur for evaluation, when Pandor and his four accomplices killed the three and buried their bodies.

While the police arrested Pateliya, Pandor gave the slip and was reported absconding ever since. Interestingly, the actual price of the ruby remained undecided, as no agency could ascertain it.

Heading: Hillary eyed as US Secretary of State - Indian Express
Content:
After Khosla ka Ghosla, Dibakar Banerjee hopes to hit the jackpot again with Oye Lucky Lucky Oye

Dibakar Banerjee does not like comparisons to Hrishikesh Mukherjee. "He had his style of filmmaking and I have mine," he defends, "the only point of similarity is that we both made films about ordinary people."

Banerjee's directorial debut, Khosla ka Ghosla about a middle-class family caught in a land scam, hit bull's-eye with the multiplex going audience. Expectations are now riding high on his next film, Oye Lucky Lucky Oye. But the pressure rests easy on Banerjee's shoulders even as he excitedly talks about his new film. "It's about a thief who's very special," he says, "unlike other thieves, who never want anyone to find out anything about them, this guy wants everyone to know he's the one who committed the crime. He has a talent for stealing and he's very proud of his 'craft'. If you haven't figured out it's him, he'll call you and tell you that he did it!"

It's obvious that Banerjee is attracted to stories that are a little out of the ordinary. And, he says, that tendency also affected the choice of his movie's leading man, Abhay Deol. "Abhay likes to look at the unusual side of things. He doesn't believe in doing what everyone else does. In that sense, we're very alike," he explains, "Moreover he's a very intense actor. That doesn't usually come out since he plays it cool, but he's one of the most focused actors I've met. This intensity of his will take him a long way," he predicts.

Banerjee is, in fact, very upbeat about all the actors in his movie. "We've deliberately not repeated any of the cast members from Khosla. We wanted to work with old and established actors like Paresh Rawal and also some new faces. In fact, there are 10 new actors in this film, five of whom have never acted before."

The music in his films, says Banerjee, also plays a very important role in the narration. "In most Indian movies, music plays a very important role in drawing the audience to the theatres and in providing breaks throughout the narration," he says, "I'm not entirely comfortable with that idea. So instead, even the songs are pushed into the background and become an integral part of the storytelling." The soundtrack of Khosla was a huge hit for the freshness of its sound and Banerjee has made sure that this time too, the audience has something new to listen to. "We've recruited a young talent called Sneha Khandwala. She actually went backpacking in Haryana and Punjab and brought back the old, forgotten melodies and poetry from those regions. You'll hear a lot of folk music on this soundtrack; we've even got folk singers singing here."

Heading: Obama top aide apologises to Arabs - Indian Express
Content:
Sen Hillary Rodham Clinton is among the candidates that President-elect Barack Obama is considering for secretary of state, according to two Democratic officials in close contact with the Obama transition team.

Clinton, the former first lady who pushed Obama hard for the Democratic presidential nomination, was rumored to be a contender for the job last week, but the talk died down as party activists questioned whether she was best-suited to be the nation's top diplomat in an Obama administration.

The talk resumed in Washington and elsewhere Thursday, a day after Obama named several former aides to President Bill Clinton to help run his transition effort.

The two Democratic officials who spoke Thursday did so on the condition of anonymity to avoid angering Obama and his staff. Clinton spokesman Philippe Reines referred questions to the Obama transition team, which said it had no comment.

Other people frequently mentioned for the State Department job are Sen. Chuck Hagel, R-Neb., Sen. John Kerry, D-Mass., and New Mexico's Democratic governor, Bill Richardson.

Heading: Indian diplomats meet US officials ahead of G20 - Indian Express
Content:
President-elect Barack Obama's White House chief of staff apologized to the Arab-American community on Thursday for remarks his Israeli-born father made to an Israeli newspaper.

Last week, Benjamin Emanuel talked about his son Rahm Emanuel's new job and told the Israeli daily Ma'ariv that "obviously he'll influence the president to be pro-Israel. Why wouldn't he? What is he, an Arab? He's not going to be mopping floors at the White House."

That prompted an outcry from the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee, which called on Rahm Emanuel, who is Jewish, to condemn the "unacceptable smear." On Thursday, Rahm Emanuel called the group's president, Mary Rose Oakar, to apologize on behalf of his family.

"These are not the values upon which I was raised or those of my family," the group quoted him as saying.

Oakar said the apology was accepted.

Emanuel spokesman Nick Papas confirmed the phone call and said Emanuel "offered to meet with representatives of the Arab-American community at an appropriate time in the future."

Heading: Designer Anand Jon guilty of rapes, sex assaults - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of the summit of the Group of Twenty (G-20) leaders in Washington on the current global financial and economic crisis, top Indian officials met with their counterparts in the Bush administration and key players in the incoming administration of President-elect Barack Obama.

Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission Montek Singh Ahluwalia, 'sherpa' of Indian delegation for the G-20 Summit, accompanied by the Indian Ambassador to US Ronen Sen had a bilateral meeting with his US counterpart Dan Price, President Special Assistant for Economic Affairs.

"The discussions focused on the issues before the summit," a news release from India Embassy said. Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ashok Chawla participated in a separate meeting of finance deputies involved in preparing the summit outcome.

Ahluwalia accompanied by the Indian Ambassador also had a meeting with former Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Congressman Jim Leach, who have been nominated by Obama to meet with delegations at the G-20 summit on his behalf.

"There was an exchange of views on issues related to the current international economic and financial crisis, the summit, and also bilateral relations. Secretary Albright, inter-alia, conveyed that the President-elect attached high priority to further strengthening of relations between India and the US " the statement said.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh along with Finance Minister P Chidambaram will attend a two day meeting here called by the US President George W Bush.
