Aravind Adiga's The White Tiger brings out the harsh truths of rural Indian life, where, given political corruption, crime is the only way out. It is a devastating comment on 60 years of our so-called democratic rule.

— P.V. Maiya

Bangalore

Roots of evil

• Indian society is characterised by millions of young people with a pervading sense of social injustice and distrust. Illiteracy and scant opportunities have choked desirable and just means of fulfilling aspirations. Consequently, they engender protests, violence and even terror attacks, all of which provide immediate release from the long state of deprivation and marginalisation. Support for education and employment is required if our "demographic dividend" is to be exploited.

— Ashwani Sharma

Ghaziabad

 

Dead fruits

• t is tragic that Margaret Alva could not see the writing on the wall. She was wrong in arguing that a ticket should have been given to her son, not because of merit but because he was her son.

However, her allegations are serious, and no matter what the Congress does about them, the stink has been raised by a very senior member of the party. Why is it that Rahul Gandhi can criticise the party with impunity but nobody else can? It seems nobody else will because they all wait their turns. The one whose influence had waned protested and was immediately punished.

Perhaps Alva will now find time to regret her decades of loyalty which have failed to pay off.

— C.N.N. Nair

Mumbai

Let them talk

• It is good that Barack Obama and Manmohan Singh have begun talking. Our top priority should be the universal one of terrorism. The next step should be the initiation of an Obama-Zardari dialogue, given Pakistan's strategic importance for both the US and the Taliban. Above all, for India and Pakistan there's Kashmir. The two should find a solution to the dispute, with Obama's encouragement, but certainly without his mediation. All problems, in order to be solved, must be acknowledged first.

— Parimal Y. Mehta

Mumbai

Music divine

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi has regaled audiences with the extraordinary range and emotional flexibility that he brought to his singing. For six decades, Joshi has inhabited the world of Hindustani classical music like a continent. The Bharat Ratna to him is most welcome and has been long-awaited.

— Yugal Kishore Sharma

Faridabad

Heading: Once completed, probe into judge’s conduct in public domain: CIC - Indian Express
Content:
On a day when the BJP announced its second list of 43 candidates for the Rajasthan Assembly elections, party MP from Bharatpur and an advisor to Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje, Vishwendra Singh, quit the party, alleging the role of "money power" in selection of candidates.

"I have been an active member of the BJP and a political advisor to Raje. I have seen things from very close quarters. I am dismayed over the sale of tickets for the Rajasthan Assembly elections and have decided to leave the party," the BJP leader said.

The allegations come days after similar charges were levelled against the Congress by its general secretary Margaret Alva, who alleged that the party sold tickets for the Karnataka Assembly elections.

"I feel I should not continue as an MP of the BJP," said Vishwendra Singh, adding that he had sent his resignation to the Lok Sabha Speaker.

Party general secretary in-charge of Rajasthan, Gopinath Munde, however, made light of the charge. "He was demanding too much from the party. We tried to do what we could but there is a limit to things," he said. Singh said he would contest the Dig-Kumher seat in the coming Assembly polls. He could be offered a Congress ticket or support from the party.

In the second BJP list, meanwhile, young leaders got as many as 20 tickets. Party ally, the JD(U), too, has been offered four seats. The BJP has already announced 94 candidates in the first list for the 200-member House.

Heading: Banning Deshdrohi not a solution, says Mumbai Cong chief - Indian Express
Content:
An inquiry into the conduct of a judge, once completed, is open for public inspection. The ruling has come from the Central Information Commission (CIC), the apex transparency body in the country. In his ruling, Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah has said judges are "public persons" who can hardly afford to keep an inquiry/investigation against them an "internal matter" as if in a "private employer/employee relationship".

"No matter who the person is, whether a judge or an official of the court, once an investigation on allegations of corruption is finished, the results should be out in the open," said Habibullah.

The November 10 verdict is in direct contrast to the Delhi High Court stand that "inquiry and investigation against an officer is an internal matter between the employer and the employee and disclosure thereof is not in public domain".

Pratap Singh Gandas, a resident of the Capital, had filed an appeal with the CIC against a Delhi High Court reply on February 26, 2007, in which he was denied the certified copy of an order by the Registrar Vigilance (Delhi High Court) given in 2004 to initiate a probe against "an officer of judicial services".

Gandas was refused access to the name and details of the Inspector who carried out the probe and final investigation report submitted in the High Court.

"As an institution, the Delhi High Court is anxious to promote transparency but cannot countenance attempts to browbeat the court. These attempts cannot be construed as being in public interest, and so is against the interest of the State and therefore worthy of exemption (from disclosure)," Rajeev Bansal, nominated counsel for the Delhi High Court, submitted before the CIC.

Bansal argued that "allegations of misconduct involving elements of vigilance against officers of judicial service are routinely received from various sources/quarters in the High Court." He said the complaints are examined under the "guidance of the honourable judges".

"This is a subject which is not only sensitive in nature, in as much as it involves independence of the judiciary, as indeed public image and reputation of the judicial officers concerned," Bansal submitted before the CIC.

The CIC dismissed the plea, saying "information with regard to public activity, which is an investigation, ordered by an institution as august as the High Court cannot be construed to be private activity".

Habibullah directed the Delhi High Court to release all information sought for within 10 days except those which may harm the confidentiality between investigators and witnesses in the probe.

Heading: Arrests, atrocities keep Lalgarh village on the boil - Indian Express
Content:
Opposing the state government's decision to impose a two-month ban on the controversial movie Deshdrohi, Mumbai Congress president and North Indian leader Kripashanker Singh said that the film must be shown after deleting the objectionable portions. "We will not support the ban. (However) The objectionable scenes in the movie should be removed (and the film cleared for exhibition)," said Singh while talking to reporters.

The Mumbai Regional Congress Committee (MRCC) president added that incidents shown in the movie, which drew flak from the MNS over its portrayal of locals, would eventually lead to a worsening of the situation in the city. Singh, who represents Santacruz in the Assembly, said that the state Government should debate the ban.

"Any film or play must give good advice," said Singh, adding that he had seen the promos of the film which showed a bus driver and conductor targeting the protagonist just because he was a north Indian. "This is wrong," said Singh, adding that such incidents had not happened with north Indians in Mumbai. He said that showing such things was "objectionable" as it would eventually affect the social fabric of the city and increase the differences within communities and was akin to "pouring ghee into the fire."

Singh said that since the movie would be shown in other states and could always find its way into Maharashtra via piracy, the only solution was to release the film after deleting the objectionable scenes.

"We are not satisfied," said Singh, while replying to questions on the role of the state police in handling the anti-outsider agitation launched by the MNS. He, however, hastened to clarify that he was critical of the state police and not the Government and also called upon Raj Thackeray to disassociate himself from "goondas" within the MNS.

Heading: Govt to rescue as ignored Aiyar goes crying to Cabinet - Indian Express
Content:
Even as blockades in Jhargram were lifted on Thursday, the agitators in Lalgarh have refused to give in. Tribals in a village in the area allege their women had been manhandled by the police after the blast in nearby Salboni on November 2, targeting the Chief Minister's convoy.

The police "excesses" and "mistakes" have triggered a rebellion a tribal agitation, isolating four blocks of West Midnapore district. For the past seven days, the tribals have been digging up roads, felling trees and damaging bridges.

The police had raided a village, Chotopelia, which is at least 60 km away from the blast spot, three days after the incident on November 5 and arrested people whom they later let off admitting that the arrests were based on incorrect information. This village is now the epicentre of the agitation. The villagers claimed that 10 women were injured during the police action.

One of the residents, Chitamoni Murmu (45), has virtually lost her eyesight. She was hit with the butt of a rifle. "We were asleep when the police broke open the door and dragged out my husband. I was hit by a policeman," she said.

The police conducted a door-to-door search for one Shamshed Alam, who was a suspected Maoist involved in the blast. Alam, a labour contractor and resident of Ram Jibonpur, frequently comes to the village to recruit labourers. For the locals, he is someone who provides them livelihood. When the police were taking away Alam, villagers resisted. Six women were allegedly assaulted by the police.

Sidhu Soren, one of the tribal leaders, said innocent tribals were being labeled as Maoists. "The arrests should have been made only after gathering evidence. The police should not have raided the village in the dead of the night," he said.

Apart from the labour contractor, the police had also picked up three students and a retired schoolteacher, all of whom are tribals. The police now admit that all these arrests were based on "incorrect" information.

District Magistrate N S Nigam admitted police excesses. "But I fail to understand why the agitation has continued when all the arrested persons, including the students, have been released," he said.

On the other hand, the villagers claimed that this wasn't the first incident of police atrocity. "Ever since the Jharkhand Party won a large number of panchayat seats in the area, police atrocities have begun," alleged Soren.

Meanwhile, after an assurance by the district administration that the nine-point demand made by the tribals would be met with, the blockades in Jhargram were lifted. The demands included stopping indiscriminate police raids and labeling tribals as Maoists. However, the siege of Lalgarh continues. A meeting to resolve the Lalgarh crisis has been called on Friday.

The state Government, which was finding it difficult to handle the situation at Lalgarh and was desperately trying to get Central forces, on Thursday met with disappointment with the Centre turning down the request saying that the CRPF would be required for conducting Assembly elections.

Heading: AGP back in NDA fold - Indian Express
Content:
Having already been pushed to the margins in the UPA Government, Minister for Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) Mani Shankar Aiyar is miffed that some Union ministries are putting up proposals related to the North Eastern Region (NER) for Cabinet approval without holding any consultations with his ministry.

Making his displeasure known at a recent meeting of the Union Cabinet over how "the ministries of Government of India do not consult us", Aiyar has now got the Cabinet Secretariat to issue instructions reiterating government rules which stipulate that when the subject matter of a case concerns more than one department, the sponsoring ministry or department is required to carry out consultations with all the concerned ministries and departments before proposal are put up before the Cabinet.

The circular, issued by Cabinet Secretariat's Additional Secretary Mrutyunjay Sarangi, explicitly states that it has been noticed that the "Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region is not consulted in respect of some proposals, schemes, projects, etc, relating to North Eastern Region".

It then goes on to advise all secretaries to the Government of India to advise concerned officials in respective ministries and departments "to ensure" that in respect of proposals concerning NER, DoNER ministry is consulted before proposals are finalised for consideration of Cabinet and various Cabinet Committees.

"During the last two years, I have succeeded in converting the DoNER ministry from just being a ministry disbursing the Non Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) to a ministry which actually represents the interests of the North East. However, there have been instances where papers come up before Cabinet without any consultations with either DoNER or the North East Council (NEC)," Aiyar said. He also said that on account of DoNER and NEC not playing a "proactive role in the past", the line ministries had been spending 10 per cent of their Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) without holding any consultations with the either DoNER ministry or any of the states in NER.

Aiyar has now assigned senior officials in his ministry to establish contact with various ministries and hold consultations while finalising details of projects and schemes for NER.

Heading: Terrorists smuggling arms via Bay of Bengal: Rajapaksa - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP's quest for allies got a boost with the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) formally joining the NDA on Wednesday.

"The BJP and the AGP will work together in the coming Lok Sabha elections to free Assam from the tyranny of Congress misrule. Both the parties subscribe to the view that to save India we must save Assam. To achieve that the BJP and AGP have joined hands and will unite all anti-Congress forces in the state," said the NDA prime ministerial candidate L K Advani, announcing the tie-up.

Supporting the BJP stand on the Bangladeshi illegal migration issue, AGP chief Chandra Mohan Patwari said: "Assam is the transit point of illegal Bangladeshi migrants to other parts of India. Both parties will work together to find a permanent solution on the issue".

The two parties declined to comment on the seat arrangements for the state for the coming parliamentary polls. Party president Rajnath Singh said: "No decision has been taken on seat sharing. The consultations are still on... more parties are likely to join in the near future."

Heading: Two parties and a sadhvi - Indian Express
Content:
Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa on Thursday said terrorists were using Bay of Bengal's sea lines of communication to transport arms and drugs, and sought the seven-member grouping around the Bay of Bengal — known as BIMSTEC countries — to cooperate in combating terrorism.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, however, asked him during his bilateral meeting that Lanka should abide by the joint statement agreed to by the two sides during the special envoy's visit that Lankan navy would not fire at the Indian fishermen. Singh also asked him to ensure safety and welfare of ethnic Tamils and talked about the "humanitarian" aspect of the conflict, said MEA sources.

This follows Rajapaksa's statement to The Indian Express in Male on Tuesday that LTTE was using Indian fishermen to get weapons in their trawlers.

Asked if he had raised this issue during his one-on-one meeting with Singh, he said, "Yes, yes. I had mentioned it as it is a national security issue. It will be taken up by the (foreign) ministers."

MEA sources said the PM also conveyed the Tamil Nadu Assembly's resolution to him and emphasised the need to find a solution within the Sri Lankan framework. The PM also spoke about 2,000 tonnes of food and relief supplies by the Tamil Nadu Government, to be distributed by International Red Cross Society to the internally displaced persons.

External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee also called for a negotiated settlement and stressed the need for further devolution of powers.

The resolution to combat terror, adopted by the BIMSTEC nations, "fully reflects our concern" over growing terrorism in the region, Rajapaksa said at a press conference with leaders of BIMSTEC countries. Asserting that maritime surveillance was required in Bay of Bengal, he said, "We discussed it (at the meeting). All countries and societies of the region are affected by terrorism."

On solution to the conflict, Rajapaksa said, "We must eradicate terrorism first, then give a political solution. We can't pass this on to the next generation...This is the practical solution. For over two decades, Sri Lanka has been facing a tremendous challenge to our democratic way of life through barbaric actions of a terrorist group, the LTTE," he said, adding,"There is no doubt that such groups have to be dealt with militarily."

On LTTE's offer for ceasefire, Rajapaksa said, "Ceasefire has been there for 20 years. There have been agreements. (But) every time we have ceasefire, they got themselves strengthened, got firepower and hit back," Rajapaksa said. "We are ready for a negotiated settlement. But we are clear that they have to lay down arms."

On the collateral damage to the Tamil civilians, he said, "We assure not only the PM but the whole world that we will look after Tamils. Nothing will happen to Tamils. We are looking after our people, it is my duty." He said the seven-nation BIMSTEC should consider setting up of a mechanism to "effectively police the Bay of Bengal, to deny these terrorists mobility and connectivity".

Earlier, Singh said all BIMSTEC leaders had stressed that terrorism posed a major threat to societies and economies and "we need to combat this threat collectively".

He said the BIMSTEC leaders would soon finalise a convention on fighting international terrorism, trans-national organised crime and illicit drug trafficking. BIMSTEC also discussed maritime security, including India's proposal for a deep-sea port in the Bay of Bengal.

Heading: First Cong rally in J&K talks peace, development - Indian Express
Content:
The alleged involvement of Hindu religious leaders in terrorist activities has become a talking point across the country but it is yet to figure in any significant manner in the election campaign in Madhya Pradesh, Sadhvi Pragya Singh's home state. The state goes to polls in less than a fortnight.

The Congress, the main opposition party in Madhya Pradesh, is reticent on this "emotive" issue: "Why should we when the BJP itself is not talking about it? If we rake it up on our own, it will boomerang on us," says Prakash Khandelwal, chief of the Congress's Gwalior unit. Former Bajrang Dal chief Jaibhan Singh Pavaiyya, the BJP candidate from Gwalior, was photographed with Sameer Kulkarni, one of the accused in the Malegaon blast case, and yet the Congress has skipped the issue. Pavaiyya sees no reason to talk about it either.

Ditto in Indore, from where two people accused in the case have been taken into custody, and where Sadhvi Pragya Singh spent a lot of time. Even opponents of the BJP's Indore-4 candidate, Malini Gaur, at whose house the Sadhvi had spent considerable time after her husband Laxman Singh Gaur's death, are avoiding the issue. Instead, the Congress is persisting with local matters and corruption cases involving some ministers.

BJP leaders say that they don't have to talk about it — the more the media harps on "Hindu terror", the better it is for the party. "The majority community believes that these blasts are just a reaction that came after a long time." But this view is expressed only in private. Officially, the line is: Everyone is innocent until proved guilty. Even the Shiv Sena, though it is contesting only a few seats, is not talking of "Hindu terror" in its campaign.

Uma Bharti's Bharatiya Janshakti is the only party that appeared to take up the issue by offering a ticket to Pragya Singh, who is still in the custody of the Mumbai ATS.

But apart from that, "Hindu terror" figures only during the press conferences addressed by national leaders. When it comes to campaigning at the local level, like public meetings or door-to-door campaigns, candidates and party workers across the political spectrum, give it a miss.

While the state BJP leaders and candidates have avoided the issue altogether, national BJP leaders from Rajnath Singh to Venkaiah Naidu and Murli Manohar Joshi have defended the Sadhvi, taking the line that there is no proof against her as yet. Their defence of her has come mainly via replies to questions on "Hindu terror". Of late, though, some of these leaders have begun targeting the ATS and the Congress-NCP government in Maharashtra for subjecting the Sadhvi to more tests in custody.

The only notable exception to the general political reticence on this issue has been AICC general secretary Digvijay Singh, who has been seen to openly take on the RSS and allied Hindu organisations in his public statements. But he is obviously going against the current in the MP Congress.

"It's absolutely not an issue here. I haven't been to Bhopal so I don't know what other leaders are talking elsewhere," says HRD minister Arjun Singh's son Ajay Singh, the Congress candidate from Churhat in Sidhi district. He is also the chairman of the party's campaign committee. "I am only talking of the BJP's five-year misrule and how the state government has failed to deliver on its promises," he says.

Asked if the Congress is worried about the issue of "Hindu terrorism" boomeranging on it, Ajay Singh says, "That may be true in Gujarat, not here. Madhya Pradesh is largely a rural state and cases against farmers for non-payment of electricity dues are an emotive issue, not terrorism." State PCC chief Suresh Pachauri has a stock response: "Terrorists have no religion. All those involved in such activities should be brought to book."

Heading: Maoists kill Cong worker, loot EVMs - Indian Express
Content:
With the controversy over the alleged sale of tickets refusing to die down even after the party removed senior leader Margaret Alva from key party positions, Congress president Sonia Gandhi on Thursday ousted another self-proclaimed whistle-blower Yogendra Makwana. He was stripped of his post as AICC Scheduled Castes cell chairperson. The action against the former Union minister was expected as he was reportedly planning to launch a new political outfit. Makwana had also supported Alva, saying he had similar complaints about money being demanded for tickets in the Rajasthan Assembly elections.

"Yogendra Makwana has been criticising the functioning of the party for a long time. The party has taken a serious view of his conduct and the Congress president has relieved him from the chairmanship of the SC department with immediate effect," said a Congress release.

Heading: TN college caste clash: police chief shifted - Indian Express
Content:
Maoist rebels killed a Congress worker, looted three Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), dug up roads and laid landmines and resorted to firing at many places in Naxalite-infested South Bastar on Thursday, a day before the first phase of polling in 39 Assembly segments of Chhattisgarh.

Police sources said Congress worker Trinath Thakur was shot at Gadapal village, under Kuakonta police station area, in Dantewada-ST constituency. He died on the spot while other party workers escaped unhurt.

State Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Dr Alok Shukla said the Maoist rebels snatched three EVMs from the poll parties, who were trekking down to polling stations at Porjem, Maruki and Mankapal in Konta Assembly segment of South Bastar. However, the rebels did not harm the poll parties and they were let off with a warning not to go for poll duty.

Dr Shukla said separate polling parties were sent to these polling stations. He said polling parties were not dispatched to seven polling centres in Bijapur district because of security reasons. "They will reach their destinations on Friday morning," he said, refusing to divulge which these centres were.

Meanwhile, police sources in Bastar said the rebels had dug up even main roads at many places in the division, apparently to lay landmines. Ten kilograms of crude tiffin bombs were recovered from a village in South Bastar. Rebels also opened fire at a patrolling party at Takilodh and Haloor villages in Bijapur. CPI (Maoist) has given a boycott call for the elections in Bastar, where polling in 12 constituencies is scheduled for Friday.

Heading: Five-year-old’s organs gift three new life - Indian Express
Content:
The violent clash between two groups of students split on caste lines at the Dr Ambedkar Government Law College in Chennai on Wednesday shook the state today, forcing the Government to announce a judicial probe by a retired justice and transfer Chennai Police Commissioner R Sekar.

Action has also been ordered against the college's principal and the police personnel at the spot who allegedly remained mute spectators to the violence.

Three students were seriously injured in the incident and one of them continues to be in a critical condition. Police sources said seven students were arrested and charged under various sections, including attempt to murder.

With tension threatening to spread to other campuses, all four law colleges in the state have been closed for the next two days and the ongoing semester examinations postponed indefinitely.

Wednesday's violent clash was telecast repeatedly by TV channels here, showing students attacking with iron rods, sticks and even knives. Even as journalists pleaded with the policemen to do something, they refused to intervene.

The trouble between the two groups, belonging to different castes, began a week ago when one of them, celebrating the anniversary of their community leader, failed to mention the name of Dr B R Ambedkar in its pamphlets. The college had seen tension over the matter the past few days, even altercation and minor attacks.

With students sharply divided on caste lines, skirmishes and clashes between various groups are a regular feature in law colleges in the city. Senior police officers say this is the reason why the force may have been reluctant to intervene. Law college students are favourite recruiting ground for political parties and, years ago, when the police had tried to enter a law college campus to quell violence, they were criticised by all parties. On Thursday, all parties barring the ruling DMK raised the matter in the Assembly, with Opposition leader Jayalalithaa equating the incident to the attack on Sun Group's daily Dinakaran's office.

Law Minister Durai Murugan made an announcement that the Government had decided to set up a commission to inquire into the violence, headed by retired High Court judge Justice Shanmugham. The Government suspended the college Principal, an Assistant Commissioner of Police and an Inspector, while the Chennai Police Commissioner and four Sub-Inspectors have been transferred.

The situation at the Law College remained tense on Thursday, with students refusing to permit police personnel to enter the campus.

Heading: Punjab to mortgage municipal properties for welfare schemes - Indian Express
Content:
The bold decision of the parents of a five-year-old girl, declared brain dead, to donate her organs has given a new lease of life to three persons.

Subha Nandini, was suffering from 'brain stem giloma' for the past eight months and was declared brain dead on November 10, following which doctors retrieved her kidneys, liver, cornea and heart.

The kidney transplantation was performed at ABC hospitals here on a 46-year-old patient. The cornea transplantation took place at the St Joseph's Institute of Ophthalmology. Since the city does not have facilities to handle heart and liver transplantation, the organs were sent to Narayana Hrudayalaya in Bangalore. A nine-year-old girl in Bangalore was the beneficiary of the liver transplantation. The heart, however, could not be transplanted due to time lapse, doctors said.

Nandini was brought to ABC hospitals on May 26. On November 8, she slipped into a coma and the following day, her condition worsened. She was put on ventilator support on November 9.

The girl's father Manikandan, who runs a cell phone servicing centre at Samayapuram village near here, said that he and his wife were happy to see that their daughter's organs had benefitted three people.

Heading: Gogoi agrees to CBI probe into Assam serial blasts - Indian Express
Content:
In another indication of the precarious state of Punjab's finances, the state Government is planning to mortgage the properties and assets of its municipal committees to raise a loan of Rs 500 crore to implement a drinking water scheme and set up sewerage treatment plants. This follows on the heels of the sale of prime municipal properties to meet expenses.

"The Chief Minister had announced these projects but we had no money to execute them. Therefore, the Government has decided to take a loan of Rs 500 crore from HUDCO. Nothing has been finalised yet about the payback modalities," said a highly placed official.

An official letter—a copy of which is with The Indian Express—has been dispatched by the Local Bodies Department to all the municipal committees in the state asking them to send details of the prevailing market price of their properties, along with attested valuation certificates. The letter further mentions that details of only those properties be mentioned which are not involved in any legal dispute.

Principal Secretary, Local Bodies, D S Bains confirmed that the Government was holding talks with HUDCO for a 15-year lease of properties belonging to 129 municipal committees in the state.

To avoid any future legal hassles, the committees have been directed to also submit duly passed resolutions by their councillors stating that the properties can be hypothecated to HUDCO for the loan. The Chief Executive Officers of the committees have been directed to give the documents by hand to the Local Bodies Department. They have been warned of official action if they fail to submit these within the prescribed time.

The Government is keen that the loan amount be released by mid-December so that these two welfare projects can be initiated before the parliamentary elections.

"This practice of keeping properties on hypothecation is prevalent in southern states. But this is the first time that the Punjab Government is resorting to it. I guess there simply wasn't any choice in view of the state's precarious financial state," said the official.

Heading: Finest in photojournalism to be honoured today - Indian Express
Content:
Two weeks after the Special Investigation Team (SIT) constituted by the Assam Government failed to come up with a single specific lead in the serial blasts of October 30, Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi has agreed to an all-party suggestion that the investigations be handed over to the CBI.

The suggestion that emerged as a unanimous resolution at the end of an all-party meeting that continued till late Wednesday evening, was later endorsed by the state Government, which also agreed in principle to ask the CBI to take over the probe. At least 11 persons have been arrested by the police in connection with the blasts so far, but there has been very little headway in terms of unravelling the conspiracy or nabbing the real culprits.

The Government has, instead, been making statements that have only added to the confusion over the identity of the people behind the blasts. While a senior Assam Police officer, within a couple of hours of the blasts, attributed them to jehadi elements, Gogoi last Saturday pointed at Bangladesh as "the biggest problem" for Assam.

On Tuesday, however, the state Government issued a statement that some members of the National Democratic Front of Bodoland, an outlawed insurgent group currently observing a ceasefire, had planted the bombs, particularly in Guwahati. This was followed by an extension of the ban on NDFB by the Centre.

Heading: UN force needed to prevent piracy: India - Indian Express
Content:
The India Press Photo Awards 2008—instituted by the Ramnath Goenka Foundation in 2004—will be given away at a glitzy ceremony at Express Towers, Nariman Point, in Mumbai on Friday.

Actor Salman Khan will be the chief guest at the function. Actor-director Anupam Kher, who is the guest of honour, and director-producer Subhash Ghai, special guest, will unveil photographs from the Express archives.

The awards are an attempt to identify, promote and reward excellence in photojournalism and documentary photography. "We, at the Express group, believe visuals often tell stories better than words and try to celebrate photographs on our pages. We are proud to be part of an effort that showcases the best of photojournalism in India because the awards not just honour the best talent in the industry but underscore the importance of visuals in print journalism as well," says Shekhar Gupta, editor-in-chief of The Indian Express.

The response to IPPA 2008—sponsored by Canon—has been overwhelming: 8,801 entries from 226 photographers. The panel of judges—renowned photojournalists Prashant Panjiar, Pablo Bartholomew and Harsh Man Rai—will choose one grand prize-winning image and one winner from each of the 18 categories. Alok Bharadwaj, Senior Vice-President, Canon India Pvt Ltd, will deliver the closing speech.

The Ramnath Goenka Picture of the Year will go to the photographer whose picture demonstrates an outstanding level of visual creativity and journalistic skill. The winner gets a cash prize of Rs 1.5 lakh. The award-winning photographs will be displayed at an exhibition in Mumbai, which will travel throughout the country.

Award categories

• Arts & Entertainment (Single and Story)

• Contemporary Issues (Single and Story)

• Nature & Environment (Single and Story)

• Portrait (Single and Story)

• Sports Action (Single and Story)

• People in News (Single and Story)

• Daily Life (Single and Story)

• General News Story

• Spot News (Single and Story)

• Winning Photograph

Heading: Sadhvi keeps to herself, reads Ramayan in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Mahant Amritanand alias Dayanand Pandey, arrested from Kanpur on Wednesday by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad which is probing the Malegaon blast case, was flown to Mumbai on Thursday after a Lucknow judicial magistrate accepted the ATS request for transit remand.

UP ATS officials, who were present when Pandey was questioned by the Maharashtra policemen, claimed he admitted he knew Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur and Lt Col Shrikant Purohit — both are under arrest for their alleged roles in the case — but denied he had anything to do with the blast. He said he came into contact with them while he was in Pune some years ago, an official said, adding that Pandey did not spell out exactly when he met them. The official claimed that Pandey also dropped names of some religious leaders-turned politicians who he said visited him at a temple in Faridabad near Delhi and in Jammu.

According to the official, Pandey said he had cleared the National Defence Academy entrance exam in 1987 and was an Air Force aspirant. He did not finish training and returned home. While in Varanasi, he came in contact with some gurus and moved to Jammu where he later became head of the Sharda Sarvagya Peeth.

Heading: Safe for democracy? - Indian Express
Content: Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur, arrested in connection with the September 29 Malegaon blasts, is keeping herself busy in Byculla jail by reading the Ramcharit Manas and Ramayan available in the jail library. Pragya, who will soon be shifted from the jail, does not interact with anyone and is closely guarded by jail officials. Jail Superintendent Sudhir Kingre said Pragya was being kept in a separate cell with two guards because of security concerns. "This is also because she is not originally an accused of our jail. She will soon be shifted, till then all necessary care is being taken," he said. The Byculla jail houses inmates like Fahmida Hanif, who is involved in the Gateway of India and Zaveri Bazaar bomb blast cases. Fahmida who has a record of picking up fights inside the jail, had even allegedly bashed up Zaheera Sheikh, the witness in the Best Bakery case when she was in the prison.

Heading: It’s no big deal - Indian Express
Content:
A massive security umbrella has been thrown all over the 39 constituencies going to polls in the first phase of elections today, including in the tribal Bastar region where the Maoists have given a call for boycott of elections. The rebels have also stepped up violence, setting ablaze vehicles and resorting to firing at many places in the tribal belt.

Unprecedented security has been mounted in five districts, comprising 12 assembly segments, in Bastar division and in Dhamtari, Rajnandgaon, Kawardha, Durg and Mahasamund districts to ensure that smooth conduct of polling. Incidents of police-Naxalite encounters were reported from several places in Bastar division during electioneering, which was low key because of the Maoist threat.

Prominent among those in the fray in the first phase are Chief Minister Raman Singh (Rajnandgaon), leader of the opposition in the assembly, Mahendra Karma (Dantewada-ST), Speaker Prem Prakash Pandey (Bhilai) and four ministers in the Raman Singh ministry.

As many as 379 candidates will test their electoral fortunes from 39 constituencies, which have an electorate of more than 63.97 lakh, including over 32.08 lakh women voters. (Here, women voters outnumber male voters). More than 11,131 electronic voting machines will be used in 8,879 polling stations in the first phase.

The Election Commission has changed the polling time to 7 am to 3 pm in 12 constituencies in Bastar, Dantewada, Bijapur, Narayanpur and Kanker districts so that helicopters carrying EVMs, polling parties and security personnel can take off from remote areas and land at base camps before sunset. In other constituencies, polling will be held between 8 am to 5 pm.

Ten helicopters have been pressed into service in order to keep vigil and to ensure speedy movement of poll parties and security personnel to polling centres located in remote and inaccessible areas. Aerial surveillance of the Naxalite areas is being carried out following apprehension that the Maoist rebels could resort to more violence, as this poll is the first since the launch of the anti-Naxalite 'Salwa Judum' movement in June 2005.

Besides the Central Reserve Police Force, Border Security Force, and Central Industrial Security Force, SAF personnel from Punjab, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Haryana and West Bengal are being deployed throughout Bastar division. Out of the total 2,218 polling stations in Bastar division, 1,118 have been classified as hyper-sensitive and 715 as sensitive. In all, about 40,000 security personnel are being deployed to ensure smooth conduct of polling here.

Security forces from outside the state have been advised to patrol the interior areas on foot and not to use vehicles in view of the possibility of landmine blasts. Bomb disposal squads and other technical experts have also been stationed at strategic locations.

A high security alert is also being maintained in Rajnandgaon, Durg and Mahasamund districts where Naxalite activities took place in the recent past. The rebels had twice stormed the Mahamaya mines — owned by public sector Bhilai Steel Plant in Durg district — and carted away explosives a few months ago.

Heading: From jobseekers, Obama seeks to know all - Indian Express
Content:
In July, buoyed by the UPA's victory on the nuclear deal in the trust vote in Parliament, the Sheila Dikshit-led government had seized upon the issue and used it to sound the election bugle in the capital. "We hail the Indo-US nuclear deal which would meet power needs in the country in the long term. It will definitely be one of the poll issues in the coming assembly elections," the Chief Minister announced on July 23.

While the party tried to shoo away the opposition's charges on inflation, claiming that price rise was a "national issue" and that Delhi government had no control over it, it held on to the nuclear deal. The calculation was that it would help it to neutralise the perceived wave of anti-incumbency that was expected to work against the party in no small measure this time.

Four months later, and barely a fortnight away from the state elections, the nuclear deal seems to be have been dumped somewhere along the way, relegated to a mere mention or a "thank you Soniaji" postscript in the 10-minute speeches made by the city's politicians across the capital.

Hauz Khas's sitting MLA Kiran Walia, who is now fighting for a seat in Malviya Nagar, claims that most residents in her upmarket locality already read newspapers and watch television — they don't need to be reminded of the deal, she suggests. Vijay Singh Lochav, who is campaigning for a seat in the rural belt of north-west Delhi, claims that his electorate doesn't really care about the deal that nearly toppled the government.

"My people are more concerned about roads and water. I occasionally do mention the nuclear deal when I am doing my door-to-door campaign and talk about electricity, but honestly Delhi is so vast that there is still a population that is more concerned about local roads than the nuclear deal," he explains.

Walia acknowledges that the nuclear deal has lost its importance over the last couple of months. "We used to hold meetings with residents at the block level when the deal was being discussed to generate public support. Then the Delhi blasts happened and later the Batla House encounter. The nuclear deal has now sort of drowned in these issues that have gripped the city over the last two months," says Walia.

Barely 2 km away from Walia's constituency, former IPS officer Amod Kant who has been roped in by the Chief Minister to fight from Sangam Vihar, the city's largest unauthorised colony, also prefers the issue of regularisation of unauthorised colonies (another Congress poll promise) in his area. "There are about five lakh residents in this area and I am already running about 20 centres of my NGO Prayas here. People are more concerned about clean drinking water which is considered a luxury here, in this part of South Delhi. The nuclear deal would not ring any bells here," he says.

DPCC chief J.P. Agrawal, however, claims, "The nuclear deal is certainly an issue in this campaign. We have told our party workers to extensively talk about it, and whoever feels the need can use our literature and resources to explain it to the voters."

Though Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit is yet to begin her political outings to woo voters in the post-delimitation New Delhi constituency, which is much larger than her previous Gole Market seat, her opponent, BJP MLA Vijay Jolly, uses the nuclear deal merely to take digs at the Congress party and Rahul Gandhi in particular.

Visiting a village near Sarojini Nagar, Jolly said on Wednesday, "Yahan unhe Kalawati nahin milegi. Sheilaji kabhi yahan khud nahin ayeen hain (they won't find Kalawati here — Sheilaji herself has never come here)."

Heading: Guantanamo will be  priority for new Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Got a domestic help? Linked to Freddie-Fannie?

Want a top job in the Obama administration? Only pack rats need apply, preferably those not packing controversy. A seven-page questionnaire being sent by the office of President-elect Barack Obama to those seeking Cabinet and other high-ranking posts may be the most extensive — some say invasive — application ever.

The questionnaire includes 63 requests for personal and professional records, some covering applicants' spouses and grown children as well, that are forcing job-seekers to rummage from basements to attics, in shoe boxes, diaries and computer archives to document both their achievements and missteps.

Applicants are asked whether they or anyone in their family owns a gun. They must include any e-mail that might embarrass Obama, along with any blog posts and links to their Facebook pages. It also asks applicants to "please list all aliases or 'handles' you have used to communicate on the Internet".

The vetting process for executive branch jobs has been onerous for decades. But Obama has elevated the vetting even beyond what might have been expected, especially when it comes to applicants' family members, in a reflection of his campaign rhetoric against lobbying and the back-scratching, self-serving ways of Washington.

"President-elect Obama made a commitment to change the way Washington does business, and the vetting process exemplifies that," said Stephanie Cutter, chief spokeswoman for the Obama transition office.

Jobs with the mortgage finance giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have served as lucrative incubators for Democratic and Republican administration officials. But those affiliations have become potentially toxic since the Government seized both companies after years of financial irregularities that have stoked the economic crisis.

Not surprisingly, then, question 18 of the Obama application asks whether "you, your spouse or any member of your immediate family" have been affiliated with Fannie, Freddie, American International Group, Washington Mutual and any other institution getting a Government bailout.

Under "Domestic Help", the Obama questionnaire asks for the immigration status of applicants' housekeepers, nannies, chauffeurs and yard-workers, and whether applicants have paid the required taxes for household employees.

"Every transition is cumulative," said Michael Berman, a lobbyist who worked in the transitions of both Clinton and Jimmy Carter.

Just in case the previous 62 questions do not ferret out any potential controversy, the 63rd and final one is all-encompassing: "Please provide any other information, including information about other members of your family, that could suggest a conflict of interest or be a possible source of embarrassment to you, your family, or the President-elect."

Some of the questions

• Please list any claims of sexual harassment of other workplace misconduct, made against you or any employee directly supervised by you, including the resolution of the matter.

• Please provide the URL of any websites that feature you in either a personal or professional capacity (e.g., Facebook, MySpace, etc.)

• With regard to each obligation of child support and/or alimony owed by you or your spouse, please state the following: Have any payments been made late or have there been any lapses in payment?... Have any actions or motions to compel payment or initiate collection of late payments and/or past due amounts been filed or threatened?... If yes, please provide details.

• If applicable, please list the names, addresses and phone number of cohabitants within the last ten years. A cohabitant is a person with whom you share bonds of affection, obligation, or other commitment, as opposed to a person with whom you live for reasons of convenience (a roommate).

Heading: Iran wary of Obama, the sweet-talker - Indian Express
Content:
The Obama administration will launch a review of the classified files of the approximately 250 detainees at Guantanamo Bay immediately after taking office, as part of an intensive effort to close the US prison in Cuba, according to people who advised the campaign on detainee issues.

Announcing the closure of the controversial detention facility would be among the most potent signals the incoming administration could send of its sharp break with the Bush era, according to advisers. They believe the move would create a global wave of diplomatic and popular goodwill that could accelerate the transfer of some detainees to other countries.

But the advisers, as well as outside national security and legal experts, said the new administration will face a thicket of legal, diplomatic, political and logistical challenges to closing the prison and prosecuting the most serious offenders in the US — an effort that could take many months or longer.

The new administration will face hard decisions regarding not just the current Guantanamo detainees but also how it will handle future captures of terrorism suspects.

Obama's transition team denied reports this week that it was contemplating some form of preventative detention backed by a new civilian national security court.

Heading: After Nov 4, Joan Baez has something to sing about - Indian Express
Content:
Since 2006, Iran's leaders have called for direct, unconditional talks with the US to resolve international concerns over their nuclear program. But as an American administration open to such negotiations prepares to take power, Iran's political and military leaders are sounding suddenly wary of Barack Obama.

"People who put on a mask of friendship, but with the objective of betrayal, and who enter from the angle of negotiations without preconditions, are more dangerous," Hossein Taeb, the deputy commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, said Wednesday, according to the semi-official news agency Mehrnews.

"The power holders in the new American Government are trying to regain their lost influence with a tactical change in their foreign diplomacy. They are shifting from a hard conflict to a soft attack," said Taeb. For Iran's leaders, the only state of affairs worse than poor relations with the United States may be improved relations.

Heading: Bush to write book; Palin may follow - Indian Express
Content:
The iconic folk singer Joan Baez opened her Wednesday night concert at the Birchmere music hall in Alexandria with a civil rights anthem that suddenly sounded celebratory: We Shall Overcome, the old protest song whose message of resolve and sweeping social change played like a valedictory in the wake of Barack Obama's election. Thirty-five years ago, at the Lincoln Memorial, Baez famously sang We Shall Overcome as she stood beside the Rev Martin Luther King Jr during the March on Washington. Now, she was heralding the ascendancy of the country's first Black President, and you didn't have to be a graying hippie to be nearly overwhelmed by the symbolism and symmetry.

The performance was stunning, even though her clarion soprano has lost some of its once-breathtaking power and lift. At 67, Baez works mostly in her middle range now, but she can still sound like an angel. If her performance — though warm and comforting — lacked the bell-like clarity that was her signature in the '60s, there was a good reason: "My voice is a little scratchy 'cause I screamed all night," she told the capacity crowd, which hollered its approval.

Baez began performing 50 years ago in the Boston area, and Wednesday's set was constructed as something of a survey-cum-celebration of her long career. For more than 90 minutes, she sang songs both political and personal, from the bright bluegrass of one of her first recorded songs, Lily of the West, and a powerful cover of the Band's The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down.

Baez was in high spirits on the evening after the historic presidential election, peppering the 22-song set with humorous stories about her nonagenarian mother, her friendship with King and her reaction to Obama's victory.

Heading: It was a hoax: Palin does know Africa is a continent after all (or does she?) - Indian Express
Content:
Republicans may have been voted out of power but they could dominate US political bookshelves with memoirs by President George W Bush and first lady Laura Bush among the possible coming attractions.

Publishers would eagerly offer Laura Bush seven figures for her memoirs, raising the question whether she could fetch more than her husband. Yet both could be outdone by Sarah Palin, the governor of Alaska and unsuccessful Republican vice presidential candidate. "Rightly or wrongly, the public seems to have taken a fancy to Palin and I would imagine she'd get more than either of them at this silly moment in our lives," said John Baker, former editorial director at Publishers Weekly who is now an agent.

Agents and publishers say both Bushes and Palin would likely command multimillion-dollar advances but not as much as former President Bill Clinton, who received a $15 million advance, believed to be a record for a non-fiction work. President-elect Democrat Barack Obama, who has already written two books about his own life. Former Bush aide Karl Rove and ex-Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld already have book contracts but there's another potential memoirist who is seen as even more intriguing: Vice President Dick Cheney.

President Bush said he would probably write a book after returning to his home state of Texas in January. "I want people to know what it's like to make some of the decisions I had to make...I've had one of these presidencies where I had to make some tough calls," said Bush. Laura Bush has expressed interest in writing a book. Agent Gary Morris of the David Black Literary Agency said intrigue about Laura Bush is linked to the success of Curtis Sittenfeld's "American Wife," a fictionalization of her life. But it is Palin who could be the real prize. "There are half a dozen publishers that would zealously bid on a Palin book," said Robert Weil, executive editor at W W Norton. "Some agents say she could sell for $7 million."

Heading: Bomber hits US convoy, kills 19 - Indian Express
Content:
It was among the juicier post-election recriminations: Fox News Channel quoted an unnamed McCain campaign figure as saying that Sarah Palin did not know that Africa was a continent.

Who would say such a thing? On Monday the answer popped up on a blog and popped out of the mouth of David Shuster, an MSNBC anchor. "Turns out it was Martin Eisenstadt, a McCain policy adviser, who has come forward today to identify himself as the source of the leaks," Shuster said.

Trouble is, Martin Eisenstadt doesn't exist. His blog does, but it's a put-on. The think tank where he is a senior fellow — the Harding Institute for Freedom and Democracy — is just a website. The TV clips of him on YouTube are fakes.

And the claim of credit for the Africa anecdote is just the latest ruse by Eisenstadt, who turns out to be a very elaborate hoax that has been going on for months. MSNBC, which quickly corrected the mistake, has plenty of company in being taken in by an Eisenstadt hoax, including The New Republic and The Los Angeles Times.

Now, a pair of obscure filmmakers say they created Martin Eisenstadt to help them pitch a TV show based on the character. But under the circumstances, why should anyone believe a word they say?

"That's a really good question," one of the two, Eitan Gorlin. They say the blame lies not with them but with shoddiness in the traditional news media and especially the blogosphere.

Gorlin, 39, argued that Eisenstadt was no more of a joke than half the bloggers or political commentators on the Internet or television.

An MSNBC spokesman, Jeremy Gaines, explained the network's misstep by saying someone in the newsroom received the Palin item in an e-mail message from a colleague and assumed it had been checked out. "It had not been vetted," he said. "It should not have made air."

Eisenstadt became an adviser to John McCain and got a blog, updated occasionally with comments claiming insider knowledge, and other bloggers began quoting and linking to it. It mixed weird-but-true items with false ones that were plausible, if just barely.

Heading: Taliban to UN: stop Afghan executions - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a fierce suicide bombing in southern Afghanistan, insurgents struck on Thursday in the east of the country when an American military convoy was attacked in a crowded market, killing one soldier and 18 civilians, according to United States military and Afghan police officials.

One of the dead was a 12-year-old boy, who died when a suicide car bomber in a Toyota Corolla approached an American military convoy and then swerved into a weekly market at around 8 am, according to US and Afghan accounts. Dr Ajmal Pardes, director of public health in the area, said 74 people were injured.

The strike was in the Bati Kot district of eastern Afghanistan's Nangarhar Province.

An Associated Press photographer said that an American military vehicle, two civilian vehicles and two rickshaws were destroyed.

US Navy commander Jeff Bender, an American military spokesman in Kabul, said the civilian death count, initially put at 10, had risen to 18.

On Wednesday, a tanker truck packed with explosives detonated outside the provincial council office in Kandahar, Afghanistan's largest southern city, killing the driver and at least six other people and wounding more than 40 others.

The blast shook the entire city, caused at least five houses to fall and left a crater near the council building, which housed an office of a national security service.

"The enemies of Afghanistan and peace once again put us in mourning," Gen Rahmatullah Roufi, the provincial governor, told reporters. He announced a "purification" operation to arrest insurgents in and near the city.

In a separate incident reported on Thursday, two soldiers from the American-led NATO alliance were killed in an explosion in the south of the country in an explosion on Wednesday, the alliance said, but did not specify the soldiers' nationality.

The Defence Ministry in London later identified the two soldiers as members of Britain's Royal Marines who were taking part in a joint patrol with Afghan soldiers in the Garmsir district of Southern Helmand Province.

The American contingent is the largest foreign force in Afghanistan but Britain has about 8,000 troops there. A survey broadcast on Thursday by the BBC said more than two-thirds of those questioned believed Britain should withdraw its soldiers over the next year while less than a quarter favored their continued deployment.

This year has been the bloodiest since the American-led invasion of late 2001 that toppled the Taliban regime, whose supporters have revived their campaign to drive out foreign forces.

The latest American fatalities brought to around 148 the number of American military deaths so far this year, compared to 111 in the whole of 2001, the Associated Press reported. Additionally, around 110 soldiers from other coalition forces have died this year.

More than 5,400 people, including almost 1,000 civilians, have died in violence related to the insurgency this year, the news agency said, citing figures provided by Afghan and international officials.

Heading: Iraqi soldier kills two GIs - Indian Express
Content:
The Taliban urged the UN on Thursday to press the Afghan Government to stop executing prisoners on death row, citing concern about fair trials.

Afghanistan resumed executions this week after a break of more than a year, with three Taliban sentenced for deadly attacks among nine people put to death in the past few days. Those executions followed a public outcry over rising crime.

The UN and EU have called on Karzai to halt the executions, citing concern about the standards of judicial fairness. The UN says Afghanistan's law enforcement and judicial systems fall far short of internationally accepted standards.

"We strongly request the UN, the EU, the Red Cross and human rights groups to earnestly prevent this barbaric act," the Taliban said in a statement on their website, accusing Karzai's Government of corruption.

Heading: Karzai, Zardari discuss Taliban with Saudi ruler - Indian Express
Content:
Two US soldiers were killed and six others were wounded by an Iraqi soldier in an attack in the northern city of Mosul on Wednesday, according to the US military, Iraqi security officials and witnesses. The shooter was killed by other US soldiers.

In Baghdad, at least 11 Iraqis were killed and 60 others were wounded in a new spate of attacks, witnesses and police officials said. The violence erupted just two days after attacks that killed 28 Iraqis in the capital, in the bloodiest day since June.

While the deaths of the US soldiers were confirmed by the US military, the circumstances surrounding the Mosul shooting remained in dispute.

Major General Mark P Hertling, commander of US troops in northern Iraq, said it began when two platoons of US soldiers stopped at a combat outpost staffed by Iraqi soldiers. Two US lieutenants went inside to an office to speak with an Iraqi captain while soldiers from both sides waited outside. Suddenly, Hertling said, an Iraqi soldier with an AK-47 that was equipped with a 70-round drum walked up to the group of soldiers, said something to an Iraqi soldier and then shot one US soldier in the head and another in the stomach. He then began spraying bullets in all directions, the general said, at which point the Americans shot him dead. One US soldier died on the spot, and the other later died from his wounds.

Hertling said the shooting remained under investigation by both sides.

Heading: Russia submarine accident inquiry indicts sailor - Indian Express
Content:
After a top-level tripartite closed door meeting between the heads of states of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Saudi Arabia, the three nations agreed to continue to pursue talks with the Taliban.

The meeting, one of the series of private meetings held at the UN on Wednesday night, attended by Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari, his Afghan counterpart Hamid Karzai and the Saudi King Abdullah agreed to continue the dialogue with Taliban initiated at the mediation of the Saudis.

Pakistan Foreign Minister Shah Mehmood Qureshi said the dialogue with Taliban was being held on the agreement of the renegade group to accept the constitutions of both Pakistan and Afghanistan. The tripartite talks come in the wake of reports that the new Barack Obama-led administrator in the United States was not opposed to talks with reconcilable elements of Taliban.

Zardari also held a meeting with US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice where he pressed Washington to ease up on US strikes hitting Taliban and al-Qaeda elements in Pakistan's restive border with Afghanistan.

Heading: Google search to track flu spread - Indian Express
Content:
A sailor has been charged for setting off the fire extinguishing system on the Russian nuclear submarine Nerpa, causing 20 people to be gassed to death, investigators told news agencies on Thursday.

"The inquiry has established that a member of the crew, a sailor, set off the anti-fire system... without authorization and for no reason," investigator Vladimir Markin said. "This sailor has already admitted his error," said Markin, a spokesman for the inquiry panel looking into Saturday's accident in the Sea of Japan that raised doubts about the safety of Russian military hardware. "In connection with this, the suspect faces charges... of negligence leading to the death of two or more people," Markin said. The sailor could face up to seven years in prison for his role in the incident.

Twenty people died when the fire-extinguishing system was triggered as the new Akula-class nuclear-powered attack submarine was being tested in the Sea of Japan, pumping Freon gas into the vessel and depriving them of oxygen. The authorities said there was no fire aboard the vessel.

Independent defence experts alleged that the sailor facing charges may turn out to be a scapegoat for a broader failure. "It will be absolutely unfair if this sailor is designated the sole person to be guilty of what happened," Alexander Golts, a defence commentator at Yezhednevny Zhurnal magazine said. "In Russia there is always a tendency to look for a scapegoat," said Pavel Felgenhauer, another defence expert. "The critical lack of qualified personnel in Russia since the fall of the Soviet Union is the cause of most disasters."

Defective gas masks may have been responsible for a number of the deaths on the Nerpa, the Russian tabloid Tvoi Den reported, citing survivors. "I saw people in convulsions ripping off their masks. I also had a breathing apparatus on, but it only worked for seven to 15 minutes," the newspaper quoted warrant officer Yevgeny Ovsyannikov as saying. "Some of the dead were found with their gas masks on. The breathing apparatuses simply didn't work," another survivor Dmitry Usachyov said. Despite the accident the Nerpa passed its tests and will be authorised for use by the Russian navy, the head of the military's general staff, Nikolai Makarov said on Wednesday.

Russian media reported earlier that the vessel was to be leased to India on a contract worth 650 million dollars, but a senior arms industry official told news agencies that this was not the case.

Heading: Don’t allow Dharamsala conclave: China to India - Indian Express
Content:
There is a new common symptom of the flu, in addition to the usual aches, coughs, fevers and sore throats. Turns out a lot of ailing Americans enter phrases like "flu symptoms" into Google and other search engines before they call their doctors. That simple act, multiplied across millions of keyboards in homes has given rise to a new early warning system for fast-spreading flu outbreaks, called Google Flu Trends.

Tests of the new Web tool from Google.org, the company's philanthropic unit, suggest that it may be able to detect regional outbreaks of the flu a week to 10 days before they are reported by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

In February, for example, the CDC reported that the flu cases had recently spiked in the mid-Atlantic states. But Google says its search data show a spike in queries about flu symptoms two weeks before that report was released. Its new service at google.org/flutrends analyzes those searches as they come in, creating graphs and maps of the country that, ideally, will show where the flu is spreading.

The CDC reports are slower because they rely on data collected and compiled from thousands of health care providers, labs and other sources. Some public health experts say the Google data could help accelerate the response of doctors, hospitals and public health officials to a nasty flu season, reducing the spread of the disease and, potentially, saving lives.

"The earlier the warning, the earlier prevention and control measures can be put in place, and this could prevent cases of influenza," said Dr Lyn Finelli, lead for surveillance at the influenza division of the CDC. From 5 to 20 per cent of the nation's population contracts the flu each year leading to roughly 36,000 deaths. The service covers only the United States, but Google is hoping to eventually use the same technique to help track influenza and other diseases worldwide.

The premise behind Google Flu Trends - what appears to be a fruitful marriage of mob behavior and medicine - has been validated by an unrelated study indicating that the data collected by Yahoo can also help with early detection of flu. "We could use this stream of information to learn about other disease trends as well," said Dr Philip M Polgreen, assistant professor of medicine and epidemiology at the University of Iowa and author of the study based on Yahoo's data.

Heading: France says it’s not swayed by Sudan ceasefire call - Indian Express
Content:
As the Dalai Lama prepares to hold the biggest conclave of exiled Tibetans in nearly six decades in Dharamsala, China on Thursday asked India to honour its promise of not allowing any separatist activities from its soil against the Communist state.

Dismissing as meaningless the November 17-22 meeting of exiled Tibetans at the seat of the Dalai Lama's Tibetan Government-in-exile, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Qin Gang said Beijing expects India to honour its promise not to permit activities "aimed at splitting Chinese territory".

"The Government of India has made solemn commitments on several occasions that (it) does not allow any activities on its soil aimed at dividing (China). We hope that this commitment can be fulfilled," he said.

In the wake of repeated failures to find a solution to the vexed Tibet issue during talks with China, the 73-year-old

Dalai Lama has convened a six-day meeting to determine the future direction of his quest for "genuine autonomy" for his homeland under Chinese sovereignty. The Dalai Lama had suggested recently that his "middle way" for Tibet, which was short of formal independence, was failing.

But Qin claimed the upcoming meeting was aimed at achieving Tibet's independence from Chinese rule.

Heading: Social workers to be probed in baby death case - Indian Express
Content:
Sudan's President Omar al-Beshir has called for an immediate ceasefire in Darfur and a campaign to disarm feared militias in a speech dismissed by rebels as a propaganda stunt for the West. A French official said on Thursday that the announcement of ceasefire is not enough to persuade France to oppose his possible indictment for war crimes.

Beshir spoke after hearing the recommendations of a government-sponsored peace initiative, a cornerstone of Sudan's campaign to suspend international legal proceedings against him but controversial for excluding Darfur rebels. "I announce immediate unconditional ceasefire between the armed forces and warring factions provided that an effective monitoring mechanism be put into action and observed by all involved parties," said Beshir.

UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon welcomed the call for a ceasefire, saying the world expects "concrete progress". Ban "welcomes President Omar al-Beshir's declaration of an immediate ceasefire between the government of Sudan and the armed movements in Darfur as well as the intention by the government of Sudan to disarm all the militias", his spokeswoman said.

"We confirm our commitment of negotiations to reach peaceful solutions which guarantee the eradication of disputes," Beshir told a conference attended by visiting Eritrean President Issaias Afeworki, ambassadors and UN officials. A committee from the so-called people's initiative would contact rebels "to call them to come and take part in peace negotiations," Beshir said.

Sudan has made similar pledges in the past that failed to produce results. "This has been done time and time again," Taher el-Faki, London-based chairman of Justice and Equality Movement's legislative assembly said. Faki said JEM would "go for a ceasefire when there is a framework agreement and declaration of principles."

Four months ago, the chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) demanded an arrest warrant for Beshir on 10 counts of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. Sudan has launched a diplomatic charm offensive to persuade the UN Security Council to invoke a one-year suspension of any legal proceedings. Bashir declared the unilateral ceasefire on Wednesday in the latest push by the government to persuade the UN to suspend ICC arrest warrant.

The UNSC, of which France is a permanent member, has powers under Article 16 of the ICC statute to block any proceedings against Bashir."What we expect from the Sudanese authorities is an immediate and radical change of attitude on several points ... and this ceasefire declaration does not represent such a change," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Eric Chevallier.

Heading: Inflation slips to single digit: 8.98% gives Govt more room - Indian Express
Content:
The organisation that regulates social workers said on Thursday it would look into the actions of staff involved in the case of Baby P, the toddler who died of horrific injuries despite being on an at risk register.

The General Social Care Council (GSCC) said it would examine the actions of social workers at Haringey Council in London whose failure to prevent the death of the 17-month-old baby boy has led to widespread calls for heads to roll.

Schools Secretary Ed Balls has ordered an inquiry into the care of children in Haringey after a report by the council found a number of failings of practice and management over the case. It was the second serious child welfare tragedy in Haringey in recent years following the murder of eight-year-old Victoria Climbie by her guardians in 2000.

"We are conducting our own preliminary enquiries to establish whether the circumstances have any bearing on the suitability of individual social workers to remain on the register," said Rosie Varley, the GSCC's chief executive.

The GSCC inquiries follow Balls' announcement on Wednesday that the schools inspectorate Ofsted, the Commission for Healthcare Audit and Inspection, and the Chief Inspector of Constabulary would review Baby P's case.

In addition, the director of children's services in Hampshire is to be seconded to work alongside his equivalent in Haringey to ensure proper children's procedures are in place.

"There is clear evidence that each agency has singly and collectively failed to adhere to the procedures for the proper management of child protection cases, said Balls.

Baby P had endured repeated beatings, one which caused a broken back, before he was killed in August last year. Officials said the toddler had been used as a punch bag, had more than 40 injuries, and looked like a car crash victim.

His mother, her boyfriend Jason Owen, 36, have all been convicted of causing the death of a child. In the run-up to his death, the baby had been seen 60 times by doctors and social workers, but no action was taken because they said the mother had concealed the truth from them.

Heading: Tricolour is set to hit the Moon this evening - Indian Express
Content:
Inflation returned to single-digit growth at 8.98 per cent after five months, falling 1.74 per cent this week mainly due to a sharp drop in oil prices. This relatively unexpected figure will allow the government to infuse more liquidity into the economy and give the Reserve Bank of India room to cut rates.

With oil prices down to almost one-third from $145 per barrel in July to $56.16 per barrel in November, fuel items such as naphtha, jet fuel, furnace oil and light diesel oil have become cheaper. Inflation had shot up to a 13-year high of 11.05 per cent, fuelled by the administered hike in prices of petrol, diesel and cooking gas for the first week of June from 8.75 per cent.

But inflation for 30 essential commodities increased to 7.74 per cent on a weekly basis from 7.51 per cent, a statement from Finance Ministry said today. The manufactured product index fell by 0.7 per cent, on account of a dip in prices of imported edible oil by 8 per cent, unrefined oil by one per cent and iron and steel by 7 per cent. Fruit and vegetable prices also went down marginally by 0.1 per cent, tea prices by 2 per cent, spices prices by one per cent.

The dip seems to have come sooner than Inflation back to single digit: 8.98 pc

expected. Chief Economic Advisor Arvind Virmani had said on August 28 that inflation was likely to come down to 5-6 per cent over a period of 12 months.

Similarly on November 11, Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Panel chairman Suresh Tendulkar had said, "Inflation seems to be on the decline as international commodity prices are coming down and the domestic harvest is good. Early next year, inflation would be in single digits." The inflation rate, however, will show upward movement next month on account of the base effect, he predicted.

Crisil Principal Economist D K Joshi said: "We see inflation at 5.5-6 per cent by March. RBI can cut rates more aggressively. I expect 100 basis points repo rate cut this year. There could also be a reverse repo rate cut of 50 basis points." It is a positive surprise, primarily led by global commodities and fuel crude prices, he added.

Rajeev Chandrashekhar, president of Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (Ficci), said the decline was much in line with the industry's forecast. "FICCI had forecast this decline during the recent meet with the Prime Minister (because of the global trend of commodity price decline) and have strongly urged that the government and the central bank totally refocus and align fiscal and monetary policy on growth". Analysts are expecting industrial growth to slow down in October as a fallout of the global financial crisis, after a partial recovery in September.

Heading: Malegaon network behind Samjhauta blasts? - Indian Express
Content:
The Tricolour will be on the lunar surface on Friday evening when the Moon Impact Probe (MIP) on board Chandrayaan-I is ejected from the mothership, ISRO chairman G Madhavan Nair told reporters today. This will pave the way for future touchdowns, including manned missions.

Apart from the symbolism that the flag bears, the 35-kg MIP has the scientific objectives of learning and perfecting pin-point accuracy in landing, studying the atmosphere during its descent, and to qualify technologies related to soft landings for moon rovers.

After its journey that started October 22, the main orbiter has zeroed in on the moon at an altitude of 100 km to study its poles through a mission period of two years. The landing would be on the southern pole.

Heading: Andhra's 'healing touch' to 'innocent' Muslims - Indian Express
Content:
The website www.sarvagyapeeth.com flaunts his connections, naming as "advisors" members of political parties, even a music maestro. And Veer Savarkar's daughter-in-law Himani recalls how Mahant Amritanand, head of the Sharda Sarvagya Peeth in Jammu, addressed the Bhopal meeting which elected her president of Abhinav Bharat — she says it was also attended by Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur — and "asked us to work for the Hindu cause".

Mahant Amritanand alias Dayanand Pandey, who was flown from Lucknow to Mumbai on Thursday by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad which is probing the Malegaon blast case, initially wanted former BJP MP (and now VHP member) Baikunth Lal Sharma "Prem" to become the patron of the Pune-based organisation. Prem turned down the offer and Himani was made the Abhinav Bharat chief at a function in Bhopal. Pragya, a former ABVP national executive member, and Ramesh Upadhyay, Sameer Kulkarni and Ajay Rahirkar — the trio associated with Abhinav Bharat — are being questioned by the ATS for their alleged role in the Malegaon blasts.

"He invited me to his Faridabad temple office on January 26 this year and told me about the Abhinav Bharat constitution before requesting me to take over as the Mukhya Sanrakshak (chief patron) of the organisation. I was not keeping well, and after shunning active politics I had joined the VHP, so I declined the offer," Prem told 'The Indian Express'.

A two-term BJP MP, who represented East Delhi in Lok Sabha, Prem quit active politics in 1997 because "all political parties, including the BJP, were in the competitive game of Muslim appeasement". He then devoted himself to what he calls "the cause of Akhand Bharat" after joining the VHP. "The Mahant was impressed by my commitment to Akhand Bharat, and I, in turn, was impressed by his belief in the Sharda Peeth," said Prem. The Mahant is known to hold similar views with "Akhand Bharat" maps dotting his offices.
