Heading: Four lakh heave sigh of relief over forest land decision - Indian Express
Content:
Capability of taking sharper turns makes monorail more flexible option in congested corridors

With the decks being cleared for the country's first monorail project to take off, the monorail idea is catching up fast. Monorail is likely to edge out a couple of metro stretches being planned in the city. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) is thinking of replacing two Metro rail corridors that are part of the Metro rail masterplan with monorail instead.

The two corridors, one between Hutatma Chowk and Ghatkopar (21.8 km) and the other from Ghatkopar to Mulund (12.4 km) are being examined by MMRDA to see if monorail corridors could be a better option, as the two corridors pass through densely populated and congested areas. Monorail is believed to more flexible making it easier for it to make its way through congested areas. The monorail can take sharper turns unlike the metro system.

The 21.8-km Hutatma Chowk-Ghatkopar corridor is part of Phase II of the Metro masterplan, while the Ghatkopar-Mulund corridor is under Phase III of the masterplan chalked out by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation.

According to MMRDA officials, it is being debated whether a monorail or metro rail would suit the corridor which is lengthy as well as congested. "Since it is a densely populated route, monorail is better suited. But there is also a school of thought that says since a higher number of commuters is expected to use longer routes, Metro system could be advisable," a senior MMRDA official revealed on condition of anonymity.

When queried about the proposal to replace the metro corridors with monorail, Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner said: "We're examining the proposal of replacing the two corridors with monorail. No decision has been arrived at, as yet."

An official, who favours the monorail system on the two corridors said, "Monorail is cost-effective. The length and density of the alignments make monorail a better option, as it can take sharper turns unlike the metro rail. We're also exploring if the route could be undertaken on a public-private partnership (PPP) model."

The work on the country's first monorail system on the Jacob Circle-Wadala-Chembur route would commence by February. The 19-km monorail corridor would be built by Malaysian firm Scomi along with Larsen & Toubro.

Heading: 12 months on... undeterred citizens leave clean-up marshals demoralised - Indian Express
Content:
Around four lakh residents living on 'forest lands' are heaving a sigh of relief. Their homes are now safe, with a Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) recommending that all constructions erected before June 2005 be "de-reserved" as forest land after paying the afforestation charges.

The charges recommended for residents is presently pegged at Rs 9 per sq foot.

"This is a welcome move," said Vasant Ganghurde, a flat owner in Emerald Cooperative Housing Society in Mulund's upmarket Highland Park area. He explained, "The earlier suggestion by the state forest department that land on which constructions weer made between 1980 and 2005 be deemed as restored lands had put residents in a fix. We are very happy that the CEC has called for a uniform rule for all constructions till 2005."

On Tuesday, the CEC formally recommended to the Supreme Court that all constructions made before June 22, 2005 be treated on par and that these lands be de-reserved once and for all after levying afforestation charges. It has called for the state to submit a revised scheme to this effect.

According to M K Kar, president of High Park Residents Welfare Association which comprises 18 societies, "An afforestation charge is acceptable as long as our homes are deleted from the reserved land list."

Meanwhile, the state had earlier suggested a concession in the afforestation charges requesting for Rs 40 paise per sq foot.

However, Anmol Bhusan, president of People's Power of Nation (PPN) said, "We are now calling on all people to file new applications as per the CEC's direction. They need to submit their housing details to us with immediate effect so that we can file it with the CEC. In a meeting on Sunday, we will inform all the affected residents to do so."

A resident added that they would later petition the state to press for some concession in afforestation charge, "but we don't want to bring up that issue now."

Heading: Mahindra, Air India split points - Indian Express
Content:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India has reacted strongly to Matthew Hayden's comment about India being a 'Third World' country, saying that the Australian opener's remark was totally uncalled for.

Back home after the 2-0 series defeat, Hayden spoke about, what he perceived, poor ground conditions and inordinate delays during the matches "that happen in Third World countries".

Not to take it lying down, BCCI finance committee chairman Rajiv Shukla lashed out at the Australian for his statement. "This was a completely uncalled for remark by him. A player of his stature should not have made the comment," an angry Shukla said.

"If slow-over rate is your habit, why blame India for that and call India Third World? We are a very prestigious nation and it was not a nice comment by him," Shukla said.

Hayden made a list of things which he felt resulted in Australia's slow over-rates in the series against India.

He alleged the Indian batsmen were reluctant to "face up" quickly enough and there was constant movement around sightscreens.

"They (opposition batsmen) are very difficult to get to face up," Hayden said.

"Often we find ourselves with hands on hips waiting for someone to either face up or someone in the sightboard to move away; all the little frustrations that happen in Third World countries and the heat as well," he added.

Australia were nine overs or 40 minutes behind schedule on the penultimate day of the fourth and final Test in Nagpur, which forced their skipper Ricky Ponting to use part-time spinners instead of pacers at a crucial juncture.

Ponting, who could have been banned for a Test for the slow over-rate, subsequently came under severe criticism for his tactics.

Hayden, however, admitted over-rates have always been a problem for Australia. "We've had trouble with our over rates for a long time now. It's not just us in international cricket that seems to struggle with it for whatever reason," Hayden said.

Heading: Prince of Tides - Indian Express
Content:
Want to see Salvador's watch melting over a tree? The new gallery at the Claridges will show its miniature reproduction, along with Picasso lithographs and Arman's violins

When Gaurav Assomull planned a gallery to showcase European art in Delhi in January, the art mart was still on a high. "There was a boom and everything was selling," says the CEO of Marigold Fine Art. Ten months hence, as he readies for the inauguration of his gallery that will replace the space occupied by Ye Old Bakery at The Claridges hotel, the timing may not seem perfect anymore, with recession seeping in, but Assomull is confident that the collection will find takers. "There is always demand for quality art," beams the 23-year-old, admiring Pablo Picasso's self-portrait in lithographs and Salvador Dali's sculptures in miniature version that will comprise the inaugural exhibition that will begin on November 22.

Among Dali's four limited-edition sculptures are Profile of Time where the watch melts like camembert on a branch and reminds you of his famous painting The Persistence of Memory; and Space Venus where Botticelli's beauty turns into a headless, surreal torso hallucinating about evanescence. The three Picasso lithos from the Portraits Imaginaires series show his vigorous, quirky strokes and. Signed by the master, they are about 65 cm x 75 cm.

Besides the Dalinian world and Pablo gazing at himself will be original works by French-born American artist Arman aka Armand Pierre Fernandez. His violins deconstructed in bronze, including the 2005 Violon Cubiste, come for Rs 8-15 lakh. There will also be original works by four young European artists and an American settled in Europe. The German Jorg Doering's canvases featuring icons like Marilyn Monroe and Audrey Hepburn will occupy one wall, and suspended close to them will be 40-year-old American David Kracov's shadow box images of Warner Bros' characters, including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck. The French sculptor Stephane Cipre, meanwhile, has made Gandhi in metal. At Rs 49 lakh, it the highest priced.

"People may not be familiar with all the artists, but those who come to see the masters will get a chance to look at other works, and might just like them," says Assomull, who spent a year researching the market, collaborating with artists across Europe and getting hands-on experience by working at Bel Air Fine Art Gallery in Geneva. "We did not want to bring anything that might create controversy," adds Assomull.

The Picasso lithographs cost between Rs 5 lakh and 10 lakh, while a miniature reproduction of Dali, authenticated by the Salvador Dali Foundation in Barcelona, is priced at Rs 15-29 lakh. "This is bound to appreciate and I'm willing to buy back a work from anyone who is unhappy with it a year later," says Assomull, who has another exhibition of European art lined up early next year and hopes to expand to Mumbai. "The response during the inaugural show will determine the future course," he smiles. And though Indian art will be absent from the display, the gallerist promises that he will have the artists in attendance for the opening.

Heading: Listening? - Indian Express
Content:
Expect him to do the unexpected. Salman Khan, who enjoys the reputation of being a latecomer, is already parked on a chair outside his vanity van at Mehboob Studio. Dressed in a brown tee, media's favourite bashing boy patiently indulges in elaborate interviews. His staff — secretary, media relations person, bodyguards, tea vendor and assorted "friends" — hang around to ensure his comfort, bringing alive the otherwise deserted studio.

His media friendliness is apparent but he candidly attributes it to his "duty" towards his producers. "With three films ready for release, the producers are on my head to promote them. It isn't that I hate the media. I'm just not the sort who talks. Why talk when a look can convey it all?" he winks. The last two years have been rather unusually quiet for Salman at the box office — he has done special appearances in films by friends and family, each of which carried a thank-you note in the credits. He insists it embarrasses him. "I wish they'd stop," he says, dropping his volume a notch. In the same breath, he stresses that he never does a film for his loved ones if he doesn't like the script.

After teasing his fans with cameos, Khan's next, Yuvvraaj, is one of the biggest releases of the year. Khan affirms that the film's family plot is what made him sign it. "But I'm not a family man yet," he says, his signature sarcasm intact.

This is the first time he is working with director Subhash Ghai. "I thought he'd bore me, pakao me, but he was okay," he smiles mischievously. The actor shares camaraderie with Anil Kapoor, but Zayed Khan had him impressed. "More than shooting, we were partying at each other's expense."

The formal look he sports, designed by Ashley Rebello and sister Alvira Khan, is a sharp contrast to his popular, shirtless avatar, but he doesn't mind that for a change. His sole complaint: "They made me spike my hair blonde." That's only one of Salman's three looks in Yuvvraaj.

"I later pull back my hair as it grows; and then there's this advantage of working with Ghai, he makes his actors wear caps," he laughs. With four releases lined up, 2009 is going to keep Salman, who turns 43 next month, busy. While Main and Mrs Khanna and London Dreams are romantic dramas, Wanted: Dead or Alive and Veer end his hiatus as an action hero after Garv in 2003. "Wanted was painful, there are a lot of gory scenes and all the stunts have been done by me," he says. On a lighter note, there's a sequel to Andaz Apna Apna, a film that never worked at the box office. "It's my favourite but Katrina didn't even smile when she saw it," he adds, disappointed. "I feel sorry for the producer — he must be dying of poverty somewhere."

Heading: Animations, Anyone? - Indian Express
Content:
It's not for publicity—playback singer Sukhwinder says he chose to be on the panel of judges in the second season of Voice of India entirely for the sake of "infuse passion into the participants."

In the city to promote the popular TV show, accompanying programme producer Gajendra Singh and shortlisted candidates, Sukhwinder justified the lack of originality in such shows saying the songs could not be credited entirely to the original singers. "These great songs are also the product of the imagination of great lyricists and composers and surely, these participants will sing them in their own style," he said.

In tandem with the show producer he promised that in future episodes, the participants would be heard singing fresh and numbers penned by Gulzar and composed by Sukhwinder, especially for the programme.

Heading: Mahant changed number 4 times in 20 days, was in touch with Kanpur blast suspects - Indian Express
Content:
Priyanka Chopra - untouched by plastic surgery, uncensored in Fashion and unedited on Dostana

Is looking good and being fit important to you?
Yes.

Have you ever had plastic surgery?
No.

A news channel recently had an interview with a surgeon, with pictures of you before and after you went under his knife. Have you met this doctor?
I found out about that doctor and he is of ill repute. And it's shocking more so because I come from a family of doctors and believe this profession is next to godliness. Sadly, such unethical doctors still practise.

Are you going to sue him?
This time, I will probably take action against him.

This has been a year of mixed fortunes for you.
And I hope to end it on a positive note with Dostana. The movie looks really good, but then I feel this way about all my films.

With the camaraderie between Abhishek Bachchan and John Abraham, did you feel left out?
All the time. They're both so fantastic that I really wish them for each other. Poor Ash and Bipasha.

Shooting in Miami was one long party.
It's been the best outdoor shoot in my entire life. Miami is a mixture of Bombay and Goa — lethargic during the day and lively at night. We even shot at that pace. With seagulls, waves and people skating around, life was a long vacation.

It's Tarun Mansukhani's debut as a director.
He scripted and directed the film and, given that Karan Johar came on the sets only five times, he carried the entire film on his shoulders. The results are fabulous. People at the preview were rolling on the floor laughing; my brother fell off his chair.

You're being pitched for the National Award for Fashion.
I'm a very practical person. It's the biggest honour but I'm not expecting anything because I don't want to be heartbroken.

In an industry dominated by male protagonists, how was it playing a pivotal role in Fashion?
I worked very hard on Meghna Mathur's character. I wanted the physical graph to come across as the character developed. Hence I gradually changed my diet and look for the film. I'm pudgy in the first half, but as the film progresses, I begin to look like a model.

What about your future projects?
I'm looking forward to Ashutosh Gowarikar's What's Your Rashee and Vishal Bhardwaj's Kaminey, which release next year.

Goldie Hawn complimented you in Fashion. Is Hollywood the next step?
Hollywood is not a target, but neither was Bollywood. But I believe I am destiny's child.

Heading: Rajya Sabha election: all 10 candidates elected unopposed - Indian Express
Content:
Mahant Amritanand alias Sudhakar Dwivedi—now called Dayanand Pandey by the Maharashtra ATS—was in constant touch with some suspects in the Kanpur blast case and had changed his mobile phone four times in 20 days to evade the police.

In fact, Dayanand Pandey is the name of a disciple that the mahant used for procuring a SIM card.

The Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of UP Anti-Terror Squad, Rajiv Krishna, said: "Our team had traced Mahant Amritanand's phone number in the course of electronic surveillance of the suspects in the (Kanpur) blast case. He was in constant touch with those people. Meanwhile, the Mumbai ATS team contacted us with the same mobile number to trace the mahant wanted in the Malegaon case."

"Since October 26 (when the Maharashtra ATS passed on the number), we were keeping a watch on him. He went to Gujarat, MP and Rajasthan before coming to Lucknow a week ago. The ATS team led by SSP Rajiv Sabbarwal and Deputy SP Ravindra Singh was watching his moves," the DIG said. He was arrested from Kanpur.

The UP ATS team had been on the trail of 12 persons involved in storing explosives and timer-devices at Rajiv Nagar in Kanpur's Kalyanpur.

With the arrest of the mahant, ATS officers are hopeful of connecting the missing links of the blast that killed two Bajrang Dal activists—Bhupinder Singh Chopra and Rajiv Mishra—on August 24. The ATS has evidence to show that Bhupinder and Rajiv received instructions from the suspects who are yet to be picked up, sources said. The ATS would seek a local court's permission for the interrogation of the suspects soon. Sources said they might interrogate the mahant, too, in the case.

Heading: Khunkhunji murder: Police arrests four, two absconding - Indian Express
Content:
The candidates who had filed their nomination papers for the 10 Rajya Sabha seats from Uttar Pradesh, were elected unopposed on Friday.

They include six candidates of the ruling Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) two of the Samajwadi Party (SP), one of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and one Independent candidate jointly supported by the Congress and the SP.

The announcement to this effect was made by the Returning Officer and the Principal Secretary of state Assembly, Pradeep Dubey. Friday was the last date for withdrawal of the nominations. Since there were only

10 nominations for as many seats to the biennial Rajya Sabha polls, the election, scheduled for November 21, was not required.

The successful candidates are Akhilesh Das, Veer Singh, Brajesh Pathak, Avtar Singh Karimpuri, Rajaram and Brijlal Khaabari of BSP; Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav of SP; BJP's Kusum Rai and Congress-SP joint candidate Mohammad Adeeb.

Compared to its tally of three in the last term, the BSP has sent six candidates to the RS this time.

The SP had four representatives in the last term. For Kusum Rai, Mohammad Adib, Brijesh Pathak, Avatar Singh Karimpuri and Brijlal Khaabri, it will be their first-time entry into the Upper House of the Parliament.

SP's general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav will enjoy his second term in the RS after a gap of one term during which he was elected to Lok Sabha from Sambhal in Uttar Pradesh. Brajesh Pathak, a sitting Lok Sabha BSP parliamentarian from Unnao, was chosen by Chief Minister Mayawati for Rajya Sabha.

Mohammad Adib, the former Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) students' union president, will make his debut in the Rajya Sabha from Uttar Pradesh.

His candidature is seen as a rallying point for the proposed SP-Congress alliance in the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls.

The Rajya Sabha members, whose term ends on November 25, are BJP president Rajnath Singh, Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi (BJP), Amar Singh, Shahid Siddiqui, Abu Asim Azmi and Uday Pratap Singh (all SP), Veer Singh, Isam Singh and Gandhi Azad (both BSP) and Akhilesh Das (Congress).

Of these Amar Singh, Veer Singh and Akhilesh Das have been renominated while Rajnath Singh and Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi have been declared Lok Sabha candidates from Ghaziabad and Rampur respectively.

The Winners
Akhilesh Das, Veer Singh, Brajesh Pathak, Avtar Singh Karimpuri, Rajaram and Brijlal Khaabari of BSP; Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav of SP; BJP's Kusum Rai and Congress-SP joint candidate Mohammad Adeeb

Heading: IIIT-A out to save Sangam from hazards of pollution - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of four persons on Friday, the Lucknow police claims to have solved the murder and robbery at the residence of Om Prakash Agarwal, owner of Khunkhunji Jewellers, on November 5.

Receiving a tip-off that the miscreants involved were coming to Musabagh, police said they combed the area and arrested the accused. The stolen goods were recovered from them as well.

Those arrested have been identified as the kingpin Ram Nath, Vikas Yadav, Raju Yadav and Balendra Pratap Singh.

A massive hunt has been launched to trace the other accused — identified as Harish Shankar Kashyap alias Anna and Ram Khelawan.

On the fateful night, the burglars broke into Agarwal's house through a rear window. Entering the room where Agarwal and his wife Usha Rani (65) were sleeping, they began to ransack it.

The noise woke Usha and when she tried to stop them, they beat her up and fled with some jewellery and cash.

Usha Rani was taken to the CSMMU Trauma Centre, where she succumbed to her injuries. Agarwal immediately called up a senior policeman, who rushed to the site. While searching near the house, the police spotted some persons running. Asked to stop, one of them fired at the police. In retaliation, the police also fired back, killing one of them — the man was identified later as Babloo alias Prem Nath.

The police said while looking into the details of Babloo, they kept a watch on the people who were in touch with him. "We had sent teams to several districts including Unnao, Hardoi, Sitapur and Kanpur to trace their whereabouts," said Vinay Chandra, Circle Officer, Chowk.

During interrogation, Balendra revealed to the police that last month, Babloo and Harish had decided to rob the Agarwal house. They went to Ram Nath Yadav's residence and told him about their plan.

After committing the crime, they went back to Yadav's residence and left the major portion of the booty there. "Before leaving the house, each of them carried small portions of their share," said a senior police officer.

Heading: Former MLA detained for ‘duping’ trader - Indian Express
Content:
With Ganga being accorded the national heritage status, the Indian Institute of Information Technology-Allahabad (IIIT-A) has come out to save Sangam — the confluence of Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati in Allahabad.

Playing the role of a vigilante vanguard, the IIIT-A is all set to take up the cause of pollution in Ganga and Yamuna and their banks by monitoring the environment prevalent at Sangam.

Under a massive exercise, a IIIT-A team will install sensitive cutting-edge instruments at strategic locations in and around Sangam to measure the level of pollution. This initiative comes under the ambitious Rs 6 crore project, which is being undertaken by the Indo-Swiss Centre of Microelectronics. The centre was recently established in the institute campus.

"Sangam has played an important role in both the Indian history and the religious beliefs of Indians. Over the years, due to various factors, the site has been severely polluted," said M D Tiwari, Director, IIIT-A.

"The area has been affected due to indiscriminate pouring of untreated wastes. This has also created an adverse impact on the lives of the marine plants and fishes," he added.

The team will be installing equipments like Air-Soil Temperature Sensors and Soil Moisture Sensors, Bio-sensors and studying the water samples from different areas within the specified zone to zero down the problem, which needs immediate attention. The team will be installing equipments like Air-Soil Temperature Sensors and Soil Moisture Sensors, Bio-sensors and studying the water samples from different areas within the specified zone to zero down the problem, which needs immediate attention. We will be taking the help of Swiss experts, too, in the project. The report of the project will be submitted to the Centre for necessary actions, Dr Tiwari said. 

A team of faculty members and researchers will start their work with special focus on site management within this week. "We have already formed a team comprising researchers and deputed faculty members including Dr Anurika Vaish and Dr Shishu Varma. I will be personally involved in the project," said Tiwari.

Heading: In front of cops, BSP leaders come to blows over cattle - Indian Express
Content:
Former Bharatiya Janata party MLA Prem Prakash Tiwari was detained on Friday in connection with a criminal case registered against him with the Hazratganj police in January.

A Muzaffarnagar-based businessman, Subhash Kulshreshtha, had accused Tiwari of breach of trust (Section 406 of the IPC) and issuing threats to life (Section 506).

A three-time MLA from Domariganj constituency in Siddharth Nagar, Tiwari was picked up from his Lucknow residence in the Narahi area.

According to the police, in September 2007, Tiwari had approached Kulshreshtha and told him he was interested in selling his petrol pump located in Domariganj.

"The case records state the deal was finalised at Rs 80 lakh. Kulshreshtha paid Rs 30 lakh as agreement money. After receiving the money, Tiwari started making excuses and did not finalise the deal. Finally, Kulshreshtha lodged an FIR in January," said Inspector (Hazratganj police station) Ajeet Singh Chauhan. "We had picked up Prem Prakash to cross-check the details of the FIR," he added.

Heading: To ease traffic, outer ring roads for Varanasi, Kanpur soon - Indian Express
Content:
First it was a case of alleged shooting, then a scuffle at the police station: the dispute was over cattle and the combatants — Bahujan Samaj Party legislators Kadir Rana and Shahnawaj Rana.

Kadir is Shahnawaj's uncle. And though they came to blows on Friday before the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) of Muzaffarnagar, no complaint was lodged.

Muzaffarnagar legislator Kadir was not available for comments.

Bijnore legislator Shahnawaj alleged that his uncle indulged in the fracas and his (Kadir's) younger brother shot at him.

Senior Superintendent of Police B D Paulson said: "There was no serious issue between them. They had a dispute over share of the cattle, which led to an argument. Both of them had approached me seeking an intervention."

Shahnawaj said his father died in his childhood and his uncle did not give him due share in the family property.

A few days ago, the family members decided to divide the cattle, which led to the dispute.

The Bijnore MLA said: "Around 12.30 pm on Friday, I was about to leave for my constituency, when Kadir and his relatives hurled expletives at me."

"When I resisted them, Kadir's brother Noor Salim alias Pappu opened fire at me but I escaped, as the bullet missed the target," he added.

Shahnawaj said he reached the Senior Superintendent of Police office to register his complaint, but Kadir was already there. The duo again entered into a scuffle before the SSP also.

Heading: Allahabad’s top cop, colleague on CID search list - Indian Express
Content:
The National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) is on its way to develop the outer ring roads along the periphery of four big cities of the state — Varanasi, Kanpur, Aligarh and Meerut.

The objective behind the project is to prevent traffic congestions in these cities by providing alternate circular routes. According to officials, the surroundings rural areas will also benefit once the roads become functional.

"The outer ring roads will be developed on a Public Private Partnership (PPP) model under Phase VII of National Highways Development Programme (NHDP)," said M K Jain, Project Director NHAI, UP unit.

The highway authorities have already invited bids to conduct a feasibility study in the four cities. While the tender process to engage companies to study the feasibility will be completed by December, the study is expected to be completed in the next six months.

"The process for selection of companies to conduct the feasibility study is underway. After the study, the companies will also prepare the detailed project reports (DPR) for the four projects," Jain said.

He added that on the basis of the feasibility study report and DPRs, NHAI will fix the configuration of alignments — its length and width, locations of the flyovers, railway overbridges and bridges that will be developed along the ring roads.

About the necessity of outer ring roads in the four cities, Jain said: "Aligarh, Varanasi, Kanpur and Meerut are fast growing cities and traffic problems are increasing day by day. Outer ring roads will provide an alternate route to the heavy traffic to bypass the city congestion."

"The companies will themselves acquire the land for construction purpose and bear the cost of the projects. They will run the project until they realise their expenditure. Later, they will transfer the project to the government for future operations," an NHAI official said.

Both state, Centre to work on outer ring road for Lucknow
Along with Kanpur, Varanasi, Meerut and Aligarh, the Centre has approved a proposal for an outer ring road for Lucknow also. The project has been under the Integrated Urban Rejuvenation Plan (IURP) scheme. Development of an outer ring road in Lucknow is already proposed in Lucknow Masterplan-2021 and Lucknow Development Authority Board has given its nod for the project. The road will be developed on the PPP model. "The length of outer ring road in Lucknow will be about 120 km and will cost approximately Rs 2,500 crore. But as this outer ring road is common in NHDP and IURP, the Centre and the state government are holding discussions to decide their share of responsibilities in the project," said NHAI (UP) Project Director M K Jain said.

Heading: Insult to prof: students blame varsity for expulsion - Indian Express
Content:
For a fortnight, a hunt is on for two policemen accused of helping a former BJP legislator illegally occupy the home of a liquor trader.

N K Singh, Circle Officer of Allahabad city and Sub-Inspector S K Singh, in-charge of Bundu Katra outpost in Agra, were indicted by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

Following the agency investigation, a Mainpuri court had issued non-bailable warrants against them two weeks ago. To trace them, the agency has even sent letters to the police chiefs of the districts concerned, but to no avail.

In January 2001, NK Singh was in-charge of Kotwali police station in Mainpuri, where SK Singh also worked.

The house in question belonged to Bharat Singh Chauhan, who registered an FIR against eight persons — including Updesh Singh Chauhan, a legislator of the ruling BJP government.

"I was out of station, when Updesh Singh and his aides came to my house and damaged the property. Showing fake documents to the women, they claimed they had purchased the house," said Bharat.

His brother, advocate Veer Bahadur Singh Chauhan, said: "The miscreants had managed to take possession of the house. We called the police but instead of helping us, they threatened us."

It was only after the locals began a protest, the police registered a case against eight persons including the legislator. "Considering that the police will not be interested in solving the case, I requested the state government to get the investigation done by an impartial agency," said Veer Bahadur.

The CID began its investigation in August 2001 and chargesheeted all eight persons named in the FIR. Moreover, it was found that the two policemen were protecting the accused, "so a case was also registered against them," said Inspector S P Tomar, Investigating Officer of the CID. The agency requested the government for sanction to prosecute the policemen, which they received in October.

As regrads the agency's letters, asking the district police chiefs to suspend the guilty officers, arrest them and produce them before the court, Superintendent of Police, Allahabad, A M Jain, confirmed that he had received the letter. Agra SP Prem Prakash said, "I will check the records that whether we have received any such letter or not."

S K Singh said, "We were falsely booked in the case. We did our job with honesty and did not support anyone." N K Singh was not available for comments. Public prosecutor Ram Prakash Pal said, "the other accused, including Upendra Singh, are currently out on bail."

Heading: Lucknow to host a fortnight forum for abandoned children - Indian Express
Content:
Three student leaders of the Allahabad University, who were recently expelled for insulting A K Srivastava — a faculty member — accused the university proctor and chief examination controller of asking them to humiliate Registrar Firdaus Wani and Srivastava.

On Wednesday, the three students — Dinesh Singh Yadav, Umendra Pratap Singh and Abhyuday Tripathi — along with Praveer Kumar Shukla, another student, were expelled for humiliating

Srivastava on June 10. Srivastava was a faculty member of the university's chemistry department.

Barring Shukla, the others held a press conference over the issue on Friday.

According to them, Chief Proctor Jatashankar Tripathi and Examination Controller Professor H S Upadhyay had assured them of all support if they insulted Wani and Srivastava.

"We did what we were told to do. We went to the chemistry department and raised slogans against the professor and the registrar. A few other students sent by Upadhyay assaulted and insulted the professor," said Dinesh.

Tending a joint public apology to Srivastava, Umendra Pratap Singh said: "When we pressed the chief proctor and the examination controller to save us from expulsion, they backtracked and served us the expulsion notice on Wednesday. We have now started a campaign against them by submitting a memorandum to the Union human resource minister and the governor in regard to financial irregularities."

Examination Controller H S Upadhyay, however, refuted the allegations.

"The charges are baseless and purported to tarnish the image of not only the authorities but also of the institution," he said.

Heading: Three killed in Etah district - Indian Express
Content:
Children's issues will now find a voice every fortnight in the city. The Media For Children and UNICEF jointly organised the first Children's Hour, a fortnight platform to bring the media and the organisations working for children together, at the Uttar Pradesh Press Club on Friday.

The participants discussed the problems of abandoned children, as four organisations shared their experiences.

Anshumali Sharma of Childline, a 24X7 helpline for children in distress, said according to our records, 16 newborn babies have been abandoned this year. "It is depressing to see an abandoned newborn. We cannot trace their homes and send them back because they were abandoned either they were girls or born out of an illegitimate relationship," said Sharma.

Shachi Singh of Ehsaas, an organisation working for children living on railway platforms, said the Juvenile Justice Act should be implemented properly to ensure that every child living in difficult circumstances receives a protected environment.

"Child welfare committees and Juvenile Justice Board should be constituted in all districts," said Singh.

Sapna Upadhyaya of Ishwar Child Welfare Foundation shared her experiences of dealing with poor children, whose parents cannot afford their treatment. Dr Brijeetha VV of the Lucknow Child Welfare Committee informed about what the committee is doing for the children in distress.

Heading: Hayden angers BCCI with ‘Third World’ remark - Indian Express
Content:
Britain's Andy Murray ousted defending champion Roger Federer from the Masters Cup, rallying for a 4-6, 7-6 (3), 7-5 victory on Friday.

Federer, a four-time winner of the season-ending tournament, appeared bothered in the third set by a sore back that forced him to withdraw during the Paris Masters two weeks ago. The Swiss star received treatment three times on Friday but refused to quit.

Federer saved seven match points while serving at 4-5, before Murray converted two games later, breaking when Federer sent a forehand long. "A win over Roger Federer means almost as much as winning the Masters Cup to me," Murray said. "He's the best player of all time. He's still playing great. I know I'm going to be tired tomorrow, but this match meant a lot to me."

Murray, who had his left hand iced during one of Federer's time-outs, will play Russia's Nikolay Davydenko in the semi-finals. Federer's loss allowed France's Gilles Simon to advance. He will meet Serbia's Novak Djokovic.

The ninth game of the third set lasted 17 minutes and went to deuce 10 times. Federer fended off the last of the seven match points with an ace, then blasted another before Murray sent a forehand long. "When you play against Roger, you got to expect him to play some great stuff, especially when he's behind," Murray said. "He hit a couple of aces, a couple of big forehands. I missed a couple of returns I maybe shouldn't have."

Federer tried to force a tiebreaker, but committed three forehand errors while serving at 15-15. Murray, who came in as one of the few players with a winning record against Federer at 3-2, already had clinched a spot in the last four from the Red Group. But he lived up to his promise not to take it easy, wanting to avoid the prospect of facing Federer again if both were to make the final.

Crowd favourite

Federer was trying to repeat last year's feat of coming back after losing his opening-round match. The atmosphere was more akin to a final than the last match of group play. The Qi Zhong stadium was packed, and while the crowd overwhelmingly favoured Federer, Murray has won over a lot of fans in his debut here. They all got their money's worth, with plenty of drama and great tennis.

The two players exchanged breaks in the middle of the first set. Then, with Murray serving at 4-5, Federer broke at love. Murray broke in the opening game of the second set, then again to pull ahead 5-2.

He had double set point while serving in the next game, only to see Federer rally to break. The Swiss star had triple breakpoint with Murray serving again for the set at 5-4. Murray forced deuce, but Federer whacked a clean forehand winner to set up another break chance, and Murray double-faulted to make it 5-5. Federer rallied from a 3-1 deficit in the tiebreaker to level, but Murray ran off the last four points.

Simon earlier beat Radek Stepanek 6-1, 6-4 in what was essentially a meaningless match because Federer controlled his own destiny - win and he was through, lose and go home.

"It was easier tonight because my match was not really important," said the ninth-ranked Simon, who got in when a sore knee forced top-ranked Rafael Nadal to pull out of the season-ending tournament before it began. (AP)

Bjorkman bids adieu

Jonas Bjorkman brought the curtains down on his 17-year career in professional tennis after bowing out of the Masters Cup doubles on Friday. The 36-year-old Swede, who won nine Grand Slam doubles titles and was once ranked number four in the world in singles, had announced at Wimbledon this year that he would retire at the end of the season.

"It's great to end my career in the biggest event of the year, even if I would have liked to have gone further. But you can't have everything," he told reporters after he and Zimbabwean partner Kevin Ullyett were beaten 6-2, 1-6, 10-6 by Poles Mariusz Fyrstenberg and Marcin Matkowski.

Bjorkman won a total of $14,567,823 in prize money over his career and three Davis Cups with his country in 1994, 1997, and 1998.

Bjorkman, who is going to dedicate his time to editing a Swedish tennis magazine, said he would miss the locker room banter but not the constant travel of the tour. "I think the umpires are not going to miss me, he said. I've been quite tough on those guys."

Heading: Murray dumps federer - Indian Express
Content:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India has reacted strongly to Matthew Hayden's comment about India being a 'Third World' country, saying that the Australian opener's remark was totally uncalled for.

Back home after the 2-0 series defeat, Hayden spoke about, what he perceived, poor ground conditions and inordinate delays during the matches "that happen in Third World countries".

Not to take it lying down, BCCI finance committee chairman Rajiv Shukla lashed out at the Australian for his statement. "This was a completely uncalled for remark by him. A player of his stature should not have made the comment," an angry Shukla said.

"If slow-over rate is your habit, why blame India for that and call India Third World? We are a very prestigious nation and it was not a nice comment by him," Shukla said.

Hayden made a list of things which he felt resulted in Australia's slow over-rates in the series against India.

He alleged the Indian batsmen were reluctant to "face up" quickly enough and there was constant movement around sightscreens.

"They (opposition batsmen) are very difficult to get to face up," Hayden said.

"Often we find ourselves with hands on hips waiting for someone to either face up or someone in the sightboard to move away; all the little frustrations that happen in Third World countries and the heat as well," he added.

Australia were nine overs or 40 minutes behind schedule on the penultimate day of the fourth and final Test in Nagpur, which forced their skipper Ricky Ponting to use part-time spinners instead of pacers at a crucial juncture.

Ponting, who could have been banned for a Test for the slow over-rate, subsequently came under severe criticism for his tactics.

Hayden, however, admitted over-rates have always been a problem for Australia. "We've had trouble with our over rates for a long time now. It's not just us in international cricket that seems to struggle with it for whatever reason," Hayden said.

Heading: Brotherhood of Gaiety - Indian Express
Content:
Priyanka Chopra - untouched by plastic surgery, uncensored in Fashion and unedited on Dostana

Is looking good and being fit important to you?
Yes.

Have you ever had plastic surgery?
No.

A news channel recently had an interview with a surgeon, with pictures of you before and after you went under his knife. Have you met this doctor?
I found out about that doctor and he is of ill repute. And it's shocking more so because I come from a family of doctors and believe this profession is next to godliness. Sadly, such unethical doctors still practise.

Are you going to sue him?
This time, I will probably take action against him.

This has been a year of mixed fortunes for you.
And I hope to end it on a positive note with Dostana. The movie looks really good, but then I feel this way about all my films.

With the camaraderie between Abhishek Bachchan and John Abraham, did you feel left out?
All the time. They're both so fantastic that I really wish them for each other. Poor Ash and Bipasha.

Shooting in Miami was one long party.
It's been the best outdoor shoot in my entire life. Miami is a mixture of Bombay and Goa — lethargic during the day and lively at night. We even shot at that pace. With seagulls, waves and people skating around, life was a long vacation.

It's Tarun Mansukhani's debut as a director.
He scripted and directed the film and, given that Karan Johar came on the sets only five times, he carried the entire film on his shoulders. The results are fabulous. People at the preview were rolling on the floor laughing; my brother fell off his chair.

You're being pitched for the National Award for Fashion.
I'm a very practical person. It's the biggest honour but I'm not expecting anything because I don't want to be heartbroken.

In an industry dominated by male protagonists, how was it playing a pivotal role in Fashion?
I worked very hard on Meghna Mathur's character. I wanted the physical graph to come across as the character developed. Hence I gradually changed my diet and look for the film. I'm pudgy in the first half, but as the film progresses, I begin to look like a model.

What about your future projects?
I'm looking forward to Ashutosh Gowarikar's What's Your Rashee and Vishal Bhardwaj's Kaminey, which release next year.

Goldie Hawn complimented you in Fashion. Is Hollywood the next step?
Hollywood is not a target, but neither was Bollywood. But I believe I am destiny's child.

Heading: 3 more vector-borne deaths - Indian Express
Content:
When the Contemporary Art (ARCO) fair opens in Madrid on February 11, India will be on display as the guest country. The director of ARCO, Lourdes Fernández, announced in Delhi that there would be a special section, Panorama for India, which would be curated by artist Bose Krishnamachari. "We have always been open to emerging art," said Fernandez. While South Korea was the guest country in 2007, it was Brazil in 2008. Fernández said she liked the works of Jitish Kallat and Shilpa Gupta, though she had yet to go deep into Indian art.

"It is a great opportunity for India and the Indian panorama has around 9,000 square feet to showcase the works," said Krishnamachari. There will be 13 Indian galleries, including Bodhi Art, Chemould Prescott, Gallery Espace and Nature Morte. There will also be a separate space for Bose to showcase a few of his favourite artists, like Ravinder Reddy and Riyas Komu. Apart from Indian galleries, there will be over 250 galleries from around the world, with 79 from Spain.

But with the market meltdown, even the Frieze Art Fair in London had seen a dip in the sales. No stranger to the economic crisis, Fernandez said, "The economic meltdown has touched us all but we are in the same position as other fairs such as Miami and Basel." Warding off fears of a lukewarm response, Krishnamachari said, "Keeping this in mind, we have suggested a limited number of artists to the galleries, with a mix of new talent and established names to balance the show." Let's wait for the Spanish show.

Heading: 3 children missing from New Alipore - Indian Express
Content:
While authorities debate the domicile of victims, three more persons died of vector-borne diseases in the state on Friday. While one person died in Kolkata, two others succumbed to the diseases in Howrah and South 24 Parganas.

Kishore Roy, a resident of 47/2A, Nandaram Sen Street in Ward 9, died at a nursing home on Friday morning. He was admitted to the nursing home on Thursday. According to his relatives, Roy was suffering from high fever for the last three days.

Chief Municipal Health Officer (CMHO) Deb Dwaipayan Chattopadhay claimed that Roy was a resident of Bihar and was suffering from various other diseases.

"He was infected with malaria in Bihar but died in Kolkata. He has several other complications and malaria is not only the reason of his death," he added.

Local councillor Mahua Mallik said: "He was a resident of Kolkata. He went to Bihar on some business. There he was taken ill and returned home. After reaching Kolkata, he was detected with malaria."

Blood tests conducted at a local malaria health clinic confirmed the presence of plasmodium falciparum in Roy's blood. The death takes the toll of vector-borne diseases in the city, including 'unknown fever' deaths, to over 30.

In Howrah, a Lakshmi Kanta Hazra (41) died of malaria on Friday morning. Hazra, a resident of Haat Lane in Ward 27 of the Howrah Municipal Corporation, had been suffering from high fever for several days and was admitted to a nursing home. Blood test confirmed the presence of malarial parasite in his blood.

CMHO, Howrah, Dilip Deb said the locals had not informed him about the spread of malaria. "We are now looking into the matter," he added.

In South 24 Parganas, Amar Patra (35), a resident of Kulpi, died of dengue in the SSKM hospital. He had been suffering from high fever for the last few days. The blood report confirmed the presence of the dengue germ. CMHO Sachhidananda Sarkar, however, said, "I am yet to receive the reports of the health centre, where the blood sample of the deceased was tested."

Son of CM's domestic help contracts malaria
The son of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's domestic help has been diagnosed with malaria and the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) officials are feeling the heat.

After Arabinda Haldar, son of Champamani Haldar, was detected with falciparum malaria on Friday, the officials started receiving several phone calls from the CM's secretariat asking them to send a special team to the area. At present, Haldar is being treated in a local malaria clinic.

A special team soon reached the place and began fumigation.

The team included borough health executive Durjai Das and vector control officer Debashis Biswas.

It was a special visit, as the special vector control work was not scheduled in the area on November 14.

The incident also confirms that while the entire city is in the grip of the vector-borne diseases, the vector control department of the KMC remains nonfunctional.

A department official said, "we conduct vector-control operations only by special requests or orders by dignitaries like chief minister, chief justice and chief secretary."

Heading: Woman slaps constable at Nandan, arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Three children of a family went missing from their homes at Mondal Temple Lane in New Alipore on Thursday. The children, aged between six and ten years, had gone out to play on Thursday, but did not return.

On Thursday afternoon, Vishal (10), Ram Kumar (6) and Rahul (8) had headed as usual for the nearaby playground.

"We did not pay much attention when they left. But they did not return," said their grandfather Jaynarayan Ray.

Jaynarayan, an employee of Roof Engineers Private Limited, was at home on Thursday.

It was not until late afternoon that the family suspected that something was wrong.

"We began a search after the children did not return after dusk," said Jaynarayan. But even after hours of searching, the trio was not found. "A local shopkeeper told us that the children were last seen going towards railway station," he added.

The family filed a missing complaint at the New Alipore police station on Friday night. "I don't know where the children could have gone. They were good students and I don't see a reason why they would leave the house," Jaynarayan said. There were no ransom calls either. "We are not rich, so it is unlikely that someone would have kidnapped our children for money. I also do not have enmity with anyone," said Jaynarayan.

"We believe they might have lost their way and are wandering around the city," he added. According to the police, all the nearby police stations have been alerted. "A hunt is on for the missing children," said a police officer of the New Alipore police station.

While Ram and Rahul are the students of Sishu Vidya Mandir in New Alipore, Vishal is a Class IV student of Adarsh Vidyalaya in Charu Market.

Heading: Cong seeks Gandhi’s intervention in Lalgarh crisis - Indian Express
Content:
Irritated by the heightened security in the Nandan premises, a woman allegedly slapped an on-duty constable and was subsequently arrested. Stopped from entering the cinema hall with a laptop, police said she even used foul language.

On Friday morning, Anupam Mukherjee, a constable of the Special Branch of Kolkata police, was on duty at the gates of Nandan, where the 14th Kolkata film festival is going on.

Chayanika Chakraborty, a resident of Dhakuria, had come to Nandan with her husband to watch a film. Around 9:10 am, when the couple tried to enter Nandan, Mukherjee stopped them. Chakraborty was carrying a laptop and she was asked her to leave it outside or not enter the grounds owing to security reasons. She requested the police to keep the laptop in the police outpost while she watched the film. She would collect it later, she said.

But the police refused to keep the laptop in their custody. An altercation ensued and during it, Chakraborty's husband's mobile fell onto the ground. She then allegedly slapped the constable.

"The woman said the constable on duty had snatched off her husband's mobile and thrown it on the ground," said an officer of Hastings police station. Mukherjee, on his part, filed a complaint at the local police station and Chakraborty was arrested from the Nandan premises sometime later.

"We had booked her under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC)," said Nakul Rajak, additional officer-in-charge of Hastings police station. She was produced before a city court and was later released on bail, the officer added.

Heading: An accomplished minister, lawyer and actor - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress has requested Governor Gopal Krishna Gandhi to intervene in the Lalgarh crisis. Congress Legislative Party leader Manas Bhuniya led a team of party MLAs and leaders and met the governor on Friday.

"We requested the governor to talk to the chief minister and the tribal leaders. He has promised to do his best to restore normalcy in the area," said Bhuniya.

The Congress also claimed that the tribal agitation is not controlled by Maoists. "We know some Maoists are involved with the tribal protest. But this is a movement of the local tribals and not of Maoists," said Bhuniya.

"The state government is trying to label it as a Maoist movement but no political party is involved in it," he added.

The Congress leader further said: "The police and the state administration have failed to handle the situation in Lalgarh. Tribals were subjected to atrocities in the area."

The CPM, meanwhile, said the police action in Lalgarh after the Salboni blast was not directed against the tribals.

State secretary Biman Bose said: "The blast in Salboni was planned. The police were only trying to find out the accused and maintain law and order."

Heading: All not well for children, remind experts on Nov 14 - Indian Express
Content:
Former Union minister and Congress leader Ajit Panja passed away after a prolonged illness at a private hospital around 4.30 am on Friday. He was 72 and was suffering from cancer. He is survived by a son and daughter.

The President, the Prime Minister, the chief minister and scores of other leaders expressed their condolence over his death. A pall of gloom descended over entire north Kolkata, home to this charismatic leader.

A former Congressmen, Panja had recently distanced himself from politics, especially from the Trinamool Congress, of which he was one of the founders. Besides being a master politician, he was a successful barrister and an acclaimed actor.

A six-time MP and a minister in the governments of Rajiv Gandhi, PV Narasimha Rao and Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Panja quit the Congress to form the Trinamool Congress with Mamata Banerjee in 1997.

He had a very warm relationship with Banerjee for four years.

Relations between the two soured after she suspended him from the Trinamool in July 2001. Panja again joined the Congress. Banerjee, however, revoked his suspension in 2003 and Panja was back in the Trinamool.

Close associates of Panja say he was neither with the Trinamool nor the Congress.

But after his death, even leaders like Somen Mitra could not hold back their tears. While Congress leaders sent condolence messages, Banerjee visited the hospital where Panja breathed his last.

An able administrator, Panja began the Metro Channel for the Kolkata Doordarshan during his stint as the Union information and broadcasting minister.

He improved the reach of Doordarshan in the northeast states. He was also instrumental in introducing mega serials and various entertainment programmes that changed the face of Doordarshan. Later, he successfully handled other portfolios at the Centre, including foreign affairs, revenue and coal.

Panja's ancestral home was in Burdwan. But he spent most of his time in Kolkata. Son of a renowned doctor, he studied law in London after graduating from the Scottish Church College in Kolkata. He married his wife Jaya at the age of 24.

He became the state Congress president in 1980 and won the Kolkata northeast parliamentary constituency in 1984. He was the MP from the constituency for six consecutive terms.

Panja was also interested in acting. His acting skills were lauded by many.

He also had an occasion to meet Saddam Hussein and Bill Clinton.

A great political organiser, even hardened Opposition leaders, including those of the Left, saluted his organising skill. After sending greetings cards to eminent voters of his area, he personally called up to inquire whether the cards had reached or not. That was his way of maintaining good vibes with his voters.

Heading: Mamata to take up PTTI issue, says govt deceived students - Indian Express
Content:
Childern's Day was observed in the city and its suburbs with schools holding special programmes and distributing gifts to children on Friday.

"I know Children's Day is celebrated to comemorate the birth annivarsary of Chacha Nehru, who used to love children," said ten-year-old Shweta Das. Shweta and her eight-year-old sister Sonali were excited about the chocolates and biscuits that they were to receive from their teacher.

Even as Children's Day was celebrated with fervour, child experts, health practitioners and child psychiatrists highlighted some child-related issues which need to be addressed soon.

According to the third National Family Health Survey conducted under the aegis of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, in the last five years West Bengal has registered the infant mortality rate of 48 per 1,000 live births. The survey report says that 43.5 per cent of children under the age of three years are underweight, while 69.4 per cent of children (between 6-35 months) suffer from anaemia.

While according to the 2001 census, India has more than 12.6 million child workers, NGOs put the figure between 35 and 60 million.

"In West Bengal, gender disparity in quality education and malnutrition are two most important issues which need immediate attention by the government," said a state government official.

NGOs claim that the increasing number of nuclear families with working parents has led to an increase in the cases of juvenile delinquents, who suffer from behavioural problems.

"Working parents do not spend quality time with their children," said Manabendra Nath Ray of Save the Children, an NGO. Child experts believe that societal changes have led to more cases of insecurity, delinquency and decline of values among children.

"We often hear children killing other children out of jealousy, something that was unheard of before. We recommend schools and parents to carry out regular counselling of children and guide them towards a better future," said Ray.

From the health perspective, paediatric dermatology and diabetes among children have been major causes of concern for doctors. On the occasion, the Indian Society for Paediatric Dermatology (ISDP) has decided to hold a two-day conference from Saturday to address their concerns.

Doctors claim that diseases like atopic dermatitis (a kind of allergy), hand foot mouth and viral infections are prevalent among children.

"Cases of diseases like dengue, paedieculosis and AIDS are increasing among children. Of total reported cases of dengue in the state, almost 50 per cent are children," said Sandipan Dhar, a paediatric dermatologist.

"We are also concerned about allergic diseases due to stress and anxiety among children," he added.

Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, meanwhile, attended a function organised by the Bustee Welfare Centre, an organisation providing education and social services to nearly 500 underprivileged children in the city. The Governor is the chief patron of the organisation.

Gandhi also spent some time interacting with the children. He asked them about the significance of Children's Day and later explained to them the importance of the day. Gandhi also joined the children in singing Saare Jahaan Se Achha.

Those who could not sing the song more than two lines, the Governor told them that they should memorise it before his next visit.

Heading: Now, non-teaching staff leads protest at BESU - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee said like Singur and Nandigram, she will also take up the cause of the Primary Teachers Training Institute (PTTI) and fight till the end. Accusing the state government for deceiving PTTI students, Banerjee assured them all help.

On Friday, a delegation of PTTI students met Banerjee. "The state government will have to employ all the students who are waiting with degrees and conduct examinations for those who still have not taken their exams," she said.

Along with PTTI students, the Trinamool chief will take part in a protest rally at Metro Channel on November 29. She has asked the students to meet Kalyan Banerjee, a Trinamool leader and also a noted lawyer, with the necessary documents to examine the legality of the issue.

Banerjee has also assured the students that she will write to the Ministry of Human Resources and Development. She has also asked Leader of Opposition Partha Chhatterjee to inform Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi regarding the issue.

"We have approached Mamata with two demands — to join our protest and ask the Centre to resolve the issue as early as possible. She has agreed to both," said Ashok Rudra, a PTTI student leader and a part of the delegation that met Banerjee.

Earlier, the PTTI students had met CPM state Secretary Biman Bose and Congress leaders Pranab Mukherjee and Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi over the deadlock.

The PTTI students have renewed their agitation after the Calcutta High Court had declared that the certificates of the students who had graduated from the 122 PTTIs as "invalid", as they had not followed the norms of the National Council of Teachers Education.

Heading: Transport dept to shift  Esplanade bus terminus - Indian Express
Content:
Though the undergraduate students of the Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) have been asked to vacate the campus, peace still eludes the 150-year-old institution.

The non-teaching staff of the university has launched protests now. The staff began a sit-in-demonstration in front of the BESU building from Friday morning.

They were protesting against the decision of the board of management to seek approval from the state higher education department for the absorption of the non-teaching staff under the university services rules.

The employees have threatened to go on a strike if their demands are not met. The 450 non-teaching employees receive their salary according to two different scales. Nearly 265 employees are paid as per the university grades and the remaining as per the scale of the state government.

Although the BESU was upgraded from a government college to a deemed university in 1993, nearly 184 non-teaching employees have continued their services as employees of a government college instead of being absorbed by the university. A few months ago, the higher education department had issued an order directing the university to offer the employees an option of either switching over to the university services or continue with the state government rules.

"The university is delaying the issue. When the state government has already given its nod, why it is seeking further approval?," said a non-teaching staff.

Four organisations, State Government Employees Federation (Unified), Besu Employees Association, Paschim Banga Nimnatama Sarkari Karmachari Samity and West Bengal Minstreal Officers Association have joined the protest.

Heading: JU students bring out their exam schedule - Indian Express
Content:
In compliance with a High Court order, the state transport department has decided to shift the bus terminus from Esplanade.

Transport Secretary Sumantra Chaudhury said on Friday that his department had already earmarked an area of 11 acres located in a wetland on EM Bypass for the new terminus.

He added the department had also approached the East Calcutta Wetland Management Authorities, seeking approval for the project. If the wetland authority does not okay the project, the department will then have to approach the High Court for permission.

While delivering an order in the Save Victoria case, the Calcutta High Court had directed the state government to shift the bus terminus from Esplanade within March 31. Following this, the transport department had moved a special leave petition in the Supreme Court seeking an order to stay the directives of the High Court. The Supreme Court had stayed the order on March 27.

Environmentalist Subash Dutta, meanwhile, had filed a petition in the Supreme Court requesting it to vacate the stay order. The case is still pending. Now, the transport department has decided to relocate the bus terminus as soon as possible.

Heading: Indian sparrow flew over Kolkata film fest - Indian Express
Content:
The engineering students of Jadavpur University chalked out the schedule for their semester examinations on Friday.

Following protests by the students, who had threatened to boycott the examinations, the university had authorised the students to chalk out the examination schedule and the academic calendar for this year.

The students submitted the schedule to the controller of examinations and pasted its copy on the wall of the union office. According to the routine, the examination of the 1st and 3rd year students of the engineering will begin from December 2, the exams for 2nd and 4th year students will begin from December 3.

The university authorities are considering the schedule and have not yet approved the dates set by the students.

The authorities had earlier decided to conduct the semester examination from November 14 but the students had opposed it saying that the syllabus and laboratory assignments were not completed.

A student said:"CAT examination was scheduled for November 16 and our examination was beginning almost simultaneously. This was not in the interest of students."

Heading: ‘2,500 posts lie vacant in govt hospitals, three batches of nurses yet to be recruited’ - Indian Express
Content:
It's not always that we are tempted to read their petulant frowns, but children are a cruelly honest lot. Something, that exactly fits into Abhaya Simha's scheme of things, a film, which explores the irony of urban life. And of course, a film that took Simha's first full-length feature film to various festivals across the world. Gubbachigalu (Sparrows) is the only Indian entrant in the children's film category at the Kolkata Film Festival and Simha hopes that good things keep coming in the way of young filmmakers like him.

A children's film is an unusual choice for a new director in this country but the category was the last things on the 27-year-old filmaker's mind. "Gubbachigalu is partly based on a story written by Ismail, a friend of mine. We were discussing the story, when the idea of the film occurred to me," says Simha.

The filmmaker chose children to play the protagonists in his film and is comfortable with the idea. "I didn't consciously try to make it a children's film. I think, even adults will find it relevant to their lives," says Simha.

Gubbachigalu, shot in Kannada, with English subtitles, sends Ila and Anirudha in search of their lost sparrow in a bustling city. During their expedition, they bump into people, which Simha hopes will enable viewers to develop a new perspective of urban life. "From environmental concerns, to the realities of a mindless urban life, the sparrow has been used as a metaphor to explore them all," says Simha.

Sparrows had been an integral part of Simha's childhood days on the outskirts of Mangalore.

"Even a decade ago, they used to be all over the place. They used to intrude houses to the point of being annoying at times," says Simha. However, with the city skyline getting crowded, Simha sees a decline in the number of birds both alarming and symbolic.

"I'm sure children today have fewer run-ins with birds than us. But they know the smallest scientific details about them, even if they have not seen them in real," says Simha.

Heading: B-schools feel the heat of global meltdown - Indian Express
Content:
The state Health Department, which has come under criticism for handling the outbreak of vector-borne diseases, may now have to deal with another problem — lack of healthcare professionals in government hospitals.

Although the government admits that there are nursing posts lying vacant, it does not specify their exact number. But the Medical Service Centre, a voluntary health organisation, claims that there are nearly 25,000 posts lying vacant in government hospitals.

"Three batches of nurses are yet to be recruited, and the batch of 2008 is about to finish its training. Despite nearly 25,000 posts lying vacant, none have been absorbed. Recently, only 700 posts were filled by the state government before the panchayat elections," said a source at the Medical Service Centre.

Officials at Shastha Bhavan, however, said there are not enough vacancies to absorb all the students passing out from nursing schools every year.

"With nearly 700 girls passing out each year, it becomes difficult to recruit them all," said Madhabi Das, a senior official at the Shastha Bhavan.

She said after the government's decision in 1997 to appoint nurses only on contract basis due to lack of funds has created a backlog that is yet to be cleared. "We cannot recruit 3,000 nurses at a time as the government does not have the money to pay them, but we have absorbed 1,307 nurses in March this year and shall recruit 1,308 in December. By 2009, all the vacancies will be filled," said Das.

Anita Majhi, who got her nursing diploma from the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital in 2005, said: "Earlier, nurses used to get immediate appointments, but now we have to wait for years. There were nearly 1,300 students in my batch who are yet to receive their appointment letters."

After struggling for years to get their voice heard, the Health Department has finally agreed to absorb the nurses of 2004-05 batch.

At the NRS Medical College and Hospital, where a new respiratory care unit was inaugurated recently, the hospital authorities had to reshuffle their existing staff, and nurses claim that the soon-to-be-opened radio therapy unit will further stretch the limited staff.

Hospital superintendent LK Ghosh, however, denied that the hospital had staff shortage.

Heading: ‘Governor to select his press secretary’ - Indian Express
Content:
Business schools are feeling the heat of global meltdown, as their placements have gone down.

"Our placement process begin in October. Last year, within the first month about 50-60 students had been employed, but this year the number is 16," said a student of the Army School of Management, affiliated to the West Bengal University of Technology (WBUT).

Unlike the IIMs, whose job offers are being hit following the global economic downturn, the placement woes of the city's B-schools seem to stem from a slowdown in banking and financial services sector in the domestic market.

In India, the biggest ramification of the global downturn has been a freely falling sensex; hence, the worst affected in the financial services sector are the broking firms, which accounted for a bulk of the placements in lower tier B-schools.

Placement cells, meanwhile, are working overtime to approach new companies .

Directors and deans of many institutes admitted that students were counselled about alternative career options other than banking and securities.

"Our placement process has started. There are a couple of companies which are not interested in fresh recruitments. Standard Chartered Bank, which recruited six students last year, is not visiting our campus this year. Same with Magma Shrachi," said Goutam Ghosh, Director of International School of Business and Media.

Somoushree Nandi, a placement co-coordinator of IIAS B-school in Ultadanga, has a tough job in her hands. She has a batch of 60 MBA students to be recruited by April 2009.

"Last year about 15 students were placed in the banking and securities sectors. This year, Standard Chartered, ICICI Lombard, Sharekhan and Indian Bulls are not coming to our campus for recruitment," she added.

Students also agree that this year's placements have been hit. "Companies that had been regularly visiting our campus for the last five years are not recruiting any candidate this year," said a student.

In the last two years, MBA courses have mushroomed all over the city. Some of these schools are registered under the WBUT, while others are directly under the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE).

Official figures state, at present there are more than 35 full time MBA courses in the state, which are churning out nearly 2,800 students every year. There are several B-schools, however, that operate without any government accreditation or are affiliated to unknown foreign universities.

"There are 24 courses registered with us and on an average 1,440 students pass out every year," said Ragikul Islam, registrar, WBUT.

In most of the colleges, placements have already begun but the crippling economy is plaguing the process, Islam added.

Heading: In Lalgarh, CPM leaders run for guns - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has decided not to enter into a confrontation with Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi over the transfer of his press secretary.

On Friday, Chief secretary Amit Kiran Deb said Gandhi will take a final decision on the matter. As per the governor's request, the government will soon provide him with a panel of candidates from where he can select a press secretary. He can also let Dhruba Basu, his current press secretary, to continue.

Basu was recently transferred to the information and cultural affairs department. Apurba Chatterjee, the chief of bureau of the department, was asked to take Basu's place. The decision to transfer his secretary without consulting him had displeased Gandhi. Following this, he had sought a panel of three candidates who can be his new press secretary.

Heading: Trousseau Treat - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to political leaders moving with a gun-toting entourage, there is little difference these days between Western Uttar Pradesh and the Maoist-affected areas of West Midnapore.

During its trip to Lalgarh, several encounters of The Indian Express with the zonal leaders of the CPM proved that panic has struck the party hard ever since the tribal agitation began on November 5.

Those blessed with clout are granted security personnel from the state's armed forces. The officials in the district administration confided that over 100 grassroots leaders now move with private protectors. The threat perception is said to be "real" from Maoists, who have strong pockets of influence in the region.

On way to Lalgarh, at Bottola Chalk near the local CPM party office, The Indian Express met Anuj Pande, the party's zonal committee secretary. Moving around with gun-totting securitymen provided by the government, Pande still looks a scared man.

Since November 5, the party office has downed its shutters. That very day, the tribal agitation had begun in protest against police excesses on women during a night raid.

But comrades like Pande fear that in the Maoists-fuelled agitation, grassroot CPM leaders would be the natural targets.

Another of such leaders was West Midnapore district secretary Dipak Sarkar, who, unlike Pande, moved around in an SUV, flanked by two men toting automatic guns.

Sarkar was aghast at the suggestion that his precautions may not be quite necessary. "Are you suggesting that we commit suicide by moving without any security cover?" he demanded. "Our leaders are being attacked over and over again. The zonal committee secretary had been attacked thrice," he added.

NS Nigam, the district magistrate of West Midnapore, admitted that the administration has to take requests for security cover by elected representatives very seriously.

"I am not sure about the exact number of people who have been provided with armed guards," he said, "but it should be well over a hundred".

Even so, CPM sources say it is not possible to depend on the police altogether. Already, many applications with them are pending. And given the figures, it is understandable. There are at least 10 zonal committees and 20 local committees in the troubled zone. That means over 200 panic-stricken leaders who demand security cover.

So what do the state police have to say about it?

Rajesh Singh, Superintendent of Police, West Midnapore, flatly refused to discuss issues that relate to "security and intelligence".

"We want to provide security to everyone," said Nigam, "but that may not be possible always".

Heading: Cinema Paradiso - Indian Express
Content:
If you are all set to tie the knot this season, here are a few must-haves

They say marriages are made in heaven. But brides are made prettier here on earth. From designer lehengas to exquisite jewellery to a meticulously put-together trousseau...it's all very much a bride's prerogative. Now with the official wedding season in full flow, going by the number of invitations pouring in, it's time to list out the trends. Are the lehengas still fish-cut or would it be wise to invest in Polki and will last season's stilettos work this year too? Interestingly, we found our answers at the Wedding Asia exhibition at the Taj that's brought in designers, jewel merchants and honeymoon planners under one roof. We took down some notes to prepare you for a perfect trousseau ahead. Read on.

BLING IN IN: No, as of now the somber mood of the economy isn't reflecting on the clothes, at least not on the bridal ones! "Bling is still very much in," tells designer Minu Bhatia who designs under her label 'Lustre'. The fit is a tad snug this year and the lehengas are making up for jewellery. "There's a lot of big stone and sequin work in use. As far as colours go, expect a lot of gold," says Bhatia. Agrees Chandigarh-based Neha Gohri who suggests going in for contemporary cuts with traditional work as must-haves in trousseau wear. "Velvet is really the fabric to flaunt," she adds. And given the fact that winter's stepped in, even shawls and stoles have gone designer. According to Sonia Mahajan who specialises in Kashmiri embroidery, "Brides-to-be must have a traditional Pashmina in their collection. This year we have designed Kaani sarees along with Sucha jari shawls," tells Mahajan, who has been working with award-winning karigars for her collections.

As far as suits go, the kalidaar still stays. "There are many coffee colours teamed with zari on yoke necks," the ladies chorus.

BAUBLE BABBLE: OK, the wardrobe done with, a bride's wish-list has jewellery at the top. "Today's bride wants practical yet traditional jewellery. She wants value for money," Anmol of A Jewels spells it out. With colour being the high point this year, Anmol recommends a lot of polki and diamonds. "Gold filigree work is both affordable and stylish," says Anmol who specialises in the same. And this season, let your ears do the talking. Designer Voila Kapoor of Voila Jewels suggests more than cocktail earrings. "There's a mix of contemporary and traditional," she says. Speaking of trends, diamonds are still the ones to flaunt - solitaires to Polki, choose your sin.

GET STONED: Bags to shoes, the bling effect follows suit. "A trousseau must have a good variety of shoes that best go with the outfits," says designer Sanjana who brings in bags and shoes under her label 'Adaa'.
