"Stones, zari, sequins...all that goes on clothes is now on your shoes as well," mentions Sanjana. As

far as totes go, it's a smart clutch affair.

IN A WRAP: With the brides being front-runners in planning out their own dos, here's what's topping their list. "Chocolates over mithai," Nikhil Mittal of Nik Baker's tells us. With zany boxes complete with bows and ribbons, weddings get a designer touch. "Even the wedding cake is no longer just single layer affair. They go with the themes now," says Mittal. Elsewhere, Seema Vij of Cesta Chocolates presents innovatively wrapped chocolates that go as part of the shagun. "Platters, boxes, curios...chocolates are sent in a smart way," Vij explains.

Heading: Rising Sun - Indian Express
Content:
This weekend, drive down to the Bollywood Carnival

It's one of the prime driving forces of the country and its mammoth of a presence cannot be undermined or simply shooed away. What television was in the '80s and '90s, cinema is today - in its golden period recording sky-rocketing revenues, immense job opportunities and reviving the much-dead thought process. Starting today, with a view to create more awareness of the potential of media and entertainment as a significant contributor to the economic development of the northern region, and the vast employment opportunities, it offers in its various segments, CMES (Centre for Media and Entertainment Studies), a venture of the ITFT (Institute of Technology & Future Management Trends) Chandigarh is organising a three-day 'Bollywood Carnival' at village Hoshiarpur, on PGI-Mullanpur road.

While the occasion saw Deputy Commissioner S A S Nagar ( Mohali) Rahul Bhandari release a concept paper prepared by the ITFT Education Group on developing district Mohali as a cinematic and rural tourism destination, the real carnival, which will go on till November 16, stood complete with a colourful film city, scenes from well-known films, a prototype of a radio station and a display of 'clips from flicks' shot in the northern Indian states.

You can catch CMES students showing off their talents as they re-enact scenes from popular films like Jab we Met, Border, Veer Zaara, Rang de Basanti, Legend of Bhagat Singh et al. If in all this activity, there's a rumble in your tummy, then head for the 'Bollywood Food Court' for flavours of the north and south. The fun doesn't end here for a carnival is never complete without the traditional touch. So don't miss on Punjab's traditional handicrafts, artisans from Patiala who would be out there weaving phulkari, making colourful juttis, parandas and other wonderful items. Apart from this, there are competitions in acting, dance, singing, make-up, mask making, set designing, Bollywood fancy dress, photography, mimicry, costume designing, street theatre, lyrics, script writing, video jockey, radio jockey and anchoring. According to the organizers, a talent bank would be developed for television and film producers who are always on the look out for fresh faces. Enjoy!

Heading: Punjabi Delight - Indian Express
Content:
Japan comes to city with the best in its cinema

The moral dilemmas of post-war Japan, web of complex renditions and melodrama, the trials and tribulations life throws, threads of unspoken relationships, the scream in a silence, viewpoint to truth...it's a reel full of human endearing and endeavours, success and struggles, all shot and immortalised by Japan's finest breed of writers, producers, directors and actors. And bringing to the city this very best in Japanese cinema is the Chandigarh Film Society, Embassy of Japan, Japan Foundation Chandigarh Tourism and Steps in their Kinoshita Keisuke Retrospective along with the works of Mamoru Hosodo, Kurusowa Akira, Yamazaki Takashi, Isao Takahata and Aymunu Watanabe.

Famous for his melodramas, Kinoshita always had a hair for experimentation, be it a dancer who believes that strip teasing is an art in Carmen's True Love, the dilemmas a family faces in The Morning of the Osone Family, or the true life account of the relation between a mother and her son during WW II, in A Record of Youth. The director had a talent to catch life's pulse especially when it came to human nature and the heart of a woman. Apart from his works, there are action-packed movies and animations.

The festival will be inaugurated by Pawan Kumar Bansal on November 15 at the Government Polytechnic for Women Sector 10 at 3 pm and will also be graced by Nizuhu Hayakawa, First Secretary, Embassy of Japan and Teruyuki Hoshina, Director of Japan Foundation.

November 15: Starting 3pm: The Girl Who Lept Through Time, Always - Sunset on Third Street and Women

November 16: Sanjuro (11am), Doraemon (4pm) and Carmen's Pure Love (6pm)

November 17: The Morning of the Osone Family (6pm)

November 18: A Record of Yout (6pm)

November 19: Spring Dreams (6pm)

November 20: The Secret of Incense (6pm)

November 21: Twelve Pairs of Eyes (6pm)

Heading: Picture Perfect - Indian Express
Content:
This weekend indulge in traditional tastes at the 'Tava Tandoor' fest

It's back after a two-year gap, but making up for the time lost is the team at Hotel Shivalik View with their annual Tava & Tandoor food festival. This year, it's gone bigger and better. "For one, we now have a theme," tells the hotel's banquet manager Jagan Chaudhry, as he takes us around the lawns that will host the spread. This year's theme is 'Pure Punjabi' and that's why you'll find earthy thatched huts dotted all over the lawns. "We have replicated the feel of a Punjabi village complete with Bhangra performances," lists out Chaudhry, as we notice the well-lit ambience with even a well to boot! That's when Chef Atul Dutta walks in with his team that has meticulously put together the special menu. "We will have different counters dishing out Punjabi specialties," mentions Chef Dutta. So you have 'Mastane Di Hatti' that will offer a range of tandoori delights. Choose from 'Murg Lajawabi' (a tandoori speciality for Rs 150), 'Murg Tikka' (Rs 150) or 'Paneer Achari Tikka' (Rs 75). If you love all that comes from the tandoor, then the 'Tandoori Phool' (cauliflower) comes highly recommended.

Keeping up with the rustic charm of the food fest, you can tuck into 'Sarson ka saag' with buttery makki rotis and Punjabi daal at 'Bhole Da Dhabha'. "The onset of winter is the perfect time to relish traditional Punjabi meals and we thought of making it a weekend spread for the family," adds Chaudhry. Precisely why there's a special counter - 'Tava Da Mazaa' that brings in 'Amritsari Machhi Sikander Di' (Rs 125). If you are wondering who Sikander is then here's a surprise. "He's one of our speciality cooks and this time we decided to name the counters by the cook who was manning them," pitches in Dutta. So in come 'Tava Meat Manoj Da', 'Paneer Taka Tak Mal Singh' and 'Pao Bhaji Jassi Di'. Completing the main course is 'Malerkotla di Biryani' (Rs 150 to Rs 175). Team it up with one of the shorbas on offer at the counter quite aptly titled 'Sochde Sochde'. But if you are one of those who like to race to the end, there's a treat in store. "For the first time we have kadai dhoodh," they chorus. And jalebi and gulab jamuns, of course.

The food festival is on Saturday (November 15) and Sunday (November 16).

Heading: Farmers see red, show red to trains - Indian Express
Content: The aim to make photography a part of every Indian houseld. With this in mind, Canon India Pvt. Limited today announced the launch of Canon Image Fest at the Piccadily hotel in Sector 22. The fest was initially launched in Jaipur and after clicking a great success there, it has come to Chandigarh. From here, it's scheduled to enter cities like Ludhiana, and Agra among others. Says Shunichi Senda, director ICP, Canon India, "We at Canon are looking forward to re-live the experience of Jaipur. The response was overwhelming and we are happy to see people's keen interest in photography. Canon now takes immense pride and happiness to bring this fest to Chandigarh. We realize how critical tier II cities are for the growth of Canon and this is a step taken towards strengthening our foothold in these tier II cities. The fest is yet another step to get closer to customers and cater to their needs.''

Heading: Shipping firms come calling for Punjabis - Indian Express
Content:
Hundreds of farmers arrested; several trains halted indefinitely; passengers harassed

After talks between the state government and farmers' unions failed and the government refused to accept any of the farmers' demands, representatives of seven farmer unions today blocked rail traffic statewide, disrupting several trains. All this despite the fact that the state government had tried to arrest major farmer leaders yesterday through the local police, forcing them to go underground. Even today, heavy police deployment at strategic points proved to be some deterrent.

It is learnt arrests were made near Khanna and Mansa, while rail traffic is still on hold near Phagwara. Nearly 100 farmers have been arrested near Khanna, while 80 farmers have been arrested in Mansa. More than 200 activists of various farmer unions were apprehended at Lalluana village in Mansa, when they started their march towards railway tracks. After this arrest, another batch of about 150 farmers reached there to be arrested.

The protesting farmers had assembled at the Lalluana village gurdwara and were demanding enhancement in bonus on paddy. When the farmers tried to head towards the railway tracks, the waiting policemen gheraoed them and bundled them in various police vehicles. Before their arrest, the farmers raised slogans against the Union and state governments.

Sukhdev Singh Kokri, general secretary , BKU (Ekta), a farmers' body that has been supporting this rail roko from the outside, said, "The mass arrest of farmers is highly condemnable. Instead of locking us up in jails, the state government should hold talks with us."

BKU Ekta (Dakonda) general secretary Buta Singh Burjgill said the arrests would not demoralise the farmers, who will intensify their struggle after coming out of jail. SSP Manminder Singh, confirming the arrests of farmer activists, said it is a preventive measure to stop agitators from disrupting government machinery or causing loss to government property.

Earlier, a delegation of farmer unions had met Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal at his residence on Friday morning, said BKU (Dakonda) state senior vice-president Manjit Singh Dhaner. He said despite farmers' persistent demands, Badal had flatly declined to announce a bonus on paddy, forcing farmers to resort to an agitation.

Meanwhile, at Ludhiana railway station, passengers had a tough time as traffic was blocked indefinitely and authorities were unable to say anything about the departure or arrival of trains.

Perminder Singh, divisional traffic manager, said they had halted some trains at the city station, while some trains were blocked at nearby stations. The trains affected include Amritsar Tata Express and Swarn Shatabdi.

Malwa Express (2919) halted at the city station, while Amarpali Express and Dadar Express were delayed for an unlimited time. The Jaipur-Jammu Express halted at Badowal station and Shaan-e-Punjab halted at Sirhind station.

In Amritsar, hundreds of passengers were seen huddled at the railway station, waiting for their respective trains, while others were seen eagerly making inquiries. Vimal Kumar, Station Superintendent, said a large number of passengers, whose trains had been cancelled, were given a refund. Meanwhile, following the crackdown on farmers yesterday, more farmer leaders were rounded up by the police in various districts today as a precautionary measure.

Heading: Delivery charges in govt hospitals abolished - Indian Express
Content:
With dollar dreams not looking as promising as before to Punjabi youth, shipping companies are now embarking on their doorstep to lure them to foreign shores.

While shipping companies such as Wallems, V-Ships and Selandia have already opened offices here for recruiting cadets, some other big names such as Doehle Danautic, Fleet Management and Applied Research International (ARI) are scouting for sites in the state. Many not-so-big names now dot smaller cities and towns as it is the hinterland of Punjab that's making up most of the numbers, forcing shipping companies to scout rural Punjab to meet its acute shortage of men.

"A whopping 95 per cent of international trade is based on shipping, but there is an acute shortage of sailors. The shipping industry was caught unawares by the boom and was not training enough cadets. The crisis of depleting numbers of seafarers from the developed world and paying them in Euros has added to the demand for recruits from South-Asian countries. With its large cluster of seafaring families and attraction for the high seas among youth, Punjab is the right place to train and recruit sailors. The need is not only to recruit more but also train more, since the latter is also a stipulation for availing exemption from tonnage tax. In fact, we at the Shipping

Corporation of India (SCI) are training much more than the statuary

requirement," SCI chairman Sabyasachi Hajara told ENS when he was in Chandigarh recently.

At times when other professions are in the meltdown mode and announcing job and salary cuts, shipping companies are selling dreams to aspiring sailors of a profession where the pay packages keep getting better, enough to retire to golf at the age of 35. "No other profession pays you a salary of Rs 1.3 lakh to Rs 1.5 lakh per month at the age of 17 and between USD 10,000 to 15,000 by the time you are 28," Daniel Chopra, the

Punjabi-Goan owner of Doehle Danautic, Indian partner of Germany-based Peter Doehle, which owns and operates a fleet of over 485 vessels worldwide, says.

The most recent one to announce its plans to launch its flagship recruitment and training centre in Punjab, Danautic is looking at wooing rural Punjabi youth with an assured job on his own fleet of ships.

"We believe that the future of shipping is in the north, mainly areas in and around Punjab. The right mix of temperament, physique and attitude makes Punjabis a great choice as sailors. Since most of our trainees are from Punjab and around, we are looking at coming to the state in a big way," says A. Rewari of Applied Research International.

However, though the good salaries and "no-hardcore academics" are the initial attractions, many young sea officers do not see merchant navy as a career destination. "I did not have to do an MBA to get into the merchant navy and to that six-digit figure salary. I sail for four to six months in a year and make between USD 8,000 to 9,000 per month. The remaining six months are for unwinding and some golf. I may move on to some other profession after a few years of sailing," says Harman Mangat, a Chandigarh-based young sea officer, son of a retired merchant navy officer. Others like Prabhjit Singh, Tarun Ahluwalia and Pranav Anand too plan to move on.

More so since the lows can also not be endured for long, adds Pranav's wife Sheila Anand, a marine journalist. "It's not just the wives, isolation disturbs men equally. Thankfully, shipping companies are now bringing in a more human touch and sailors are being provided facilities to connect to their families in the middle of the high seas in any part of the world via Internet and satellite communication."

Heading: A goodbye long overdue: 28 Pak prisoners released - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Health Department, through a notification, has abolished delivery charges in government hospitals in the state. As per the earlier charges, that were effective from October 16, 2000, Rs 300 were charged in government hospitals against each delivery.

The office of Bathinda Civil Surgeon today received the Health and Family Welfare Department notification (dated October 24). As per the notification, a copy of which is with The Indian Express, the parchi fee (OPD slip fee) has been increased from Re 1 to Rs 2. The air-conditioned and cooler room charges have also been doubled from Rs 25 and Rs 5 to Rs 50 and Rs 10, respectively. The ambulance charges have been hiked from Rs 3.5 per kilometre to Rs 5 per kilometre. The notification has been issued following a Cabinet approval on the issue.

Health officials say abolishing the delivery charges is aimed at promoting institutional delivery and discouraging delivery at home, as per the guidelines of the National Rural Health Mission.

The information accessed by The Indian Express from the office of District Registrar, Birth and Death, revealed that of the total 1,565 births in Bathinda district in October 2008, 359 deliveries took place in homes. In terms of percentage, the home deliveries account for almost 23 per cent of total deliveries.

"In deliveries at homes, there is always a risk of complications. The abolition of delivery charges would go a long way in promoting institutional delivery," said Bathinda Assistant Civil Surgeon Dr Indu Bhushan Aggarwal.

Punjab Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla, while terming the abolition of delivery charges as a good step, maintained that increase in other charges was not going to make much difference as far as earning any revenue was concerned.

"The charges had not been revised for a long time. Even now, if we charge Rs 50 for an AC room as per the revised charges, we still don't achieve the break-even point in meeting the electricity bill," said Chawla.

Heading: Paddy bonus to be given through online banking - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty eight Pakistani prisoners, who had completed their jail term for various crimes, were sent back home on Friday through the Attari-Wagha joint border check-post.

The prisoners, held on charges that included illegal border-crossing and smuggling, however, complained of non-compliance of the order by Punjab and Haryana High Court asking the state government to pay Rs 100 per day to the prisoners for each day in jail after the completion of sentence.

Among those released was Farzana, a middle-aged Pakistan women, who had completed her sentence in a fake currency case on November 25, 2007, but had to stay in the transit camp in the Central Jail here for want of clearance from Pakistan High Commission. "I am taking home one year extra in jail as a gift," she remarked, sarcastically.

Of the 28, 17 prisoners were from the Amritsar Central jail, eight from Jammu and Kashmir, one from Gujarat and two from Rajasthan's jails. Seema, another woman who served a sentence in a fake currency case, was released along with her husband Ahmad. Their release was made possible due to the intervention of the High Court, which had directed the state government to release foreign, especially Pakistani, prisoners who had completed their sentences.

Farzana's lawyer, Ajay Vermani, who had spearheaded the movement to get these prisoners released, said he was upset that the compensation due to them was not paid by the government. "I am in the process of taking up the cases of Pak prisoners lodged in other jails and to ensure compensation for them as well," he said.

A Hizbul terrorist, Fahaul Shekhawat, was also released from a J&K jail. He was wounded in an encounter with the Army in 2002 and was sentenced to 14 years in the jail. He went home after 16 years with a pledge to never indulge in such an activity again. "All these years were painful but now I hope to see my family," he said.

The prisoners thanked the Indian officials for the efforts made for their release. "There were times when it seemed that we would never see the families back home, but finally we are going to see our family members," said Gulzar Ahmed, a resident of Bahawalpur in Pakistan. Two more prisoners, Mohammad Asif from Delhi and another from Mumbai, were to be released too but they could not reach Amritsar for the repatriation and are likely to be released within few days.

Heading: Dhaadi, two others get five yrs’ RI in ’06 explosives case - Indian Express
Content: In a move that could cut down on delay, the Punjab government has chalked out a plan to credit the paddy bonus of over Rs 650 crore to more than 1 crore farmers directly in their bank accounts through online banking system. Announcing this here on Friday, Food and Civil Supplies Minister Adesh Partap Singh Kairon said usually, there was an inordinate delay in making payment of bonus and sometimes, disputes lingered on for years. "To improve the system and ensure immediate payment, this decision has been taken," he said. He said that he had called a meeting of GM of all leading banks of the state and advised them to open zero-balance accounts free of cost for farmers. The Centre has already approved the system.

Heading: Phagwara becomes bottleneck - Indian Express
Content:
A fast-track court in Jalandhar today sentenced former terrorist Paramjit Singh Dhaadi and two others to five years' rigorous imprisonment in a case dating back two years, when the three were caught just before the last Assembly elections in 2006 along with 11 kg RDX and other explosives. Additional Sessions Judge Ravinder Singh pronounced the sentence. A fine of Rs 500 has also been levied upon the three, failing which they would have to undergo another year of imprisonment.

For the record, then opposition leader, Parkash Singh Badal, had claimed that the RDX was meant to eliminate him.

Dhaadi (56) is a UK national, while the two others are Amolak Singh (54) and Jaswinder Singh (23). Dhaadi was booked in another case earlier for recovery of nearly 30 kg RDX, but was acquitted. Today, too, he said he would appeal in the High Court against the sentence, claiming that he was falsely implicated.

It may be noted that in the same case, police had claimed that they had recovered 11 kg RDX, 11 detonators, 11 timer devices, four hand grenades, two batteries, two pistols with four magazines, 100 cartridges and a walkie-talkie set from the accused in December 2006. Police had also claimed to recover most of the explosive from Dhaadi's village, Gakhal in Jalandhar, but that claim could not hold much water.

Heading: ‘Congress exposed by Alva’s allegations’ - Indian Express
Content:
Rail traffic was worst-hit at Phagwara due to the farmers' agitation. Nearly 400 farmers blocked the railway track by sitting on the tracks in the morning. They were still blocking rail traffic at the time of filing of this report, despite efforts made by the Kapurthala DC and SSP. When the authorities tried to force the farmers to lift their dharna, they threatened to pelt them with stones lying on the rail track.

Thousands of passengers were seen at Jalandhar railway station trying to get refunds. "We were to go to Mumbai to attend a function, but had to get our tickets cancelled at the last minute," said Jatinder Kaur of Jalandhar.

"I had to join duty back in Bangalore on Monday, but now I have no other option but to go by air after taking a road route to Delhi," said Anuj Sharma, an IT professional.

Heading: Two thermal power units trip at Ropar - Indian Express
Content:
Cabinet Minister Bikramjit Singh Majithia today said the allegations of senior Congress leaders, including Margaret Alva and R.L. Jalappa, regarding money changing hands for securing election tickets has exposed the murky face of the Congress.

In a statement released today, Majithia said Alva and a host of other leaders have paid a heavy price for speaking the truth.

Majithia said instead of being apologetic or ordering an independent inquiry into her allegations, the Congress had tried to silence her by expelling her from party posts.

Majithia said, "The time has come for the people to exercise their right to vote and unseat the Congress in the ensuing Lok Sabha polls."

Heading: Bathinda Improvement Trust postpones auction indefinitely - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab was forced to undergo long power cuts for upto six hours after two units of the Ropar Thermal plant tripped today, leading to acute shortage of power. The state lost as much as 420 MW power on Friday due to the tripping of the two thermal power generation units at the Ropar power plant.

While one of the Ropar Thermal plant units tripped due to a boiler tube leakage yesterday, the other tripped following a generator earth fault, which could be located only by the evening on Friday.

PSEB engineers were busy rectifying the fault and trying to restart the operations, sources said. Meanwhile, due to the tripping of the thermal units, producing 210 MW each, the lower availability of power the gap between the demand and supply of power to Punjab widened further. While power available to the the state on Friday was 780 lakh units, the demand rose to 1,000 lakh units.

Heading: Hafed to explore new markets - Indian Express
Content:
The Bathinda Improvement Trust today postponed the restricted auction of goods booking agency sites under the Transport Nagar Scheme for an indefinite period. The trust has decided to first reply to the notice of motion issued by the Punjab and Haryana HC.

The High Court had issued a notice of motion after a goods carrier firm, Delhi Punjab Goods Carrier (DPGC) Private Limited, alleged favouritism in the selection of bidders and filed a petition in the court. The court also issued directions that the company in question be allowed to participate in the auction.

DPGC's name was removed from the list of companies participating in the auction in a list released by the trust on November 4. The trust had earlier selected DPGC's application in August last.

"After discussions at the government-level, it has been decided to reply to the notice of motion first and see the contents of petition filed by the goods firm," said Bathinda Improvement Trust administrator Kamal Kishore Yadav, confirming the postponement .

Heading: Parties look for prospective candidates for LS polls - Indian Express
Content:
It has started marketing its products in Gujarat and Bangalore

The Haryana State Cooperative Supply and Marketing Federation (Hafed) is exploring new markets for promoting its products. The Federation is looking at the Southern and Western states to launch its consumer products. To begin with Hafed has started marketing its products in Gujarat and Bangalore. It has appointed a distributor for marketing of Hafed Consumer Products in Bhavnagar and the first consignment of rice has been dispatched.

A senior official of Hafed told the Indian Express that a container full of 15 tonne rice has been dispatched to Bhavnagar . "Our consumer products namely basmati rice, non-basmati rice, kachchi ghani mustard oil, refined soyabean oil, refined cottonseed oil, branded sugar, desi wheat, organic wheat etc. are already popular in Haryana, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Delhi, Bangalore, West Bengal, Orissa, Jammu and Kashmir. With the introduction of Hafed's products in Bhavnagar, we are entering new markets as there is a lot of potential for marketing the products, especially rice," said the official.

Hafed is also planning to enter markets of Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and Chennai within the next couple of months. It has done aggressively marketing for mustard oil and other products in Jammu and Kashmir, Leh, Srinagar and Kargil. The official said, "During the first six months of the current financial year i.e. from April to September, the sale of our consumer products has more than doubled as compared to the same period of the previous year. We have registered a growth of 122 per cent in our turnover of consumer products between April to September and the target is to achieve a growth of 150 per cent in consumer products by the end of this fiscal."

Hafed has recently started marketing its organic products by introducing organic desi wheat and mustard oil which has been accepted by the consumers in Haryana, Delhi, J&K and other regions. "Organic moong and many more products will be soon launched in the market. Apart from the domestic market.

Heading: New scheme to curb anaemia among women, children - Indian Express
Content:
With Lok Sabha elections drawing near, political parties in the state have started looking for prospective candidates, best suited from each of the ten Parliamentary constituencies in the state. In the last Lok Sabha polls, the Congress had won nine out of ten seats.

For the Ambala Lok Sabha constituency, which is a reserved seat, the Congress candidate is likely to be sitting MP Selja. Selja had quit her previous constituency, Sirsa, to contest from Ambala in 2004. She had secured 4.15 lakh votes, 48.99 per cent of the total, to register a won from Ambala (SC) constituency.

Selja's main opponent then, Rattanlal Kataria of the BJP, who had procured 1,80330 votes to stand second, could be the main candidate if the BJP-INLD alliance gives him a green signal. However, if Selja opts for Sirsa again, in place of sitting MP, Atma Singh Gill, Congress will have to look for another candidate.

The BSP has already named Chandrapal for the Ambala constituency. The party has a good hold in the region and the only BSP MLA in the state, Arjun Singh, belongs to Yamunanagar constituency.

The Haryana Janhit Congress (BL) is yet to open its cards. The party has not given any indication who its candidate would be from the Ambala constituency.

In the 2004 polls the INLD and the BJP had fought the election separately. But the total number of votes of the the two parties together was less than that of the Congress. However, it will not be easy for the Congress this time around against the alliance of the two parties.

Heading: HC stays transfer of defence plots in Hisar - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Women and Child Development Department will implement a new scheme to curb anaemia among children, adolescent girls and pregnant and lactating mothers.

The state government has allocated Rs 10 crore as one time Central assistance for the current financial year.

Announcing this on the occasion of Children's Day today, Haryana Women and Child Development Minister, Kartar Devi said children and women would be provided iron and folic acid tablets once a week.

De-worming would be done with the help of Mebendazole tablets twice a year. She said children would be given doses of Vitamin-A as per immunisation schedule by the auxiliary nurse midwife (ANM) in anganwadi centres.

The Department of Women and Child Development would implement the scheme in close coordination with Health Department which will advice them, provide infrastructural assistance and views of experts on doses and frequency of administering tablets.

She said the medicines would be purchased by district-level committees, of Civil Surgeons and Programme Officers of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme, to be formed under the chairmanship of Deputy Commissioner at district level.

The Deputy Chief Medical Officer or incharge of Reproductive Child Health Programme would be convener of the committee and district health society would monitor the purchase of medicines and other related health activities at district level.

She said the scheme would benefit about 21.67 lakh children upto six years of age, 4.02 lakh pregnant and nursing mothers and 70,000 adolescent girls in the state through a network of 17,444 anganwadi centres.

Kartar Devi said anaemia was widespread in the country and it especially affects young women, children and adolescent girls.

According to the findings of National Family Health Survey-3 for the year 2005-06, the incidence of anaemia in children between the age of six to 35 months and women was still as high as 82.5 per cent and 56.5 per cent respectively due to low dietary intake, poor iron and other nutrient intake.

Heading: Revamping and augumentation of power transmission - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court stayed the transfer of defence plots in Sector 5, Hisar, to general quota on a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by ex-naval personnel welfare society.

The directions were passed by a division bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh. The petitioner had sought quashing of the condition by which JCOs are not allowed to apply for bigger plots.

Terming the condition as completely discriminatory, Advocate Vivek Khatri, counsel for the petitioner said that such condition should not be imposed in future. He demanded that JCOs should also be allowed to apply for bigger plots. "The draw of plots of Sector 5, Hisar, should be stayed," he said.

The state government introduced one sector in each district, which is reserved only for defence and paramilitary forces personnel.

Officers of rank of Colonel and above are eligible to apply for kanal plots only whereas other commissioned officers up to Lt Col and equivalent rank are eligible for 14 marla and 10 marla plots.

The JCOs and other ranks are eligible for plots of eight, six and four marlas. Taking note of the contentions, the High Court has stayed the transfer of defence plots to general quota.

Notice to home secretary for 'non-functional consumer forums'
A division Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh issued notices to the state of Haryana and the home secretary on a petition filed by Advocate G D Gupta of Jagadhari.
The High Court has directed the Additional Advocate General, Haryana to explain the position vis-a-vis the allegation of the petitioner. According to the petition, the consumer forums at Yamunanagar, Kurukshetra, Panipat and Hisar were non-functional because of lack of quorum.
It is not entitled to hear any matter as per the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, if the quorum is incomplete.
The petitioner alleged so far approximately Rs 1 crore has been spent by the state on these non-functional forums, which is purely wastage of public money. Despite holding interviews in August and September, the presidents and members have not been appointed. The case would now come up for resumed hearing on November 18.

Heading: No real progress during latest round of talks with China: Dalai - Indian Express
Content:
Centre has sanctioned Rs 40 crore for revamping and strengthening of transmission and distribution system and Hisar will soon get uninterrupted power supply.

Sources said under this scheme, the DHBVN plans to revamp and augment power transmission and distribution system in Hisar by adding power transformers in sub-stations, providing capacitor banks to improve power factor and better voltage, replacing existing low capacity equipment and old conductor of 33 KV lines.

The Nigam would provide additional distribution transformers to improve the low voltage problem and to meet the increasing load. The scheme also includes replacement of worn out conductor of distribution lines, creation of high voltage distribution system (HVDS) in slum areas, maintenance of distribution transformers, meters on transformers and relocation of consumer meters.

HVDS would be created in the areas fed through 11 KV feeders at Jahajpul and Vinod Nagar at a cost of Rs 9.70 crore. Under this system transformers would be used in larger number and insulated conductor would be used for safety. With the creation of HVDS system people would get qualitative power supply at better voltage level with minimum interruptions. Aggregate transmission and commercial (AT&C) losses, which are presently 60-70 per cent on these feeders, would reduce considerably with the creation of the new system.

Heading: 12 injured in bus mishap near Shimla - Indian Express
Content:
The Tibetan spiritual leader and temporal head the Dalai Lama has expressed his disappointment that "no real progress was made during seventh and eight round of talks held this year with officials of the People's Republic of China (PRC).''

In a message to Tibetan people on the eve of a special meeting being convened to discuss the issue, the Dalai Lama gave the entire background of the talks held with the PRC officials, and the 'middle way approach' adopted by him and his administration.

He said that since coming into exile, the Tibetans have exercised the essential functions of a democratic system by inviting their people to express their opinions about important political decisions on the future of Tibet. The current mutually beneficial middle-way approach was formulated in the early 1970s as a result of much deliberation and discussion with leaders who represented the Tibetan people, he said.

"Moreover, I have specifically stated in the Strasbourg Proposal that the Tibetan people will make the final decision,'' the message conveys. The Dalai Lama said, "After the sixth round of talks in 2007 with officials of the PRC, there were no plans to hold further talks in the immediate future. But because of the urgency of the situation in Tibet after the events of March this year, we held informal discussions in the beginning of May, followed by the seventh and eighth rounds of talks in July and at the beginning of November (respectively), so as not to leave any stone unturned. Nevertheless, no real progress was made,'' he stated.

The Tibetan spiritual leader said that in March this year, Tibetans from all walks of life in Tibet risked their lives by courageously expressing their long-felt dissatisfaction with the PRC policies, in a peaceful and lawful way. "At that time I was hopeful that the PRC government would find a solution based on the reality on the ground. However, on the contrary, the Chinese government has completely ignored and rejected Tibetan feelings and aspirations by brutally cracking down on them, using the accusation that they were 'splittists' and 'reactionaries' as an excuse. During those testing times, out of profound concern and a deep sense of responsibility, I exercised whatever influence I have with the international community and with China, including writing personally to President Hu Jintao. But my efforts hardly made any difference,'' the Dalai Lama said in his message.

He pointed out that until now, the Tibetans have followed the middle-way approach and eight rounds of talks have taken place since contact with the PRC was restored in 2002. "Despite this approach receiving widespread appreciation from the international community, as well as the support of many Chinese intellectuals, there have been no positive signs or changes in Tibet. Indeed, PRC policies towards Tibet and the Tibetans have remained unchanged,'' said the Dalai Lama.

The Dalai Lama said that the special meeting is being convened to know the opinions of the Tibetan people through free discussions. "It must be clear to all that this special meeting does not have any agenda for reaching a particular predetermined outcome," he said.

Heading: Buy premium petrol at HPC pumps, normal ‘out of stock’ - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve persons were injured when a Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) bus went off the road at Bayechri, about 15 kilometres from Shimla.

The injured were admitted to IGMC Hospital. Fortunately, there were causalities in the mishap. The bus was going from Shimla to Dhamoon village, and the accident occurred at about 4 pm.

The hospital authorities said that the injuries were of a minor nature, and the condition of all the injured persons is stable. According to the police, about 30 passengers were on board when the accident took place.

As per the passengers, the bus was going downhill on a high speed, due to which the driver could not negotiate the curve. After rolling down, once the bus got stuck in a tree, which proved to be godsend for the passengers. The driver Jagdish has also been injured.

The passengers complained that the road is also in a bad state, and has not been repaired for many years. The Pradhan of Bayechri, Jagdish Chand, told The Indian Express that an accident had occurred at the same spot about one and half years ago. The bus was going uphill but went off the road, as the weak retaining wall along the road gave in.

"The spot is still dangerous as the retaining wall is weak, and the curve is sharp. Despite many requests, the government has not taken any remedial measures," said Jagdish Chand. No inquiry has been ordered into the accident so far. Sub Divisional Magistrate Man Singh Verma visited the hospital and gave financial help for the treatment of the injured persons.

Heading: Bitumen scam: Defaulting companies fined Rs 2.85 crore - Indian Express
Content:
Petrol pumps across Himachal Pradesh that are fed by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPC) are giving the customers a tough time by claiming to have inadequate stock of 'Normal Unleaded Petrol'. As a result, people are forced to buy the premium brand, Power, that is costlier by Rs 4 four.

The problem is being faced in all pockets of the state. Of the 260 petrol pumps in Himachal Pradesh, 30 per cent are fed by HPC.

Director Food and Civil Supplies RS Gupta says the state has taken up the matter of shortage of normal petrol in the HPC-fed petrol pumps with the Union Petroleum Ministry for three months now, but there has been no action. "The matter is to be solved by the Petroleum Ministry and the HPC authorities. It has been nearly three months since we took up the issue, and have sent several reminders. But remedial measures have not been taken, and we are unable to help the consumers, who are bearing the brunt."

Today too, Pineview Filling Station near Shimla barrier did not have adequate stock of normal petrol, costing Rs 53 a litre. The staff claimed that the stock finished by about 1 pm, and customers were forced to buy Power brand, priced at Rs 57.08.

At Anup Service Station near Tara Hall, the supply line from the storage tank where normal brand of petrol is stored is stated to be out of order since 20 days. Here too, people are forced to buy the premium brand.

Owner of Pineview Filling Station Ashwani Dogar said, "The problem with the supply of the normal brand is on the side of HPC. Earlier, the difference in the prices of normal and the premium brands was of only a few paise, so the sale of the premium brand was higher, as it is better. The normal brand is in short supply now because suddenly, the difference of price between both brands has increased to Rs 4."

Interestingly, the storage tanks for normal petrol have lower capacity as compared to those for premium brand. This is despite the fact that demand is higher for normal petrol.

Heading: Notices to Baddi industries for violation of rules - Indian Express
Content:
A penalty of Rs 2.85 crore approximately has been imposed by Him Agro Industries Corporation (HAIC) on four transporter companies involved in the bitumen supply scam in 2007-08, by delaying the supply orders.

HAIC had been appointed as the nodal agency for bitumen supply. The State Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau had earlier expressed its displeasure at the Corporation for not taking action against the defaulters.

SP Special Investigation Unit (Vigilance) Hardesh Bisht said that according to the information given by the Corporation, MK Enterprises has been imposed with a fine of Rs 94.33 lakh; Amit Singla with Rs 1.67 crore, Brij Lal Mohan Lal with a fine of Rs 13.75 lakh and Haryana Transport Company Samalakha with a fine of Rs 9.23 lakh.

As per terms and conditions of the tender, the fine has been imposed at the rate of Rs 10 per day, for each day of delay beyond the target time.

Interestingly, despite major default on the part of the transporter companies, HAIC had extended the contract with them till June 30, 2008. The original contract was till March 31, 2008.

The scam was investigated by the Vigilance in May 2008. The Vigilance has asked the Corporation to clarify why the transportation contract with the defaulting transporters was extended. The scam pertains to 22 divisions of Public Works Department, and involved supply of thousands of litres of bitumen, to be procured from Panipat Refinery.

The supply was inordinately delayed, and in some cases the bitumen went missing too. The payments for the stocks were released by the Public Works Department (PWD) before receiving the supply. Sources say the scam is expected to run into several crores. Vigilance has already registered an FIR in the scam for two divisions, Una and Badsar.

Heading: Virbhadra lashes out at BJP govt - Indian Express
Content:
The Industry Department today issued notices to over a dozen industrial units at Baddi, for violating the government's order that at least 70 percent jobs in these units must be given to persons of Himachali domicile.

The violations were detected by a team of officials of the Departments of Industry, Environment Protection, Labour, and the Pollution Control Board. The team conducted raids at several units in and around the township today. The raids were conducted on the instructions of the government, after receipt of a large number of complaints concerning the violation of the government's order, and other labour and industrial laws.

The team also took samples of polluted water from some of the units, and sent these for chemical analysis to the laboratory. The team comprised Executive Engineer Brij Bhushan Sharma of Pollution Control Board, Member Secretary Industry Department TR Sharma, and officials of the Labour Department.

The team found during the raids that the managements of Kanha Bio-Tech, KRM Tyres, Unix Bio-Tech and other units were flouting the norms by not providing 70 percent jobs to Himachalis. The team members also took the records of some of units into their possession, for scrutiny.

Heading: Movie reviews - Indian Express
Content:
Former chief minister Virbhadra Singh today accused the BJP government of rampant corruption, poor governance and dividing the state on caste and regional basis.

The former CM alleged that the BJP government, instead of accelerating the pace of development, was focussing more on misleading the masses and taking advantages of the developmental schemes initiated by the Congress government. Singh charged said that developmental activities have virtually came to a grinding halt ever since the Dhumal government assumed power. "Except inaugurating and commissioning the works completed and initiated during the Congress rule."

Heading: ‘Climate change will destroy economies around the world’ - Indian Express
Content:
Dasvidaniya
CAST: Vinay Pathak, Neha Dhupia, Ranvir Shorey, Rajat Kapoor, Saurabh Shukla, Gaurav Gera, Suchitra Pillai;
DIRECTOR: Shashant Shah
Every once in a rare while, a film comes along to pleasure you in unexpected ways. Dasvidaniya, about a man who learns to live in the little time's that left to him, is one such, and it's gone right up there, on the top of my list.
Amar (Vinay) gets to know that he has the Big C, and that he is, not to put too fine a point on it, dying. Now he's always been the kind of man who makes lists, so this is his last chance whip out a pen, and write on a piece of yellow paper: things to do before I die. A big car? Check. He gets himself a spanking red one. An old love? Check. He tracks down the pretty girl (Neha) he's always had a crush on, and confesses all. Dump the boss? Totally. He stares down the overfed, oversized bully (Saurabh) who's made him miserable all his working life, and quits his job. Getting estranged younger brother (Gaurav) home? Oh yes.
It's easy to go wrong with films about people jousting with death, and more often than not, what we get is an overdose of maudlin melodrama. Dasvidaniya (goodbye in Russian, and yes, there's a reason for this, but we'll let you discover it for yourself) is just right: bitter-sweet, matter-of-fact, laced with little joys and sorrows, just like life. Be ready for involuntary tears, though.
And Vinay Pathak is pitch perfect. Nowhere does he send up the Amar-the-loser. No artificial sympathy is garnered. We've all known the Amars of this world, and there's a little bit of Amar in all of us: pretty girls do sometimes run off to another, some best friends (Rajat) are happy to get the bigger share of everything, and their wives (Suchitra) are often mean and suspicious. So who says life is fair? This is Vinay's finest performance, much more nuanced than his much-hyped one in Bheja Fry.
Dasvidaniya is a little gem. Go watch.

Dostana
CAST: Abhishek Bachchan, John Abraham, Priyanka Chopra, Bobby Deol, Boman Irani, Kirron Kher, Sushmita Mukherjee;
DIRECTOR: Tarun Mansukhani
YOU may not agree with its politics, but Dostana is all set to do for the word 'gay' what Taare Zameen Par did for 'dyslexia': bring it out of the closet.
On second thoughts, being political would have made it a deeper, complicated film. All debutant director Tarun Mansukhani, and producer Karan Johar want you to do is to have a blast. Accordingly, in order to rent a swish apartment in Miami, Sam (Abhishek) and Karan (John) are made to be gay. Note, not homosexual. Not queer. Just gay, the word that used to denote happiness in simpler times.
And why the leading men need to be pretend-gay is the only little wrinkle in the plot which is otherwise as straight as an arrow: two boys, one girl, and post interval, one more boy. So who gets her? Sam the male nurse, wearer of brightly-flowered shirts? Or Karan, he of the golden bronze chest, and gleaming pectorals? Or late entrant Abhimanyu, shiny in his Armanis, and Guccis? The eye candy is blinding: designers Manish Malhotra and Aki Narula have clearly worked as hard on this project as the director.
Equally clearly, Miami has been chosen because where there are beaches, there are babes, and other hot bods. The stars get by on very few clothes, particularly John, who looks most fetching in his very brief briefs. Priyanka, with her collagen-ed lips and chic wardrobe, looking much better here than in Fashion, fits right in. Abhishek makes up for his fully-clothed appearance by being nicely goofy.
Only Sindhi aunty-types (Sushmita) and Punjabi mammas (Kirron) have the vapours at the sight of touchy-feely moments between John and Abhishek: they are all over each other, and there is even, ohmigod, a lip lock. Everyone else seems to take their gayness very coolly, including the supposed couple. But the gallery is played to, as well, with lots of nudge-nudge wink-wink gay gags. A limp-wristed Boman Irani shows up to drool over the boys, and when a strangely understated Bobby Deol is added to the mix, the party is complete.
Only when Tarun gets emotion in, does the film start to drag. Mistake, because no one does tears like Karan. Ignore those bits, stay with the fun ones, and get laughing. And confirm, like we did, that John has the cutest butt in Bollywood.

Deshdrohi
CAST: Kamal Khan, Gracy Singh, Manoj Tiwari, Hrishita Bhatt, Zulfi Syed, Aman Varma;
DIRECTOR: Jagdish Shama
If you are a 'bhaiyya' from UP or Bihar, Mumbai isn't a good place for you. Deshdrohi, which must have been in the works long before the violence in Maharashtra peaked last month, should have been, by rights, both timely and important. But it is so tackily produced and shoddily acted, that there is no danger of that happening: the ban in Maharashtra is only going to get people curious about a rank bad film.
Producer Kamal Khan places himself in the lead role. And a more unsuitable leading man would be hard to find: utterly unprepossessing, zero acting skills. He plays, what else, a 'bhaiyya' who fetches up in Mumbai to make a fortune. And runs into a gang of Marathi-speakers who are out for his blood. And that of his fellow sufferers from 'Uttar Bharat'.
A Dawood look-alike makes the startling claim that he is the one who chooses the chief minister of Maharashtra. And you always thought that it was a duly elected seat. A wily UP-wala politician turns out to as corrupt as the Maharashtrians, leading our hero to come to the conclusion that it is the 'netas' who are the 'asli deshdrohis'.
An overweight Gracy Singh (last seen in Lagaan) plays the heroine, who goes around on a motorcycle, bashing up those who bash up 'bhaiyyas'. Wonder what Behen Mayawati would make of this.

—SHUBHRA GUPTA
shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

EAGLE EYE
CAST: Shia LaBeouf, Michelle Monaghan, Billy Bob Thornton, Michael Chiklis
DIRECTOR: D J Caruso
THE question may have occurred to you before: if "they" are listening in to every phone call you make, reading every message you send, watching everything you purchase, monitoring everywhere you go, how do they keep track of all that information?
Here's your answer, imagined by Caruso as a shiny golden mother computer, surrounded by lots of her mini-mes, and burrowed 36 floors down inside the Pentagon.
All that intel goes inside this computer, and "she" monitors it to give the US Government "credible" — give that a wide berth—¿ leads on what seems suspicious.
One day she gets very, very angry, and as all of us know from Hal 9000 (2001: A Space Odyssey) onwards, that isn't good news. Considering she can rig almost anything automated, from traffic lights to F-16 bombers to cranes sorting out trash to electric towers, not to mention mobile phones, that's even worse news.
Caught in the middle of the madness are Jerry Shaw (LaBeouf) and Rachel (Monaghan), for reasons revealed much later. Suffice to say that one fine day, they get these mysterious calls and then messages springing up virtually everywher— ¿ from signboards to traffic ligh—s ¿ telling them to be there, carry something and do that.
"Refusal is not an option," the unknown voice (we find out soon that it's the mother computer) tells them, underlining it with frying up a man with high-voltage electric cables in front of their eyes.
As long as there is a terror threat around and cars to blow up, Eagle Eye isn't the first or likely to be the last film about over-reliance on technology backfiring, and Caruso certainly doesn't let the pace slag. As for plausibility, it would be foolish to seek the same in a film such as this.
However, this is LaBeouf's vehicle, and you have to admit he does a commendable job of it, surviving almost everything thrown his way without letting you forget that he could be you or me having a very bad computer day.

—SHALINI LANGER
shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: A year on, not a single laptop recovery, arrest - Indian Express
Content:
Greenpeace, an independent environment watchdog, held a unique interaction with children at the Sukhna Lake on Friday. The activists, dressed as penguins, said their niche was melting due to a rise in global temperature, which has been destroying the environment and their habitat.

The interaction was part of the group's campaign to raise awareness on the impending danger of climate change.

Talking about the urgent need to address climate change, Pankaj Kumar, coordinator for Greenpeace in the city, said climate change is threatening life and unless we take serious action now, climate change will destroy economies, societies all around the world.

They said climate change has been widely recognised as the greatest challenges of the 21st century.

The activists said children are the best proponents of the environment and there is a dire need for information and immediate action to address the issue.

The volunteers also urged residents to replace bulbs with CFLs, use public transport or car pools, switch off lights and turn off taps when not in use, refill and reuse water bottles and use less paper and plastic.

Heading: A common incinerator for city on the anvil in Dadumajra - Indian Express
Content:
It has been more than a year since a spate of laptop thefts had rocked the tricity, but the Chandigarh Police has failed to trace the culprits in all these months.

While investigations are still on in most of the cases, the police have filed an "untraced report", expressing its inability to trace the stolen laptops and nail any of the culprits, in the theft that caused maximum loss.

It was in the months of October and November last year, when around 120 laptops, computer accessories, a number of mobile phones and more than 20 LCD plasma screens were stolen from various electronic and computer shops across the tricity. The dealers faced losses to the tune of lakhs of rupees each.

The worst affected was Iqbal Singh, Director of Fastrack Computing Limited, who runs a shop in Sector 20. Besides computer accessories, 52 laptops costing around Rs 20 lakh each were stolen from his store in December. The thieves cut an iron grill and broke the lock of the main door to enter the shop and then decamped with dozens of laptops.

Despite running from pillar to post, Iqbal Singh did not see any hope to get the stolen items back. He had provided the police with the identification numbers and serial numbers of all the 52 stolen laptops and their bills. All the police could offer him in return was an "untraced report".

Iqbal said if the police could get the identification numbers of the laptops on surveillance, through Internet, they could get a clue whenever somebody used any of the laptops. According to Iqbal, the police did not do a satisfactory job.

"What more could you expect from the police when they did not even bother to question the watchman who was on duty the night my store was burgled. They did not question any of my staff members either. I pursued the matter for several weeks, but moved on after losing all hopes. Now, they have issued me an 'untraced report', stating that the case is closed," Iqbal Singh told Newsline.

Most of the other burglaries, too, met with a similar fate,

leaving the police perplexed and clueless.

"The case of burglary at my store was transferred from Sector 19 police station to their cyber wing. Officers met me, recorded my statement and went away, but could not do anything substantial. When the 'untraced report' was submitted by the police in the court, I was asked if I was satisfied with the police investigation. I had to reply in the affirmative; I could not have even claimed the insurance otherwise," said Iqbal Singh.

The Station House Officer of the Sector 19 police station, Inspector SS Bhullar, who was supervising the investigation in the case, has already retired and was hence not available for comment.

Heading: 8 firms apply for study of high-speed rail corridor - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration today decided to install a common unified bio-medical waste facility for the entire city in Dadumajra.

This was said in an undertaking given in the wake of a petition filed by ten residents of Sector 16 in Chandigarh, demanding a stop in the

operation of the incinerator in General Hospital in Sector 16, next to the residential area, which is being used for burning bio-medical waste without any air pollution control device in place.

State counsel Anupam Gupta further said the Administration will soon float expression of interests (EoI) for the installation of plant.

Notices were then issued to Director Health Services, the chief architect, department of Urban Planning, UT Municipal Corporation and Secretary Health, UT Administration on October 19.

The facility will dispose the entire bio-medical waste with proper air pollution control devices as opposed to separate incinerators for each hospital in the city like PGI, GH-16 and GMCH-32, Chandigarh.

The petition had further demanded stopping the construction of a seven-storey OPD block in front of the houses of the petitioners.

The reply filed by the Administration on the last date of hearing read: "Having separate incinerators for each hospital and monitoring their disposal is a tedious task since vehicles carrying the waste are to be properly covered."

Recording the statement of state counsel Anupam Gupta, the Division Bench comprising of Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh adjourned the case till next month.

Heading: ISRO men share ‘moment of pride’ with city - Indian Express
Content:
The request for proposal (RFP) floated by the Indian Railways for the pre-feasibility study of the Rs 60,000 crore 'High Speed Passenger Corridor' between Delhi-Chandigarh-Amritsar received applications from eight companies on Tuesday, the last date for submission of applications for the same.

The project, to come up on the basis of a public private partnership (PPP), had not attracted even a single consultant for a pre-feasibility study of the corridor earlier.

Senior officials handling the project said the exorbitant cost and a great deal of planning could have served as a deterrent for them.

Sources, meanwhile, say that eight companies have applied this time, of which, some are said to be global players and another month is needed to finalise the consultant.

The consultant will be appointed to carry out the study report to evaluate the financial viability, technical feasibility, maintenance and management of facilities on the proposed corridor.

This will be followed by a more detailed study focusing on the traffic pattern, funding plan, stakeholders' view, fare structure and other related issues before work on the corridor begins.

The report will be made with a comparative study of various technologies available including Shinkansen between Tokyo and Osaka.

As the proposed train is to cross Panipat, Karnal, Ambala, Chandigarh, Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Kapurthala and Phagwara, the cost of the pre-feasibility study will be shared by Punjab, Haryana and the Railway Ministry.

"The entire stretch will be fenced and there won't be any crossing to avoid collision. For this purpose, new tracks will be laid with new locomotives and rakes. With such a high cost proposition, the tickets are also expected to be costly," a senior railway official said. Besides Delhi-Amritsar, the railways has also decided to conduct pre-feasibility studies on four more high speed passenger routes. They are Pune-Mumbai-Ahmedabad, Hyderabad-Dornakal-Vijaywada-Chennai, Howrah-Haldia and Chennai-Bangalore-Coimbatore-Ernakulum.

Heading: Court pulls up new UT legal remembrancer - Indian Express
Content:
It was a day the Indian tricolour marked its first presence on the moon after Chandrayaan-1's Impact Probe, with the Indian flag painted on it, detached from the ship and landed on the lunar surface. Needless to say, scientists from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) who were at the PGI on Friday were a jubilant lot. The scientists are here to take part in a national telemedicine conference.

Distributing pamphlets, stickers and literature concerning India's first unmanned spacecraft lunar mission, the men from ISRO said it was a moment of pride for them.

A Bhaskaranarayana, Scientific Secretary, ISRO, said: "We have the contingency fuel ready for the mission in case more is required than what is estimated. But so far, we are pleased to say, all our estimates are bang on target. Steering of the spacecraft to its final orbit was crucial and we achieved it with precision. Since the contingency fuel is lying unspent, we can contemplate extending the mission by another year."

The mission was first conceived in 2003 when Dr A P J Abdul Kalam was the President. While the scientists talked about the Chandrayaan-1 at PGI, the former President was incidentally at a separate function in the city, asking the countrymen to take pride in the ISRO's achievement.

"We had made the presentation of the Chandrayaan mission before him (Dr Kalam) when he was in office in 2003. We received a lot of encouragement and guidance. In fact, he was the main brain behind the moon impact probe (MIP) technology in Chandrayaan," said A Bhaskaranarayana.

MIP is one of the 11 scientific instruments onboard Chandrayaan-1, which was launched on October 22 and entered the lunar orbit on November 8.

Stating that the lunar mission so far is on the "right track", Bhaskaranarayana said the biggest challenge for the ISRO before the launch of the spacecraft was perhaps to determine the exact target in the varying temperature of the moon. "The radio signals begin weakening by the time they reach earth. Indian Deep Space Network performs the crucial task of receiving these signals through the indigenously developed antennas."

Chandrayaan II will involve sending a rover, an automatic robot, to the moon to collect matters like rock from deep below the lunar surface. The scientists said this would further help in gathering more accurate information about the moon. The rover will send information to the mothership that will be received by the earth station.

So what next? "ISRO is busy developing cryogenic engines (rocket motors designed for liquid fuels — hydrogen and oxygen — that have to be held at very low "cryogenic" temperatures to be liquid; they would otherwise be gas at normal temperatures) indigenously. The project should see results by April next year," signed off Bhaskaranarayana.

Heading: Where has innocence gone? - Indian Express
Content:
HC: Dhonchak causing hindrance in inquiry by repeatedly filing applications

Newly appointed UT Legal Remembrancer M M Dhonchak earned the wrath of Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday for causing hindrance in a judicial inquiry pending against him, by repeatedly filing applications in the court.

A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh came down heavily on M M Dhonchak, posted as Additional District and Sessions Judge (Ad hoc) of Fast Track Court, Ambala, at present. He has filed an application demanding quashing of the chargesheet issued to him by the Full Court four years ago.

"This officer needs to be dealt with properly. He is trying to convolute us in a web of applications. He just does not allow the inquiry to go on smoothly. Tell your client to cooperate. We will not allow him to make a mockery of the law," an angry Thakur told the counsel appearing for Dhonchak.

Advising the counsel to withdraw the application filed by Dhonchak, the Division Bench held that if the officer felt wronged, the aspect would be looked into. Dhonchak was present in the court on Friday. Sitting in the back row, he stood up immediately after the Chief Justice asked his counsel if Dhonchak was present. "Kyun bhai! Inquiry nahin karni deni (Don't you want the inquiry to go on)?" Thakur asked.

Dhonchak replied: "I have not been given an opportunity to say anything. My career, bread and butter are at stake. My every application speaks the truth." Not convinced with the averments, the Chief Justice said: "You face the inquiry and prove your innocence. If you think the inquiry officer is biased, we will examine that issue but you cannot make a mockery of the law like this." The application was finally dismissed as withdrawn.

The High Court had issued a chargesheet to Dhonchak on July 14, 2004. There are as many as 19 charges against him. Dhonchak was chargesheeted when he was the additional chief judicial magistrate of Sirsa. The first charge against him was that he had got annoyed with the counsel for the accused in a case. It was further alleged that while sentencing the accused on January 7, 1998, Dhonchak had directed that the sentence would not run concurrently. It was also alleged that an exorbitant fine of Rs 63,000 was imposed without assigning any specific reason.

Dhonchak had demanded quashing of the chargesheet on several grounds. He had submitted that the copy of the order pertaining to the appointment of an inquiry officer was not supplied to him.

"There is no likelihood of an impartial inquiry since the chargesheet was approved by the Full Court. Some of the judges who were members of the chargesheet committee formed part of the Full Court at the time it passed the decision to hold inquiry against the petitioner. The very presence of them in the Full Court meeting has vitiated the order of holding inquiry against Dhonchak," his application reads.

Heading: For them, it’s just another day - Indian Express
Content:
Police records show crime by juveniles on a steady rise in the city

2006: A 15-year-old was arrested as one of the accused in the rape and brutal murder of a 71-year-old woman in Sector 15. The news had sent shockwaves across the nation. The minor, lodged in a juvenile home at present, had allegedly committed the ghastly act under the influence of drugs, especially white correction fluid. The sale of this fluid to children has been banned in the city ever since.
February 2007: One of the four people arrested for the murder of a Palsora resident included a minor boy.
March 2008: The Manimajra police arrested five minors in a rioting case. All school dropouts, the teenagers had attacked another group after a tiff.

On Children's Day, when the entire city celebrated innocence, there were many minors who spent the day in juvenile homes. They were all caught on the wrong side of the law in the recent past. The city's crime graph shows a disturbing trend — the number of crimes involving juveniles is on the rise.

This year's data shows culprits in over 68 thefts were juveniles, 14 were involved in rioting, six in injury cases, four in robberies, nine in burglaries, one each in kidnapping and assault. A total of 120 children were arrested in 2008. The number was 118 last year.

From petty thefts to rape, abduction and murder, crime cases involving children are rising with each passing year. 

A glance at Chandigarh's crime graph reveals that several juveniles are indulging in mobile phone and vehicle thefts, chain snatchings and burglaries to make a quick buck.

According to the police, their sole objective behind taking to crime is to lead a life of luxury — trendy clothes, two-wheelers and dining at good restaurants.

While various factors have contributed to this, the police mainly attribute the disturbing trend to their living conditions as most of them are from the colonies and slums.

According to statistics, a total of 81 cases involving juveniles have been reported this year under various sections of the IPC. Last year, a total of 68 such cases were registered.

Two minors have also been arrested this year under the Excise Act while one was caught with drugs.

Police officers say a huge number of children in conflict with the law (above 60 per cent) are illiterate or school dropouts.

Police statistics also reveal that the age of a majority of the youngsters varies between 12 and 15 years. The maximum cases involving juveniles are reported from Sector 17 and Manimajra.

"Most of the arrested juveniles are school dropouts who loitered around throughout the day before taking to crime. Some of them have attended school till Class V while there are many who shunned studies after Class X," says a police officer.

Psychologist Dr Ashok Gupta says: "Besides urbanisation, lack of social controls, both at home and in schools, has been largely responsible for children going astray. Changing lifestyles, crumbling joint families and a market-driven society have rendered our children valueless," he said.

Heading: Chandrayaan-1 success a result - Indian Express
Content:
For eight-year-old Pappu, there were no cakes, balloons, gifts or new clothes. His day passed as usual — sifting through garbage, segregating the saleable material and cleaning utensils at a dhaba.

On Friday, this correspondent cornered Pappu at one of the garbage dumps, where he was at work along with Chhotu. Asked if he knew it was Baal Diwas (Children's Day), he gave a blank look and replied: "Baal diwas kis bala ka naam hai (What does Children's Day mean)?"

When asked about "Chacha Nehru", Chhotu giggled: "Mera koi chacha, taya nahin hai, sirf ek baap tha, jo do baras pehle mar gaya (I don't have uncles, had a father who died two years ago)."

Wearing a torn and dirty pair of trousers and a shirt, which barely protected him from the dipping mercury, the illiterate ragpicker's story is heart-rending. While he never saw his mother who had died immediately after his birth, Chhotu's father, a drug addict, died when he was five. Since then, he had been working hard to earn his bread.

On Children's Day, 10-year-old Ramu's tiny hands were breaking bricks. Abandoned by parents, he has two younger sisters who depend on him.

Most of the underprivileged children this reporter spoke to had no idea of Children's Day and neither did they want to know about its importance. To manage two meals a day, these children work all day, sifting through garbage, cleaning utensils, selling tea, begging at public places, breaking bricks and doing anything that can earn them a few bucks. Evidently, the amended Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, which was enforced across the country on October 10, 2006, has failed to serve the purpose.

Heading: Airline to pay Rs 5,000 for baggage loss - Indian Express
Content:
"The success of Chandrayaan-1 is result of team effort. This is the reason for which every Indian should feel proud," said Dr A P J Abdul Kalam, former President of India, the brain behind the Moon Impact Probe (MIP) technology used in Chandrayaan.

He said this while inaugurating the national seminar on Recent Advances in Aerospace Technologies, Maintenance and Optimisation (AEROTECH-08), organised by the Chandigarh branch of the Aeronautical Society of India and Terminal Ballistics Research Laboratory, Chandigarh.

He later interacted with schoolchildren and greeted them on the occasion of Children's Day.

The main objective of the seminar was to provide a platform for the free flow of information and sharing of knowledge and experience between the veterans and the youth.

Dr Kalam said that India has made significant growth in aerospace technology during the last five decades and appreciated the efforts of the scientists of the Indian Space and Research Organisation (ISRO) for the successful placement of Chandrayaan in the lunar orbit.

The other guests included Dr Satish Kumar, chairman, Aeronautical Society of India - Chandigarh branch, Dr VG Sekaran, associate director, Advanced Systems Laboratory and project director AGNI, besides BN Gokhale, former Vice Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal and Professor R C Sobti, vice-chancellor, Panjab University, among others. The two-day seminar will conclude on Saturday.

God is abstract while science is figurative, Kalam tells students

"India is not far from becoming a super power and its greatest asset, the youth, will lead it to the path of glory," said former President Dr A P J Abdul Kalam while addressing the students of Bhavan Vidyalya on the occasion of Children's Day today.

The one-hour session with the "People's President" provided an opportunity to students as he answered their questions from diverse fields like politics, science and spirituality apart from regaling them with anecdotes from his life. When asked about the relation between man and god, he said that even though spiritualism and realism are two different aspects, one must try to strike a balance between the two.

"God is abstract while science is figurative. Instead of following either of the two blindly, we should try to imbibe the good aspects of both. It is neither essential nor feasible to view life with a scientific outlook," he said.

When a student asked him if he saw any scope of improvement in the current state of politics in the country, he said: "There are two types of politics; one political and the other developmental. While in the former, one competes for a seat in the Assembly, the latter has more to do with the development of the nation, both economic and social. To improve the state of affairs, we should follow the ratio of 70:30; i.e. 70 per cent development politics and the rest political."

Residents get a dose of 'Kalamism'

The auditorium was jam-packed, the gathering did not move till his speech got over, a majority were eager to try their hands at the tricky little questions being thrown at them and a thunderous applaud greeted him at the end of a long inaugural lecture.

The gathering of budding and seasoned Biochemists at GMCH-32 was a testimony of the charisma that former President of India Dr A P J Abdul Kalam holds over the masses and the scientific community alike.

"I am sorry for having pushed you all by two hours. My programme was changed at the last minute," he said, referring to a change in his schedule, before beginning his talk on "Biochemistry Challenges in Medicine" at the annual national conference of Medical Biochemists in the city.

So, what was the country's most famous scientist's message for the Biochemists? It was a vision for the future. "The first phase of genetic mapping of the Indian population is complete and the results were out in April this year. This should be made a part of the curriculum in schools so that students can develop medicines for the needs of the Indian people," he said.

Next, he gave them advice to study the newly developed test for typhoid. "Defence Research and Development Establishment, Gwalior, has developed a new test for diagnosing typhoid, which affects a large number of children in the country. Your institute should also work on this test to make it affordable."

He also put a deadline of 3 years before them for developing medicines for chronic ailments like cardiovascular diseases and diabetes.

His lecture also included the contribution of two well-known biochemists, Professor G N Ramachandran and Dr Har Gobind Khorana.

In between the scientific talk, there was space for some practical humour too. One such occasion arose when he made the doctors take an oath asking them to repeat: "I love my profession, particularly medical profession which is a noble profession. I realise removing the pain is a godly vision. I will treat all patients with kindness and care," towards the end of the lecture. And the young doctors repeated his words in cue, till he said: "I will take special care of 20 rural patients." This was received amid chuckles.

Heading: Hotel charges VAT but does not give bill, told to pay up - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed an airline company to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for loading the baggage of a family to another airport. The compensation will be paid for the mental and physical harassment the complainant faced due to the negligent act.

Anil Salwan, a resident of Sector 39, had booked a holiday package of three night and four days from October 14-17, 2007, with return tickets from Delhi to Port Blair for Rs 1,98,823.

The complainant, along with other three members of his family, boarded the Sahara Jet Life flight from Delhi to Port Blair on the scheduled day. Their luggage was duly deposited in the cargo before the flight. When the flight landed at Port Blair the same day, the complainant was told that his luggage had been mistakenly offloaded at the Kolkata airport.

After a complaint to the concerned authorities, Salwan was told that due to some misunderstanding their employees had offloaded his luggage and he would get it in the next flight of Jet Airways at 8 am the following morning. The luggage never reached in the next flight too.

Salwan was then told that the luggage will arrive in the own plane of Sahara Jet Lite scheduled to reach Port Blair on October 15, 2007. The complainant averred that by that time, more than one and a half of the four-day holiday had become a dull affair. As all the clothes and articles of daily use were in the luggage, the complainant stated he had to spend another Rs 3,500. It was averred that the complainant went through a harrowing time as some valuable articles were also lying in the baggage.

The family spent Rs 2 lakh for the tour but the entire aura was spoilt, read the complaint.
