In its reply, Sahara Jet lite said what happened was only due to the mistake of the airlines or the airport's ground handling staff.

The forum said that missing the luggage was a negligence act of the airline.

Heading: High Court disposes of Tahar Singh case - Indian Express
Content:
Holding that it is mandatory for any hotel or restaurant to issue a printed bill if it charges value added tax (VAT), the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed a restaurant to pay compensation and refund the amount charged as VAT.

By not issuing a printed bill to the customer after charging VAT, the forum said, Yummy Yummy Food Court in Sector 37 indulged in unfair trade practice and should hence refund Rs 58, in addition to a compensation of Rs 1,000.

The complainant, Rajeev Chaudhery, a resident of Sector 7, Panchkula, had gone to the restaurant along with his family in May this year.

They ordered three buffet meals for Rs 149 each, totalling to Rs 447.

After they had finished with the dinner and demanded the bill, a waiter verbally told them to pay Rs 505, including VAT. Chaudhery asked the waiter to give him a bill, showing the break-up, upon which he was given a "handwritten bill" on a plain piece of paper.

Demanding a printed bill, Chaudhery asked the waiter to call the manager, who came after 15 minutes and said they were unable to provide a printed bill but would issue one on the hotel's letter pad.

The complainant then told the manager that they could not demand VAT without giving a proper, printed bill to the customer. after which the latter allegedly got angry and used foul language, forcing Chaudhery to pay Rs 505 as the total bill.

The complainant then moved the consumer forum.

On receiving a notice from the forum, Pushpinder Singh, managing director of the restaurant, appeared on the first hearing and sought time to file a reply. Noone, however, turned up on behalf of the hotel thereafter.

The forum observed that charging VAT without issuing a permanent, printed bill surely amounted to unfair trade practice and deficiency in service. This way, the forum said, the hotel charged Rs 58 extra which it should refund to the customer.

Heading: Forest Hill Resort case: IFS officer demands quashing of FIR - Indian Express
Content:
Almost a year and a half after an 'unusual' order by Justice Uma Nath Singh sent Advocate Tahar Singh to mental asylum, leading to a furore in the legal fraternity, the petition challenging the same was disposed of by a Division Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

The petition was disposed after a Division Bench comprising Justice M M Kumar and Justice Surya Kant was told that Tahar and his wife were divorced.

The orders were passed on July 23, 2007, after Tahar's wife alleged in a letter that she was being mentally harassed. After the court's orders, the CBI had taken Tahar in custody and almost to the mental asylum. However, the then chief justice had constituted an immediate division bench in this regard, which had stayed the orders passed by Justice Uma Nath Singh.

Choosing not to go into the propriety of the original, the Division Bench held on Friday: "The fundamental dispute to the necessity of passing of order for his medical examination had arisen on account of matrimonial differences between Tahar and Sujata Sharma, which stand settled. Therefore, at this stage, no useful purpose will be served by going into the propriety or illegality of passing the order dated July 23, 2007, which led to the filing of this petition, especially when the order does not amount to any declaration declaring Tahar as suffering from any mental incapacity".

Dispensing the judgment, the Division Bench observed: "A long drawn battle has come to a nice end." The ex-wife of Tahar thanked the court.

Meanwhile, counsel appearing for Tahar submitted that he would not visit his wife at her residence where his children are also residing. He had undertaken not to even go near around the said place of residence. "Accordingly, this statement will continue to operate," the High Court held.

Heading: Students protest lack of facilities in college hostel - Indian Express
Content:
In a fresh twist to the ongoing Forest Hill Resort case, Harsh Kumar, an Indian Forest Services (IFS) officer filed an application in the Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday demanding the quashing of the FIR registered against him. At present, Kumar is posted as Conservator of Forests, Research and Training, Hoshiarpur.

Kumar alleged that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is hand-in-glove with the rival party, a retired IFS officer, in the case. The CBI had registered the case against Kumar on the basis of a written statement given by S K Bhatti, an advocate and a key witness. In his application, Kumar referred to Bhatti's statement before a lower court that he (Bhatti) did not implicate Kumar in his complaint.

Terming the case as false, Kumar demanded that the FIR be quashed and action be taken against the CBI. The application was taken on record and will come up for hearing next month.

On August 4, the High Court had allowed an application filed by the CBI wherein it has sought permission to place on record the final status report of the infamous Forest Hill Resort case. The CBI had recommended criminal prosecution and registration of FIRs on charges of cheating, corruption and violation of the Periphery Act against several IAS and IFS officers involved in the scam. The resort is located at Karoran village in the Ropar district.

Heading: The joys of childhood - Indian Express
Content:
After students of MCMDAV College, it was the turn of girls from Guru Gobind Singh College for Women to hit the streets to press for their demands. Huge drama prevailed outside the college on Friday after the hostellers protested against the lack of facilities. Girls from the hostel sat in protest at the gate and did not even allow the faculty to enter the college premises for over two hours. The students stated that though they were being charged Rs 35,000 as hostel fee, they were not getting adequate facilities.

The classes remained suspended due to the protest and the police had to be called in after the girls refused to move. After almost two hours, the girls agreed to speak to the principal.

It was during this discussion that it was decided that a meeting would be held on Saturday to resolve the issue.

The girls, meanwhile, maintained that they would not allow classes to proceed even tomorrow or till their demands were met with. The students also claimed that the hostel fee has been increased from Rs 25,000 to Rs 35,000. The authorities, however, stated that the prospectus clearly mentions the hostel fee as Rs 35,000.

The girls also raised slogans against the college authorities with banners and posters in their hands. Preeti, a BCom III year student, said, "We have many a times complained of fungus in the rooms and also of cockroaches in the food. However, no action has been taken till date."

Another B Com III year student, Kanika rued, "The washrooms are leaking and the rooms too are full of filth. The hostel authorities are cramming up more girls in less space and the quality of food would fail any test. We have complained on several occasions but it seems to have fallen on deaf ears."

College principal Harinderjit Kaur, meanwhile, said, "We are trying our best to provide every facility to the students and as far as the hostel fee is concerned, it has clearly been mentioned in the prospectus so we can do nothing about the same."

Heading: On their day, kids from rural Punjab celebrate confidence - Indian Express
Content:
Schools across Chandigarh celebrated Children's Day. Students and teachers took part in competitions like painting, declamation and fancy dress that were organised to mark the occasion

Sacred Heart School: As a tribute to Pandit Nehru and his love for children, students of the school celebrated Children's Day in the school premises with great joy and enthusiasm. A variety of entertainment programmes including skits, music and dance shows were organised by teachers to mark the celebrations. Sister Sebastina, principal, and the staff renewed their commitment to the welfare of children and pledged to live by Chacha Nehru's dream. A painting competition was also organised for students of Classes VI to XII. 

St Xavier's Senior Secondary School: Children's Day was celebrated at the school with great pomp and show. A special assembly was organised where teachers spoke on the life and works of Pandit Nehru to enlighten the children about his personality. Competitions like slogan-writing, poster-making, rangoli and tattoo-making were also organised.

Kendriya Vidyalaya, High Grounds: The school celebrated the day with fun and fervour. Children of primary and secondary sections took part in a fancy dress competition. A quiz contest based on the life of Jawaharlal Nehru was also held.

 

Kendriya Vidyalaya I, Chandi Mandir: A function was organised for the students of the primary section by the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan, Chandigarh Region. Colourful folk dances of Bihar, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan were presented by students on the occasion.

 

Saupin's School: The school organised a special cultural programme to celebrate Children's Day. While teachers spoke about being a good educator, the students talked about the responsibility of being a good citizen. A western and Punjabi dance was also performed by the teachers of the school.

 

Government Model Middle School, Sector 23: During the day, a host of programmes and activities including a speech competition, dance and instrumental performances were presented by the participants.

Sherwood Convent School: Tiny tots came dressed as Chacha Nehru with red roses carefully tucked in their sherwanis and holding the National Flag. Speeches were delivered by the students highlighting the life and works of Pandit Nehru. Principal Kusum Singhal advised students to follow the footprints of Nehru and contribute to the development of the nation.

PML SD Public School: Tiny tots of the junior wing participated in a number of sport activities such as frog race, banana race, spoon and lemon race, badminton and a cricket match.

 

Shemrock School: Students participated in the cross-country race. This was followed by art and rangoli competitions. Students of Classes I and II made bookmarks while students of Classes III and IV participated in a story illustration competition. The winners were awarded medals and bags by The Indian Express.

 

Satluj Public School: The celebrations began with the students delivering speeches on the significance of the day. Students recited poems in English and Hindi as a tribute to the great leader. A cultural event 'Freedom of Expression' was also held on the occasion. The day culminated with a basketball match between the students and teachers.

 

AKSIPS, Sector 41: Tiny tots of pre-primary and primary classes took part in various races such as biscuit race, lemon race and frog race. Personifying Chacha Nehru, Anurag gave an inspiring speech highlighting the incidents of his life which brought him close to children.

Dev Samaj College: Dev Samaj College of Education in collaboration with the ENVIS Centre, UT department of Environment had organised an environment fest. The aim was to create awareness regarding the preservation of environment among schoolchildren. Over 182 students from 17 schools participated in various competitions including poem recitation, group song, poster-making, paper bag making and best-out-of-waste products.  

St Xavier's High School, Panchkula: A cultural show consisting of games for the students, Antakshari, speeches and poems was organised by the teachers of the school on the occasion. The 'Xavarian Rockers' consisting of Neil Kulkarni, Katrike and Saumya entertained the audience with Bryan Adams songs. 'Xavarian Swash Swingers' captured the imagination of the students as they danced to the rhythm of Camp Rock. Principal George S Shear addressed the gathering and reminded students of their duties as future stakeholders of the country.

Hallmark School, Panchkula: Children's Day at the school was dedicated to the caretakers in the school. The students, apart from organising games for their caretakers, also showcased a vibrant dance performance. A round of singing and dancing was followed by the prize distribution ceremony. The director of the school, Jivtesh Garg, emphasised that present day kids need to be sensitised about the dignity of labour. Principal Neelinderjeet Sandhu said that the entire show was aimed to instill the qualities of compassion, caring and sharing in the students.

Blue Bird High School, Panchkula: The teachers at the school took a lead to entertain the students .They came dressed as students of the school and spoke about Jawaharlal Nehru. Director Principal R Bhatnagar also addressed the students on the occasion. A face-painting competition was organised for the students of Class IX and X.

Ryan International School, Patiala: The montessori section started celebrations a week ago in the form of a Children's Week from November 7 itself. Various competitions and games were organised for students of Classes I-VIII. A good handwriting competition was also organised by Hindustan Pencils Pvt Ltd.

PGI: The department of Paediatrics at PGI organised a cultural programme in association with an NGO Sankalp of Government College, Sector 11 for children admitted in the hospital on the occasion of Bal Diwas. Students also distributed fruits and biscuits among children.

Senior Citizens Association: Children's Day was also celebrated by the Chandigarh Senior Citizens Association. Members of the association visited the physically challenged children of Prayaas, a rehabilitation centre. The association adopted two underprivileged children and will provide financial help to them.

Heading: Day after, student gets admission in school - Indian Express
Content:
While the city and its adjoining areas celebrated Children's Day with the usual trappings today, an educational institute near Ropar is celebrating the spirit of the day round the year — by shaping the lives of about 50 children from the rural heartland of Punjab.

At the GCS Collegiate School, Bhaddal, the difference was there for all to see at the Children's Day function organised on the campus on Friday. Boys and girls in their mid-teens, who used to be tongue-tied among their urban counterparts earlier, spoke impressively. Their English may not have been all that correct, but they are working on it. Today, it was their confidence that made one sit up and take notice.

The school is part of the 'Rural Development and Social Welfare' efforts of the Institute of Engineering and Technology (IET), Bhaddal. The school charges a nominal fee and was opened by the institute last year for Class IX. This year, it has two classes, IX and X. The authorities plan to extend it to Class XII, and also begin a kindergarten.

So what has sparked off the change in the children? "Our overall emphasis is on education. Students are in the school from 9.30 am to 4.30 pm, and we encourage them to interact with their teachers for any problem. Our children should have no need for tuitions," says Ravinder Singh, the CEO of the institute.

The school follows the curriculum of the Punjab School Education Board (PSEB). The teaching of Science and Maths is in English medium.

And what gives it the winning edge is that special personality development classes are held daily for children.

Indeed, the efforts are paying off. Talk to the children and the difference is apparent. Nishant Raj, from Mandwara village, is a student of Class X. "Coming to this school has made me focus on academics in a whole new way. I have fixed hours for study now. My parents are astounded to find me studying even as the whole house is sleeping," says Nishant, who wants to grow up to be a chartered accountant.

Gurpreet Kaur, a student of Class IX, has been here only since April when the new session began. She says there is a change not only in her, but in her two younger sisters as well. "I now encourage my sisters to talk like me, to conduct themselves like me, and also to study like me," she says candidly. "We are all more focused on studies now. I know I will be a computer engineer when I grow up," says the confident one.

Seema Thapar, who teaches the students Social Studies and Hindi, says she is often touched by the change in them. "Take the case of Gurwinder Singh, who is in Class X. He used to study in the previous school where I taught, and had failed in Class VIII. Here, he is a different boy altogether," observes Seema.

Gurwinder, a resident of Bhaddal village, says there is no question of failing now. "I want to excel now and in every field. I study hard, and I will prove myself," he says with a quiet determination.

The children daily wait for the class of Ruchika Dogra, who takes the sessions in personality development. "Every day, I see a change in their social conduct, their personal interaction and their self-confidence," Ruchika notes.

The institute's CEO says he observed that most of the students coming to IET Bhaddal were from other places, and not the local areas. "We are committed to develop our local area. So we decided to start our own school and bring the students into the science stream, and also study in English medium. Now, their personality development is way ahead of their peers in other local schools. The infrastructure we provide them — access to the Internet, the library and laboratory, the excellent teachers, and also the sports facilities — are all of college level."

Gurinder Singh, a Class X student who comes from Chamkaur Sahib, says he and his class-fellows are inspired when they see the engineering students here.

Agrees Nirbhay Singh of Class IX, "One day, I will study engineering too. I will work hard and realise my dream."

Heading: Red Ribbon Express reaches Ambala - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Newsline reported about the negligence of the Education department while giving admission to a student Prakash Jha, officials swung into action to grant him admission in a course he is eligible for. The department has decided to admit the student in Class XI in Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 23 in the vocational AC and Refrigeration course.  

Department officials have also sped up the process of completing the documents required for his admission. Since it was reported on Thursday that the student's form had gone missing from the department's records, Director Public Instructions (Schools) clarified the department's stand saying, "As Prakash is seeking admission in a new course, we will start the procedure from the scratch. He will be filling a new application for the course. Hence, the previous form stands void." 

Prakash, meanwhile, expressed satisfaction over the redressal of his problem. "I am happy that the officials have taken personal interest in the matter. I was very worried about losing a year but now I am hopeful of attending classes in the new school soon," said Prakash.  

Newsline had reported yesterday about Prakash, who had secured admission in Class XI in Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 33, in the IT course for the current academic session. But when he went to attend classes in the school, he was told that he was not eligible for the course as he did not have the required aggregate for the course. While the cut-off for the stream was 60 per cent, Prakash had scored 57 per cent. The school authorities also told him that they had neither received his form nor the fee, failing which they could not issue him a migration certificate.

Heading: ‘Present crisis in state result of Centre’s wrong policies’ - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Financial Commissioner and Principal Secretary, Health, Anuradha Gupta flagged off six teams that will travel in the Red Ribbon Express train to create awareness about HIV/AIDS among villagers. The teams were formed and trained by the Nehru Yuva Kendra.

Hundreds of children from different schools and trainees from a few nursing schools gathered at the Ambala Cantonment railway station where the Red Ribbon Express reached on Friday. National AIDS Control Society secretary Daman Ahuja, who is travelling in the train, briefed them about the aims and objectives of the project.

On a year-long journey across 24 states, the train was flagged off from Delhi on December 1, 2007, by UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The seven-coach train, in which an exhibition is on, has an auditorium to impart training, counselling and provide clinical services.

The train will have a two-day stopover at Ambala, during which Nehru Yuva Kendra volunteers, under the supervision of coordinator K P S Gill, will hold corner meetings and present skits and songs.

After taking a round of the train, Gupta said the dreaded disease was on the rise in the country.

She said there were 30 lakh HIV patients with 42,000 positive cases in India, of which 286 positive HIV cases had been found in Haryana.

No official from the railways was present at the function. A senior official said the rail administration was not involved in conducting the programme, though it was held on the railway premises. Neither the district administration, nor the National AIDS Control Organisation reportedly extended a formal invitation to them.

Earlier, Deputy Commissioner S P Sarow administered oath to the students and members of the teams to dedicate their services in eradication of the disease. Indian Medical Association's local unit president Dr D S Goel assured of full cooperation to the movement.

Interacting with the media later at the PWD Rest House, Anuradha Gupta said Rs 50 lakh had been granted to each of the 20 districts for distribution of free medicines among patients. She said there would not be any shortage of health staff, including doctors in the civil hospitals, especially at delivery huts.

She said inverters had been supplied to each delivery hut to cope with the shortage of power supply. She warned that erring officials would be dealt with strictly if found indulging in prescribing medicines for purchase from outside the hospital.

Heading: MC can hold Apni Mandi in Sector 15: court - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government has prepared a four-point programme to usher in a socio-economic revolution in the state, Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh said, while inaugurating the week-long celebrations to mark the 55th All India Cooperative Week at Verka Milk Plant in Phase VI, in Mohali on Friday. The programme will be implemented through the Cooperative department.

He added that the strategy has been formulated to bail out the state from the serious economic crisis being faced at the moment.

Under the programme, the Cooperative department will formulate plans for the social, economic and political empowerment of women to make them self-reliant and ensure their equal participation in every field.

He said the scheme also plans to provide houses to the economically weaker sections of the society and this responsibility has been entrusted to Housefed.

"Special efforts will also be made to generate more and more job opportunities to remove widespread unemployment in the state," he said.

He said the present crisis in the state is the result of wrong economic policies adopted by the Centre, under which, input instruments and other ingredients are provided to farmers in the state on high costs whereas prices of their produce are fixed lower than even its actual cost of production.

"Crop diversification is being encouraged with special emphasis on dairy farming and other alternative works with a view to bring farmers out of this mess," he disclosed.

Referring to Milkfed, the Minister said its milk procurement has increased by more than 30 per cent in the last one year after it succeeded in winning the confidence of those producers who were earlier attached with other multinational companies.

He said the Cooperative department has tied up with three multinational companies including Escorts India Pvt. Ltd, Philips and Dixon India Ltd for the supply of household goods at 30 per cent less rate to more than 50 lakh members of Cooperative Societies in the state.

Heading: Pherurai case: HC directs Punjab govt to finish probe - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant decision, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has clarified on Friday that there was no stay on holding Apni Mandi in Sector 15.

Leaving it to the UT Municipal Corporation to decide if it wants to hold the mandi, a Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur and Justice Jasbir Singh made it clear that the court had never passed any such orders.

A letter issued a couple of years ago by an advocate representing the MC seeking instructions as to whether the mandi should be held in Sector 15, was mistook as the High Court orders by the civic body. Owing to this, the MC had stopped holding the Apni Mandi in Sector 15.

On the other hand, Advocate Anupam Gupta, senior standing counsel for the UT Administration, said the Administration did not object to it. The directions were passed in the wake of a public interest litigation (PIL) wherein the decision of the Chandigarh Administration to stop holding the Apni Mandi had been challenged.

Applications were filed by the Residents Welfare Associations of Sector 11, 14, 15 and 16, demanding that the mandi be held regularly.

Moreover, on October 16, the High Court had stayed any further construction or change in the ownership of a one-acre land near Floral Garden in Sector 15.

The change in the ownership was stayed after apprehensions were raised that the one acre plot in Sector 15, where the Apni Mandi was held earlier, will be handed over to some private party so that the mandi is not held in future. Since the High Court has cleared that there is no stay orders, it is for the MC to decide if it wants to hold Apni Mandi again in Sector 15.

Heading: Affair gone wrong: woman strangled - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Punjab government to complete the inquiry to find out if the police witnesses had resiled under pressure in a fake currency case, resulting in the acquittal of retired senior superintendent of police G S Pherurai.

The High Court has given two weeks time to the state government to submit its report. Punjab Advocate General (AG) H S Mattewal submitted that the inquiry was already on and a report has been given to the state government but it is yet to be submitted in the court.

Pherurai had been acquitted by a trial court in the fake currency scam after the police witnesses and a bank manager turned hostile. The High Court had, however, taken a suo motu note of the witnesses turning hostile in the case and issued notices to all of them, asking them to file affidavits.

In their reply, the witnesses had alleged that Pherurai, along with other senior police officials including the then SSP Jagraon and SP Vigilance, had threatened them to resile from their statements else they will be booked in false cases.

The defence counsel for Pherurai submitted on Friday that the inquiry officer is not looking into the fact that the case registered against the former SSP was false.

Heading: A Dalliance with dali - Indian Express
Content:
Illicit relations between a couple working as Class IV employees in a private hospital ended in a murder on Thursday. Thirty-year-old Sangeeta Devi, a resident of Colony Number 5, was killed by her paramour Ashok Kumar. The incident occurred in Mauli village in Mohali, Sohana Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector Mohinder Singh told Newsline.

After the murder, Ashok walked to the police station and confessed to his crime, following which, he was arrested. He has been sent to a day's police remand, said the SHO.

Sangeeta and Ashok had entered into a verbal dual at around 8 pm on Thursday, following which, he strangled her to death, Sangeeta's husband Balram Mauriya told the police. Mauriya said that on Wednesday too, the duo had had a duel which was later sorted out.

Mauriya rushed to Ashok's rented accommodation in Mauli village on Thursday after Sangeeta did not return home, where he found the room bolted from inside.

Mauriya said he saw Ashok strangling his wife and Sangeeta was dead by the time he could help.

Preliminary investigations revealed the two were having an extra-marital affair for the past couple of years and Ashok was insisting that she marry him. As Sangeeta was reluctant, the issue snow-balled, revealed the SHO. Both Sangeeta and Ashok have two children from their marriages.

Heading: Northern Light - Indian Express
Content:
He may have earned reputation as an entertainer, but Salman Khan hates to talk

Expect him to do the unexpected. Salman Khan, who enjoys the reputation of being a latecomer, is already parked on a chair outside his vanity van at Mehboob Studio. Dressed in a brown tee, media's favourite bashing boy patiently indulges in elaborate interviews. His staff — secretary, media relations person, bodyguards, tea vendor and assorted "friends" — hang around to ensure his comfort, bringing alive the otherwise deserted studio.

His media friendliness is apparent but he candidly attributes it to his "duty" towards his producers. "With three films ready for release, the producers are on my head to promote them. It isn't that I hate the media. I'm just not the sort who talks. Why talk when a look can convey it all?" he winks.

The last two years have been rather unusually quiet for Salman at the box office — he has done special appearances in films by friends and family, each of which carried a thank-you note in the credits. He insists it embarrasses him. "I wish they'd stop," he says, dropping his volume a notch. In the same breath, he stresses that he never does a film for his loved ones if he doesn't like the script.

After teasing his fans with cameos, Khan's next, Yuvvraaj, is one of the biggest releases of the year. Khan affirms that the film's family plot is what made him sign it. "But I'm not a family man yet," he says, his signature sarcasm intact.

This is the first time he is working with director Subhash Ghai. "I thought he'd bore me, pakao me, but he was okay," he smiles mischievously. The actor shares camaraderie with Anil Kapoor, but Zayed Khan had him impressed. "More than shooting, we were partying at each other's expense."

The formal look he sports, designed by Ashley Rebello and sister Alvira Khan, is a sharp contrast to his popular, shirtless avatar, but he doesn't mind that for a change. His sole complaint: "They made me spike my hair blonde." That's only one of Salman's three looks in Yuvvraaj. "I later pull back my hair as it grows; and then there's this advantage of working with Ghai, he makes his actors wear caps," he laughs.

With four releases lined up, 2009 is going to keep Salman, who turns 43 next month, busy. While Main and Mrs Khanna and London Dreams are romantic dramas, Wanted: Dead or Alive and Veer end his hiatus as an action hero after Garv in 2003. "Wanted was painful, there are a lot of gory scenes and all the stunts have been done by me," he says.

On a lighter note, there's a sequel to Andaz Apna Apna, a film that never worked at the box office. "It's my favourite but Katrina didn't even smile when she saw it," he adds, disappointed. "I feel sorry for the producer — he must be dying of poverty somewhere."

Heading: Be First - Indian Express
Content:
Norwegian designer Julie Skarland opens her innings in the Capital, blending Arctic nostalgia with Indian extravaganza

When Julie Skarland left Oslo for New Delhi, it was meant to be a brief stopover. Or so she thought. It has been three years since, and the Norwegian designer has abandoned her Arctic nostalgia to soak in the relatively pleasant Delhi winters. But what lured the 46-year-old, who has a boutique in Paris, were the classic designs, the weavers of Bengal and the artisans of Almora. "India happened to me, and I kept on extending my stay here, finding reasons to stay back in this beautiful country. It's almost home to me now," says Skarland, who is now settled at Defence Colony and works out of her studio at Lajpat Nagar.

And when she put up her debut show in the country on Friday, the guest list was like a power list. It was a lavish cocktail organised by the Norwegian Ambassador Ann Ollestad to honour RK Pachauri and Indian and international business leaders, including Ratan Tata. Skarland put out 30 ensembles — dresses, skirts and jackets, trousers and cocktail gowns — all drawn from her Norwegian roots and influenced by her years of training in Paris. The colours were soothing, ranging from smoked blue and fawn to beige and ivory, and the embellishments blended Indian extravagance with her Norwegian experience, as tigers and peacocks were fused into motifs, along with icebergs and northern lights. There were tees with slogans for peace and harmony, all in organic fabrics. Recycled hand-knitted sweaters from Norway's Salvation Army were used in ball dresses while shoes were replaced with wooden clogs flown down from her home. "I am hoping this collection opens up avenues for me in India. I would love to retail here as well," says the unassuming Skarland, who retails across Japan, France, the US, Italy and Norway.

Skarland, who grew up at Trondheim in Norway, moved to Paris to study at Studio Bercot, and eventually opened her own workspace near the white-domed Basilica of the Sacre Coeur. "Paris taught me a lot about creative freedom, about how to infuse your sensibility with the trends of the age, and then, when I moved to India, I realised how a rich tradition of art and craft can enrich your designs," she says. Even watching Manish Arora's show proved to be a revelation. Skarland says she is happy with the way things have shaped up so far. "When I went to Paris, I had no idea that I would open a studio there. Likewise, I had imagined India to be a stopover, but here I am now. I go with the flow. Whatever has to happen, will happen," she smiles. That is pretty Indian.

Heading: Is it curtains for Bhandari? - Indian Express
Content:
Poets who complain they get a raw deal compared with blue-chip novelists and artists, rejoice. Open Space, an outreach initiative of the Centre for Communication and Development Studies, and HarperCollins India have collaborated to organise a poetry contest on the theme "Borders" — and these could be between people, genders, classes, castes, cultures or nations. "We want to encourage reading and writing of poetry among the youth and promote the genre. With a theme like Borders, we are looking for varied interpretations," says VK Karthika, chief editor, HarperCollins India.

Anyone above 18 years can enter the contest. You have to submit your original, unpublished (in print or online) poem in English on the given theme. The poem can be up to 50 lines long, and can be written in any style. The participant is required to pay a registration fee of Rs 100. The contest is to be judged by Keki Daruwala, Priya Sarukkai Chabria, CP Surendran and Karthika. The first prize is Rs 20,000, followed by Rs 10,000 and Rs 5,000 as the second and third prizes. The last date for submission of poems is November 30.

For contest details and to download the form log on to www.openspaceindia.org

Heading: Starry Mumbai suffer Delhi hospitality, DDCA style - Indian Express
Content:
Veteran Delhi pacer insists he wouldn't be part of Ranji squad unless guaranteed a spot in playing XI

He shook hands with each of his team mates and wished them luck. Made to sit out for four days and watch Delhi bowlers go through the grind from the sidelines, veteran fast bowler Amit Bhandari seemed to have had enough.

Expecting a similar treatment in the home match against Mumbai, starting at Ferozeshah Kotla on Sunday, Bhandari bade the team goodbye, in case they didn't see him again in the dressing room. On Friday morning, the bowler with 300-plus scalps for Delhi made it clear to the senior selection committee that unless he's required to play in the XI, he should not be picked in the squad.

Narwal included
With coach Vijay Dahiya and skipper Aakash Chopra giving no guarantee, the selectors had little choice, excluding Bhandari from the 15-member squad and drafted in seamer Sumit Narwal.

"Horses for courses, that's what I will say," selection committee chairman Chetan Chauhan told Sportline. "The team management decided they cannot play Bhandari on this wicket against Mumbai, so we didn't pick him. We don't want to humiliate a senior player by making him sit out.

"Whenever we think he's the man, we will call him. It's not end of the road for Bhandari. We won't allow a senior player to exit like that," he added.

Anil Jain, another selector, concurred. "Bhandari still has the potential to get wickets, but he cannot sit out like that. We had asked the coach and skipper that if Bhandari has to be selected, then he will have to be played. I have no idea why they backtracked from their words, this isn't the way to handle senior players," Jain said.

Meanwhile, the 30-year old veteran of 95 matches said he himself wasn't thinking of retiring yet. "I am just taking a break. If the Delhi selectors want to use my experience in future games, I am available but I will stick to my stand. If I am called, I should be in the XI," Bhandari said.

"I am hurt that despite bowling well against Punjab, they treated me shabbily. I can't bowl at speeds of 140 plus but does that mean I am ineffective? I got vital breakthroughs in the first match and you need wickets to win. Pace alone can't get you success," he said. The team management got flak for not playing a second spinner in Hyderabad. The selection committee also sought clarification on Ashish Nehra's fitness.

No injury, Nehra fit to play
Ashish Nehra's MRI scan has revealed no muscle tear and the fitness report faxed from team physio has cleared the left-arm seamer for the game. However, the team management wants to take the call on Nehra on the morning of the match.

The team management has instructed the curators to prepare two pitches — a green top and a typical flat Kotla wicket. With 12 points from two matches, Mumbai have virtually qualified for the quarterfinals while Delhi, with just four points from two outings, need an outright result to stay afloat.

Though the team initially contemplated on playing on a green top in search of five points, they're likely to play it safe in this match, if Nehra is not fit.

Heading: Manhas, Chopra get cash awards - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai are one of the biggest teams, when it comes to Ranji Trophy, with stars including Wasim Jaffer and Ajit Agarkar in the squad.

In town to play their Elite Division match against Delhi starting from Sunday, however, the Mumbai stars were in shock at the state of the hotel they were supposed to stay for the tie.

In away matches, the home association arranges for the accommodation of the visiting team. And so, the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) officials did no homework on Hotel Kocchar International, before booking the reservations. They merely faxed a request letter to the Delhi & Districts Cricket Association (DDCA) to facilitate their stay there.

The team were shocked at the shabby surroundings and interiors of the hotel and requested for an immediate change of stay. "The rooms are too small for our liking," Mumbai coach Pravin Amre said.

Team's local manager JK Kapoor confirmed that the team had issues with the hotel and they are moving to a new hotel. "They didn't like the hotel and so are shifting to Rajdoot hotel," Kapoor said.

But accommodation wasn't the only headache for the team from Mumbai on Friday. They were supposed to come down to the Ferozeshah Kotla for light training, but were left with no transportation facilities. "We waited for our transportation for over an hour at our hotel. It never came, so we had to cancel our training for today," a frustrated Amre said.

But DDCA washed its hands of by saying the flight delay was the reason for the cancellation. "Their flight was delayed and landed only at 2 in the afternoon. And then some of the team members got stuck in the traffic jam near the airport, so that's why they didn't come for practice today. We had the vehicles ready to take them to Kotla," Kapoor, who was asked by the DDCA to liaison for the visiting team, said.

Heading: Akalis optimistic of tipping the ‘balance’ in their favour - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi & Districts Cricket Association (DDCA) on Friday announced cash awards for Delhi skipper Aakash Chopra and Mithun Manhas for their achievements in First Class cricket when they turn out against Mumbai on Sunday.

"We have decided to give Rs 1 lakh to Manhas, who will be playing his 100th match, and Rs 1.25 lakh to Aakash for his 125th match," DDCA sports secretary Sunil Dev said. Interestingly, the DDCA has announced the awards despite the fact that this would only be Chopra's 124th match.

Manhas said he was touched by the gesture. "I had no clue. But I am happy that the DDCA is appreciative of my efforts. But I am treating it like any other match," he said.

"It is a special feeling to reach this milestone, but at the moment I am only concentrating on helping my team win this tie," he said. His team mates, though, have lined up a celebration. "We will definitely think of something to celebrate his 100th match," Chopra said.

On his own part, Chopra was happy that DDCA was recognising both his and Manhas's long innings in First Class cricket. "It feels good to know that DDCA is honouring us for our hard work," he said.

Heading: With me around people feel secure, says former IPS - Indian Express
Content:
Law and order is an issue of key importance in the city. I have always insisted the Delhi Police be directly accountable to the Chief Minister and not the Home Ministry.
— AMOD KANTH, CONGRESS CANDIDATE FROM SANGAM VIHAR

This is the first Assembly election that Shiromani Akali Dal will be fighting it with their own symbol, 'balance', in Delhi, or anywhere outside Punjab. For the Akalis, who have never won a single seat in the Delhi Assembly, it is a season of hope.

Akalis are fighting the election in an alliance with the BJP for four seats — Shahdara, Adarsh Nagar, Jungpura and Rajouri Garden. Akali candidate Avtaar Singh Hit would be fighting the election from Rajouri Garden for the first time ever. The electoral history of the area is not in their favour. Akalis fought twice in 1998 and 2003 from here and lost both times. In all the three Assembly elections, in 1993, 1998 and 2003, Congress candidate Ajay Makan had a clean sweep.

The vote margin was as high as 24,000 in 2003 between Makan and Akali candidate Sarabjeet Singh. "I've been working for the last 30 years for the Sikh population of Delhi as a member of the Delhi Sikh gurudwara committee. I am well-prepared," Hit told Newsline. He faces old-timer Dayananad Chandilla in the area.

Chandilla's son and daughter-in-law are both MCD councillors in the area. All members of the Chandilla family, including his wife, have won several elections as independents. Chandilla is a sitting MLA from Vishnu Garden. He had fought as an independent candidate and later joined the BJP. At the end of Assembly session, he defected to the Congress.

"In past, I have won from the area as an independent candidate several times. Wth Congress support, there is no way I can lose," Chandilla said.

In Jangpura, an interesting fight is on the cards with two-time Congress MLA Tarvinder Marwah facing a much younger Akali candidate Manjinder Singh Sirsa. Marwah had won the last elections with a difference of over 20,000 votes against the Akali candidate.

Sirsa, meanwhile, is a sitting BJP councillor from Punjabi Bagh who has managed to negotiate an Akali seat despite the BJP's embargo on giving tickets to sitting councillors. Sirsa runs a leather goods business from Sirsa in Haryana and had declared as assets worth nearly Rs 100 crore during nomination.

At Sirsa's office in G-block of Jungpura, there are posters with the population analysis of the constituency. "I have a database of each voter in my laptop. I do not go for campaigning with drums or a band of followers but alone, so that I can chat up residents," Sirsa told Newsline.

Meanwhile 21 per cent of the population of the area is OBC and the SC population is 17 per cent. The Bahujan Samaj Party has been trying their luck in the area for the last three elections. Last time, it had garnered only 658 votes, but is optimistic this time.

Marwah managed to wrest the ticket after a power struggle with Congress old-timer Tajdar Babar. Babar's son Farhad Suri, the sitting councillor in the area, is not cooperating with him.

"Sirsa has broken the trust of the people of Punjabi Bagh by abandoning them midway. He has no base in Jungpura, only rented a house for a month of campaigning. I have grown up here and am here to stay," Marwah said.

In Adarsh Nagar and Shahdara, both Akali candidates are pitched against Congress heavyweights. In Adarsh Nagar, Akali leader Ravinder Singh Khurana is standing against Congress minister Mangat Ram Singhal. Khurana had lost last time too to Singhal with nearly 9,000 votes. Here too, the BSP factor is very strong.

In the last elections, the BSP had got 8,296 votes. In Shahdara, Jeetender Singh Shenti will be facing Narender Nath of the Congress. Nath has held the seat for the last 10 years while Shenti is a Congress defector.

BJP leader Ram Niwas Goyal had rebelled and filed his nomination after the seat was given to the Akalis. Goyal, however, withdrew his nomination on Wednesday. Goyal had won from Shahdara in 1993, however since then he has not been given a ticket.

Heading: Sheila harps on development, regularisation of colonies, girl child - Indian Express
Content:
Former police officer Amod Kanth is giving his politico avatar his best shot. Having joined the Congress barely two weeks back, Kanth, is going the extra mile to garner not just Poorvanchali votes in his constituency, Sangam Vihar, but reaching out to a wider audience. He hopes his career in the police and as a social activist will swing things in his favour.

Reacting to criticism from the Opposition and within his own party, Kanth said on Friday, "I have been working for the last eight years through the 45 centres of Prayas in Sangam Vihar. I am not an outsider and have closely confronted the problems here," said Kanth. Despite his police background, Kanth's list of issues for the upcoming polls is a laundry list of every politician in the city - water, electricity, sewerage system and environment topping his priorities in the agenda.

Kanth however admits his USP will be his previous career in the police. "I am told people feel a sense of security with me around. After serving the longest term as DCP crime branch, I do have an edge in addressing law and order issues."

Congress insiders said it was his police background, apart from his Samastipur background, prompted Dikshit to handpick him. The Chief Minister has repeatedly said Delhi Police should fall under the jurisdiction of the state and not the Home Ministry.

On why he chose the Congress, Kanth said he found the party 'more inclusive, secular and liberal.' He confessed the push to politics came from Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit, who pins faith in the former head of the Anti Terrorist Cell.

"A good road network and sanitation are absolutely essential. I would like to create a small team to plan and be associated with people at large. A grievance redressal system is also on my agenda," was Kanth's pre-electoral promise.

Heading: VOTERS SPEAK: Suresh Kumar Jain - Indian Express
Content:
With the Assembly elections just a fortnight away, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit addressed a public meeting at Tughlaqabad extension on a misty Friday morning. The rally, meant to show solidarity with Congress candidate Amod Kanth, reportedly handpicked by Diskhit to woo the migrant Poorvanchali population in the unauthorised colony, however turned out to be a damp squib, with a dismal turnout.

Sangam Vihar constituency represents around five lakh people and Kanth is facing over 10 independent candidates from the area.

Standing in the middle of the locality market reeking of stagnant drain water and next to an overflowing garbage dhalao, Diskhit said, "The Congress has never been in power in Sangam Vihar. There is development all over the city, but here because we haven't had the opportunity to represent this area," Dikshit said while promising to resolve the issue of drinking water in the area.

While area MP Sajjan Kumar was not present, Kalkaji MLA Subhash Chopra and Tughlaqabad candidate Shishpal were present. Congress worker Haneef Mallik who withdrew his nomination as an independent from Sangam Vihar was also present for the morning meeting.

Referring to former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi's initiative towards information technology, Dikshit said the nuclear deal too would bring in a revolution in the country.

"The nuclear deal will facilitate power generation and farmers will have more irrigation faciities. There will be more industries creating employment for people," she said.

With Sangam Vihar up for regularisation, Dikshit said regularisation is a historical decision. One of the major achievements of her government is the regularisation of unauthorised colonies in Delhi after 30 years.

Dikshit said her government has worked towards the uplift of women by introducing the Laadli Scheme. "I would urge all women to vote for the Congress and also send their girls to school," she said. With the BJP bringing out a chargesheet against the Congress government this week, Dikshit added, "If people feel the Congress has failed, they should provide proof," she said.

Heading: Explosion in a dustbin: two minors injured - Indian Express
Content:
Age: 61 years
Profession: Cigarette vendor
Constituency: Nangloi

Suresh has been running a small open shop selling cigarettes on the main road of Nangloi for more than 20 years now. He says it is his only source of income to sustain a family of five. Like all previous elections this election too is not going to bring any change in his life, he feels.

On basic amenities in Nangloi
We do not get clean water and sufficient electricity in our village. We have failed to get rid of the mosquitoes in the area.

On roadside shops
I had applied for a shop when the government was giving licences to roadside vendors. Twenty years have passed and I still have not managed to get a permanent structure.

On bribing local cops
I am tired of bribing the beat constables. Every week, they come to my shop to collect their share. It is my hard earned money, but I have no choice. If I it will just take them ten minutes to throw me out of this place.

Heading: BJP gets ‘specialist’ leaders from states to cut language barrier - Indian Express
Content:
Two children were severely injured in an explosion that occurred in a dustbin in Sector 22 here on Friday. The police, however, are still unsure of the nature of the explosion.

The explosion took place around 1.10 pm, when the brothers Monu (5) and Roshan (8) were picking waste from a dustbin at a market. "There was a loud explosion and we heard screams of the children. Initially, no one dared go near the site. But seeing that there were two children who were injured, people came forward to help. The police were called in soon," said Shyam Kumar, a shopkeeper of Chaura Raghunathpur area market where the explosion took place.

Both brothers were taken to the district hospital. "The burn injury that Roshan received is quite serious as he was holding the stuff that exploded. His arm has been hurt. He has been referred to the Safdarjung Hospital as there are no specialised burn wards in any private hospital in Noida. His younger brother has received minor injuries," saidd Ashok Tripathi, SP (City), Noida.

"We did not find any shrapnel and are not sure what caused the explosion, but it could be crackers. We have sent samples of the waste to the lab to find out what the material is," added Tripathi.

The incident, however, has raised questions on security and the lack of a bomb disposal squad in the district. "The squad arrived at 2.30 pm, almost one and a half hours after the explosion. Administrative officers arrived even later," said a shopkeeper at the market.

Heading: 6 policemen accused of 2006 custodial death surrender in Noida court - Indian Express
Content:
Speak to each and every voter in his own tongue is the BJP mantra to reach out to the mixed population of the Capital. Through the next fortnight, BJP leaders and workers from different parts of the country - be it South India or Haryana - would be camping in Delhi as the party mounts an aggressive campaign.

"Each constituency has a different population. Our aim is to reach out to the people in their own language," said Delhi BJP spokesperson, Mewa Ram Arya.

The teams would be meeting regional associations and holding rallies in areas according to the population. The team of workers from South India is headed by George Kurien who is a member of national executive committee of the BJP and the head of the Kerala BJP. Kurien will bring with him workers and leaders from all four southern states. Kurien's team will be meeting residents in Mayur Vihar, R K Puram, Karol Bagh and other pockets which have a dense population of South Indians.

From Bihar, Ranvir Nandan, the state secretary of the Bihar BJP would be coming with his own entourage. Delhi has a population of 40-50,000 Poorvanchalis. From Uttranchal, around six ministers are going to camp in Delhi for the next fortnight till the run up to the elections. These people would be targeting trans-Yamuna constituencies including Kasturba Nagar and Laxmi Nagar. From Meerut, a team of nearly 40 workers are specially coming for the 16 constituencies of trans-Yamuna area.

From Haryana, Om Prakash Dhaukat and former minister in Chautala government Sita Ram Singhala would also be touring the rural belt adjoining Haryana. For Badarpur and other constituencies in Southeast Delhi, BJP has got former MLA Yashpal Singh Gurjjar.

For the five constituencies in the New Delhi parliamentary constituencies, Greater Kailash, Jungpura, New Delhi, Kasturba Nagar and Rajender Nagar, the BJP is getting an entourage from Himachal Pradesh headed by former MP Suresh Bhardwaj.

"We wanted not only senior leaders to go campaigning, but also workers to reach out to the people of each constituency for better results. These people are going to stay here, tour the constituency and even camp at polling booths," Arya added.

Heading: No relief for youth writing exam for another student - Indian Express
Content:
Six UP policemen, against whom the Crime Branch of the Criminal Investigation Department of Uttar Pradesh had issued arrest warrants for allegedly causing the death of a youth while in custody in September 2006, surrendered before the Noida court on Friday. The accused were later produced before the Additional Judicial Magistrate, Saroj Yadav, who remanded all six in 14 days' judicial custody and sent to Dasna Prison.

"All six surrendered before the Chief Judicial Magistrate but their bail applications were rejected. They then forwarded the bail applications to the sessions court, where the judge also threw out their bail pleas saying there was no sufficient grounds for granting bail," added Rajender Nagar, advocate of the accused.

All accused will file a fresh bail application in the High Court soon.

The incident took place on September 2, 2006, when Sonu (25), the son of Dalbeer Singh, was detained by the accused, three of them then in the Special Operations Group of the Noida police. Sonu was picked up on charges of stealing vehicles from Hazratpur village of Khurja. He was found dead in the lockup the next morning.

"The family alleged that he was beaten to death and then hanged to make it look like a suicide," sources said.

Arrest warrants were issued against Hindveer Singh of the Anti-Terrorism Squad, Vinod Pandey, station house officer of Pahasu, Bulandshahar and Mahesh Mishra, Sub-Inspector, Bulandshahar, along with constables Pradeep Kumar and Haripal Singh of the Sector 20 police station and constable Pushpendra Kumar of Sector 39 police station.

All have been charged with relevant sections under the IPC sections pertaining to a public servant framing incorrect documents with intent to cause injury, abetment of suicide, wrongful confinement and voluntarily causing hurt to extort confession.

Heading: Children gather at Rajghat to talk tough on child rights - Indian Express
Content:
Taking stern action against a youth who was allegedly caught impersonating and writing a friend's Class XII Boards English examination in 1997, a city court has refused to drop penal charges against him and sent him back to the lower court to face trial.

Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) A K Arya threw out the revision petition of Vinod Singh, who had challenged the magistrate's order of charging him for the alleged offences of impersonation for the purpose of cheating and forgery.

After forging the admit card of one Anil Kumar, Singh had reportedly appeared in his place for the English exam on March 3, 1997, at the Sarvodaya Sahshiksha Uchcha Vidalaya, Janakpuri.

A teacher, however, noted the fudging of the admit card and caught him. The police were subsequently called and an FIR under relevant provisions of the IPC was registered against Singh.

Following a long-drawn case, a magistrate framed charges against him only last year. Singh subsequently filed a petition in the sessions court, claiming the order was arbitrary and illegal.

He argued that since the original report of a handwriting expert — that had been adduced to implicate him after comparison of his handwriting and that on the answer sheet— could not be produced in the lower court, there was no evidence to make him stand trial.

The argument, however, did not find favour with ASJ Arya, who noted that a photocopy of the original record was available with the prosecution and the same could be proved under law at a later stage in the trial.

"The trial court is not required to sift and weigh oral as well as documentary evidence placed on record. Its scope is limited to whether a prima facie case can be made against the accused or not. Singh was caught in the examination hall. Therefore, a prima facie case as ordered by the trial court exists against him," said the court.

The Supreme Court, in a recent order, had also advised the authorities to check such malpractices, which affect the country's progress and academic standards, with an "iron hand".

Dwarka Bar Association votes for office-bearers
The first election for empanelling office-bearers of the newly-constituted Dwarka Bar Association saw 3,096 lawyers exercising their franchise on Friday The votes were cast for the posts of president, vice-president, secretary, treasurer and member executive.

The election was conducted under the supervision of the High Court appointed court observers R P Lau, V P Singh and Raj Birba— all senior advocates in the Capital.

Heading: 29th Sanskriti Awards held at IIC - Indian Express
Content:
Child representatives from various states gathered in Delhi for the National Child Rights Assembly from November 12 to 14. A group of ten representatives from eight states gathered for the assembly in Delhi and created a memorandum of proposals and recommendations on securing child rights. The event, involving children from a cross¿section of the society, was organised by World Vision, India and the India Alliance for Child Rights (IACR) at the Satyagraha Mandap at Rajghat.

Oscar Fernandez, Union minister for Labour and Employment attended the valedictory function and accepted the document.

An exhibition of newsletters and cartoon strips created by children depicting their varied problems and demands was also held in the same area. "As part of the programme, we had workshops on journalism and photography. Then we went around putting forth questions to the general public and created newsletters that we pasted on the walls of schools or prominent buildings in our respective communities," said 17-year-old Arti Kumari from Jharkhand.

"World Vision works with children's groups at village, district and state levels. We provide them financial aid and also awareness about their rights. District-level meets or Bal Sabhas are also organised to tackle issues in their localities," said Jessy, a project member of World Vision.

"We have a children's parliament at each level and were subsequently elected to represent our respective districts and states," said Irshad Ali from Uttarakhand.

Sadhna from Maharashtra added, "We're taught about child rights and health issues. We help people getting access to education, and help them out financially , too."

Heading: Transport tax evasion scam: two of gang arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Sanskriti Pratishthan, a public charitable trust, held the 29th annual Sanskriti Awards at the India International Centre on Friday evening, to encourage young talent in the fields of Literature, Journalism, Art, Performing Arts and Social-Cultural Achievement. The awards had been instituted in 1979.

Five young achievers were conferred the honour by Magsaysay award winner Aruna Roy.

"The awards are presented to young and emerging talent from 25 to 35 years. Each award carries Rs 25,000 in cash and a citation," said Ashok Vajpeyi, chairman, awards committee.

Inderjit Nandan bagged an award for her contribution to Punjabi Literature while Chitrangada Choudhury, a former journalist with The Indian Express and currently working with The Hindustan Times was awarded the Prabha Dutt Fellowship.

Ranjani Shettar won the Kalakriti Fellowship.

Violinists-turned vocalists, Ranjani and Gayatri walked away with the Mani Mann Fellowship. Ability Unlimited India, the nation's first professional dance theatre, took away the award for outstanding social achievement.

The organisation aims to educate and employ the differently-abled through innovative choreographic works and public performances.

Heading: Chubby children cute, but at risk of Type 2 diabetes - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida police have arrested two of a gang of criminals involved in a tax evasion scam in the district, using fake tax collection receipts, duplicate stamps, a laptop with data of road tax evasion and a stamp-pad to avoid tax meant to be deposited with the transport department of Uttar Pradesh.

The two arrested are Karamveer Singh, resident of Hisar in Haryana and Gurwinder Singh, resident of Fatehabad. "We have recovered four stamps, carbon copies of fake state transport department tax receipt books, five fake receipt books (Form 1 B), a laptop with the data of tax evasion and a stamp pad," said the Superintendent of Police R K Chaturvedi, Gautam Budh Nagar.

Talking on the gang's modus operandi, SSP Chaturvedi said, "In 2006, a law related to movement of commercial vehicles was introduced which ruled that all cars coming from Delhi and Haryana into Uttar Pradesh will be paying Rs 14,000 and Rs 6,000 respectively per month to the state transport department."

He added that all BPOs operating in the district hired travel agencies for to take care of their employees' commute. "While the companies in their agreement agreed to pay the tax amount that the agencies have to pay to the state government for their vehicles, these travel agencies forged documents of road taxes to pocket the money. We are also investigating the involvement of the state transport department in this scam," added the SSP.

The police have admitted that there are a dozen more people in the group. "The arrested have also confessed to the involvement of accounts department officials in the respective companies, who were the ones to pass the bill. The accused have admitted that 170 cars owned by these travel agencies have been in the services of various companies," added Chaturvedi.

Heading: MOVIE REVIEWS - Indian Express
Content:
Prateek Rao (name changed) was always the cutest, chubbiest kid around - a child in love with fast food and aerated drinks. His family did not realise their child was literally eating himself to death until he was hospitalised and diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes, normally seen in adults over 40, at the age of 14.

In the past, young diabetics suffered from Type 1 or insulin-dependent diabetes. In Type 1, insulin-secreting cells of the pancreas are damaged or unable secrete enough insulin to maintain the normal blood sugar level. The treatment for this is lifelong dependence on insulin injection. Type 1 diabetes in children was rare.

Type 2 on the other hand, is solely be attributed to an unhealthy lifestyle. "Children gorge on fast food and their lifestyle is largely sedentary. This is the main reason why there is an alarming increase in diabetics among adolescents," said Dr Anoop Misra, diabetologist, Fortis Hospital. The diabetes explosion has affected people in age group of 14-25 years most.

The good news here is that the effects of Type II diabetes in Indian children is mild.

"The sugar levels are not very high and with lifestyle and dietary modifications diabetes can be brought under control. Studies have indicated that if a type 2 diabetic can control his weight, reduce waist circumference and maintain normal blood sugar levels, there are 40 per cent chances that his or her diabetes will be reversed," said Dr S K Wangnoo, diabetologist, Indraprastha Apollo Hospital. The youngest Type 2 diabetic under Dr Wangnoo's care is a 10-year-old girl with Polycystic Ovary syndrome.

The current Indian diabetic population is estimated to be about 42.5 million, according to statistics available from hospitals and medical practitioners. Of this figure, 14-18 per cent diabetics are children suffering from Type 2 diabetes. The total diabetic population of India is likely to double by 2015.

A recent study published in UK medical journal Diabetic Medicine, said chances of developing diabetes increase by a shocking 112 per cent if the child is obese, has an immediate relative suffering from diabetes and has high blood triglycerides level. The increasing rate of type 2 diabetes among children is believed to be a result of the dramatic rise in adolescent obesity, particularly central obesity or belly fat, which has been found to trigger the body to resist insulin.

Not so sugary
Type I diabetes is an auto-immune process which makes its prevention impossible. It can be treated only by insulin.

Type II diabetes has more to do with the kind of life one leads. But oral medication, right exercises and a nutritious diet can keep Type-II cases in control.

Heading: Gun on victim shoulder, BJP aims at BRT - Indian Express
Content:
Dasvidaniya
CAST: Vinay Pathak, Neha Dhupia, Ranvir Shorey, Rajat Kapoor, Saurabh Shukla, Gaurav Gera, Suchitra Pillai;
DIRECTOR: Shashant Shah
Every once in a rare while, a film comes along to pleasure you in unexpected ways. Dasvidaniya, about a man who learns to live in the little time's that left to him, is one such, and it's gone right up there, on the top of my list.

Amar (Vinay) gets to know that he has the Big C, and that he is, not to put too fine a point on it, dying. Now he's always been the kind of man who makes lists, so this is his last chance whip out a pen, and write on a piece of yellow paper: things to do before I die. A big car? Check. He gets himself a spanking red one. An old love? Check. He tracks down the pretty girl (Neha) he's always had a crush on, and confesses all. Dump the boss? Totally. He stares down the overfed, oversized bully (Saurabh) who's made him miserable all his working life, and quits his job. Getting estranged younger brother (Gaurav) home? Oh yes.

It's easy to go wrong with films about people jousting with death, and more often than not, what we get is an overdose of maudlin melodrama. Dasvidaniya (goodbye in Russian, and yes, there's a reason for this, but we'll let you discover it for yourself) is just right: bitter-sweet, matter-of-fact, laced with little joys and sorrows, just like life. Be ready for involuntary tears, though.

And Vinay Pathak is pitch perfect. Nowhere does he send up the Amar-the-loser. No artificial sympathy is garnered. We've all known the Amars of this world, and there's a little bit of Amar in all of us: pretty girls do sometimes run off to another, some best friends (Rajat) are happy to get the bigger share of everything, and their wives (Suchitra) are often mean and suspicious. So who says life is fair? This is Vinay's finest performance, much more nuanced than his much-hyped one in Bheja Fry.

Dasvidaniya is a little gem. Go watch.

Dostana
CAST: Abhishek Bachchan, John Abraham, Priyanka Chopra, Bobby Deol, Boman Irani, Kirron Kher, Sushmita Mukherjee;
DIRECTOR: Tarun Mansukhani
You may not agree with its politics, but Dostana is all set to do for the word 'gay' what Taare Zameen Par did for dyslexia: bring it out of the closet.

On second thoughts, being political would have made it a deeper, complicated film. All debutant director Tarun Mansukhani, and producer Karan Johar want you to do is to have a blast. Accordingly, in order to rent a swish apartment in Miami, Sam (Abhishek) and Karan (John) are made to be gay. Note, not homosexual. Not queer. Just gay, the word that used to denote happiness in simpler times.

And why the leading men need to be pretend-gay is the only little wrinkle in the plot which is otherwise as straight as an arrow: two boys, one girl, and post interval, one more boy. So who gets her? Sam the male nurse, wearer of brightly-flowered shirts? Or Karan, he of the golden bronze chest, and gleaming pectorals? Or late entrant Abhimanyu, shiny in his Armanis, and Guccis? The eye candy is blinding: designers Manish Malhotra and Aki Narula have clearly worked as hard on this project as the director.

Equally clearly, Miami has been chosen because where there are beaches, there are babes, and other hot bods. The stars get by on very few clothes, particularly John, who looks most fetching in his very brief briefs. Priyanka, with her collagen-ed lips and chic wardrobe, looking much better here than in Fashion, fits right in. Abhishek makes up for his fully-clothed appearance by being nicely goofy.

Only Sindhi aunty-types (Sushmita) and Punjabi mammas (Kirron) have the vapours at the sight of touchy-feely moments between John and Abhishek: they are all over each other, and there is even, ohmigod, a lip lock. Everyone else seems to take their gayness very coolly, including the supposed couple. But the gallery is played to, as well, with lots of nudge-nudge wink-wink gay gags. A limp-wristed Boman Irani shows up to drool over the boys, and when a strangely understated Bobby Deol is added to the mix, the party is complete.

Only when Tarun gets emotion in, does the film start to drag. Mistake, because no one does tears like Karan. Ignore those bits, stay with the fun ones, and get laughing. And confirm, like we did, that John has the cutest butt in Bollywood.

Deshdrohi
CAST: Kamal Khan, Gracy Singh, Manoj Tiwari, Hrishita Bhatt, Zulfi Syed, Aman Varma;
DIRECTOR: Jagdish Shama
If you are a 'bhaiyya' from UP or Bihar, Mumbai isn't a good place for you. Deshdrohi, which must have been in the works long before the violence in Maharashtra peaked last month, should have been, by rights, both timely and important. But it is so tackily produced and shoddily acted, that there is no danger of that happening: the ban in Maharashtra is only going to get people curious about a rank bad film.

Producer Kamal Khan places himself in the lead role. And a more unsuitable leading man would be hard to find: utterly unprepossessing, zero acting skills. He plays, what else, a 'bhaiyya' who fetches up in Mumbai to make a fortune. And runs into a gang of Marathi-speakers who are out for his blood. And that of his fellow sufferers from 'Uttar Bharat'.

A Dawood look-alike makes the startling claim that he is the one who chooses the chief minister of Maharashtra. And you always thought that it was a duly elected seat. A wily UP-wala politician turns out to as corrupt as the Maharashtrians, leading our hero to come to the conclusion that it is the 'netas' who are the 'asli deshdrohis'.

An overweight Gracy Singh (last seen in Lagaan) plays the heroine, who goes around on a motorcycle, bashing up those who bash up 'bhaiyyas'. Wonder what Behen Mayawati would make of this.

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

EAGLE EYE
CAST: Shia LaBeouf, Michelle Monaghan, Billy Bob Thornton, Michael Chiklis
DIRECTOR: D J Caruso
The question may have occurred to you before: if "they" are listening in to every phone call you make, reading every message you send, watching everything you purchase, monitoring everywhere you go, how do they keep track of all that information?

Here's your answer, imagined by Caruso as a shiny golden mother computer, surrounded by lots of her mini-mes, and burrowed 36 floors down inside the Pentagon.

All that intel goes inside this computer, and "she" monitors it to give the US Government "credible" — give that a wide berth — leads on what seems suspicious.

One day she gets very, very angry, and as all of us know from Hal 9000 (2001: A Space Odyssey) onwards, that isn't good news. Considering she can rig almost anything automated, from traffic lights to F-16 bombers to cranes sorting out trash to electric towers, not to mention mobile phones, that's even worse news.

Caught in the middle of the madness are Jerry Shaw (LaBeouf) and Rachel (Monaghan), for reasons revealed much later. Suffice to say that one fine day, they get these mysterious calls and then messages springing up virtually everywhere — from signboards to traffic lights — telling them to be there, carry something and do that.

"Refusal is not an option," the unknown voice (we find out soon that it's the mother computer) tells them, underlining it with frying up a man with high-voltage electric cables in front of their eyes.

As long as there is a terror threat around and cars to blow up, Eagle Eye isn't the first or likely to be the last film about over-reliance on technology backfiring, and Caruso certainly doesn't let the pace slag. As for plausibility, it would be foolish to seek the same in a film such as this.

However, this is LaBeouf's vehicle, and you have to admit he does a commendable job of it, surviving almost everything thrown his way without letting you forget that he could be you or me having a very bad computer day.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Harried, worried in many seats, Congress still trying to woo back dissidents - Indian Express
Content:
Party's chief minister candidate Malhotra rakes up issue on death anniversary of Mayank Gulati

A year since the High Capacity Bus Corridor in South Delhi claimed its first victim, the BJP has catapulted deceased Mayank Gulati into the poll arena by raising its pitch against the "killer" BRT stretch.

Gulati, 25, had died on this day last year.

On Friday, Gulati's family members said they are yet to receive any help from any political leader, despite assurances from all quarters. And, on his death anniversary, BJP's chief ministerial candidate V K Malhotra promised to scrap the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project if his party comes to power. Calling the BRT a "murderer", Malhotra said in a statement: "Eight persons have lost their lives on this corridor till date. The government has wasted Rs 20 crore of public money on the project and thousands of trees have been cut down for it.

"When people raised serious objections against this corridor, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit shed off her responsibility and held the technical team responsible for all flaws."

But the family has urged politicians to refrain from making Gulati's death an election issue. "We do not want Mayank's case to be turned into a political issue. We do not know if this is just another vote-gathering tactic but if they (BJP) have raised the issue, we will support them," Gulati's uncle Sunil Bhatnagar said.

Bhatnagar said no one has yet come forward to take responsibility for the young entrepreneur's death. "A few days after the accident, the state transport minister (Haroon Yusuf) met and assured us that justice would be done and that the project would not become functional." But he said no one from the government or the HCBS has contacted the family in the last six months.

Bhatnagar said though he is aware that the BJP is "trying to raise the issue of BRT corridor in their campaign" but no one from the party has contacted the family.

Gulati's friend Sohail Khan said the governing party has not taken any action, and though the BJP is raising the issue, "it might forget the issue after coming to power".

Gulati's friends and relatives are meanwhile keeping their campaign alive. A candlelight vigil was held in Gulati's memory on Thursday evening at the spot where he died, and friends and relatives put up handmade posters with slogans against the project. A group of his friends have also applied for the registration of Humsay, the NGO that they plan to launch as to help families of all road accident victims.

They also plan to file an RTI against the "brain" behind HCBS, IIT-Delhi professor Dinesh Mohan, Gulati's friend Sohail said.

Gulati, who ran a management firm in East of Kailash, died last year when his motorbike dashed against a median placed arbitrarily on the High Capacity Bus Corridor. He was returning from work when the incident occurred, around 2.30 am.

No one has been arrested so far and despite some initial statements about their culpability, no action has been taken till date against officials of either Delhi Integrated Multimodal Transport System, which is overseeing work on the corridor, or RITES, consultant for the project.

Heading: Heavy construction ahead of 2010 Games making Delhi dimmer: study - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress may be in a spot of bother in many Assembly constituencies with rebels filing nominations against the party's candidates, but the Delhi Congress is still hoping to conciliate with at least five dissidents who may spoil the show in the Assembly polls.

Sources within Delhi Congress said the party has managed to safeguard Amod Kanth's Sangam Vihar seat by "tackling" dissident Congress worker Haneef Mallik, who was a "grave threat" to Kanth. The former IPS officer already has his hands full, facing, as he is, at least six candidates including candidates from the BJP, BSP and the Samajwadi Party. But the party is still trying to negotiate with dissident MCD councillor Satbir Singh, who had filed his nomination against Health minister Yoganand Shastri.

Shastri is the sitting MLA from Malviya Nagar and has been selected for Mehrauli this time. The decision came after the party allotted Hauz Khas MLA Kiran Walia, who lost her present constituency after the delimitation process. Party sources said the only option left before Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee (DPCC) president J P Aggrawal to nip the rebellion in its bud is to cancel party membership of the dissidents. But top leaders, they added, are still trying to woo them back.

Friday (November 14) was the last day for withdrawing nominations.
