"People like Satbir Singh are important for the party in the elections because they have a following, a certain standing in their constituencies, a Delhi Congress leader said. "The party is still trying to negotiate and, if possible, at least ask them to not campaign against the Congress candidate in their constituencies."

The other potential threats to Congress candidates are Dulichand Lohia from Rajouri Garden, who has pitched himself against Dayanand Chandila, taken in the Congress wing after quitting the BJP in September); Bir Singh, who has joined the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP); Ajit Chaddha from Tilak Nagar (fighting against Congress's MCD councillor Anita Babbar); and Ramesh Dutta from Matia Mahal, who is fighting against Congress candidate Mehmood Zia.

While Haneef Malik's withdrawal from Sangam

Vihar has boosted the Congress's chances in the South Delhi seat, Delhi Congress chief Aggrawal said, "We haven't decided to expel any dissident from the party yet. Let us negotiate; we will see in a couple of days."

On the last day of the withdrawal of nominations, the total number of candidates in the fray came down to 936.

Heading: Pollution board downs shutter on Gurgaon mall - Indian Express
Content:
Frenzied constructions ahead of the Commonwealth Games may be responsible for the Capital getting dimmer, smoggier, and unhealthier.

A recent study by the Central Pollution Control Board for Delhi reveals that despite the CNG conversion of commercial transport vehicles in the city, Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) and Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM) — the major air pollutants — have gone up. The study echoes another one, just released by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), which warns that "cities from Beijing to New Delhi are getting darker".

"Man-made atmospheric brown clouds (is) being formed over 13 megacities in the world," the UN study reiterates.

And at least part of the problem in Delhi is particles raised by constructions, say experts from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee. "SPM and RSPM are particles less than the size of 10 microns suspended in air. These are often ingested in human trachea (or windpipe)," a pollution control board members says.

"In Delhi, though, vehicular pollution is not responsible for the high RSPM and SPM. They are also, and now primarily, caused by the high level of construction in the city."

The CPCB report finds that RSPM has gone up by 21 per cent between 2000 and 2008: from 159 miligram per metre cube to 192 mg per metre cube. The UN report says: "Brown clouds (formed over Delhi) contain a variety of toxic aerosols, carcinogens and particles, including particulate matter of less than 2.5 microns in width."

The report warns that these pollutants are linked with several health hazards, including respiratory disease and cardio-vascular problems.

The UNEP report has also warned that the city is getting dimmer as the brown clouds block sunlight. The brown cloud over Asia, which stretches between Beijing and Delhi, can also thwart the monsoon because adequate sunlight may not reach the surface.

WARNING: DARK DAZE AHEAD RSPM IN DELHI AIR
2006: 155 miligram per metre cube
2007: 169 miligram per metre cube
2008: 192 miligram per metre cube
72% decrease in sulphur dioxide and 50% decrease in carbon monoxide between 2000 and 2008, suggesting converting public transport to CNG has helped

'BROWN CLOUD' HOTPOTS
Bangkok, Beijing, Cairo, Dhaka, Karachi, Kolkata, Lagos, Mumbai, NEW DELHI, Seoul, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Tehran

Soot levels found at 10% of total mass of all human-made particles in these megacities

(Source: UN Environment Programme report)

Heading: A fair trade: ‘Partners’ Pakistan happy to be back at trade fair - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Plaza Mall near Sector 53 in Gurgaon was sealed on Friday for flouting pollution norms.

Haryana Pollution Control Board (HPCB) regional officer (Gurgaon region) Dr C V Singh said the Board had issued four notices to the mall owner, one Vijay Dixit. "We issued the first notice some seven months ago, when the complex was still under construction," Singh said. "It gave him ample time to apply for a no-objection certificate (NOC) from HPCB. But the owner did not bother to meet us even after four notices and a call for personal hearing from the HPCB chairman."

Singh said there are separate sections for getting consent for establishing and operating any building. "The owner not only operated the complex without a licence from HPCB but also did not meet basic requirements of (installing) an effluent treatment plant for waste water treatment," Singh said.

"The plant is mandatory for any building with a (waste water) discharge of 10 kilolitres and more."

HPCB chairman Dr A S Chahal, who passed the order for sealing, said: "A notice for personal hearing on November 6 was issued to the mall owner after he failed to reply to any of our notices."

The mall has sold all its stores; not one is on rent. In order to de-seal the establishment, the owner will now have to apply for an NOC from the pollution control board, deposit Rs 7.5 lakh as guarantee, an affidavit as an undertaking that he would obey rules, and plan an effluent treatment plant.

The property was sealed under Section-33A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.

Heading: Residents up in arms after butcher’s knife falls on stray dog - Indian Express
Content:
The bonhomie just goes on. As politicians this side of the border get set for the elections, and politicians on that side get set to settle down after the elections, the people to people contact between India and Pakistan got a boost at the India International Trade Fair (IITF) that opened its doors for the 2008 edition on Friday.

Pakistan is the partner country this year, and Faisal Malik from Lahore, a first timer to the fair, said: "Setting up a stall at the IITF was only an excuse for coming to India."

Nargis Sadaat from Karachi, though, has been a regular since 1995, setting up her stall of bridalwear every year. And the response, she said, has been good every year. "We have managed to sell all our goods every time we come here," she said.

But there are hiccups nevertheless: while several stalls were still to open on Day One of the fair, many pointed out that they have been waiting for consignments to be cleared by the Customs office. "We had sent the consignment more than two weeks back but it has still not been cleared," Malik said. "Only clothes we had brought with us are on display at the moment."

He said consignments of several others have met a similar fate.

M Shoaib Ishaq, from Ambers Collection in Karachi, said there's still reason enough to rejoice: "Customers here are crazy about clothes from Pakistan, and we know what colours, design and embroideries appeal to them." But he said there's need to facilitate contact and open up trade opportunities further: "While we find that clothes Pakistan are immensely popular here, there is little opportunity to export directly to India besides this trade fair.

"Instead, our products have to come here via Dubai."

THE HIGH THREE: Return of the Kabuli-wallah
After a successful stint last year, the Afghanistan pavilion is back, with several new entrants. "Since last year our brand has been the figure of the Kabuli-wallah, which has a tremendous draw here," said Walid Tamim of Afghanistan Investment Support Agency. Besides a steady popular demand for dry fruits, considerable investments were also made in the area last year. This year carpets, spices, garden products and handicrafts are also on sale.

Evil-eyes do the trick
Nazar Boucuck, a shop selling nazar or Turkish evil eye charms, seems to have caught the fancy of Delhi. Set in jewellery, trinkets, wall and car hangings, the charm is meant to ward off ill-effects of "evil eye"; the tradition goes back to 600 years in Turkey.

Delhi: The Green Way?
The Fledge, a zero-emission car designed by seven Delhi College of Engineering students, drew curious onlookers at the Delhi Pavillion. It won its creators the Annual Green Championship Award in the US, and this is the first time it is being marketed. The first hybrid car in the country, the Fledge runs on a 346-cc engine, with a mileage of 320 km per litre.

Heading: Demolition drive conducted at Mall, Cemetery roads - Indian Express
Content:
In a world where it's hard to find compassion for the needy, a stray dog's plight succeeded in raising the hackles of the residents of Ganesh Nagar in Janakpuri this afternoon.

After a butcher attacked the dog with a knife, the residents took the injured mongrel to the clinic at Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Science University for treatment and also forced the police to register a case against the meat-shop owner.

Narrating the incident, Jatinderpal Singh, one of the shopkeepers who took the dog to hospital, said: "The man hacked the dog with his carving knife, which is usually used to cut goats and chicken. The poor dog fell on the ground and could not stop howling with pain. We all saw the brutal scene and held a dharna against the merciless butcher." The dharna ended only after the police registered a case against the shopkeeper.

The accused was identified as Mohammad Jacky, owner of Jacky Meat Shop.

In-charge of the Janakpuri police post, Avtar Singh, said: "Jacky was irritated by the dog's frequent visits to his shop to nibble at scraps. In a fit of rage, he attacked the animal with the same knife that he used to cut the meat."

A case under Section 428 (killing or maiming an animal) of the IPC and 1/1 of the Animal Act, 1960, has been registered against Jacky.

"We knew that every one would try to hush up the matter saying it was just a dog. But we wanted the authorities to take action," added Davinderpal, an eyewitness. After the veterinarians discharged the injured animal, the market committee has voluntarily consented to take care of the dog.

But the veterinarians do not hold out much hope for the dog's survival. A vet told Newsline: "The knife sliced the animal's spinal cord and I believe he may not recover."

Heading: Farmers’ agitation forces rail traffic to a halt - Indian Express
Content:
Following directions issued by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in response to a public interest litigation filed by a resident, the Municipal Corporation conducted a demolition drive on the Mall road and Cemetery road on Friday morning.

In three under-construction buildings, stairs constructed in the parking area were demolished.

Assistant Town Planner S S Bindra said: "The stairs were constructed in the area meant for parking and had to be demolished. The owners have been told to rectify other violations as well. Last week, the Department of Town Planning had issued notices to 16 such buildings but the owners did not heed the warning."

Heading: ‘People like me are seen as change agents in Pakistan’ - Indian Express
Content:
Rail traffic at the Ludhiana railway station came to a halt on Friday due to the 'Rail Roko' agitation launched by the Bharat Kisan Union in the state.

With all trains passing through the city terminated, utter chaos prevailed at the station with stranded passengers waiting for hours. Finally, the railway authorities arranged for 15 buses to send the passengers to their destinations.

Station Superintendent Ashok Singh Salaria said over 5,000 passengers were stranded at the station. The trains which were terminated in Ludhiana included the Shatabdi, Malwa Express, Jaipur-Jammu Express, Tata Express, Jalianwala Bagh Express, Shan-e-Punjab, Indore-Jammu Tawi Express and Amrapali.

Confusion regarding resumption of rail traffic prevailed till late in the evening. The backlog had not been cleared completely till the filing of this report.

Heading: Children’s Day celebrated in city schools - Indian Express
Content:
Zaiena Haider, a fashion designer in Islamabad, is in the city to attend the Inter-School Youth Festival

Zaiena Haider from Islamabad is like any other aspiring professional in today's Pakistan — she feels it's time for Pakistani women to gain the same kind of empowerment as in India and asserts that the progress has already started.

"Mindsets are altering now with people like me being seen as change agents," beams the young London School of Fashion graduate and now a fashion designer in Islamabad.

"I am here to represent the young, modern and educated Pakistani woman," she says.

Haider is in the city to attend the Inter-School Youth Festival — Fusion 2008 — as part of the 10-student delegation from the Islamabad College of Arts and Sciences.

Her mother Farida Fayz ur Rehman, vice-principal of the college, and Nusrat Tahir Kitchlew, director-cum-principal, have been visiting the festival for three years now.

"Today, I am working in a private fashion house where 36 designers from across Pakistan churn out the latest designs. Women can now wear what they want to without any hindrances as long as it is not vulgar. Anyhow clothes have nothing to do with God, so there should not be any objections, but one needs to be elegantly dressed," she says describing the fashion scenario back home.

"About 40 per cent of the urban milieu in Pakistan are now liberal to an extent. And it is women like me who carry the responsibility to transform the way women are looked at. But I was taken by surprise when I saw the totally independent Indian women. Yesterday, I saw two women on a bike, chatting with each other, oblivious of what is going around them," she smiles.

Recounting the warm welcome she received when she stepped across the border, Haider said: "Indians are very warm hearted. Most of my friends in London were Indians and I gelled extremely well with them, even more than people from my own country."

Haider latest plan — tour India to gather creative fashion talent. Touche.

Heading: Dhanda: No more mushrooming of illegal colonies - Indian Express
Content:
Close on the heels of National Education Day celebrations, Children's day was celebrated with gaiety and fervour at Ryan International School here on Friday. It was a fun-filled day for the students. The teachers made the day special, as they had a lot of fun-filled activities lined for them. All the cultural items were organized and performed by the teachers. So the day had the theme 'With love - from teachers to students'.

The day began with an informative and entertaining "Radio show" by the teachers. Special assembly was held at different levels which had informative play, enactment, songs etc. The students enjoyed all the items and there was a giggle on the face of every Ryanite. The students went to an orphanage and shared some special moments with the people living there.

Vardhman International Public School celebrated Children's Day with great pomp and show. The uniqueness of the programme was that the students were the chief guests while Asha Rani Jain was the guest of honour, and Ruchika Malhotra, Alka Jain, Monica Malhotra, Nisha and Shelly were the special guests at the function. The junior head girl, Smily Malhotra and the head boy Prabhdeep along with the members of managing committee lit the lamp and paid rich floral tributes to Chacha Nehru. The teachers presented a colourful theme-oriented cultural programme for the children. The guest of honour, Asha Rani blessed the students and distributed sweets among them.

The day was celebrated with great enthusiasm and fervour at Kundan Vidya Mandir, Civil Lines. The campus was buzzing with excitement and joy as the beautifully dressed-up children participated in various activities organised for them. The primary children were told the importance of this day. Songs and dances were also presented.

At MGM Public School, Dugri, a magic show was organised for the students. A scintillating dance performance was presented by Jasjot of Class X. A picnic was organised for the students of KG wing. Principal Mona Singh greeted the students on this occasion and exhorted them to follow the path of honesty and hard work as shown by Pt Nehru. Gajjan Singh Thind, director of the school, gave the message of peace and harmony to the students and urged them to follow the ideals of Pandit Nehru.

At Bhartiya Vidya Mandir, Kitchlu Nagar, various competitions like poem-writing, fancy dress, essay-writing, dance and drama were organised to mark the day depicting Pandit Nehru's love and passion for the children. The tiny tots of junior classes came dressed as Chacha Nehrul. In creative writing competition, Parul Jain, Manisha Singla and Sakshi Singhal secured first, second and third positions respectively.

Heading: Fusion fest kicks off - Indian Express
Content:
'Our govt has inherited the 'mess' created by Capt govt'

"We are cleaning the mess created by the previous government led by Capt Amarinder Singh," said MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon and Chief Parliamentary Secretary (CPS) Harish Rai Dhanda while speaking about the government's approach towards developing new colonies and regularising the already existing illegal colonies all over the state. They said that the government was serious about not allowing mushrooming of illegal colonies.

Dhanda and Dhillon said this while addressing a joint press conference on Friday. Dhanda, along with the officers of Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA), had attended a meeting with the Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal at Chandigarh yesterday. This meeting was also attended by the mayors, municipal commissioners and other government officers from other cities.

Giving the details, Dhanda said that the Chief Minister had asked them to identify the areas and to suggest remedial measures about the already existing illegal colonies. He said that within 15 days, they would be discussing the matter with the chief secretary and after that the government would formulate a policy about the urban housing development. "This meeting had been convened as there were many doubts in the minds of private colonisers about the urbran housing development," Dhanda added.

Dhanda said that during the tenure of the previous government, many illegal colonies had mushroomed and the people were living there without any civic amenities. He said the SAD-BJP government had provided basic facilities of sewerage and water to the residents of these colonies.

Heading: Old boys’ team defeat Sacred Heart School - Indian Express
Content:
Fusion-2008, an inter-school youth festival and BCM's most awaited mega event got off to a colourful start here on Thursday evening.

Nearly 33 elite schools from Punjab, UP and abroad participated in this grand event.

A delegation of students and teachers from Islamabad College of Arts and Sciences, Budhanikantha school, Nepal, and Indian School, Darsait, Muscat, arrived here to be a part of this festival. The ceremony was inaugurated by Dr.G S Wander, co-ordinator, Hero DMC Heart Institute, DMCH.

The programme started with a welcome address by the principal, Paramjit Kaur, which was followed by a choreography. Balloons and glitters created a colourful ambience in the hall at the inaugural ceremony. Nusrat Tahir, director-cum-principal, Islamabad College of Arts and Sciences, was the guest of honour for the capture-foot event.

Heading: CM hasn’t delivered on VAT promise, rue businessmen - Indian Express
Content:
The old boys' team of the Sacred Heart Senior Secondary School, BRS Nagar defeated the current team of the school by 42 runs. An all-round performance (two wickets and 16 runs) by captain Shavinder Singh Sandhu helped the team secure the win.

The match between the old students' team and the current team of Sacred Heart saw some great action. It was a high octane encounter that saw some intense cricket from both sides and saw the old horses come out in flying colours.

The match started with the old boys' team winning the toss and deciding to bat first. Openers Ashish Thapar and Shavinder got off to a steady start taking the score to 43 for no loss at the end of the sixth over

At the half way mark of their innings the old boys were placed well at 67 for the loss of one wicket, setting a good platform for the final 10 overs.

The old boys team set a target of 156 to the school team at the end of their twenty overs.

The School team got of to a tottering start with the first wicket falling in the third over while the score was just 12. The school team tried to steady the ship with the middle order coming good and Saurabh and Vishal making 18 and 23 respectively. But the target was never easy and the school team collapsed at 113.

Brief Scores: Old boys team : 155 for 6 in 20 overs (Varun Gupta 44, Ashish Thapar 34, Dheeraj Malhi 26, Vaibhav 3 for 23); Sacred Heart : 113 all out in 19.3 overs (Vishal 23, Saurabh 18, Ashish 3 for 20).

Heading: 3 jailed for possessing poppy - Indian Express
Content:
The local industrialists are sore that Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, who is also the incharge of the excise and taxation portfolio, has failed to keep the promises he made during the meetings held with them in recent past.

According to the wholesalers, while on one hand value added tax (VAT) on pulses has not been reduced from 4% to 1% as promised by the CM, on the other he has deprived the state coffers of much needed revenue by not imposing 1% VAT on besan, although the manufacturers and even the traders have expressed their willingness to pick the tab.

A special deputation of Beopar Mandal had met the Chief Minister about one and a half years ago and the CM had reportedly agreed to both these demands in November last year. However till date, no notification has been issued on any of the issues, rue the mandal members.

Mohinder Aggarwal, general secretary of Beopar Mandal, Ludhiana branch, said, "There is no VAT on pulses in the neighbouring states of Punjab and this way, already Punjab is loosing crores of revenue because the traders bring the product from Delhi or other states to avoid 4% VAT. Still, our members agreed to pay 1% tax, but it has not been notified till date. We had reminded the CM about the matter in the sangat darshan held in the city as well, but with no result."

Further, the members said that as besan was tax free, the bills of pulses, which were purchased from the outside states, come in flour mills' names and later they show in papers that they had converted pulses into besan and hence are not liable to pay any tax.

Aggarwal said, "This way excise department is losing tax worth crores. As the CM heads the excise department, he should show some urgency in fixing the problem. Already a year has been lost."

Heading: Shilaj hit-and-run case: Sidhhant Gandhi arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Special Judge-cum-Additional Session Judge (ASJ) Ashok Kumar today sentenced three persons to 14 years of imprisonment for possessing poppy husk .

The judge also ordered the accused — Dilbagh Singh alias of Rakba village, Chhinder Singh alias Peter of Jalandhar and Ajmair Singh alias Ghola of Dullaian village in Ludhiana district — to pay Rs 2.50 lakh each as fine. In the case of a default in payment of ine, they will have to further undergo imprisonment for two years.

The ASJ held that prosecution had successfully proved with convincing evidence that poppy husk was indeed recovered from the accused even as he turned down the plea for leniency raised by the accused.

An FIR was lodged against the accused on February 12, 2006 under Section 15 of the NDPS Act at Dehlon PS.

Heading: Tuition fee reverse scheme gets a thumbs down from colleges - Indian Express
Content:
The Sarkhej police on Wednesday arrested Sidhhant Gandhi in connection with the Shilaj hit-and-run case. They also traced his three friends who were accompanying him in the Swift car when the accident took place on Sunday night.

Deputy Superintendent of Police R B Rana informed the media about Sidhhant's arrest in a press conference at the office of the Local Crime Branch of the Ahmedabad Rural Police on Thursday night. Sidhhant has been booked under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code and Motor Vehicle Act.

His three friends were identified as Badal Shah, Niva Doshi (both residents of Paldi), and Mansi Gandhi from Naranpura. According to the police, the four are college friends and had gone on a long-drive when the accident took place on their way back home.

Rana said: "When they were returning home, Sidhhant saw a group of bikers from his college. He got scared that they might see them and blackmail them. During this moment of anxiety, a dog came on the road. To avoid hitting it, he tried to apply brakes but instead accelerated the vehicle by mistake, resulting in the accident."

He further said that the four came out from the front door of the car and took lift from those bikers whom they were trying to avoid. Two of the bikers have been identified as Himalay Rathod and Pulin Shah, both residents of Paldi.

Three persons were killed and two others were injured in the accident. While the police said none of the four were drunk at the time of the accident, the recovery of two empty bottles of beer from the car after the accident is a matter of investigation. Rana said if they find any evidence that any of the four were drunk, required legal action will be taken against them.

Meanwhile, Shilaj village Sarpanch Prahaldji Thakor said: "We have heard that the boy has been arrested and booked. This I think is contrary to what some of the eyewitnesses said as they claim to have seen a girl coming out from the right front door of the car."

On Thursday, the Thakors in the village held a condolence meeting which was attended by a few prominent political leaders.

Sessions Court grants bail
Ahmedabad Rural District and Sessions Court on Friday granted bail to Siddhant Gandhi, who was arrested in connection with the Shilaj hit-and-run case.
The court of the Judicial Magistrate First Class rejected the five-day remand application of the Sarkhej police. The court castigated the police for seeking remand after booking him under bailable sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), while the offence was of a serious nature.
Among other charges, Siddhant was booked under Section 304-A of the IPC for causing death by negligence. It is a bailable offence that carries a maximum punishment of two years.
There have been past instances where offenders in such cases have been chargesheeted for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. It is a non-bailable offence.

Heading: A bus stop with a difference - Indian Express
Content:
Only 25 per cent engineering and pharmacy colleges in the state have so far implemented the tuition fees reverse scheme— a voluntary programme under which tuition fees of students coming from weak financial backgrounds are waived.

There are 37 self-financed engineering colleges with a capacity of 13,000 students and 17 government-aided colleges, having 5,374 seats. The number of self-financed pharmacy colleges is 31 and there are four pharmacy-engineering colleges with a total intake capacity of 4,400. This year, only 830 students out of nearly 22,770 have been benefited by the scheme. Last year, the number was 689.

As per the scheme, if any engineering and pharmacy college is interested in helping financially weak students or wants to do charity for them, they can register themselves for this scheme with the India Council for Technical Education (AICTE).

The council has urged the colleges to give 10 per cent of their total seats under this scheme, against which the AICTE will allot them as many extra seats to cover the cost.

"As this scheme is totally on a volunteer basis, we cannot force any college to implement it," said M N Patel, member secretary in the Admission Committee for Professional Courses. He is also principal of the state's biggest engineering college — L D College of Engineering, Ahmedabad.

He added: "Last year, we requested a few colleges to implement this scheme and they agreed. This year, we sent a written letter to all the colleges requesting them the same. But none of them said 'Yes'. The new fee structure and some new management admission policies of the government is said to be some of the reasons behind it."

Chandrakant Patel, a trustee of Dharmaj Degree Pharmacy College, Anand, told Newsline: "We want to implement such schemes, but it's been only three years since our college was established. At this moment, we cannot afford to let off tuition fees."

M C Gohel, principal of L M College of Pharmacy, Ahmedabad, said: "College never decides whom to cover and whom not to under the scheme. At the time of admission, it is clearly mentioned in the forms that those who want to benefit from this scheme will have to mention it in their form."

On the basis of this, the Admission Committee for Professional Courses directs colleges to waive the tuition fees of such students, he added.

Heading: Cops to inspect mobile phones of more VHP leaders - Indian Express
Content:
The AMTS Pattharkuva Bus Stop on Relief Road is a bus stop with a difference. Apart from being a bus stop, it is a prime spot for roadside vendors, who put fancy belts and wallets on display everyday. In fact, these vendors have completely taken over the place, leaving no space for commuters waiting for buses.

Nazir Ahmed Sheikh, a vendor, said that he has been selling the items for the last 15 years, when there was no bus stand at the spot. "AMTS made this new bus stand in the year 1998-99, thus blocking the view of my wares."

However, Sheikh is all praise for AMTS and the traffic police, who have never sought to remove them from the spot all these years and neither have the commuters complained.

The buses which ply from the stand are 38 (Vasna- Juhapura), 48 (Himmatlal park- Prahladnagar garden), 56 (Judge's Bungalows- Iscon Mandir), 1122133 (Laldarwaja), 561 (Gujarat University) and 2 (Circular route- Laldarwaja).

Heading: I have always raised my voice against pouch scam: Shrivastav - Indian Express
Content:
Investigators say more than 4,000 SMSes were sent, which maligned Modi and the state govt

Police will inspect mobile phones of some more Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) leaders in the state in connection with the recent sedition charges against the Parishad's Ahmedabad city general secretary, Ashwin Patel. The investigating officers, who interrogated VHP leaders – Kaushik Mehta, Rajesh Shastri and Jadish Dwivedi – on Thursday, said this on Friday.

Patel, a 42-year-old Ahmedabad-based businessman and VHP leader, is accused of allegedly sending derogatory and defamatory SMSes about Gujarat Chief Minister, Narendra Modi. Patel was arrested on October 27 on charges of sedition, defamation and for allegedly inciting communal violence. He is presently in judicial custody at the Sabarmati Central Jail here.

The Local Crime Branch of Gandhinagar police had on Wednesday evening summoned Mehta (VHP state general secretary), Shastri (VHP president, north Gujarat) and Dwivedi (a VHP worker) for questioning in connection with the case and interrogated them for more than four hours on Thursday.

Gandhinagar DSP M L Ninama, investigating officer in the case, said: "During our investigation, we had found that these three VHP leaders had received the SMSes sent by Patel. We questioned them in connection with this."

Ninama said that the three have been asked to deposit their mobile phones with the police soon, for examination. "We can seize their mobile phones, if they do not cooperate with us," he said.

Sources in Gandhinagar police said that they want to find out if these three had forwarded these SMSes to any person and if yes, to whom. "For this, these instruments need to be scrutinised by forensic experts," sources said.

Police investigation so far has revealed that more than 4,000 odd SMSes were sent in the period of about four months. "While most of the recipients were members of the VHP, some media persons and politicians had also received these derogatory messages," Ninama said.

Heading: MSU teachers do the disappearing act during teaching hours - Indian Express
Content:
A day after BJP leader Madhu Shrivastav resigned from the party, the Waghodia MLA said on Friday that a notice slapped on him in connection with the Baroda Dairy's pouch milk packing scam forced him to take this step.

Shrivastav and 18 other Baroda Dairy office bearers have been issued notices under Section 93 of the Gujarat Cooperative Society Act 1961.

Shrivastav said: "Even before I was appointed chairman of the Baroda Dairy, I had been raising my voice against the scam. How can the Registrar of Gujarat State Cooperatives slap notice without any inquiry?"

Maintaining innocence, he said, "Soon after I took over as the chairman in July 2007, I cancelled the contract of Vadodara-based pouch packing firm Parul Electronics. I gave the contract to Surat-based Sigma Electronics." He rubbished the reports pertaining to his resignation as the dairy chairman.

Chandravadan Patel, one of the dairy directors who also resigned from the post, said: "In his telephonic conversation with Bharatsinh Parmar, Shrivastav demanded an immediate inquiry into the scam. Gujarat BJP president Purushottam Rupala also contacted the MLA and enquired about his resignation."

Meanwhile, Vadodara district BJP president Satish Patel and vice-president Ramsinh Rathwa visited Shrivastav at his residence. Refusing to speak on the leader's decision to quit, the two said they tried to find out if he was involved in the scam.

Rathwa said: "Through our discussion, we found that he along with other government nominated directors in the dairy were against it (scam)."

The notice served on Shrivastav said that between November 11, 2006 and July 15, 2007, bills worth Rs 54.73 lakh were generated for the Parul Electronics.

According to the notice, "Even as the packaging cost of one pouch was Rs 1.62, (payment of) Rs 2.25 per pouch was decided, which cost Rs 17.85 lakh extra."

Heading: Family background has nothing to do with Geeta Rathod’s arrest: SIT - Indian Express
Content:
The case of absenteeism seems to be the other way round in M S University (MSU), with the teaching and non-teaching staff in Commerce, Science and Arts faculties playing truant during teaching hours.

While Science faculty's officiating dean Prof M Daniel opted for Gandhigiri for his late-coming clerical staff, deans of other faculties passed on the buck to the Heads of the Department.

Prof Ashok Hingorani, Commerce faculty Dean, said: "Each faculty in MSU has a coordinator who is supposed to keep tabs on how punctual a teacher is."

There is a stipulated time frame set up by the University Grants Commission, which says the teaching staff should be present for at least fours hours.

When asked about this, Prof Hingorani said: "Our unit coordinators are supposed to do all this. As of now, I have not received any report from them in this regard."

Commenting on the teachers playing truant in his faculty, Vicky Shah, Commerce Faculty Representative (FR), said: "A former NSUI student leader had raised the issue about teachers' absenteeism in the Commerce faculty in 1997-98 and a committee was formed to look into this. However, the situation is back to square one, where teachers are more interested in politics than teaching."

Prof Bhuvan Parekh, Dean, Faculty of Technology, said: "There was a system made by Anil Kane, former MSU Vice-Chancellor, wherein teachers were to specify a time table in his department as to when are they available for the students."

Heading: HC refers petition in Rajnish Rai case to another bench - Indian Express
Content:
Geeta Rathod may be the first woman to be arrested in connection with the 2002 Gujarat riots, but in her family, she is the third person to be held on riot-related charges.

Her brother Mukesh Rathod, an advocate by profession, and father Ratilal Rathod were also arrested

in connection with the Naroda Patiya massacre case of February 28, 2002.

"The father-son duo was arrested on charges of rape and murder. While Ratilal committed suicide about two years ago due to depression, Mukesh is out on bail and practices law in the metropolitan court here," said a senior officer of the Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT).

Geeta, 30, who was arrested by the SIT from her residence in Krishnagar near Naroda Patiya on Wednesday evening, is accused of supplying kerosene and kerosene soaked rags to the mob that burnt alive numerous Naroda Patiya residents.

Former CBI director and SIT chairman R K Raghavan said: "We have strong and concrete evidence against Geeta. She was arrested on the basis of these evidence and the corroborating statements of the victims. Her arrest has nothing to do with her family background."

Deputy Superintendent of Police V V Chaudhary, who is guiding the SIT further investigate into the case, said, "We have evidence that Geeta had procured and later supplied kerosene to the rioters. She is also accused of passing to them rags dipped in kerosene."

A Class X dropout, Geeta was produced before a metropolitan magistrate on Thursday. The SIT had sought for her remand on grounds that they wanted to interrogate her to find out the source and quality of kerosene that she had supplied to the rioters.

Geeta, who was married off to factory worker Raju Shinde nearly three years ago, stays with him in Krishnagar. Her brother, along with mother and younger sister, stays in Gaogotari Society near Naroda Patiya, the police said.

Eighty-nine people had fallen victim to the riots that broke out in Naroda Patiya the day when the Vishwa Hindu Parishad had called for a statewide shutdown to protest against the torching of S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express at Godhra a day earlier. Fifty-nine karsevaks had died in the train carnage.

The DCB had in 2002 arrested 46 people, including the then Bajrang Dal leader Babu Bajrani in connection with the Naroda Patiya case.

The SIT, which is further investigating the case as per the order of the apex court, has so far arrested 12 people in this connection.

Heading: GISF guards allege ‘exploitation’ at the hands of government - Indian Express
Content:
The petition had challenged the order of a single judge bench quashing the decision of the Examination Reforms Committee of the GU

A division bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice Akil Kureshi on Friday referred a petition challenging the orders of a single judge bench, which had quashed the decision of the Examination Reforms Committee (ERC) of the Gujarat University in the Rajnish Rai case, to another bench.

When the matter came up for hearing, Justice Kureshi said "not before me".

Senior IPS officer Rajnish Rai was declared failed in the examination for second semester of LLB (first year) after he was caught possessing a foot-scale allegedly having objectionable writing on it.

Justice Jayant Patel on October 24, quashing the university's action against Rajnish Rai, had directed the university to declare result of the police officer in second semester of LLB (first year) exam by November 14. Justice Patel, in his order, had observed that the university's inquiry into the case was in total disregard of the principles of natural justice and fair play.

The ruling also allowed Rai to appear in the examination of the first semester along with the exam of the second semester of LLB (second year) in April 2009, overlooking the attendance criteria as the case was pending in the court.

Ruling that the material found from the possession of the student must be relevant to the subject of examination, the judge had said that the university had miserably failed to establish it in this particular case.

Justice Patel had stated that the foot-scale in question, on the basis of which the officer was punished, should have been preserved.

It was Rai who had arrested IPS officials D G Vanzara, Rajkumar Pandian and Dinesh MN in the Sohrabuddin fake encounter case.

Heading: Girl attempts suicide; alleges she was sold by her mother - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat Industrial Security Force (GISF) personnel have threatened to launch an agitation to protest against their "exploitation" at the hands of the state government.

One of their main grievances is that many of them have not been paid wages for the last two months. Even those deployed in the new and old Sachivalaya complexes and offices of government-run boards/corporations in Gandhinagar, have not received wages.

"We celebrated Diwali and New Year without any glitter, as we have not been paid for the last two months," said a GISF guard, adding that they are also demanding

that their services should be regularised and they be paid salaries as their counterparts in the government services.

"I receive a pay slip of Rs 5,800 a month, but my take-home salary is only Rs 3,200 after the deduction of service tax, PF and other taxes. I get peanuts for standing guard for over eight hours daily in the services of ministers and bureaucrats in the Sachivalaya complex," lamented another guard.

GISF chief executive officer J L Rana told Newsline that most of the 4,000 security guards and officers attached to the force have been paid their salaries.

"We have already deposited money in their bank accounts, and those being left out will get it soon," he said.

Rana, a retired IPS officer, refuted the allegations levelled by the security guards that they were being exploited by the government.

"There is no question of them being underpaid. We have to deduct PF, services and other taxes as per the government rules," he said.

Heading: Priest arrested with Rs 1.2-lakh hemp - Indian Express
Content:
An 18-year-old girl attempted suicide after her mother allegedly sold her to a 70-year-old man in Rander.

The girl who tried to end her life by consuming poison at her brother's house in Unn Patia in Surat is undergoing treatment at the New Civil Hospital and is reported to be out of danger.

According to case details, Ashiya Shaikh, a resident of Ikbal Nagar slums in Rander, started staying at her brother Mohsin's house at Unn Patia in Surat after she was tortured and forced by her mother Zahedabibi to marry an old man.

According to Ashiya's complaint registered with Sachin police station, her mother Zahedabibi was pressurising her to marry 70-year-old Shoeb Ismail Jeewa. Zahedabibi has worked at Shoeb's house as housemaid for last 14 years. Ashiya's father had gone missing 10 years ago.

As the family had financial problem, four months ago Ashiya was forced to leave school and work at one of the offices owned by Shoeb.

Ashiya said that at the office, Shoeb would often harass her physically. When she complained about the matter to her mother, she ignored it. "She had fixed up my marriage with Shoeb after taking Rs 20,000 from him. When I refused to marry the old man, I was beaten up every day," she said.

"Shoeb also tried to win over me by offering me money," said Ashiya.

Earlier, on 9th November, Ashiya had tried to end her life by jumping into the Tapi river. However, some people had prevented her from jumping into the river and took her to her brother Mohsin, an auto rickshaw driver.

On Thursday evening, Zahedabibi went to Mohsin's house and asked Ashiya to marry Shoeb. Ashiya said she was also threatened by Shoeb to marry him. Irked by their threats, she tried to end her life by consuming poison.

According to Sachin police, Ashiya has lodged her complaint against her mother, Shoeb, her aunt Zohra Memon and niece Taslim, all residents of Rander.

Sachin police inspector K R Bhuwa said, "The victim has alleged that she was sold by her mother to an old man." He said the police have begun the investigation in the case.

Heading: Dalit families finally get their due in Amreli - Indian Express
Content:
The Junagadh Special Operation Group (SOG) police on Thursday night raided a temple in Keshod city and arrested the priest for possessing dry hemp and cultivated hemp flower plants in the temple premises.

The police recovered 16.550 kg of the prohibited drug, worth Rs 1.2 lakh from the priest, Babudas alias Babu Bhagat (66), and booked him under various provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.

According to police sources, SOG police along with Keshod city police conducted a joint raid at the Ramapir Temple located in Indira Nagar area of Keshod. During the search operation, the team recovered 3.550 kg of dry hemp kept in a bag, besides cultivated hemp flower plants, together weighing 16.550 kg, from the temple premises.

The police arrested Babudas on the spot. SOG sub-Inspector H M Kansagara has lodged a complaint against Babudas with the Keshod police. The case has been handed over to the Keshod police for further investigation.

According to the police, the accused will be produced before JMFC Court, Keshod, on Friday evening.

Heading: Cops foil plan to kidnap Gandhinagar businessman - Indian Express
Content:
Win nine-year-long legal battle against the Kotdi Gram Panchayat in the Gujarat High Court; get possession of land to build houses

It's harvest time for seven-odd Dalit families of Kotdi village of Rajula taluka in Amreli district. After winning a nine-year-long legal battle against the Kotdi Gram Panchayat in the Gujarat High Court, they have finally got the legal possession of the land, which was given to them by the State Government to build houses.

Although the government had officially given the two-acre land to the Dalit families, the physical possession of the same was never given to them. The official rigmarole in giving the land to the Dalits reached the Gujarat High Court, which recently passed an order that the Dalits be allowed to build houses on the land given to them by the State Government.

Interestingly, the upper caste villagers had encroached upon the land by constructing a road and cultivating cotton crop on it. However, following the High Court's order, the District Collectorate machinery razed the encroachments on Friday.

Dalit activist Valjibhai Patel, who guided the Dalits in their legal fight under the banner of Council for Social Justice, laid the foundation stone for the construction of houses. The complex will be called Adhikar Nagar.

Dalit activist Raju Solanki said: "The movement of the Dalits of Kotdi village is significant because they fought for their rights and got them without shedding a single drop of blood. The atmosphere here was amazing as hundreds of Dalits from nearby villages gathered to celebrate the victory of their rights."

Many retired Dalit bureaucrats like T D Soyantar and Bhupendra Kapadiya were also present at the foundation stone laying ceremony.

Heading: Surat bombs: Accused admitted to New Civil Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Chotila police rescued a businessman who was allegedly kidnapped because of his inability to return the money borrowed by him five years ago.

According to the case details, three armed men allegedly kidnapped Gandhinagar-based shopkeeper, Ketan Patel, in a car late on Thursday and robbed him of valuables worth Rs 23,000.

The accused trio, police said, were recovery agents of a city-based moneylender, Rajdeepsinh, and that the incident was fallout of Patel's not being able to pay back the loan of Rs 5 lakh he had taken from Rajdeepsinh about five years ago.

The accused – Bhagirathsinh Chudasma, Sonusinh and Arunsinh – all residents of Gandhinagar, allegedly kidnapped Patel in a luxury car near his residence in Sector 28 in the state capital on Thursday evening. The accused, who were drunk, then sped the car towards Rajkot, along with Patel in their captivity, police said.

Patel's ordeal came to an end near Popatpura, about 1 km from Chotila in Surendranagar district, when a police team stopped the car for a routine check. Police rescued Patel from the captivity of his kidnappers and arrested the trio on the charges of kidnapping, loot and for violating the state's prohibition rules.

In his complaint filed with Chotila police, Patel has accused Rajdeepsinh of having carried out the kidnap for extorting the money he owed him. "Patel had taken a loan of Rs 5 lakh from Rajdeepsinh about five years ago. The deal was that the former would pay the latter Rs 8 lakh within the stipulated time. Patel, however, has been able to pay back Rajdeepsinh Rs 1 lakh only till now," Chotila police said.

The complaint was later transferred to Sector 21 police station in Gandhinagar. Police inspector G H Algotar said that his team was investigating the case.

Heading: Adverse climatic conditions hit major oil crops - Indian Express
Content:
Tanveer Pathan, who stands accused selecting the areas to plant bombs in Surat in July this year, has been admitted to the New Civil Hospital after he complained of fever. He is currently in the custody of the Crime Branch in connection with the case.

According to the police, Tanveer complained of coughing and high temperature a couple of days ago, following which he was taken to the hospital where he was admitted to the prisoners' ward.

Crime Branch sleuths had arrested Tanveer and Zahir Patel, both residents of Ved Road in Surat for allegedly showing the spots for planting bombs and harbouring other accused in the city.

Crime Branch Inspector P M Parmar said: "We got the chance to interrogate Sajid Mansuri, Tanveer and Abu Bashar. But Tanveer fell sick, which has created a problem for us. We also wanted to find out the role of Kayamuddin in the plantation of bombs and involvement of other people."

Heading: Now, find information about public authorities online - Indian Express
Content:
Scanty and untimely rainfall in western and southern states during August-September has dented major oilseed crops such as groundnut and soyabean, leading to a seven per cent fall in industry's initial estimates on production.

The Central Organisation for Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT) has now projected an output of 164.1 lakh tonnes for kharif 2008, compared with 175.5 lakh tonnes in its first advance estimate released on September 29.

G G Patel, convenor of COOIT's crop estimate panel, said: "The dry spell in August, and unseasonal rains spanning from September-end to the middle of October have been a major factor for damage to groundnut and soyabean crop in Gujarat."

Moreover, adverse climatic conditions impacted these crops in southern states like Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, he added. From its first advance estimates, the industry body has revised downward soyabean and groundnut output figures by eight lakh tonnes and four lakh tonnes, respectively.

Soyabean output in 2008, however, is projected at 98.9 lakh tonnes, compared with 107 lakh tonnes in the first advance estimate. But the production is higher than that of the last kharif at 94.6 lakh tonnes.

In groundnut, COOIT has projected the output to decline to 45.2 lakh tonnes in this kharif from 49 lakh tonnes in the earlier estimate. The output this kharif is lower than 48.7 lakh tonnes in kharif 2007.

The association has projected total oilseeds production during the kharif 2008-09 season at 164.1 lakh tonnes, marginally down from last year's 164.9 lakh tonnes.

However, according to the government's first estimates, total oilseeds output in kharif 2008-09 will be 179.47 lakh tonnes, against 198.42 lakh tonnes last year.

Heading: Congress leader asks Chief Minister to drop Fisheries Minister - Indian Express
Content:
RTIPAD project aims to bring more transparency and help curb corruption in government schemes

Next time you seek general information on the grant received by a gram panchayat or utilisation of funds under a particular government scheme, you need not submit an application under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, nor wait for 30 days to receive the required information.

The state Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) is planning to introduce a project that will make it mandatory for the public information officers (PIOs) to put all the information — which is under the pro-active disclosure — on the website.

Significantly, it will reduce the number of general information applications by 80 per cent, bring in more transparency, and make the access to information easy for the common man.

"A large number of applications under the general information category deal with information about funds used by the gram panchayat or the utilisation of money by the municipality. As per the Section 4 of the RTI Act, the PIOs are required to disseminate information without it being sought through application," says RN Das, the state CIC.

For the first time in India, the general information about various public authorities and departments will be put online with the help of this project called RTIPAD (Pro-Active Disclosure) . Under this, the PIOs will be required to upload all the general information on the portal (rtipad.com) which is categorised under proactive disclosure on the website

"It's a win-win situation for the administration, PIOs and information seekers. The best part about it is that it will bring in more transparency in the system," says Harinesh Pandya of Janpath, an NGO which facilitated implementation of the RTI Act. "Since the information will be available online, everyone will be free to track the developments. This will further help curb the corruption. It will also reduce the number of applications seeking general information by about 80 per cent," he said.

A private company has prepared the software, which will help the PIOs to upload and update the information on a portal in a structured manner irrespective of the department they belong to. "We have developed a software with a particular format. This will be required to fill in the general information. The software not just uploads the data online but also create alerts in case the information gets outdated," says Haren Shah of Peach Computers, a company that specialises in Management Information Systems.

The project is currently underway on an experimental basis at the Industrial Training Institute (ITI) Gandhinagar, where the students are helping the PIOs to update and upload the information about their departments on the Internet. Once successful, it will be replicated across the state.

Heading: HC serves notices on POTA review committee, Godhra carnage accused - Indian Express
Content:
Demands CBI inquiry into the granting of fishing contracts

Leader of the Opposition in the Gujarat Assembly, Shaktisinh Gohil, has demanded that the Chief Minister drop the Fisheries Minister from his cabinet following the indictment of the minister by the high court for awarding fishing contracts to certain co-operative societies in contravention of the state policy.

Gohil has also asked Narendra Modi to order a CBI inquiry into the fishing contract scam if "the CM really believed in his much-hyped claim of neither indulging in corrupt practices nor allowing others to indulge in corruption".

Addressing a news conference here on Friday, the Congress leader quoting from a copy of the high court judgement, said, "Evidently, the impugned contracts have been awarded by the state government instead of by the competent authority who under the resolution are the district officers. Obviously, the minister concerned has usurped the power vested in the competent authority… We are, therefore, of the opinion that the contracts of fishing lease have been granted arbitrarily. The respondents — societies concerned — have been shown undue favour for extraneous reasons."

Gohil, also a prominent lawyer, said the Gujarat High Court in its September 29 order had quashed the fishing contracts the government had granted to the co-operative societies concerned. The court also directed the competent authorities to grant fishing lease through a tender process as mandated in the government resolution dated February 25, 2004.

Alleging the involvement of Fisheries Minister Dilip Sanghani and Gujarat Minister of State for Fisheries Purshottam Solanki in the scam, the Congress leader demanded that Modi should immediately remove the two ministers from in the light of the observations made by the HC.

"On July 25, I had written a letter to the Chief Minister urging him to institute a high-level probe into the fishing contracts awarded to certain co-op societies without issuing tenders, and also to cancel the contracts forthwith. But the CM responding to my letter, informed me that he was directing the Secretary, Fisheries, to inquire into it," Gohil said.

"Can an officer bring out the truth by conducting an inquiry against the ministers of his own department?" asked Gohil.

He alleged that the government had awarded fishing contracts for about 30 reservoirs, mainly in Saurashtra, at throw-away rates to certain co-op societies without inviting bids. This has resulted in a loss of nearly Rs 3 crore to the government treasury.

Heading: Pandit Nehru fades from leaders’ memory in central, south Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat High Court issued notices to the Central POTA Review Committee and the accused in the Sabarmati Express carnage case, on Friday.

A Division Bench comprising justices D A Mehta and Abhilasha Kumari issued the notices, which are returnable by November 21. The notices were issued on a petition challenging the conclusions of the review committee pertaining to the accused in the case.

The petition was filed by Sardar Maganji Vaghela, relative of a victim of the incident. The petitioner had contended that since the committee report was not consistent with the evidences collected by the investigating agencies, its findings should not be made binding on the court and investigating agencies.

The committee in its report in May 2005 had stated that the provisions of POTA were not attracted towards the case accused, hence they should not be tried under this Act.

"After appreciating the evidences made available and considering the arguments of the defence and prosecution counsels, this committee is of the view that the incident had taken place as alleged by the prosecution, but certainly not as a part of a conspiracy envisaged under the provisions of POTA," the committee headed by Justice (retired) S C Jain had observed.

The report had also recommended that the accused be tried under the provisions of the Indian Penal code, Indian Railways Act, Prevention of Damages of Public Property Act, and Bombay Police Act among others, but not under POTA.

The recommendations could not be implemented owing to this petition pending in the court along with another petition filed by a relative of the accused, challenging the refusal of the state government to accept the recommendations. A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court, however, on October 21 upheld the findings of the committee and maintained that it was binding on the Gujarat government.

But the apex court made it clear that the opinion of the committee could be challenged under Article 226 of the Constitution by any aggrieved person. The court had not granted stay on the committee's recommendations.

Heading: Two child labourers rescued from DC office complex - Indian Express
Content:
It may be difficult to believe, but it is a matter of fact that barring a couple of statues in Ahmedabad and Rajkot, most of the cities in the state, particularly in central and south Gujarat, have no life-size statue of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

This becomes evident every year when the country's first Prime Minister is remembered on his birthday on November 14, which is celebrated as Children's Day.

While both the government and private offices across the state celebrated the day with much fanfare, in central and south Gujarat, the occasion was marked by paying floral tributes to the leader's photo in the absence of statues.

Those at the helm of affairs at the municipal corporations in Vadodara and Surat said that there was no proposal to install Nehru's statue. Reacting to this, Congress office bearers and senior leaders admitted that it was a major lapse on the part of the party and that it has failed to popularise its own political icons like Nehru.

"It is true that there is not a single statue of Nehru in the entire city. We have never received any request or proposal from any individual, organisation or even political parties to install it. As far as celebrating Children's Day is concerned, we do it by offering flowers to his framed photos," said a Cultural Committee official of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation.

In Surat, too, where statues like the Laughing Buddha and abstract art forms have been installed at several traffic points, Panditji is missing. The city of traffic islands does not even have a single bust where at least a garlanding ceremony can be held. Even the Congress members bring along their own Nehru photograph and garland those on the occasion.

"Yes, the city does not have a single statue of Nehruji. No one ever seriously thought about it," said Surat Congress president Sunil Bhukhanwala.

Similarly, Vadodara city Congress president Suresh Patel admitted that this issue was never discussed. "In the last two years, no proposal in this regard has been made and neither has the issue been discussed at party meetings. Nobody actually thought about Pandit Nehru's 'absence' in the city."

"It is indeed sad that we do not have a single statue of his. Now, we would think of having one in Vadodara," said Maulin Vaishnav, who has installed several statues through a trust in the city.

Interestingly, even Bal Bhavan, which is affiliated to the National Bal Bhavan, an autonomous body functioning under the Union Ministry of Human Resource Development, does not have his statue in its premises. "We organise several programs on Bal Divas, but as far as having a statue is concerned, we never thought about it," said an official at Bal Bhavan.

Heading: City gets another first: Managed Network Services - Indian Express
Content:
State labour officers raided the office of Amreli district collector and rescued two children working at a tea-stall inside the complex on Friday. The raid came two days after Newsline reported the presence of child labourers inside the building.

The rescued children were later sent to an observation home in Amreli. The Labour officers said they were planning to take legal action against the canteen owner, who had employed the two.

Assistant Labour Commissioner Ashok Shah, who led the raid, told this paper: "The collector had asked me to look into the matter. We formed internal teams and raided the complex, during which two children were found working at Har Bhole canteen. One boy was nearly 10 years of age, while the other one was approximately 13-year-old."

Shah said the statement of the canteen owner has been recorded and the process was on to take legal steps against him.

An office-bearer of Ahmedabad-based Dalit Hak Rakshak Manch (DHARM) had spotted the two boys distributing tea inside the collector's office during an official visit on November 6.

DHARM secretary Rajesh Solanki informed the district collector about the same and requested him to eradicate child labour from his office as well as from the district.

The collector is the chairperson of his/her district's Child Labour Rehabilitation and Welfare Committee, and is responsible for the proper implementation of the anti-child labour provisions.

Heading: Special zones, on SEZ lines, for nomadic tribes - Indian Express
Content:
Small and medium businesses and enterprises to benefit from pilot project launched in city

A one-stop solution to small and medium businesses and enterprises for their connectivity needs, with better manageability and network security.

That's what the Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) is offering and Pune has been chosen for the pilot project.

BSNL chairman and managing director Kuldeep Goyal on Friday launched the Managed Network Services from Pune. Calling this service a 'new chapter' in the history of BSNL, Goyal said, "We chose Pune to run the project on a pilot basis, as we are sure of getting a good feedback here."

Goyal said the pilot would later be extended outside Pune. "Till now, BSNL has been providing various services to its customers, but now, people want integrated solutions to their IT needs, which is what we are going to provide through this new service," he said.

The service will be available in Pune, Nashik and Aurangabad on a pilot basis for a couple of months before it's extended to other parts of the country. However, the customers of the pilot project cities will get services across the country. The minimum tariff has been kept at Rs 7,999 per month.

"The assured service with fixed monthly charges and no capital expenditure investment will reduce the entry barrier to the customer and help in expanding our service. Initially, we are targeting 50 small and medium enterprises as our customers." he added.

The integrated secured data service is actually a bundle of hardware, connectivity package and completely managed services, including the 24x7 proactive monitoring of customer network and remote configuration of troubleshooting.

BSNL has tied up with two private players- Cisco and Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services Ltd. While Cisco will provide end-equipment, Trimax will offer the actual service, including 24x7 proactive network monitoring and troubleshooting. BSNL has designed three packages, EntCom, BizCom and EasyCom, for different requirements of customers.

"As per the projections, the market opportunity in small and medium business and enterprise segment is huge and almost 62 per cent of customers from this segment want to have integrated services, which is why, we are targeting this segment," Rajesh Chainani, senior vice-president of Cisco India, said.

BSNL chief general manager (Maharashtra circle) Chandra Prakash, principal general manager V K Mahindra, CEO of Trimax Suryaprakash Madrecha were also present on the occasion.

3G mobile service by December-end
Sharing BSNL's other plans, BSNL CMD Kuldeep Goyal said that by December-end, BSNL would roll out 3G mobile services in the north India.

3G networks enable mobile phone users to access a wider range of more advanced services including wide-area wireless voice telephony, video calls and broadband wireless data.

"We are also looking at launching TelePresence, a new conferencing technology, which is an interesting combination of video, audio and interactive elements," he said.

By the end of the current financial year, BSNL is also going to provide Wimax cover that provides for the wireless transmission of data to 24,000 villages in India, he said.

Heading: Free house plan for conservancy staff taking shape - Indian Express
Content:
The National Commission for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-nomadic Tribes set up by the Union Government has recommended Special Socio-economic Settlements Zones (SSZ) for nomadic tribes similar to the Special Economic Zones (SEZ) for the industry.

The commission has also recommended 10 per cent reserved seats for denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes in the country in education, jobs and politics.

The commission has suggested a ceiling on the maximum land to be given for the purpose and has sought an act to be passed to this effect, said Balkrishna Renake, chairman of the commission on Friday while talking to reporters.

"The nomadic tribes for years have been deprived of basic amenities. The commission has termed them as "denizens". If the government really wants to improve their condition, SSZ is the answer," said Renake.

"These settlements would have schools, hospitals and other basic amenities including an independent Gram Panchayat. The commission has also recommended some part of the land for the economically backward people from upper caste in the SSZ," he said.

Renake rubbished the claims made by nomadic tribes leader Laxman Mane that the Union Government had disapproved the report of the Renake Commission. "I personally talked to Social Justice and Empowerment Minister Meira Kumar and she denied any such thing," he said.

The commission has estimated the population of nomadic tribes in the country at around 12 crore.

Many of the nomadic tribes are at present included in the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe list in many states. "The leaders of SC and ST expressed opposition to sharing their reservation with nomadic tribes. Therefore, the commission recommended an independent quota for nomadic tribes," he said.

The commission is of the view that the government should start sensitising programmes to ease the process of assimilation of these deprived tribes into the mainstream.

"Even though the government has abolished the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, the society is still not ready to mix with these tribes. Some tribes are still considered criminal by birth," said Renake.

The Renake Commission
The Union Government had set up this commission on February 6, 2006 to study the condition of denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes in the country and recommend steps to improve their life. Initially, the commission was given a one-year deadline, which was extended by 18 months. The members of commission visited 80 districts in 18 states, talked to people and experts and submitted its report on July 2, 2008.

Heading: Does name of the game matter, if  fun is main theme? - Indian Express
Content:
In a relief to thousands of conservancy staff of municipal corporations and councils in the state who live and work in pathetic conditions, efforts by the state to provide them with better living conditions have taken a formal shape. A government resolution has been passed directing civic bodies to provide free houses, with a carpet area of 269 sq ft, to conservancy staff who have put in 25 or more years of service.

But many disagree with the condition — 25 years of service.

Under the Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Shramsafalya Avas Yojana, permanent houses will be provided to them at the time of retirement and in case a worker dies during service period, his/her heir or close relative is entitled to own the house, which will be non-transferable.

The state's decision came after a sustained campaign by The Indian Express in October 2007, highlighting the pathetic working conditions of conservancy staff in the city. The state announcement had come on September 18 after a cabinet meeting.

In a notification issued by the state urban development secretary Manu Kumar Srivastava on October 22, the government said it would reserve 15 per cent of the houses in existing projects — Low Income Group housing, Integrated Housing and Slums Development Programme (IHSDP), Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP) and surplus flats generated under the Slum Rehabilitation Scheme — for conservancy workers.

In case the civic bodies do not have land available for these projects, the state government has asked them to acquire government-owned surplus land, which was released after the repeal of the Urban Land Ceiling Act (ULC) and directed the revenue and forest departments to release their land for the purpose at nominal rates.

All local bodies have been directed to reserve five per cent of their budgetary provision for the weaker section each year for the purpose of constructing houses for conservancy workers. The state government will also release funds for such projects as and when required.

It also states that if the civic body decides to implement a mass housing project for such workers on its land or on land owned by the state, then the project will be granted a maximum Floor Space Index (FSI) of four. If the same project is carried out through a private builder, he will be allowed 50 per cent of the total built up area as his incentive FSI.

Meanwhile, a corporator in Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), Dr Siddharth Dhende, has demanded the removal of the 25-year service period as condition for the scheme. "Once a conservancy worker completes 25 years of service, the allowance given for working in miserable conditions is stopped. Therefore, all the conservancy workers, who are in service presently, should be provided free housing under the scheme," Dhende said.

"Secondly, if private developers are allowed 50 per cent of the total built up area as incentive FSI under the scheme, conservancy workers should be provided a housing of 400 sq ft instead of the 269 sq ft carpet area as mentioned in the state resolution," he added.

Heading: ATS probe biased: VHP - Indian Express
Content:
Hong Kong Cricket Club Hotties come calling, but to play rugby

Though they go by the title 'cricket club hotties', their preferred game is rugby. This is what rugby lovers in the city will find out when the seven-a-side rugby tournament organised by the Western Indian Rugby Football Union (WIRFU) gets flagged off next Saturday.

For the Hong Kong Cricket Club Hotties, an invitational girl's club team, it will be the first chance to play in India, a country that's usually identified with cricket.

"We are excited to plan a tour to such a wonderful destination. The competition will serve as a team-building exercise for our team but that apart, we are looking forward to some positive inputs for local rugby in Pune," team captain Anna Holmes told The Indian Express.

When asked about the rather exotic team name, she said, "Our club is called 'Hong Kong Cricket Club' and we adopted the name to represent the femininity. We came up with 'The Hong Kong Hotties,' which we toured as before but as we have a stronger club representation this tour and wanted to include the club name too. We are quite aware that cricket is almost like a religion in India and thought such a name might attract some extra attention."

The Hong Kong Cricket Club Hotties is a professional outfit that regularly competes in the tertiary league in Hong Kong. The team comprises British, Kiwi, German, Chinese, Singaporean and American players who have been rucking together for the past ten years. The average age of the team is 26 years and it has previously participated in the Singapore Rugby 7's tournament in 2006 and the Macau Beach Rugby tournament earlier this year. The team is thrilled to be coming to the city.

Surhud Khare, coach of the Khare's Football And Rugby Academy (KFANDRA) and Pune rugby team, feels that women's rugby in the city will receive an impetus with the participation of the international club team.

"Pune rugby will receive a massive boost thanks to the upcoming tournament. It will increase media coverage for the sport and people will realise how serious Pune is about women's rugby. Our girls will be able to learn a lot from the Hong Kong players, who have a lot of experience."

The competition, which kicks off on November 22, will see five club teams from across the country vying for top honors at Go Sports Academy in Kondhwa. The response to the inaugural edition has been encouraging, with teams from Jammu & Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala participating.

Hosts Pune will field two teams. The event is being held under the auspices of the India Rugby Football Union (IRFU) and hosted by Pune District Rugby Football Association and KFANDRA.

Heading: Photo expo on Bhimsen Joshi to mark Sawai Gandharva fest - Indian Express
Content:
The VHP claims investigations by the state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) into Malegaon blast case are biased.

"The ATS is trying to link the suspects in the Malegaon blast case with the blasts at Nanded, Parbhani and Jalna, files of which were closed long back. We find no reason other than vote-bank politics (of the government) behind the move," alleged Babuji Natekar, leader of the Western Maharashtra unit of the VHP at a press conference here on Friday.

He added: "Abdul Karim Telgi named some top political leaders during his narco test. Police never interrogated them. If the government believes narco test produces false results, why are Sadhvi Pragya, Lt. Col Purohit and other suspects being subjected to narco tests repeatedly?" Natekar announced a nationwide agitation against injustice to Hindus and said a rally would be organised in Pune on November 23.

Mahant met Purohit in city, reveals probe
Mahant Amritananda alias Dayanand Pandey who was produced in Nashik court on Friday has reportedly told ATS he came in contact with Purohit and Sadhvi Pragya Thakur in Pune a few years ago. Pande did not spell out exactly when.

Meanwhile, Pune police would seek custody of Malegaon blast suspect Sameer Kulkarni to investigate if he was involved in the attack on Pastor Silway of the Vineyard Church in Bopodi on August 25, 2007. Kulkarni, a resident of Chinchwad, was the pointman of Abhinav Bharat in Bhopal. Abraham Mathai, General Secretary of All Indian Christian Council, had demanded police action against Kulkarni and four others. Police are likely to take Kulkarni into custody on Tuesday.

Heading: Soon, each district to get child courts - Indian Express
Content:
Come December and music lovers in the city are in for a special visual treat. With the Sawai Gandharva Music Festival beginning from December 11, Arya Sangeet Prasarak Mandal (ASPM), the organising body of the festival is planning a photo exhibition of Bharat Ratna Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, photographed in different moods. This edition promises to be one of a kind and will acknowledge the services rendered by the maestro to Hindustani classical music.

Shrikant Deshpande, joint secretary, ASPM, confirmed that the organisers had a plan to have such an exhibition. "Panditji has recently received Bharat Ratna and we want to do something big to recognise his work. There is a plan of arranging an exhibition of photographs capturing different moods of Pandit Joshi. We have not finalised the proposal officially but the idea is definitely there," he said.

The members of the ASPM in the recently held meeting mooted the idea of the exhibition. "It will be befitting to salute Panditji in the festival, which he started in the memory of his guru Sawai Gandharva, 56 years back," said a member. "We had organised a photo exhibition last year also. It is like a value-added feature of the festival," he said.

According to the member, the exhibition will have over 50 photographs showcasing different moods in Joshi's singing. "Some photographs will be from his younger days. There will be some photographs that have not yet been printed anywhere. It will be a visual journey into maestro's music career," he said.

The Sawai Gandharva Music Festival will be held from December 11 to 14 at the playground of New English School, Ramanbaug at Shaniwar Peth. While on December 11, 12 and 13, there will be only one session from 4 pm to 10 pm, on December 14 there will be an extra session in the morning from 8 am to noon, apart from the regular 4 pm to 10 pm session.

Heading: AIDS awareness: NGOs gearing up with various programmes - Indian Express
Content:
Cases related to child labour, child trafficking and child abuse in the state would now see rapid clearance, as every district in Maharashtra is set to have a child court dedicated to these cases.

"Orders will be issued to all district courts within a fortnight asking them to designate one court for children-related cases," said Harshvardhan Patil, State Minister for women and child welfare. "In addition, we are planning to establish new child courts in Pune, Nagpur, Ahmedabad and Mumbai that will ensure zero pendency of the cases," Patil said.

He was in the city to felicitate meritorious students from government observation homes on the occasion of Children's Day on Friday. The programme was organised by Women and Child Development Department (WCDD).
